text.ACTION:
Part 1: ???: In Medias Res
	Part 1: ???: In Medias Res
Music- Wake Up, Get Up, Get Out There (Listen to this)
There’s a whole nifty animated intro with the characters ice-skating through the streets, but let’s just jump right in here.
This title screen is pretty similar to Persona 4’s original opening screen, but with masks replacing glasses.
There’s a bunch more free DLC for this game, but this is the important one. We’ll explain why in time.

text.Igor: Similarities between characters or events to persons living or dead in your world are purely coincidental.

...The contract has been sealed. The world is not as it should be. It’s filled with distortion, and ruin can no longer be avoided. Those who oppose fate and desire change ...  From time to time, they were referred to as Tricksters. You are the Trickster ...  Now is the time to rise against the abyss of distortion.

text.ACTION: A helicopter flies towards a cityscape.
It approaches a casino and the camera pans in.
A black-clothed figure leaps stealthily through the air, crossing the room via the lights above.
Well, aren’t you pleased with yourself?
Music- Life Will Change (Listen to this)

text.Futaba Sakura: Stay calm! You can get away now!

text.Makoto Niijima: We’ll retrieve the briefcase on our end.

text.Futaba Sakura: Hm ... ? What was that...?

text.Morgana: Don’t worry about us. Just concentrate on getting away!

text.ACTION: Our hero jumps across the lights stylishly.

text.Morgana: Nice work as always, Joker.

text.Ann Takamaki: I bet Skull wouldn’t pull it off that smoothly.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: This happens because you have no sense for aesthetics.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Nobody asked you, Inari!

text.Futaba Sakura: Just run! Get out of there!

text.Haru Okumura: Everyone remember where we’re meeting up?

text.Futaba Sakura: No worries. I can guide you all.

text.ACTION: The agents transform into masked creatures.
...before landing directly on top of the enemy, grabbing its mask, and...
The enemy’s body bubbles up and explodes into a mass of red and black goo.
It then turns into whatever the hell this monstrosity is.
For future reference, this is the battle menu. It’s pretty rad.
Joker dispatches the creature with the help of the shadowed figure behind him.

text.Morgana: Good. You defeated them with ease.

text.Futaba Sakura: More of them? Be careful!

text.ACTION: Joker dodges the attack with a sick backflip and jumps up to a higher floor.

text.Futaba Sakura: Joker, behind you! Go through that door!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, can he even hear us!?

text.Futaba Sakura: Don’t worry, I’m picking up everyone’s voices. Just go, Joker!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Tch. We got away from those guys in black, but there’re still loads more of ‘em...

text.Agent: I can’t confirm the intruder’s location.

text.ACTION: Joker quickly takes cover behind a nearby box.

text.Futaba Sakura: Hide in the shadows, and sneak past when you see an opening!

text.ACTION: From there, he can leap from object to object to conceal his presence.

text.Agent: Understood. I will continue the search!

text.ACTION: Joker is now free to run up the stairs into another cutscene.

text.Futaba Sakura: Something wrong? The exit should be up ahead.

text.Joker: Through there...?

text.Futaba Sakura: Nnh...! That’s just how it is. After that commotion, the bottom floor’s--

text.Makoto Niijima: --completely closed off. Hey, can you make it!?

text.ACTION: Joker hops the railing and runs across it to the other side of the room.

text.Futaba Sakura: What a showoff.

text.Morgana: You’re so reckless, you know that?

text.Futaba Sakura: Enemies, here!? These readings ...  It can’t be!

text.Makoto Niijima: An ambush!?

text.Morgana: Joker, can you handle this!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Joker!

text.Haru Okumura: Oh no!

text.ACTION: It looks like we might just make it away after all.
Friendly Mr. SWAT introduces Joker to the butt of his rifle.

text.Agent: You have your teammate to thank for this. You were sold out.

text.ACTION: Joker is appropriately shocked to hear this news.

text.Detective: Wake him up.

text.ACTION: One of the officers splashes him with a bucket of water.

text.Detective: No dozing off. You still don’t get it, do you?
Are you thinking it can be used as video evidence?
So you’re not that dumb.

text.ACTION: Please stop kicking me, kind sir.

text.Joker: (cough) Nngh ... ! (wheeze)

text.Detective: Obstruction of justice, blackmail, defamation, possession of weapons...
To think that all these crimes were led by a punk like this... And you seemed to be enjoying every second of it... Huh?

text.Joker: I was ...  enjoying it ... ? Everything’s hazy ...  I can’t remember...

text.ACTION: And here’s the difficulty select screen. The difficulty in Persona 5 primarily just messes with how much damage you take and inflict, and at both extremes, how much money and experience you get. We won’t be messing with it and will keep it on Normal.

text.Detective: You should know your place.
It’s a confession under your name.

text.ACTION: The protagonist just bats it away with his hand.

text.Detective: I see. I need your hand to sign this, but ...

text.ACTION: And in retaliation, the cop stomps on the protagonist’s leg.

text.Detective: Don’t expect to walk out of here in one piece. We’re going to make you understand ...  One must take full responsibility for their actions ...

text.ACTION: I’m beginning to think I shouldn’t trust the police.

And here’s the naming screen. We’ll stop here for today, but feel free to suggest a name. If not I’ll just go with the canon-ish name from the manga which is Akira Kurusu. I’d prefer something more interesting though if I’m going to be staring at this for the rest of my life. There won’t be a lot of votes in this thread but I feel I can leave this at least up to the audience.

Part 2: ???-4/9: Lap Of Luxury
	Part 2: ???-4/9: Lap Of Luxury

We’re just ordinary high school student infamous thief Mark Hamill. I know you guys picked this because of the "Joker" connection, but now that I think about it, it also works really well as a reference to "Trickster," huh.

text.Sae Niijima: I’m Niijima from the Public Prosecutors Office.

text.Detective 2: The Prosecutors Office? What business do you have here?

text.Sae Niijima: Just let me through; it’s urgent. There’s something I need to confirm with the suspect.

text.Detective 2: Niijima-san, I believe this case is no longer in your jurisdiction. Besides ...

text.ACTION: I’m fairly certain this detective shares a voice actor with Dojima from P4 and it freaks me out every time.

text.Older Detective: There’s a call from your director. Hurry and get it over with. To be frank, you’re being an inconvenience.

text.Sae Niijima: I’m responsible for this case, yet I’m not even being allowed an interrogation!?

text.SIU Director: I’m calling because I knew you’d bring it up.

text.Sae Niijima: I will not be convinced unless I confirm it for myself. This is MY case.

text.SIU Director: (sigh) Good luck to you then. I won’t be expecting much though.

text.Older Detective: Ah, Prosecutor. I forgot to mention something important. Your time will be cut short. We can’t permit you to talk with him for long.
It’s for your own sake. His methods are unknown. After all, we don’t even know if it’s safe to simply meet and speak with him.

text.ACTION: Why, sure. That sounds not suspicious at all.

text.Sae Niijima: ...I understand.
You’ll be answering my questions this time.
Can you hear me? It seems you’ve been through a lot. Almost anything can happen here ...  and I can’t stop them. That’s why I need you to answer me honestly. I don’t have much time either.

text.ACTION: Oh, screw off with this transparent good-cop/bad-cop BS. Don’t tell ‘em a damn thing.

text.Sae Niijima: What was your objective? Why did you cause such a major incident? I didn’t think it was a prank from the get-go, but I couldn’t assemble a case for prosecution. It’s because I couldn’t figure out the method behind it.

True. There’s no way I could be convinced of such a "world" just by reading the reports. It seems you’re coherent. When and where did you find out about that world? How is it even possible to steal another’s heart? Now, tell me your account of everything. ...Start from the very beginning.

text.ACTION: Music- The Poem of Everyone’s Souls
All the light in the room drops out, and a blue butterfly flies past Maaku.

In Persona 3 and 4, the blue butterfly appears exceedingly briefly, but is implied to be Philemon, a character capable of awakening peoples’ Personas in Persona 1 and 2. He’s one of the only connections to the PS1 era of the series remaining, and this is his only appearance in this game.
The voice of a young woman reaches out to Maaku.

text.Lavenza: A prisoner of fate to a future that has been sealed in advance. This is truly an unjust game ...  Your chances of winning are almost none. But if my voice is reaching you, there may yet be a possibility open to you ...  I beg you. Please overcome this game ...  and save the world ...  The key to victory lies within the memories of your bonds--the truth that you and your friends grasped. It all began that day ...  when the game was started half a year ago ...  For the sake of the world’s future ...  as well as your own ...  you must remember ...

text.ACTION: Maaku wakes up looking just unbearably like Harry Potter.

text.Train Intercom: Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for riding with us today. We will be arriving in Shibuya shortly. This is the last stop for this line. Please transfer here for all subway lines. The doors to your left will open.

text.ACTION: A drunk man is accosting a woman, who’s screaming for help.
The man drunkenly slips and falls.
Maaku stares at his hands while the man recovers.
Back in the present, we overhear a conversation.

text.Schoolgirl: To a person, though? That’s gotta be a joke! You really love all that occult stuff, don’t you?

text.ACTION: Later, Maaku is walking through Shibuya, staring at his phone for guidance.
...everyone around him comes to a halt.
The flow of time has completely stopped.
Beyond the crowd, a blue flame emerges.
It erupts into a winged figure.
Its wicked smile transforms into a yellow-eyed version of Maaku’s own face.
And just like that, time has begun to move again.
Maaku does the only sensible thing and drags the app straight into the garbage can.
And so we arrive in Yongen-Jaya.
Good to know. Whenever we need an objective, the top-right corner of the screen will tell us what we’re currently doing.

text.Joker: His house should be in the backstreets of this residential area...

text.ACTION: We can also talk to people or just eavesdrop in their conversations like a goober.
...But we do actually need directions, so…

text.Joker: I want to ask for directions.

text.Unfriendly Officer: Hm? You want to get to the residence at that address...? It’s in an alley a bit further back. Take a right after that apartment with the stairs.

text.ACTION: I like how Maaku automatically turns away and puts his head down when he eavesdrops. He knows how much of a creep he’s being.
Up ahead we find the Sakura residence.

text.Joker: Even after ringing the doorbell, it doesn’t look like anyone will answer the door. Maybe he’s gone out...

text.ACTION: A deliveryman in a familiar uniform arrives.

text.Deliveryman: Well, Leblanc’s in the back alley so I should make my other deliveries first ...  Mmm, next I need to take this package to...

text.ACTION: Let’s turn back around and head toward Leblanc, then.
Inside, the only customers are fixated on the television.

text.Tabloid Show Host: The citizens can’t live in peace if this keeps up.

text.Elderly Female Customer: What could be going on? Didn’t something similar happen just the other day?

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...Oh, right. They did say that was today.

text.Elderly Male Customer: We’ll be going now. The payment’s on the table.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Thanks for coming.

text.Elderly Male Customer: This place is in the back alley, so there’s no worries of a car crashing in here.

text.Sojiro Sakura: A what now?

text.Elderly Male Customer: There’s been a string of those rampage accidents, you know. I just hope none of them happen around here.

text.Sojiro Sakura: It’s none of my concern.

text.Elderly Male Customer: Haha, we’ll see you next time.

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...Four hours for just a single cup of joe.

text.ACTION: Uh, sure, let’s go with that.

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...Uh-huh. I’m Sojiro Sakura. You’ll be in my custody over the next year. I was wondering what kind of unruly kid would show up, but you’re the one, huh? Have you been told? A customer of mine and your parents know each other and-- Well, not that that matters ...  Follow me.
I’ll at least give you sheets for your bed. You look like you wanna say something.

text.ACTION: Let’s not get on this guy’s bad side immediately.

text.Sojiro Sakura: It’s on you to clean up the rest. I’ll be leaving after I lock up each day. You’ll be alone at night, but don’t do anything stupid. I’ll throw you out if you cause any trouble. Now then. I got the gist of your situation. You protected some woman from a man forcing himself on her, he got injured, then sued you. Right? That’s what you get for sticking your nose in a matter between two adults. You did injure him, yeah? And now that you’ve got a criminal record, you were expelled from your high school. The courts ordered you to transfer and move out here, which your parents also approved.

text.ACTION: Thanks for the incredibly unsympathetic exposition, Sojiro.

text.Sojiro Sakura: It’s best you not talk about anything unnecessary. I am in the restaurant business, you know. Behave yourself for the year. If nothing happens, your probation will be lifted.
Cause any problems, and you’ll be sent straight to juvie. We’ll be going to Shujin tomorrow.
Shujin Academy--the school you’ll be attending. We’ll introduce ourselves properly to the staff there. There’s rarely a place that’ll accept someone like you, you know. What a waste of my Sunday ...
Your "luggage" arrived earlier; I left them over there.

text.Joker: I’ll be living here starting today ...  I should check out what’s in here ...

text.ACTION: You could check, but all you’d learn is “IT’S DUSTY” and “THERE’S CRAP EVERYWHERE.” Instead, let’s go ahead and open the box.

text.Joker: It’s full of clothes and daily necessities. I’ll change into more comfortable clothes for now.

text.ACTION: Why were you wearing your school uniform in the first place?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Though it’s only natural you’d want to keep your room tidy. Why don’t you go to bed for tonight? You don’t have anything better to be doing, right? I’m going to close up shop and get out of here myself. I won’t be the one looking after you if you get sick from staying up too late, you got that?

text.ACTION: Attempting to leave the room causes the game to remind you that yes, you should go to sleep.

text.Joker: That day ...  I had to go home early...

text.ACTION: So here we are, in Maaku’s “Hometown Neighborhood.” An altercation is audible in the distance.

text.Drunk Man: You think you’re worth causing me trouble? Huh?
Heh, call them if you want! The police are my bitches. They’re not gonna take you seriously.
Someone called the cops, huh? Get in the car! Incompetent fools like you just need to shut their mouths and follow where I steer this country!
This ain’t a show. Get lost, kid. See? This is all because you’re so damn slow! Get in the car!

text.ACTION:
Part 3: 4/10-4/11: Everybody Hates Maaku
	Part 3: 4/10-4/11: Everybody Hates Maaku
Video: Velvet Room (Worth watching just for the snippet of Igor, that voice filter is something else)
Maaku wakes up in an unfamiliar location.

text.Caroline: (chuckle)

text.ACTION: Oh, hey, Igor. You got something in your throat?

You’ll be able to hear it in his line in the clip but Igor is now voiced by David Lodge under a ridiculous voice filter instead of Dan Woren, because his Japanese VA died. For the P4 spinoffs Igor was either conspicuously absent or had his voice lines from previous games reused because of this. There was also that weird moment in Ultimax where he was voiced by Vic Mignogna, but let’s not talk about that.

Anyway, because his Japanese voice actor passed away, when they were forced to recast him they clearly went in the exact opposite direction from his more high-pitched voice in games prior, jeeeeeeesus.
Music- The Poem of Everyone’s Souls

text.Justine: The you in reality is currently fast asleep. You are only experiencing this as a dream.

text.ACTION: Being dragged into the Velvet Room while you’re sleeping is a pretty common occurrence in Persona.

text.Caroline: You’re in the presence of our master! Stand up straight!

text.Igor: This place exists between dream and reality, mind and matter. It is a room that only those who are bound by a "contract" may enter. I am Igor, the master of this place. Remember it well. I summoned you to speak of important matters. It involves your life as well.
The state of this room reflects the state of your own heart. To think a prison would appear as such.

text.ACTION: The prison, however, is new. In Persona 3 the Velvet Room was an elevator and in Persona 4 it was a limousine.

text.Igor: In the near future, there is no mistake that ruin awaits you.

I speak of the end to everything. However, there is a means to oppose such a fate. You must be "rehabilitated." Rehabilitated toward freedom ...  That is your only means to avoid ruin.  ... Do you have the resolve to challenge the distortion of the world?

You didn’t decline, hm? Very well, that is enough. Allow me to observe the path of your rehabilitation. Ah, pardon me for not introducing the others. To your right is Caroline; to your left, Justine. They serve as wardens here.

text.Justine: ...That is, if you remain obedient.

text.ACTION: Caroline and Justine also follow the naming scheme of previous Velvet Room characters, in that they’re named after characters from Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein. Justine is named after a character who was framed for a murder committed by Frankenstein’s monster, and Caroline is named after Victor Frankenstein’s mother.

text.Igor: I shall explain the roles of these two at another occasion. Now then, it seems the night is waning ...  it is almost time. Take your time to slowly come to understand this place. We will surely meet again, eventually...

text.Caroline: Time’s up! Now hurry up and go back to sleep.

text.Joker: Ruin ...  Rehabilitation ...  What does it mean ... ?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Well then, let’s go introduce ourselves properly to the staff about your transfer. The school you’re attending is in the Aoyama district. It’ll cost you a bit to ride the train there, and the route transfers are a pain. I’ll drive you there, but just for today. Let’s go.

text.ACTION: I failed to mention it before but Sojiro is voiced by the consistently amazing Jamieson Price. He’s one of my favorite performances in this game.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Do me a favor and behave yourself, all right? Don’t get me wrong--I don’t care what happens to you. Just don’t cause me any trouble.

text.ACTION: Oh my god, what the fuck am I looking at? It’s like Wilson Fisk did a fusion dance with a runny egg.

text.Principal: Honestly, I hesistated on accepting someone like you, but there were some circumstances on our side ...  You might have done a variety of things in hiding in your hometown, but you will behave yourself here. If you are thrown out from our school, there will be no place for you to go. Keep that in mind. This is the teacher in charge of your class.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Be sure to read the school rules. Any violations will send you straight to the guidance office. And if by chance you cause any problems, I won’t be able to protect you at all. ...That IS your promise, yes, Principal Kobayakawa?

text.Principal: He is responsible for all his actions.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: But really though, why me ...  There should have been better candidates.

text.Principal: It was a sudden transfer, and your class was the only one that had an opening.

text.Sojiro Sakura: If you’re done explaining things, mind if we get going? I got a store to get back to.

text.Principal: Sakura-san, please keep a close eye on him. Don’t let him cause any trouble outside...

text.Sojiro Sakura: Well, I’ll be sure to have a serious talk about the situation he’s in.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Come to the faculty office when you arrive at school tomorrow. I’ll show you to your classroom.

text.Sojiro Sakura: I guess that’s what it means to have a criminal record. Turns out your past follows you wherever you go. By the way ...  if you get expelled now, I won’t hesitate to kick you out. Got it?
(sigh) School never changes, huh ... ? Come on, we’re going home.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: I can’t believe they pushed someone with a record on me. A male teacher would be better suited for this...

text.Suguru Kamoshida: Why in the world was someone like that admitted here?

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Who knows? It was the principal’s decision. I was told that it’s for the school’s reputation.

text.Suguru Kamoshida: I would have thought that my volleyball team has contributed more than enough to cover that.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: That’s certainly true.

text.Suguru Kamoshida: Be careful, OK? Then again, if anything were to happen, I’d kick out a student like that right away.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: I keep wishing that he’d just end up not coming to school. Still, that isn’t something I should be saying as a teacher...

text.Suguru Kamoshida: Well, I should be returning to practice.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Oh, right. The tournament’s coming up, isn’t it?

text.Suguru Kamoshida: Hehe, having such high expectations placed on you by others is quite a problem in itself. We’ll have to work hard to make up for the track team too.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Yes ...  that’s true.

text.ACTION: Even the teachers hate our guts.

text.Sojiro Sakura: You’re taking the train, starting tomorrow. ...So how was it? The school, I mean. Think you can manage?

You brought it on yourself though. Still, you were expelled once already. To think you’d re-enroll at a different one. It’s not like anyone will be sympathetic with you. ...If that’s what it was like at school, people might say stuff about me in the future too ...  What a troublesome kid I’ve taken in.
I was asked to do it, and I just ...  happened to agree to it. I’ve already been paid for it too, after all.
...Another accident? So that’s why it’s so crowded. There’s been a lot of those lately.

text.ACTION: It arrives, faster than they expected.
The conductor, eyes rolled back and drooling black goo, continues pushing forward.
The image moves to a corner of the screen, revealing a newscaster.

text.Female Newscaster: That was direct footage from the accident. According to the police, the engineer’s life was not in danger, despite his injuries. After questioning, even he could not explain his high speed when approaching the station. No further comments were made. Police are still looking for a plausible motive.

text.ACTION: The camera pans out from the television, revealing Sae and her superior watching the feed.

text.SIU Director: It’s less an operating accident and more a crime of the company and the government.
Seems the company and the Ministry of Transport both turned a blind eye to the truth.

text.ACTION: Wait, what? I guess the dead-eyed ghoul possessed by some unholy force didn’t make it onto the news. What’s this guy talking about?

text.Female Newscaster: Now onto our main story. With this derailment accident, as well as other recent incidents of unknown motive, concern is spreading among the general public. Just what could be causing such a drastic change so suddenly in these people?

text.ACTION: More stuff like this has been happening? That’s terrifying.

text.SIU Director: Everything’s linked–that’s what you’re thinking, correct? ...Ah well. Are you free? You and I haven’t gone for a drink in a while.

text.Sae Niijima: Thank you sir, but I have another meeting to attend. I must be going.
Not quite. I want your opinion on something.

text.Goro Akechi: Sure. Your judgement is quite often correct, though. Can we discuss this over sushi, perhaps? You are making a student work late, after all.

text.Sae Niijima: Conveyor belt only.

text.Sojiro Sakura: I wasn’t able to open the cafe today ...  ...Whatever. Just head upstairs. There’s something I need to give you.

You may be under probation, but there’s no special limitations on what you do in particular. Besides following the law, that is. However, I’m obligated to report on you, which is why I’m having you record your daily activities.

text.ACTION: So I’m living above a coffee shop owned by a grumpy old man whose only method of checking what I’m doing is reading my diary. Japanese probation is weird as hell.

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...I’m about to leave right now. Don’t worry. I’ll be there in no time. ...Uh-huh. I’ll see you soon.
Oh, but don’t mess up my store. If something goes missing, I’ll hand you right over to the cops. You got school tomorrow ...  You better head off to bed, all right?

text.Joker: I should write down what happened today in my diary...

text.ACTION: Writing in our diary is actually how we save.
This is the only corner of the save menu I can actually show, however, because the rest is full of spoilers.

text.Joker: I have an early day tomorrow ...  I should rest up...

text.ACTION: Before Maaku makes it to bed, he hears a ringing sound from somewhere.

text.Joker: That ringing sound isn’t coming from my cell phone...

text.Sojiro Sakura: Uhhh ...  I closed up shop, but I forgot to flip the sign to CLOSED. It’s too much of a hassle for me to go back, so you flip the sign for me.
Sorry. I make it a habit not to save guys’ numbers on my cell phone.

text.ACTION: Okay, I changed my mind, Sojiro’s amazing.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Anyway, I’m glad you answered the phone over in the shop. OK then, I’m leaving you in charge of the door sign.

text.ACTION: Time to head outside and flip the sign over.
Don’t savor this taste of freedom; you can’t stray more than ten feet from Leblanc in either direction.

text.Joker: Looks like I need to go out to Shibuya, then transfer there. More news about that subway accident ...  It sounds like a lot of people were hurt. I bet this’ll affect the timetables for tomorrow too...
It keeps showing up...
I should probably reboot my phone, just in case ...  My eyelids are starting to get heavy...
Hopefully I can get there without getting lost ...  I don’t want to be late on my first day. I should head out now...

text.ACTION: Neat little detail- Maaku automatically grabs his bag on the way down.
Let’s greet Sojiro before we leave.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Here, I’ll feed you. Just make sure you finish it before the customers start coming in.
What’s that reaction for? Just eat it.

text.Joker: I can taste complex flavors within the bold spiciness...

text.Sojiro Sakura: It’s time for you to go.
Thanks. ...Hurry over to school. You’ll end up late if you get lost on the way.
Don’t forget to do that for me, all right? Now, you better hurry on out. You’re gonna be late if you get lost, country boy.

text.ACTION: Time to head to the train station.

text.Joker: It turns out the rumors about the Tokyo subway are true ...  They’re showing the news up on the LCD screen ...  It seems like there are still some lingering effects of yesterday’s accident...

text.ACTION: I hear this game’s representation of Shibuya is pretty accurate, particularly the train station. I don’t know much about that, but I do know that it’s a pretty accurate representation...
We finally find our way out of here and above ground.

text.Protesting Man: Could this puzzling accident be a coincidence? To ensure the safety of the people, countermeasures must be taken immediately...

text.ACTION: This protestor, for example, is apparently parodying the real-life phenomenon of a group known colloquially in English as the Bible Distribution League. As you might have guessed, they distribute religious materials. Their counterparts in Persona 5 are more likely to drone on about the Sun God, but it’s fascinating what they bothered to reproduce here.
While running around aimlessly, we see this. Seems like Rise’s doing well for herself. Good for her.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Huh? It’s raining outside?

text.Man in a Suit: It just started all of a sudden ...  This is why I hate the early spring.

text.Sojiro Sakura: That reminds me ...  Did he take an umbrella...?
Don’t mind me. So, what’ll it be?

text.Newscaster: The effects of yesterday’s subway accident continues on today as various lines suffer delays and--

text.Man in a Suit: There’s been a lot of nasty accidents lately. You know, I mean the subway accident that the news is talking about ...  My coworker got caught up in it and is in the hospital now ...  But that aside, it’s kinda creepy. The people who caused these accidents supposedly went crazy all of a sudden. I heard that some of them suffered from nervous breakdowns during interrogation.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Huh.

text.ACTION: Students run to school in the rain.
Maaku, however, is stuck hiding under an awning.
The mysterious app reappears on his phone.
A hooded figure hurries past to hide under the same awning.
The girl notices Maaku staring at her oddly, but doesn’t seem to mind.
A car drives up and stops in front of the pair.

text.Joker: Nah.

text.ACTION: The girl looks distressed before the car drives off.
A boy with bleached hair runs after the car.

text.Joker: ...Pervy teacher?

text.ACTION: The strange app responds to Maaku’s voice.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You plannin’ on rattin’ me out to Kamoshida?
Huh? In that car just now. It was Kamoshida. He does whatever the hell he wants. Who does he think he is--the king of a castle? Don’t you agree?

text.ACTION: That’s a bit of a labored analogy, but okay.
I’m a big fan of taking the options in Persona games that make the protagonist seem like a total dipshit.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uh, it’s just a sayin’ ...   ...  ...   ... .Wait. You don’t know Kamoshida? Are you for real? You’re from Shujin, right?
What ... ? No other high school’s got a uniform like this. A second-year, huh ...  We’re the same grade then. Never seen you before though. Oh, you a transfer student?

text.Joker: (nods)

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then no wonder you don’t know him. This rain ain’t too bad. We better hurry up, or we’ll be late.

text.ACTION: There’s a flash of purple and both Maaku and the other boy grasp their heads.

text.Joker: I feel light-headed for some reason...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uuugh, my head hurts ...  Dammit ...  I wanna go home...

text.Sae Niijima: I assume you know of the uproar that the public calls the "psychotic breakdown incidents."

You say that like it’s none of your business. It was all over the news, and one of the victims included a teacher at your high school. I’ve no doubt you heard about it. On that day ...  were you still an "ordinary" student?

... Let me change the question. You transferred to Shujin Academy, correct? An ordinary prep school that could be found in any city ...  ...That’s what it should have been. What happened around that time? Tell me everything--truthfully.

text.ACTION: Inside Maaku’s bag, the app turns itself on...
The boy’s reaction is decidedly understated.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, this should be right...
What’s goin’ on here ... ? I guess we’ll just have to go and ask.

text.ACTION:
Part 4: 4/11: That's Gonna Scab
	Part 4: 4/11: That's Gonna Scab
When we last left them, Maaku and Vulgar Boy were just entering this castle.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It should be ...  It said "Shujin" on the gate ...  What’s goin’ on here?
The sign was for the school, right?

text.ACTION: Look at this weirdo in the knight costume. Real fuckin’ elaborate, you dork.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Who’re you? You a student? Man, your costume’s impressive ...  Is that armor real? C’mon, don’t just stand there. Say somethin’.
...This shit’s real.

text.ACTION: These cut-ins are a really great addition. I won’t be able to show them all off because they’re pretty frequent but I’ll try to at least grab one if I see it’s new.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We gotta run!
Stop standin’ around and run!
Oww ...  Y-You’re gonna break my bones, dammit! The hell you think you’re—Aagh!
Hey! Wake up!
Yeah, more or less. Looks like this ain’t no dream ...  Ugh, what’s goin’ on!?
Dammit, where are we!? Is this some kinda TV set ... ?

text.ACTION: In the distance, more cries of agony can be heard.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whoa ...  Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa ...  You’re shittin’ me, right ... ?
Isn’t there some way outta here!? C’mon, we gotta do something!

text.ACTION: We get a brief moment to interact with the cell here. Emphasis on “brief.”

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, should we hide in here and trick the guards? It prolly wouldn’t work like it does in the movies though ...  Huh? You hear that?

text.Shadow: Your charge is "unlawful entry." Thus, you will be sentenced to death.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Say what!?
Huh? Wait ...  Is that you, Kamoshida?

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: Are you trying to disobey me again? It looks like you haven’t learned your lesson at all, huh? And you brought a friend this time ...  because you can’t do anything for yourself.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This ain’t funny, you asshole!

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: Is that how you speak to a king? It seems you don’t understand the position you’re in at all. Not only did you sneak into my castle, you committed the crime of insulting me—the king. The punishment for that is death. It’s time for an execution! Take him out!

text.ACTION: Sakamoto shoves one of the soldiers over...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I ain’t down for this shit! C’mon, we’re outta here!

text.ACTION: Maaku makes a valiant effort to fight the knight off, but to no avail.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Just go! Get outta here ... ! These guys are serious!

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: Oh? Running away, are we? What a heartless friend you are.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: He ain’t a friend.

text.ACTION: Look, you hurt Maaku’s feelings. You should apologize, Sakamoto.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: C’mon! Hurry up and go!

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: What’s the matter? Too scared to run away? Hmph, pathetic scum isn’t worth my time ...  I’ll focus on this one’s execution...

text.ACTION: What an amazing, despicable, punchable face.

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: A peasant like you isn’t worth beating. I’ll have you killed right now.
Hm?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: No, I don’t wanna die!

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: Hahaha!

text.ACTION: The voice calls out to us again, and we see the butterfly once more…
(I totally forgot about this scene when I said Philemon only makes one appearance)
Another voice, deep and male this time, rings forth in Maaku’s head.

text.Arsene: Are you forsaking him to save yourself? Death awaits him if you do nothing.

text.ACTION: Everything turns purple, and Maaku starts screaming in pain.

text.Arsene: Vow to me. I am thou, thou art I ...

text.ACTION: ...because there’s a fire in his eyes.

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: Execute him!
What was that ... ?

text.ACTION: The blow knocks off Maaku’s glasses...

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: Hmph ...

text.ACTION: A burst of wind through the room knocks the knight off balance before he can strike.
Suddenly, a strange mask is attached to Maaku’s face.
He tries to rip it off...
Blood becomes flame, and flame becomes the stuff of nightmares.
The fire rises from Maaku’s body and becomes a figure of its own, standing behind him.
It’s got a cravat and a dope top hat, and it’s here to party.
With a wave of his hands, Maaku sends the guards flying.

text.Arsene: If you so desire, I shall consider granting you the power to break through this crisis.

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: Who the hell are you...!? Guards!

text.ACTION: The guards turn into strange pumpkin creatures.

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: You’ll learn the true strength of my men!

text.ACTION: Let’s use a skill. Arsene knows a light Curse skill, Eiha, right off the bat, so let’s use it. It costs 4 SP, but we don't have to worry about skill costs right now at least.
We can also attack with our physical weapon. In Maaku’s case, it’s a knife.

It did a good deal less damage, you probably noticed. While our starting weapon isn’t great, melee attacks are generally inferior to physical and magical skills of appropriate strength. There are certainly times to use melee attacks, but those moments are rather infrequent.

Sweet, Maaku leveled up. He can now cast Eiha a whopping eight times from full SP. If that seems low, just wait. This game somewhat radically shakes up the SP economy established in Personas 3 and 4. Running out of SP is a much greater concern, but we'll get to that later.
Maaku examines his sweet new duds.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What was that just now ... ?

text.ACTION: Sakamoto just runs up and bowls him over.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You like that, you son of a bitch!?
OK, it’s locked!

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: Damn you!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey ... ! What was that just now!? And ...  your clothes ... !

text.ACTION: “Kamoshida” startles the two by slamming the bars.

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: You bastards!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: God, this’s effin nuts! Anyways, let’s scram! You lead the way!

text.ACTION: Sakamoto hucks the keys as far as he can.

text.Shadow Suguru Kamoshida: Goddamn thieves...! After them! Don’t let them escape!
You think you can get away with doing this to me?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: C’mon, let’s get outta here!

text.ACTION: Let’s turn around and talk to this “Kamoshida” fellow. What sage words does he have for us?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, we gotta ignore him and look for a way out!

text.ACTION: Our only way forward, however, is blocked.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It ain’t openin’!? Dammit! Let’s try and find another way through!
Huh? ‘Sup?
Wait, think we can jump across?

text.ACTION: Further in, we encounter more obstacles that must be jumped or crawled past.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: They’ll prolly call for backup if we try and take ‘em on. We should go some other way ... !

text.ACTION: And so we’re forced to turn around and take an alternate route.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Over there ...  They’re lookin’ for us, right? I ain’t playin’ along with this anymore! We gotta find a way outta this goddamn place!

text.ACTION: The enemies are now blocking the path behind us. No way to go but forward.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, let’s get the hell outta this place!
This ain’t the exit!? What the hell is this place!?
Is, uh ...  Is he OK ... ?

text.ACTION: Figures wearing strange masks are locked in cages. That’s troubling.
We can’t do anything to lower the bridge for now, so let’s continue forward.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit! How the hell’re we supposed to get outta here!?

text.Morgana: Look, the key’s right there!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We’re trying to get the hell out of here ... ! I mean, you obviously look like an enemy too!

text.Morgana: I’m locked up here, so how can I be your enemy!? Help me out!

text.ACTION: In the distance, the shuffling of guards can be heard.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: They’re catchin’ up already ... !
How the hell do we get out ... !?

text.Morgana: Hey, you two! You wanna know where the exit is? Let me out and I’ll take you there. You don’t want to get caught and executed, right?
I never go back on my word!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This thing sounds like it’s all talk...

text.Morgana: If you guys think you can get out on your own, then be my guest!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whadda we do ... ?
Are you seriously not messin’ with us!?

text.Morgana: If you don’t hurry, they’ll catch you.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: F-Fine...
Now, where’s the exit, you monster cat!?

text.Morgana: Don’t call me a cat! I am Morgana!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Shuddup and hurry it up! You wanna be locked up again!?

text.Morgana: A-All right, sheesh! Follow me, and stay quiet!

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Sakura-san said that Hamiru-kun left the house this morning. Should I contact the police ... ? No, that’ll just be more of a hassle ...  (sigh) What did I do to deserve this ... ?

text.ACTION: So, we finally met our starting Persona, and it only took four updates! Arsene is based on Arsène Lupin, a fictional gentleman thief from French writer Maurice Leblanc (yet another connection I just now noticed). The first Lupin story, “The Arrest of Arsène Lupin,” was published in 1905. Lupin was a force for good in that he exclusively targeted worse villains than himself, which is absolutely relevant to the themes of this game.
As our starting Persona, Arsene learns physical and Curse skills. Also, I really like that we now have a Persona that’s not mythological or anything, it’s just straight-up fictional.

Part 5: 4/11: What Is It With This Series And Talking Animals?
	Part 5: 4/11: What Is It With This Series And Talking Animals?
Last time, we inadvertently cut class, ripped off our own face, and met a weird talking not-cat. What was in that curry, Sojiro!?
Morgana stops in front of this statue.

text.Morgana: What does it look like I’m doing? I’m lowering the bridge. You, Frizzy Hair. It seems like you pick up on things faster than our Blondie over here. Try checking around the mouth of this statue, OK?

text.ACTION: Maaku pulls down the mouth of the statue...

text.Morgana: Hmph, amateur. Come on, let’s keep going!

text.ACTION: Another guard pops out ahead. Sakamoto promptly begins freaking out.

text.Morgana: Zorro!

text.ACTION: Music- Keeper of Lust (Listen to this DDS-ass music, good lord)

text.Morgana: It means they’re holding nothing back and are serious to kill us! I’ll back you up, so fight like your life depends on it! Let’s go!

text.ACTION: Time for another fight. Let’s go.
Eiha works, but not well enough.

text.Morgana: This is how you fight!

text.ACTION: Morgana takes the initiative here, by which I mean he’s outside of player control for this sequence. Unlike in 3 and 4, the player characters generally start in “Direct Commands” mode by default.
Also, yes, Morgana is male, despite his name. They go into it a bit later but I’m not gonna write around it for twenty updates.
The pumpkin-thing is weak to wind attacks, which happen to be Morgana’s specialty.
Use skills the enemy is weak to, knock them down and get more actions, that’s the 1 More system in a nutshell. There’s slightly more to it in this game, but nothing we can introduce yet.

Arsene learned a new skill. I’ll introduce skills when party members learn them, but for the record Cleave is a light Physical attack. Like in the previous games, Physical skills are cast from HP instead of SP. They also work off a percentage of maximum HP instead of a flat cost.

text.Morgana: Hm, it looks like you don’t have full control over your power yet. The transformation shouldn’t normally dissolve like that. After all--

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Rrgh, that’s enough! This crap doesn’t make any sense!

text.Morgana: Can’t you just sit still and listen for once, Blondie!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Don’t call me Blondie! My name’s Ryuji ...

text.ACTION: Finally getting a first name for Sakamoto here. We skipped basic introductions with all the naked kings and literal self-actualization.

text.Morgana: Actually, there’s no time for me to lecture you! You wanna escape this place in one piece, right? Let’s go! Oh, but before that ...  take these. Use them carefully, OK?
Come on, we should hurry. It’s not much farther to the exit.

text.ACTION: So, a cool new feature in this game is that you can restore all the party’s HP automatically out of battle. I don’t end up doing it much because it can end up pulling SP from a party member you want to keep topped up and you generally don’t always need full HP, but it’s good to have.
Despite the Medicines we just received from Morgana, this does not consume items. It instead uses skills, which are also usable from this menu.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit! I’m too flustered! I can’t remember a damn thing!

text.ACTION: It’s clearly some sort of sports uniform, and it has the name of your school on it. We’ve never even been there, but it seems pretty obvious what he’s wearing.

text.Morgana: Come on, let’s go!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hold on, dammit!
But ...  who are these guys?

text.Morgana: Do you really think you have time to worry about other people right now!? Besides, they’re--
I’m glad you stick to your guns. Looks like it’s raring to go too!

text.ACTION: These enemies are weak to Curse skills, making Arsene perfect.

Another neat addition is that the game will tell you if an enemy in the fight is weak against one of your skills, as long as you’ve already hit that weakness before. It unfortunately includes enemies that are already knocked down which can get a bit confusing, but it’s still really handy.

text.Morgana: You really don’t get it, do you? Hrgh ...  There’s no time to explain. Look, I’m going. If you don’t want to follow, be my guest!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit ...  Fine, I’m coming!

text.ACTION: Glad we’ve settled on “abandon the needy” as our course of action. What brave heroes we are.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Finally! We’re saved ... !
...It’s not openin’! D’you trick us, you jerk!?

text.Morgana: Don’t jump to conclusions! Over here!
Ugh, amateur ...  This is the most basic of basics.
We would’ve done that earlier if that was possible! The ventilation shaft, you morons! You guys should be able to squeeze through it one at a time.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I see ...  Then we just gotta get that metallic mesh off!
Seriously, we’re finally gettin’ outta here ... !

text.Morgana: You should wait on celebrating until you actually get out. Now, get going.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But ...  what about you?

text.Morgana: There’s something that I still have to do. We’re going our separate ways.
Heh. You’ve got manners. Be careful on your way.

text.ACTION: Ryuji and Maaku climb the shelf and leave.

text.Morgana: Especially the frizzy-haired one, if my judgment’s right...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Returned ... ? ...Does that mean we got away?
I dunno what to think anymore...
The hell’s goin’ on!?
Huh? No! We were tryin’ to get to school, and we ended up at this weird castle!

text.Aggressive Officer: ...What? Hand over your bag. You better not be doing any drugs.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Why would you think that!?

text.Timid Cop: Then you should go to school. Take him with you.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Like I’m tryin’ to say ... ! I don’t know what’s goin’ on either!

text.Aggressive Officer: We passed by Shujin on our way here. There was nothing out of the ordinary about it. If you spout any more nonsense, I’ll contact your school. Is that what you want?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: (to Maaku)
Uh, that’s not what I meant ...
...Fine, I’m goin’!

text.SIU Director: (chuckle) Things are going as planned ...  Sae Niijima ...  That reminds me ...  (sigh) Better to leave it be for now.

text.ACTION: So a Minister of Transport resigned after the subway incident, and this is “going as planned.” How does Sae factor into this? I’m not sure I like where this is headed...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I’m sure we came the same way ...  What’s goin’ on here ... ?

text.Counselor: We received a call from the police.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That damn cop snitched on us after all!

text.Counselor: It’s rare not to see you alone. Where were you roaming around until this time?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uh ...  a ca-- a castle?

text.Counselor: So you have no intention of giving an honest answer?

text.Suguru Kamoshida: What’s this about a "castle"?
You seem so carefree, Sakamoto. Quite a difference from when you did morning practice for the track team.

text.Counselor: How dare you speak that way to Mr. Kamoshida! ...There’s not much leeway left for you, you know?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: He’s the one that provoked me!

text.Counselor: Do you really want to be expelled!? In any case, you’ll have to explain yourself! Follow me!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What!? This is bullshit!

text.Suguru Kamoshida: Come now. I should have been more considerate, too. Let’s just say that we were both to blame.

text.Counselor: Well, if you say so ...  Still, you’re coming with me. It’s undeniable that you’re extremely late.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Fine...

text.Suguru Kamoshida: By the way ...  you’re that new transfer student, correct? Maaku Hamiru...

text.ACTION: Ryuji shoots Kamoshida a glare before continuing up the steps.

text.Suguru Kamoshida: That’s right ...  I remember now. ...Well, I’ll overlook this just for today.

text.ACTION: We’re already pushing things here, let’s not go further than we need to, as satisfying as it would be to stand up to this condescending ass.

text.Suguru Kamoshida: At any rate, hurry up and go to the faculty office. I’m sure Ms. Kawakami’s tired of waiting.

text.Sae Niijima: A talking cat ... ? Are you hallucinating from an overdose? I won’t put up with you if you’re simply joking around.

text.ACTION: It seems like everyone thinks Maaku’s just high, both then and in the future. Including myself. Get your life together, man.

text.Sae Niijima: I’m going to have you continue the story. The one who received a "calling card" from the Phantom Thieves was an Olympic medalist.

It’s true that what he did were deplorable crimes from ...  indulging his desire. He confessed to it all. But there should have been no connection between the two of you since you had just transferred. Why did you target him?
Try and recall it once again ... !

text.ACTION: Ah, school. How great it will feel to be greeted with open arms to this hallowed hall of learning.

text.Ushimaru: Late on the first day, too. You like causing trouble for the school?
What’s with that attitude? Show some respect! Do you even want to be reformed? I bet this is a good sign of what you’ll be like here.

text.ACTION: Rumors spread fast, I suppose. We’re already being labeled a criminal who smokes and drinks, the two worst crimes of all.

text.Carefree Female Student: I can’t believe he’s still behaving like this after what he did to the track team. And he’s still not expelled because Mr. Kamoshida’s covering for him, right?

text.Timid Female Student: Mr. Kamoshida’s too nice for not abandoning a punk like that ...

text.Male Volleyball Player: Yeah, I heard about him. All the second-years are talking about it. Apparently, he’s such a problem student that no other schools will take him.

text.Female Volleyball Player: Why does he have to come here ... ? I hope he doesn’t try anything funny with the volleyball team.

text.Male Volleyball Player: It’s fine. Mr. Kamoshida’s on our side. The transfer student won’t do anything to us.

text.ACTION: I feel like we’re not getting the whole picture here. The students seem to love Kamoshida, but Ryuji...

text.Panicked Male Student: What!? But you already promised to recommend me...

text.Teacher 1: I’m sorry, but you’ll have to accept that this was decided by the school. They want to prioritize students from our highly acclaimed volleyball team ...

text.ACTION: This volleyball team seems really important to the school.
Oh no, Ms. Kawakami’s class! I got so caught up in what I was doing I forgot all about it! She’s gonna kill me.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Being over half a day late on your first day ... ? Can you explain yourself?

How could you have been lost for this long? It’s almost lunchtime. Well, it’s probably true that you’re not used to the area yet ...  but you’re still way too late. Will you pull yourself together? You were given fair warning yesterday. More importantly ...  I heard that you were caught along with that Sakamoto-kun?

Don’t get involved with him, OK? He’s nothing but trouble. He wasn’t like that when he was devoting his time to track and field though ...  ...Anyway. Break’s almost over. Classes will end after fifth period today because of the subway accident.

text.ACTION: It was really more of a “collision” than an “accident.”

text.Sadayo Kawakami: I’ll have you introduce yourself when class resumes. Follow me.
Be serious about it even if you’re lying to the class, OK? Do NOT say anything unnecessary.

text.Quiet Student: But he might slug us if we look him in the eye...

text.Sadayo Kawakami: ...Well, I’d like to introduce a transfer student: Maaku Hamiru. Today, we ...  had him attend from the afternoon on since he wasn’t feeling well. All right, please say something to the class.

text.Prim Female Student: He seems quiet ...  but I bet when he loses it...

text.Brown-haired Student: I mean, he was arrested for assault, right...?

text.Sadayo Kawakami: ...Uhh, so ...  Your seat will be ...  Hmm ...  Over there. The one that’s open. Sorry, but can the people nearby please share your textbooks with him for today?

text.Brown-haired Student: Does that mean he hit on her before transferring here?

text.Prim Female Student: That means she’s cheating on him with Mr. Kamoshida. Then again, this is Takamaki-san we’re talking about...

text.Brown-haired Student: For real. That side of the room is totally awful.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Oh, right! The volleyball rally’s in two days ...  Everyone’s just changed classes, so make sure you use that time to get to know each other. Well then, let’s get class started. Who’s on duty today?

text.Yuuki Mishima: Everyone, please rise...

text.ACTION: The school fades out, revealing the castle.
Maaku grasps his head in pain.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Hm? What’s wrong?

(sigh) Are you sure you’re OK? Also ...  it seems like people are already talking about you, but I’m not the one who told them. I can’t even catch a break ...  Why do I have to deal with this? You should head straight home without stopping by anywhere. Sakura-san sounded pretty angry.

text.ACTION: Great, now Sojiro hates me even more. This place sucks.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Oh, and about Sakamoto-kun. Don’t get involved--
Speak of the devil ...  What do you want? I heard the police caught you cutting classes today.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ugh ...  It was nothin’.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: And you haven’t dyed your hair back to black either...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Sorry ‘bout that.

text.ACTION: Ryuji whispers to you before walking off.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: See? That’s why I don’t want you getting involved. Understood?

text.ACTION: The principal and Kamoshida walk up.

text.Suguru Kamoshida: A student with a criminal record, and the culprit of an assault case. At this rate, it’d be pointless how much I contribute to the school.

text.Principal: Now, don’t be like that ...  This school counts on you, Kamoshida-kun. You are our star. Still, a steady build-up is necessary behind such brilliance as well.

text.Suguru Kamoshida: ...Your troubles never seem to end, do they, Principal Kobayakawa? All right, I understand. I’ll continue to do my best to answer your expectations of me.

text.Joker: I should meet him on the rooftop...

text.ACTION: But first, let’s go talk to some more people.

text.Newspaper Club Member: Wah! What!? You’re talking about the one at the center of all the rumors online? Alcohol, smoking, theft, violence ...  The teacher would never approve of such an article.

text.Timid Female Student: Everyone’s afraid of him ...  I hope he gets expelled soon...

text.Carefree Female Student: Our school’s seriously full of troublemakers. Didn’t something like this happen last year too?

text.Timid Female Student: (sigh) And we’re supposed to be an elite college prep school. I wish they’d fix this problem.

text.ACTION: Okay, so Shujin’s “an elite college prep school,” which I suppose explains why the uniform is so snazzy. It makes it slightly less plausible that they’d accept Maaku in the first place, though, but hey, without it there’s no game.

text.Motivated First-Year: Maybe he called someone up there so he can punch them.

text.Energetic First-Year: Oh, do you mean like what happened at track practice last year? I heard it was a big fight...

text.Motivated First-Year: Stay away from him! We only just started high school ...  I’m too young to die!

text.ACTION: From what we’ve gathered so far, Ryuji quit track and field, most likely due to whatever altercation occurred at practice last year. Wonder what’s going on with that.

text.Scary-looking Student: Then again, I’m sure you two losers get along because the both of you are nothing but garbage. Get it? You’ve already gotten on Kamoshida’s bad side. That means the whole school’s against you!

text.ACTION: This place is intense. While I’m goofing around, I should mention that “Shujin” is a homophone for the Japanese word for “prisoner,” which just seems hilariously on-the-nose for the name of a school.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Sorry for callin’ you up here like this. I bet Kawakami already told you stuff like "don’t get involved with him," huh?
Heh, we’re pretty much in the same boat. I heard you got a criminal record. Everyone’s talkin’ about it. No wonder you were so gutsy.
It wasn’t a dream ...  right? You remember it too, yeah?
Well, just ‘cause we both remember it doesn’t mean much though ...  I mean, even if it was a dream, you saved me from Kamoshida. So yeah ...  Thanks, Maaku.
But man, that Kamoshida we saw there ...  You prolly don’t know about it, but there are some rumors about him.

Yeah, the ripped mophead. That asshole who was all full of himself at the castle. No one says anything against him cause he’s some medalist who took the volleyball team to nationals. The way Kamoshida was king of that castle felt crazy real ‘cause of that ...  ...I wonder if we can go back to that castle again...
Sorry to drag you out here like this. That’s all I had to say. You know, we might be pretty similar. I feel like we’re gonna get along just fine as "troublemakers."
I’ll come talk if I see you around. Don’t ignore me, all right? Seeya.

text.Joker: I guess I’ll just head home for today...

text.ACTION: Nothing to do but head home and face the wrath of Sojiro. Yikes.

text.Sojiro Sakura: It’s only your first day and you’re already showing up hours late?
And here I thought you got up and left on time this morning. Look, just behave yourself. Your life’s forfeit if anything happens. You understand the meaning of probation, right?
OK then.

text.ACTION: I expected way worse than that. Sojiro’s a pretty chill guy.

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...Yeah, I just closed up shop. I’ll be there in half an hour.
...No, I just hired a part-timer.
...Yup, I’m leaving now. I told you, he’s a part-timer.

text.ACTION: Antonio Banderas, thou art I. As you saw, Morgana already has a Persona, Zorro.

“Zorro (Spanish for "fox") is the secret identity of Don Diego de la Vega, a fictional character created in 1919 by pulp writer Johnston McCulley. He is a Californio nobleman living in Los Angeles during the era of Mexican rule (between 1821 and 1846), although some movie adaptations of Zorro's story have placed him during the earlier Spanish rule.

The character has undergone changes through the years, but the typical image of him is a dashing black-clad masked outlaw who defends the commoners and indigenous peoples of the land against tyrannical officials and other villains. Not only is he too cunning and foxlike for the bumbling authorities to catch, but he also delights in publicly humiliating them. . . . His favored weapon is a rapier, which he often uses to leave his distinctive mark, a Z cut with three quick strokes.”

Morgana is relatively useful throughout the game for a few abilities he gets. He’s the party’s best all-around healer, being the only one to learn every HP restore spell, and does great damage with his wind attacks. He learns some incredibly useful physical strikes as well all of which combine to earn him a spot in the starting lineup for a good long while.

Part 6: 4/12: Wilson Would Be Ashamed
	Part 6: 4/12: Wilson Would Be Ashamed

text.Joker: I feel exhausted. Maybe it’s because of all the weird stuff that’s been happening to me...

text.ACTION: Maaku wakes up in the Velvet Room once more.

text.Caroline: On your feet, Inmate!

text.Justine: Our master wishes to speak with you. It’s for your own sake that you take his words to heart.

text.Igor: First off, let us celebrate our reunion. Oh ... ? You’ve awakened to your powers. And special ones at that. Your rehabilitation can finally begin.

There is no need to understand it all for the time being. You will be training the power of Persona, which you have awakened to. Personas are, in other words, a "mask"--an armor of the heart when confronting worldly matters. I have high expectations for you.
There is no need to worry. You will learn when the time comes. By the by ...  have you come to appreciate the Metaverse Navigator? Using it will allow you to come and go between reality and Palaces.
...I bestowed it to you as a means to train you as a thief.

text.Caroline: The Metaverse Navigator is a gift from our master! You better take care in using it, Inmate!

text.Justine: Devote yourself to your training so that you may become a fine thief.

text.Igor: It must be disheartening to make use of the Metaverse Navigator alone. Should there be others who would prove beneficial to you, I will grant it to them as well. This is all for you to grow as a most excellent thief...

text.Caroline: Hmph, it’s time. Go back and enjoy whatever rest you might have...

text.Joker: Fate ...  and awakening ... ? More importantly ...  I need to hurry and get ready for school...

text.Mellow Student: Didn’t you hear? The guy totally lost it. It’s been happening a lot lately.

text.Light-Hearted Student: All these accidents are because people are suddenly losing their minds, right?

text.Mellow Student: Well, between the economy sucking and how depressing the news always is, it’s not that surprising.

text.ACTION: On the path to school, we get another opportunity to eavesdrop.

text.Awful friend of Melancholic student: I am not looking forward to that. Why’d I have to be on the same team as Takamaki? She’s only a magazine model because of her stupid ridiculous body. Being near her disgusts me.

text.Melancholic Female Student: Yeah, but we can’t just ignore her, either, because of what happened with Mr. Kamoshida.

text.Awful friend of Melancholic student: Dealing with her is such a hassle. I wish she’d just not come to school.

text.ACTION: Seems like the other students have something against Takamaki.

text.Ushimaru: Hmph ...  You all look like you’ve been spoiled growing up. Before we learn society’s rules, maybe I should start with the rules of being a decent human being. Hey, new kid.
The Greek philosopher Plato divided the human soul into three parts. A soul is composed of appetite, spirit, and what else?
Correct. So you knew that, huh? Plato’s teacher, Socrates, said that evil is born from ignorance. People who’ve been babied, taught that evil is due to individuality, can only become society’s scum.

text.Prim Female Student: He seems like a punk, but maybe he’s actually serious about studying?

text.Joker: I feel like I got a little smarter from being able to answer that question...

text.ACTION: This right here is our social stats screen. The five stats in this game are Knowledge, Charm, Kindness, Proficiency, and Guts. These aren’t terribly relevant yet, but in the future these are going to be the bane of my fucking existence. They still don’t show you how close you are to the next rank, too, which is really frustrating.

From that we got Knowledge +1. I’m not sure if different activities have different outputs in regards to what’s displayed, but I am fairly certain that the five stats have wildly different thresholds in regards to how much is needed to rank up. Knowledge takes forever, for example, while Proficiency can be done far more quickly.

text.Ushimaru: Bizarre incidents have been occurring frequently. Those are but the actions of such scum. We don’t need crude people like that in this school. Understand?

text.Suguru Kamoshida: You looking for a ride home? Things have been pretty dangerous lately with all those accidents.

text.Ann Takamaki: Sorry, I have a photoshoot today. It’s for the special summer issue, so I can’t afford to miss it...

text.Suguru Kamoshida: Hey, now ...  Being a model’s fine and dandy, but don’t work your pretty little self to the bone. You mentioned you weren’t feeling well, right? Something about appendicitis?

text.Ann Takamaki: Yes, I keep planning to go to the hospital, but I’ve been too busy ...  Sorry to worry you.

text.Suguru Kamoshida: You must be lonely too. I feel bad for keeping your best friend at practice so often. That’s why I asked you out in the first place. Oh, and ...  be careful around that transfer student. He’s got a criminal record, after all. If something were to happen to you...

text.Ann Takamaki: ...Thank you. Please excuse me.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I wanna talk about that castle from yesterday. I tried tellin’ myself it was all just a dream ...  but I couldn’t do it. I can’t act like nothing happened. It’s all connected to that bastard Kamoshida, after all. I wanna find out what’s up with that place, no matter what. And y’know, you’re the only person I can rely on for this stuff. So, you in?

Ooh ...  Looks like I managed to talk some sense into you. I think we should just try and retrace our steps from yesterday. In the meantime, you’re walkin’ to the station, right? Let’s go together. Lemme know if you notice any other weird buildings on the way.

text.Joker: Ryuji doesn’t seem like a bad guy. I should probably just go along with this...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: When’d they build something like that though? We walked that way from here, right?
When you put it that way, I’m not so sure anymore ...  ...All right, this way. Lemme know if you notice something.
We’re at school ...  There wasn’t anything out of place along the way, right? I didn’t see no castle either ...  ...We must’ve made a wrong turn somewhere. Let’s try again.
C’mon, you gotta stick with me to the end. Let’s go.
Is it smaller than we think it is? What do you think?
I already did that. I didn’t see anything like it around here ...  Huh? Phone ...  Hey, that reminds me—didn’t you have a navigation app thingy on, back then?

I dunno if it was or not, but I heard stuff that sounded like one comin’ from your phone. Y’know, didn’t it say stuff like "returned to the real world" or something like that? Lemme see your phone for a bit.
What’s this eyeball-lookin’ thing?
Wait, what? What a weird app ...  ...Oh wait, this is it!
Oh man, I’m such a genius! Let’s try usin’ it.
Why? All we’re doin’ is startin’ an app.

text.Nav: Kamoshida ...  Shujin Academy ...  Pervert ...  Castle ...  Beginning navigation.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: There we go! ...Then, we went in a certain direction, and--
...Huh? What the hell!?
...Yeargh! Those clothes...!
That happened last time too, huh!? What’s with that outfit!?
You LIKE it!? What’s goin’ on here!? This makes no effin’ sense at all...

text.Morgana: Stop making a commotion.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ah ...  You!?

text.Morgana: The Shadows started acting up, so I came here wondering what it could be ...  ...To think you guys would come back to the entrance when you barely managed to escape.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What is this place? ...Is it the school?

text.Morgana: That’s right.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But it’s a castle!

text.Morgana: This castle IS the school. ...But only to this castle’s ruler.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: The castle’s ruler ... ?

text.Morgana: I think you called him Kamoshida? It’s how his distorted heart views the school.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Kamoshida ...  Distorted ... ? Explain it in a way that makes sense!

text.ACTION: These games always need one party member who needs everything explained thoroughly to them just in case the player’s even denser than they are.

text.Morgana: I shouldn’t have expected a moron to get it...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’d you say!?
What was that!?

text.Morgana: It must be the slaves captive here.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real!?
Oh, shit ...  It’s for real! We saw other guys held captive here yesterday ...  I’m pretty sure they’re from our school.

text.Morgana: Most likely on Kamoshida’s orders. It’s nothing out of the ordinary; It’s like that every day here. What’s more, you two escaped yesterday. He must have lost his temper quite a bit.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That son of a bitch ... !

text.Morgana: Ryuji ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...This is bullshit!
You hear me, Kamoshida!?

text.Morgana: Doing that isn’t going to open it, you know ...  Still, it seems you have your reasons.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, Monamona!
Do you know where those voices are comin’ from?

text.Morgana: You want me to take you to them? ...Well, I guess I could guide you there. But only if he comes with us.
I just want to get a better look at your powers. Even if you don’t agree, I bet this guy’ll go on even if he has to do it alone. Are you gonna leave him?
It’s settled then!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real ... !? ...Thanks, man.

text.Morgana: All right, let’s do this. Follow me!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ain’t that where we escaped outta last time ... ?

text.Morgana: That’s right. Not barging in through the entrance is one of the basics of phantom thievery.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: How’re we supposed to know about that stuff ... ?

text.Morgana: I’ll make sure to teach you as we go. Come on, follow me!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So, uh ...  sorry for draggin’ you into all of this ...  But I can’t just forgive that bastard Kamoshida doin’ whatever the hell he wants! Really though, thanks for comin’ along. I owe you big time!

text.ACTION: Music- King, Queen, and Slaves (Another Version)

text.Morgana: Mm-hm. Now, make sure you do exactly as I say, all right? ...Follow me!

text.ACTION: The room changes appearance suddenly, then changes back.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I was seein’ double or something just now ... ! Was that Shujin!?

text.Morgana: I’ve told you before. This place is your school. Regardless, we don’t have the time to stand around. Who knows when a shadow might show up. Come on, this way!
It looks like we won’t be able to avoid conflict from this point forward.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: F-For real ... ?

text.Morgana: Oh well. I’ll just teach you the basics of battle right now. You had better remember all of this. As a rule of thumb, try to ambush as many enemies as you can. Attack them from behind whenever possible. You’ll need to rip off their masks to momentarily break the control the Palace ruler has over them. If you succeed, the enemy will be caught off guard, allowing us to jump in for a preemptive attack.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So we wanna ambush ‘em and go for the first strike ...  All right, I got it!

text.Morgana: Uh, you know you’re just going to be watching, right? You can’t use a Persona ...  Anyway, let’s go!

text.ACTION: Sneak up behind, tear off the mask…
...and get to act first in battle.

However, ambushing can really mess you up sometimes if you’re not careful, because the enemy gets two actions after your party acts: Once guaranteed after the full party goes, and then again after the order resets and it gets its usual action. If it’s a strong enemy it might get to act twice in a row, and if it’s hitting weaknesses it can be even more than that. It’s a bad scene all around. I’m not saying don’t ambush, but know what you’re getting into if you can’t kill the enemy in one turn.
Music- Last Surprise (Probably listen to this)

Also worth noting is that we get our first taste of the battle theme here, Last Surprise. You can listen to it now, but for the true experience of reading this update just play the first ten seconds, stop, then repeat 3 times or so, because you’re not gonna hear any more of it than that fighting these enemies.

text.Morgana: Quiet down!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh yeah, there were more of ‘em further in too ... !

text.Morgana: They might have been transferred already...
It would be a problem if they discovered us now ...  Hey, let’s head into that room. We should be able to hide in there until they leave.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: (gasp) (pant) How can you tell?

text.Morgana: There’s a lack of distortion here, meaning the ruler’s control over this area is weak.
Now do you understand? This place is another reality that the ruler’s heart projects.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This is Kamoshida’s reality ... ? Shit makes no sense at all!

text.Morgana: One could say it’s a world in which one’s distorted desires have materialized. I call such a place a "Palace."

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: A Palace ... ?

text.Morgana: This is happening because he thinks the school is his own castle.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So, it became like this ‘cause he just thought of it like that!? Hahaha ...  That son of a bitch!

text.Morgana: You must really hate this Kamoshida guy.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hate doesn’t even cover how I feel. Everything is that asshole’s fault!

text.Morgana: I don’t know what happened between you two, but don’t let your emotions get the better of you. His lackeys are everywhere inside.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, I’m curious as hell about it too.

text.Morgana: That’s also because of this world.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: More stuff that makes no sense...

text.Morgana: Anything distorts according to how a ruler pleases within his Palace. A school can turn into a castle like this, after all. In order to prevent such distortions, one must hold a powerful will of rebellion. Your appearance is a manifestation of that. It’s the image of rebellion that you hold within.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uuugh, I’m so fed up with all this! I’m more curious about you than his clothes! What the hell are you anyways!?

text.Morgana: This is, well ...  It’s because I lost my true form. ...I think.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You think?

text.Morgana: But I do know how to regain my true form. The reason why I snuck in here was for a preliminary investigation of those means. Well, I ended up getting caught though ...  Besides, I’ve been tortured by Kamoshida too! I’m gonna make him pay for sure!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What is this, a comic book? This is seriously crazy...

text.Morgana: If we’re gonna keep going, we should hurry along. I’ll be counting on your skills this time too, rookie. Got it?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Don’t worry, I’m not gonna force it all on you. I thought it might help, so...

text.ACTION: Ryuji, did you bring a gun to school?

text.Morgana: That’s a toy!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But it looks totally real, so it’ll at least fake ‘em out. I brought some medicine too. You know what they say: "Providin’ is pre...something." Huh? Huh?

text.Morgana: So you were planning this from the start ...  Well, fine. If you’re ready to go, we’ll resume our infiltration.

text.ACTION: And so we obtain the sacred power of GUN.

text.Morgana: Let’s use this time to sort through our current situation.

text.ACTION: Safe rooms are a new concept to the series. They let you warp between them, leave the Palace, save, check your progress, serve as checkpoints when you die, and even let you use special healing items within them.

text.Shadow: They’re all in the training hall. I’d assume they’re screaming in pain by now.

text.Armored Soldier: Very well. By the way, I heard we may have intruders around. Stay on your guard.

text.Morgana: Did you hear that?
I think that’s just a little further ahead. Let’s go!
The way to the training hall should be just past those bars...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So ...  what’re we gonna do? Do we gotta fight it?

text.Morgana: Seems so. Just don’t let it notice you beforehand ...  If it does, the Palace’s security level will rise.

text.ACTION: Being forced to leave the palace at 100% is dire indeed. We’ll have to take care not to get caught too many times.
Being at 0% is awesome because you can just ambush from wherever you want. It’s great. You can be smack dab in front of their face and as long as they haven’t “noticed” you you’re golden.

text.Morgana: Yeah, it’s a little further. Make sure you watch out for any guards along the way.
Shoot ...  I had a feeling there would be a lot of enemies. It’d be impossible to dodge all of them...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then, what do we do? Should we try and take ‘em down like before?

text.Morgana: It’s not that simple. We still have a long way to go, so we should be conserving energy.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I-I see ...  Sorry ...  Dammit, I wish I could fight ...  I’d at least be able to help out a little bit ...  But all I got is this toy from earlier ...  I’m such a loser.

text.Morgana: Huh? Do you mean that gun?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah ...  It looks real n’ all, but it doesn’t shoot anything...

text.Morgana: I see ...  Well, there is a way ...  Okay, we’ll use that to take down the enemies!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What!? Were you listenin’ to me? It don’t even shoot pellets...

text.Morgana: Don’t worry, I’m sure this’ll work. Attack away, Frizzy Hair!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, dude! I keep sayin’, it’s not gonna fire anything!

text.Morgana: You have the gun with you, right? Point it at a Shadow and fire!

text.ACTION: Guns are a good source of knockdowns against enemies weak to it. A lot of winged enemies are weak to Gun, for the record. There’s a price, however...

text.Morgana: How about that? Surprised? Be mindful of how much ammo you have left!

text.ACTION: Limited ammo. There are ways to restore ammo but they’re not very good. While it’s technically true that dumping an entire clip into an enemy will generally do more damage than a physical attack, there’s no reason to, especially because ammo is so limited and you’re generally not going to be upgrading your gun for better damage very often. It’s pretty much never worth it. Of course, weapon types vary across party members, and have different ammo counts and do different amounts of damage.
Morgana for instance, has a Bart Simpson-esque slingshot...
...that he wastefully tears through ammunition with.

text.Morgana: This is a cognitive world. As long as our opponent sees it as real, it becomes such. It’s a good thing it’s realistic-looking.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...I don’t get it.

text.Morgana: I wasn’t expecting someone with your brains to understand. How about you, Frizzy Hair? Did you get what I said?

text.ACTION: I feel kind of bad for Ryuji, constantly getting shit on by this fucking cat.

text.Morgana: Maybe I was expecting too much...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, if it’s better havin’ something realistic, why do you got that slingshot!? And it was just as strong as a goddamn gun! What about your whole cognitive whatever!?

text.Morgana: W-Well, um ...  (sigh) Fine, you can choose to understand it however you want. Oh, by the way, we should decide how we divvy up our roles in battle from here on out.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: He totally dodged my question...

text.Morgana: As you can see, there are quite a lot of enemies. It’ll be important to coordinate our moves well. I can keep providing intel for us, but you should decide how we fight, Frizzy Hair.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whaddya mean by "how we fight"?

text.Morgana: Basically, what we do in battle. He can order us directly, or let us decide what we do. ...Though I guess I’m the only other one fighting right now...

text.ACTION: So, we can set Morgana to take orders from us from now on, which the game helpfully does for us.
We can also automatically use skills that will hit the enemy’s weakness, if we know it.
Finally, to speed up trash fights, we can use Rush, which will quickly make every party member auto-melee.
