text.Ann Takamaki: And I’ll try to dig up some dirt online.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We went and formed the Phantom Thieves group, but we can’t even find a target ...

text.Ann Takamaki: There, there...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I guess sometimes things just don’t go the way we want ‘em to ...

text.ACTION: We’ve been looking for exactly one day, you guys. Relax.

text.Principal: You saw the state Kamoshida-kun was in, didn’t you? It’s as if his personality has completely changed. Something is definitely wrong here.

text.Makoto Niijima: I’m not sure I follow...

text.Principal: From what I’ve heard, it appears as though some students were meddling in his business. If they did something to him ...  Who could they be ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: Are you saying that these students may have caused Mr. Kamoshida to change ... ?

text.Principal: That is what I wish to know ...  Even if it takes some probing into student matters ...  I would like you to look into this for me.

text.Makoto Niijima: It is true that there are many rumors regarding Mr. Kamoshida, but ...  Do you mean all of this talk about those Phantom Thieves?

text.Principal: It is undeniable that Mr. Kamoshida has "changed" in some way. I’d like to have a grasp of the cause. This shall also ensure that I handle the mass media and police in the correct fashion.

text.Makoto Niijima: Oh ...

text.Principal: I will continue speaking to Mr. Kamoshida myself. Unless you find whomever did this, these irresponsible rumors will likely never die down. Don’t you agree? You have been at the top of your class since day one. Your conduct is good, and teachers favor you.

text.Makoto Niijima: Th-Thank you ...

text.Principal: Your lineage must certainly play a part in this excellence. Your sister is still young, yet she holds an admirable position at the Public Prosecutors Office, no ... ?
If something disappointing were to happen here, that wouldn’t reflect very well on your sister ...  ...Do you understand?
How wise. It’s no wonder you’re our student council president. I’d appreciate if you looked into this as soon as possible. I ask that you begin at once.

text.Makoto Niijima: Yes. If you’ll excuse me then.

text.Principal: It’s me, sir. My apologies for troubling you at such a busy time ...  Yes, it’s about the matter we discussed earlier ...  I have all bases covered. The investigation will begin immediately ...  Of course ...  Yes, I will get results ...  I should be able to update you soon ...  Well then, I must be going. Thank you very much for your time ...

text.Ann Takamaki: I saw them too! They were talking to the teachers!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That change of heart thing’s seriously amazing, huh!?

text.Ann Takamaki: Still ...

...You guys are the Phantom Thieves, aren’t you?

text.ACTION: This guy really needs to take a hint.

They can’t let this end after just one target. That’s why I wanted to make a forum where people could post their problems. There are probably a lot of people who have high hopes for the Phantom Thieves’ next move. So I’ve also implemented an anonymous poll on the site.
I ...  hope someday my forum is filled with supportful posts. I’d really like to help out in the Phantom Thieves’ acts of justice! ...Can I, please?

Also, how do you not know who Mishima is? If we’ve gained any sort of notoriety, and judging from this framing device we have, surely you’ve already looked into the Phan-site? You know that you can just run a fucking whois on that, right? Unless Mishima’s hiding behind eight proxies, scrub.
Oh shit, it’s what P3 and P4 were sorely missing, the ability to have backup party members gain experience! Spoiler, I guess: we gain more party members. It’s not 1:1, but it’s still great.
The Moon Arcana represents illusion, fear, and insecurity, as well as confusion and unhappiness. It’s a card of mystery and the subconscious.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Geez ...  It was a little awkward tryin’ to figure out when to walk over here.

text.Ann Takamaki: So that forum is Mishima-kun’s ...

text.Morgana: Has he figured out our identities?

text.Ann Takamaki: Even so, I think it’ll be fine. He seemed to be playing it cool.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I guess we should have a little chat about this later.

text.Morgana: I will say though ...  a forum where people can post problems may prove unexpectedly useful.

text.Ann Takamaki: And we need to stay sharp until we manage to find one. Once we do, we’ll have to head into another Palace, so we should prep our equipment and--

Anyway, we find someone else worth talking to over in the Practice Building...

text.Joker: Hang out with her

text.Ann Takamaki: ...It’s Shiho. Well ...  I went to visit her in the hospital. She ...  She said she was sorry. Sorry for not telling me about Kamoshida ...  about all the things he was doing to her ...  But it was my fault too. I didn’t realize how much trouble she was in ...  I wasn’t there for her ...  So, I apologized as well.

I’m glad I finally got to tell her everything I couldn’t bring myself to say before. And, um ...  remember how Kamoshida threatened to take Shiho off the team if I didn’t sleep with him? I had only agreed to it so that I wouldn’t ruin Shiho’s dreams ...  But now that I think about it, he never would have put her on the bench and cost his team games ...  I seriously should have dared him to try and take her starting spot. ...But in the end, maybe I just didn’t believe in her ability.

text.ACTION: You actually get more points if you agree with her here, but to hell with that, I’m here to try to make her feel better, not indulge her bullshit self-loathing.

text.Ann Takamaki: But ...  it all happened because I was weak. That’s why I believed Kamoshida’s authority outweighed Shiho’s own ability to earn her starting spot. Maaku, do you remember the last time I talked to you like this? When I got that phone call from Kamoshida ...  and cried. I felt so alone ...  scared, even ...  But because you were there for me, I decided not to go. I was a little surprised at how pushy you were about it ...  but I see now you just wanted to help. ...Thanks.

Back then, people used to call me all sorts of names ...  "Prissy bitch," "Kamoshida’s girl" ...  I got tired of it pretty quickly. But to tell you the truth, someday I want to be able to take labels like that in stride. Hey, um ...  Personas are the power of the heart, right? That means if my heart gets stronger, my Persona will too. So ...  I want to strengthen my heart. And I want to use that strength to help the people around me. I hope we can save people from trouble, just like we did when we changed Kamoshida’s heart. Though honestly ...  I don’t even know what "strong" is. But I’m going to find the answer, I promise.
(giggle) I guess that doesn’t really count though, huh? Well ...  I’ll be relying on you. Let’s train together and make our hearts super strong!

text.Joker: I sense a heightened motivation from Ann...

I mean, they’re free, so not getting any would mean you have a strong heart!
...Is that not right? Well, I’ll see you later.

text.Morgana: You got the job! Nice going!

text.ACTION: Instead of heading to that job, we’re just going to accept the other available job, because that’s the one we’re actually here for.

text.Morgana: Ooh, a part-time job at the beef bowl shop, huh? Seems tough, but you might improve your Proficiency. What do you wanna do? Gonna apply?

text.Joker: Apply

text.Morgana: Yeah, we can go to Shibuya at night now! Let’s call them right now!

text.Manager: Hello. This is Ore no Beko on Central Street. How many people are you ordering for? Oh, you’re calling about the job opening. This is great timing. We’re in need of some extra hands. I’d take just about anyone at this point. You don’t mind working at night, do you? Stop by any time you’re free to work. I’ll be waiting! We’re right by the entrance to Central Street. Hope to see you soon.

text.Morgana: That settles it. You’d better work hard, OK?

text.ACTION: Let’s head over to Central Street, then.

text.Transient Man: The world the way it is, a lotta people been finding themselves roofless. I had a life once, you know. I was an art student. Yeah, I was cool and everything.

text.Foreign Barker: Hey, man! Thanks for giving me the time of day. Everyone avoids me because my Japanese is pretty rough. I’m just trying to promote this bar, y’know? You’re just a kid, though. I can’t let you in. Sorry, man.

text.ACTION: Based on this interaction, I assume that in Japanese he’s speaking rudely or informally by accident, but if so it simply didn’t translate at all, which makes the other options hilariously dickish for no reason.
Time to head to Untouchable to hand over that bag.

text.Munehisa Iwai: Are you gonna try and sell me somethin’ weird again?

text.Morgana: That modified model gun should be a powerful weapon to use during Palace battles. Let’s ask him about what was inside the bag! ...Don’t freak out, Maaku! Just ask him!
...Should we not?

text.Munehisa Iwai: Hey, you gonna buy somethin’?

text.ACTION: Sorry, no. For reference, Dauntless is Rank 4 Guts. We’re still at Rank 2, meaning we’re going to be holding on to that bag for the next several months, and every time we come in here it’s going to notify us that we’re too chickenshit to talk to him about it.
It’s a shitty situation all around.

text.Morgana: Time for work? All right, work hard and make that money.

text.Manager: No need to introduce yourself. I actually need you to start working right away. Do you have any questions about the job?

Not quite. Our budget’s been cut despite being short-staffed ...  so you’ll have to do everything alone. You’re a spry young dude, right? You’ll be fine. I’ll pay you more to make up for the extra work! Anything else?

Take customers’ orders, prep them, serve them, ring them up, and then clean the store. The meals are all ready-made, so it should be simple. Just make sure you’re nice to the customers, OK? OK, I need to head out for a bit! Keep an eye on the shop until I get back.

text.ACTION: Oh jeez, I’m alone on my first day.

text.Morgana: Oh, well. Just give it your best shot, I guess. I’ll be cheering you on.
Hey, someone wants to change their order. Add an egg? They should have told us earlier.

text.Manager: This is your pay today. Thank you. Well, I hope you can keep it up.

text.Morgana: But you still managed all those orders by yourself. If you ask me, you were pretty proficient.
Come on, let’s leave.

text.Train Monitor: "Volleyball Beating Investigation!" The school claims to have left teaching methods up to its staff. It has denied once again that it had any knowledge of the beatings. "Pollen Warning as of Next Week!" Greater volume and arriving later than in previous years. "Hotspots of Tokyo!" Experience art in Shibuya! The Madarame exhibit opens next week.

text.Morgana: People are really talking about the Kamoshida incident. No one in this car knows that we’re the ones who did it...

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Anyway, today we’ll be talking about "The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter." Most theorize it’s the oldest story in Japan; for some, it’s the oldest science-fiction story in the world. But if you ask me, it’s the oldest story in Japan about a terrible woman. I mean, Princess Kaguya gives her suitors absurd tasks, demands fancy gifts, then runs off to the moon. Some men lose their fortunes, some are humiliated, and some even get serious wounds or go blind. Women like Princess Kaguya actually show up in a lot of stories from around the world. Now then, Hamiru-kun. What do people generally call a woman who has a charm that sometimes leads men to their doom?

text.ACTION: Really tempted to pick “Elizabeth” there, but alas.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: That’s right. The answer is femme fatale. Literally translated, it means "fatal woman." Some famous examples are the witch Morgan le Fay from Arthurian legen and Queen Salome from the Bible. Not to mention the wild, seductive dancer of opera, Carmen.
...Let me just warn you that exams aren’t so easy that you can pass them with a single night of cramming. Take your time and make sure you understand the material, OK?

text.Morgana: ...You heard her. Must be rough being a student. Well, you have nothing to lose from studying. Give it all you got.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: There ain’t even a hint of a hint about a new Palace...

text.Ann Takamaki: We can’t get everything online ...  Finding a post with a name and location is asking a lot ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Guess we just gotta find one ourselves then!

text.Morgana: Are you seriously suggesting we look for a target that even the police have overlooked?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...Yeah, you’re right. We should prolly just hold off ‘til exams are done with, huh? We can wait and see for a little longer, then worry about comin’ up emptyhanded if it happens ...

text.ACTION: Morgana jumps out of sight via Ryuji’s head.

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...We’ll get outta here once we’re done chattin’. Anyways, what’s Miss Council President want with us?

text.Makoto Niijima: The troublemaker, the girl of rumor, and the infamous transfer student ...  Interesting combination.

text.Ann Takamaki: Great way to start a conversation...

text.Makoto Niijima: By the way ...  It seems as though you got to know Mr. Kamoshida pretty well.
Are you playing dumb with me?

text.Ann Takamaki: It just goes to show how little interaction he had with him.

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm ...  I heard Mr. Kamoshida used a volleyball team member to spread details of your past record. Don’t you hate him? Mr. Kamoshida, I mean.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’s all this about? My friend here’s an upstanding guy.

text.Makoto Niijima: I don’t mean to offend. Many students have been shaken up by what happened with Mr. Kamoshida. The rumors about that odd, calling card-esque posting aren’t going away either.

text.Ann Takamaki: I didn’t expect someone like you would care about tactless stuff, Niijima-senpai.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Anyways, we done here? We can’t leave if you keep talkin’ to us.

text.Makoto Niijima: At least try to understand my position. Being forced to deal with this horseplay...

text.Ann Takamaki: Horseplay ... !?

text.Makoto Niijima: Ah yes, by the way ...  It’s been decided that this place will be closed off due to the incident. I heard some people are coming up here without permission, after all.

text.Ann Takamaki: What was that about?

text.ACTION: She figured us out! Damn, if only it weren’t completely obvious to anyone with half a brain!

text.Morgana: That girl seems rather sharp. We should be cautious of her.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: She really pisses me off!
Talk about a pain in the ass...

text.Morgana: That reminds me ...  Study hard. Especially you, Ryuji. There are bound to be traps that will need to be solved with brains. Keep in mind that everything you do in your daily lives has an impact on your abilities.

text.Ann Takamaki: True, studying won’t be so bad if we just think of it as helping us prepare to be phantom thieves ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I guess you got a point ...  But man, it’s just so lame ...  I was all fired up about helpin’ people, not about studyin’...

text.Morgana: Well, I do have somewhere interesting to show you beforehand. You guys did originally promise to help me out with my mission, after all.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Mission?

text.Morgana: Follow me.
Just do as I told you.
Look for a post with a full name in it.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I already said there’s no info on any big shots. Don’t you remember? But man, people actually go put someone’s real name on here. That’s some scary shit...

text.ACTION: In this game’s world people are doxxing people they know so strangers they have almost no reason to believe exist will brainwash them. What a fucked-up future this is. Also remember that Kamoshida turned himself in like five days ago, which means that these rumors and the Phan-site have spread amazingly quickly even if it seems like no one’s buying them.

text.Ann Takamaki: "He won’t listen to what I say" ...  No wait, there’s no name on this one.

text.Morgana: Ignore those. Aren’t there any posts about more serious trouble?

text.Ann Takamaki: "I don’t know what to do about my ex who’s stalking me. His name is Natsuhiko Nakanohara." It says he’s a teller at City Hall.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: A government worker’s stalkin’ someone ... ?

text.Morgana: That should be a suitable target. All right, now get the Meta-Nav ready.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We’re just gonna jump right into a Palace? Fine by me!

text.Ann Takamaki: Hey, what happened to all that talk of "unanimous decision"? What do you think we should do, Maaku?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That’s what I’m talkin’ about!

text.Ann Takamaki: OK then. Let’s go.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We need a name and a place, right? So the name is...

text.Morgana: Actually, we don’t need a location this time. Just enter exactly what I say. The keyword is ...  "Mementos."

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? What’re you tryin’ to pull?

text.Morgana: Just listen to me. It should work ...  I think.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Geez, that again ... ? Uhhh ...  "M-e-m-e-n-t-o-s," was it?

text.Morgana: Just as I thought!

text.Ann Takamaki: It ...  kind of feels like I’m walking on air ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Is this that Nakanohara guy’s Palace?

text.Morgana: That’s half right, but half wrong. This is a type of Palace, but it’s different from the normal ones. Come on, let’s head down. The Shadows here lurk underground. I don’t quite understand why. It may be because they’re drawn to something.

text.Ann Takamaki: Underground? How are we going to get there?

text.Morgana: How? You use it every day on your way to school. Follow me!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, our clothes changed!?

text.Ann Takamaki: The Shadows know we’re here!?

text.Morgana: Since the moment we stepped in.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You should’ve told us!

text.Morgana: We’re still safe right here. I’ve come to investigate a number of times. Shadows never come up to this floor. But it’s a different story once you go down. This place is simply teeming with them.

text.Ann Takamaki: More importantly, what is this Mementos!? It’s about time you start explaining.

text.Morgana: A Palace as grand as the previous castle only forms when a person’s wishes are extremely distorted. So, instead of many individual Palaces, the general public has one gigantic shared Palace. That’s where we are now ...  Mementos.

text.Ann Takamaki: Now that you mention it, this place feels a bit different from Kamoshida’s Palace...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: When you say shared ...  you mean they’re all put together? Even though they’re just strangers ... ?

text.Morgana: Think of it as the collective unconscious ...  No, never mind. You wouldn’t understand that.

text.Ann Takamaki: So what you’re saying is ...  Using this place, we can even change the hearts of people who don’t have a Palace?

text.Morgana: Correct! The steps to do so are slightly different though.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But this place looks pretty huge. Are we gonna be able to get around just by walkin’ ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: A car ... !?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: No way!

text.Morgana: This comes from the way cognition materializes in the Metaverse, plus a bit of extra training. It’s not dissimilar to how you guys transform.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You turnin’ into a car is totally different than our clothes changin’!

text.ACTION: this is a really good joke

text.Ann Takamaki: Why a bus though?

text.Morgana: ...No idea.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, why didn’t you do this at the castle!?

text.Morgana: I would have if I could!

text.ACTION: Ryuji attempts to… board… Morgana. What the hell.
Ann notices and chases after him.

text.Ann Takamaki: Hey, Skull! Ladies first!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Stop pullin’ me! That’s dangerous!

text.Morgana: Panther! Please be gentle!

text.ACTION: I should mention that any time Morgana emotes in this form he does so by jumping up on his back tires, it’s incredible.

text.Morgana: I’m not going anywhere unless someone drives me.

text.Ann Takamaki: THAT’S what you’re worried about?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Eh, who cares. We’re drivin’ a cat car through the Metaverse.

text.Ann Takamaki: All right then, we’ll leave the driving to you!

text.Morgana: Oh, there ...  That feels sooo goooooood ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uh, is that purrin’ I hear ... ? What a creepy-ass car!

text.Morgana: Don’t underestimate my meowtary engine.
We’re going full throttle! It’s time to fly!

text.ACTION:
Part 25: 5/7-5/8: All Aboard The Cat Bus
	Part 24: 5/7-5/8: All Aboard The Cat Bus
Loop that track about 40 times. Congratulations, you now have the Mementos Experience. Isn’t it great?

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah, I guess it’d be strange driving on the tracks like this in the real world ...  Anyway, Nakanohara’s somewhere in here, right?

text.Morgana: Most likely in a segment of his own creation. Don’t worry, it won’t be the size of a Palace. Our next step is to find an entrance to that segment.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: And what’s this entrance gonna look like?

text.Morgana: I have no idea, but strong distortions should be a pretty obvious visual clue.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So we just gotta go wanderin’ around for it then? What a goddamn pain in the ass...

text.ACTION: So, our objective now is to ride around the subway tracks looking for a distortion to find Nakanohara.
Over here, we see a roaming Shadow.
Our strategy- ram the fuck into it.
These Slimes make up most of the encounters on this floor, and have a nasty tendency to blow themselves up. Thankfully, they’re weak to Wind and Fire.
We also get a chance to see Ryuji’s follow-up attack down here.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, the hell is this ... ? It’s all wavy and shit.

text.Morgana: This is the place ...  I sense the target up ahead. Now, are you ready, Joker?
That seems to be Nakanohara’s Shadow.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Lemme see. Some front desk guy at City Hall became a stalker, right?

text.Ann Takamaki: I don’t know how much evil he’s done, but we have to do something if he’s bothering other people.

text.Morgana: All right, we’ll go talk to him.

text.Ann Takamaki: Are you that stalker!? Haven’t you ever stopped to consider how your ex feels?

text.Shadow Natsuhiko Nakanohara: She’s my property! I can do whatever I want with her! It’s not like she didn’t treat me like a plaything! What’s wrong with me doing the same!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You can’t treat someone like shit just ‘cause they did it to you! What a load of crap...

text.Shadow Natsuhiko Nakanohara: There are millions of people far worse than me! What about Madarame ... ? He stole everything from me, but you’re letting him off the hook!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...Madarame? The hell’s this guy goin’ on about?

text.Shadow Natsuhiko Nakanohara: Look ...  This is a winner-takes-all world. Come fight me and I’ll show you what I mean!

text.ACTION: Shadow Nakanohara starts by increasing his Attack. This could be a problem, but...

Skull Cracker immediately inflicts Confusion, forcing it to spend its turns doing nothing, throwing items away, or throwing money away. Those last two are great for us because we get the spoils, but it also means this thing doesn’t get a single turn to attack before we kill it, which is why I didn’t even bother posting a video of the fight like I usually do. A lot of Mementos minibosses are susceptible to ailments, which can trivialize them.
Everyone leveled up and gained new skills from this fight, too.
Ryuji learns Headbutt, which is Medium Physical with a medium chance of Forget.
Morgana learns Media, which is a light heal to the entire party.
Finally, Ann learns Tarunda, which is single-target Attack down. It’s pretty handy.

text.Shadow Natsuhiko Nakanohara: That evil teacher used me, then threw me out on the street. That’s what caused my fixation on her...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Could it be that Madarame guy he was talkin’ about earlier?

text.Shadow Natsuhiko Nakanohara: Yeah ...  I just didn’t want anyone to throw me out again ...

text.Ann Takamaki: So some selfish bastard was making you suffer too ...  Still, you shouldn’t have dragged an unrelated woman into your mess.

text.Shadow Natsuhiko Nakanohara: Yes, I know that now. I’ll put an end to my love for her ...  ...Hey you can change people’s hearts, right? In that case ...  Won’t you change Madarame’s heart!? Before more people fall victim to him...

text.Ann Takamaki: Change ...  Madarame’s heart?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hm? What’s that shinin’ thing?

text.Morgana: It’s the bud of a Treasure. Had we left it be, it very well may have blossomed into a Palace. Joker, this will make a perfect reward!
Most likely.

text.Ann Takamaki: But how are we supposed to know if we succeeded?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: The lady posted the dude’s name online. If he really does change, she’ll prolly comment again.

text.Morgana: Hm, you do have a point.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Either way, trainin’ against Shadows down here’s the best! It’s great prep for our next target!

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s also nice to be able to give courage to the people who post their problems online.

text.Morgana: On top of that, we can sell whatever treasure we get for some cold, hard cash!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ... All right, we did it!

text.Morgana: Hold on. There’s somewhere I want to show you guys before we leave.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What, there’s more?

text.Morgana: Don’t worry, it won’t take long.
There’s something I’d like to check in an area further down. That platform we saw earlier should be the way down. Let’s head there first.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, you’ve been here before, right? Don’t you got like a map or something?

text.Morgana: That would hold no meaning in this place. The layout changes every time you enter.

text.Ann Takamaki: Wait, so our path changes too!?

text.Morgana: This place is the fused cognition of a countless number of people. It’s constantly shifting. Even so, our destination should be pretty close. I’m counting on you, Joker.

text.ACTION: Yep, Mementos is randomly generated, just like P3's Tartarus and all of P4's dungeons.
Before we head down, though, let’s check the item we got. This Attachment Pearl nulls Forget.

text.Morgana: Of course they are. We’re in the subway, you know.

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah, but I thought this was a Palace!

text.Morgana: Then maybe this is how the public views this place? I don’t know.

text.Ann Takamaki: People go through this darkness ...  every day ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Forget that! You sure we’re cool runnin’ around on these tracks!?

text.Morgana: It should be fine as long as we’re not on the same ones ...  I think. I’m no train expert.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You’ve gotta be kiddin’ me...

text.Morgana: Anyway, let’s head to the lower area. It should be right after we go down to that escalator.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: And a dead end at that. Why’s it even exist?

text.Morgana: Now hold on ...  Just watch. This is most likely not an ordinary wall. If my hunch is correct...

text.Nav: A new area has been confirmed in the depths. Updating guidance information.

text.Morgana: See!? It’s just as I thought!

text.Ann Takamaki: What do you mean?

text.Morgana: That wall wouldn’t budge when I came here by myself before. But it’d be weird for the deepest part of Mementos to be some normal place like this, wouldn’t it?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So you were thinkin’ there’s gotta be more?

text.Morgana: Yeah! Now that Kamoshida’s Palace is gone and people are actually starting to talk about us ...  I knew something had to have changed down here!

text.Ann Takamaki: How deep is it? Should we try going further down?

text.Morgana: Let’s not. That’s not why we’re here today, remember? We’ve already accomplished our goal. We should head back and I’ll explain more once we’re home.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh, and what was that wall thing we saw at the end?

text.Morgana: I’m not entirely sure, but it blocked us from going in past a certain depth. If Mementos is the public’s Palace though ...  it might be affected by the general public’s belief in us.

text.Ann Takamaki: Why do you know so much about it, Morgana?

text.Morgana: My memories are a little foggy in that regard ...  However, I need to know what lies in the depths of Mementos, no matter what.

text.Ann Takamaki: No matter what ... ?

text.Morgana: Mementos is not just everyone’s Palace, it’s the source of all Palaces. It used to be that Palaces like Kamoshida’s with one ruler simply didn’t exist. So if we can do something about the greatest cause of distortions, I’m certain my appearance will ... !

text.Ann Takamaki: You wanted someone to save you too...

text.Morgana: I-I just needed pawns.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I see ...  So that’s why you came pokin’ your nose around with us.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...I’ll help you. I hope you can regain what you’ve lost.

text.Morgana: I’ll ...  be relying on you guys.

text.Ann Takamaki: By the way Morgana ...  are you a boy? Or might you be a girl?
That is a possibility!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I wish I could deny it, but ...  I just can’t be sure.

text.Morgana: ...In any case, of course I’m male! I mean, I ...

text.Ann Takamaki: ...What is it?

text.Morgana: No ...  it’s nothing. We’re done talking about that! Anyway, we now know that we can perform minor changes of heart in Mementos. If we come across any eye-catching leads, it may be worth dealing with them for a bit of combat practice.

text.Ann Takamaki: There weren’t any other outstanding ones though...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I bet we’ll get tons of ‘em if we can change someone famous and make the Phantom Thieves well-known. The big fish are our main targets after all.

text.Morgana: First you need to find a way to get through your exams.

text.ACTION: The game’s all, “you should really just fucking chill. Study for those exams or whatever, you’re still at Rank 1 Knowledge, dumbass.”
A mysterious stranger stares at us...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: If we can take down some kinda big target next, we’re totally gonna get famous.
See?

text.Ann Takamaki: I don’t think that you’re necessarily wrong ...  But should we really be doing this at all if we don’t have a reason like with Kamoshida?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You mean we shouldn’t be sticking our noses into other people’s business? I dunno, man. If someone’s in trouble, it’s only natural to wanna help ‘em out!

text.Ann Takamaki: I mean, I agree with that. And I guess I was glad we were able to solve the stalker case.
The same goes for me.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We don’t got much time to be arguing over this either. That Madarame(?) guy bothers me.

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah. But no getting carried away, you understand? And don’t do anything to stand out like fail your exams.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh crap! Speaking of that, I haven’t studied at all ...

text.Morgana: Is it Ryuji? Did he mention anything about Mementos? If there’s anything you want to know, I can tell you.

text.ACTION: Let’s take Morgana up on that.

text.Morgana: Well, it’s the collective Palace of the general public. Deep inside each and every human’s mind is an obscured thought process known as the unconscious. These thought processes then meld together and form what I like to call the collective unconscious.

text.ACTION: Yeah, sure, you totally didn’t just steal that from a psychology textbook.

text.Morgana: In other words, Mementos is a shared cognitive world created by the joint distortions of society as a whole. You can just think of it as the big Palace made from everyone’s hearts though.

I would bet it was because of the shift in public opinion caused by Kamoshida’s change of heart. Those kinds of big changes in the tide will surely have an impact on what goes on in Mementos. In other words, we might be able to get even further if we can rouse up more public acknowledgement. We’ll need to take down another target in order for that to happen though!

text.ACTION: In other words- It’s gated by the story, idiot.

text.Morgana: I have a feeling that something deep within that place has caused me to take my current form. That’s why I’m so invested in reaching the depths of Mementos. If we can figure out the cause of my distorted form, I should go back to normal ...  I think. Either way, I’ll be counting on you guys to help me out.

Oh, and it’s important to note that both Mementos and the Palaces are affected by real world happenings. Weather’s a great example of that. I mean, weather affects your mood, doesn’t it? Same goes for Mementos. You should try heading in on a day with bad weather. I’ll explain in more detail then.

text.Tabloid Show Host: Tomorrow on Good Morning Japan, our guest is Japanese artist Ichiryusai Madarame. A master who brings fantastical scenes to life, how does he feel about his latest exhibition?

text.ACTION: Duhhhhhhhh, I wonder if that could be the person we’re looking for.
No, I have to go work at the beef bowl shop so the speech man will love me! Damn you, cat!
I mean, I want to argue, but that last one is probably the exact reaction I would have.

text.Yuuki Mishima: It’s OK, you don’t have to say it. I know deep down in my heart that it was useful.

text.ACTION: Okay, I kinda wanna pants this twerp.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Anyway, I’m in Shibuya right now. I’d love it if you could come hear me out about your future actions! I’ll be waiting at the diner in Shibuya. You gotta swing by!

text.Morgana: Either way, it sounds like he has something important to say. Why not go see what it is? I won’t be joining you though. There’s something in Mementos I need to go look into. Well, hopefully Mishima has something useful for you ...

text.Yuuki Mishima: Oops, sorry about that. I haven’t been getting a lot of sleep lately. I’ve been staying up managing the Phan-Site all night, every night. I think it’s called ...  PR?

The Phantom Thieves Aficionado Website! Phan-Site for short. You need a catchy name if you want people to notice you. This is all a bit of P-Thieves propaganda! Basically, there’s no point to taking down bad guys if nobody’s gonna know about it. That’s why I’ve started a blog for posts from people you guys saved, while filtering out the haters. We need the Phantom Thieves to be seen in the proper light if we want to make the name popular, right?

text.ACTION: Eh. let’s throw him a bone.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Though actually, I really wanna know how you punish people ...  Don’t worry, I’m not gonna ask. It wouldn’t be any fun if you just up and told me. After all, the Phantom Thieves have a reputation for being secretive!

But I’ll still be here to draw attention to the stuff you do! You can leave that part to me! I’m gonna use my Phan-Site to promote the Phantom Thieves, and weed out any negative comments. Your popularity is gonna be at my mercy ...  or uh, my fingertips. It’s like I’ll be your strategic image management representative, so to speak.
