text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Not a single hit ... ?

text.Morgana: ...Should we come back another time?

text.Ann Takamaki: A building that’s related to artists ...  If we think from there, what would it be ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Didn’t have much of a choice. I think we just happened to get it right.

text.Morgana: What if I hadn’t noticed, and then wandered off and got caught by an enemy!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You prolly woulda figured it out once you started walkin’ on two legs.

text.Morgana: Grr ...

text.Ann Takamaki: So even you can slip into the Metaverse without realizing it, Morgana?

text.Morgana: Yup. In a place with minimal cognitive distortion, the differences can be subtle.

text.Ann Takamaki: Let’s go check it out!
It’s a museum ...  right?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This is Madarame’s?

text.Morgana: A Palace is a scenery driven by desires, just like how Kamoshida’s Palace was a castle.

text.Ann Takamaki: Madarame’s artwork is on display at museums in reality too, though. His exhibit was popular, and people already respect him. Why would he fantasize about a museum?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You got a point ...  It ain’t related to plagiarism or abuse either.

text.Morgana: Let’s try looking around. Racking our brains here won’t do us any good.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...Right. That aside ...  Ain’t a museum a must for phantom thieves!?

text.Morgana: Now that’s our Joker. I feel the same.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But man, just look at that insane crowd...
Ugh ...  Are we gonna have to wait in that gigantic line?

text.Morgana: Don’t be stupid. We’re not going in the front door.

text.Ann Takamaki: But there’s a high wall around the building...

text.Morgana: We’ll just have to find our way up over it then. In any case, let’s get going!

text.ACTION: Our way over the wall is this conspicuous truck.

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s just not hitting me that this is that old guy’s Palace ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That’s why we’re here, right? C’mon, let’s go check it out.

text.ACTION: Once we make it over the wall and through the garden, we see an open window.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ooh! The skylight’s open! I think we can get in here.

text.Ann Takamaki: But it’s a pretty far drop ...  Will we be able to get back out this way?

text.Morgana: Hehe, don’t worry ...  I have a rope! I’m our tool specialist, after all! So, what’s your call, Joker? Want to head inside?

text.Joker: Let’s do this.

text.Ann Takamaki: H-Hey ...  This...

text.ACTION: The painting shifts, the colors swimming, as if beneath the surface of a pool of water.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: C’mon, we’re in a Palace. That ain’t anything to be freakin’ out over.

text.Morgana: Hm, the Palace reflects its ruler’s heart ...  We may want to check these paintings out.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...It’s someone’s name and age? What the hell?

text.Ann Takamaki: That can’t be the title of the painting ...  right? Do you think it’s the artist’s name?

text.Morgana: ...  ...  Let’s check out the other paintings too. I think there might be something important about them...

text.ACTION: There’s something uncanny about all these portraits.

text.Ann Takamaki: But the portraits on display here look the same ...  This is way different from what was at the--

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait a sec!

text.Morgana: Natsuhiko Nakanohara. His name’s written on the plaque.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, I don’t get it! Why’s there a paintin’ of him in here!? And more important, why’s his name written under it?

text.Ann Takamaki: You’re right ...  Doesn’t art usually have like, the title of the piece or the artist’s name?

text.Morgana: Hm ...  This is quite the mystery ...  All right, let’s keep looking around for now.

text.ACTION: Further in, we see something else that alarms us…

text.Ann Takamaki: What ... ? No way!

text.Morgana: It says "Yusuke Kitagawa." There’s no mistaking it.

text.Ann Takamaki: Huh ... ? Wait a second ...  What do you think these paintings are ... ?
I think you’re right.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real? All of ‘em ... ? But it was only Yusuke when we went to his place before...

text.Morgana: This must include former pupils as well. Only one remains now ...  Taking into account what that Nakanohara guy said earlier, things are getting clearer. All right, let’s keep investigating. We need something to further confirm our deductions.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’s up? You find something?

text.Morgana: We’re here to investigate, so we should check everything that catches our attention.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This is gettin’ way too detailed for a freakin’ Palace ...  Why’d he bother makin’ something like this?

text.Morgana: Oh, there’s a museum guide on here. Let’s take it with us!
That is a possibility. At the very least, it should be good reference for the scale of this place.
I see ...  It says it’s one out of two.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...Then the two outta two’s gotta be around here somewhere, right? Just how big is this place ... ?

text.Morgana: We can worry about that another time. Right now our objective is looking into Madarame’s cognition. We may have to reconsider our plan depending on what we find.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I mean, he’s got a Palace ...  Seems pretty fishy to me.

text.ACTION: Before we proceed, we find another locked chest. We happen to have two Lockpicks at the moment, so let’s open it.

The Training Whip is a rather decent upgrade for Ann, the Pearl can be sold at a high price, and the Snuff Soul is 50 SP back. We made out rather well on that one, I’d say. Also they didn’t so much animate Morgana jumping off your shoulder as much as they had him just fall off.
Up ahead, we see a weird sculpture.

text.Ann Takamaki: "A conglomerate work of art that the great director Madarame created with his own funds. These individuals must offer their ideas to the director for the rest of their lives. Those who cannot do so have no worth living!" Hey ...  This is most likely about the plagiarism, right ... ?

text.Morgana: In other words, his pupils are his property. He doesn’t even qualify as an artist if this is true. He’s stealing the ideas from talented students in exchange for securing their livelihood. I wondered about those portraits on display ...  They must all be his "pupils" through his cognition. This even says that they have no worth. Couldn’t this be about the abuse? Madarame will keep them around as long as they’re useful to him, but the moment they’re not...

text.Ann Takamaki: He did say that he owes Madarame his life for being taken in...
When we were at the exhibit, I praised one of the pieces on display. But ...  Kitagawa-kun acted strange. Maybe that piece was plagiarized too...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’s the call? Ain’t this enough to target Madarame!?

text.Morgana: Hold on, you two. We should confirm these facts with Yusuke once more.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Confirm what though!?

text.Morgana: It means we should get solid evidence that such crimes actually took place.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What a pain in the ass...

text.Morgana: Besides, there’s too much we don’t know about Madarame yet.

text.ACTION: That’s true. We haven’t seen that much of his Palace, and this rabbit hole’s only getting deeper.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...Mm, you’re right. I’ll try contacting Kitagawa-kun. I might be able to get the truth out of him if I accept his modeling offer.

text.ACTION: I love whenever Morgana’s eyes go tiny from shock.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: A famous, renowned artist, huh? This might be tougher than Kamoshida. Well, we’ll just prep ourselves until we get confirmation from Yusuke. This is our first mission as real phantom thieves. We’re gonna succeed no matter what!

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m not so sure anymore.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Something wrong?

text.Ann Takamaki: I mean, I know Madarame is a bad person, but still ...  Maybe I’m so hesitant because I haven’t actually met any of his victims.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, I guess that part’s totally different from what happened with Kamoshida.

text.Ann Takamaki: This might be an extreme line of thinking ...  But if an evil person isn’t causing any trouble now ...  Is there really a point in us stepping in?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well ...  you got a point.

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah ...  I guess we could talk some more after that. OK. Let’s meet in Shibuya after school tomorrow.

text.ACTION: Looks like it’s all about what Yusuke wants to do. Somehow, considering the interaction we had earlier today, I don’t see this going in our favor...

text.Chatter: Detective ...  You’ve got me. I’ll confess. I was the one who killed him.

text.Morgana: Huh, he figured it out pretty fast. I wonder if actual investigations are like this.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I just can’t forgive Madarame, but what Ann said made me think ...  To Yusuke, are we just a bunch of thugs?

I knew it ...  It ain’t like he thinks it is! Pisses me off just thinkin’ about it! Good people have to put up with so much crap while shitty adults do whatever they want. Makes me sick. I’m not wrong ...  am I?
Aww yeah! Don’t tell Ann I called you, by the way. Seriously. Well, see you tomorrow.

text.ACTION: Ryuji seems pumped. Good to know.

text.Ann Takamaki: Still waiting for his response.
Can you at least try to take this seriously?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Look, you don’t gotta go all out for this. You’re only doing it so you can get dirt on Madarame, remember?

text.Ann Takamaki: That is true. It sounds like Kitagawa-kun wants this to be a private picture of his though ...  Well, I guess I’ll let you guys know when he contacts me again.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Perfect. He prolly changed his plans immediately just so he could get you over there.

text.Ann Takamaki: We need to find out from Kitagawa-kun if what we saw in the Palace was true...

text.Morgana: Hey, quiet down. It’s that student council president.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yikes ...  She got hold of Mishima today? It’d suck if she noticed us. C’mon, let’s split up.

text.Ann Takamaki: OK, see you later.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: C’mon, let’s get some dirt on Madarame. But man ...  Ann’s late.

text.Ann Takamaki: I was thinking about some things and didn’t notice how much time had passed.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Thinkin’ about what ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: Don’t you think Kitagawa-kun has to be protecting Madarame? I mean they live together, so he’d have to be aware of Madarame’s true nature. The only reason I can think for him doing that is that Madarame has something on him ...

text.ACTION: Or maybe he’s in on it!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, that’s weird. But that’s why we’re goin’ to check it out, right? You ready to be a model?

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah, I’m prepared.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whaddya mean prepared? Prepared for what? Something seem different about her to you?
Ooh, nice eye!

text.Ann Takamaki: I didn’t cut them.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: H-Huh. Well ...  let’s get goin’.

text.ACTION: And so this mystery will go forever unsolved.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We gotta talk to Yusuke.

text.Ann Takamaki: Kitagawa-kun seemed really happy when I agreed to be his model. Once he finishes drawing and gets a little friendlier, we should bring up Madarame.

text.ACTION: It’s amusing that Yusuke keeps getting upset that we’re showing up, but he should really be realizing by now that Ann is a Power-type Stand that can’t exist more than a few meters outside of our presence, and that joke was absolutely not worth the laborious effort it took to make even for the few of you who got it.

text.Ann Takamaki: Wouldn’t you get nervous too, if it was just the two of us?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We’re here to keep an eye on you, so don’t try anything perverted, ‘kay?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Stop making such odd assumptions. I have absolutely no interest in her as someone of the opposite sex.
Is there a problem?

text.Ann Takamaki: ...No, not really.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Well then, let’s get started.

text.Ann Takamaki: Kitagawa-kun?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You hear her?

text.Ann Takamaki: ... It’s no use.

text.Morgana: This isn’t what we planned! We were gonna catch him off guard and make him spill his beans, weren’t we?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: How were we supposed to know this was gonna happen ... ? Guess we just gotta wait ‘til he’s done ...  What an effin’ pain in the ass...

text.Morgana: Perhaps I should try going outside this room...
Heh, who do you think you’re talking to?
It’s weird how flashy that door is ...  And ...  is that a lock? A door with a hefty lock ...  What could be in there?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It’s no good ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...What?

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m sorry ...  Am I the problem?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: No, not at all. It’s just ...  I’m having trouble staying focused today. I’m sorry, but we’ll have to resume this another time...

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m sorry ...  We had another reason for seeing you today ...  We needed to talk to you.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s about those rumors regarding your sensei.

text.Ann Takamaki: That painting I saw at the exhibit ...  You’re the one who actually painted it, right?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That’s ...

text.Ann Takamaki: I knew it.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Your sensei’s seriously messed up. He just thinks of his pupils as tools. That’s why he doesn’t give a damn whether he steals their work or physically beats them. I’ll make this clear, there’s no point in hidin’ stuff from us.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hahaha ...  I have no idea what you’re talking about...

text.Ann Takamaki: You couldn’t go against him, could you? I’m sure we can help you out though ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Stop it...

text.ACTION: Maaku’s got the “!?” going on too, but we can’t see it due to the vignetting.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Don’t misunderstand me though. I offered my ideas to him myself. As such, it can’t be called plagiarism. Sensei is simply suffering from artist’s block right now.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, still ... !

text.Ann Takamaki: Kitagawa-kun...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then why’re you stickin’ around!? All his other pupils ran away! Aren’t you the only one left!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: There are no victims here! Stop pushing your self-centered righteousness on me!
...  ... ! I’m supporting Sensei as his pupil. Where’s the wrong in that?
Then you leave me with no choice...
I’m reporting you to the police.
I asked Takamaki-san to be my model today, but I don’t recall ever calling you two here!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What the eff, man!?

text.Ann Takamaki: Ryuji! Stop it! Calm down, OK

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit ... !

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I won’t report you ...  but only under one condition.

text.Ann Takamaki: What’s that?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I want you to continue being my model, Takamaki-san.

text.Ann Takamaki: But you said that it wasn’t working out today...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That’s because I was unconsciously being modest for your sake ...  However, I have nothing to worry about anymore. If you’re willing to bare everything to me...

text.ACTION: Uh-oh! Seems like the Phantom Thieves have gotten themselves into yet another wacky situation!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Of course, you two won’t be allowed in, and I ask that you forget about our discussion today, as well. If I don’t submit a new piece to Sensei soon, there will be some ...  inconveniences.
Because those are my terms.

text.Ann Takamaki: But that’s--

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, ain’t that bad!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: (to himself)

text.Ann Takamaki: Will you give me a second here!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Of course, I’m willing to wait. I’ll make time according to your plans. But, please come before the exhibit ends.

text.Ann Takamaki: No! That’s not what I mean! Why are you not listening ... !

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Sensei will be returning home soon. We’re done for today. Takamaki-san. I’ll be waiting for you to contact me.

text.Ann Takamaki: No no no! We are not done talking here!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey ...  What should we do?

text.ACTION: Maaku is getting a headache from this shit.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah ...  Dammit. He got us good this time.

text.Ann Takamaki: Don’t give up so easily!

text.ACTION: So, to recap- currently, a teenage girl who has been previously sexually harrased, trying to protest against a situation that also makes her uncomfortable sexually, is being completely ignored by the (otherwise sympathetic) character putting her in this situation, as well as her friends. This scene is kind of a clusterfuck of weird, bad decisions. But uh, hey, comedy!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You moron!

text.ACTION: Ryuji bends down to pick Morgana up.

text.Morgana: Mraow!?
How dare that Yusuke ... !

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: The way he said it, it’s not gonna be semi, but full-on nude...

text.Morgana: F-Fu-- F-F-Full nudity ... ? Lady Ann’s gonna ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Drop it!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You know, you won’t have to worry about that if we make Madarame confess before the exhibit ends.

text.Ann Takamaki: But Kitagawa-kun thinks he owes his life to him. Is there a need to make Madarame confess?

text.Morgana: Then, Lady Ann ...  you’re fine with baring it all!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Madarame’s no different from Kamoshida. That asshole’s usin’ Yusuke, who doesn’t have parents. You’re tellin’ me we should just ignore how he’s bein’ treated horribly like the other pupils?

text.Ann Takamaki: No ...  It is frustrating to leave this along, even if Kitagawa-kun is fine with it himself...

text.Morgana: You can’t leave it be because you’ve endured a lot yourself, with Kamoshida.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...Yeah.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Anyways, we gotta go after this guy. Madarame’s the kind of target we’ve been waiting for. Let’s help Yusuke come to his senses too ...  before he ends up like us.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...Right.

text.Morgana: We need to look into Madarame first.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: There might be tons more stuff that hasn’t been exposed yet, too.

text.Morgana: It may become easier for us to investigate his Palace if he’s preoccupied with his exhibit.

text.Ann Takamaki: Also, there’s the thing about me modeling! Kitagawa-kun said there’d be "inconveniences" unless he submits a new piece. Maybe that’s going to be announced soon as Madarame’s next work...

text.Morgana: We must deal with Madarame, no matter what, before his exhibit ends!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Let’s start after school tomorrow. It’ll be a pain if Miss President finds us on the rooftop again, so where to meet up ...  Let’s see ...  I guess that walkway-like place in Shibuya would work. It’s near Madarame’s place, too.

text.Morgana: ... Changing our hideout periodically, huh? That’s a plan I don’t mind backing.

text.ACTION: And just like that, our hideout has changed.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...Huh?

text.Ichiko Ohya: From the looks of things, you don’t seem like the ordinary, stalking fans.

text.Ann Takamaki: Uh ...

text.Ichiko Ohya: Oh, sorry. I should’ve been more clear. I’m actually looking for people that know Madarame’s pupils. There’s this painting, "Sayuri," that was supposedly stolen in the past. But there’s this rumor that it was taken by one of his pupils in retaliation for being abused. Have you heard anything about that?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I don’t know nothing!

text.Ichiko Ohya: I see ...  There’s no case unless there’s a victim, and if there’s no proof of abuse ...  I can’t write either. Looks like I’m back to square one. Sorry for taking your time.

text.ACTION: Hey random high school student, got any hot scoops???

text.Ichiko Ohya: See you then.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...I guess we should go home for today.

text.ACTION: Two calls in 24 hours? Geez, Maaku’s Mr. Popular. I just want to know what kind of sociopath still uses a phone to call people.

text.Yuuki Mishima: I have some interesting news. Someone who received a change of heart contacted me on the Phan-Site. Said he wants to meet with you to discuss another person who needs a change of heart.

You’re better off talking to him in person if you want specifics. All I know is his target is a terrible person. And that it might complicate things if he posted the name online. I’ll have him wait for you at Shibuya Station after school.

text.ACTION: Um, Mishima, why are you referring people to meet us in person? You’re new to this whole discretion thing, huh?

text.Yuuki Mishima: The guy’s name is "Nakanohara."

text.Morgana: Nakanohara ...  That’s Madarame’s student.

text.ACTION: Nakanohara! It seems like this can only be about one thing...

text.Yuuki Mishima: I told him to approach you. Good luck.

text.Ann Takamaki: That journalist was looking into Madarame too. It could be real.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Someone died though. No one’s talking about it ...  I bet it was covered up.

text.Ann Takamaki: I wonder if Kitagawa-kun has heard anything ...  It’d be great if he could come help us out.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ain’t that asking a bit much? After today, he’s prolly gonna be on edge about us. Well anyway, Madarame’s still a piece of crap! Let’s meet up tomorrow. It’ll be our first time at the new hideout.

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s that passageway in Shibuya, right? Got it. See you guys tomorrow.

text.Morgana: If the rumor Ryuji just spoke of is true, there have to be other victims...

text.Newscaster: This scandal has rocked the sports world—everyone ever involved with him is being pressed for answers. The volleyball association is currently considering banning him permanently, and...

text.Morgana: Drummed out of the volleyball association, eh? Well, he deserves it.
Speaking of Shibuya, didn’t Mishima say Nakanohara would be there, now, too?

text.Ann Takamaki: We’re about to head to the hideout too. Who’s that ... ?

text.Morgana: That’s Nakanohara. Mishima told us to meet him here in Shibuya today.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real ... ?

text.Natsuhiko Nakanohara: ...My name is Nakanohara. Natsuhiko Nakanohara, the one who was posted about on the Phantom Aficionado Website.

text.Ann Takamaki: He seems pretty nice. Doesn’t seem like the stalker type. I think the change of heart must have worked.

text.Natsuhiko Nakanohara: The administrator of that website contacted me ...  They told me to look for someone in a Shujin uniform with a cat...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So? Whaddya want?

text.Natsuhiko Nakanohara: You may have already heard, but there’s someone I wish to trigger a change of heart in. ...An artist by the name of Madarame.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ooh, you think this is it? Is the pupil gonna confess his master’s secrets?

text.Ann Takamaki: His Shadow did mention Madarame as well...

text.Natsuhiko Nakanohara: I’m ...  one of Madarame’s former pupils. He gave me lodging at his home, where I thought only about art. I genuinely wanted to be an artist ...  There was another pupil as well. A very talented man, multiple years my senior. Obviously, Madarame kept tabs on him. Everything he made was claimed as a Madarame original. He wasn’t the only victim though ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All right, we got some real proof of the plagiarism.

text.Natsuhiko Nakanohara: In response to Madarame’s actions ...  that senior pupil committed suicide.

He must have been unable to bear seeing his work praised under Madarame’s name. That was when I disobeyed Madarame’s pleas and left. ...But he quickly pressured other parts of the art world, and my life as a painter was destroyed. I tried to turn over a new leaf working at a ward office ...  but it was no use. My attachment to art warped my emotions. Soon I began getting attached to everything ...  In the end, I even turned into a stalker ...  Ha ...  Haha ...

text.ACTION: Nice supervillain origin story you got there.

text.Natsuhiko Nakanohara: ...I’d like to ask again. Please, make Madarame have a change of heart. Not only for me. It’s ...  to save the life of another man as well.
Even now, there is still one young man remaining under Madarame’s tutelage. I think he’s about your age.

text.Morgana: That has to be Yusuke.

text.Natsuhiko Nakanohara: Not only is he a talented artist, he also owes Madarame for taking him in after his mother passed ...  He is the perfect target.

I actually spoke to him a few times back when I was still living at Madarame’s. I asked him if he found it painful to stay with Madarame ...  and do you know what he said? "If I could leave, I would..."

text.Ann Takamaki: Kitagawa-kun...

text.Natsuhiko Nakanohara: I have no right to say this given my prior cowardice, but I don’t want to see another suicide ... ! I’d like to find a way to save this young man. He has a bright future ahead of him ...  Please consider that when thinking about changing Madarame’s heart.

text.ACTION: Nakanohara leaves. I guess he just knows we’re the fucking Phantom Thieves now.

text.Morgana: It sounds like we don’t have the time to deliberate whether or not to change Madarame’s heart.

text.ACTION: Yeah, let’s save the dude who’s blackmailing us!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hell yeah! Madarame’s just a piece of shit who preys on the weak!

text.Ann Takamaki: Plus, we finally got to hear how Kitagawa-kun really feels!

text.Morgana: Well, since we’ve reached a unanimous decision, how about we continue this at our new hideout?
We all saw that Palace. We’ll pay dearly if we assume it’s just going to be like the last one. And furthermore ...  Lady Ann’s chastity is on the line!

text.ACTION: You know, I came into this update not thinking much of this weird plotline except that it was really silly and dumb and not that great, but these jokes are actually pushing me over the edge and now all I can think about is the word “regrettable.”

text.Morgana: We’ll need to do what we did with Kamoshida. First, we secure an infiltration route in the Palace. After that, we send our calling card. Once the Treasure has materialized, we steal it.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oooh, I got a question! Madarame doesn’t know that we were doin’ stuff in the Palace yet. Why are we already gettin’ treated like criminals in there?

text.Morgana: You’re learning, Ryuji. Well done. It must be because he doesn’t trust anyone. Any unknown person may as well be an enemy.

text.Ann Takamaki: Or maybe he’s just super salty from all those rumors that have been spreading about him ...

text.ACTION: I’m super salty that I just heard the words “super salty” in this motherfucking video game.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then his Palace bein’ so crazy had nothing to do with us ... ?

text.Morgana: Either way, we should stay on our best behavior. It’ll be harder for us to steal the Treasure if we needlessly increase the security level.

text.Ann Takamaki: We need to be careful of Kitagawa-kun this time too. I’m sure that whatever he sees will just get passed on to Madarame.

text.Morgana: That’s right!

text.Ann Takamaki: Hey, what is Madarame’s Treasure going to look like anyway? Another crown?

text.Morgana: I’d doubt that. But my sixth sense will know when I see it.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh yeah, you go completely nuts, huh.

text.Ann Takamaki: Our time limit is when the exhibit ends, right? That means ...  June 5th.

text.Morgana: We’ll carry out the plan after we’ve sent out the calling card. So, our infiltration route will need to be set in stone two days prior, on June 2nd.

text.Ann Takamaki: Now listen here. We can’t mess this up, NO MATTER WHAT! OK!?

text.ACTION:
Part 31: 5/18-5/19: The Most Adorable Stalker
	Part 30: 5/18-5/19: The Most Adorable Stalker
Let’s just forget about the last update’s unpleasantness.

text.Morgana: Come on, it’s time to get this mission started!

text.ACTION: Cool detail here- the “Mission Start” logo casts a barely-visible shadow in the lower-right corner.
Um, what? This sounds like an annoying complication. I have to leave in the middle of a Palace infiltration?
But let’s just leave for now.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That’s all for today?

text.Veteran Pick-Up Artist: Everyone knows whatever’s been on TV. You could talk about the Madarame exhibit. Some witty wordplay, maybe an impersonation could work too. Just get their attention first, OK?

text.ACTION: Fucking impressions? What, are you going to pick up chicks by appearing on SNL? These are the lamest pick-up artists ever.

text.Calm Student: Hey, not so loud. He’s been showing up pretty regularly, so it looks like he’ll be sticking around.

text.Energetic Student: I see, so is the thing about him having a criminal record not true, then?

text.Calm Student: I don’t know, I’m too scared to ask. Anyway, it’s probably best not to get too involved with him.

text.ACTION: Looks like we’re still not gonna make many new friends here.

text.Starry-Eyed Student: Y-Yes ... ! Kamoshida tricked people into thinking he was a hero, but he wasn’t! Oh, and don’t tell anyone my true identity. No one can know that I’m a Phantom Thief!

text.ACTION: Over on the first floor, we find… Uh...
...Excuse me for a moment, let’s move somewhere a little less crowded.
...Yeah, okay, she’s definitely following us while pretending to be reading that book.

text.Makoto Niijima: I had heard you were quite the troublemaker, but you seem to be behaving yourself.

text.ACTION: You are adorably bad at this.

text.Tae Takemi: Has anyone ever studied the correlation between the rise in temperature and weirdos ... ? So, what are you here for today?
...Looks like I have a patient with an emergency.

text.Girl s Father: I’ve heard rumors about this place. I’d like for you to examine her. She was diagnosed with bronchitis, but the medicine she was given hasn’t been working at all. She has a fever that won’t go away, and she’s losing weight because she’s not hungry ...

text.Tae Takemi: A young girl losing weight is definitely not good. You should go to a bigger hospital. I can’t provide a thorough examination here.

text.Girl s Father: We’ve been going to a big hospital! A university hospital in East Shinjuku! But all they tell us is that it’s persistent bronchitis ... !
The doctor there performs exams like he’s on an assembly line. I think he’s famous or something ...

text.Tae Takemi: A famous doctor, huh ... ? I’m just a general practicioner out here in the sticks. As you can see, I don’t even have any staff.

text.Girl s Father: W-Wait! I’ve heard there’s a medicine that can only be acquired here ... !

text.ACTION: Back off, pal. I was here for that sweet, sweet panacea long before you were.

text.Girl s Father: Please! I’ll pay you! Please, at least just examine her!

text.Tae Takemi: (sigh) ...Fine.
Is your vision blurry? How about your throat, does it hurt ... ? Hm. No signs of swelling.
Hmmm...

text.ACTION: This is likely a reference to the Devil Social Link from Persona 4, who was a nurse named Sayoko Uehara.

text.Tae Takemi: There’s something I’d like to ask him about a case that was in last month’s medical journal.
I see. Guess the ones in stock will have to do...
You’ll need to help me administer the medicine. Also, bring the beaker with the red label in the fridge, a towel, was basin, and measuring spoon...

text.Joker: (nods)

text.Tae Takemi: It was a very unique strain of an infectious disease. It can’t be detected by conventional exams. I temporarily suppressed the symptoms. We’ll make adjustments as her condition improves. OK, that’ll be one million yen for today.

text.Girl s Father: A-A million yen ... !? Th-That’s outrageous! You’re completely taking advantage of ...   ...  ...  I mean, all right ...  I agreed to pay. You don’t ...  take credit cards ...  do you? I’ll go withdraw some cash right now!

text.Tae Takemi: By the way, that famous doctor you mentioned earlier ...  Was it Medical Chief of Staff Oyamada?

text.Girl s Father: Yes ...  are you familiar with him?

text.Tae Takemi: ...I knew it. In that case, I’ll make this free of charge.
...Hehe.
...By the way, thanks to your outburst earlier ...  I’m going to perform a very special exam on you today...

text.Girl s Father: So, is he your ...  assistant? He seems awfully young...

text.Tae Takemi: Yes, my assistant ...  guinea pig. He’s about to put in a LOT of hard work today. Aren’t you?

text.Joker: It feels like my bond with Takemi is growing even deeper...

text.Sick Girl: Um, Doctor ... ? Can I go back to school now?

text.Tae Takemi: Not for a while. You need to start eating and regain your strength first. Can you do that for me?
Don’t mention it ...
Maybe you won’t even be able to make it home...

text.Joker: I feel like cooperating in that shady clinical trial has increased my Guts...

text.Tae Takemi: OK, good work today.

text.ACTION: Shut up Morgana, we can’t do that yet.

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...Another box came for you.

text.Morgana: ...What did you get?

text.Newscaster: Recently, personal info stored by several domestic companies was decrypted and leaked online. Hundreds of thousands of people’s info is believed to be leaked, and many are voicing their anxiety. According to experts, there is a high chance that an international group of hackers is involved...

text.Morgana: So someone stole all that personal information about all those people ... ? Wow.

text.ACTION: The world’s fucked up. There’s no joke here, only the quiet dread of having to continue to interact with this hellfucked species for yet another day.

text.Young Female Customer: Whaaat? But I want to watch TV. There’s a special on that guy they call a "Detective Prince," Akechi.

text.Young Male Customer: It’ll still be on the news. You can watch at home. That pretty boy’s been on TV a lot lately. You can see his face any time, actually. Well, thanks for the coffee.

text.Sojiro Sakura: This taste ...
...The flavor profile is bland. You should practice more to bring out the roast’s full potential.

You see a lot of different customers come through when you have a cafe like this. Even if someone looks like trouble, I’ll serve them the same cup of coffee I serve everyone else. That’s my job. I have pride in what I do. You’re like a customer, too. One that takes a tremendous amount of effort. You have the potential, so keep training.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...I hope you understand.

text.ACTION: What’s there to understand? You’re blackmailing us so my friend will get naked for you. Simple.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I warn you. Don’t involve yourself any further.
Don’t play dumb. I’m saying you’re an inconvenience. I won’t forgive you if you continue making a mockery of my sensei. Am I clear? This is a warning.

text.Morgana: It looks kinda dumb...

text.ACTION: I didn’t realize you could actually examine this until I tried again.

Part 32: 5/19: Artsy Fartsy
	Part 31: 5/19: Artsy Fartsy
You’re right, I did already know that.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then we send the callin’ card. Yeah, yeah, we know the drill. Anyways, let’s get ready!

text.ACTION: But first, let’s enter the Velvet Room.

text.Igor: You must surely be accustomed to infiltrating Palaces by now?

Regardless, you have yet to obtain a truly acceptable number of Personas. This is not the full potential of the power of the wild card. Hm, I suppose this is a prime opportunity to help further your rehabilitation along. Don’t worry ...  This assignment is not mandatory. Think of if almost as a test of strength.

text.Justine: We will have you bring us the mask we specify.

text.Caroline: You just gotta show us the Persona we ask for!

text.Justine: First off ...  we would like for you to bring us a Jack Frost.

text.Caroline: That’s too easy, Justine! It should be a challenge. Hmmm ...  I want it to have Mabufu too! You got that, Inmate? Bring us a Jack Frost with Mabufu.

text.Justine: Very well. We ask for a Jack Frost with Mabufu. Please speak to us again when you have it.

text.Igor: This will not be mandatory for your rehabilitation, but you will be handsomely rewarded for it. I encourage you to at least try your hand at this.

text.ACTION: These requests are more-or-less identical to Margaret’s requests from P4, but with greater rewards. We won’t be attempting to fulfill this request just yet, but I just wanted to show that it was available.
See those tiny red lines, barely visible through the image resize and compression? Those are the lasers.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hold on, there wasn’t anything like this last time though!

text.Morgana: The rumors might slowly be making Madarame become more wary of us ...  Joker! They’re not easy to see, but you should be able to do it with your skills. Be careful!

text.ACTION: Note that you can just dash or hold X to totally cheese the entire system, ha.
More lasers have been added all around this area.
As for enemies, these Mokoi like to boost their own Attack.
Hua Po attacks by casting Fire.
And Apsaras uses Wall skills to guard the weaknesses of its allies.

text.Morgana: The security will probably get a little more fierce as well. Make sure you don’t touch anything or run into any of the displays, all right?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...What’re you lookin’ at me for?

text.ACTION: Up ahead, we come to a room with many paths and a lot of enemies.
These Koropokguru are weak to Fire, so they go down real quick and don’t get turns to show off.

Finally, these Onmoraki mainly just attack, and they’re only weak to Gun, which is annoying but easy to exploit. Occasionally, however, they cast Mudo, an instant-kill Curse spell, which suuuuuuuucks on the off-chance it actually hits.
Soon enough, we’re at the stairs to the next area.
Maaku hammers the button repeatedly, but the door doesn’t open.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit, it ain’t openin’...

text.ACTION: In this room, two areas are beyond our reach, sealed by glass walls, and we’ve also got this suspicious vase in the center.
No time for that, Panther. Let’s move.

text.Morgana: I know it might be tough to take it with us, but don’t you think it’d sell for tons?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hold on, you’re steppin’ on something!

text.Ann Takamaki: Isn’t this bad!?

text.ACTION: Joker immediately does a sick backflip...
...dodging out of the way of the lasers that pop up.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Urgh, and you were the one makin’ us be careful too ...  So, whaddya wanna do? Run outta here?

text.Morgana: No, passing through all of these lasers will draw far too many enemies to my location!

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, hold on! Joker’s not trapped!

text.Morgana: Sorry Joker, but we’re going to need you to search for a way to turn off these infrared lasers! This is a museum, so there has to be some switch to let the workers avoid these lasers. Find it ... !

text.ACTION: Over in the corner, we can climb up on top of this vending machine to reach a higher level.
There’s a guard roaming around, but the fight is just a single Hua Po.
Down on the ground, we find a button.

text.Joker: I wonder if I should press it...
Press the button
It looks like Panther was able to get out...

text.ACTION: By climbing back up, we can also reach the other side, and find another button. Pressing this one, however...
If we follow the footprints on the ground, we see a crooked portrait.

text.Joker: Move the painting
Press the button

text.Ann Takamaki: You did it! Let’s hurry up and get back together with him!

text.ACTION: Welp, bye cat. I’d say it was nice knowing you, but, well...

text.Morgana: There has to be a control room for them! I don’t know if it’s nearby though ... !

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...We just gotta trust him. C’mon, let’s try lookin’ for it!

text.ACTION: We find a vent in the corner.
Conveniently, it leads into the security room.

text.Ann Takamaki: But ...  it looks like we need a password to use it.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uh, they probably ain’t gonna just leave it lyin’ around.

text.Ann Takamaki: Then what are we supposed to do ... ? Look for someone who might know it?

text.Shadow 2: Hey, did you hear about those intruders?

text.Shadow 3: Yeah, you mean the thieves sneaking around in here? I got a call telling me to change the password, just in case.

text.Shadow 2: And? What did you change it to?

text.Shadow 3: I said, hello! 07734. If you read the numbers upside-down, they spell out the word hello.
Eh, it should be fine as long as nobody else find out. It’s not like anyone’s eavesdropping on us.
Anyway, don’t forget: when you see the code input, be sure to say hello.

text.Ann Takamaki: Did you hear that?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Sure did. C’mon Joker, let’s go say hello to that terminal thing!

text.Joker: The password should be 07734...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Sweet! Let’s go grab that stupid cat and get movin’!
Sheesh ...  Weren’t you the one tellin’ us not to go around touchin’ shit in the exhibit?

text.Morgana: Urgh, that is true ...  I can’t believe I made such a novice mistake, even for solid gold ...  But something was drawing me to this vase ...

text.Ann Takamaki: What do you mean ... ? Isn’t it just an ordinary gold vase? I wonder if there’s something special about it. Should we take a closer look just in case?

text.ACTION: ...and a giant diamond appears out of nowhere!

text.Ann Takamaki: What is this!?

text.Morgana: Oh, I see ...  So that’s why I was drawn to it! Joker, catch it! I’ll explain the rest of this later. Just get after it and attack!

text.ACTION: So, now we’re fighting… a villain from a rejected episode of Courage the Cowardly Dog.
And for good measure, it resists almost everything.
We manage to take it down nonetheless, getting a large helping of money and experience for our troubles.
Morgana learns Lucky Punch, which is Miniscule Physical with a high chance of Critical damage, resulting in a knockdown.
Meanwhile, Ann learns Maragi, Light multi-target Fire.

text.Ann Takamaki: What was that ... ?

text.Morgana: That, Lady Ann, was a rare Shadow that occasionally resides in pricey items. I call them Treasure Demons. They’re great. Not only do they give you a lot of experience, they are useful for your Personas too. However, they run very fast, and attacks don’t deal very much damage to them.

text.ACTION: These guys are the equivalent of the rare Gold Shadows from Personas past. They’re more frequent when the security level is higher (which is part of the reason I rarely see them), giving you an incentive to keep it high, and can also be fused into Personas if you convince one to join you. Ironically, the skill we just got for Morgana helps with that greatly, because again, they resist almost everything, so critical attacks are the best way to knock them down.
Up ahead, we run into a hallway blocked by more lasers, forcing us to climb up and around.

text.Morgana: Calm down. Look at where the security guard is walking...

text.ACTION: Anyone have to use the restroom?
Might as well check out the ladies’ room too.
Further in, we come to a large room full of more paintings.
In a shocking development, we’re barred from exiting.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Crap, let’s get outta here, fast! Which way’s the exit!?

text.ACTION: Both entrances are sealed, so we’re locked in here with these enemies until we can find a way out.
For the record, the strong Shadow fight here consists of five (!) Onmoraki. It’s rather trying on our bullet reserves.
Eventually, we find another crooked painting.

text.Ann Takamaki: Does this painting look crooked to you?

text.Joker: Let’s take it off the wall.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Who cares about that shit? Just hurry up and try pushin’ it.

text.Ann Takamaki: All right! It looks like it’s unlocked now!

text.Morgana: This should let us move forward. Nice work, Joker!

text.ACTION: Further in, we have our progress halted to look at this shiny building.

text.Morgana: It definitely looks like something important would be hidden away in there ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Let’s go find out!

text.ACTION: The walls open to allow us to pass.

text.Ann Takamaki: Are these ...  infrared lasers? There’s no way we can get past them ...

text.Morgana: This level of security only proves there’s something worth protecting up ahead.

text.Ann Takamaki: Wait, there’s something written on the sign ...  "All personnel: This door can only be opened via the security room that lies beyond it ...  Please be cautious, as it is impossible to open from the outside."

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So, it’s never gonna open!? How’re we supposed to get past ... !?

text.Morgana: Wait ...  That door ...  I think I’ve seen that pattern somewhere...
Guys, let’s head back!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Why!?

text.Morgana: I think I know what real-world door that’s based on. There may be another way to open it! In any case, I’ll explain later! Come on, let’s go!

text.Joker: I suppose we should listen to Morgana for the time being...

text.ACTION: There’s a safe room nearby, so we can just check out.

text.Joker: Return to the real world

text.Nav: Now returning to the real world from Madarame’s Palace. Thank you for your hard work.

text.Morgana: I think we’re almost halfway through. I’m starting to get a faint sense of the Treasure near here.

text.Ann Takamaki: That means we’re at least making some progress, right ... ? Hey, when do you want to come in here next? Let me know when you decide ...  I’ll be waiting!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I dunno ...  You think there’s some kinda off switch somewhere?

text.Ann Takamaki: Mona ... ?

text.Morgana: I have a suspicious place in mind.
Remember? This shack is the basis for Madarame’s Palace. I actually scouted it out the last time we were here.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whoa ...  So this was your plan from the start ... ?

text.Morgana: Correct.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...You only went "scouting" because you were bored.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So? Where’s this suspicious place?

text.Morgana: It’s on the second floor. I noticed an unnaturally hefty lock on a door up there.

text.Ann Takamaki: If it’s locked, that means there’s something in there he doesn’t want people to see.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But don’t we wanna be openin’ the door in the Palace?

text.Morgana: Yes, and we’re going to do that by opening the real one in front of Madarame’s eyes. Basically, we’re going to change his cognition that the door is unopenable.

text.Ann Takamaki: In other words ...  when we open the one in Madarame’s house, that area in his Palace will open on its own?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I’m not really gettin’ it ...  Is that gonna work?

text.Morgana: Trust me! There’s no chance it won’t open! ...I think! You understand, don’t you, Joker?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well yeah, but...

text.Ann Takamaki: But even then, there’s still that hefty lock we have to deal with in reality, right?

text.Morgana: Oh, that’ll be a breeze. Just give me a hairpin and I’ll handle it. It will take some time though. Doing everything by myself in front of Madarame would be impossible. If only there was someone who could distract him for a while...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh ...  Ohhh!

text.Ann Takamaki: What?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I guess the only way is ...  having you go nude.

text.Morgana: Fancy you say that, Ryuji. I was just thinking the same thing.

text.Ann Takamaki: This isn’t funny!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We’re not sayin’ you should really get naked.

text.Morgana: It’s simply the best excuse for you to enter Madarame’s house without raising suspicions ...  So, we’d like for you to play the role of decoy, Lady Ann.

text.Ann Takamaki: This is way too sudden ...  I mean, I don’t even know where the locked door is.

text.Morgana: Don’t worry, I’ll accompany you.

text.Ann Takamaki: But that’s still technically only me ...  Worst comes to worst, what if I get found out ... ?

text.Morgana: We can run into the Palace! ...Or something?

text.Ann Takamaki: I mean, you’re not giving me much confidence in this plan! Do I have to be the bait ... ?
Why can’t one of you guys go nude!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That ain’t what he wants.

text.Ann Takamaki: Then make it so he does!

text.ACTION: All right, let’s go change Yusuke’s cognition!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All you gotta do is trick Yusuke, have him take you to that room, then just open the door.

text.Ann Takamaki: You make it sound so easy ... !
Urghhhh! God!
Seriously, you better pull this off!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We’ll be countin’ on you, Morgana! Don’t let Yusuke notice ya, all right?

text.Ann Takamaki: If he tries to force my clothes off ...  I’ll tear that house down! I’m really gonna lose it if we do all this and the Palace door doesn’t open. Got it!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We’re workin’ to get dirt on that guy’s crimes either way. It won’t go to waste. All right, let’s get down and dirty tomorrow.

text.Ann Takamaki: Tomorrow!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Earlier the better.

text.Ann Takamaki: Um, b-but ...  will Kitagawa-kun agree?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I dunno, just say something like "I really need it to be tomorrow." That should work, yeah?

text.ACTION: This is the rainy night theme. It’s pretty close to the normal theme, but it’s still good.

text.Morgana: I’ll get it open right before his very eyes.

text.Ann Takamaki: Mm-hm. He asked me to come by tomorrow.
Yeah ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Man, this is such a pain ...  We gotta open that door AND have Madarame see it, right?

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah. Morgana said that’ll change his cognition.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh, and one more thing. Let us know if any weird shit goes down and we’ll be there to back you up ASAP.

text.Ann Takamaki: Kk, got it.

text.ACTION: Shit like the “be careful” option and what Ryuji just texted make me think that they knew how weird and skeevy and scary this all was, but it’s already in the game, so it’s too little too late.

text.Morgana: A Palace is a reflection of how its owner views the real world. So if Madarame’s cognition of reality changes, it’s only natural that his Palace would be affected. And all jokes aside, we really will need Lady Ann to strip for Yusuke. It’s the only way.

text.Game Show Host: A: Unconsenting cutting of hair; B: Using noise to cause distress; Which of the two would be considered a case of bodily harm!? You be the judge!

text.ACTION: B seems ridiculous, so it’s probably right.

text.Game Show Host: The correct answer is ...  B! If you drive someone crazy with noise, that’s bodily harm!

text.Lawyer on Game Show: If it disrupts the body’s functions, it counts as bodily harm, even if there’s no physical contact! Hair grows back, so it doesn’t count as a wound. That’d be a case of "assault," not bodily harm.

text.Morgana: Hey, you got it right. I’m impressed by how much you know about law.

text.Joker: It feels like I’ve improved my Knowledge.

text.ACTION: Occasionally there’ll be a quiz show on TV, and answering correctly will increase our Knowledge. It’s silly but helpful.

Part 33: 5/20: Mission: Imbeciles
	Part 32: 5/20: Mission: Imbeciles

text.Caring Young Friend: I thought you liked that place ‘cause the pay was good. What happened?

text.Pale Young Man: Sure, the pay’s fine, but I’m the only one there at night. That job magazine said it was a "fun, friendly workplace." (sigh) Maybe I should just quit...

text.Morgana: Like he says, work can be pretty trying ...  But it’s a worthwhile experience. Don’t give up.

text.ACTION: What would you know about work, cat? You spend 80% of your time in that bag.

text.Female Student: I can’t believe it ...  I at least wanted to hit the average...

text.Joker: I wonder what score I got ...  It might be faster if I counted from the bottom up...

text.Morgana: Hm ...  Nothing notable.

text.ACTION: Welp, we sucked. All right answers and still that Rank 1 Knowledge was enough to drag us down to below the average. We’re dumb-dumbs, sadly.
Ryuji, we’re kinda busy right now with Madarame, maybe this could wait?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Apparently he’s been hanging out at a monjayaki shop a lot. I heard he gets real drunk there and brags to his coworkers.

Right! That’s where you come in. He knows me, so I ain’t gonna be able to get anywhere near him ...  But that ain’t the case for you! I bet you could even sit next to his booth if you wanted! Prolly. Soooo ...  I’ll let you know once I figure out when he’s going drinking. Til then, we’re gonna put a hold on our training. Well, I’ll be counting on you!

text.ACTION: Well, looks like Maaku’s gonna be going after Yamauchi soon.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Me and Maaku’re banned from goin’ there, so all we can do is wait here...

text.Morgana: No, you two have something different you’ll need to do.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whaddya mean ... ?

text.Morgana: You have to wait inside the Palace. Once that door opens, sneak in and look for some kind of control room. We need to make sure the door can’t close anymore after it’s open.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ohhh, I get it. Mkay, you can leave that to us!

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m sorry it was so sudden.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Oh, it’s not a problem. But as I told you yesterday, Sensei will be returning in about twenty or thirty minutes. So um ...  I’m sorry if that causes some anxiety on your part.

text.Ann Takamaki: (whispering)

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What was that?

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh no, it was nothing!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: By the way ...  Have you gained some weight?

text.ACTION: As uncomfortable as everything surrounding it is, this is a really solid joke, and it’s accompanied by an amazing music sting.

text.Ann Takamaki: You think so? I weigh the same as always ...  Maybe I’m bloated today?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So, then ...  can you, um ...  get ready here?

text.Ann Takamaki: I ...  need to take my clothes off, right?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Y-Yes please...

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m embarrassed. Could you look the other way ... ?

text.ACTION: Clothes continually land on the floor near Yusuke.

text.Ann Takamaki: Phew, that was tight...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Tight ... ? No, I’m doing this for art ... !

text.Ann Takamaki: Don’t look over here, OK ... ? Hey, your sensei’s coming back soon, right?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I believe so...

text.Ann Takamaki: Hm ...  Do you think we could do this somewhere else then? A little more atmosphere would be lovely...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: This should be good enough...

text.Ann Takamaki: But wouldn’t a room with a lock be a bit better?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: A lock ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: Must a girl say more ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Wha!? But the only one with a lock is ...  Sensei’s room ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Then why not there?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I can’t intrude ...  Besides, I don’t have the key...

text.Ann Takamaki: (whispering)

“Ishikawa Goemon was a Japanese outlaw. The historical Goemon is only mentioned in two sources, both of which were created after his death. The first one, the Toyotomi Hideyoshi fu, details his attempted assassination of the shogun Hideyoshi Toyotomi, his capture, and his execution alongside his young son in 1594. Goemon's death by being boiled alive was also described in a second historical source by Pedro de Morejon who transcribed his name as "Ixicava Goyemon". As time passed, Goemon's story was expanded to make him a hero similiar to Robin Hood, robbing the rich and giving his spoils to the poor. Stories from the 19th and the 20th century also make him out be a skilled ninja. Goemon and his infamous death eventually became the subject of various Bunraku and Kabuki plays. The legend was also adapted into movies, anime shows and video games, the most popular of which is the Ganbare Goemon series by Konami.”

text.Usami: The golden ratio used in the Mona Lisa and the Parthenon is a famous example. But a different ratio has been used in Japanese art and architecture since ancient times. Do you know what it is? Now then, Hamiru-san. Take a look at this.

One theory says it’s because Asians have rounder faces than Westerners, so they prefer a similar shape. This ratio was used in things like ukiyo-e paintings and the pagodas at Horyuji Temple. One you should all be familiar with is B4-size paper. Those proportions are the silver ratio.

No Sae flashforward this time. Strength is the arcana of inner strength and determination, as well as physical strength, though it’s not the focus, unlike the Chariot. It represents concepts like patience, but when reversed signals weakness and self-doubt.

The Triangle Spread, which let you fuse three Personas in 3 and 4, is curiously absent from Persona 5. Instead, you’ll do almost all your fusing from two Personas and select few special Personas are only attainable through the Group Guillotine, which takes its place. The Group Guillotine requires you to place specific fodder Personas into preset “recipes” to work, unlike the open system of regular fusion.

text.Tae Takemi: If you’re feeling OK, you can go home now.

You remember that girl from the other day? The Chief of Staff Oyamada’s patient? Her dad’s been bringing her here to be treated, even though I referred them to another hospital. I even told them about the medical error I made...

I’m just a quack though ...  The medical error was well documented. Everyone in my field knows about it. I led the development of a new drug for an incurable illness called "Crawford-Ende’s disease." Although I wasn’t the one who administered the medicine, it was the cause of the error.

With Crawford-Ende’s, certain cells indiscriminately attack other cells throughout the body. When it reaches the muscles, the patient slowly begins to die ...  There hasn’t been much progress made on it-- partly because there haven’t been many cases of it. I worked with a pharmaceutical company that had reached the final stage of production, but ...  One day, I was suddenly removed from my position. That Chief of Staff Oyamada, my superior at the time, took over the entire operation.

He made careless mistakes and rushed completion so he could use it on a patient named Miwa. Miwa-chan had a reaction and lapsed into critical condition. The chief panicked and laid the blame on me. Miwa-chan and her family resented me ...  ...No matter what I said, I couldn’t change how they felt about me.

Well, that doesn’t matter ...  The development of the medicine was suspended, so I had no reason to stay at that hospital. At least now I can keep working as a general practitioner, on my own terms ...  with my guinea pig.

That’s the new medicine I’ve been trying out on you. This version is in the final stage of testing. It searches for those cells that take the offensive and destroys them upon detection. That’s why it’s harmless for people who don’t have the disease ...  probably.

text.Joker: It feels like my bond with Takemi is growing even deeper...

text.Joker: Help him out

To get your message across, be tenacious in conveying your thoughts to the audience. Have a firm point of view, and communicate it clearly—that’s the first rule of negotiating. Haha! You have me reliving the fighting spirit I had when I first became a politician.

text.Joker: Yoshida explained the basics of speech-giving. I feel like my bond with him is growing deeper...

text.ACTION: Diplomacy lets you ask for more money or items after succeeding once, and is a great way to get tons of money from enemies by just asking over and over until they reject you and then knocking them back down and doing it again. Unfortunately, later upgrades to Sun make this impossible, to the point where I’ve seen people suggest keeping Sun at Rank 2. We won’t be doing that, because there’s other ways to get money, and it’s not all that scarce to begin with. Besides, not doing the best Confidant in the game because it’s sub-optimal isn’t my style.

Haven’t you heard of it? It’s a condition where your senses can cross over each other, like seeing music as color. Mr. Hamiru. You were staring off into space, weren’t you? Well, your number’s up. The root words of synesthesia are "syn" and "aisthesis." What do they mean?

Good! You’ve been studying! Unfortunately, synesthesia’s something you have to be born with ...  You can’t learn it. Some of the geniuses over the course of history have had synesthesia. The composer Franz Liszt instructed his orchestra to play the color purple.

text.ACTION: Must’ve been hard teaching them all to act! ...I’m sorry.

text.Chouno: The poet Arthur Rimbaud was also said to see colors in letters.

text.ACTION: Maaku gains Knowledge +1, and is still at Rank 1, fucking hell.

OK, let’s head there now!

text.Morgana: No, not just anyone will have one. It’s primarily those with strong distorted desires ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: They basically gotta be criminals. Real bastards like Kamoshida or Madarame.

text.Morgana: On the other hand, Palaces can’t exist within Persona-users. It’s just impossible for them to form. Basically, your Persona is the true feelings of your heart, which arise from conquering your inner Shadow. Then since you have full control of your emotions, there’s no way your desires can get distorted.

	Part 35: 5/23: Paint Me Like One Of Your Ukiyo-e Girls
