text.ACTION: We approach the octopus on the side of the boat.

text.Morgana: I guess it is just a painting, after all. I’m sure we’ll be OK...

text.ACTION: The boat shakes and the octopus swings one of its tentacles…
...knocking us straight out of the painting.
We land unharmed on the floor.
Fighting these enemies gives Morgana Magaru, finally letting him hit multiple enemies.
Ignoring the previous incident, we make our way back up to the boat painting, jump out, and hit the button.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Ah, there are no longer any empty frames at this point.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I bet there’s a new path again too. Let’s get in there and check it out.

text.ACTION: We can’t jump back into the boat painting from here, so we’re forced to jump down and re-enter from the desert painting, then head right to the shrine and forward into the gate.
Back in the forest, we climb along the scenery and head forward once we reach the peak.

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: My fine mansion, my lifestyle among the chosen few ...  Those things are the true "art"!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So running your atelier out of a shabby, run-down shack was simply an act after all ...  How foolish I was to have been deceived for so long...

text.Ann Takamaki: Fox...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: How despicable ...  We have encountered so many of his paintings, yet not once did he mention a love for art. These are no "paintings" ...  They are just meaningless self-assertions placed into picture frames ... !

text.Morgana: I’m excited to see how the change of heart alters him. Now, let’s hurry!

text.ACTION:
Part 37: 5/23: Goddammit Game, You Made Euclid Cry
	Part 36: 5/23: Goddammit Game, You Made Euclid Cry
The dev team is devious enough to hide a stationary Shadow in one of the bathrooms, ready to pounce if you run in. This isn’t important, I just thought it was really dumb.
An MC Escher hellscape! I don’t see what the big deal with this style is, you guys. I can draw things bad, too.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Shit ...  What the hell is up with this place!?

text.Ann Takamaki: There’s so much gold ... ! It’s hurting my eyes...

text.Morgana: The distortion is especially bad here ...  It’s barely holding up. Plus, it’s not even on our map ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So we must ascertain the truth through our eyes alone...

text.ACTION: We run into more Shadows here. These Koppa Tengu are still weak to Ice.
We head into the mysterious blue gateway.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It seems even the paths beyond these apertures are distorted in the same way as this room...

text.ACTION: Warping again, we come to an area with two paintings.

text.Morgana: It’s probably some kind of illusion. We’re in a Palace, after all. Well, I guess the painting itself might be correct though.

text.Ann Takamaki: You say "correct," but aren’t they all counterfeit? Although maybe the real one’s here too...

text.Morgana: I wonder ...  Either way, the fact that this is here might mean it’s connected to this space in some way.

text.ACTION: ...puts us right back at the start. Because everything has to be a gimmick.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It seems this is a trick after all ...  He would not let us proceed that easily...

text.Ann Takamaki: Isn’t that a fake? I mean, this is Madarame’s Palace...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: There is an obvious difference if you look closely. It shouldn’t be too difficult to tell them apart.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, maybe it’s obvious for you ...  What do you think, Joker?

text.ACTION: So, here we have to correctly identify the true Sayuri ...  from memory. I really hope you were paying attention to what color she was wearing one of the two times we saw it prior, because otherwise you’re screwed!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Unfortunately, this is a fake. The real "Sayuri" has vibrant crimson garments.

text.ACTION: What? Oh, uh… I knew that! Just showing off the penalty for failure for the LP! Yeah, let’s go with that!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: O-Oh, right ...  Now that you mention it...

text.ACTION: By the way, that penalty is...
This Makami loves to cast Mafrei (multi-target Nuclear) and Double Fangs and is weak to Electricity. We make sure to pick one up for later.

text.Joker: It’s the real thing.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That is correct. It seems you have quite the eye for detail, Joker.

text.ACTION: He says, after I fucked it up once and chose the only other option.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real ...  That’s amazin’...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The vibrant crimson clothes, her beautiful hair, the sublime balance between subject and background ...  This may only be an illusion, but it is without a doubt a spitting image of the true "Sayuri."

text.ACTION: If you know what it looks like so goddamn exactly why am I doing this instead of you!?
The painting turns into a light that shoots into the doorway. We enter it.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Seeing past the false image has opened a path to the truth ...  Hm, this golden place filled with counterfeit work is a prime example of the alchemy of Madarame’s brain. And here, just as in reality, he entraps those who cannot see through his lying facade...

text.Morgana: You might be right ...  No wonder the distortion is so strong here.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, so ...  what does that mean?

text.Ann Takamaki: I think it means finding the real "Sayuri" should break through the distortion and open a path.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So do we just gotta check all of ‘em?

text.Ann Takamaki: Why would we do that ... ? Let’s just look for the real one ...  assuming we can differentiate it.

text.ACTION: From here, we can see all four paintings. Can you spot the correct one? I’ll give you a hint: It’s the third one. Thankfully, this is more spot-the-difference (the tree branch is missing) than rote memorization, because all the counterfeits here are the same.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes, this is the true "Sayuri." It may be an illusion, but there can be no mistaking its allure. Nicely done, Joker.

text.ACTION: And in the next hall, we see yet more obvious fakes. I say “obvious” because, well...
...the developers couldn’t be bothered to add new fakes, so all these are just repeats of the old forgeries. As such, they can be dismissed outright. However...

...with the last two, they get tricky. You’ll probably get it in a few seconds because I’ve helpfully screenshotted them both (and they’re both onscreen at the same time here), but in my first playthrough I was reduced to outright guessing, and even in this run it took me a number of minutes before I spotted the difference. I was looking at the kanji in the corner, at the fog patterns, at the budding flowers on the tree branch… It’s pretty embarrassing in retrospect.
If you somehow can’t figure it out: her hair is wrong in the first one. It’s supposed to go over her shoulder.
The light from the painting shoots off far below us.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh ... ? Where the shit did it fly off to!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We have seen all of the false images. Something must have changed somewhere...

text.ACTION: Walking into the nearby gateway will send us back to the start, but now a new gate is open.

text.Morgana: Just be careful, OK? The distortion is growing much stronger the deeper we go...

text.ACTION: From here, it’s just a straight shot back to the comparatively more “normal” museum.

text.Ann Takamaki: Then is the Treasure behind him?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s kinda hard to tell from here. Let’s get a close look!

text.ACTION: Music- Disquiet (This song plays for almost the entire rest of the Palace outside of battle)

text.Ann Takamaki: Doesn’t it look a bit hazy?

text.Morgana: For the time being. Once we send the card and make Madarame aware it’ll be stolen, it’ll materialize like "Yoohoo!"

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I wonder what form it will take...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Who knows? Bet it’s something like a self-portrait.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The source of what distorted Madarame’s reality this much...

text.Morgana: Hmm ...  We know where the Treasure is, but I’m not sure that we’ve necessarily secured the route...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Why’s that?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You must be talking about the infrared lasers surrounding it.

text.Morgana: That, and the outer perimeter is swarming with guards. Forcing our way through will be difficult.

text.Ann Takamaki: So we’ll need to find a way to steal it too ...  This is tougher than it was with Kamoshida ...

text.Morgana: We just have to make one final push. Let’s check this floor ... !

text.ACTION: We find the control room further in.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Nothing happened...
The heck? There was no point in even comin’ here then ... !

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm,. It seems disabling the infrared lasers is not within the realm of possibility for us...

text.Ann Takamaki: Let’s try the other ones too.

text.Shadow 2: I-I am not sure! It seems we have lost power ...  The backup generators should bring it up again in no time!

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: Hm ...  Could this also be ... ? Hey, someone!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Tch, it came back on pretty damn fast...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes, and the infrared lasers remained active even during the power outage.

text.Morgana: So we’ll only be able to turn the power off in there for a few seconds...

text.Ann Takamaki: Wait a second ...  Aren’t those guards that just ran out headed this way!? What else should we try? We might be in trouble if we don’t hurry...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All right!

text.Morgana: Now there are more places we can explore...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Crap, we got company!

text.ACTION: The encounter, while not quite a boss or a miniboss, consists of three Makami who like to spam Mafrei and Double Fangs and actually managed to kill me once (but there’s a safe room nearby, so whatever). It’s more annoying than difficult.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All we really managed to do was open the shutters ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: On top of that, we can only turn the lights off briefly, while the lasers remain unaffected.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh well ...  Guess we just gotta go see what’s past those shutters.

text.ACTION: A lot of the encounters on the way up this winding hall that circles the main room consist of Shiki-Ouji, better known as “that fucker who blocks Physical.” He still likes to pull the same old tricks, hitting you with Rage, boosting his Attack, and using Gun attacks, but now we have to deal with our dwindling SP resources on top of it all. Suffice it to say I ran from at least one of these encounters.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: No, it is most likely where all the mechanisms in the exhibition hall are controlled from. Given the number of hanging works, it would make sense to have a room dedicated to controlling them.

text.Ann Takamaki: The observational skills of an artist are out of this world...
Oh, look! There aren’t any lasers above it!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: This is quite a large hole in their security ...  but what do we do? Jump down to retrieve it?

text.ACTION: Not if you don’t want your legs to snap like twigs.

text.Morgana: We wouldn’t be able to get out if we did that though. Look up.
The controls should probably be around here somewhere. Let’s find them!
Hm, this could be useful...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Do you plan on descending on that hook? Would they not spot you the moment you were lowered down?

text.Morgana: No ...  Not necessarily. There’s something I can do to make sure that doesn’t happen.
Exactly! That’s our Joker!

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh right ...  We were able to turn the lights off over in that other control room!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Only for a few seconds though. There would not be enough time to make it all the way here.

text.Morgana: That’s why we’re going to split up the tasks and work together to pull off this heist! One person will shut the power off here, one person will lower the crane, and I’ll grab the Treasure!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You sure that’s gonna work? Seems to me like they’d realize what’s going on at some point.

text.ACTION: Smart thought, Ryuji, but basically, no one else has a better idea, so fuck it!

text.Morgana: Sometimes bold moves have the greatest payout. Unless someone has a better idea?
Well said, Joker! You understand what being a phantom thief really means!

text.ACTION: I’m actually not totally sure on what being a phantom thief really means. That archetype isn’t that much of a thing over here.

text.Morgana: All right, it’s settled. Our infiltration route is secured!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You gotta be kiddin’ me ...

text.ACTION: It amuses me that Ryuji is the only one with any objection to the genius plan of “let’s tie the cat to a rope and lower it like it’s fucking Looney Tunes.”

text.Morgana: Now then, it’s time for the calling card!

text.Joker: Return to the real world

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well, I’m still kinda worried ...  but we gotta do this.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I cannot even begin to fathom what Madarame’s Treasure may be ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Either way, we’ll steal it for sure. Oh, and you all did great today!

text.Morgana: We finally secured out route to the Treasure! All we need to do now is send the calling card.

text.Ann Takamaki: You’re right ...  And once we send it, the heist is the only thing left ...  We have to succeed ...  I’ll let you decide when we do it, Joker. Let’s make sure we’re ready before then!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All right, it’s finally time! Now all we gotta do is decide when we’re gonna do it.

text.Ann Takamaki: Shouldn’t we talk to Yusuke about that first?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uhhh, why?

text.Ann Takamaki: I mean, Madarame was his teacher.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, this problem’s bigger than just the three of us.

text.Ann Takamaki: Anyway, how about we all meet up at the hideout?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yup, sounds good.

text.Ann Takamaki: OK. Lemme know when you want to meet and I’ll tell Yusuke.

text.ACTION: This would have been handy in the Palace. Oh well.

text.Newscaster: With the recent economic slump, many companies are limiting their number of new hires. Popular companies are overwhelmed with applications, accepting applicants at very low rates.

text.Morgana: In their suits, everyone all looks the same. It must be tough to look for a job.

text.ACTION:
Part 38: 5/24-5/26: Coen-Level Criminal Idiocy
	Part 37: 5/24-5/26: Coen-Level Criminal Idiocy

text.Morgana: Ishikawa Goemon was a thief without peer. So he was a hero of the common people, huh?

text.ACTION: Halfway through that book for now.

text.Ichiko Ohya: I guess I’ll come back later. It’d be a problem if they called the police on me or something.

text.ACTION: Looks like this lady’s still trying to check up on the Phantom Thieves rumors.
Over in the Velvet Room, we can fuse a Shiisaa using Makami and Jack Frost.

text.Shiisaa: You have mask ...  You and me ...  Don’t worry, be happy!

text.ACTION: Somebody cut Meher Baba a check.
Anyway, Shiisaa is an Okinawan protective spirit.
Not only does it get Mabufu from Jack Frost and the Frei we needed from Makami, we also learn Rampage, which is Light Physical that hits 1-3 times. It’s very useful.

text.Caroline: Ooh, that’s ... !

text.Justine: I see you have brought us a Shiisaa with Frei.

text.Caroline: (chuckle) Very well ...  Your assignment’s done.
Hmph. I guess at least you’ve got the will to work.
Don’t gimme that smug attitude! This is your duty, Inmate!

text.Justine: That said, you have completed the task surprisingly easily.

text.Caroline: You might actually be worth our time after all. Justine, tell him his next task. It’s on that list, right?

text.Justine: Indeed ...  Now then, I will assign your next task. Be aware that the tasks on this list will increase in difficulty as we go. Are you prepared?
How admirable.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Caroline and Justine is growing deeper...

text.Justine: Once again, we would like to bestow a new privilege upon you ...  However, it is exceedingly powerful. We ask that you fulfill another task before receiving it.

text.Caroline: (snicker) Life isn’t gonna just hand you success!

text.Justine: Now, I will assign you your next task...

text.ACTION: Let’s back out and check on the new goodies Takemi has.
Takemi’s got a new section open for accessories now.

The Regen Patches give Regenerate 1, 2, and 3, which restore 2, 4, and 6 percent of HP each turn, respectively. But those are terrible and unimportant compared to the SP Adhesives, the third one in particular. The SP Adhesives give Invigorate 1, 2, and 3, which restore 3, 5, and 7 SP each turn, respectively. Not “percent.” 3, 5, and 7. While that may seem like a bummer, it’s really not. 7 SP a turn is massive for most of the game and having four of them on your party members can carry you through even the longest Palaces. Remember how I said Takemi’s accessories were “mandatory”? I meant it. This is the way you manage to clear the later Palaces in a day. There’s really no point in even bothering with 1 or 2, as that’s wasted money better spent elsewhere. Unfortunately, we can’t afford to buy an SP Adhesive 3 yet as it’s one of the most expensive items in the game, so we’re forced to wait.
Over at the diner, we order a Nostalgic Steak. Maaku gains Kindness +1 and Knowledge +2.
We finally get Rank 2 Knowledge, holy shit.

text.Pro Shogi Player: That must be such a difficult loss to accept. I wish we could let him have some time to himself ...

text.TV Interviewer: Well then ...  Let’s move on to the postmortem, where we analyze what happened in the game.

text.Sojiro Sakura: There is no mistaking it ...  This is Hawaiian Kona...
...The flavor profile is bland. You should practice more to bring out the roast’s full potential.

text.ACTION: Those words are going on my suicide note.

text.Makoto Niijima: It appears you’re lying low lately. What’s with the change?
Really ...  Is it just my imagination then?
Anyhow ...  I wish the culprit would come forward soon ...  It’s absurd to pretend I can do the police’s job ...  I wish he considered my feelings before asking me this.

text.ACTION: Maaku’s just standing there awkwardly listening to her complain to herself.

text.Joker: I want to do a clinical trial.

text.Tae Takemi: I’ve been really busy lately with all my new patients buuut ...  What the heck? Oh, everything’s set up already. Oh, that old lady from earlier forgot something ...  I wonder if she’s still outside ...
...It was right in front of me, so...

text.Kind Old Woman: Oh my! You’re a shy one, aren’t you?

text.Tae Takemi: (blushing)

text.Kind Old Woman: My neighbor speaks highly of you. She says your medicines are better than those at the big hospitals. It’s very reassuring to have such a distinguished doctor right here in town. I’ll see you again soon.

text.Tae Takemi: ...Thanks to you.

There’s a lot of talk going around town about me, started by that girl and her dad ...  Apparently, they’ve been telling everyone that I can make all these amazing medicines and remedies. So now the number of patients I’m seeing has increased dramatically. I don’t know what some of these people are thinking though. I’ve had a lot of crazy requests. Like, yesterday a patient requested a "sweet-smelling" compress. And the other day, I had a request for a "cold-buster." Ha! A drug like that deserves a Nobel Prize. Other requests have included hair and skin tonics ...  I even had to do a consultation about a cat ...  Sheesh. It’s not like I’m some kind of genius doctor.
This is all interfering with my development. I’m only interested in completing my new drug. That’s my role as the Plague. I’m not suited for all this other stuff.
What ... ? Really ... ?

But a "town doctor," huh ... ? That sort of lifestyle profession might’ve been possible for me at one time, but now ...   ...  ...  Oh yeah, about those clinical trials ...  With so many new patients, it’s taking longer to analyze the data, so I’ll need to catch up. This is a bit on the stronger side, but I’m sure you’ll be OK.

text.Joker: It feels like my bond with Takemi is growing even deeper...

text.Tae Takemi: It looks like that girl is going to make a full recovery. The treatment seems to be a good match for her. So at least I can breathe a little easier, for now. ...Hopefully she’ll be able to attend school soon.
Well then, let’s have some fun.

text.Joker: I feel like cooperating in that shady clinical trial has increased my Guts...

text.Tae Takemi: OK, thanks for your hard work.

text.ACTION: Ryuji finally contacted us on the Yamauchi situation.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You’ll go with me to help investigate undercover, right!?

text.Morgana: So, what’s it going to be? Will you listen to Ryuji’s request?

text.ACTION: For this rank of Ryuji’s Confidant, we have to participate in a special night event. These aren’t terribly frequent (by which I mean this may very well be the only one) and can only be done on specific dates. First things first though, our daily ritual must be upheld.

text.Newscaster: Scams are much more intricate now, and many young people have fallen victim to them. Police are working to protect people from scams, but struggle to come up with countermeasures.

text.Morgana: It sounds like more people have been getting scammed. I feel bad for people who fall for those.

text.ACTION: All right, now we can go.
And we got a new spot, where we can take people who enjoy… monjayaki. Sure, I know what that is.

ChaosArgate posted-
Monjayaki is a dish pretty similar to Okonomiyaki. For those who don't know what that is either, Okonomiyaki is sort of a grilled pancake made mostly of cabbage, batter, and whatever else the customer wants. This can include meat, like beef or pork, vegetables, like corn, or even potato chips. The batter in Okonomiyaki is pretty much just a binder to hold everything together while it cooks. Monja is similar; it's also cooked on a grill and made of mostly cabbage and batter, but there's more batter in Monja and it's a lot runnier. It's like a liquid Okonomiyaki and it has a consistency that's kinda like melted cheese. People also tend to eat it right off the grill with tiny spatulas, whereas people can just cut up and eat Okonomiyaki off their own plates with a fork or chopsticks or whatever.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Sorry, but I’m gonna be hiding in the bathroom.

text.ACTION: Ryuji is nothing if not dignified.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Please, Maaku! Just leave your phone on so I can hear what they’re saying.

text.Yamauchi: Mmm, I’ve had some experience. Back in my college days, we’d rent a yacht for the weekend and have massive parties. I must say though ...  the sake’s been tasting particularly sweet today.

text.Fellow Teacher: No surprise there. Things have been much calmer without Kamoshida. Those were some real dark times for Shujin though, huh? But now that he’s gone, you finally get the chance you deserve, Yamauchi!

text.Yamauchi: Don’t flatter me, haha. He had his strengths, sure ...  but because of him, our volleyball team will be forever scarred. The only real option now is to abandon it completely. There has to be a way to bring Shujin back into the limelight though. That’s where I come in...

text.Fellow Teacher: You mean with the track team, right?

text.Yamauchi: The students who went through so much hardship under Kamoshida rise again with a caring new advisor ...  It’ll be the rebirth of a team that found themselves in the depths of despair ...  The public will love it. Despite my lack of track and field knowledge, I’ll form a tight bond with the students ...  I’ll be the protagonist of my very own tear-jerker ...  And of course all the praise for reviving them will go to me, their incredible, loving advisor. I’ll have to hire a great coach if I want to pull this off though.

text.Fellow Teacher: So you’re gonna pretend to coach them while someone else does all the legwork? Amazing, Yamauchi!

text.Yamauchi: Such stunning achievements will look great when it’s time to hand out bonuses ...  But I’m not gonna stop there either ...  I’ll publish books, give motivational speeches...

text.ACTION: I’m noticing quite a few holes in this plan, such as “what if literally anyone catches on to the fact that you’re not actually coaching them.”

text.Fellow Teacher: What about all the troublemakers on the team? I’ve heard that Nakaoka kid is especially bad.

text.Yamauchi: Nakaoka ... ? Oh, you mean the one who asked them to bring the pre-Kamoshida coach back? Don’t worry, I’ve already taken care of him ...

There’s this other boy on the team ...  Takeishi. Doesn’t really excel in much of anything. Well, I said I would make him the new captain if he could get rid of that troublemaker Nakaoka. I might’ve mentioned something about how Nakaoka was working with Kamoshida too ...  ...Subtly, of course.
Apparently, Takeishi chased him away ...  The plan worked perfectly! And the best part is, not only are Takeishi’s parents loaded, but his mother’s the president of the PTA.

text.Fellow Teacher: I see ...  He’d make a great pawn!

text.Yamauchi: Perhaps, but a nothing like him could never captain a successful championship-winning team. He may have to have an unfortunate "accident" at practice one day.

text.ACTION: Look at this criminal fucking mastermind here, blabbing off about his plan to injure a minor in front of a random teenager.

text.Yamauchi: But until then, he can show the others the value of obedience.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So ...  they’re just gonna have to decide on their own. Y’know, track ain’t a team sport. At least, sprintin’ wasn’t.

You’ve got teammates, sure ...  but you’re really just lookin’ out for your own time. That’s why I never thought about askin’ people for help or tryin’ to solve our problems together. But ...  I can’t ignore the stuff they’re goin’ through now. I mean, even though we had our own goals n’ shit ...  We were still runnin’ together. They suffered with me, gritted their teeth with me ...  Honestly, I think it was only ‘cause of them I was able to run at all.
I know that ain’t the coolest thing to say, but it’s how I feel.
...For real? Thanks, man!

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Ryuji is growing deeper...

text.ACTION: Insta-kill is an odd ability. For starters, it only works on enemies substantially weaker than you, to the point where I’ve only very rarely seen it outside of Mementos floors I was way overpowered for. You don’t get experience or money from these skipped encounters, but if you have room in your Persona deck it’ll automatically give you a mask of one of the Shadows you would have encountered. If you don’t have room, you can’t even choose to throw an old mask away, you just get nothing. This means that if you’re fishing for a specific Persona, you have to keep throwing old ones away from the menu. All in all, it’s honestly kind of pointless beyond speeding up travel through old Mementos floors and trying to get Personas you’re so overpowered you’ll kill in one hit.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Anyways, I’m starvin’! Let’s eat some monja while we’re here. Right now all I’ve seen of this place is the goddamn toilet! Thanks for hangin’ with me, man.

text.ACTION: I spent an awful amount of time trying to spin a Rick and Morty reference out of this before I gave up. This space is instead dedicated to how much I suck for attempting to make such a boring, tired joke in the first place.

text.Young Office Worker: That parliamentarian from when I was a kid ...  Toranosuke something.

text.Glasses-wearing worker: He hangs out at train stations giving speeches these days, but no one pays him any mind. He used to be a rising star in politics, but wound up involved in scandal after scandal.

text.Young Office Worker: Huh ...  Yeah, I saw him in line for food. It was weird seeing a politician eating at the same place as we do.

text.Glasses-wearing worker: Well, that’s probably his new gimmick, right? Pandering to middle-class people.

text.ACTION: Man, poor Tora. People are even doubting his motives.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Don’t think you can get away with copying stuff from some website. I’ll know. Got it? Stealing someone’s ideas is plagiarism. It’s as much of a crime as stealing anything else. It’s so annoying dealing with copyright crap these days ...  Oh yeah, did you know this? So, you know how Sir Arthur Conan Doyle has the famous character Sherlock Holmes? One time, another author used Holmes in his own story without permission, and Doyle protested. Now then ...  Hamiru-kun. What was the name of the other famous novel that Sherlock Holmes appeared in?

Oh, do you like mystery novels? You’re right. It’s the ultimate showdown between the gentleman thief and the famous detective. But afterward, Maurice Leblanc—the author of the Lupin series—changed Sherlock’s name in his books. He changed it to "Herlock Sholmes." He just moved the S to the start of his last name.

text.ACTION: That’s the kind of hilarious dick move that I can totally get behind.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Both Lupin and Holmes would go on to appear in a number of other works ...  But those were homages, not plagiarism. Now, Arsene Lupin is synonymous with the idea of a "phantom thief." He’s recognized all over the world.

text.Morgana: Wow, it looks like some phantom thieves never go out of style!

text.Morgana: Madarame’s going to be a changed man. There won’t be any way to revert it though. Are you sure you’re OK with that?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I have thought it over carefully, and I cannot think of a future in which he does not pay his dues. He has preyed not only on the art world, but on countless talents ...  so I humbly request your help.
I apologize for making you do this...

text.Ann Takamaki: Not at all. We just didn’t want to impose if you weren’t feeling up to it, Yusuke. But if you’re already determined to do it, then there’s nothing more for us to say.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: If I recall, our next step is sending a "calling card," correct? What a suave maneuver.

text.Morgana: It’s not about acting cool. The calling card is a way to trigger a change in his cognition.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: A change in cognition ...  That reminds me, you went through some trouble regarding that before ...

text.ACTION: I thought we weren’t talking about that.

text.Morgana: Ah, you must be talking about when we forced open that security gate in the courtyard.

text.Ann Takamaki: The Palace is a cognitive world, so changing its ruler’s cognition changes the topography! ...I think!

text.Morgana: Very nicely put, Lady Ann! You’re absolutely correct. This will be a vital tactic from here forward.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Actually, may I ask a truly basic question? You continue to mention cognition quite readily ...  But why does this world formed from materialized cognitions even exist to begin with? Don’t tell me ...  Has it always existed, while we go about our daily lives completely oblivious?

text.Morgana: Honestly, I’m not sure. At the very least, I know it existed before the Kamoshida incident ...  but that’s all.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I see ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Crap, he totally caught me off guard with that ...  It’s kinda weird thinkin’ there might be whole worlds we just don’t know a damn thing about ...  ...Did the thought ever cross your mind, Maaku?

text.ACTION: Other worlds? You watch too much television, Ryuji.

text.Morgana: Don’t be so anxious. You don’t even know everything about the city you live in, after all. All that’s important is that we know how to make use of that world and how to traverse it.

text.ACTION: So, with that philosophical quandary neatly packed away, time to discuss the order of the day: the calling card.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: He is famous, after all ...  He has often received slanderous letters till now, as well.

text.Morgana: Wait. Are you going to write it again, Ryuji? That last one was questionable at best.

text.Ann Takamaki: You should do it then, Yusuke! Make it really artistic and stuff!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: No. It’ll end with him figuring it out. He knows my drawing and writing styles all too well.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh, then I’ll think it up, and you make it cooler!

text.ACTION: The final result of Ryuji’s directive can be seen here:
This is absolutely the worst, most terrible, awful joke I will ever make in the entirety of my blighted existence, and you know what? I’m not fucking sorry.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Designing a calling card, hm ...  Interesting. It shall become proof that the Phantom Thieves do exist.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s decided then!

text.Morgana: You guys better come fully prepared!

text.Ann Takamaki: Looks the same to me.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Maybe it’s just for the group and doesn’t show up in here ...  Well, you should take a look later. It’s that Phantom Thieves logo I had Yusuke draw for us. The calling card turned out great ‘cause of him too. Anyways, this is the first job for the Phantom Thieves. We really can’t screw this up, k?

text.Ann Takamaki: I know.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: And make sure Yusuke gets a lot of rest today, OK?

text.ACTION: I’m not sure how he wants us to make sure of that, but whatever.

text.Ann Takamaki: See you tomorrow!

text.ACTION: This is the new logo Ryuji mentioned, for the record.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Nothing goes your way in life. You’ll end up failing if you tense up like that.

text.ACTION: I missed it last time, but Sojiro has this unique bit of dialogue on the night you send the calling card. Thanks for the advice, Fake Dad.

text.Game Show Host: Confessions of crime are the ...  A: "queen" of evidence/B: "jewel" of evidence/Which one is right? You be the judge!

text.ACTION: I don’t feel like either I’ve heard either of these, but I’ll pick the one that sounds more natural.

text.Boy on Game Show: The correct answer is A, "queen." Yes, that’s a very famous expression in the field of law. Confessions are very powerful evidence—people used to even resort to torture to get them.

text.ACTION: Okay, we get it, Mr. Know-it-all.

text.Lawyer on Game Show: That’s a high school prodigy for you. Today, forcing a confession is forbidden under law, and...

text.Morgana: I’m surprised you knew that. Did you just guess? Torture, though ...  That’s pretty brutal.

text.ACTION: We make three Lockpicks (thanks to our Proficiency now being Rank 2) and gain Proficiency +2, which I admittedly tried to savescum for a better result and gave up on.

text.Ichiryusai Madarame: Please excuse me for a moment.
A letter?

text.Exhibit Staff: You are an artist who uses his authority to shamelessly steal the ideas of his pupils. We have decided to make you confess all your crimes with your own mouth. We will take your distorted desires without fail. From, #Millennials ...

text.ACTION: There we have it, his sin is vanity. Not greed or envy, vanity. Though, this game likes to play a little fast and loose with the sins.

text.Exhibit Staff: We don’t know! The same letter has been posted everywhere ...

text.Ichiryusai Madarame: What about the security cameras!?

...What now!?

text.Morgana: The Treasure should appear right about now.

text.Morgana: That’s right. Are you ready, Joker?

text.ACTION: Panther emerges from behind a plant.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You seem to be enjoying this.

text.Morgana: Only the best can appreciate these critical moments. Plus, this feels like we’re really phantom thieves!

text.ACTION: We are really phantom thieves, though.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We’ll be counting on you, Mona. And Panther as well.

text.Ann Takamaki: Good luck, everyone! Let’s do this ... !
Wait, where’s Mona?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That was amazin’, Mona!

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: Ngh ...  How dare those vermin ...  But now we’ll corner them like the rats they are! Lock all the doors at once! They have nowhere to run!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We can look into that later. For now, we must escape.

text.Morgana: Yeah, it’s time to go!

text.ACTION: Fun detail here- for the brief time between now and the end of the Palace Mona has the painting tied to his head.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Now is no time to be lost in thought. We must go!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whoa, this shit’s real high up...

text.Morgana: But at least we’re outside! Is there a way down out here!?
We don’t have time to lose. Just go through it! Now’s our chance!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real!? But ...  I guess there’s no other way!

text.Morgana: I knew it! All that security would’ve been meaningless if it just led back inside!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It seems we managed to escape their siege.

text.Morgana: Mrrrr ...  Meowww...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude ...  Why’s Mona gettin’ excited now of all times ... ?

text.Morgana: I just can’t take it any more! Let’s take a look at this Treasure ... !
Hrm!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: THIS is the Treasure!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Get back!

text.ACTION: The characters all leap eight feet backwards.

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: Is this what you’re looking for?

text.ACTION: Wait, you… brought it with you? Why?

text.Morgana: What nonsense that you used a mousetrap on me!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So you had a fake prepped, huh!?

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: Counterfeits are accepted in the world of Japanese art.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What made you change like this!? Is it because you became famous!? Can’t you understand how much it pains me to inquire about the crimes of my foster father!?

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: ...Now that I think back, the only reason why I took you in was due to my ties with your mother. That woman never lost her passion for painting even after her husband died. Her skills and talents were quite astonishing ...  That’s why I decided to look after her.

text.Ann Takamaki: How low can you sink ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Genuine ... ?
That’s ...  the real "Sayuri" ... ? This can’t be ... !

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh!?

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: Indeed it is. This was painted by your mother. It’s a portrait of herself. A woman who knew her death was coming painted her last wishes, for the son she would leave behind. That is the truth behind the mystery of "Sayuri"’s expression!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You stole something THAT personal ... !?

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: I knew at first glance. I knew it’d be a huge success, if I added a touch to the painting and announced it under my name!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: But the baby in the picture ...  Why did you paint over it ... ?

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: ...It was all to stage it. If the babe is erased, the reason for the woman’s expression will become a mystery ... !

text.ACTION: This just makes it more hilarious that people thought it was so great in the first place. “Yeah, there’s this big ugly fog over a third of the painting, but I can’t tell why she’s smiling. It’s a masterpiece!”

text.Ann Takamaki: I always felt something was off about all this ...  Now I know what it is. If you really treasured that painting, you wouldn’t even think about replicating it for profit! You don’t love art at all!

text.Morgana: Though you have a real Treasure, your true skills are nothing more than those scribbles on that fake!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It makes me laugh, asshole!

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: So you’ll defy me no matter what ... Well then, since you’re my work of art, Yusuke, I’m going to reap you for the sake of my future. ...Along with those insolent friends of yours there.

text.Ann Takamaki: I can’t believe you’re treating both mother and son like they’re objects ...  You’re inhuman!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’ve heard that you destroy your "art" once they outlive their usefulness ...  ...Did that include my mother as well?

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: She just so happened to have a seizure in front of me. That’s when a thought crossed my mind ...  If I don’t call for help and leave her be, I could obtain her painting without any strings attached.

text.Ann Takamaki: No ...  You let her die!?

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: She was physically weak. No one would doubt if she just dropped dead because of a seizure. Above all, Yusuke, didn’t you think it was odd—that I discovered your talent when you were only three? The reason why I kept you around was to keep you from realizing the truth behind "Sayuri."

text.ACTION: I’m not quite sure I understand this. He kept Yusuke around… so he wouldn’t recognize his mother as Sayuri… by exposing him to it constantly? I guess it almost makes a twisted kind of sense if you squint real hard.

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: The artistic talents you inherited from your mother were a delightful miscalculation, though. If I’m to steal ideas, it’s much easier robbing the future of brats who won’t talk back than adults. It’s thanks to you that I came up with the idea. You have my gratitude.

text.Ann Takamaki: Yusuke ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Every reason for me to forgive you has disappeared without a trace at this very moment! You aren’t some rotten artist ...  You’re a despicable fiend who wears the skin of an artist!

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: All you good-for-nothings ... ! Barging into my museum and doing whatever the hell you want ...  Those who have the connections make the rules; those who don’t, follow them. Not to mention, the value of art is all subjective! I make the rules in the art scene! I am the supreme being! I am the god of the art world!

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: There is a world the mediocre cannot understand!

text.ACTION: This is The Painter’s Face, and he’ll be our boss for this evening. If you don’t know what you’re doing this can be a bit of a trial but it’s honestly pretty simple.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You aren’t even worth the art you "create" ... !

text.ACTION: So, for this fight, we’ll be using just the Shiisaa we fused recently, as it knows a lot of good Physical skills like Double Fangs and Rampage, as well as resist Physical itself. Eventually we’re gonna have to make a good healing Persona, but between Morgana and the Takemedic-All Vs (100 HP to every party member) we got from Takemi, today is not that day.

Each part of the face is a different target with a different HP bar. Unfortunately, they also each have different elemental affinities, as can be seen here. The mouth absorbs Physical and is vulnerable to magic, and vice versa for the eyes. The nose absorbs nothing, because it sucks.

Another annoying aspect of them each being separate is that they each get their own turn. The eyes go first, in between some of our party members, followed by the nose and mouth when the cycle completes. The Right Eye (our left) uses single-target Fire, Electricity, and Ice attacks, while the Left Eye uses Tarukaja on the mouth and Rakunda on the party. Not bringing a Persona with buffs or Ann’s Dekaja, and the fact that we haven’t even seen a Persona with Dekunda (neutralizes debuffs on the party), all compound to make this rather annoying to keep up with, especially if it targets Morgana, who’s rather squishy.
The nose uses single-target Wind attacks or will start twitching, meaning we should focus it down.

If we fail to take it down quickly (it doesn’t have a ton of health, unlike the mouth), it’ll use Dust Flurry, a multi-target Wind attack. This is really only dangerous for Ryuji, but it’s good to not have to experience it at all. You’ll probably figure out that you should take it down naturally. In fact, I had to film another take where I intentionally let it happen so I could find out what happens and get those two screenshots.
For its part, the mouth does nothing but bite. This is your body on Resist Physical.

This is your body on “being the squishy mage on the receiving end of both Rakunda and the enemy’s Tarukaja.” It’s not pretty. Remember that Dia only heals about 50-60 HP and you’ll see where the problem is and why we need those Takemedics.
It takes a bit of time to down all the parts. I generally always ended up saving the mouth for last because Rampage hits three out of the four parts and magic does less than multi-hit Physical.

Anyway, once you do manage to get them all down, the face retreats, and the true boss emerges, Madarame, or as this form is really known, Azazel. Unlike with Asmodeus, Azazel has nothing to do with any corresponding sin, instead being associated with the scapegoat rite from Leviticus, or alternately the name for a fallen angel.

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: The Madarame who gathers a full crowd every time he opens an exhibit! I’m not someone that worthless brats like you are allowed to defy ... !

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You still have the nerve to say such things!? You will fully taste the wrath of those who were preyed upon by you!

text.ACTION: On his turn, Azazel will use (heh) “Madara-Megido,” a trivially weak attack that does 10 damage to every party member. Our job is just to hit him with all we have at this stage.
After two turns, Azazel will retreat.
And, of course, the painting comes back.

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: It seems you need a good whipping to make you understand!

text.ACTION: The parts respawn with less than full health, which is nice, but the face has some new tricks up its sleeve.
The Right Eye can now cast The Artist’s Grace.
The afflicted party member becomes covered with paint and weak to everything.

text.Morgana: There has to be more than just our color changing! We should be cautious!

text.ACTION: The only thing to do when it happens is just guard and pray for the best.
Unfortunately for us, the nose can now also Dust Flurry whenever it wants.
The paint wears off in two turns, thankfully.

text.Morgana: Dammit ...  Those things can come back if we don’t take them down at once!?

text.ACTION: But just in case there wasn’t enough bad news, the first time we knock down one of the parts, one of the others will immediately use Restore to bring it back up. From now on, we have to make sure we don’t leave a lot of time in between destroying each part or they’ll bring each other back, albeit with a paltry amount of health.

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: Stop it, you brats, or else ... !

text.ACTION: Now, it’s actually very easily possible to take Azazel down in two cycles, but there’s a bit more fight to show off if we hold back.

text.Morgana: ...  ... ! Isn’t that the same thing Madarame’s been using? Let’s try covering him with paint!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Time to bestow the humiliation of being painted over to him ... !

text.ACTION: There’s really only one choice here.
Two turns of holding off the face later...

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: Wh-What the ... !? My powers ...  They’re suddenly draining...

text.ACTION: We make short work of the painting after that.

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: Even if you cry for help someday ...  you’ll regret this ...  No adult will help you...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I hope you’re prepared to go down, Madarame!

text.ACTION: From there, it’s a simple matter to finish him off.
Ryuji learns Rampage (1-3 Light Physical strikes to all enemies), which would have been amazing to have during that fight.

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: No one cares for true art ...  All they want are easily recognizable brands ... !

text.ACTION: Take it up with Andy Warhol.

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: I’m a victim in this too ... ! Wouldn’t you agree!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Excuses now ... ?

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: The art world revolves around money after all ...  You can’t rise up without any money ...  Yusuke, you understand, don’t you!? Being a poor artist is truly miserable ... !

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You’re done for, along with this abominous world!

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: (shriek) No, please! Just ...  don’t kill me ... !

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Return to yourself in reality and confess your crimes—all of them!

text.Shadow Ichiryusai Madarame: Y-You’re not going to kill me ... ?
(shriek) All right ...  All right! Wh-What about the other one though? The one with the black mask?

text.Ann Takamaki: A black mask? Wait, who’s he talking about ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: There’s no time! Hurry!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...Put an end to all this and use your own artwork for once.

text.Ann Takamaki: Yusuke!

text.Morgana: It would be bad if people started getting suspicious of us. We should leave at once.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yusuke, c’mon.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Right...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ugh, so bitter ...  Why’d you get it black?
You’re not gonna get all teary-eyed and say stuff like "Mom ... !" are you?

text.ACTION: Ryuji is kind of a dick.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: To think that this painting was the source of Madarame’s distorted desires. The only saving grace is that my mother won’t know of what transpired ...

text.Morgana: The genuine painting at his atelier has been altered, after all ...  Ironic as it may be, this one here is her true self-portrait now.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...It’s a wonderful painting. And ...  although it took some time, it’s in your hands now, Yusuke.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...I’m thankful for it. However, it’s impossible for this painting to be acknowledged by society anymore...

You may be right ...  Seeing my mother’s expression here, it’s doubtful that she would’ve wished for fame. So this is my mother ...  There’s no way that I would remember her face clearly ...  But I was right about the rush of emotion I felt when I saw this painting.

text.ACTION: Ryuji gets up and returns chugging a drink.

text.Ann Takamaki: Stop that!

text.Morgana: You’re so vulgar, Ryuji.

text.ACTION: I have no idea what the point of that was.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So, what’re you gonna do now? We’re gonna keep targetin’ big shots.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...Why do you do such things?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s to get back at scumbags and like ...  society in general?
We also wanna give courage to the people that’re sufferin’ ‘cause of selfish adults.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Courage, hm ...  What good does that do? You mean the courage to stand up for themselves, correct? Will acquiring that make them happy?

text.ACTION: Jeez, we just kind of assumed it would, I dunno.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...Yeah. There’s no knowin’ whether it’ll turn out good for everyone or not. Still, we won’t know unless we give it a try.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...In other words, it all depends on the person, hm? Then the same can be said about myself right now. I also suffered because of an adult’s selfish act. Moreover, if we investigate these Palaces, it may expand my artistic repertoire.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You really only think about art, huh? You’re impressive.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Well I won’t take part in any inelegant plans, all right?

text.Ann Takamaki: Plus, we have a rule that says we always have to decide on a target unanimously.

text.Morgana: How about it, Joker? We can give our calling cards a lot more oomph if we have Yusuke on our team.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I will try and live up to those expectations.

text.Morgana: At any rate, I’m curious ...  Another intruder besides us, huh?

text.Ann Takamaki: Our only clue’s a black mask, so that doesn’t necessarily mean it’s just one person, right?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But there’s no way to check anymore. The Palace is gone.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’ll try probing Madarame. I may be able to learn something from him.

text.Ann Takamaki: Are you sure? I mean--

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’ll contact you all if anything turns up.

text.Ann Takamaki: We should probably exchange our contact info with you then.

text.ACTION: We haven’t done that yet? How were we contacting him in the first place?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: An artist and a phantom thief ...  It seems I’ll be engaging in two trades from here on ...  Very well. You only live once, after all. Still, the incident about this other intruder does concern me a little...

text.Morgana: Goodness, things are going so well!

Hehe ...  Could the day our name becomes common knowledge be nigh? But I have to say, you sure are something special. This is our fifth Persona-user. It’ll help broaden our battle strategies as well. Besides, having an eye for beauty is a must for phantom thieves. We’re lucky to have Yusuke. An artist is a talent you rarely come across. I mean, he IS a bit strange, but still ...  An artist, huh ...  What kind of person do you think I was? There’s no way I’d turn out to be some bad guy in the end, right? I get so engrossed with the embodiment of human desires ...  And that’s not all. When it comes to the Metaverse, I’m the only one who can transform into a car ...  I’m special ...  but it’s still odd. Who could I actually be ... ?

Will you give it a rest!? That’s definitely not the case! (sigh) What a half-assed answer. Well, there’s no way someone like me, who has honorable aspirations, can be evil. A man who saves those in trouble in the west, while punishing evildoers who may lurk in the east! A man who chastises people that smoke inside in the south, while saving bullied cats in the north. A man who has a sturdy body and vows to always do one good deed a day, be it rain or shine.
I’m that kind of ideal person. ...Or so I hope. So if I turn back to being human ...  surely she’ll take notice of me, won’t she?

Me!? Don’t be ridiculous! People chase after me when it comes to love! Where should I go when I become human ... ? I wonder where she’d like to go ...  An amusement park, a movie theater, a fancy cafe, shopping ...  What do you think?

text.ACTION: Morgana’s follow-up is crazy, for the record. I’ll see if I can’t show it off sometime soon.

text.Ann Takamaki: We all did our best.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Allow me to express my thanks once again. Because of you, I was able to retrieve the painting that had been filled with my mother’s love.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hearing you say that makes the whole thing worth it, Yusuke!

text.Ann Takamaki: Seriously. I wasn’t sure you’d really want to change Madarame’s heart.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah. We did it just like with Kamoshida.

text.Ann Takamaki: By the way, I’m curious about what he said at the end.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You mean about the other intruder besides us? IT was something about a black mask, yeah?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That may have been nothing more than a lie. Madarame was quite deranged at that point, after all. For now, we should wait for his change of heart in peace.

text.Ann Takamaki: OK.

text.Igor: However, that man’s remarks are concerning. It seems another has made their way into the Metaverse.
That is beyond my knowledge ...  But your rehabilitation is progressing smoothly. ...That is for certain. May the devotion to your rehabilitation grow even deeper. ...I have high hopes of you.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Igor is growing deeper...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’m calling about Madarame’s state. For the time being, he hasn’t suffered a mental shutdown. Other than that, his demeanor seems to have softened a bit. Is that ...  the change of heart?

I see ...  I was curious and looked into Kamoshida as well. It’s as if he was an entirely different person. Will the same be true for Sensei ... ? ...I’m sorry to have taken your time. That’s all I wanted to tell you. Good-- Oh. I’ll try asking him about the black-masked intruder from the Palace when the time is right. Goodbye then. This time for sure.

text.Morgana: Why don’t you try drawing the Phantom Thieves logo? I bet it would look really cool!
That’s the spirit!

text.Chatter: Prolly some kinda prank by those "phantom thieves" or whatever ...  Did he draw this? Who’s he trying to impress ... ? Wait, does he seriously think they exist? That’s kinda embarrassing...

text.Morgana: They’re just treating us like some kinda joke ...  Nobody believes in our existence ...  This is a good way to tell how popular we are. You should try drawing it again some other time.

text.ACTION: If the literal meter wasn’t enough for you, another barometer for your prowess as the Phantom Thieves is drawing on the class blackboard, which leads to your classmates viciously mocking you. We can check back after different events in the story and the reaction will change, so we’ll make them eat crow later. Hopefully.

text.Newspaper Club Member: That’s true, but ...  I’m going to write about it so that the same thing won’t happen again!
But maybe I should’ve covered that artist, Madarame, instead. Everyone’s talking about him...

text.Veteran Pick-Up Artist: It’s all part of the process. Success will come, but only after you fail again and again. It’s like they said on Madarame’s show. The big shots at the top all started as beginners.

text.Novice Pick-Up Artist: I think I get it ...  I’m starting to feel like I can do this!

text.ACTION: At least they nailed the core defining feature of pickup artists being terrible at actually getting laid. I keep checking up on these guys because it’s fascinating to me that they chose to put PUAs in their game and have them seem mostly normal. I’m not even like, complaining. It’s just weird.

text.Tae Takemi: Could you head to the back?

text.Joker: Hang out with her

text.Tae Takemi: It’s thanks to you that I was able to progress this far. Now you can drink this stuff with no problem, right?
Oh, are you going home already? If you have some time, why don’t you stay and enjoy an apple?

text.ACTION: If an apple a day keeps the doctor away, being offered one by your doctor means they probably can’t stand you, right?

text.Tae Takemi: It’s a gift from one of my elderly patients. She gave me a lot.

text.Doctor: There was a medical conference nearby, so I thought I’d check up on you. Who’s this? He doesn’t look like a patient.

text.Tae Takemi: He’s a part-time staffer. I’m having him handle some miscellaneous tasks for me. So, do you have some business with me?

text.Doctor: ...I hear you stole one of my patients. A girl with bronchitis. She came here with her father...

text.Tae Takemi: ...Bronchitis, you say? Well, I had no intention of taking her from you. I certainly didn’t encourage her to visit my clinic.

text.Doctor: Now there’s talk that the care at a university hospital is inferior to that of a general practitioner! "Original medicine." Ha! What you’re doing here is simply absurd!

text.Tae Takemi: ...You’re right.

text.Doctor: I would’ve turned a blind eye if you had just rotted away out here in this little town ...  But this is your final warning ...  Shut this place down and resign your medical license.

Hmph, you seem to be quite fond of her. Perhaps I should reveal this woman’s true identity. She’s a monster who tortured a patient with her unregulated medicine! Terrible, isn’t it? She was such a brave girl, always smiling...

text.Tae Takemi: What ... !?

text.Doctor: Perhaps you’ll suffer the same fate, hm? Hahaha ...  She is the Plague, after all.

text.Tae Takemi: She was slowly recovering ...  Her condition couldn’t have deteriorated that quickly!

text.Doctor: But it did. You must’ve misjudged. Now, back to the reason I’m here. Don’t ever take another patient away from me again. ...You don’t want to make me angry.

text.Tae Takemi: No, no no ...  But she’s all I’ve been working toward, all this time ...  Curing her was my only ...  There’s no way...
...  ...  What have I been doing all this time ... ? What was even the point ... ? I can’t...
Yeah, you’re right ...  I feel better now ...  Thanks for your help, my little guinea pig ...

text.Joker: It feels like my bond with Takemi is growing even deeper...

text.ACTION: Discount is great. Not only does it work on everything in the clinic, but it reduces prices by a whopping fifty percent. It’s what we’ve been blitzing through Takemi’s Confidant for, because it makes getting four SP Adhesive 3s much, much easier.

text.Tae Takemi: Ugh. I wish I hadn’t shown you that side of me...
Go on home for today. ...We will continue this another time.

text.Joker: I feel like cooperating in that shady clinical trial has increased my Guts...

text.Tae Takemi: Take care...

We can still do it, but he won’t be there and we won’t get points with him, which was half the reason we were doing it in the first place. Note that also, we’re still not even near close enough to rank up with him, because Rank 3 to Rank 4 takes an absurd amount of points.

It’s just Batman voice: I am nothing like you. You’re a psychopath who bakes for money!

text.Souse: S’fine. I gets shtronger the more I drrrink. Let ‘em try n’ fight me. I’ll deshtroy ‘em. (retch)

text.Toranosuke Yoshida: I feel more confident when you’re around.

text.Joker: Help him out

text.Toranosuke Yoshida: Well then, let’s get started.

To make your decisions based simply on loss and gain is to act like a heartless machine. The reason so few people care about their fellow man is because so few have the energy to do so. We politicians have fallen short of our goal to change society. We need your support more than ever!

text.Matsushita: You’re going to completely lose the hearts and minds of the people.

text.Toranosuke Yoshida: Again, what I’d like to say is--

text.Matsushita: Do you know about the Kuramoto Children?

That was nearly 20 years ago. I’m impressed that you’re so interested in politics. I was a member of the Kuramoto Children as well. Yoshida and I joined the same year. I made an amazing career change, going from a pro wrestler to a Diet member.

text.ACTION: You know, I might’ve guessed that, just because you’re still goddamn huge.

text.Matsushita: I was elected easily, but I had no idea what I was doing. I realized I wasn’t elected on my own merit when I failed to be re-elected for a second term. That was true for the both of us.

text.Toranosuke Yoshida: You made a great comeback, though. You’re truly an inspiration.

text.Matsushita: As are you, old friend. You’re working harder than anyone on the campaign trail.

text.Toranosuke Yoshida: Oh, there’s no need for false praise to impress the boy here.

text.Matsushita: Yoshida’s well-informed about the inner workings of politics, so I’m sure he’ll be a great teacher. However, I suggest you only do as he says and not as he does, if you want to become a Diet member.

text.ACTION: I assume he means YOU STOLE ALL THAT MONEY AND ACTED LIKE A DUMBASS

text.Matsushita: I’m guessing he doesn’t know ... ?
You really think you can win the election by being completely honest and making good arguments? You’ve got to secure votes! Or else you’ll be forever known as No-Good Tora!
Heh ...  It’s been a while since I’ve heard one of your grandiose speeches.
Hamiru-kun, was it? Tell me, what about Yoshida here drew you in?
You address matters quite directly for a young person. It seems you have been taught well.

text.Toranosuke Yoshida: I intend to teach him everything I know. That’s what we agreed on.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Yoshida is growing deeper...

text.ACTION: This is the skill that, ironically, has a chance to ruin longer fundraising efforts. You’ll get more money than normal if it procs, but that proc instantly ends the battle, meaning you can’t ask again.

text.Matsushita: By the way, how are things between you and old man Kuramoto?

text.Toranosuke Yoshida: We’re still not on speaking terms.

text.Matsushita: There’s something I’d like to get your opinion on, so I’ll be in touch.

text.Toranosuke Yoshida: Very well.

text.Matsushita: You may still distrust me because of what happened with the missing party funds ...  But I’m not the one who pointed the finger at you. That’s all I’m going to say.

text.Morgana: So, you’ve finished reading The Gallant Rogue. That splendid spirit that pays no mind to the bad guys ...  He’s a true example of a gentleman thief. After reading this, I’m sure you have a better understanding of a chivalrous thief’s courage.

text.ACTION: And we get another rank up.

text.Inui: I can’t go sea fishing because I get seasick easily. So much for my dream of being a sailor. Oh right. When people think of sailing the high seas, they tend to think of pirates. Even though they’re ruffians who plunder other ships and coastal settlements through force ...  For some reason, they ended up getting romanticized. Now then, Hamiru-kun. Who was the pirate who said that he hid his treasure in a certain place just before he was executed?

text.ACTION: Pshh, this was part of my Persona trivia like 30 updates ago.

text.Inui: That’s right. The answer is William Kidd, also known as Captain Kidd. Kidd was a merchant who had raised money from aristocrats. He should have been subduing pirates ...  ...But in order to turn his commission into a profit, he ended up becoming a pirate himself.

The money he used for his exploits was essentially the aristocracy’s. He himself wasn’t considered rich. Still, several novels were written based on his legend, and people still look for his treasure today. By the way, I’ve heard that there’s an island in Kyushu where Kidd’s treasure is said to sleep ...

text.Morgana: Kidd’s secret treasure, huh ...  Regardless of its actual worth, there’s still value in letting that many people dream about it.

text.ACTION: Yeah, dream it. Don’t give it up.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I need your help with something ...  I found this flyer stuffed in my mailbox.
"Housekeeping Service"! It says that a cute maid will do anything for you! A maid, dude! A MAID! Who’ll do ANYTHING for us! Right? ...Right!?

text.ACTION: Oh god, it’s time for Horny Ryuji. Well, at least it’s no Horny Yosuke, the worst character in Persona 4.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...You’re a guy, right? You know what I mean! Let’s give it a try. Yeah? Yeah!

Luckily, some guy on my floor just moved out so there’s a vacant apartment in my complex. The key is behind the mailbox, so we can get in anytime. The landlord seriously doesn’t care. The place is all set, so...

text.Yuuki Mishima: Um, can I, uh ...  ...Get in on this?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh-ho! You mean you’re into this kinda stuff? Wow! Okaaay ...

text.Yuuki Mishima: I-I’m not into it! It’s just for research!

text.ACTION: “I’m just writing a trashy novel about sex workers, I promise!”

text.Yuuki Mishima: What does it mean that they’ll do "anything"? And do the maids look exactly as they’re advertised? We need to determine whether or not this company just pretends to offer housekeeping services!
I-I ...  ...Just want to punish the bad guys! And in order to do that, I have to see it with my own eyes!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, we gotta see it with our own eyes. Every little detail ...  (snicker) We’ll have to do this at night, so let us know when you’re ready.

text.Yuuki Mishima: So what’s the code name for this operation ... ? Hmmm ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Nice! I like that!

text.ACTION: With that nonsense out of the way, it’s time for other things.
First, let’s trade in The Gallant Rogue for The Great Thief at the library.
We also go to the diner. Maaku gains Kindness +1 from the Nostalgic Steak and Knowledge +3 from studying due to the rain.

text.Yuuki Mishima: You know, about that flyer! We need to look into the truth behind that housekeeping service. I’m over at Central Street right now, so come talk to me if you’re interested.

text.Morgana: Looks like Mishima’s waiting for us in Shibuya. Do you think we should go see him?

text.Joker: Decide later

text.ACTION: We have other plans. But first…

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...Another box came for you.

text.ACTION: These Wild Clogs give Resist Fear. We probably won’t ever equip them.

text.Newscaster: He’s received even more praise for his dynamic art style. Requests for commissions are flooding in.

text.Morgana: It seems that even people outside of Japan love him too. I don’t really get art ...

text.ACTION: What happened to you being such a cultured phantom thief?
Since it’s Monday and we haven’t been in a while, we go to the baths. Maaku gains Charm +3.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: By the way, the exhibit’s ‘til the end of this week, huh ...  We did what we could, and now we wait for the results.
Nope. That’s one option that’s a definite "no." School’s enough for studyin’. Let’s exercise, man!

text.ACTION: Let’s hang out with Ann today.

text.Ann Takamaki: Strengthening my heart is turning out to be harder than I thought ...  Do you think we can maybe talk some more about it?

text.Joker: Hang out with her

text.Ann Takamaki: Then let’s head back to Inokashira Park. We can talk there.

This place seriously feels amazing. It’s not even that far from Shibuya, but it feels so different here. You know, Tokyo is so strange. There are tons of people and tons of stores, yet there are still duck-filled parks here too. It has everything ...  but it feels like I can’t understand any of it. It’s honestly kinda scary.

When I first got here, I had a super tough time adjusting. It’s so crowded, and everyone walks really fast ...  almost like they’re angry or something. Even at school, I was only ever the "foreigner." Nobody really knew me; they just spread rumors. I thought maybe my looks were the problem. I even considered dyeing my hair black to match everyone else ...  But that was when Shiho talked to me. The first thing she said was, "Takamaki-san, your paintings suck."

According to her, they were so bad that she just HAD to tell me. Pretty mean, huh? Still, that was the first time someone here talked to me without mentioning my looks. We sorta just grew closer after that ...  and Shiho’s been my best friend ever since.
There’s something else I need to talk to you about!
Do you remember what I told you the last time we came here? About that female thief in the anime I used to watch? Well, I thought of something!

You know how the villains in those shows are always going on about world domination? Well, even though they get beaten by the heroes every time, they never give up. That means they must have really solid hearts ...  And that’s why I’m going to try and learn from them!
So I’ve decided...

text.ACTION: Reminder- Ann is the world’s worst actress.
Goddammit, I have to stop being sarcastic, nobody ever gets it.

text.Ann Takamaki: All right, I’m making this my ultimate goal for the future. You know, I’ve never really thought much about what I wanted to do in life ...  but now I have an objective! And that only happened because of talking to you, Maaku! Thanks!

text.Joker: I sense a heightened motivation from Ann...

text.Ann Takamaki: Well, if I want to be in action movies, I’ll need to work on my actions! I wonder how many sit-ups I’ll have to do ...  Wait, Ryuji said he knows a good gym! I should ask him for advice!
She’ll definitely be happy to hear that! Come on, let’s jog to the station!

text.TV Interviewer: Oh, he just moved his pawn to 9-5 ...

Y-Yeah! Operation Maidwatch!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: If it turns out to be sketchy, we can just bail. The apartment’s vacant, so it’s not like we’ll be messing with anyone’s home.

text.Yuuki Mishima: To think ...  Sakamoto has a brain. But if that’s the case, then ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then...

text.Yuuki Mishima: Yep!

text.ACTION: I’m just as lost as you, Maaku.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: OK, give ‘em a call!
Well, I guess he could do it too. OK, go for it, Mishima.

text.Yuuki Mishima: I-I’m not good with that kinda stuff! Seriously! Please, Hamiru!
They answered!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Shhh!

text.Yuuki Mishima: S-Services ... !

text.Victoria's Housekeeping: Is there anyone in particular you’d like to request?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: A-Anyone we want to request!? What should we do, Maaku?

text.Victoria's Housekeeping: Very well! Let’s see here ...  We have a maid available in ...  20 minutes. May I ask for your address?

text.Yuuki Mishima: A maid’s "services" ...  Hey ...  What should we have her do? I was thinking we start with some cooking ...
Of course, I wouldn’t mind some of the other services either ...  ...Should we hold a strategy meeting to discuss?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: They said 20 minutes, right ... ? I gotta use the bathroom ...

text.Yuuki Mishima: You were in there for a while ...  Are you OK? Hey, did you wash your hands?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...  ...  Huh? What? Who? Me?

text.Yuuki Mishima: Y-You’re really nervous. Ahaha ...  haha ...  uh...
Are high school students even allowed to use this type of service?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh?

text.Yuuki Mishima: What if they find out who we are!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: H-How should I know!? But why would how old you are matter when it comes to housekeeping?

text.ACTION: Oh Ryuji, you pure, sweet, innocent flower.

text.Yuuki Mishima: We would’ve been screwed if your number had shown up on their caller ID...
What!? Already!? She’s five minutes early! What do we do!? I’m not mentally prepared!

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Oh, the door’s unlocked ... ? Um, may I come in ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I-I can’t do this ... ! My stomach’s actin’ up! And my hands are all sweaty!

text.ACTION: This was your idea and you’re bailing!? Goddammit, you putz.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I’ve got your back! Just ...  From way back! Like, from the balcony!

text.Yuuki Mishima: Wh-What? I can’t do this either! Hamiru, we’ll leave it to you!

text.ACTION: Now, I can’t even really be mad at Mishima, because I’m honestly impressed he hasn’t thrown up or wet himself. Fine, whatever, I’ll get all the action myself!

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Excuse me ...  Oh, there you are!
I’m going to fill your tired heart full of lovely energy. Meow! ♥ I’m Becky, and I have the pleasure of serving you today. ♥

We’re going to get along so well! Meeeooowww! ♥♥ Oh my ...  how thoughtless of me! I should explain our services to you, Master! What would you like me to do today? The basics include cooking, cleaning, laundry ...  But there are other "services" we provide if you desire. ♥
Are you ...  perhaps ...  ...In high school?

text.ACTION: This game is really good sometimes.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: ...  ...  You’re not lying to me, are you ... ?  ...  ...   ...  ...   ...  ...  Hmmm, I’ll wait to provide those other "services" until you’ve matured a bit, Master. ♥ Sooo ...  I’ll be going now. ♥

text.Yuuki Mishima: Quiet ... !
Oh no ... !

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Shit! Run, Mishima!

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Mishima? Sakamoto-kun?
This is our first meeting. Yes, the first time ever, Master. ♥
Ugh, this is unbelievable ...  Yes, it’s me ...  your homeroom teacher.

text.ACTION: This night is a profound tragedy on every level. It is a cancer upon my soul.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: I’m so done ...  I can’t believe I got caught by some of my own students...
I should’ve taken a job outside of the city. But I needed it to be close to school so I could go there after I finished work ...  ...Who did you hear about this from?
Ms. Chouno, the English teacher ...  She’s been snooping on all the teachers ever since that incident with Mr. Kamoshida. ...Are you going to tell Ms. Chouno about this?

text.ACTION: Let’s not fucking blackmail this woman.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Hmmm ...  It doesn’t seem like you’re playing dumb ...  In any case, I’ll get in big trouble if you tell on me.  ...  ...  Hey, if you’re going to side with a teacher, side with me. I’m in charge of your class, after all. And if you promise not to tell Ms. Chouno about this, I’ll do anything for you!

text.ACTION: This is tragically the less skeevy option.
Kawakami’s got some great facial expressions.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Hey ...  It won’t be any better for you if people find out that you called a maid service. This isn’t even your home address to begin with, is it? I guess you at least thought about that. Well, I’ll promise to keep this a secret too ...  so why don’t we both forget this ever happened? I’ll treat this as if you had canceled, so you won’t have to pay anything. OK?
Don’t say anything about this at school, OK!? Just act as if nothing ever happened! Got it? OK, bye!
