text.Morgana: Oh ...  Cautiousness is good, but let’s not linger in one area for too long, OK? In Mementos, there’s a certain Shadow that’s far stronger than the rest ...  We’d have no chance against it.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wha--!? Are you for real!? You shoulda told us that from the start!

text.ACTION: If you move through Mementos at any appreciable speed whatsoever you’ll never run into The Reaper. It’s not even like Persona 3 where there were special floors where he’d spawn faster, it just takes a number of minutes for him to spawn, to the point where you can easily avoid him. I went through the entire game without once encountering The Reaper.

Anyway, this is the start of our money grind. We have about 42,000 yen at the moment. We need about 200,000 by even a rather conservative estimate. No, really. All that’s barely going to last us until the next Palace.
This is what it looks like when Yoshida’s Rank 3 procs, by the way.

Because I’m a damn fool, I decide to waste all my SP grinding in Aiyatsbus instead of the block we just unlocked. See that money amount? That’s decent for this block, but depending on the enemy in the next block I could be getting 3-6 times more per pull. Using Yoshida’s Rank 2, I can get up to about 3,000 yen up to four or five times in a row on some enemies. Even better, they don’t die in two hits in the next block, so I can do that multiple times.

And then there’s the RNG, which hates you. The amount of money you get is supposedly based on the enemy and your Persona’s Luck stat, but even when picking Personas specifically for that, sometimes you just get crap like this. Also, this is with a proc on Yoshida’s Rank 3 ability. I finally understand why people suggested leaving him at Rank 2, because his Rank 3 is terrible. Remember how I said when Rank 3 procced it gave you more money but ended the battle? Forget the “more money” part, because sometimes it just gives you way less! I would legitimately have been better off just killing the enemies because you get far more from killing them than this.
All this is to say, I fucked up big time and wasted a bunch of time and SP on scrub enemies that give you garbage.
Meanwhile, this is Yoshida’s Rank 2. It’s much handier.
Eventually, though, you can ask too much and the enemies will get mad and attack you.

text.Morgana: Mementos is different. While other Palaces exist because of just one person, this one’s from the public. From that perspective, it’d take more than a few intruders to make a mark on the security level. You’d have to do something so bad that the entire public sees you as an enemy. So ...  be careful, OK, Skull?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, shut up!

text.ACTION: While exploring Mementos, members of the party will occasionally spout out little lines, and other party members will respond to them. It’s cute.

text.Ann Takamaki: Huh ... ? Those are ...  They’re people ...  right?

text.Morgana: Well, I’d say they’re most likely Shadows...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’re Shadows doin’ here? It’s not like they’re gonna be catchin’ a train or--
I-It stopped ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: They got in...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey ...  Where’s that go?

text.Morgana: If I had to guess ...  I’d say into the deepest part of Mementos.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What? This place seriously don’t make any sense ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Isn’t it a waiting room? I didn’t expect there’d be one here too...

text.Morgana: It looks like we’ll be able to use this to take a break. Make sure to utilize it well, Joker.
Mm ...  It seems like this is some kind of safe zone separate from the other areas.

text.ACTION: Even Mementos has safe rooms, of course, and you can do anything in them you could normally do.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well, yeah ...  Even I can see that. I mean, just look at the place.
Woah, Takama-- Uh, Panther. You’re really into this!

text.Morgana: What could this mean ... ?

text.ACTION: Probably that we’re nearing the end of the block.

Remember that request Mishima just gave us about the sadist? That’s a boss that guards the end of the Mementos block. Once we defeat it, we can progress onwards. Pretty much all the blocks have bosses like this at the end once you progress far enough in the game to reveal them. We could take them on now, or we could circle back to the second floor of Aiyatsbus and take on the bully that we got the request for a month ago and we never did anything about. Whoops!

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh my god!

text.ACTION: We also open a locked chest to find this garbage, a Balm of Life. Not only do we get three of these with that free DLC item pack, we can just buy items that serve the exact same function.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This guy’s bullyin’ is really bad. From what I hear, it’s mostly blackmail, takin’ money from people, that kinda thing.

text.Ann Takamaki: If we don’t make him have a change of heart, his bullying might get even worse.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Let’s go.
That’s no reason! How’s it their fault when you don’t give ‘em any choice, huh?

text.Ann Takamaki: You’re the lowest of the low. Bullying people weaker than you, knowing they can’t fight back!

text.Shadow Takanashi: The hell!? You’re all ganging up on me, too! Are you Phantom Thieves some kind of gang!? Protectors of justice, my ass! Don’t act high and mighty with me when you don’t know anything!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You’re the one who doesn’t know anything! Let’s get ‘em!

text.ACTION: It can inflict fear, which is no big deal.
It also likes to use Lucky Punch to score cheap crits and follow them up with Stomach Blow, which inflicts Hunger.

We could defeat it easily, or we could attempt to gain even more money another way. See, about half of the Mementos minibosses are vulnerable to Confuse. And, if you remember way back to the list of status effects, one of the effects of Confuse is that it causes the affected character to throw away money. See where I’m going with this?

What we do is use Pulinpa (high chance of Confuse), hope it hits, and if it does, we get a free 8,000 yen… if it doesn’t choose to throw away an item or do nothing instead. Unfortunately, Confuse wears off 2-3 turns later, and even spamming Pulinpa every turn we get, without a skill like Confuse Boost, we’re lucky to hit at all. We can’t do this forever, either, because we don’t have any SP Adhesive 3s to let us regenerate SP. We’re best off taking what we do get and moving forward instead of trying fruitlessly to get as much as we can from this one enemy. And remember, the amount you get is based on your Persona’s Luck stat and the amount of money the enemy gives upon defeat. The reason this works so well in the first place is that as minibosses, they give substantial amounts of money when killed. In case you’re wondering, yes, this does mean that the money rewards from this strategy will grow exponentially as the game goes on! This is probably the best, easiest way to get money in the game, though we’re attempting this at pretty much the worst possible time (it gets substantially easier when our party learns specific skills), in case my paltry return of only about 16,000 yen seems rather low.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What are you talkin’ about?

text.Shadow Takanashi: If I don’t go after him, I’m the one who’s gonna get bullied! I can’t take it, I just can’t!

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, I get it now. There’s an even bigger bully—ordering this guy around—who’s behind all this.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey! Didn’t you just say it’s people’s own fault for not standin’ up for themselves?

text.Shadow Takanashi: Thank you! Oh, thank you, you wonderful phantom thieves!

text.Morgana: This guy ...  Fickle fellow, isn’t he?

text.Shadow Takanashi: I’m counting on you ...  You guys promised.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Fine, but you better apologize to those people you bullied!

text.ACTION: We get a single Protein. Lame.
Now that we’ve taken down that Shadow, we can progress further through Mishima’s Confidant. Oh joy.
From here, we need to return to the gate and take down the new Shadow.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: She really seems like a sadist...

text.Morgana: She’s calling someone her slave and ordering him around, right?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: In a way, she’s denying his existence. I certainly wouldn’t want to be a victim of that.

text.Ann Takamaki: Let’s go talk to her.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s ‘cause you made some guy your slave! That’s all kinds of wrong right there.

text.Shadow Shimizu: That’s what he wants! He worships me more than any god, you know.

text.Ann Takamaki: Uh ...  I don’t know where to begin to explain how you’re wrong...

text.Shadow Shimizu: I beat him and I hurt him, and he sees it as a sign of our love and friendship! He’s so happy!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You are so delusional.

text.Shadow Shimizu: I’m pretty, and my grades are good! It’s my right to order people around! I’ll start by giving orders to you pigs! Lick my shoes, peasants!

text.ACTION: Shimizu starts by using Oni-Kagura, which fucks us up pretty good.
After a round of attacking, she’ll boost her Attack and then Charge up, which is our cue to take her down quick.

text.Ann Takamaki: Why did you start treating him like that?

text.Shadow Shimizu: He just kept going along with it, so I misunderstood and thought I could do anything I wanted ...  Actually, I ...  wanted to be more than friends with him.

text.Ann Takamaki: More than friends? You mean like as a boyfriend!?

text.Shadow Shimizu: Yes. I had a crush on him, but then I got possessive. Those feelings went out of control...

text.Ann Takamaki: Be careful that you don’t make things worse for yourself than they already are...

text.ACTION: We get a Whip Sword, a new weapon for Ann.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whoa, we did it!

text.Ann Takamaki: This is because more people believe in us now, right?

text.Morgana: That has to be it. Now then, let’s get in there!

text.ACTION: And so we enter Chemdah, meaning desire.

text.Morgana: Looks like it’ll be a new area from here on. I’m starting to understand how this place works...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes ...  It is quite a marvel to find the subway system down here.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uh, Earth to Yusuke! It’s always been like that!

text.ACTION: This isn’t an important shot, but Zorro spawned facing backwards for some reason and it’s weird.

text.Ann Takamaki: The last floor had seven areas, but the one before that only had two, right?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I suppose it varies, depending upon the location...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Guess that means it ain’t easy to tell how much of a floor we got left to cover, huh?

text.Morgana: That’s right. We won’t know how many areas are on a floor until we make it to the end. But judging by the vibe I’m getting from the Shadows ...  this floor isn’t any smaller than the last.

text.ACTION: The first image here is a normal gain, while the second is a Yoshida Rank 3 proc. As you can see, both are much more lucrative than their counterparts from the last block.
But there’s also new dangers. If we push too hard...
After nearly getting steamrolled by this Nue, we decide we’ve had enough fun for the day.
We made it to the next safe room, which means it’s about time to head home, because I’d rather save my SP items for the real Palace.

We end the day with 158,000 yen, with about 38,000 of that coming from Aiyatsbus (not counting the 12,000 we got from Shadow Shimizu) and 56,000 coming from Chemdah, which goes to prove how much better an idea it would have been to grind there instead, considering how much less time and SP we spent down there. We’re still well under what we need, but we have enough assorted junk to sell to Untouchable to get us to about 193,000 or so, which is acceptable if not perfect. We’ll have to make do.

text.Newscaster: Complaints about the authenticity of artwork are flooding in from buyers after the Madarame debacle. It seems this scandal will continue to cause confusion in the art world for some time.

text.Morgana: The people who bought art from Madarame should have accepted the truth about him by now ...

text.ACTION:
Part 47: 6/8-6/10: Meddling Kid
	Part 46: 6/8-6/10: Meddling Kid

text.Murmur: Oh, I’ve seen him on TV!

text.Whisper: He’s famous, but he still rides the train like everyone else...

text.Murmur: Hey isn’t that that detective?
The Phantom Thieves are kinda cool, huh?

text.Mature-Looking Girl: Yeah, I think it’s just like the one sent to Kamoshida. People online are saying the Phantom Thieves are behind this. There’s already a Phan-Site with a bunch of requests posted on it.

text.Gentle Girl: I can’t believe there are real-life superheroes. If it’s happened twice, it’s probably going to happen again. Can’t wait to see who’s next.

text.Ushimaru: It’s a good chance to think about your future. Be sure you’re paying attention. ...You’d better not make a ruckus. Am I clear? It will reflect poorly on our school. There’s a group going to a television studio this year, correct? Hamiru. Here’s a question for you. With the advent of the color TV, something else started appearing in color. Do you know what it is?

text.ACTION: If this is true, holy shit that’s amazing.

text.Ushimaru: Exactly. Before, most people’s dreams were in black and white. But research shows that once color broadcasts became the norm, dreams started being mostly in color. What’s fascinating is that people see the world in color, regardless of TV’s existence. It’s strange that our dreams had been in black and white until TV’s inception.
In the future, if 3D televisions become normal and let us sense flavor, smell, and heat ...  Then dreams might become indistinguishable from reality.

text.ACTION: That’s completely insane, and also not what 3D is.

text.Morgana: Dreams with flavor ...  I could get behind that!

text.Sharp Student: It’s probably because of Mr. Kamoshida, right? Considering what happened with Suzui-san ...
I heard Principal Kobayakawa knew about the sexual harassment too and just turned a blind eye to it. I bet he wants to snuff out any rumors now. Even the volleyball team was told to keep quiet...

text.Loud Student: That’s the worst ...  So that’s what he’s using Niijima-senpai for?

text.Sharp Student: Oh yeah, rumor has it she knew as well. Isn’t that horrible? She acts all noble about it too.

text.Ann Takamaki: Niijima-senpai knew ... ?

text.ACTION: Uh-oh, looks like there’s a false rumor spreading about Makoto. This’ll create some drama.

text.Principal: It was all for your sake. I thought the more information you had, the easier your investigation would become. And? Did any information arise about the case I asked you to look into?

text.Makoto Niijima: (sigh) Nothing yet. I will pass the details along if anything comes up. Right now, there is a more pressing issue ...  It appears there are students at Shujin who are being threatened by a criminal organization.
A student who saw your posting came to us looking for help ...  I’d like to request a countermeasure.

text.Principal: I-Isn’t this some sort of mistake? I can’t believe this would happen to the students of our academy. Now is no time for such problems. There is still lingering concern regarding the Phantom Thieves...

text.ACTION: You’re really dead-set on this whole Phantom Thieves business, huh?

text.Makoto Niijima: But we received a request for help...

text.Principal: I-I’m rather busy at the moment. If you wish to do something, you will need to act on your own.

text.ACTION: Not only is this dude totally spineless, he’s completely hanging her out to dry.

text.Makoto Niijima: Are you sure about this? I am still investigating your case as well ...

text.Principal: Y-Yes, that’s correct. It works out perfectly! My intentions have borne fruit. This criminal organization must be the connecting factor. If you pursue this criminal issue, you’ll surely find clues about the Phantom Thieves!

text.ACTION: What the hell are you talking about?

text.Makoto Niijima: But that’s absurd ...

text.Principal: So ...  let’s say this rumor is true. Do you intend to ignore those students in trouble?
Your sister would have solved this easily if she were in your position.
My expectations of you are very high. I hope you don’t disappoint.

text.ACTION: Seems like Makoto’s up against a wall.

text.Ann Takamaki: Hmmm ...  I wonder ...  I guess it’d have to be someone who’s the talk of the town?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, this ain’t some kinda video game!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Either way, we’ll need a lead before we can begin anything.

text.Ann Takamaki: We’ll just have to look for that as we go...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: If only there was a big target just lying around for us...

text.Morgana: Maybe our next target will be a celebrity?

text.Makoto Niijima: Oh ...  Don’t mind me. I was simply talking to myself.

text.Veteran Pick-Up Artist: Steal their hearts ...  Kind of like those Phantom Thieves, eh? I think you’re onto something. I think this might really work for you. Try using something like that for one of your lines.

text.Novice Pick-Up Artist: I-I see! I’ll go with "I’ll take your heart!"

text.Young Homeless: I heard it was the Phantom Thieves who did it ...  I guess there’s still hope in this world. Maybe I’ll even start painting again...

text.Aggressive Reporter: Do you hear what he’s saying? This youth thinks that the world is pathetic for being so easily deceived. Modern Japan robs the young of their hope, and dirty politics casts a dark shadow over us all. And that concludes our on-the-spot coverage.

text.Protesting Man: That’s right, young man! Those who believe will be saved!

text.Clear-Eyed Man: Great Sun God, are you not going to have your apostles the Phantom Thieves punish the evildoers?

text.Protesting Man: Worry not. Their mission has already been appointed. The good news shall reach everyone in time!

text.Ichiko Ohya: The direct approach just isn’t going to work, but now I’m sure they’re hiding something.

text.Boy 7: Don’t worry about the money ...  I-Is everything OK with you?

text.Daisuke Takanashi: No, I’ll talk to Sakoda-senpai and get you your money back. I just want to do the right thing for once. I won’t drag you into it.

text.ACTION: Looks like Daisuke’s change of heart went through.
Maaku heads to the diner afterwards and gains Guts +1 and Knowledge +2.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I’m thinking we might find our next target there.
With that much money, they’ve prolly got their fingers in all sorts of dirty business.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm ...  That phrasing has quite the immoral ring to it ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, you always react to the weirdest stuff...

text.Ann Takamaki: Anyway, we get to observe a live recording of a show, right?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ooh, maybe we’re gonna be on TV!

text.Ann Takamaki: We’ll just be in the crowd, remember? Any TV appearance would be for like, two seconds.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm. Try not to pull any fanciful stunts to garner attention, OK?

text.Diligent Office Worker: You remember the cyber attack? Tens of thousands of people’s personal information was leaked.

text.Young Office Worker: Oh, right. I heard about those hackers. I hear they’ve been causing damage around the world.

text.Diligent Office Worker: They act like they’re fighting an unjust system, but they’re still a problem to people like us.

text.Young Office Worker: Thank you. The curry was delicious.

text.DTD Reporter: So many Chinese restaurants! Yes, high-quality Chinese food is true perfection. Good smells are coming from all over this place. It’s easy to find something great to eat here.

text.Joker: I don’t think my bond with Sojiro will deepen just yet...

text.ACTION: Sojiro’s Rank 4 takes an absurd number of points to reach.

text.Joker: Help him out

text.Sojiro Sakura: Put your stuff down, and grab an apron. Don’t forget to wash your hands.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Sojiro will grow stronger soon ...

text.Sojiro Sakura: Hey, thanks for helping out.

text.PR Woman: I’m sure you know about commercial breaks? Well, those are actually sponsor-related product placements. To sum things up, ratings are vitally important for a station’s production funding, and...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh...
He ain’t even listenin’...

text.PR Woman: Thus, the scheduling department is where we decide what time we broadcast which program. I suppose you could say it’s the place where the scheduling is determined.

text.Ann Takamaki: Could this get any more obvious ... ?
(yawn) So sleepy...

text.PR Woman: So, the best parts are taken from the footage in order to cut down the program to the desired length. The place where this filmed footage is edited would be the editing room.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I swear, I’m not gonna last...

text.Morgana: Hrgh ... !?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, assho--

text.PR Woman: My apologies! I’ll have them leave right away! Now then, it’s time for a bit of hands-on experience!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit ...  Who does that jerk think he is?

text.ACTION: A different man looks Ann up and down.

text.Ann Takamaki: Huh?

text.Bossy AD: You’ve got a slammin’ bod, after all. Hehehe ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Uh ...  I’m on a school trip...

text.Bossy AD: Just gimme a call if you’re interested. I’d greatly welcome a message from you, day or night.

text.Ann Takamaki: Uhhh, yeah...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Greatly welcome, my ass. It’s obvious what he’s after. Do these rotten adults care about anything other than looks!? I’ll yank their stupid hearts out, dammit!

text.Bossy AD: Well then, uhhh ...  Let’s have you see what it’s like to be an AC. Oh, that stands for "assistant camera." When we’re moving cameras, we need people who’ll get the cables from getting tangled up ...  The blond will do. He seems like he’s got energy to spare anyway. Guy next to him, you can come too if you’re feeling lonely. C’mon, hurry up and grab the cables!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit ...  This sucks!
This is totally killin’ my vibe ...

text.Joker: We fought valiantly against the long cables...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Aren’t we supposed to be guests? Why the hell do we hafta be doin’ manual labor!? This is bullshit! Goin’ to the bathroom didn’t even make me feel better!

text.Ann Takamaki: I get how you feel though ...  That sucked for the both of us.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We gotta do more of this tomorrow too ... ?

text.Morgana: No flaking out, Ryuji.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I know, I know. I gotta be a "good boy," right? Bein’ phantom thieves ain’t easy ...

text.ACTION: Yeah, sure, let’s just discuss this openly in an unfamiliar location with lots of blind corners people could be waiting behind.

text.Ann Takamaki: That reminds me, we get to go home straight from here today. We don’t spend much time in this area, so why don’t we relax and check out some shops beforehand?

text.Morgana: It looked delicious! What was that?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ohhh ...  You mean Dome Town? The round part is a baseball stadium, then along the outside they’ve got an amusement park.

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s right in the middle of a business area, but they have some pretty hardcore rides there too.
Going on a scary ride doesn’t really prove any kind of courage.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Not like cats can get on anyways.

text.Morgana: Really ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Really. You might be able to sneak in if you stay in the bag, but you’d totally puke if you did that.
But uh ...  Let’s just go to Dome Town! I’m really feelin’ it now!

text.Ann Takamaki: Me too! My stomach’s ready for roller coasters!

text.Morgana: Uhhh ...  I think I’ll pass on the puke rides...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, whaddya want?

text.Goro Akechi: I happened to be passing by, so it seemed polite to greet you. We’ll be filming together, after all. Ah, where are my manners? My name is Goro Akechi.

text.Ann Takamaki: Akechi ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Filming? What, you a celebrity?

text.Goro Akechi: Only to the extent of appearing on TV a couple of times.

My apologies, I truly was just passing by. I must be going. There’s a briefing for tomorrow’s recording that I have to attend. So, you’re going to go have cake now? I missed lunch today, so I’m quite hungry myself...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Cake ... ? What’re you talkin’ about?

text.Goro Akechi: Oh, am I mistaken? I thought I heard something about delicious pancakes ...  No matter. Welp, see you tomorrow.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: He’s never gonna get popular with that kinda hair though.

text.Ann Takamaki: You don’t get it...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Eh, it’s fine. We’ll see him again tomorrow anyways. C’mon, let’s go to Dome Town!

text.Morgana: This is why I spoke against it.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude ...  It’s not fair ...  Usin’ your cathood as an excuse ...  only at times like this ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Anyway, are you guys feeling hungry? How about some pancakes?

text.ACTION: What is with today and pancakes?

text.Morgana: Let’s go home. We have another full day ahead of us tomorrow.
Well, try not to stand out too much—that’s what Ryuji’s for.

text.Newscaster: It is still unclear what led Mr. Madarame to confess his crimes.

text.Morgana: It’s just like with Kamoshida, right? He doesn’t realize what happened to him.

text.ACTION: The girls in the audience start squealing.

text.Chatter: It’s Akechi-kun!
He’s so cooool!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ain’t that the guy from yesterday ... ?

text.Bossy AD: Cutting back from commercial! Seven, six, five seconds till start, four, three ...

text.Cute Announcer: After his last appearance was so well-received, we decided to bring back this fine gentleman today. It’s the high school detective, Goro Akechi!

text.Chatter: (more cheering)

text.Goro Akechi: Hello there.

text.Cheerful Host: Thank you for taking the time to join us today, Akechi-kun. Your popularity is stunning.

text.Goro Akechi: Even I’ve found it to be quite a surprise. It is a bit embarrassing though...

text.Cute Announcer: Moving along, we’ve been told there’s a case on your mind right now. Care to share, detective?

text.Goro Akechi: Ah, yes. That would be the scandal involving the master artist Madarame.

text.Cheerful Host: There it is! All of this phantom thief excitement has caught your attention too, Akechi-kun! Allow me to be blunt for just a second. What do you think of these justice-oriented Phantom Thieves?

text.Goro Akechi: If they truly are heroes of justice, I sincerely hope they exist.

text.Cheerful Host: Ohhh, so you don’t deny the possibility that they’re real?

text.Goro Akechi: I may not seem like it, but I sometimes wish that Santa Claus actually existed.

text.ACTION: Look at this fool who doesn’t believe in Santa Claus.

text.Goro Akechi: Although if he did, I’d have to arrest him for breaking and entering.

text.Chatter: (raucous laughter)

text.Goro Akechi: But hypothetically speaking, if these Phantom Thieves are real...

text.Cheerful Host: That’s quite the statement. Are they committing crimes? Some people even say that the Thieves are actually helping their victims abandon their evil ways.

text.Goro Akechi: What the artist Madarame did truly was an unforgivable crime. However, they’re taking the law into their own hands by judging him. It is far from justice. More importantly, you should never forcefully change a person’s heart.

text.Cheerful Host: You have a point. These people are calling themselves the Phantom Thieves, after all.

text.ACTION: Actually they’re calling themselves #Millennials, but you can’t voice act that.

text.Cheerful Host: Amazing as always, Akechi-kun! I could listen to you for days! You have the most radiant charisma!

text.Goro Akechi: I have to say though, I would be embarrassed if it turns out these Phantom Thieves don’t exist. If that were the case, I’d summarize it into a report as a school project.

text.Cute Announcer: Now then, let’s try asking some students the same age as Akechi-kun about the Phantom Thieves! First, please press your button now if you think the Phantom Thieves exist!

text.Cheerful Host: About 30% or so? What are your thoughts, Akechi-kun?

text.ACTION: That’s weird, considering we’re currently hovering just below 17% on our own goddamn website.

text.Goro Akechi: I’m a bit surprised. That’s higher than I was expecting. I’d love to hear some more detailed opinions on the Phantom Thieves’ actions.

text.Cute Announcer: All right, let’s try asking this student here. Hypothetically speaking, what are your thoughts on these Phantom Thieves, if they were real?

text.Goro Akechi: You say that with such firmness.

text.Cheerful Host: This completely goes against the opinion you had about them being tried by law, Akechi-kun.

text.Goro Akechi: In that case, there’s one more question I’d like to ask ...  If someone close to you, for example your friend next to you ...  If his heart suddenly changed ...  wouldn’t you think it was the work of the Phantom Thieves?
I see. But how can you be so sure? Whether the Thieves’ actions are good or not, I feel there is a more important issue at hand.

The matter of how they change people’s hearts. If they honestly possess that ability ...  it could be used for more than extracting confessions. It could be that what seem to be ordinary crimes are actually being perpetrated by these methods...

Oh, please don’t misunderstand. This is all purely hypothetical ...  It is only if people who can use such a power truly exist. Either way though, this cannot be ignored. The existence of the Phantom Thieves would be nothing but a threat to our everyday lives. To be honest, I’m already working alongside the police to help sort out this matter.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: He made it sound like we’re the baddies. I don’t like it.

text.Ann Takamaki: But that stuff about the police ...  Do you think it’s for real?

text.Morgana: He can say whatever he wants. The justice of it all is something we can decide for ourselves.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh sorry, I gotta go take a leak. Can you guys wait here? I’ll be right back.

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh my god ...  I’m gonna keep going, OK?

text.Goro Akechi: To paraphrase Hegel, advancement cannot occur without both thesis and antithesis...

text.ACTION: I can use the smart words too! Synecdoche! Puerile! Antidisestablishmentarianism!

If your Knowledge is Rank 5 the rest of this cutscene should be an in-depth discussion about Hegelian dialectic. “Hm, yes, only through sublation of the initial, abstract thesis can we land upon something concrete. What are your thoughts on Marx and Engel’s perspective on the matter?”

text.Goro Akechi: Haha, my apologies. What I mean is that our discussion was quite meaningful. Few people around me are so willing to speak their minds as freely as you did earlier. Adults are only interested in using the young, while they simply do as the adults say. I feel like our discussions could prove quite fruitful. Would you mind talking with me again?
Thank you. It makes me glad to hear that. The students from Shujin are truly quite interesting. I look forward to seeing you again. Well then...

text.Morgana: There’s probably a lot we can learn from him though.

text.Joker: It seems the detective Akechi has taken a liking to me...

text.Sae Niijima: The only logical explanation is that someone in the police has ties to the Phantom Thieves ...  Explain yourself!

text.ACTION: Justice is the arcana of, well, justice. It represents law, fairness, and truth, as well as unfairness and dishonesty when reversed.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I can’t stand that high and mighty attitude ... ! Just breathin’ the same air as him makes me sick. C’mon, Maaku. Let’s go.

text.ACTION: Maaku looks back for a moment before following Ryuji.

text.Ann Takamaki: He clearly tried to discredit everything we’re doing.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: And he just had to say it on live TV too!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Don’t be so sour. There are, without a doubt, people we have saved. Those people could not have been saved if not for the heroics of the Phantom Thieves. I am living proof of that.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Awww, what a nice thing to say!

text.Ann Takamaki: Still ...  was what Akechi-kun said actually wrong? I feel like he had a point.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Why you gotta bring that up now?

text.Ann Takamaki: I mean, is it really OK to be doing this to people just because they’re criminals? Doesn’t it seem a little selfish?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We are phantom thieves, Ann. I doubt everyone would forgive us for what we did to Madarame. Yet, I still decided that it was a necessary act.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Kamoshida too. We weren’t gonna do shit to him through any normal methods.

text.Ann Takamaki: I guess I can’t really think of any other way...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm. I believe our best path forward is sticking to our justice, not that of the law. Shouldn’t that be enough? And with the unanimous decision rule in place, I doubt we’ll lose our way.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...Yeah, you’re right. Sorry for bringing that up. And don’t worry, I’m not thinking about quitting the Phantom Thieves or anything.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Just you watch, Akechi. Someday you’re totally gonna see who was right!

text.Ann Takamaki: OK, let’s stop talking about this for now.

text.Morgana: That detective Akechi seems to have a lot of influence on the media. It’d be dangerous to get too close to him, but he may actually prove useful in some situations.

text.Yuuki Mishima: You heard what Akechi said, right Hamiru? How dare he declare the Phantom Thieves are criminals! As the administrator of the Phantom Aficionado Website, I can’t stay quiet about this. I’m going to show Akechi how people online really feel! I’ll change up the survey question tomorrow morning. Justice is with the Phantom Thieves! Keep on doing what you do best!

text.Morgana: ...Why is he of all people getting angry about this? Anyway, he means the survey on the Phan-Site, right? I guess we should look forward to it.

text.DTD Reporter: On these irregularly broadcast specials, we share limited-edition items that are all the rage! Today, we’re going to talk about Soothing Soba, the dish that’ll help you endure the summer heat! It’s on sale now in convenience stores around Tokyo, and it’s expected to sell out fast.

text.DTD Co-host: It even puts some Chinese food to shame. It’s surprising you can buy it at convenience stores.

text.ACTION: We’ll have to pick some of that up sometime.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: You know, I’ve been hearing Shibuya’s getting more dangerous lately. I’m sure you pass by that area on your commute to school, but don’t make too many detours, OK?

text.Joker: I don’t think my bond with Kawakami will deepen just yet...

text.ACTION: We’re paying 5,000 yen and she doesn’t even rank up, ugh.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Ok, I’ll get dropped off from the store then. Please clean up your room and wait for me. ♥

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Kawakami will grow stronger soon...

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Thank you for your patronage!

text.Murmur: So the Phantom Thieves were the bad guys?
I guess now that you mention it ...

text.Whisper: I’ve felt that way the whole time.

Part 48: 6/11: Sojiro's Attic Full Of Teenagers
