text.Anon: this has to be fake, lol

text.ACTION: Mishima changed the question, leading to new replies.

text.Loud Lady: Ah, on that talk show? It was simply dreadful.

text.ACTION: When this line hits, there’s a generic voice line of a woman saying “THE PHANTOM THIEVES ARE SUPER LAME,” and it’s one of the goofiest things in the entire game. It’s great.

text.Loud Lady: How can anyone seriously suggest supernatural beings are stealing people’s hearts? That ...  child is a phony. There’s simply no way that the Phantom Thieves exist.

text.Heavily Made-up Woman: Unfortunately, my precious children all think they’re real—and worse, that this detective is amazing ...  Children are far too impressionable to see such vulgar content on TV.

text.Morgana: Looks like people still don’t think we’re real...

text.Loud Student: I can’t believe a high schooler moonlights as a detective. He’s just like the Detective Prince.

text.ACTION: That makes two references to Naoto.

text.Loud Student: He’s smart AND handsome. He’s almost TOO perfect!

text.Sharp Student: We had front row seats. I could practically reach out and touch Akechi-kun! I was so nervous! He was really working that uniform, and without seeming like a snob. He’s a natural at public speaking. I hear he’s an orphan who grew up poor. It’s part of what makes him so amazing! He wants his last high school memory to be capturing the Phantom Thieves. This isn’t a game to him!

text.Loud Student: See, I hear his dad’s the head of some big financial conglomerate. I will say, I love that he hates the media. Makes me believe that he doesn’t do this for the fame.
People say he’s so good that he’s made enemies in the police force ...  Oh, yeah—apparently yesterday’s interview was so popular they’re going to air it again tonight.

text.Usami: Why someone would steal something like a heart, which can’t be turned into money, is beyond be.
If I were a phantom thief, I wouldn’t go after "hearts" or works of art—I’d go after gold.
Now then, Hamiru-san. Can you imagine how much gold has been excavated by humanity over the course of history?
Correct. Surprisingly little, don’t you think? That rarity is what drives its value.

Incidentally, they say that 16% of the world’s gold is in Japan. Was your first thought the Tokugawa Clan’s buried gold? It’s actually in discarded home electronics. In other words, a junkyard is much more valuable than someone else’s heart.

text.Morgana: Hmph! You can’t measure the value of a Treasure with money!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Let’s see him do it, then!

text.ACTION: Ann chops Ryuji in the back of the head.

text.Ann Takamaki: (while eating)

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Who cares? Everybody’s talkin’ about this stuff anyways. It’d just be more suspicious if we were whisperin’.
Gimme some!

text.Ann Takamaki: Sorry, just ate the last one.

text.Morgana: You guys are too laid back. The police are getting involved now, you know.

text.Ann Takamaki: So you think it’s true ... ? We’ll be OK if we keep doing this ...  right?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We can’t let the cops scare us outta bein’ phantom thieves.

text.Ann Takamaki: But ...  what about that weird guy from Madarame’s Palace ... ? Isn’t there a lot we don’t know?

text.ACTION: Uhhh, hope she didn’t hear any of that conversation

text.Makoto Niijima: You three seem to be having so much fun. I’m a little jealous.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Are you snoopin’ on us again? We said before, we don’t know nothin’.

text.Makoto Niijima: Why do you think I’m here to question you? Could it be that you’re hiding something? My ears are always open to the troubles of my peers, you know.

text.Ann Takamaki: You’re really that hungry for a good letter of recommendation? ...Of course you are. Nobody would take on your annoying job if they weren’t.
...You’re student council president, right? Wouldn’t you have known about Kamoshida?

text.Makoto Niijima: Of course not! He honestly was a good teacher until that day ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, but you always take the teacher’s side. That’s what a good council president does, right?

text.Makoto Niijima: Then ...  how about you? What did you do for your friend?

text.Ann Takamaki: There wasn’t any way to help! By myself ...  I couldn’t do anything for her!

text.Makoto Niijima: There’s no need to shout.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: If those Phantom Thieves are out there helpin’ people ...  I’d root for ‘em, no questions asked. They’ve gotta be more dependable than some people I know.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Just make sure you show up to your classes, all right?

text.Ann Takamaki: I’d be ashamed to let it end now...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hell yeah. It’s about time we find our next target too.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: "A criminal group with unknown goals that does whatever it wants in the name of justice." Huh ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s prolly ‘cause of Akechi ...  TV’s got some crazy sway.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: He’s free to deny our actions, but being cursed by his influence is another thing entirely.

text.Ann Takamaki: Just when we were starting to get people to believe in us too ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All we gotta do is take down another hot shot, yeah?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Well, do you have any ideas who this next "hot shot" could be?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I ain’t got a thing yet ...  Dammit, this is real irritatin’ ...  By the way, what’s up with that luggage?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: They were not only filthy, but too noisy as well ...  No true art could come from such a place.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’re you gonna so then? You can’t go back to that shack, right?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I was planning on staying at Takamaki-san’s— I mean, Ann’s house.

text.Ann Takamaki: WHAT!? There’s no way that’s gonna happen!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Impossible...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You’re the impossible one!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: But I spent everything I had on these delectable Japanese sweets...

text.Ann Takamaki: That’s not the issue here! Seriously though ...  what’re we gonna do about him?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s way too small. Plus, my folks’d never agree to it.

text.ACTION: Oops, looks like the writers forgot Ryuji’s mom is single!

text.Morgana: Well, seeing as Yusuke is an important member of our team ...  I’ll lend a hand! Come stay at our place! It’s dirty, but at least you’ll have somewhere to sleep!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Why’re you the one calling the shots?

text.Ann Takamaki: Don’t you two live in a cafe? I’ve been wondering about that for a while. Yongen’s not too far, is it?

text.Morgana: Nope! And the cafe’s only a minute walk from the station.

text.Ann Takamaki: How about we go there now? We can have a party to celebrate Madarame’s change of heart!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ooh, good idea! We can make it a welcome party for Yusuke too!

text.Ann Takamaki: All right, it’s decided!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Sorry to cause you trouble. By the way ...  I prefer sleeping on a futon.

text.Morgana: It’ll be up to you to convince the chief.

text.ACTION: Maaku shakes the bag. Morgana yelps.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This place looks so outdated ...  I can’t say I hate it though.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: People refer to that as "retro."

text.Ann Takamaki: Hello!

text.Sojiro Sakura: A girl too ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: Maaku has really helped us a lot lately.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Heh, I bet you’re the ones doing all the helping.

text.Ann Takamaki: No, really, he’s been great.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Huh ...  Sit down. This round’ll be on the house.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Indeed, there’s great depth to its acidity.

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh yeah, I remember now! I think I’ve seen Leblanc mentioned in a magazine before...

text.Sojiro Sakura: That was a long time ago.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real? Gimme a taste.
Blech!
It’s so bitter! This has gotta be cruel and unusual punishment!

text.Sojiro Sakura: Eh, I didn’t drink coffee when I was a kid either.

text.Ann Takamaki: Ooh! I wanna see!

text.Sojiro Sakura: It’s only an attic.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Man, that bitter taste just won’t leave my mouth ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Thank you very much for the drink.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Up these stairs? ...Oh, and thanks for the soda!

text.Sojiro Sakura: So, you’re uhh...

text.Ann Takamaki: Ann. Ann Takamaki.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Ann-chan, huh ...  That’s a nice name. You got a boyfriend?

text.Ann Takamaki: Nope. Never have, either.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, you gotta get up here! This place’s freakin’ insane!

text.Sojiro Sakura: Go on.

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, right. Thank you for the coffee!
Sheesh. They had to leave the Mona bag down here?

text.ACTION: Ann grabs the bags and walks upstairs.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Huh, sweet girl.

text.ACTION: Yeah, I agree, that Rise poster is pretty incredible.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It seems quite ordinary to me.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real ... ?
See? Ain’t this crazy?

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s cleaner than I thought it would be.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What!?

text.Morgana: Well, sit wherever you’d like.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Even those who previously believed in us have been influenced by the comments made on TV.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This is all that effin’ Akechi’s fault!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Keep it down. We don’t want anyone hearing us.

text.Ann Takamaki: At this rate we’re just going to worry everyone instead of give them courage ...

text.Morgana: We need to find a way to make our rightfulness known to society. It’s time we think about our next move. You were planning on discussing that today, right?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes. First, we need to search for a candidate.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s not like we’re just gonna stumble upon some important target though. You guys don’t know anyone, do you?

text.Ann Takamaki: I don’t...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Me neither...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whaddya think, leader?

text.Morgana: Well ...  there probably are a lot of famous targets on TV ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: However, the suspects on the news are already being pursued by the police. Even if we make them confess their crimes, the police will take the credit. That won’t do.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit ...  We’re never gonna prove Akechi wrong at this rate ... !

text.Morgana: What the...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Sorry ...  I haven’t eaten anything since yesterday ...

text.Ann Takamaki: And you spent all your money on that box of sweets!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, how much did you have ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: Anyway, we’ll just have to sit tight until we can find another target. So ...
How about that welcome party?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Someone’s excited.

text.Ann Takamaki: Can’t we make hot pot on it?

text.Morgana: That sounds great! I’ve heard that eating hot pot together brings people closer!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Anything with meat’s fine by me!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I only ask that we finish it off with porridge. Extra parsley, of course.

text.Ann Takamaki: So, what do you say?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Whattt!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whattt, my ass! You don’t have any cash! C’mon, let’s go buy ingredients.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’ll need gingko nuts, wonton wrappers, and...

text.Ann Takamaki: (to Maaku)

text.Morgana: We should go grab that pot and set up the portable stove too.
But let’s forget about him for now and just focus on having fun. Come on, we need to prepare. Oh and by the way ...  who’s going to be seasoning the hot pot?

text.Sojiro Sakura: As you should be. Food always tastes better with friends. Her name was Ann, right? She’s a nice girl.

Oh, I just had a chat with her. She said your friend doesn’t have anywhere to go. Asked if I could take him in for a bit. I guess she thought it’d be too pitiful for you to ask, since you’re already freeloading. Anyway, I should have a big pot somewhere around here.
It’s almost time for the others to get back from their shopping trip, so I’ll leave you be. I’ll be down here for a while though ...  Just be careful with the fire, OK?

text.Sae Niijima: This tastes a bit bland ...  But I’m relieved. A lot’s happened, but it seems your grades haven’t dropped.

text.Makoto Niijima: School’s been going fine. I’m more worried about you, Sis. Are you tired? You’re probably lacking sodium.

text.Sae Niijima: Do I seem so?

text.Goro Akechi: (TV)
(TV)

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Is it a crime to manipulate someone’s heart?

text.Sae Niijima: ...Depending on the means, yes. He’s absolutely right.

text.Makoto Niijima: Even if it makes someone admit their evil deeds and helps make them pay for their crimes?

text.Sae Niijima: Why the sudden interest?

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s nothing...

text.Sae Niijima: Do you believe that these "allies of justice" exist?

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Of course not.

text.Sae Niijima: You don’t need to think about such unnecessary things. ...You understand what I’m trying to say, right?

text.Makoto Niijima: Study hard and go to a prestigious college...

text.Sae Niijima: Moving up in the world is difficult as a woman. Yet, you can’t do much if you don’t have the authority. I’ll use every method necessary to make it happen. All you need to do is remain focused on what must be done now for your future’s sake.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Sorry.

text.Sae Niijima: ...Oh, that case.

text.Makoto Niijima: What must be done ...  Justice...
What do I want to do ... ?

text.Morgana: That was delicious, Lady Ann. I’m sure you’ll make a wonderful bride some--

text.ACTION: Well, at least there’s no more Persona 4 jokes about the ladies hilaaaaaaaariously sucking at cooking.

text.Ann Takamaki: (yawn) Sorry, I’m gonna have to borrow the sofa.

text.ACTION: Ryuji and Morgana try to… ugh.
Ann notices and waves them off.

text.Morgana: What’s wrong, Yusuke?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We haven’t finished our meal. What about the porridge, or even udon ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Just leave it for next time, man...

text.Ann Takamaki: (snoring)

text.Morgana: She’s asleep already ... !?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’d be weird if she wasn’t tired. We should let her sleep.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: By the way, Ryuji ...  how do you know Ann?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Oh, we went to middle school together.

text.Morgana: What was Lady Ann like back then?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Not so different from now. Once we got to high school, we ended up in different classes and stopped talkin’ ...  I don’t think she had many friends. I mean, she grew up overseas, plus there’s her looks. The popular kids hate her; the quiet ones stay away.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I see ...  So, what about you two?
This is a great opportunity to get to know each other better. You know every detail of my past at this point. It’s only fair you tell me every detail of yours.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So you got nothin’ to lose, huh? All right, I’ll tell you. It’s just a normal story about a rotten kid though.

I was actually tryin’ to get a track scholarship so I could make things easier for her. In the end, I just screwed it all up. Turns out I’m a pretty bad son, huh? (sad chuckling) Back when I was a first-year, my mom got called out to school for me raisin’ my hand at Kamoshida. All the teachers kept houndin’ her for what I did, but she just stayed quiet through it all ...  I’ll never forget the look she had on her face though ...  On the way home, she ...  she apologized to me. For bein’ a single mom and all ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So that’s what happened ...  They say at school that everyone is equal, but in reality that’s a gross oversimplification ...  ...I understand how you feel.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well when it comes to gettin’ labeled, nobody’s got it worse than Maaku.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Is this about his past?

text.Morgana: Now that I think about it, we never have heard the details.

text.ACTION: They’re not even trying to hide who it is any more.

text.Struggling Woman: If you keep this up ...  Then I’ll report about the money! Is that fine with you!?

text.Masayoshi Shido: All I have to say is that you did it on your own, and it’s over.

text.Struggling Woman: But ...  I just did as I was told...

text.Masayoshi Shido: Who do you think I am?
Hey. Make this statement to the cops. "This kid suddenly attacked me." Got it?
If you even try to say anything else, you know what’ll happen to you, right?
Shut up. You’re done for. You’re gonna learn what happens when you cross me...
So, what happened? Explain it to the good officer.

text.Struggling Woman: ...  ...  That young man suddenly attacked him ...  He shoved this gentleman to the ground. And this man ...  got injured ...

text.ACTION: “I’m very conspicuously not mentioning his name… for dramatic purposes...”

text.Masayoshi Shido: ...It’s as she says. Also ...  make sure you deal with this so my name isn’t mentioned at all.

text.ACTION: The cops even have power over the flashbacks! Those fiends!

text.Masayoshi Shido: You understand what that means, correct?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Goddammit ... ! You got an assault on your record just for that?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The woman sounds quite horrible as well. She’s stayed quiet this whole time ...

text.Morgana: That man is just the kind of person whose heart we should steal! Who is he, and where can we find him!?

You can’t remember, huh ... ? Well it was at night, and I’m sure you were in shock after getting arrested. I understand all too well the pain of not being able to remember important details of your life.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The victim’s personal information is always kept secret. Identifying that man will prove difficult ...  Besides, the courts already made their ruling, didn’t they? Even if we manage to get revenge, Maaku’s past record won’t go away.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I can’t stand it ...  This world is so messed up! The weak’re left to fight for themselves, while rotten adults get away with whatever they want!

text.Morgana: And those in power don’t do anything to help the situation.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Can’t we fix this though ...  Nobody would even know ...  We just need to show the world what true justice is. We’ll make them come to their senses.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You’re right, Yusuke! That’s gotta be what our powers’re for!

text.Morgana: Sounds good to me. The flashier our missions are, the cooler we end up looking!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You’ve all taught me so much.

text.ACTION: It’s really messed up that Ann apparently missed all of that.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh, sorry ...  Did we wake you up?

text.Ann Takamaki: Nah, not really. I’ve been up for a while now. Still, this weird feeling came over me while I was listening to you guys ...  It almost feels like I’ve known you all forever ...

text.ACTION: Can’t wait to find out we were all raised at the same orphanage and our Personas made us forget.

text.Ann Takamaki: Do you think it’s because our backgrounds are so similar?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well ...  it sure ain’t ‘cause of anything good.

text.Morgana: Similar, huh ...  I’m the only one who doesn’t fit in...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hm?

text.Morgana: I don’t have any past to look back on ...  No memories...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whaddya mean? We could search the whole world and we wouldn’t find a bigger misfit than you. And the reason we’re goin’ to Mementos is to get your memories back, right?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’m sure your past will be just as troubled as ours.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: No doubt.

text.Morgana: Hmph, we’ll see about that!

text.Ann Takamaki: I actually feel like I’ve known Morgana for a really long time too. It’s so strange ...  I can’t really put it into words.

text.Morgana: Look, I’m helping you guys out for my own sake. Don’t get me wrong! If you don’t get stronger, investigating Mementos won’t be anything but a pipe dream!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That sure was a quick turnaround. One second you’re depressed, the next you’re actin’ all tough...

text.Ann Takamaki: All joking aside ...  let’s take this seriously. We should go as far with it as we can ...  I want to punish those corrupt adults and give courage to people in trouble ...  Only we can do that!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ha! You can say that again!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Being a member of the Phantom Thieves will surely help me grow, both as an artist and as a person.

text.Morgana: Of course. You’re under my tutelage, after all. There’s nothing we can’t accomplish!

text.Ann Takamaki: Well ...  I hope we can keep this up. We should be all right with you as our leader.
...Whoa, it’s this late?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I guess now’s a good time to call it for the night!

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, that reminds me! The owner said you’re free to crash here, Yusuke.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That’s ...  very kind of him.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You convinced him, didn’t you? You go, Miss Older-dude-charmer!

text.Ann Takamaki: What kind of nickname is that!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm, I won’t be able to sleep unless I take a bath ...

text.Morgana: There’s a bathhouse nearby, so you can go there. I won’t be able to join you though.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ooh, that sounds great! I wanna come too! How ‘bout you, Ann?

text.Ann Takamaki: You guys go on ahead. I should get going. Well, good night, Morgana!

text.Morgana: I can’t let her get taken by someone else ... !

text.ACTION: An old man is continually turning the faucet behind the three.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It’s a bit hot though...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You know, I’ve been wonderin’ for a while now ...  But what do you think about Ann? As a "girl," I mean.
No, that’s not what I meant ...  C’mon, can’t you act a little more like a guy our age? Doesn’t she at least look better than a celebrity?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’ll be sure to share what you’ve said with Ann.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Please don’t. Seriously...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That aside, we need to hurry and find our next target.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: About that though ...  Is targetin’ famous people enough? Seein’ people’s reactions these days has been makin’ me think twice about what we do ...

text.ACTION: I love that we’re having this conversation in front of this old man who isn’t even paying attention.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...True. Pursuing only what’s best in the short term may end up becoming fruitless for us. We need a strategy to appeal to the public...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh? Whaddya got in mind?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Do I look like someone who could come up with such a thing?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I was an idiot for askin’. I’m more like the charge commander ...  and Morgana’s a specialist of that world ...  Hmmm ...  Hrmm ...  Still ...  ...Ughhhh! It’s frickin’ hot!

text.ACTION: Ryuji gets out of the water.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...I can’t stand it anymore! Anyways, let’s meet up again early next week. I’ll contact everyone!

text.Morgana: I’m not talking about you! Wait ...  Don’t eavesdrop on me!

text.ACTION: Tell me more about those diabolical millennials!

text.Newscaster: They have high appeal among young people and are said to be involved in Mr. Madarame’s confession. Their methods are unknown, and many are voicing concern that this group may be dangerous, but ...

text.Joker: It seems a lot of people have started talking about the Phantom Thieves.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I will be fine here. I sleep in my studio on occasion, so this is luxurious in comparison.

text.ACTION: Yusuke, if you’re gonna stay here, we have to establish some boundaries. I may order a maid from time to time, and I’m gonna need you to be cool about this.

text.Caroline: You’re in the presence of our master. Stand up straight!

text.Igor: The bonds that you have reeled in are quite intriguing ...  In other words, they all have been unfairly labeled by society and are standing up against such fates. Have you noticed? Your heart seems to inspire theirs. (chuckle) Outcasts of society ...  In other words, you’re picaresque. Deepen your bonds with them. Those will become the strength behind your rehabilitation.  ... I look forward to it. I shall grant you an ability befitting of your newfound growth. Consider it a gift. May you continue devoting yourself to further rehabilitation.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Igor is growing deeper...

text.ACTION: And we finally get to 10 Persona slots.

Part 49: 6/12-6/13: Blackmail The Second
	Part 48: 6/12-6/13: Blackmail The Second

text.Anon: if ur so just, show ur face

text.Goro Akechi: May I talk to you for a moment?

text.Makoto Niijima: Is it about the Phantom Thieves ...  Akechi-kun?

text.Goro Akechi: ...You’re quite perceptive. I was wondering if there were any points in common between Kamoshida’s and Madarame’s cases. There have been victims, after all. The Phantom Thieves need to be pursued.

text.Makoto Niijima: You criticize the Phantom Thieves, yet you don’t doubt their actual existence.

text.Goro Akechi: Oh, you saw that show on TV. Common sense can get in the way at times when pursuing the truth. Many details become logical if I think on the premise that they do exist.

text.Makoto Niijima: Is this ...  because my sister told you to do so?

text.Goro Akechi: It was just a coincidence.

text.Makoto Niijima: Why do I get the feeling that you’re enjoying this?

text.Goro Akechi: ...You may be right.
Phantom thieves that use calling cards and succeed in their crime ...  As the so-called "Charismatic Detective," it’d be hard for me to not see them as my rival.

text.ACTION: Calling yourself that is kind of the opposite of charismatic.

text.Makoto Niijima: You have such high self-esteem. So the Phantom Thieves are evil, and you are just?

text.Goro Akechi: Compared to people who manipulate others’ hearts as they see fit, I believe I’m on the side of justice. Besides, I’m only using my natural-born talents for the sake of serving the world. Don’t you think the same about yourself too?
... Oh, that’s surprising. So you’re just the good-girl type of pushover.
See you later. Give Sae-san my regards.

text.Sojiro Sakura: You could stay until you find a place, you know. I can’t promise it’d be comfortable here though.

text.ACTION: Well, that was fast. Bye, Yusuke.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Thank you, but I’ll return to the dorms. I realized something after talking with everyone last night. Perhaps it’s due to my upbringing, but I don’t know anything of the world, let alone other people. If I’m to depict people in my art, I need to learn more about them; I must interact with them more. I’ll return to the dorms ...  and start over by talking with the people closest to me.

text.ACTION: I thought everyone was shunning you because of Madarame?

text.Sojiro Sakura: I see. Good on you for realizing that yourself.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: There’s no need to exaggerate. May I come again sometime to enjoy your coffee?

text.Sojiro Sakura: My doors are always open.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Maaku’s been through a lot too, from what I’ve heard ...  Are you related to him?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Huh? Oh ...  How would I describe it ...  We’re just acquaintances. Not family or anything.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I may be overstepping my bounds, but why did you decide to take him in?

text.Sojiro Sakura: My reason, huh ...  Probably because ...  he reminds me of my old self.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That’s all?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Doesn’t take much when someone takes consideration on someone else. Your art instructor-- Um, "former" art instructor. He must’ve felt something for you too, besides just stealing your talents.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Truth be told ...  I cannot hate him from the depths of my heart either. I should probably get going...
Even if I kept it at the dorms, it’d only be met with skepticism. I doubt it would want that. Adding a hint of color to an otherwise ordinary day ...  I’m sure my mother would’ve done the same.

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...I see. I’ll hold onto it for you then.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Thank you for the coffee.

text.Morgana: That’s the first thing you have to say to me ... ? You guys sure do eat a lot ...  That reminds me, I haven’t seen Yusuke around. Maybe he went downstairs?

text.Sojiro Sakura: That kid ended up going back to his dorms.

Don’t be ridiculous. I’d never let go of a beauty like this. This painting is amazing. Not only is the mother stunning, but the expression on her face ...  The regulars will probably freak out when they see it in here. Still ...  I feel like I’ve seen it somewhere. It’s a bit different from how I remember it, though.

text.ACTION: I appreciate that Sojiro kind of knows about Madarame (mostly through Yusuke), but is otherwise so out of touch he can’t recognize the fucking Mona Lisa, which has been all over the news the last week, by sight.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Well ...  If you’re up for the day, go on and get dressed. I opened shop hours ago, so go take the cat out somewhere.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Apologies for leaving so quietly, but your rest seemed peaceful. After a great deal of inner struggle, I have decided to return to the dormitories. Furthermore, I’ve entrusted the "Sayuri" to your protector, Sojiro. That painting should no longer exist in reality ...  but it is truly what my mother painted. I am simply satisfied that we were able to obtain it. And it was all because of you guys. I cannot thank you enough. PS, I still believe porridge is the best way to end a hot pot.

text.ACTION: That’s Yusuke, all right. Udon or death!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: There’s some kinda thread on there looking for info about burglars using the Phantom Thieves name. Sounds pretty lame to me.

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, I saw that too. They target restaurants, right? I actually found a really interesting post on there. "My brother has suddenly started acting violent towards everyone. I might end up getting killed at this rate ...  I wonder if it’s because he got caught up with all those weird people in Shibuya."

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You think he means those burglars when he’s talking about them "weird people"?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It may be too soon to assume that.

text.Ann Takamaki: The post said he started spending a bunch of money lately, too ...  Isn’t that kind of suspicious?
I thought you’d say that.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Although how exactly will we go about investigating?

text.Ann Takamaki: We’ll go to Shibuya in the middle of the night and catch them red-handed! No way. The police’d totally nab us if we were out that late.

text.Morgana: Plus it would be bad if the chief knew you were out in the middle of the night.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm, if they target restaurants ...  Aha! What if we drew them to Leblanc?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What!?

text.Morgana: There’s no way ...  Who would go after a shop like this?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yup. I mean, you’d get kicked outta Leblanc if we failed.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Oh, I suppose I left the "Sayuri" there as well. I had forgotten.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: How’d you forget something that important!?

text.Ann Takamaki: Either way ...  I don’t really want more thieves to be posing as us in the future. I wish there was some way we could make an example of these ones...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: At the moment, our lack of info means we will just have to wait. We can continue searching for more information wherever possible, though.

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I’m gonna try looking for stuff too!

text.ACTION: So, nothing to do but wait, the ever-present Persona refrain.

text.Newscaster: Since the year started, scam victims have been on the rise, mainly in the Tokyo metro area. A massive mafia group is rumored to be behind these scam incidents, but ...

text.Morgana: A mafia group? Huh. I wonder who they might be.

text.Haughty Regular: This just shows that many fail to truly understand what is art. Did you see past Madarame’s lies?

I understand if you feel art is beyond you, but it’s good to take an interest in the finer things. That said, there is no depth to Madarame’s work. It is cheap and base, like instant coffee. Don’t fret if these concepts are difficult to grasp. Art is deep and complex ...  like this coffee.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Yeah, right. Well, you look like you’re on good terms. As long as you don’t cause problems, it’s fine.

text.ACTION: This again? Maaku gains Proficiency +1, sigh.

text.Joker: I don’t think my bond with Ann will deepen just yet...

text.Ann Takamaki: Hm, what should we do today?

text.Joker: Let’s go somewhere fun.

text.Ann Takamaki: OK! Where should we go? Somewhere popular would be nice!

text.Morgana: Shibuya, huh? That’s where the Wilton buffet is ...  Want to go?

text.Joker: Go

text.Ann Takamaki: That buffet we went to before? I’ll need you to make sure I don’t eat too much, OK? Let’s go!
This place has so much on their menu, it’s hard not to overeat ...  Oh! How about this? Operation: Eat a Bit of Everything!

Honestly ...  it was crazy how much my stomach expanded last time. But I’ve reflected on my actions ...  and I won’t make the same mistake again! But, Maaku ...  can you keep an eye on me? I think as long as you do, my resolve won’t crumble.

text.Joker: (nods)

text.Ann Takamaki: Well then, let’s get eating. The order you eat things seems important. Let’s start with the stuff that digests quickly...
No wonder this place is expensive ...  I’m amazed they give out stuff like this! ...I feel like I’d just eat from it nonstop if I kept it at my house ...  Can you take it?

text.ACTION: What on earth am I going to do with this?

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Ann will grow stronger soon...

text.Ann Takamaki: Thanks for today!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Well that’s sudden.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well after what that guy said, sitting around doing nothing just pisses me off!

text.Ann Takamaki: You’re talking about Akechi-kun, right? I know how you feel.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: C’mon, you gotta be more confident about this kinda stuff!

text.Ann Takamaki: But he did mention that the police are starting to mobilize ...  Either way, I don’t think we should leave Akechi-kun be.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: This is the perfect time to meet and discuss what our strategy should be going forward. Let us gather at the hideout tomorrow.

text.ACTION: How the hell did I lug this thing home? And where did I get all the chocolate?

text.Rocker: That’s why I’ve poured my soul into this song—to help restore our hope. I give you ...  "Fake Glory"! Fake shake, fake/Shake, fake, shake/Fake one, if you want fame/You gotta deceive yourself/Fake two, if you want skills/You gotta steal ‘em from others/Fake three, if you want glory/You gotta trick your very soul/Truth, lie, fake with a shake/My future is an unknown fate/ Thanks, bay-bee! How’d you like the new tune?
No way! My songs are the real deal, y’all!

text.Foreign Barker: Naturally! They’re dope! Things’ve been so down in Shibuya lately ...  I keep hearing about all these gangs. Guess Japan’s not so different from my own country...

text.ACTION: We should probably hang out with Mishima now that we can again, since we haven’t done it in a while. I guess.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Oh yeah! As your strategic image management rep, I thought I should come up with more ways to help you. Do you have time today?

text.Joker: Hang out with him

text.Yuuki Mishima: How does the diner sound to you? Come on.
But we’re meeting up with some Phangirls today.
All thieves are supposed to have some special ladies, right?

Wait, really ... ? Phantom thieves are supposed to steal girls’ hearts! Everyone knows that! Basically, I met some cool girls on the Phan-Site, and we thought it’d be fun to do an in-person meet-up. Oh, that reminds me, they think we’re just part of the Phandom. I made up this whole story about how we stumbled on the Phan-Site one day, so let’s stick to that. Don’t spill the beans, OK?

Either way, you should be excited about this! Mingling with your loyal supporters is a noble cause indeed! Plus, remember how I said I’d help publicize the Phantom Thieves? This is just the beginning!

Though to be honest, I’ve never actually met someone from online in person ...  I wonder if I’ll be able to do it right ...  I did lots of research though. I know all about footing the bill and buying desserts for the girl. Apparently if things go well, you might even t-t-take her home ...

text.ACTION: Let’s not get ahead of ourselves, Mishima.

text.Yuuki Mishima: It’s way past our meeting time...
About our meet-up ...  You’re still at home!? And what about your friend ... ? Oh, um ...  yeah. Uh-huh ...  No, we’ll be waiting here...

Wait, was that a train announcement? I could swear I just heard someone say "Shibuya" over a loudspeaker ...  Are you close by ...  Huh? Oh, no! I’m not calling you a liar ...  OK ...  Yeah ...  Maybe next time...
Ahaha ...  (sigh) It seemed like they were really into the idea on the forum...
I was so busy with all the new forum posts, I didn’t have time to really vet them too much.

Don’t worry, I’m not! This was just a learning experience! But all this aside, I have some really good info for you guys! I won’t let you down ...  I’ll prove just how useful I can be to the Phantom Thieves!

text.Joker: Mishima seems extra motivated...

text.ACTION: Oh yeah, gimme that sweet sweet EXP bonus.

text.Yuuki Mishima: It wasn’t supposed to turn out like this though ...  I bet those girls would never have flaked on me if they knew I’m friends with the real live Phantom Thieves.

text.ACTION: Ixnay, Mishima. We have enough problems with Ryuji constantly spouting off about it.

text.Yuuki Mishima: (sigh) Being a guardian of justice isn’t so easy, huh ... ?

text.ACTION: Oh yeah, your job is real tough and real important.
Same, Maaku. Well, at least we’re getting used to Mishima letting us down.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Well, let’s head home.

text.ACTION: Oh, for fuck’s sake, the cops are everywhere

text.Goro Akechi: I didn’t think we used the same station. Meeting here must be fate. How are you doing?

text.ACTION: Because you’re boring me to death.

text.Goro Akechi: Did you stay up too late? Are you all right? ...Ah, I do like that response. It’s honest, and it keeps the conversation from dragging. ...I’ve been getting interviewed a lot lately, so I’ve been wondering how to answer such questions ...  I suppose it is best to simply be yourself and say what you think. You’ve given me much to consider. If it isn’t too much trouble, may I speak with you again sometime?

text.Ushimaru: But what I gave them was a bona fide Japanese bank note. Don’t tell me young people these days don’t know who Hirobumi Ito is. I shudder to think that these will be the people shouldering Japan’s economy ...  I hope you all know your stuff. Here’s a quiz just to make sure. Hey, Hamiru. Paper money is issued by the Bank of Japan, but who issues the coins?

That’s right. Unlike paper money, coins are issued by the government. Originally, the government made both coins and paper money. However, with the ability to make as much money as they wanted, the economy fell into chaos. An independent organization—namely the Bank of Japan—has been tasked with printing paper money since.

Coins, which don’t have as much of an effect on the economy, are still produced by the government. You simply can’t trust a moron to look after your finances. The best they can manage is pocket change.

text.Morgana: Being able to get as much money as you want, whenever you want it ...  I hope the next Palace is somewhere awesome like that...

text.Sadayo Kawakami: She says there’s no report of a lost item, so she wants you to start filling out some paperwork.

Telling me that isn’t going to get you out of this. The student council room is on the third floor, next to the library. Got it? Why am I running errands for a student? I know she’s the Principal’s favorite or whatever...

text.Morgana: What could she want ... ?

text.ACTION: Let’s just take a moment to admire this drawing of Akechi.

text.Female Council Member: I don’t know ...  She does seem a little worried. All I hear her tell us is, "Just leave it to me!"

text.Bespectacled Council Member: It’s great she’s looking out for her fellow students, but I wish she’d let us help her sometimes.

text.Student Council Member: Our president wants a word with you. Don’t cause her any trouble, OK?

text.Morgana: What were we called here for? This is rather strange.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Have a seat.
Mr. Kamoshida and Madarame. Won’t you tell me the truth behind the Phantom Thieves’ incidents?

text.ACTION: I like that Morgana reacts, but Maaku is fucking stone-faced.

text.Makoto Niijima: Can’t answer that? Ah, of course. There’s no way you would admit to such things.

text.Ann Takamaki: So you think it’s true ... ? We’ll be OK if we keep doing this ...  right?

text.Makoto Niijima: ...What could all this mean?

text.Morgana: We screwed up...

text.Makoto Niijima: Was it blackmail? Hypnosis? How do you corner someone into making them confess? Won’t you tell me how you did it?
...You want to say that this doesn’t prove anything, don’t you? I believe that you three are the Phantom Thieves. Now, what would the police think if they heard my recording?

text.Morgana: It’d be bad if we’re put under police surveillance. There’s no telling what’ll happen to you, too!

text.Makoto Niijima: If you confess the truth, I don’t mind just leaving this between the two of us ...  You’ll tell me, won’t you?

text.ACTION: This seems too good to be true.

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s the same as admitting to it, you know.
Go ahead.

text.Morgana: That idiot ... !

text.Makoto Niijima: As loud as always ...  but his timing’s perfect. I’d like everyone else to hear this as well. Won’t you take me to your friends?

text.Morgana: I guess it can’t be helped now ...

text.ACTION: Time to sell the others out!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hm? He here?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Is that girl a friend of yours?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wh-What the hell?

text.Ann Takamaki: What’s the meaning of this?

text.Makoto Niijima: Ryuji Sakamoto, Ann Takamaki ...  And you’re Kitagawa-kun, correct? Second-year at Kosei High and former pupil of Madarame?
While those affected by their acts were just coincidentally meeting up ...  How could that not raise suspicions?

text.ACTION: The others look around at each other.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What do you intend to do? Have you come just to say you’re going to report us?

text.Ann Takamaki: I bet someone told you to find us. The school can’t have ties to criminals, after all! And yet they turn a blind eye when it comes to suicide and sexual harassment. Those adults are just using you. I feel sorry for you.
Huh ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What?

text.Makoto Niijima: I’m the only one who knows about you. If you prove what you’re doing is just, I’ll erase this.

text.Morgana: She wants to make a deal...

text.Makoto Niijima: There is someone whose heart I’d like you to change.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Who?

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm, so you’re not saying it’s impossible. However ...  I cannot tell you that just yet. Let’s continue our talk after school tomorrow. On the roof. Assuming you accept my offer, that is.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Anything to say, Ryuji?

text.ACTION: I mean, it’s completely and totally Ryuji’s fault, no doubt. But also, this isn’t the time to be pointing fingers, because we’re completely fucked up a creek.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Why’re you singlin’ me out? Ann got recorded too, y’know!

text.ACTION: Ann didn’t use the words “Phantom Thieves,” though.

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m so sorry...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, what should we do? That girl’s got dirt on us ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: A recording seems to be insufficient evidence though. And even with that, there’s no way they could prove our methods.

text.Ann Takamaki: Considering who we’re dealing with, I think it might be a trap.

text.Morgana: Regardless, Maaku would be in real trouble. He’s on probation, after all.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Things’d get rough if we didn’t have our leader ...  and I totally don’t wanna deal with the police...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Then ...  we have no other choice but to go along with it.

text.Morgana: Yes, it’s best we agree, at least for the time being. We made a crucial mistake ...  but not a critical one. We’ll just have to recover from here on out.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, yeah. My bad. So ...  we doin’ this?
All right. We’re meetin’ on the school rooftop tomorrow, yeah?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What about me? I could always sneak in if necessary.

text.Ann Takamaki: That’ll draw too much attention. You should just wait outside, Yusuke. What could she be scheming ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Do we just gotta do what she says ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Considering what has happened, it seems we have no other choice.

text.Ann Takamaki: I wonder whose heart the student council president would want us to change.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I am curious myself ...  She mentioned how she wants us to prove our justice, did she not?

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah, she definitely did.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Then there must be some reasoning behind her choice. Please contact me immediately if you find anything out. And don’t go picking any fights, OK? Do you understand, Ryuji?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Why’re you singling me out!? I ain’t dumb!

text.ACTION: Oh geez, what a mystery. Why would someone single out Ryuji for idiocy today of all days?

text.Morgana: She’s a shrewd one. We best be prepared for anything.

text.Newscaster: The Kanto region is expected to enter its rainy season soon.

text.ACTION: Great news if you use Water-types.

text.Newscaster: The Japan Meteorological Agency reports that we should be getting average rainfall this year.

text.Morgana: That means there’ll be more rain from now on, right? It’s gonna be more humid...

text.ACTION: Wonder how all that rain will affect Mementos...

text.Morgana: We’ll see our way through this somehow.

text.Anon: I secretly root for them XD
They seem full of it, so NO

text.Murmur: Do you know about that Phantom Thieves forum?

text.Chatter: People said when they made a request there, it got granted!

text.Whisper: Really? That sounds super useful!

text.ACTION:
Part 50: 6/14-6/15: (Vaguely Witty Title)
	Part 49: 6/14-6/15: (Vaguely Witty Title)
Oh hey, random lady I met once a month ago. I totally remember you.

text.Ichiko Ohya: Morning! Going to school now? I’m just heading home! The morning sun is too bright...
I pulled an all-nighter. Journalist Ichiko Ohya works around the clock, you know! Well, you work hard on your studies.

text.Ann Takamaki: So, whose heart do you want us to change?

text.ACTION: Getting right to the point for once, I like it.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...A mafia boss.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’re you talkin’ about!?

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s what they call themselves. This group seems to be the cause of the rise in phishing scams. What’s worse, once you’re in their sights, they won’t stop threatening you until you get what they want. They’ll force you to take part in their scams, threaten your family, and ultimately destroy your life.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Holy shit...

text.Makoto Niijima: It appears that their victims include some of our students.

text.Ann Takamaki: No!

text.Makoto Niijima: They primarily target juveniles.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’s their boss’s name?

text.Makoto Niijima: Nobody knows.

text.ACTION: Well, uh. Fuck. Can we get an easier one?

text.Makoto Niijima: The victims are being threatened not to testify, so even the police can’t get a grasp of the situation.

text.Ann Takamaki: That’s where you want us to start!?

text.Makoto Niijima: You should be able to pull it off ...  If you’re really the righteous Phantom Thieves. Or is Akechi-kun correct when he says you act without justice?

text.Morgana: Can’t you say something witty back at her?
I knew you were gonna say that!

text.ACTION: Another fun detail of that response I like is that Makoto has no response to it. She just totally ignores you.

text.Makoto Niijima: Their main hub of activity is in Shibuya ...  That’s all the information I have. You have two weeks. Once that has passed, I’ll submit all the evidence I have to the police and to the school.

text.ACTION: Two weeks!? We had more than that for even Kamoshida, and we knew his name!

text.Makoto Niijima: I hope you don’t let me down...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: "Don’t let me down" ...  Dammit, she was just bossin’ us around...

text.Morgana: Come on, we should get in touch with Yusuke.

text.Sae Niijima: Are you saying that Makoto was sticking her nose into this Phantom Thief business ... ?
That’s not the issue here ... ! Why would Makoto...
Fine. I’ll listen to everything you have to say before I decide the truth of your statements.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The mafia? Hm...

text.Ann Takamaki: Can we really do this ... ?

text.Morgana: Either way, we have almost no information on our target. This guy’s a crime boss, so I wouldn’t be surprised if he had a Palace. Still...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Isn’t this a prime opportunity for us though?

text.Ann Takamaki: How!? We’re in huge trouble!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Even after we punished an evil man who seemed to be good, the public did not acknowledge us. However, if we take down an actual criminal, let alone a target the police don’t have answers for...

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, right ... ! That might make people believe in us!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I get it! That means even Akechi’ll hafta acknowledge us as the Phantom Thieves!

text.ACTION: Have you idiots learned nothing? We need a better hideout.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whaddya say, leader?
Hell yeah! We just gotta do what we always do!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Our time limit is two weeks, correct? We can’t afford to waste too much time. ...I’ll ask around Kosei and see if there are any victims.

text.Ann Takamaki: OK, I know some girls who go to Shibuya pretty often. I’ll check with them about it.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All right, then I’m gonna see what I can find on the net.

text.Morgana: I’ll back you up.

text.ACTION: I feel so much better knowing the cat is here with me.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All right, let’s get back together at the end of the week once we’ve got all our info! I’ll get in touch with you guys later!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Could I have a moment?
Well, it’s ...  I had a yearning to see the "Sayuri" ...  So, if you’re heading homeward, I’ll accompany you.
I’m glad I chose to leave it here.

Through my artistic career, there have been moments I’ve struggled with particular motifs or techniques ...  However, those struggles came to pass on each occasion. Yet now I find myself in a similar situation ...  but the more I try to escape it, the worse it becomes. It seems I am trapped in what we in the art world call a "slump" ...  Are you aware that I am attending Kosei on an art scholarship? Such coveted grants are not given as charity. I must continually achieve within my field to remain eligible ...  Were I to lose my scholarship ...  I would likely have no choice but to leave the school as well. In the earlier days of my career, I would exclusively paint what I desired, when I desired it. The only goal I had in mind was the pursuit of pure beauty ...  That goal is what drove me onward. I wanted nothing more than to attain the lustrous allure of the "Sayuri" in my own work ...  Yet what reason do I have now? Holding on to my scholarship? Keeping a roof over my head? Worldly desires are all that spur my brush to move ...  and the resulting work reflects such impurity of mind. To be honest, I am unsure as to whether I can even call myself an artist anymore...

...My apologies. It seems I got somewhat carried away there. But ...  I simply cannot accept this lack of purpose in my work. That is why I am so upset with my own indecision. Such vague ambition is, in essence, a sin of sorts ...  Though I suppose allowing my young career to come to an end here would be even more sinful. I only wish to create a work I can be genuinely proud of ...  Maaku. Please look over there at the "Sayuri." Her incandescent figure, alluring gaze ...  That is the meaning of pure beauty!

text.ACTION: I’m not sure I would use the world “alluring” to describe my mom, but okay.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yet no matter how hard I try to replicate it, an elegance so sweet remains elusive to me ... ! Why is that, you ask? It is surely because the painter behind the work differs ...  Because the soul differs ... ! But if my estimations are correct, the "soul" is nothing but another way to speak of the human heart. What, then, is the heart ... ? How does it bring forth such beauty? I must understand ... !

text.ACTION: This is getting a little heavy for me, man.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...  ...  To be perfectly frank though ...  I am unsure of how to do so. Maaku ...  Would you be able to provide me assistance? You have already brought profound change to my world. Hence, I believe you of all people may be able to bring me closer to the truth.

At the moment, my art teacher has yet to notice any drastic changes in my work ...  But I cannot hide forever. Impurity of the heart will undoubtedly seep onto an artist’s canvas eventually. I must go now. My curfew approaches. I look forward to speaking about this matter again.

text.Joker: I walked Yusuke to the station...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Now, in my expert opinon, Iida of class 2-D is guilty.

text.Ann Takamaki: You mean Iida-kun from our class? Wait, start at the beginning. What’s he guilty of?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Supposedly he’s been spending money left and right recently. Said it’s because of some great part-time job he got.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I see. That may very well be worth looking into.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Right? Can you try asking him about it, Ann? I don’t think he’d be cautious around a girl.

text.Ann Takamaki: In that case, yeah. I don’t mind giving it a try.
Thanks, that’s a huge help.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I’m hoping for some great things this time from Takamaki-san’s world-class wonderful acting.

text.Ann Takamaki: Shut it.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I hopes this will get us even marginally closer to their so-called boss. I leave this Iida to you two. And I have high hopes for your acting as well, Ann.

text.Ann Takamaki: You’re both missing the point!

text.Morgana: Is it true that Iida guy’s guilty? Well, we’ll need to dig up some dirt first thing in the morning.
I can really sense her kindness and tenderness from it. Mothers really are strong.

text.Haughty Regular: Have you ever given it any thought? What is "justice" to you?

I see. That’s one way to look at it, but you only perceive what is on the very surface. The boy who was featured in that TV discussion is still in high school. Akechi, was it? He was well-spoken and skilled in the art of debate—almost as good as I was at that age.

text.Newscaster: A team of reporters followed a police investigator who is on the mafia case. What was clear is that there is little the police can do.

text.Morgana: Even the police are having a hard time. We can’t let our guard down.

text.ACTION: Next, we head over to the diner. Maaku gains Guts +1 and Knowledge +3.

text.Morgana: Ah, the legendary gentleman thief, Arsene. It’s hard not to idolize him—he’s preeminent in our field.

text.Anxious Student: I didn’t think it had anything to do with me, but there are even victims in my class...

text.Fast-talking Student: Oooh, I know all about that! These guys supposedly come asking if you want an easy, high-paying job ...  But then if you say yes, you get dragged into some real shady stuff ...  The teachers or student council prez’ll do something about it though. People’re real worried.

text.Anxious Student: Oh, are you talking about that posting? I wonder if she was serious about it ...  I heard she knew about Kamoshida and the sexual harassment ...  she prolly won’t be too much help...

text.Ann Takamaki: Leave it to me!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That level of motivation actually makes me a little more nervous ...  In any case, let us know if you learn anything.

text.Principal: Apparently the damage done by this so-called mafia has even reached our student body!

text.Makoto Niijima: Well...

text.Principal: Not only are there victims, there are even rumors that some are involved with such crimes ...  I’ve even received inquiries from their guardians. Why is this happening ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: Unfortunately, I do not have the answer to that...

text.Principal: This is the greatest disgrace in the history of this academy ...  If it were to be discovered ...

text.ACTION: I dunno, the principal, teachers, and affected family members actively covering up sexual and physical abuse so outrageous a girl attempted suicide over it still seems a little worse than this.

text.Principal: This is a vital issue for the student council! Did I not ask you to resolve it!?

text.Makoto Niijima: I’m ...  doing the best I can.

text.Principal: A-And I can trust you!? You must do something about this at once! You’re the only one who is reliable around here ...  Don’t let me down...
From what I’ve heard, even the other students are starting to be dissatisfied with you. At this rate, you and I will both lose our roles at this school. Do you understand?

text.Makoto Niijima: I do. Please, just give me a little more time...

text.Hiruta: It’s the only month of the year with no holidays, and it’s filled with rain—truly a season of hell. I’m exaggerating, you say? Haha. You’re all just ignorant ...  After all, what’s falling from the sky is acid rain that can melt metal. Hamiru-kun. Let’s test your knowledge and imagination. What would happen if you keep washing your hair with water that’s contaminated with metal?
That’s right. By the way, your hair will turn green if the metal is copper or red if it’s rust. However, acid rain can’t melt gold or silver. If you want to dye your hair gold, use bronze coins.

text.ACTION: Fuck yeah, gold hair. I’m gonna look like the lamest Super Saiyan.

text.Hiruta: Thinking you could save money by skipping a visit to the hair salon? ...It seems you still don’t understand the horror of acid rain.
London once had acid rain on the level of stomach acid. More than four thousand people died. Perhaps one day such a deathly rain will fall on Japan ...

text.ACTION: Jesus christ, this is one morbid teacher.

text.Hiruta: My heart, too, is overcast, just like the rain that falls on the city ...  Oh rain!

text.Morgana: ...I’m tired of thinking up witty comments.

text.ACTION: I was going to remark on the sudden laziness of the writer, but holy shit, you’re allowed to just stop trying to come up with jokes? Fuck me, this LP is going low-effort from now on!

text.Morgana: You’re gonna back her up, right?

text.ACTION: (tired joke where I refer to Morgana as “cat”)

text.Ann Takamaki: Can you tell me about this easy part-time job? I’m sure you know about it, Iida-kun. Please!

text.Iida: ...  ...  You don’t need my help. A girl like you could probably get a job anywhere, right?

text.Ann Takamaki: Huh ... !? Ummm ...  Now that you mention it ...  Yes ...  So, um ...  What I mean is...

text.Morgana: This is going south fast.

text.Ann Takamaki: O-Oh, Francois!

text.Morgana: Hey, what are you--

text.Ann Takamaki: My cat Francois got run over by a car ...  and also has an incurable illness! I need money fast!

text.Morgana: That’s not convincing at all ...  Is she talking about me ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: If Francois were to die, I think I’d die too! Probably ...

text.Iida: Come on, don’t talk like that...

text.Ann Takamaki: If you don’t like it, then tell me about that easy part-time job. You know something, don’t you? I’ve heard the rumors.
Nishiyama ... ?
Hey, what was that about Nishiyama?

text.Morgana: She actually got the momentum back. She’s not acting anymore now, is she? Come on, let’s leave this guy to Ann and go look for that Nishiyama fellow.

text.Yuuki Mishima: You’re looking for something, right? I want to help you out, so please ask me anything.

So that’s why Takamaki-san was chasing him ...  Rumor is that he’s been spending money like crazy lately. I also hear that he’s been acting ...  weird. If you’re curious about Iida, I’d say it’s best to ask Nishiyama ...  I’m sorry, I don’t know where he is right now ...  He usually stays till late, so I think he’s probably still somewhere in the school. I’ll keep digging around while you’re looking for him!

text.Morgana: ...Well, I guess we can let him handle this.
We’ll have to ask someone else about Nishiyama’s whereabouts. Can you think of anyone who might know?

text.Newspaper Club Member: The student council is on edge. Hurry up ...  Do you have anything you want to ask about?

I heard the muggings, scams, prostitution, and drugs are making them tons of money. Most of their victims have been high schoolers, leading our school to warn its students as well. But ...  nobody actually knows how they operate. Even the police are completely lost.

text.ACTION: (curious response to relieve insecurity regarding my amount of commentary)

text.Newspaper Club Member: The principal asked for us to come forward with any information we might have, right? I heard someone did come to the student council, saying they were being threatened ...  I don’t want to assume this of you ...  but you didn’t have anything to do with that, right?
Iida-kun, from your class? I’ve heard he’s a serious student ...  Although he has seemed a little down lately. I wonder what happened...

Nishiyama-kun? Are you looking for him? He’s a really serious student with great grades. I always see him at the library after school. The library’s just up on the floor above this one ...  Why don’t you go talk to him?

text.ACTION: (pleasant surprise at Newspaper Club Member, one of the better NPCs, having plot-critical information)
(self-deprecation about pushing this gimmick too hard)

text.Friend of Scared Student: Yeah, I heard it’s because of the mafia. They’re even forcing girls to work as prostitutes for them.

text.Scared Female Student: I can’t believe there’s drug dealers in Shibuya now. I wish someone would get rid of them ...

text.Friend of Scared Student: Maybe we should ask the Phantom Thieves? They fight for justice, take down bad guys, right?

text.Studious Male Student: They can’t just tell us to stay away from Shibuya. I have to go to cram school there.

text.Friend of Studious Male Student: This is so dumb. The mafia’s just a bunch of lowlife losers, aren’t they? I don’t care if people want to be criminals, but don’t do anything that might affect my life. Geez.

text.Makoto Niijima: Ah ...  It’s nothing. I was just looking at the bulletin. Anyway, how is the investigation going? I don’t believe there’s much time left at this point.

text.ACTION: (annoyed rebuttal that there was never much time left, and besides, she gave us this mission yesterday)

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm? Perhaps I misjudged your ability? Anyway, this is a very important matter for our school. I hope you can return with good news. And don’t worry ...  I’ll keep my promise as long as you uphold your end of the bargain.

text.Nishiyama: You’re THAT transfer student, right ... ? You need something?

text.ACTION: (mention of overpowering laziness preventing me from making a portrait for this guy)

text.Nishiyama: Iida ... ? How do you know about that? Are you doing something to him!? He’s been acting really strange lately...
Wh-What do you mean? Is he really wrapped up in something shady?

...One day the two of us went to Shibuya, and a man approached us over near Central Street. He asked if we were interested in an easy part-time job ...  I said it wasn’t, but Iida was into it ...  He was asking the guy all sorts of questions.
U-Um, I don’t know ...  I was so scared I ended up going home alone ...  But according to Iida, it only takes ten minutes, and is good for people who don’t stand out.
Iida statted spending a lot of money. That’s when his strange behavior began too ...  But that’s all I know ...  That’s enough, right?

text.Morgana: A man on Central Street, hm? That is suspicious ...  Maybe he was making him commit crimes?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I have tried looking into this high-paying part-time job myself. People seem to be talking about it here as well. Supposedly a man will talk to you in broad daylight over on Central Street ...  And your job is to deliver a small envelope he hands you. Well, I will contact you again if I learn anything more.

text.ACTION: (reminder to the audience that Makoto said these guys were behind phishing scams, which this is emphatically not)

text.Morgana: So that means this part-time job is somehow crime-related ...  It takes ten minutes, is good for people who don’t stand out, and involves a small envelope ...  ...Does that ring any bells? It’s something the mafia would definitely be up to.
What does that have to do with envelopes? And it’s not really something you can do unnoticed. Hmmm ...  Any other ideas? It’s something the mafia would commit.
Like illegal drugs ... ? Maybe they made Iida smuggle drugs for them. That definitely fits with the small envelope, and you can get arrested just for possession...

text.Yuuki Mishima: Well, I looked into Iida on my own anyway. Rumor has it he got involved in some kind of suspicious part-time job. And that job’s apparently totally insane ...  Something about trafficking drugs, I think. I hear they ask you to take part in it down on Central Street. In broad daylight, even ...

text.Morgana: So he is smuggling ...  This won’t be pretty. Come on, let’s go back to Lady Ann! We’ll ask Iida directly!

text.Yuuki Mishima: No problem. I just want to see you guys succeed. You wanted to ask Iida something, right? He’s still in the classroom with Takamaki-san.

text.ACTION: (defeated sigh at no one ever understanding sarcasm)

text.Morgana: She’s still doing that ... ? All right, take over for her.

text.Iida: Hamiru ... !? Come on, you too ... ? I already told you, I don’t know...
He did!? That bastard ...  Dammit!  ...  ...  Shit ...  Well, if you already know about it, fine ...  But I don’t want to talk about it here. Let’s go somewhere a little quieter.
Yeah, I got a job! So what? Isn’t that normal? ...What’re you getting at?

text.Morgana: That’s right! You have to smuggle it to people while it’s still hot! I mean, not that kind of smuggling! Tell him what you heard earlier!

text.Iida: I don’t know what you’re talking about.

How do you ... ? I’ve only told one person about that ...  Of all people, I can’t believe you were the one to find out ...  Y-You’re right ...  They told me they had an easy part-time job for me, and I ended up smuggling drugs ...  All I had to do was put envelopes into coin lockers, and they said they’d give me a hefty paycheck. I didn’t know what was in the envelopes though! Still, this is what came out of it...

So you knew, huh ...  They started threatening me right after they deposited the money into my bank account ...  They had pictures of me carrying the goods. Said they’d expose what I did unless I paid them off ...  You know ...  why are you even asking me this stuff ... ? Are you just gonna use my job to blackmail me too ... ?

text.ACTION: (statement mourning the death of Maaku’s reputation)

text.Iida: I see ...  Well even if you were planning on doing that, I don’t have any money I could give you ...  If you’re really interested in that job, try heading over to Central Street. That’s where they told me about it ...  I-I told you everything you want to know, right? Can I go? Well then...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Did Ann’s acting help at all? I’m thinking prolly not.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So they ask you to deliver drugs...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That’s serious. I just searched for "Shibuya drugs" and got tons of hits too.

text.Ann Takamaki: So they’re making people traffic drugs, then threatening them ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That must be what I heard people talking about in Shibuya. They seem to be going about this quite openly during the daytime. What bold methodology.
I see. Yes, more students will be out during the day, while the police will be more cautious at night.

text.Ann Takamaki: Ryuji, you’re over in Shibuya now, right? Do you see anyone like that there?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, I’m at Central Street. It’s tough to tell though.

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah, that seems like our only choice now. We can split up and search separately then.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: In any case, we have some new intel. Let us call that progress for today.

text.Ann Takamaki: Whoever asks us to take on that job should know who their boss is too.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All right, I’ll get in touch with you guys later tonight and we can come up with a plan.

text.ACTION: (joking expression of equal disappointment to see Sojiro)

text.Sojiro Sakura: I never get many customers when it rains. The cash register is gonna run dry at this rate...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes. It is highly likely that this part-time solicitor is somehow related to the mafia.

text.ACTION: (confusion at the continued use of the word “mafia” rather than “yakuza”)

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: If we tail him, he may lead us straight back to his boss.

text.Ann Takamaki: That’s not a bad idea. Cats have nine lives, right? Morgana can spare one for this.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wouldn’t the mafia get caught off guard if they had a cat coming to deliver drugs for ‘em?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: In other words, Maaku will be going. I have no objections.
Tricking people and using that as blackmail ...  These bastards are true cowards.

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s kinda scary to think people like that are all around us in this city...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well guys, we gotta brace ourselves. We’re up against a serious criminal here.

text.DTD Reporter: Relaxing at the park is nice, and the view from the Ferris wheel is really something!

text.DTD Co-host: Yes, the Ferris wheel is really popular among couples. I’d love to ride it with a cute girl someday.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: I barely get any customers on rainy days ...  Umm ...  Master, are you hungry at all? Now we’re offering special services like "Maid’s Cooking" and "Together with a Maid"! ♥
With the request fee included ...  It’ll only cost you 5,000 yen! It’s practically a steal!

text.Joker: Call her over

text.Sadayo Kawakami: What!? ...Seriously? I-I mean, thank you for requesting me. Then, please wait for me, Master! I hope you have a big appetiiiite!
The high-end cup noodles really do make a difference, don’t they?
They are pretty complicated though ...  It says to drain the hot water once and leave the sauce packet on the lid so it gets warm ...  Don’t request me if you’re going to complain.

text.ACTION: (confusion at the change in tone caused by the conversation branch, though maybe she thought that was sarcasm)

text.Sadayo Kawakami: ...Besides, I thought I warned you already. Why would you request me again ... ?

Hmmm ... . Are you sure that’s really the reason? ...Well, I guess I’m in no position to complain, since I’m making money from it. (yawn) I’m so tired ...  We had a faculty meeting just the other day. Why do they have to last so long ... ? Thanks to the Phantom Thieves ...  The students have been really restless lately. The teachers can’t agree on what to do about them or the Phantom Thieves. I wished they talked more about our bonus instead. I heard they might even cut the teachers’ salaries ...  I’m so sick of it...
I’ll continue to serve you with all my might, Master! (sigh) ...I’m going to be in trouble if I don’t pick up more shifts.
What ... ? How much!? I can’t ...  ...Yes, but ... ! That ...  That’s true ...  ...Sure.  ...  ...  Yes ...  Yes, I understand ...  Yes, it’s my responsibility, after all ...

Uh, apparently it’s some crazy incurable disease, so there’s a lot of fees and extra charges! That’s why it would really help if you requested me more ...  Oh, never mind. You’re my student. I can’t keep relying on you ...  Ughhh ...  What am I going to do ... ? Anyway, it’s time for me to go. Hey, feel free to call me to do housework. It doesn’t have to be through the maid service. I live close by, so I can stop over whenever you need me. Besides, I’m worried that you can’t cook or do laundry because you don’t have your parents ...  Oh, and if your friends suddenly come over, I can always leave out the back way.

text.ACTION: (expressed internal confusion over how massive a nightmare of a situation this is)

text.Joker: I feel Kawakami’s kindness...

text.ACTION: (confident summation of critical gameplay feature that turns out to be totally incorrect after like six corrections from the audience)

text.Sadayo Kawakami: In any case, I need to talk to my boss about giving me more shifts ...  I need to get requested more ...  Good night.

text.Morgana: Oh yeah, something weird happened in food service before, right? Some employee cooking naked ...  With all these extortions and scams ...  this world’s really messed up.

text.Dissatisfied First-Year: I hear her older sister’s involved with the investigation. Maybe she’s just trying to play detective, too.

text.Energetic-Looking Guy: Are you kidding me? I can’t handle a student council president with no focus. She and the principal can both get lost.

text.Morgana: We might end up running into the mafia. Be ready for anything!

text.Makoto Niijima: I hope something comes of it. I’ll be counting on you.

text.Patrolling Officer 2: They appear and disappear as they please ...  Not only that, but they blend in with normal teenagers...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Is she keeping an eye on us?

text.Ann Takamaki: Maybe. I guess she’s curious about all of this.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well let’s just ignore her if she’s not getting in our way. More importantly, how’re things on your guys’ end?

text.Ann Takamaki: Nothing so far. I’m going to try staking out the underground walkway.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then I’ll check around the Inogami Line. I guess I’ll get there from the underground.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I will gather some more intel in the underground shopping mall as well. Please continue on your end, Maaku.

text.Morgana: Everyone’s really going about this seriously. They’re definitely worth of being phantom thieves. We can’t fall behind either. Let’s look for that homeless man.

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm ... ? You’re trying to find a homeless person? That’s a good idea. They would know a lot about what goes on in this town. I haven’t seen any here, but I would bet there are some in the underground area...

text.Morgana: Underground ...  I don’t like the idea of it, but we should go check it out.

text.ACTION: Sure enough, it’s the homeless guy we chat with from time to time.

text.Homeless Man: A part-time job ... ? You’re not talking about some ordinary job, huh? Take my advice: Don’t do it. They’ll squeeze every last penny out of you with threats and extortion. Some of my friends have fallen victim to their schemes ...  That mafia is evil, I tell you.

It’s easy to say that, but none of them have places to go ...  Just don’t go anywhere near that mafia. But just so you know who to avoid, I’ll teach you how to tell them apart from normal people. They use some weird phrases. Code words, you know. That’s how they communicate with each other. Anyway, watch out if you hear any of that stuff. They’ll try to come for you even during the day. They’re relentless when it comes to targeting teens.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Ah, so you’ve grasped something already. As to be expected of someone like you, Maaku.

text.Ann Takamaki: Why don’t we just go over the intel we’ve gathered so far?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I’ll start. Supposedly some guy near the accessway talking about some kinda "strong drugs." I’m not counting on anything, but I’ll go check it out.

text.Ann Takamaki: As for me, I heard about someone soliciting a "high-paying job" in the station plaza. Apparently they’re mostly targeting girls. I’ll go see what it’s about.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: On my end, I heard there are people saying strange things in the back alley near the arcade. Something about ice and vegetables, and something about snow tomorrow ...  I will go observe, just in case. The arcade is on Central Street, correct?

text.Morgana: All right, we should do what we can to help them out. I have no idea which of these leads are real. Try going to the most suspicious-sounding place.

text.ACTION: Let’s think this through. Despite Ryuji and Ann’s leads sounding more outright suspicious, they don’t have any elements of code words, leading us to conclude it’s almost certainly Yusuke’s lead that’s the correct one. That said, we should at least check out those other two first because they might be funny.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uhhh ...  Go down those stairs, then turn left. Be careful, granny.

text.Kind Old Woman: Oh, Shibuya is so complicated. These bones don’t move like they used to either. How troubling.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Arghhh, c’mon...

Sorry, my lead didn’t end up bein’ anything. That dude at the stairs ...  Pretty misleadin’, huh? Sheesh ...  Oh, what about Ann and Yusuke? You should go check on ‘em. Hey, granny, you OK? You’re lookin’ pretty shaky, so I don’t mind givin’ you a hand.
Uh, thanks. I dunno what I’m even doin’ here though ...

text.Morgana: He said his lead didn’t amount to anything. We should leave this area to him, OK? Come on, let’s go see Lady Ann and Yusuke.

text.Tall Man: I’ve heard it’s super effective. Even the most barren deserts will become lush forests of hair ...

text.Morgana: So that’s who Ryuji was talking about. Lush forests ...  I don’t really want to know. I guess I can see how you’d mistake him for what we want though.

text.ACTION: I’ll do whatever! Squat cobbler, you name it!

text.Lighthearted Scout: Huh? You ...  want to be in one of our videos? I guess I can’t say there’s no demand ...  but our company only hires girls. Sorry.

text.Morgana: ...Be in a video? What kind of job is that? Though I guess that doesn’t have anything to do with drugs. It must not be him.

text.Ann Takamaki: Look, someone’s asking about a video shoot over by the train ...  but I guess that’s for models? In any case, they’re not here. Go try seeing what Ryuji and Yusuke have.

text.Cop: Arcade ... ? You’re a high school student, aren’t you? You’d better not be looking for trouble. All kinds of shady activity happens at arcades.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What are you talking about? It’s nothing more than a place you go to play games...

text.ACTION: This must be the alley Yusuke was referring to.

text.Makoto Niijima: Well ...  you aren’t wrong about that.
It seems we didn’t have to look very hard in the end.

text.Over-Friendly Guy: You’re high schoolers, yeah? Don’t you want something more than just your allowances?

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm ...  by delivery, do you mean that of suspicious materials?
So you won’t answer me? Then I was right...

text.Over-Friendly Guy: What’s up with you anyways? Why’re you asking all these questions, huh?

text.Makoto Niijima: Oh ...
U-Um, if you don’t want to deal with us, we could always go see your boss ourselves.

text.ACTION: No seriously, what the hell are you doing?

text.Over-Friendly Guy: You’re really gonna say that, knowing who he is? Heh, no way I believe that. Welp, I’m outta here. You guys are annoying me.

text.Makoto Niijima: I think we should get some proof before we do that. I tried to trick him into saying something, but he dodged all the traps I was laying down.

text.ACTION: Yeah, real great attempt there. Not only did you not learn anything, you almost got your ass kicked.

text.Makoto Niijima: By the way ...  thanks for standing up for me. I’m going to go now.
