text.Morgana: No wonder the police are having trouble catching him. Anyway, you have some serious guts. You didn’t back down at all against that hooligan. Though we still didn’t end up with any new information ...  Let’s stop here for today.

text.Ann Takamaki: That would be best. We did ask tons of people, so there’s a chance we’re being followed.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Just to be safe, we should refrain from doing anything to make ourselves stand out. The sun will be setting soon, so let us disband for today and report on our findings tomorrow.

text.Ann Takamaki: Why don’t we meet at karaoke tomorrow? We can talk in private, and it’ll be cheap after school.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Ah, that must be what they call hustle hour.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, it’s muscle hour. Wait, is that wrong too?

text.Ann Takamaki: Um, hello? Happy hour. Muscle hour just sounds sweaty ...  Anyway, see you guys at karaoke tomorrow.

text.Makoto Niijima: Thanks. For earlier.

...I wanted to apologize. I got a hold of your number without asking you, so ...  I realize I’m apologizing after the fact, but ...  It just didn’t feel right, keeping it from you, so ...  ...That’s all. Bye.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Speaking of, some girl called looking for you around noon. Said she’s the class president. Said she’s got something that belongs to you. She seemed to know you, so I gave her your number.

text.Morgana: She must’ve looked up Leblanc’s address trying to contact you. That Niijima sure is thorough! Then again, she called you just to apologize ...  It’s a bit weird, but maybe she’s not so bad after all.

text.Newscaster: An employee was arrested, but claims to be unable to recall any details of the crime. When questioned about his motive, the employee insisted he did not know what came over him. Incidents with suspects whose motives are unclear have been happening often in the restaurant industry ...

text.Morgana: It’s weird that they don’t remember. How is anyone supposed to prevent these weird crimes?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Are you helping out today?

text.ACTION: We can finally rank up, so let’s hang out with him.

text.Joker: Help him out

text.Sojiro Sakura: I’ll teach you how to make good coffee. Its taste all depends on you though.
These beans are Colombian, a medium-fine city roast. Oh, and don’t let the water boil too much. ...You’re gonna be fine. I’ll be here the whole time.

...Not bad. Though I guess anyone can do something as simple as just brewing it. Making a blend, on the other hand, is a different story. Mixing beans at random won’t do you any good. That’s because the acidity and the flavor profile all depend on the bean ratio. Pretty deep, huh?

If you’re really that interested, feel free to try out whatever combinations you want to. ...Oh, but hands off the expensive beans, got it? Next up is the curry. There’s something special about its flavor. The truth is, a scientific genius actually came up with the perfect spice combo to complement my coffee.

Something about the quantification of taste ...  There’s no formula for flavor, but it IS pretty damn good. Anyhow, we don’t make compromises when it comes to food service. Our stuff’s gotta wow the customers. This is a tiny shop, after all. Self-satisfaction is the only thing that keeps me going.
Haven’t I already told you I don’t have the money? Look at this place. You see many customers in here?

text.Futaba's Uncle: Oh, no need to hide it, Sakura-san! You must have saved plenty from your time working in the government. Aren’t you taking care of that employee right there too, for nothing more than charity? I wish you’d show me the same kindness you show others.

text.Sojiro Sakura: If you’re not planning on buying anything, can you please leave? I’m expecting a phone call, so I don’t have time to chat with you.

text.Futaba's Uncle: I don’t mind if you take the call in front of me. I can talk to your little friend here in the meantime. So, should we keep talking until your call comes in? Or would that be too inconvenient for you?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Well ...

text.Joker: It looks like Sojiro’s in trouble. What should I do ... ?

text.Sojiro Sakura: They come ‘round pretty often to make sure this guy’s not getting in any trouble. Want me to introduce you?

text.Futaba's Uncle: ...Oh, that’s right! I have some business I need to take care of myself! I’ll come back later!

text.ACTION: Wonder what all this is about.

text.Sojiro Sakura: (sigh) I guess I should explain what’s going on. He might try and drop by when I’m not around. ...That man is an old acquaintance of mine who’s short on cash right now. Looks pretty friendly, yeah? Don’t let him fool you—It’s all an act. I have to say though ...  I’m surprised you were quick-witted enough to pull that stuff off.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Sojiro is growing deeper...

text.ACTION: Curry restores 20 SP for all allies, but you can only make it on certain dates, and it still consumes time. Considering how packed our nights already are, it’s not really worth it, especially once we get those SP Adhesive 3s from Takemi. Also, it counts as a “food” item and can’t be used in battle.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Still ...  why do you poke around into other people’s troubles? It’s way easier to ignore them. I guess that’s just the kinda person you are though, huh...
(sigh) I’d report him to the cops if he wasn’t related to her...
Oh, uh ...  never mind that. Anyway, that’s it for today. Go ...  study or something after you close up.

text.Joker: I can see the compassion hidden beneath Sojiro’s actions ...  I feel my Kindness growing...

text.Murmur: I’ve got a job you could do. Wanna hear more?

text.Chatter: Another psychotic breakdown?
Oh, you mean how they’re increasing security in Shibuya?

text.ACTION:
Part 52: 6/17-6/18: A Hate Crime
	Part 51: 6/17-6/18: A Hate Crime

text.Goro Akechi: Speaking of murky ...  there haven’t been any new developments in the phantom thief incidents. If they go so far as using calling cards to get attention, I doubt Madarame’s case will be the last. What kind of target will they choose next? What do you think?

The Phantom Thieves only target criminals, huh ...  Is that really true? Supposing it is, there are plenty of villains in the world. How do they choose who to go after?  ...  ...  ...Oh, sorry. I’m getting lost in my head ...  I have to stay on top of any Phantom Thieves activity due to what I said on the air. If you hear any rumors at school, I hope you can let me know.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real!? We didn’t get anything!?
Man, we’re goin’ nowhere with this ...  Hey, can’t we ask Miss President to change it up?

text.Ann Takamaki: You mean ...  change our target?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We just gotta show our justice to satisfy her, right? There are tons of shitty adults in this world. It’s not like it matters who we’re goin’ after. She says this is for the students, but I bet it’s just so she can go brag about it on college apps.

text.Ann Takamaki: But that mafia’s stealing money from kids. We can’t just accept that! It doesn’t matter who the target came from anymore.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Ann’s right. We want to give courage to the weak. Isn’t this the perfect target to accomplish that goal?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I never thought it’d be this noisy if you weren’t singin’ ...  Anyways, I’m sure we’ll shut Akechi up if we pull this off, but--

text.ACTION: Oh? Akechi? I ran into him earlier today, we had a nice chat.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That’s exactly why we should do it.

text.Morgana: It all comes down to intel in the end ...  If we don’t start finding tips on that front, we’ll never get any further than this ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: There has to be someone who has what we need.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...That’s right! What about that journalist?

text.Morgana: You mean the woman who was staking out Madarame’s house?

text.ACTION: Yusuke has no questions at all about this mysterious woman who was staking out his home.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh yeahhh. I completely forgot about her! Didn’t she give you her card?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...This is for a rather major publication.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You think we can trust her?

text.Morgana: There’s no other way.

text.Ann Takamaki: OK, let’s contact her!
He says our time’s up. Should we extend it?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Happy hour’s over, yeah? C’mon, let’s just go.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: How wasteful!

text.ACTION: Yusuke starts chugging his drink and begins to cough.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Let us know ASAP when she responds! Got it, Maaku?

text.Joker: (nods)

text.Morgana: The chief’s as sharp as ever ...  But it’s more like we’re the ones being dragged into things...

text.ACTION: We can hang out with Sojiro today, too. I’m gonna let you in on a little secret, though: we can’t rank him up for a long-ass time.

text.Newscaster: The police stated that they are dedicating all their efforts to prevent more victims of the mafia. However, they have failed to make good on that promise, and the public’s unease has only grown.

text.Morgana: They’re hurting a lot of people. I really wish we could find some sort of lead.

text.Joker: I don’t think my bond with Kawakami will deepen just yet...
I feel like my bond with Kawakami will grow stronger soon...

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Thank you for your patronage!

text.Sae Niijima: They were asking if you’ve made any lifestyle changes recently.

text.Makoto Niijima: Huh ... ?

text.Sae Niijima: I gave them a suitable enough answer, but ...  is there some kind of issue at school?

text.Makoto Niijima: No ...  It’s nothing. I’m sorry to worry you.

text.Sae Niijima: I doubt you would do such a thing, but try to avoid wandering around Shibuya late at night. I’ve heard stories of girls your age throwing their lives away out there. They got involved in criminal acts and were blackmailed into working at illegal sex establishments...

text.Makoto Niijima: ...  ...  I’ve heard rumors about that as well. People have been mentioning it at school.

text.Sae Niijima: ...These aren’t mere rumors. I know of a few such cases.
Well, it should be nothing or you to worry about. Just concentrate on your studies for now.

text.ACTION: “Don’t go out late or you’ll get blackmailed and forced to work as a prostitute! Well, good night!”

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We only just emailed her the other day. Why are you so hasty?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I dunno. I’ve been looking for info, but I can’t find a damn thing ...  We only got two weeks left, man. Duh we’re in a hurry.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: To be more precise, it’s ten days.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We ain’t gonna have much time, even if we start right after she responds.

text.Ann Takamaki: Looks like this battle will have to be a quick one then.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We must also consider what we do in case she fails to respond entirely.

text.Ann Takamaki: Hey, don’t jinx this!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I am merely discussing all the possible outcomes.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ain’t you nervous about this?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Nervousness will not help us solve anything at this point. Were that the solution to our problem, I would be much quicker to turn to panic.

text.Ann Takamaki: Wow, he’s like some kind of philosopher ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I think he’s just an idiot...

text.Iida: You said you would keep it a secret, but rumors have started getting out ...  Wait ...  You didn’t leak that information, did you!?

text.Makoto Niijima: Calm down ...  They’re still targeting you?

text.Iida: Even that delinquent found out. He might try and threaten me too ...  Why is this happening to me ... ? I can’t afford to keep paying...

text.Makoto Niijima: I’ve found some clues regarding your incident. I just need you to wait a bit longer.

text.Iida: You’re really gonna help ... ? Everyone thinks you’re just doing it for a letter of recommendation...

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s not true. My goal here is to protect the students of this school ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: However, do you remember that thread about the group of burglars in Shibuya? It seems the one who posted about his brother is a student at my school. And so after some prodding, I was able to pry a few more details out of him.

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, right! I was actually wondering about that. It didn’t sound like they had anything to do with the mafia we’ve been chasing.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Indeed. Now, I was able to ascertain his brother’s name ...  It’s Kazuya Makigami.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, it’s freaking crazy that someone involved in that shit goes to your school. Nice going, Yusuke!

text.Ann Takamaki: And you even found the name of the guy we’re looking for! That was super awesome!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All we gotta do now is punish him in Mementos. This burglar guy isn’t gonna be near as scary as the mafia. He’s just a plain dude, right? We’ll show him what being a phantom thief’s really about!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It seems we are unanimous then. We can further discuss the details at the hideout.

text.Morgana: We have our target! We also have the mafia to deal with too, so make sure the timing’s right. Anyway, let’s all meet up at the hideout when you’re ready.
Hey, shouldn’t you tell the others about what Mishima told you?

text.ACTION: I have no idea what you could possibly be referring to, cat.

text.Energetic Student: Right? It’s like he’s a prince. He’s the Detective Prince!

text.ACTION: Uhh, that title is already occupied, thank you.

text.Energetic Student: I love hearing that suave and soothing voice of his too! I wish he would talk to me like that.

text.Calm Student: But you know, Hamiru-kun actually debated with Akechi-kun, and he didn’t do too badly.

text.ACTION: Aww yeah, people are finally treating me with the respect I deser--*trips and splits my head open on a desk*

text.Newspaper Club Member: Don’t you think it’s terrible how he insists that the Phantom Thieves are dangerous?
His prettiness is irrelevant to me! Professional journalists need to be impartial. Is what the Phantom Thieves did that bad? The truth is that people have been saved by them.

text.ACTION: Remember that scene we shared with Yusuke a little while back? That let us start hanging out with him.

text.Joker: This may be a good opportunity to deepen my bond with Yusuke...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Maaku, do you have time?

Do you remember how I mentioned my need to understand the heart? Well, I am having a hard time grasping it. How will I be able to reach the truth of pure beauty ... ? Maaku, what should I paint to capture the contents of the heart?

Hm. The scenery of one’s heart ...  Ah, I see ... ! Mementos! The desire that emanates from that place is the root of humanity! Incredible! You honestly have a unique perspective on things. With that destination in mind, let us make haste!

The same thing which brought forth the beauty of the "Sayuri" can also create such morbid fabrications ...  But I actually find that aspect to be quite fascinating ...  The heart is akin to an abyss ...  Now, regarding the source of my slump ...  I actually have an idea. In that other dimension, I saw the perversion of Madarame’s heart ...  At that moment, the art realm I had so much faith in was distorted by greed and unchecked desires. That is when the true ugliness of the world became clear to me ...  And from that point forward, my brush has been stayed by crippling hesitation ...  Does pure beauty truly exist ... ? And if so, can hands tainted by Madarame’s depravity capture it ... ? Considering such intense questions only served to distance me from reality. Doubt filled my mind. I struggled to find a reason to move my brush again ...  And honestly ...  I still have yet to discover a suitable answer.

text.ACTION: Oh my god you can just talk forever, can’t you?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Please, do not rush me. I only need a little more time ...  Hm. The lingering uncertainty present in this place seems to be sharpening my senses ...  I feel a revelation approaching ...  Hm, yes ... ! Inspiration has struck ... ! That must be it ... ! Such brilliant composition! Ah, my heart races ... !
Hmph, how inelegant! You wish to carry out your distorted will, foolish Shadow? I shall cut you down for interrupting my work ... !

text.ACTION: Don’t fuck with Yusuke. Lesson learned.

We’ve got five Viscid Rotting Meats to take care of, and while they pack more health than normal Slimes, they go down fairly simply to a healthy combo of Mabufu and Yusuke’s Vicious Strike to score those sweet sweet Technical bonuses.
And we get a Blank Card for our troubles. Keep that in mind going into this next scene.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’m glad you were here. You have my thanks. You’re like Theo.

... I worry that you may not get what I mean. It was a figure of speech. I was referring to Van Gogh’s brother, Theo. Van Gogh did not achieve fame in his lifetime, but found an admirer and supporter in his brother.
Well, there aren’t many who are willing to deal with my ...  eccentricity. By the way, what’s in your hand ... ? A card?
...  ...  Whenever I see blank paper, I have the urge to draw something on it. ...May I?
(chuckle)  ...  ...  Impossible!  ...  ...  Good ...   ...  ...  What!?  ...  ...  Hrrm ...   ...  ...  A satisfactory result.
My picture ...  turned into a real skill card?

Indeed ...  Maaku. Would you mind helping me further? If I can overcome this slump, I should be able to aid our group like earlier—perhaps even more so. I know ...  Why don’t we act as the thieves we are and strike a deal?
Yes. You can rely on me.

text.Joker: I can sense Yusuke’s trust in me...

text.Sae Niijima: I don’t have a clue how these cards were used, but someone proficient in the arts was close to you ...  ...What were you having this person do!?

text.ACTION: The Emperor is the arcana of authority and structure, but also excessive control and inflexibility when reversed. It represents the patriarch.

This is very similar to a feature that was in Persona 3 Portable, except this time you actually get to choose the card and it only takes a day. Again, skill cards are a great way to break the game but a more casual player won’t need them much, especially due to their relative infrequency in this game.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’ll contact you once it’s done. I’ll see you later.

text.Joker: The journalist responded to me...

text.Morgana: This is from that journalist, right? She wants to meet you there now ... ? Looks like this Crossroads place is in Shinjuku. A meetup in Shinjuku...
Let me see ...  I guess to put it simply, it’s a nightlife district for adults.

text.ACTION: Well, now I’m concerned as to why the cat knows what Shinjuku is like.

text.Morgana: You should send everyone a message and let them know what you’re up to.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That sounds rather dangerous.

text.Ann Takamaki: Where should we meet up?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Stand by, Ann. It’ll be easier to move around with less of us.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: My apologies. I don’t have the money to take the train there.

text.ACTION: My god, Yusuke, how are you still alive?

text.Ann Takamaki: If Maaku’s going, I guess there’s no need to worry. We’ll leave it to you then.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well, I guess that’s that. Let’s meet up in Shibuya.

text.Ann Takamaki: Be careful, you two.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I shall be sure to save money for situations like this from now on.

text.Morgana: It would be bad for you to stand out. You should change before you go.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? No choice. I didn’t have the time to go home. People aren’t gonna notice anyways with this t-shirt over it.

text.Morgana: That’s not the issue! Are you both idiots? I’m just saying now, I won’t be to blame when you get caught by the cops.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Don’t worry about it. That place ain’t so different from Shibuya. C’mon, I’ll guide you. If we’re goin’ to Shinjuke ...  we should probably hop on the JL. Just get outta this building and then the ticket gate should be on the right. It’s go time!

text.ACTION: Yeah, can’t wait to enjoy some of that nice “conversation.”
We’re somehow only getting the tutorial about train fares now.

text.Morgana: Stop looking around so much. You look like a tourist.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I-I was just tryin’ to find that place we’re lookin’ for. Crossroads Bar’s right up ahead. I’m sure we’ll get there if we keep goin’ straight.

text.Bar Promoter: Oh? In that case come in for an hour or two!

text.Morgana: How did you get caught up in this!? Come on, ignore him!

text.ACTION: Further down the street, we are accosted yet again...

text.Suspicious Salesman: Touch all you want, no added fees. We have the cutest girls in town too.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Did you really just ask that?

text.Morgana: Just ignore that guy, you idiot. No matter what way you cut it, he’s a shady character.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Maybe they got some cool stuff to read. Wanna go check it out a bit?

text.ACTION: Yeah, I’m sure it’s full of… enlightening material.

text.Morgana: You don’t have time for that right now. Save it for later. Meeting with that journalist comes first!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, OK. We’ll go here some other time.
Yup. People mistake us all the time for younger kids though.

text.Patrolling Officer: Wait a second ...  I’ve seen the pattern on those pants before. Maybe it was on the news ...  Oh yeah, it was on that segment about the teacher who was harassing kids! Is that a school uniform ... !?

text.ACTION: Foiled once again by that stylish plaid!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...Shit.

text.Patrolling Officer: You kids have got to be high schoolers! Come with me!

text.Morgana: Shoot! This is why I said uniforms were a bad idea! Let’s run!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, it ain’t our fault we had to deal with that detour! Our school’s gettin’ real famous!

text.ACTION: Oh hey, random woman. I wonder why you have a portrait.

text.Chihaya Mifune: In any case, horrible disaster is coming for you! Please let me examine your future further!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What!? Me?

text.Chihaya Mifune: Yes, I suggest you get your fortune told! What I say will surely come to pass!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: More of this shit ... ? Sorry, but we’re in a hurry. I don’t really believe in that stuff anyways.

text.Chihaya Mifune: I see. My apologies. However ...  if you change your mind, I’ll be waiting here in this spot at night. May your fortunes be well...

text.Morgana: Beer, whiskey, wine ...  Looks like nighttime is bar time.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Goin’ in our uniforms is probably a bad idea ...  We got caught last time too...
I came all the way to Shinjuku and can’t even go in ... ? Fiiine. I’ll kill time somewhere nearby ...  Just lemme know when you’re done.

text.Lala Escargot: How old are ya, boy?

text.Ichiko Ohya: Sorry, Lala-chan. He’s with me.
Go on back there. I’ll treat you to some water!
Haha, what a surprise. I thought you were joking, yet here you are.

text.ACTION: Remember Drunk Yukiko from Persona 4? Well, the rest of this conversation is the same voice actress doing pretty much the exact same voice with a slightly older affect. It’s kind of uncanny.

text.Ichiko Ohya: I respect that bravery, so I’ll listen to what you have to say. Well, what do you want to know?
Oh? Why that?

Hm ...  Well I do happen to know something about that. I could tell you, but ...  Do you know the Phantom Thieves of Hearts? You know, that case the public has been focused on lately. I was pursuing the issue of people randomly entering into a shut-down state, but I’m lacking intel ...

text.ACTION: Wow, that sounds way more important that our dumb shit.

text.Ichiko Ohya: That’s why I’m currently looking for new material to write about. So, do you have any info on these Phantom Thieves?

text.ACTION: I know a thing or two.

text.Ichiko Ohya: Hm ...  Something like that. You’re a Shujin kid, right? I remember you wearing their uniform the last time we met. I thought maybe you might have some insider knowledge on the Phantom Thieves because of it. Their first incident was that of Kamoshida, you know? Ideally, I’d like to get some exclusive coverage from a student who suffered Kamoshida’s abuse. I would love an introduction if you know of someone who fits the bill. After all, it seems like handling this matter in the open would be an inconvenience to us both...

text.Morgana: Hm, a student who suffered from abuse ...  ...Oh! What about that Mishima guy? He always seems to be on the side of the Phantom Thieves.

text.Ichiko Ohya: It’s a deal then. Send me your friend’s contact info later.

text.Morgana: You’d better be thankful. My quick wit is the only reason we’re getting this far.

text.Ichiko Ohya: ...Now that I think about it, those mental shutdowns and the Phantom Thieves both seem supernatural ...  Could they be related ... ? Or am I just hoping for a coincidence ... ? Oh, sorry. I have a tendency to talk to myself on occasion. Well then, you can’t exactly consider this an upfront payment, but...
I think he’s probably the guy you’re looking for.

text.Morgana: Yes!

text.Ichiko Ohya: You should check him out further if you’re curious ...  but I’m not responsible for what happens next!
Lala-chan, can I get a refill for this kid? We need to make a toast to our new acquaintance!

text.Morgana: It’ll be a problem if you stay too long. You should leave right after you finish your water...
Let’s meet up with Ryuji.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real!? Awesome! Anyways, we should meet up ASAP. I’ll be in front of the movie theater, so head on over. It’s that kinda open area you passed on your way to the bar.

text.Morgana: So we just have to go back the way we came, huh? All right, let’s go.
Not so loud!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Here we go! Mkay, now we just gotta get some info on the distortion. Once we know that, it’s Palace time!

text.Morgana: Let’s try tomorrow. It’ll be better when we have the whole team together.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Right. I’ll tell everyone to meet up in Shibuya. This is totally crazy though ...  It’s a huge catch! I’m pumped.

text.ACTION: OK, so, this part coming up is just inexcusably bad. I’m sorry to say this game has got some ass-backward politics, and as a show of defiance I’m not going to make real portraits for the characters involved. Instead, I have replaced their portraits with photoshops from the covers of Chuck Tingle novels. I hope, in some small way, that this does something to abate the terrible affront to decency that follows.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Gah! Wh-Who are you!?

text.Beefy Trendsetter: Gwahahaha! I’m the naughty troll of Shinjuku! I’m gonna eat you up!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: H-Hey, wait ...  Lemme go! Dude, help! You can hear me, can’t you!?
Don’t look at me like I’m some kinda dog in a kennel! Your friend is in serious trouble here!

text.Beefy Trendsetter: Hehehe. What an energetic studmuffin. I’ll give you all the freebies you could ever desire!

text.Scruffy Romantic: The night is young, and so are you! Let’s party it up!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Gaaaaaahhh!

text.Morgana: Come back alive...

text.ACTION: This has been today’s session of Katsura Hashino’s LGBT Sensitivity Training. We have a lot of progress to make in the future. That was mercifully brief, at the very least.

text.Ann Takamaki: You did it! Well then, let’s meet up at the hideout tomorrow!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Understood. Ryuji seems to be absent from this conversation. Should we contact him separately?

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m sure he’ll figure it out when he checks his phone later.

text.Morgana: We’re pretty much already in Kaneshiro’s Palace! That was surprisingly easy!

text.Yuuki Mishima: For real!? You’re not pulling my leg, right? Ohya-san...

Looks like my time in the female limelight has finally arrived ...  This is all thanks to you. I feel like starting the Phan-Site has really changed me. Anyway, I can handle this. You introduced me, so I’ll make sure I don’t embarrass you. And I’ll totally let you know if we end up hooking up!

text.ACTION: This might be my favorite joke in the game, which makes it all the weirder that it immediately follows the objective worst joke in the game.

text.Morgana: It’s a fascinating place, don’t you think? We should go back sometime.

text.ACTION: What, and get attacked by those roving bands of homosexuals? No thank you, sir!

text.Newscaster: The arrested employee continues to state that he cannot recall ever committing the crime. With no testimony to link to a motivation, the cause remains unclear. Crimes with suspects unable to explain their motives continue to occur in the restaurant industry.

text.Morgana: There’s all sorts of incidents going on ...  Arson is pretty scary.

text.ACTION:
Part 53: 6/19-6/20: Makoto, Makoto, Makoto
	Part 52: 6/19-6/20: Makoto, Makoto, Makoto
Let’s just forget that ever happened, please.

text.Ann Takamaki: What’re you talking about?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...Nothing! Just start it up, Yusuke.

text.Morgana: All we need now are the two other keywords: what he thinks of as his Palace, and where it is. But we don’t have any clues other than people falling victim around here ...  We’ll just have to try whatever keywords we can come up with.

text.ACTION: It’s really strange from a narrative standpoint that we haven’t even met this dude and we’re already trying to pick his brain to find his palace, so we’re just aimlessly guessing.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Urgh, that’s gonna be impossible ...  How many buildings do you think there are in Shibuya?

text.Ann Takamaki: No complaining.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: If we can figure out what the Palace is, we may be able to guess where it is by association.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hmmm ...  It’s prolly somewhere he’s got complete control over ...  Maybe a garden?

text.Ann Takamaki: He likes money, so ...  what about a money bath? I’ve seen people online with things like that!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: No ...  Not even close. How about it, Maaku? Can you think of anything?
I see...
OK ...  That’s a hit! So, he thinks of somewhere in this city as his own bank!

text.Ann Takamaki: I thought it’d be something less realistic. That’s all it is, huh?

text.Morgana: Now then, what location would Kaneshiro think of as his bank?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: If we’re talkin’ about a place where he keeps his cash, maybe his own hideout?

text.Ann Takamaki: How about ...  a real bank?

text.Morgana: His cognition wouldn’t be distorted in that case.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit, we ain’t gettin’ anywhere...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: This may be difficult to explain ...  but doesn’t it seem we’re thinking a little too inside the box? Palaces emanate a passionate madness ...  It feels as though we’re missing that aspect.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: The hell’re you talkin’ about ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: This Palace is a bank for someone who extorts money with criminal acts. It’s something more...

text.Ann Takamaki: But what other ways can we think about it ... ? Oh, could it mean a place you withdraw money?

text.Morgana: Hold on! Do you think it might have something to do with the victims? He’s taking money from his victims’ wallets, right? That means his bank is wherever they are!

text.Ann Takamaki: That’s terrible ...  but you may just be right.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Wait a second ... ! ...I have a hit.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh ... ? Wait, what? D-Did I say something right ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The place that Kaneshiro thinks of as a bank is ...  "All of Shibuya."

text.ACTION: Congrats, Ryuji, you were accidentally smart.

text.Ann Takamaki: What!? Like ...  the entire city?

text.Morgana: I see. That’s certainly where his victims are ...  It turns out he really is a terrible criminal.

text.Ann Takamaki: But wait, is it OK for us to go into the Palace right out of a crowd like this?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Eh, nobody notices if a piece of trash disappears from a trash can. This ain’t any different.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: In that case ...  Let’s go.

text.ACTION: Why are we trusting Ryuji on matters of discretion?

text.Ann Takamaki: What are those...?

text.ACTION: Huh, walking ATMs. It’s like a really shitty episode of Black Mirror.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Walking ATMs ...  That must be his cognition of people. So this is what Kaneshiro considers a "bank"...

text.Morgana: I never thought it would be the entire district. Look around us ...  The distortion is affecting the whole of Shibuya.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Whaddya mean?

text.Ann Takamaki: Ohhh, that’s right! Even when we were in the castle and the museum, the city outside looked normal.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: He sees everyone in Shibuya as his patron.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: No surprise for a mafia boss.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It’s best we focus on finding Kaneshiro’s location and stealing his Treasure as soon as possible.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, his hideout’s gotta be somewhere around here. Let’s go look for it.

text.ACTION: Walking down the distorted Central Street brings us to a few new leads.

text.Ann Takamaki: Excuse me, can we--

text.ATM: I-I don’t have any more, please! I’m telling you, not even one yen!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whoa, cool it. We’re not tryin’ to mug you or anything.

text.ATM: Please, I don’t want to end up like the others ... !

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Were you assaulted?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: There’s no doubt he’s a victim, but he can’t even hold a goddamn conversation ...  Let’s try someone else.
What the hell...

text.Morgana: I don’t think we can talk to any of the ones here...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That would appear to be the case, but there is nobody we can speak to, let alone a bank anywhere ...  Let us try checking around the station once more. We may have overlooked something important.

text.ATM: It’s no use ...  It’s all over ...  I’ll end up just like them...
Can’t you tell ... ? I’ve fallen ...  fallen so far ...  From a place where Kaneshiro leaves no tracks...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm, what could that mean ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, you gotta tell us a little more than--

text.ATM: I’m ...  too tired ...  Please ...  let me rest...

text.ACTION: The ATMan collapses to the ground. You like that name? I just came up with it. They should pay me to name Doctor Who villains.

text.Morgana: ...I don’t think he can speak any more. Kaneshiro leaves no tracks ... ? Does he mean that literally, or could it be figurative?

text.Ann Takamaki: Hey, why don’t we go over all the intel we have now?

text.Morgana: Wait a second ...  They’ve "fallen" from a place that Kaneshiro doesn’t leave any tracks ... ? Could that mean ...  they were actually thrown down from somewhere high up?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What, y’mean like a skyscraper? Uhhh, there ain’t any of them around here, I don’t think...

text.Ann Takamaki: W-Wait ... ! What’s that!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Up in the air ...  No wonder we couldn’t find it.

text.Morgana: "Kaneshiro doesn’t leave any tracks," huh ... ? Figures it’d be floating.
No ...  just a car.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You’re useless! C’mon, don’t you have some kinda secret gadget or something!?

text.Morgana: Shut it! I’m not some robot cat! I mean, I’m not a cat at all!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: This may be the limit of what we can do today.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We gotta find a way to get up there ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Let’s think about it some more tomorrow, OK?

text.Morgana: All right, we should get out of here for now! Run for it!

text.ACTION: Why are we running? Beats me!

text.Morgana: It’s that woman who reeks of alcohol ...

text.Ichiko Ohya: All right. I have a bit of advice for you. It’s about that Kaneshiro guy. He’s more dangerous than I thought! The police haven’t tracked him down, so I dug a little deeper ...  Turns out he has some real shady connections. I won’t say any more than that.

text.Morgana: Shady connections...

text.Ichiko Ohya: He’s not someone a teenager like you should mess with. You should really back off, OK? Well, that’s all I wanted to say. See you!

text.Morgana: Proving our justice isn’t going to be easy ...  We’d better discuss this with everyone tomorrow.
What a pain. I’m sure the police are tired of this guy, too.

text.ACTION: Yeah, I’m sure they hate being physically unable to get near him due to his flying sky bank. That must really suck for them.

text.Morgana: That reminds me, the home shopping program is airing today ...  You wanna check out the TV?

text.Male Host: Here’s what we’ve got for you today! 20 boxes of Mental Floss! Floss with these and you’ll magically remember things you never knew!

text.Female Host: It’s true, I always think about all sorts of random things while I’m just flossing my teeth.

text.Joker: Order for 1980 yen

text.Makoto Niijima: About those Phantom Thieves, I mean. If Dad were still alive ...  Sorry, I ...  I shouldn’t bring this up while we’re eating.

text.Sae Niijima: It’s OK. Keep going.

text.Makoto Niijima: I just wonder if he would’ve been on their side ...  That’s all...
That’s not--

text.Sae Niijima: You don’t have to do a single thing, and you’re provided with food, clothes, a home ...
I’ve had no time to think on such ridiculous thoughts. Would Dad have been happy with them? I don’t care. He died upholding some lofty sense of righteousness, leaving all his responsibilities on us.

text.ACTION: This is kind of a lot.

text.Makoto Niijima: A-All I was trying to say was--

text.Sae Niijima: Isn’t it about time you grew up and acknowledged our situation!?
(pant) Sorry, that was uncalled for. I’m just ...  really tired. ...I’ll be eating dinner out from tomorrow on.

text.ACTION: There’s two important parts of this: Sae decides to start avoiding Makoto, yeah, which has just got to rub it in. But also, hilariously, right after saying this: Sae goes right back to eating. Sae’s not just a complete asshole, she doesn’t understand anything about human interaction.

text.Ann Takamaki: Are we out of luck ... ?

text.Morgana: It’s no fair his Palace is up in the sky...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: If only we could contact the real Kaneshiro ...  ...Hm?

text.Makoto Niijima: Nothing in particular. I just saw you all together here.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That so?

text.Makoto Niijima: You seem to be having quite a bit of trouble.

text.Ann Takamaki: So you’re here to check up on us? You may be the student council president, but when it comes to what we do, you’re useless.

text.Makoto Niijima: Useless ... ?

text.Sae Niijima: All you do is eat away at my life.

text.ACTION: Nice job, Ann! Pour some salt right in that festering wound!

text.Ann Takamaki: Just stay on your high horse and watch. Or do you wanna eavesdrop, since you’re so good at it?

text.Makoto Niijima: That is what you were just discussing, weren’t you? It seemed you just needed to find out where he is.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, you don’t gotta answer her honestly!
What was that?

text.Makoto Niijima: Fine. I’ll help you meet Kaneshiro.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What exactly is she planning on doing?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: She had a dead-serious look in her eyes...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Does this mean she has an idea as to where Kaneshiro may be?

text.Ann Takamaki: I highly doubt that.

text.Morgana: I didn’t like her stern face ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Hrrgh! What is up with her!?

text.Makoto Niijima: Just stay on the phone and listen. Make sure you record the call as well.

text.Ann Takamaki: Huh? Who is it?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That idiot ... ! What’s she doin’!?

text.Makoto Niijima: I heard I could find someone named Kaneshiro if I came to Central Street.

text.Ann Takamaki: Central Street!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: She’s being too rash!

text.Makoto Niijima: He’s blackmailing the students of Shujin Academy, is he not? Tell him if he doesn’t want me talking to the police about it, he’d better agree to meet with me.
You better be taking me to Kaneshiro.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, wasn’t that--

text.Morgana: It’s the guys that messed with us the other day! So they were connected to Kaneshiro!

text.Ann Takamaki: She still on!?

text.Makoto Niijima: Where are we going?

text.Pierced Man: I guess we can’t do anythin’ to her if she’s Kaneshiro-san’s customer.

text.Makoto Niijima: Hey, I asked a question here. Where are we going?

text.ACTION: You really don’t know when to shut up, do you?

text.Ann Takamaki: We gotta go after them!
Ryuji!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hurry up and get in!

text.Junya Kaneshiro: You know what happens to anyone who snaps at me, don’t you?

text.ACTION: Here's a video of this dude’s voice, because holy shit it’s so weird and great.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Niijima-san!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What the hell’d you do to her!?

text.Morgana: Holy moly ... !

text.Junya Kaneshiro: That bag you saw the other day—the crocodile one. How much was it?

text.ACTION: Kaneshiro takes a large stack of bills out of the briefcase and offers it to the woman.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What ... ?

text.Junya Kaneshiro: I’m royally pissed right now. Can you tell? You know how spending money relieves stress? It’s you goddamn brats sniffing around like dogs and barging in here like you own the joint ... ! See this empty space? I’m so pissed that now there’s a three million yen gap here. It pisses me off even more if I don’t fill it up. I’m a perfectionist. So, good luck.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What is that supposed to mean?

text.Junya Kaneshiro: Come on, you all look so tense. I think I’ll call it ...  "Debauchery of Minors at a Club." So, can I send this to your school?

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s--

text.Junya Kaneshiro: Oh, damn, I got booze and cigs in the shot! Maybe some drugs too?

I feed on dumbshits like you.  ... Understand, pretty little student council president? Now listen up. Run your mouth to the police, and I’ll break all of you, starting with your families. I want to give you the usual month, but well, you have such a large group here ...  Three weeks. Bring three million yen by then. No less. Summer bonuses are around the corner, you know? It’ll be easy if you beg your mommies and daddies.

text.ACTION: Oh man, the guy we’re targeting for his history of blackmail is blackmailing us! Who could have possibly predicted this?

text.Junya Kaneshiro: Now get out of my sight. I’m about to have some fun.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What!? To hell with that!

text.Morgana: Don’t bother with him. Makoto’s safety is more important right now.

text.Joker: Three weeks for three million yen ...  Things have taken a serious turn for the worse...

text.ACTION:
Part 54: 6/20: Blackmail, Part Tres
	Part 53: 6/20: Blackmail, Part Tres

text.Makoto Niijima: I didn’t mean to drag you in like this...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real.

text.Makoto Niijima: I was stupid...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I must agree. You should’ve easily imagined this happening.
master of tact.

text.Ann Takamaki: Hey, Yusuke...

text.Makoto Niijima: I was so caught up in trying to be useful ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: All right, enough of the blame game! What’s done is done.

text.ACTION: Ryuji’s awful laid-back about this, considering how boned we are.

text.Makoto Niijima: I’m going to cause trouble for Sis too...

text.Ann Takamaki: Sis?

text.Makoto Niijima: My older sister has a commendable job, and she’s a much more remarkable person than me ...

text.ACTION: Oh man, is the party not gonna find out what Sae does until a pivotal moment of the story? That could be interesting. Might get a little forced, but I can deal.

text.Makoto Niijima: A lot happened after we lost our father three years ago, so it’s just us living together ...  But I’m still a child, so all I am is a burden to her...B

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...  ...  ...And that’s why you were so reckless?

text.Makoto Niijima: I just wanted to be useful in some way to someone ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Y’know, I might not get your whole situation, but ain’t it a bit off saying that you’re useless to her?

text.ACTION: Those were her exact words, Ryuji.

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s the truth though ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Eh?

text.Makoto Niijima: Now that I think on it, the truth about Kamoshida must’ve been covered up by the whole school. I had my suspicions, but ...  I couldn’t do anything about it. ...No. I didn’t do anything. Had I cared enough, I could’ve done something...
People like me ...  must really be what others call scum of the earth.

text.Ann Takamaki: Real scum wouldn’t call themselves that.

text.Makoto Niijima: ... Huh?

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m the same. It’s just like you said before: I was closest to Shiho, but I didn’t do anything ...  Besides, Kamoshida’s the one to blame. Shiho understands that ...  and I do too.

text.Makoto Niijima: Takamaki-san...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You didn’t have a place to belong either ...  Isn’t that right?

text.Makoto Niijima: Me either ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: We won’t let anyone fall victim again. Now, what should we do from here?

text.Makoto Niijima: I’ll do something about the money ... ! So can we please just drop the case with Kaneshiro.

text.ACTION: What? How on earth are you going to get over 28 thousand dollars in cash, in three weeks, by yourse--oh. Well, nuts to that.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: No can do. We’re all caught up in this.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We can’t have you rushing things on your own anymore and making the situation worse.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: If only we could do something about that bank...

text.Makoto Niijima: Bank ... ?

text.Morgana: Oh, right, the bank ... !
Hear me out, you guys!

text.Ann Takamaki: Our key in? What do you mean?

text.ACTION: I guess we’re just giving up on discretion, then.

text.Morgana: We’ve become Kaneshiro’s targets. That means we’ve become customers of Kaneshiro’s bank!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I see. The reason why we couldn’t enter before was because we weren’t considered his customers...

text.Morgana: And wouldn’t you say that she in particular is a special customer?

text.ACTION: (I have no idea what he’s getting at)

text.Morgana: Let’s take her with us. She is responsible for our current situation.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whoa, I don’t follow this at all...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: She risked her very right doing something so reckless. At the very least, she has the right to know. Won’t you come with us?

text.Makoto Niijima: What? ...Wait. To where?

text.ACTION: We’re going to the Palace, you idiots.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It’s Fox...

text.Morgana: Be quiet. The Shadows are going to notice us.
I’m noooooot!

text.Ann Takamaki: That’s Morgana, the cat that was in Maaku’s bag. This is what happens when we come here.

text.Makoto Niijima: That voice ...  Takamaki-san? Where are we ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: We’re inside Kaneshiro’s ...  well, the "world" inside his heart.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...What?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It’s another reality in which Kaneshiro’s distorted desires have materialized.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Another reality?

It’s floating in the air!? Th-This is reality!? My goodness ...   ...  ...  I’m sorry, it’s just ...  But since this really exists, I can’t doubt it ...  A reality that one’s heart shows ...  Is it like the application of optical illusions in social cognitive psychology ... ?

text.ACTION: You can’t trick me, I know that doesn’t mean anything!

text.Ann Takamaki: That’s something we have no idea about...

text.Makoto Niijima: That may be like overwriting their cognition ...  I think I kind of get the logic behind it...

text.ACTION: Finally, someone who just gets it without a million years of explanations.

text.Morgana: W-We’re about the same!

text.Makoto Niijima: Then, does that mean there’s an ATM version of myself somewhere in this world too?

text.Morgana: Perhaps. Regardless, we can change Kaneshiro’s heart and make him confess if we steal his Treasure. ...If it all goes well, that is.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We’ll make it go well. Everyone’ll notice us for sure if we take someone like Kaneshiro down!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Our justice will also become resolute.

text.Ann Takamaki: Think we’d be able to give courage to those in need if it happens!?

text.Makoto Niijima: For the sake of those in need, huh ...  ...You sound like my father.

text.Ann Takamaki: Your father ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: ...No, don’t mind me. You want to go to that bank, right? Let’s go then. If I’ve become a customer of that bank, then they’ll have to let me in.

text.Ann Takamaki: For real ... !?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It came to us!

text.Morgana: It’s just as I calculated.

text.Makoto Niijima: I thought that I’d be able to get in since I have the same identity as such customers. I’m Kaneshiro’s source of revenue, after all.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Ah, that makes sense.

text.Ann Takamaki: But wow ...  This place is huge.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I rarely gotta go to the bank, so ...  this’s makin’ me kinda nervous.

text.Ann Takamaki: Being in a bank with costumes like these is so obvious—we’re totally robbers.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You got that right...

text.Morgana: It seems there will be a lot of Shadows from here on.

text.Makoto Niijima: Huh? What’s that about?

text.Ann Takamaki: Enemies attack us here.

text.Makoto Niijima: I see ...  I’ve trained in aikido. Don’t worry; I can defend myself.

text.ACTION: I don’t think a martial art based around protecting the opponent from harm is going to do much good when you’re fighting a giant ass or whatever the fuck we’ll see in here.

text.Morgana: Self-defense won’t do much good against Shadows, but then again, it’s better than nothing.

text.Makoto Niijima: We have to go in from the front, don’t we? I’m an honorary customer, so I better act like one. ...I will be useful for you guys.

text.Morgana: All right, we’re going in!

text.Ann Takamaki: I had a feeling this would happen.

text.Makoto Niijima: Come at us!

text.ACTION: What? No! Chill for a second.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: No no! Wait!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: She’s one of Kaneshiro’s customers.

text.Makoto Niijima: I’d like to speak with the bank president.

text.Security Guard: Excuse me, but do you have an appointment?

text.Makoto Niijima: I need to talk to him. Now let me through!
That voice ...  It’s Kaneshiro!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You mean a bank has a president?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: They make good money.

text.ACTION: What? The translation lost its mind for a second there.

text.Security Guard: Reception is further in to the right. I strongly advise that you do not attempt to go elsewhere.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well, I guess anything goes in a Palace.

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: That comes to three million yen in total. You’re here regarding that, correct, Miss Beautiful President?

text.ACTION: He’s just purple. No, I don’t know why. Shut up.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You gonna call it off then?

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: No—a loan. The interest rate is ten percent a day.

text.Ann Takamaki: Ten percent interest a day ...  Um ...  Uhhh ...  That means ...  One day is ...

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s three hundred thousand yen.

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: There’s no need to be alarmed. I have a more manageable option for people like you.

text.Makoto Niijima: That was your plan from the beginning, wasn’t it?

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: Niijima-san.

text.ACTION: Facial expressions for this guy are on-point even for his Shadow.

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: ...Or should I say, the younger sister of the beautiful prosecutor Sae Niijima?

text.ACTION: Oh. Well, uh... Guess they’re not doing that.

text.Makoto Niijima: How do you know that!?

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: Please don’t underestimate our intelligence network. My, what wonderful goods have come falling into my lap.

text.Ann Takamaki: Don’t be ridiculous!

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: Young women are so useful. They lack physical strength and are dumb. It’s as if they only exist to be devoured by the strong. That just might be the rule since the dawn of history.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You truly are despicable ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You better be ready, Kaneshiro! We’re gonna snatch your Treasure from you!

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: My citadel has the highest security installed in it.
Anyone will do anything for money. I’ll rob you of your lives as easily as I breathe air. (snicker)

text.ACTION: This is legitimately a really tough fight. We’re up against two Onis, who have no weaknesses, resist Physical, and love spamming Rampage to get multiple hits on the whole party. A smart person would’ve brought Ann instead of Ryuji for her additional healing and magic damage, but I’m not here to make good decisions.

text.Security Guard Shadow (Oni): The target is still alive! We must deal with them at any cost!

text.ACTION: Second verse, same as the first! Did you think we were done? Nope! Two more Onis just spawned.

text.Security Guard Shadow (Oni): Don’t let them escape! We must take them down!

text.ACTION: And one more pack for good measure.

text.Morgana: We’re in trouble at this rate! Let’s run!

text.Makoto Niijima: Could those have been the Personas you mentioned ... !?

text.Morgana: Does now really look like the time to be asking that!? We need to retreat! Makoto, make sure you don’t get separated from us!

text.ACTION: So, why did we come in through the front door again? We already knew we could get in thanks to Makoto, but it seems like we didn’t think this part through.

text.Morgana: Hurry, Joker! The exit’s just over there!

text.Ann Takamaki: There’s no end to them ... !

text.Makoto Niijima: Guys!

text.Morgana: How dare you sneak around, Kaneshiro ... !

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: Those would be my words. However, I do thank you for providing me with such wonderful goods. ...It’s time you disappear.
Managing a bank is tough—that’s why I make it a case to kill troublesome customers. Having one impertinent brat disappear is enough to set an example in that other world.

text.Makoto Niijima: Please stop!

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: I’ll eliminate others besides my goods. You’ve no need to worry. Your sister is quite a beauty though. I’ll make sure to make her my personal slave. Once I get bored, I’ll just sell her off. Oh, poor Sis ...  She could’ve been successful, if only her younger sister wasn’t so dumb.

text.Makoto Niijima: My sister has nothing to do with this!

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: The you better start taking customers tomorrow. All you gotta do is endure it and do as you’re told.

text.Makoto Niijima: Endure it ...  Do as I’m told...

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: You’ll earn three million yen in no time. Although, your life and everything along with it will be a complete wreck by then! Gwahahahahaha!

text.Johanna: Please ...  Never lose sight of it again.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: No, dude ...  That’s a bike...

text.Makoto Niijima: My "self" ...  Me ... !

text.Ann Takamaki: Wow ...  Nice!

text.Morgana: I’ve never seen anything like it...

text.ACTION: Love watching this tiny-faced shithead crap his pants.

text.Makoto Niijima: I will not lose heart again, ever. I’ll go full speed, non-stop!

text.ACTION: Johanna is based on the (apocryphal) figure of Pope Joan, a legendary Medieval woman who was the pope for a short period of time, going against the Catholic Church’s traditions, and was stricken from historical record. She was also not a motorbike, but hey, some things are just too cool to not do.

Part 55: 6/20-6/21: Mad Makoto
	Part 54: 6/20-6/21: Mad Makoto

text.Makoto Niijima: Let’s go, Johanna! Full throttle!

text.ACTION: As we can see, Makoto has a fairly diverse skillset even from the start. She can use Nuclear attacks to hit weaknesses or deal Technical damage against disabled foes, hit the entire enemy party with Vajra Blast, a Medium Physical attack, use single-target (and second tier, the first we’ve yet seen!) healing, and even raise an ally’s defense with Rakukaja.
The Onis still don’t have any weaknesses, but the Sui-ki in the middle is weak to Nuke, conveniently enough.
They go down without too much trouble, and Yusuke learns Mabufu for his troubles.
My favorite thing about Makoto’s outfit? Probably the sweet mini-cape.

text.Morgana: We know how to get in now. Our objective’s been accomplished!

text.Ann Takamaki: But how are we getting out?

text.Makoto Niijima: There’s only one exit, right?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ‘Sup, Miss Post-Apocalyptic Raider.

text.Makoto Niijima: Do you want to get smacked? I’m going on ahead, so follow me!

text.Morgana: OK, we have a path!
Get in!

text.Shadow Junya Kaneshiro: There’s no escape in reality, nor will you break through the security system here. There’s not a snowball’s chance in hell that a bright future lies ahead for you!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That was no aikido—that was some hardcore ass whoopin’!

text.Ann Takamaki: I am SO not pissing her off ...  I feel like she’ll rip off my arm.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: She does exude that aura...

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Oh, stop it!
But ...  it felt pretty great. I never thought I’d become part of the Phantom Thieves I was after.

text.ACTION: I mean, I guess you can join if you want. We haven’t really discussed it, though.

text.Makoto Niijima: Sis might faint if she found out.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You mentioned her earlier.

text.Makoto Niijima: She’s a prosecutor for the district—and she’s investigating the Phantom Thieves.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, ain’t that bad!?

text.Makoto Niijima: No need to worry. A normal investigation would never lead them to a world like that. Then again, it must’ve been fate for this to happen ...

text.Ann Takamaki: What do you mean ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: I can’t be like my sister. I had a feeling that there’d come a time when we wouldn’t see eye to eye anymore.
I’m thankful to have a sister who works so hard, but ...  there are times I feel sorry for her too. And after hearing my Persona’s voice, I clearly understand how I feel now.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It appears you’re not as reserved as you make yourself seem.

text.Makoto Niijima: I was just doing whatever the adults told me to.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Won’t she be perfect as our advisor? She’s fearless and has a sharp mind.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Sounds good to me! We’ve needed someone like that for a while now!

text.Makoto Niijima: I’d be honored if I can help out.

text.ACTION: Finally, we have someone smart on the team.

text.Ann Takamaki: We had way too much testosterone anyway, so I feel much better hav--

text.Makoto Niijima: So the Kaneshiro over here doesn’t know what happened inside the Palace.

text.Morgana: That’s right, but his Palace will be affected if the real Kaneshiro’s cognition changes. We can’t be lax.

text.Makoto Niijima: It seems it’d be best to avoid unnecessary contact with him until then.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Three weeks left, huh...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: There’s that security system too.

text.Ann Takamaki: But if we pull this off, it’ll definitely be great!

text.Makoto Niijima: We’ll crush him like a fly. I’ll make him regret making me angry...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Anyways, let’s begin our operation tomorrow!

text.Ann Takamaki: First, we need to secure a route to the Treasure like always.

text.Morgana: You guys are finally starting to get used to this.

text.Makoto Niijima: I’ll be waiting for the call to meet up.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I wish my Persona was like that.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yours is on a ship though.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, you kidding!? Motorcycles are way cooler than dumb boats! It’ll be just like the song! "I’m a phantom, on a steel horse I ride..."

text.Makoto Niijima: Don’t say such things. And for the record, I am most certainly not "wanted."

text.ACTION: Actually, all of you are wanted. For copyright infringement.

text.Ann Takamaki: Honestly, I’m mostly just surprised you know how to ride a motorcycle at all, Niijima-senpai.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Do you got a license?

text.Makoto Niijima: A regular one, yes.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Niceee ...  I can’t wait to get my hands on one too.

text.Makoto Niijima: That aside, mind if I change the topic for a moment?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What is the matter?

text.Makoto Niijima: I’m sorry, everyone. I know I’m not in any position to be saying that. I truly do ...  However, I must apologize. I was my actions that dragged you into this mess. On top of that, I misunderstood your true intentions in this. If only I could have realized what was happening to Suzui-san too ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Come on, we don’t need to talk about that now.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It seems there are still lingering issues on everyone’s minds.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Now’s not the time to be talking about that shit though! Don’t we gotta be doing something about Kaneshiro?

text.Ann Takamaki: He’s right.

text.Makoto Niijima: Very well, I understand. Anyway, I will do my best to make sure I don’t slow you all down.

text.Morgana: Well, we were at odds with each other until just a while ago ...  But Ryuji’s totally right. We need to work together to overcome this!
But now we’re going up against a real criminal. Stay on your toes, OK?

text.Sharp Detective: They’re happening out there in the real world. Understand?

text.Chatter: Um ...  Why are you telling me this?

text.Morgana: This detective knows what’s going on. Drawing on your own firsthand experience is important.
You know, I can turn into a car too, so it’s like ...  I feel a sense of familiarity?

text.ACTION: All of these options are so good.

text.Morgana: You better not throw up in me! Well, motorcycles are nice too, but it can’t carry large numbers of people. I really am special after ...  all ...  huh? Carry ... ? No ...  Take somewhere? Something just crossed my mind ...  ...It’s no use. I can’t remember at all ...  Eh. There’s nothing I can do about it if I can’t remember. I need to concentrate on Kaneshiro for now. Unlike you guys, Makoto’s clever, so we can expect great things from her. But Maaku, you really do have something special.
Looks like I better step up my game too!

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Morgana is growing deeper ...

text.Morgana: I know! After we deal with Kaneshiro, I should consult her about Mementos too. I’m sure Makoto’s brain can--
...  ...  We got Yusuke, and now Makoto ...  This guy has quite the luck ...  ...Could there be some reason for it? Nah, that can’t be...

text.ACTION: I love the phrase “Nah, that can’t be” because without exception the person saying it is currently revealing that they’re a huge dumbass.

text.Makoto Niijima: I’ve been thinking a lot about Personas and Palaces since yesterday ...  That floating bank really reflects Kaneshiro’s personality. He’s flying around so no one can trace his steps ...  He doesn’t trust anyone. I bet security’s tight in there too. That’s why we should get moving soon. Why don’t we go to the Palace today?

text.ACTION: It’s been one day, settle down.

text.Makoto Niijima: Understood. I’m sure you have your reasons as the leader. I’ll leave my schedule open after school, so talk to me anytime.
Oh no, it isn’t a problem ...  I actually find it refreshing to be asked to the student council room. Although it’s somewhat nerve-racking as well.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...I think I’m a bit nervous myself.
I wanted to apologize. I’m ...  really sorry for everything.

text.Makoto Niijima: What do you mean ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: You know how I blamed you for Kamoshida’s sexual harassment? Well, I wanted to apologize for that ...  I’ve honestly been meaning to this whole time.

text.Makoto Niijima: Takamaki-san...

text.Ann Takamaki: I realized later that Shiho was calling out for me ...  and I wasn’t there to help her ...  I didn’t want to admit my own guilt ...  so I took it out on you, Niijima-senpai.

text.ACTION: This makes no sense, considering that in her own Confidant she came to the exact same conclusion that it was her fault (which is bullshit, for the record).

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m ...  very sorry.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Hey, there is no need for that. In fact, I think the two of us are pretty similar.

text.Ann Takamaki: Huh ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: I was unable to save anyone. Not Suzui-san, and not any of Kaneshiro’s victims. I kept telling myself I wasn’t at fault because I was simply following orders ...  But that was all a lie. It felt like I would be admitting my own worthlessness had I not shifted the blame off of myself. Fear of that worthlessness was probably why I acted so harshly toward you and your friends. ...I’m deeply sorry as well.

text.Ann Takamaki: I see ...   ... In that case, wanna call it even?

text.Makoto Niijima: Even ... ? (chuckle) You’re right ...  How about we leave this conversation in the past?

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, but ...  one more thing. You’re not worthless, Niijima-senpai.
You were a bit reckless, but you’re the reason we found a way into Kaneshiro’s Palace. And you even obtained the power to change people’s hearts. You did that all yourself, Niijima-senpai.

text.Makoto Niijima: (chuckle) That way of thinking is very much like you, Takamaki-san.

When you confronted me about Suzui-san, I realized how dishonest and small I was. You’re always very direct ...  That’s what helped me finally realize the error of my ways. It turns out I’m a little slow on the uptake at times ...  Hey ...  Can I call you Ann?

text.Ann Takamaki: Um, yeah! I ...  I’m going to do the same, M-M-Makoto ...  Rgh, that’s so embarrassing!

text.Makoto Niijima: (chuckle) How about we get something to eat before we go home for the night?

text.Ann Takamaki: Ooh, I know a place! There’s a crepe shop at Central Street that totally stuffs their crepes!

text.Makoto Niijima: Do you want to split one?

text.Ann Takamaki: Mmmm, let’s each get a whole one and then we can go half and half on those!

text.Makoto Niijima: Well, shall we?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I believe some courtesy should be shown to those who are our senior.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh yeah ...  Should we call you Niijima-san, or like, Niijima-senpai?

text.ACTION: Makoto doesn’t seem to have an issue with us texting in class.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Would that not be rude?

text.Ann Takamaki: I already just call her by name.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real? Did something happen?

text.Ann Takamaki: That’s a secret between us girls!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit, that sounds like fun...

text.Makoto Niijima: All of you may call me by my first name. No need to hesitate.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Very well. I shall do just that.

text.Morgana: We’ll take care of him ourselves and leave the world speechless!

text.ACTION: No idea why they’re only giving us this tutorial now.
Mishima seems to have some new info for us.

text.Yuuki Mishima: It’s not even anywhere on the forum yet ...  Anyway, do you remember that bully Daisuke Takanashi whose heart you changed earlier? Well, it turns out there was someone pulling the strings the whole time!
Right!? It’s totally unacceptable. This person has to be somewhere in our school, right? You should go take a look around. In the meantime, I’ll secretly do a little more research too!

text.Morgana: If we want to go after this target, we’ll need a name. Let’s go investigate the school.

text.Energetic Student: Something like that sounds like it could lead to a lot of trouble. Akechi-kun mentioned that too.

text.Calm Student: I guess it does sound like they’re pretty dangerous, after all ...  There was a poll or something about the Phantom Thieves, and not too many people support them.

text.Starry-Eyed Student: It can’t be helped. After the Madarame incident, my acclaim has skyrocketed, apparently.
Heh, I understand if you think that way. Heroes are lone wolves who are often misunderstood. This is for the best. It’d be irresponsible to involve innocents in the fight for world peace.

text.Teacher 1: I was on the track team. Well, it’s been a while since I’ve done any running ...

text.Gaudy Female Student: Track? That’s so hilarious! We don’t even have a track team after they disbanded. It’s because of Sakamoto, right? He’s a problem kid, just like us! Hahaha!

text.Teacher 1: I know it isn’t right for me to say it, but Sakamoto really had some bad luck ...

text.ACTION: Kind Faculty Member is the only person at Shujin not affiliated with the Phantom Thieves who shows any sympathy for Ryuji.

text.Female Student in a Jersey: Why don’t you try consulting with the student council? They were taking applications before.

text.Female Volleyball Player: They probably can’t do anything for me. And I don’t hear good things about their president.

text.Fiery Soccer Player: Is there anyone good out there that we can recruit? I hear that Sakamoto is quick on his feet.

text.Calm Basketball Player: Him? You can’t just recruit a guy who spends all his time lazing around in Shibuya!

text.Boy 7: Well, it’s getting dangerous here too. On TV, they report about all the crime going on in Shibuya.

text.Boy 13: I suppose the widening gap between the winners and losers is causing the losers to commit more crimes. If you don’t want to lose in life, you need to put in the effort. Otherwise, what do you expect.

text.ACTION: I’ll take that into consideration, Just World Fallacy Student.

text.Makoto Niijima: The month is almost over. We don’t have time to waste. So, shall we go today?
But ...  No, I should leave you to your own methodology. I’m sorry for being so restless ...
You’re right ...  Maybe I should try to take my mind off of it all. Call me when you’re ready to act.

text.ACTION: Actually, let’s see if we can hang out before going into the Palace.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...I would prefer to focus on Kaneshiro at the moment. Furthermore, and I don’t mean this in a rude way, I’m not sure spending time with you is worthwhile for me ...  If you have the time to spare, maybe you should study instead.

text.ACTION: Well, and I don’t mean this in a rude way, fuck you too.

text.Morgana: It looks like you’ll need to be pretty smart if you want to invite Makoto out. On top of that, she’s too worried about Kaneshiro right now. You probably shouldn’t bother her.

text.Motivated First-Year: Whoa, really? But Shibuya’s not safe right now, and I don’t know it very well.

text.Energetic First-Year: But maybe Akechi-san will save us from danger and the two of us will fall in love!

text.Motivated First-Year: Yes! Yes! He’d make like, the perfect boyfriend.

text.ACTION: Looks like we found the guy controlling Daisuke.

text.Yoshimora Sakoda: Hey, you did all that on your own. You really want me to show this to your teachers, huh, Takanashi-kun? Another word out of you and I’ll debut your film to the whole world. The "Yoshimori Sakoda Tapes" will be a huge hit!

text.Daisuke Takanashi: C’mon, you MADE me do it! Damn it...

text.Morgana: So, a bigger jerk was pulling the strings all along. We gotta do something about this!

text.ACTION: We can go take Sakoda down in Mementos whenever we choose now.

text.Sad Old Man: We can’t trust these suspicious Phantom Thieves. I hope the police finally get their act together. It’s getting more dangerous to go outside. If this keeps up, we won’t even be able to take walks.

text.Kind Old Woman: People are saying there’s been a lot of bank transfer scams, too. We really need to be careful.

text.Young Cameraman: Let’s stop covering the mafia ...  It’s getting dangerous ...  The higher-ups don’t want us covering whatever we want. I bet the director’s going to scold us.

text.Aggressive Reporter: Don’t get cold feet now! As long as we keep increasing our ratings, he won’t say a thing!

text.Protesting Man: However, the Sun God will not be deterred by such things! I will continue to protect Shibuya! Those frightened by the criminal organization need only accept the power of the Sun God!

text.Clear-Eyed Man: Whoa, I can see it ...  Healing is taking place ...  thanks to the Sun God’s blessings.

text.ACTION: These chuckleheads are always worth a laugh.

text.Rocker: That’s why I’ve poured my soul into this song—to help restore our hope. I give you ...  "Lullaby of Ruin"! Inside a ball of dirty bills/A tempter dances in the dark/Ready for a crazy party, baby/A night of greed, covered in money/Ten percent interest every ten days/Be sure to spend it ... /Wisely ... / Thank you, thank you so much! How was the live performance?
No it wasn’t! I’m all about rock n’ roll!

text.ACTION: Out in Shibuya, we spot a wild cop.

text.Goro Akechi: I had some time until the taping began, so I decided to walk around for a while. I’ve heard many rumors about a criminal group lately. I hope you have avoided involvement.

Ah, lovely. However, you needn’t hesitate to ask if you require help. I have police connections, you know. By the by, this city is never short on excitement. First that train accident, now this mafia ...  Not to mention the Phantom Thieves. I’ve thought of a great many things during my stroll. That reminds me, did the Phantom Thieves go to the Madarame exhibit before committing their crime?

text.ACTION: Yes. I mean, uh, I don’t know.

text.Goro Akechi: What is their goal? And who might be their next target ... ?

text.Chatter: Ahhhh! It is! I’m gonna go ask for a picture with him!

text.Goro Akechi: ...It seems I’ve been gaining more recognition lately. I would love to chat more, but I really must be going. I hope to speak to you again soon.

text.Young-Looking Woman: Yeah, Akechi-kun! The way his eyes look to the side is pretty sexy ...  I love the way he runs his hands through his hair too ...

text.Middle-Aged Woman: Did you hear what I just said? You really like younger guys ...

text.Veteran Pick-Up Artist: Patience is a virtue at times like this. Don’t try to be as cool as Akechi. Go for more casual!

text.Novice Pick-Up Artist: More casual ...  Wait, how would I do that?

text.Veteran Pick-Up Artist: Uhhh ...  you know. Take her out to a cafe or something instead of a bar...

text.ACTION: Let’s check out the Velvet Room.

text.Justine: Our master admires the progress of your rehabilitation, and hence has given you use of a special ritual.

text.Caroline: It’s the Gallows, used to strengthen Persona abilities!

text.Justine: Any further questions regarding this ritual can be directed toward our master himself.

text.Caroline: He’s apparently gonna consider making even more rituals if your rehabilitation goes as planned. Work hard for it, Inmate!

text.ACTION: So, let’s try the Gallows. It’s a means of conferring experience (as well as a semi-random skill) to a Persona by sacrificing another Persona.
By sacrificing our Inugami, we get enough experience on our Shiisaa for it to level up, so let’s do that.

text.Igor: It seems the sacrifice has been absorbed into your mask, imbuing it with greater power...

text.ACTION: Shiisaa learned Dodge Curse from leveling up, and also...

text.Igor: Your Persona is inheriting the power of the sacrifice...

text.ACTION: ...gains Dream Needle from Inugami’s skills. Personas have certain inheritance types that determine what skills you can give them from fusion (though skill cards ignore this), and the Gallows process picks randomly from the applicable skills. As you can imagine, this is abusable as hell, though you can only do it once per Persona per day (or for as long as that Persona remains in your inventory).
Let’s get back to eavesdropping, shall we?

text.Modest Housewife: Fortunately, his salary is so low we’ll never have to worry about something like that...

text.Arrogant Housewife: That’s so brave of you. We’re much too afraid to put ourselves at risk.

text.Modest Housewife: I suppose there are just things a rich family like yours could never understand...

text.Homeless Man: Say, I’d like to ask you something. In the city, I keep hearing about phantom thieves. What kind of trick do they use to steal people’s hearts? Haha, well, I guess you wouldn’t know ...  Oh, right. If you happen to see me at night ...  Would you make sure you stay a safe distance?

text.Easygoing Shujin Girl: Hmm, I think so. Akechi-san was talking about them on TV, after all.

text.Stylish Male Student: It’s like what happened with Kamoshida. I think the calling card is the key. Do you have any idea who put it there?

text.Easygoing Shujin Girl: Oh yeah, the culprits are still a real mystery ...  I wonder if they really are from my school.

text.ACTION: Oh, hey Ann. Weren’t you hanging out with Makoto in that scene I wasn’t actually present for?

text.Ann Takamaki: Are you sure about that? We still haven’t found the Treasure...
I guess there’s no point in worrying if you’re so sure ...  I really wanna eat something sweet right now ...  You’re in the same boat as me, right? Right ... ?

text.Joker: Hang out with her

text.Ann Takamaki: All right! In that case ...  Let’s go get crepes! With tons of extra toppings!

text.ACTION: I’ve been informed by the cat that I do not enjoy crepes.

text.Ann Takamaki: I have the worst luck...
Looks like it’s from the agency. I wonder what they could want ...  Huh ... ? Mika!?

text.ACTION: Fuck yes, return of the only good character

text.Ann Takamaki: They want me to head over for a shoot now ...  Feels pretty familiar, doesn’t it? Basically, this men’s magazine is running a Mika special to try and capitalize on her recent popularity. But apparently, she asked for me specifically to star alongside her for the shoot ...  I wonder why...

text.ACTION: Yeah, I’m sure that must be it.

text.Ann Takamaki: Hold on though ...  Why would you trick someone you admire? Well, I guess I won’t know what she wants unless I head over! Have you been to the Sky Tower before? How do you get there ... ?
Oh, and ...  c-can you come with me? Actually, I’ve already decided for you. You’re going. Come on!
You asked for me, right? Wow ...  I barely recognize you. Did you lose weight ... ? Or maybe change your makeup?

text.Mika: The theme for today’s shoot is "the elegance of woman." So, I conditioned my body to be more elegant.

text.Ann Takamaki: Wh-What do you mean?

text.Mika: Controlling what you eat, how you move ...  That’s all. It may sound easy, but it’s pretty tough. You have to write down everything you eat, making sure to check the nutritional and caloric content. I even hired a personal trainer to take special note of my diet and oversee my exercise regimen.

text.Ann Takamaki: Whoa ...  That’s amazing! Does that mean you don’t get to eat double chocolate crepes?

text.ACTION: The correct response to Ann’s idiocy.

text.Mika: Not to mention the other stuff I do! I take herbal medication, wear warming socks, do pilates and yoga ...  Day after day ...  How many squats do you think I do in a week!? Ugh, a natural beauty like you could never understand how much work I put into my modeling!
Sorry, did I say natural beauty? What I meant was natural airhead.

text.Ann Takamaki: Grrr ...

text.Mika: (giggle)

text.Ann Takamaki: I see now ...  This is a test ...  Well, I’m not gonna lose ... !

text.Cameraman: Um, Ann-chan ...  could you try being a little ...  sexier?

text.Ann Takamaki: M-Mika!? Why are you doing this? I thought you looked up to me!

text.Mika: You should have known that was a lie ...  but I guess you’re just as naive as you look. Anyway, stupid amateurs like you really piss me off. You better not drag me down, OK?

text.Ann Takamaki: Grrr ... !

text.Mika: Introduce me, pleeease? Mm-hm, mm-hm! The owner even invited me to dinner! Y’know, working with all of you just makes me so ...  happy!

text.Ann Takamaki: ...  ...  Um ...  I’m heading home...

text.Joker: We’ve arrived back in Shibuya...

text.Ann Takamaki: Why did Mika ask for me ... ?
I see ...  Then she was just trying to be mean ...

text.ACTION: I don’t know what you’re talking about, Mika’s great.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...  ...  If that’s the case, I probably deserved everything she did ...   ...  ...
