And here we see the new fusions available. They’re all far, far above our level and thus unavailable.
Now, we can head into the pyramid. But what is a pyramid, really? Well, to answer that question, let’s take a nice long look at the Wikipedia page:

Hey guys! Ari here. I’ve secretly edited my own Let’s Play into my brother’s. I don’t think he’ll notice though, he doesn’t seem to read these before posting them, which explains why he makes so many mistakes.

We’ll be playing Sphinx and the Cursed Mummy, an old PS2 game I dug out of my brother’s collection. It’s all based in Egyptian mythology, which I don’t really care about but whatever. We’ll see as much as we can or at least as much as I care to show before I get bored.
This is Sphinx. He’s boring and sucks and I’m going to ignore him as much as possible.
These other two are Imhotep and Horus. Horus is a jerk and he smells bad.
He dies pretty early though, which is good.
All right, now to the good stuff. This is Tutankhamen, the real hero. Happy birthday!
First thing we need to do is pick what to wear. We can wear this blue shirt…
Or the pink one. My brother says that gender roles are outmoded constructs, whatever that means, so let’s go pink.
Except it doesn’t even let you!? BOOOOOOOOOOOO this game!
In my childish rage I smash this innocent flowerpot.
This causes the maid to move away from this wardrobe, which we can open to find this weird amulet.
All right, I’ll put on the dumb blue shirt.
Outside we talk to this creepy old lady who wants our amulets. Get your own! Anyway, there are… 8 of these things? Geez, that sounds exhausting. What to do?
Why, thank you YuGiOhFm2002 slash YuGiOhAngel! Also, shout out to the dude writing a walkthrough for this game on the original Xbox as late as 2011.
We also engage in other forms of recreation, such as chasing a crow around for a letter. Thrilling! At this point, I’m getting pretty bored so I skip around a bit.
This is our brother Akhenaten. He’s incredibly obviously evil and plotting to murder us. My brother wouldn’t do that. I hope.
I’m still mad about the maid not letting me wear the pink outfit, so I take it out on the silverware.
This Whole Thing Smacks Of Gender!
We find a key in the room where bro was being evil that lets us open the sarcof--scaroph--coffins we keep seeing around. Pretty morbid, but they actually let us—teleport? Yeah, okay.

Once we find all those amulets, we teleport straight into the middle of this weird demonic ceremony with big bro. It’s pretty goth. Then there’s this whole thing where the brother turns Tut into a mummy to like, steal his appearance or something, but the ceremony gets interrupted by Sphinx, and the evil dudes and mummy Tut get sucked into a huge portal that then explodes. It’s weird. Anyway, Tut’s dead.
…And that’s why pyramids are the perfect thought-form incubator. Well, I learned a lot from that, didn’t you? Let’s finally enter this pyramid, then.

The giant boulder destroyed the stepping stones, so we’re forced to move around the side.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: No point sittin’ around though. Whaddya wanna do, Joker?

text.Morgana: Not a bad idea. Considering how humongous this building is, there have to be other ways in.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We will have to investigate every suspicious place we see, both inside the pyramid and out.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ugh, outside ... .!? You mean we gotta deal with that heat!?

text.Makoto Niijima: No complaining. Let’s begin our investigation right away.

text.ACTION: But as we make to leave...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We’re only here ‘cause we gotta be! I can’t believe you tried to drop a boulder on us! You want us to steal your goddamn Treasure or not?

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: Hm, why don’t we make a deal? You wish to proceed further, yes?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: A deal, you say?

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: There is a town nearby. I would like you to take back that which the bandit there stole from me.

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh yeah, I think I remember seeing a town on the way here.

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: If you bring what was stolen back to me, I will give you a reward. I’ll even tell you how to proceed.

text.Makoto Niijima: Can’t you tell us any more details? Anything about this bandit, or what was stolen?

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: You’ll learn all the information you need to know once you arrive.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...We’ll need to head outside if we want to go to the town. We can go when you’re ready, Joker.

text.ACTION: Music- The Days When My Mother Was There (Another Version)

text.Ann Takamaki: She said it’s nearby ...  We could probably see it from here, right?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Good point. Let us observe the surroundings and search for any towns that may lie about here.
Yes, I can see what appear to be buildings over there.

text.Morgana: Want to head over to the town, Joker? It’s pretty far away, so this is my chance to shine!

text.Joker: Let’s go.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It looks quite desolate ...  She said only bandits reside here, but still.

text.ACTION: There are also new enemies roaming about here. These are Sandman (Sandmans? Sandmen?), who use Wind, are weak to Electricity, and put party members to sleep, being the sandman and all. However, they also have another, more annoying tactic:
After a few turns, they’ll panic and try to run away. If we don’t defeat them in time, they’ll succeed.
That, or we can use one of our Thieves’ Guild charges to block them.
We choose not to, and the problem there is that it causes the security level to go up. Nothing major, though.

There’s also Anzu, which uses Wind as well and is weak to Gun and Nuclear. We’re going to grab one immediately, because in three levels or so it learns the Dekaja we need for the next Strength rank. Unfortunately, my attempts to get the experience needed to make it learn Dekaja will heavily stifle me going forward in a few ways. First, as I’m trying to facilitate two goals that are often in direct conflict, ending battles with All-out Attacks for maximum money gains and trying to keep Anzu on my person at the end of most (if not all) battles, I end up half-assing both. Second, Anzu is not a great Persona. Its only offensive skill is Garula, and its only other useful skill is Masukukaja. Plus, it’s pretty fragile. Third, my understandable reluctance to use party members with redundant skill types means that Morgana’s Wind affinity benches him for most of the dungeon, causing him to not learn a critical skill for the next boss fight. All things considered, I’d probably have been better served just using Gallows, resummoning Anzu, and using Gallows again until it reached the level I needed, but I didn’t want to waste the money.
Heading into the square in the middle of town, we come across a new event.

text.Pyramid Shadow: Welcome to the desert, fellow trader.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm? What does he mean by "trader"?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We don’t care about your welcomes. You’re a bandit, right? Just cough up the thing you stole.

text.Pyramid Shadow: ...Well, you’re gonna have to catch me if you want it.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Me!?

text.Makoto Niijima: We’ll have time to talk later. Let’s go after him.

text.ACTION: You’re too slow, moron. You’ll never catch me at this rate.

text.Morgana: He ran off again! Hurry up and catch him, fast!

text.ACTION: The bandit runs off once more.

text.Makoto Niijima: We’ll never catch him if we do nothing but follow his path ...  We should corner him somewhere.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Corner him? But how?

text.Makoto Niijima: Let’s use that square from earlier. We can sneak around him and trap him in there!

text.ACTION: This plan is really only as complicated as, “run around to the other side.”
He traps himself without much of a hassle.

text.Ann Takamaki: There he goes ... ! We finally chased him into the square!

text.Makoto Niijima: Perfect. He has nowhere else to run now ...  Let’s do this, Joker!

text.Pyramid Shadow: Tch ...  Don’t even think about comin’ one step closer.
Heh, don’t be ridiculous. You’ve gotta let me go. I mean you guys came to raid that tomb too, right? Why don’t we work together and share the plunder?

text.ACTION: I dunno, the last time a Shadow offered to help me out he turned out to be a huge pervert with an annoying voice.

text.Ann Takamaki: Don’t talk to us like we’re the same as you! We came here to save Futaba-chan. Now give us back what you stole!

text.Pyramid Shadow: So you wanna do this no matter what, huh? Well in that case ...  I guess I don’t have a choice!

text.ACTION: Okay, so the Raging Bird God is actually a pretty annoying fight. It’s got two main skills it likes to use:
(Ma)Garudyne, which does Heavy Wind damage, which is especially bad for Ryuji…
…and Brain Jack, which is a full-party Brainwash skill. It’s probably the real danger, especially if it hits Makoto.
The good news is that Anzu repels Wind, meaning that even though the Raging Bird God nullifies Wind, it pretty much can only hurt Joker indirectly through other Brainwashed party members.
Music- The Days When My Mother Was There (Another Version)

text.Morgana: Is this ...  some kind of papyrus parchment? It looks like there’s something written inside.

text.Ann Takamaki: Hey, no peeking at a girl’s belongings without permission!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Y’know, just what the hell’s happenin’ in her heart? There’s this bandit, those weird voiced sayin’ "you killed her," and who knows what else ...  It’s a total freakin’ mess.

text.Ann Takamaki: Futaba’s supposed to be the queen of this Palace, but even she can’t control it?

text.Morgana: I don’t know ...  I’ve never seen a case like this ...

text.ACTION: Well, let’s really sit and think this through. Clearly it’s well worth our time to diagnose this fictional character, especially based on what little we’ve seen, and thus I say--
When we last left off, Tut was dead.
Yeah, rip. Anyway, Sphinx is now in Abydos. How’s that going?
“Imbecile” is my middle name! Jump in, Sphinx!
Tut’s brother survived, whisked away to this evil castle...
...And is revealed to be a different obviously evil dude!
Also Horus is alive, which is a huge downer. I’m not gonna stop posting that picture though, because I love it too much.
Sphinx rejoins with Imhotep, who says that part of Tut’s soul Sphinx recovered from the ceremony can be used to briefly bring him back in mummy form, which will be useful for… spying and stuff.
Also the agent of this plan is this random basket which Imhotep brings to life and will teleport to Tut, because why not, right?
Bas… Ket? This game is a crime.
Anyway, the Mummy now has to find items to help Sphinx outside of the castle, and these are easily the best, most creative parts of the game. Take this treasure chest, for example:
OH GOD IT WAS ACTUALLY PAIN
Now that the Mummy is somehow carrying an electric charge, he can bring power to different objects.
Like this… thing? Which fires him out of a cannon! For some reason!
But that’s not all the Mummy can do, besides bomb at the box office, har har! He can also...
He just gets crushed flat for a period of time.
Now he can walk through these bars!
Look at how happy he is! Aww! (This game ends in a cliffhanger that will never be resolved)
Also we can set him on fire so he can burn things. (Give me fuel, give me fire, give me that which I desire)
Once we complete the level, the Mummy conveniently runs out of time and is transported back to where his body fell, for some reason. (This game was not thought out very well)
And so the Mummy is dead once more.
May God have mercy on his soul.
...And that is the exact combination of disorders I think Futaba has, including several I just made up right now. Thank you for your time.

text.Makoto Niijima: We’ve completed Futaba-chan’s request. Let’s go see her again.

text.Morgana: Sounds good. I’m curious about that reward too!

text.ACTION: Music- The Days When My Mother Was There

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: Well done. It is yours now.

text.Ann Takamaki: Wait, what ... ? Didn’t you want us to get it back because it’s important?

text.Makoto Niijima: Why are you letting them just do whatever they want? This is your Palace, isn’t it?

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: All that matters is that the map is now yours. Just come further in and ...  Oh.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What in the ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Goddammiiiiiiiiiiit!

text.Morgana: Quicksand! Everyone, swim with all your might!

text.ACTION:
Part 78: 7/26: I Hate Sand
	Part 76: 7/26: I Hate Sand
Music- The Days When My Mother Was There

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...Hey, you guys still alive?

text.Ann Takamaki: Oww ...  First a boulder, then this ...  Did we piss her off somehow?

text.Morgana: I don’t think it has anything to do with us angering her ...  I suspect the problem is that she can’t control her instinct to push people away from her.

text.Makoto Niijima: A simple defense mechanism ...  Considering what she’s been through, I don’t blame her for mistrusting others.

text.Ann Takamaki: Joker, let’s save her! We’ve gotta help Futaba-chan open the door to her heart!

text.Morgana: I have no objections, but we should worry about ourselves first and foremost. Come on, let’s look for a way back above ground. Otherwise this place is going to end up our tomb too.

text.ACTION: These are Naga. They’re weak to Wind and use Electricity and Physical.
The room contains a few miscellaneous treasure chests and a lot of assorted loot, but the only really important thing in it is the way out at the top.

text.Morgana: (sigh) Thank god we can finally get out of here. This was all around a horrible experience.

text.ACTION: Yet more dog Shadows in here.

This one isn’t an actual dog though, it’s Thoth, a baboon. It’s weak to Psy and uses Nuclear and Almighty damage. We’ve seen Almighty before with Madarame’s Madara-Megido, but that was a rather pathetic attack. Almighty is neutral damage that cannot be resisted. While that applies to both sides of the battle, it also means a lot of lategame enemies will just love to try to nuke you with it.
There’s a midboss hanging around this passage, but we ignore him for now and head for the door leading out.

This is what it looks like when Morgana’s Pickpocket Confidant skill procs, by the way. I believe this is the only time in the entire dungeon it activated for me, though, which is a little disappointing.
These are Lamia. They’re weak to Ice and use Foul Breath to increase ailment susceptibility followed by Ominous Words to inflict Despair.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: At least we have secured our escape route. We can finally go about exploring this place now.

text.Makoto Niijima: Let’s use this as our entrance from here forward. It should be more stable than the front.

text.ACTION: From Fui-Ki and Take-Minakata, we make Principality.

text.Principality: Order and discipline come before anything else. Take my mask, and let us defend our honor together.

text.ACTION: The “Principalities” are the angels that guide and protect nations, groups of people, and institutions such as the Church. They are guardians and educators, and inspire living things to ends such as art and science.
Back in the pyramid, Makoto levels up, learning Flash Bomb. It’s a move that deals Medium Physical damage to all enemies, as well as inflicting Dizzy.
Music- The Days When My Mother Was There

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Heh, you don’t gotta freak out about it! Let’s beat its ass!

text.Joker: Here we go.

text.Morgana: Brace yourselves. This is definitely no normal enemy!

text.Pyramid Shadow 2: HENCE, THERE SHALL BE NO PATH FORWARD FOR YOU. IT IS TIME YOU PERISH!

text.ACTION: I CAN SPEAK IN ALL CAPS LIKE A HUGE DORK TOO
Thankfully, that’s not quite the flavor of bullshit we’ll be dealing with here today. Instead, well...
It can just turn our party members into mice!

As you might have imagined, “rattled” party members are completely unable to act until the ailment expires in three turns or so. It’s pretty annoying. A cute detail though is that the mouse is still wearing its respective character's mask.
How’s this dude fit that horn inside the coffin?
It can also summon Lamia, which isn’t a big deal either. All that and its Wind weakness mean it goes down pretty quick.
Music- The Days When My Mother Was There

text.Makoto Niijima: We should make sure we don’t get reckless though. It’s better to proceed one step at a time.

text.ACTION: The next room contains this huge weapon.

text.Makoto Niijima: Oh, that’s a stationary weapon back from the middle ages called a ballista.

text.Ann Takamaki: You even know about stuff like this, Queen? I guess that’s pretty fitting for you.

text.Makoto Niijima: And what’s that supposed to mean ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hold up, that thing ain’t gonna shoot us or nothing, right?

text.Makoto Niijima: Well, there’s an arrow in here, but it seems to be broken. On top of that, it’s slanted away.

text.ACTION: In the same room, we find a door we can’t open.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So what, does that mean we ain’t gonna be able to open it?

text.Makoto Niijima: No, I think it’s the opposite. How we open this door should provide a hint for unlocking the other one.

text.Morgana: We might find something out if we investigate the area around here! Let’s go, everyone!

text.ACTION: In a neighboring room, light is shining down, hitting a mirror, and reflecting into a wall.
There’s nothing we can do about that in this room.
However, if we climb up onto this nearby ledge…

text.Morgana: Think before you go touching that, OK? It might be a trap. Although, I’m curious about it myself...

text.Makoto Niijima: As they say, "Nothing ventured, nothing gained." Very well.

text.ACTION: ...sending the light pouring through the newly formed hole in the wall, hitting the door.

text.Morgana: I’m not so sure about that ...  It looks like pressing that button has changed something in here.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes, there is now light being cast on that door. It is a markedly obvious difference.

text.Makoto Niijima: You’re right. Let’s go take a closer look.

text.ACTION: Hey again! I got bored of bad 2003-era game design, so I ditched Sphinx. Instead, how about some bad 2006-era game design?

I hear this game isn’t very well liked these days, and from what I can tell from this save screen, my brother seems to agree, considering that he got about halfway through it and hasn’t played in a year and a half.
We don’t start out in the actual dungeon yet, so we have to make our way through another area first.

We can use arrows to kill these Bokoblins (Wait, they’re called Bulbins? What? That’s dumb) in the watchtowers before they notice us. I know this because I had to rerecord this part I’m just that good.
Oh crap, let’s punch this hog!
I was not expecting a reward, ma’am. Just doing my job.
King Bulblin is mad at me and takes it out on the pig, which is uncalled for. I give him what for.
And in return, he sets the place on fire!
Now we’re in the Arbiter’s Grounds proper. It’s… a dungeon.
There’s a lot of annoying sand that’ll suck us down if we stay in it for too long, forcing us to jump across platforms and Hookshot (Wait it’s the Clawshot here? Why?) to specific points.
Hey, Mr. Little Skullman! Please don’t stab me with that!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So shining light upon the door is what caused it to unlock ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Wait, doesn’t that mean we can open the door at the great stairs the same way!?

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s a definite possibility. In any case, we should push on.

text.ACTION: In the next room, we see a tablet.

text.Makoto Niijima: Let me see ...  "The light shed by the god of the underworld shall become the sign for those who traverse the pits." What could this mean ... ?

text.ACTION: This charming gal on the left is Isis (NOT THAT ONE). She uses Makarakarn to reflect a single magic attack, which is pretty annoying. She’s also weak to Psy.
The room we’re currently in climbs upward, with the occasional side room. One such room contains this gem.

text.Makoto Niijima: This is Anubis, the Egyptian god of the underworld. It seems to have some kind of shining orb ...

text.ACTION: Um, no. He’s the god of the dead. Osiris is the god of the underworld. Ha! ...What a sad life I live.

text.Ann Takamaki: That sounds kinda familiar. Something about light from the god of the underworld ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm, this may come in handy somewhere. Shall we take it?

text.Joker: Yeah, that sounds good.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Very well. This may prove to be an object of great import.

text.ACTION: As we leave, more enemies spawn.
Defeating them levels Ann up and gets her Tentarafoo, which we use to replace Agi. Tentarafoo inflicts Confuse on multiple targets.
Further up, another statue with another gem.

text.Morgana: The god’s name is Anubis. It really isn’t hard to remember, Skull ...  So, do you think we should take this gem?

text.Joker: Sure, let’s take it.

text.Morgana: All right. Let’s grab it and continue onward.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That means we are directly above where we ended up after coming through the front entrance.

text.Ann Takamaki: We had to shine light on that one to get it to open, right? Do you think this is the same mechanism!?

text.ACTION: What to do? Over in the corner, there are two suspicious objects...

text.Ann Takamaki: Maybe we should put that thing from the Anubis statue in here.

text.Joker: Let’s try it.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Nothing seems to be happening.

text.Morgana: Calm down. From the looks of it, there’s more than one pedestal.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, weren’t there two of those gem-holdin’ dog things? Let’s try puttin’ the other one in!

text.Joker: Here we go.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So shining light upon it is what causes it to open. That is the same as the door underground.

text.Makoto Niijima: We can’t rest on our laurels though. Let’s stay cautious and proceed forward.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We seem to be pushing our way through the doors of her heart.

text.Ann Takamaki: ... I don’t know if I’d phrase it like that. Anyway, let’s keep going!

text.ACTION: Up ahead, we find a safe room, another wall, and another door.
Now we have to deal with all these Poes.
Blasted things are taking the fire from the and closing the door so we can’t keep going!
Look at them there, mocking us...
It’s like a weird hybrid of a dementor and a Nazgul, which actually isn’t that weird because they’re kind of the same thing. Whatever, we killed it.

These ReDead Knights (just make them ReDeads, god, you don’t have to make everything dark and scary as part of your overreaction to the idiots complaining about Wind Waker) can scream and petrify you for several seconds. And then they’ll hit you with a big sword.

I remember watching my brother play Wind Waker with the sound off because those ReDeads scared the bejeezus out of him, but those guys didn’t have a sword to attack with, so they just humped your face. Wholesome. What was I talking about?
Oh yeah, I could be playing Wind Waker instead of this. That’d be nice, but the Wind Temple is really late in that game and I wanna keep the theme going.

You know, my brother 100 percented Wind Waker? I don’t know why you’d even do that, the end of it’s a lot of looking up where the submarines are for the last few pieces of heart and treasure charts, and there’s no real reason to do it, but that game’s good so I won’t complain about it or nothing.
Anyway, here’s a dumb Poe. Whatever.
In this room, we start walking slowly for some reason. Let’s turn into the wolf and find out if there’s something we can’t see.
Oh. It was ghost rats. Fun. I’m… I’m going to go hide on top of the bed now.

This Stalfos will come back to life unless you kill it with a bomb. There’s a US foreign policy joke to be made here. Or maybe there isn’t. I have no real conception of politics yet, I’m just repeating buzzwords I hear from people older than me! Deficits!
Wait. We’re back at the entrance? But that’s only three! Where the hell is it? This dungeon sucks!
Let’s enter the next section of this pyramid.

text.Ann Takamaki: That’s to be expected ...  We’re basically raiding her tomb, after all. We’d better be cautious as we go, you guys!

text.ACTION: Our attempt to follow her is met with considerable resistance.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Holy shit! Is she tryin’ to kill us or something!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes, but unless we can do something about this trap, we will not be able to proceed.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ugh, what a pain in the ass!

text.ACTION: This here is Anubis, god of the dead and embalming, associated with mummification and the afterlife. Why, here, according to Wikipedia, he—shit.
I’m not wrong! You’re all wrong! Shut up! This didn’t happen!
Anubis the Shadow doesn’t have any weaknesses at all, which is hella annoying, especially because he’s too high a level to grab for our collection. He loves using Bless and Curse skills, including...
We slot in Speed Master (Automatic Sukukaja at the start of battle) to replace Giant Slice.
In some areas of this Palace, the floors will collapse, forcing us to find alternate ways around.

text.Ann Takamaki: Hold on, there’s an inscription on this stone slab here ...  "Any who attempts to steal this gem shall be cursed ... " Uhhh...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, we can’t let this "curse" shit get to us, right? C’mon, let’s just take it.
Sweet, we got it. Let’s go.

text.ACTION: Arrows fly out of the wall.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whoa, that was too close!

text.Ann Takamaki: It doesn’t seem like this is gonna stop any time soon. Maybe that "curse" is real after all ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ughhh, what the hell’re we supposed to do!? Goddammit!

text.ACTION: Let’s go put the gem back.

text.Joker: Put back

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah, we can always come back and get it if we need to later.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Could the "curse" perhaps have been lifted? We should check to see if anything has changed.

text.ACTION: We can now proceed past where the arrows were firing.

text.Joker: Press the button

text.Morgana: That might do it ...  Let’s go and see if we can go after Futaba’s Shadow now. ...Let’s hurry, you guys!

text.ACTION: We could jump down right here and follow Futaba’s Shadow… or we could be sneaky.
Let’s go take this gem now that we don’t need to go that way again.

text.Joker: Take the gem

text.ACTION: Yeah, yeah. Whatever, buddy. We know your tricks. This time, we go back the way we originally came, bypassing the trap.

OKAY. We found the last Poe, which was hidden in a place you are pretty much guaranteed to miss the first time around, whatever. We progressed to a new area of the dungeon, which is still not great, but now we’re hanging out by this cool sword with all the ropes attached. Let’s cut one, because there’s no other way to progress and sometimes you just need to act like an idiot to get through life, I guess.

Also we’re capped on Rupees, which is wasteful because this game can’t stop pouring rupees down your throat. The only way to get the next wallet up is to catch all the bugs in the game, which I’m pretty sure no human being has ever done because why would you subject yourself to that much tedium for Twilight Princess of all things?
We can only see this thing in wolf form, and we can only attack it when it glows blue during its own attacks.
Once we beat on it enough, it turns solid. From there, it’s just a matter of hitting it with an arrow and then whacking it with our sword a bunch.
That was a shameful performance. You dare call yourself a midboss? Pathetic.
The Spinner? What? Laaaaaaaaaaame! This is one of those dumb gadgets that we’ll never see in another Zelda game again because it’s so useless and forced, right? Pff, stop wasting my time with this.
It doesn’t even go that fast.
Huh, actually, this is kinda cool. We’re going a lot faster now, and look how high we are!
OH MAN THIS IS RAD WE’RE BOUNCING ALL OVER THE PLACE
To rotate this wall and progress, we have to put the Spinner in this crevice and crouch and stand up repeatedly in a rather lewd manner. I’m glad Louis isn’t watching, he’d find this “queer.”
Oh hey, it’s this dude. Uhh. Whatshisface. Grasshopper-Man. Yeah, that’s it.
Dude stabs this sword into the big skull.
And unleashes a nifty boss fight! Not a great one, but an interesting one, at least!
So, there’s a Spinner track at the edge of the arena, and corpses acting as obstacles popped up throughout. The goal is to hit Stallord’s spine a bunch.
Hitting it enough times will cause that section to break. Each section takes fewer hits than the one before it, which is good...

...Because it gets progressively harder to do. See, these corpses will form a wall that pops up on our approach, and it’s not really possible to go around and still hit the spine. So, we hit them, bounce back, and hit the wall again, trying to temporarily knock down enough of them to get through.

On the third section of the spine, a second wall of five corpses will form directly in front of the spine, in addition to the earlier wall. It’s tricky, and control is kind of an issue, especially because of how fast we’re moving on the Spinner. This fight is still pretty impossible to die on, though.
Three segments down, the sand drains from the arena, and Stallord seems defeated...
But nope! He’s still kicking, and knocks us off this platform!

Now to climb back up! The Spinner track on the inside wall of the arena is a spiral heading upward, unlike the outside, which are just circles. We use this to get back up until Stallord shows his ugly mug again.
Now, he’ll fire balls of… flame (actually, they appear to be balls of terrible particle effects) in an attempt to knock us off, forcing us to jump from the inside to the outside or vice versa.
Eventually, he’ll get in close and we can jump into him, knocking him down.
From there, it’s just a matter of beating the sword in his head up.
He’ll get back up, but from there it’s just a matter of avoiding the new obstacles on the path and doing it once more.
And that’s a decent boss fight for this awful, boring dungeon down. What’s next?
Implady is emotional that the… mirror? is broken!
Oh great it’s Ganondorf, of course it’s Ganondorf, yawn.
Okay, so heading further in, Ryuji replaces Rampage with Swift Strike, which instead of Light Physical 1 to 3 times per enemy, is Light Physical 3 to 4 times per enemy! It’s a lot better.
Also we run into one of these goddamn Treasure Demons, but we can’t find its vulnerability before it escapes.
Hmm, another Anubis statue, but with no gem this time.

text.Ann Takamaki: Let’s see ...  "Any who attempts to steal this gem shall be cursed..." Wait, it says the same thing!?

text.Makoto Niijima: But this statue isn’t actually holding a gem ...  What could be the meaning of this?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hold up, we got one with us. Wanna try puttin’ it in there?

text.Ann Takamaki: I guess that’s probably safer. The gem we have didn’t come from this statue to begin with, after all.

text.ACTION: Now, let’s head further in, I’m sure nothing will interru--

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm ...  We’ve seen this trap before. It had something to do with that "curse" ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Does that mean this one’s related to that gem too?

text.ACTION: Let’s head back to the statue we were just at.

text.Joker: Place the gem

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm, the atmosphere has changed in some intangible way ...  Perhaps the "curse" has been lifted?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That thing wasn’t even holdin’ a gem to start with! It ain’t fair makin’ us put one in!

text.ACTION: Now we can head back and press the button.

text.Makoto Niijima: That must’ve been the ballista. It sounded like it was quite destructive.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Mkay, let’s go find out if anything happened!

text.ACTION: Now that the wall is destroyed, we can climb up through where it was standing.
Not a great payout, but not terrible, I suppose.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Odd. The design seems to be scrambled somehow.

text.Ann Takamaki: Maybe it’s like a puzzle? Joker, can you change the picture?

text.ACTION: This isn’t difficult at all, the only issue being that pieces swap places, meaning any movement will displace the piece you’re moving “through.” This can be easily worked around by starting at one of the edges, though.
And done. This took about ten seconds.

text.Ann Takamaki: What’s this a picture of?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: This adult seems to be reading something to a crying child ... ? Hm, the emotions of the artist are often depicted in the art they produce ...  I can sense ...  serious pain harbored in her heart.

text.Makoto Niijima: Is that voice coming from the mural?

text.Adult Male Voice (Futaba's Palace): "She was always such a bother ... " It seems you caused your mother a great deal of trouble, Futaba-chan ...  She must have had some kind of maternity neurosis...

text.ACTION: The light is reflected toward the mural, which disappears.
The light passes through to the door on the other side.

text.Makoto Niijima: Based on its contents, it sounded almost like a suicide note ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Could that be what Futaba remembers of her mother’s suicide?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But that’s a fuckin’ sick thing to do to a kid if that’s really how it all went down.

text.Morgana: There’s no doubt we’re getting closer to the Treasure. Come on, let’s keep moving!

text.ACTION:
Part 79: 7/26: Technicolor Dream Pyramid
	Part 77: 7/26: Technicolor Dream Pyramid
Before we get back into the Palace, let’s fuse!
First is Zouchouten from Ame-no-Uzume and Clotho.

text.Zouchouten: My power to encourage growth in all that worships me shall become a mask and protect your soul...

text.ACTION: Zouchouten is one of the Four Heavenly Kings of Buddhist faith, who each watch over one cardinal direction and fight evil. Zouchouten himself guards the South and leads the troop of Kumdhandas and Pretas.
Next, Lilim from Principality and Nue.

text.Lilim: I’ll leave the realm of dreams for a while and become your mask...

text.ACTION: Lilim are daughters of Lillith from Jewish folklore and similar to succubi.

And here’s where I fuck up. See, I forgot that I needed to get Anzu to level 28 for Dekaja (it’s currently about halfway to 27 or so) and decide to start fusing up Neko Shogun anyway. Kodama is one of the constituent parts of Neko Shogun, so I fuse it first (using Agathion and Berith).

text.Kodama: I’ll turn into a mask and head on out with you! I’m gonna echo inside your heart, bro ...  Wahoo!

text.ACTION: A Kodama is a spirit from Japanese folklore that live in trees. Cutting down trees with a kodama inside is thought to bring misfortune.
Finally, Neko Shogun using the Group Guillotine from Anzu, Kodama, and Sudama.

text.Neko Shogun: Your future shines bright like a diamond! I am your mask now!

text.ACTION: "A prophetic taoist god, originally known as Mao Shogun. Due to a linguistic error involving the Chinese word for "cat," his name was changed to Neko Shogun."
It’s a weird pun, got it.
We have to re-fuse this guy later though, which is gonna be pretty annoying.
Music- The Days When My Mother Was There
Back in the Palace, another slab.

text.Ann Takamaki: Huh? What is it talking about?

text.Makoto Niijima: I haven’t the slightest idea. It may be a hint of some kind.

text.ACTION: I’ve actually played this game all the way through and I had no idea what this meant until I had to literally draw a diagram for the purpose of this LP.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Urghhh, that’s it! I’ve had it up to here with her!
I’m sick of this bullshit! What the hell is she thinkin’!?

text.ACTION: Well, that was unfortunate, but let’s try agai--
It’s hard to see in this picture, but on the other side of the corridor there’s a space small enough to crawl through. That’s where we need to go.
Wait, what? No. This isn’t gonna work. Like half of this game is desert.
This room contains 12 coffins, 10 of which have control panels next to them. We can’t do anything with them yet.

text.Makoto Niijima: There’s nothing visible on the slab ...  What do you think we should do?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Nothing is happening.

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s odd. Is it broken? Or could there be another step to this mechanism?

text.ACTION: Up ahead, a door and a plank standing upright next to a gap.
Not much of a puzzle there, but the path forward is clear.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Sounds pretty useless to me. Whaddya wanna do, Joker?
Oooh! It’s shinin’!

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm, the devices controlling the murals seemed to react in a similar fashion.

text.Ann Takamaki: Something showed up! It says B01010!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That may be a clue of some sort. Either way, we should search to see if anything has changed.
Quite the impressive contraption. Why don’t we examine it closer?

text.Makoto Niijima: It looks like we should be able to turn the holograms on or off by accessing each control panel. Do you think this is related to that code from earlier?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The color of this hologram is different as well. It’s blue.

text.Makoto Niijima: That might be pointing us toward what we need to do. Blue ...  You know, that sounds familiar ...

text.ACTION: Here’s a helpful diagram I made showing which holograms get left on. Yellow is on and white is off:
It’s fairly simple to reason that 0 is off and 1 is on, leading to this pattern when facing the coffins.

text.Ann Takamaki: Ah! The door opened!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I suppose this is the first step in the process? The next device must be beyond this point.

text.Ann Takamaki: By the way ...  what’s up with these things? Are they all because of Futaba-chan’s mental state?

text.Morgana: It’s hard to say ...  But it does prove that she might not be as simple a target as we were hoping she’d be...

text.Makoto Niijima: I wonder about the meaning behind that stone slab as well ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, our path’s open now. Can we just keep goin’?

text.ACTION: Shut up Ryuji, we’re trying to be depressed here.

text.Makoto Niijima: Touching this one will probably activate it too. What do you want to do, Joker?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Woo! It’s lit up now, just like we were expectin’!

text.Makoto Niijima: There are red inscriptions on there this time. They say ...  R01100 and B10011.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: If this code is similar to the prior one, these would surely be hints for those buttons.

text.Makoto Niijima: To be honest, it somewhat reminds me of binary.

text.Ann Takamaki: It makes sense, given Futaba-chan’s hacker background. Well then, let’s go see if anything has changed.

text.Morgana: Something changed in the room, just like we expected.

text.Makoto Niijima: There should be some connection between that and the code that appeared on the stone slab.

text.ACTION: Going by the way we solved the last one, it should be this, right? Well...

text.Makoto Niijima: Just blindly entering whatever you please will be dangerous. We need to be careful, Joker.

text.ACTION: It’s actually this, because the game is trying to trick you. See, the fact that “R” is before the code tells us that the red coffin needs to go before the pattern, meaning that we have to input it in reverse. It’s surprisingly devious for this game’s generally rather simple puzzles, especially because only takes about two seconds to notice and correct, making me wonder what the point is.

text.Makoto Niijima: Guys, look!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, they ain’t stoppin’! Is this gonna be OK!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Ngh ... ! That only made it worse!

text.Morgana: D-Do something about this, Joker!

text.ACTION: Joker just fucking kicks it, because what the hell.

text.Makoto Niijima: Is this what the slab could have meant by "form a path"?

text.Morgana: ...It’s broken. Well, I guess it would be a little more precise to say we broke it.

text.Ann Takamaki: We can’t get through like this! What’re we gonna do!?

text.Makoto Niijima: Perhaps we could walk over the giant boulders? Let’s try it.

text.ACTION: Sure enough, Makoto provides the path forward.
We find another beam of light this way as well.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then we just gotta touch it and make something happen, yeah? C’mon, let’s try it out.

text.Morgana: It must be scrambled as well. Let’s use the controls to put it back together.

text.ACTION: This one involves rotating the pieces, and it’s a bit more annoying than the last one because, as triangles, the pieces rotate with their pair. Still, it’s not a huge problem to overcome.

text.Makoto Niijima: Is she jumping in front of a car ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: Could this be the moment when Futaba’s mother committed suicide ... ? Hm? Another voice...

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s horrible ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So, did her desire to forget those memories cause her to repress them?

text.Ann Takamaki: We’re pretty far in now, right? This has to be past halfway.

text.Morgana: Yeah, the Treasure is definitely close. You better be excited!

text.ACTION: Always love when they let you input a name.
Hehe. Huh? What do you mean that’s his real name? That doesn’t make any sense.
Okay, we’re finally at the Pyramid. Lenna and Galuf are both dead and we need to get the tablet to unlock the Sealed Weapons.
The entrance is guarded by these Gargoyles, who will revive their partner if they’re left alive for too long after its death.

We have Butts, our Thief, who lets us steal, sprint at lightspeed, flee, and prevent back attacks, you know, generally useless stuff like that. There’s Faris, our Mystic Knight, who can apply spell properties to her swords. Finally, there’s Krile, our Chemist, who can break the game. Lenna’s currently deceased, but she was our Ninja, who could dual-wield and throw weapons. Our main damage dealer is actually our Thief currently, because he just acquired a weapon called the Chicken Knife that powers up every time we run from a battle, but has a 25% chance of making us flee instead of attack. We can circumvent this by selecting “Mug” instead of “Attack,” however.
And so here we enter the pyramid.
I always wanted a snake, but Mom said a pet would be too much work. I think they just gross her out, though.
One fun feature about this dungeon is that it’s chock full of monster-in-a-boxes! Awesome!
*Surreptitiously adds Flee to my abilities so I can get out of this nightmare dungeon without fighting anything because it’s annoying enough to deal with these enemies with a full party*
We enter a maze filled with roaming Mecha Heads.
They’re normally pretty annoying, but Faris’ Thundaga Sword is an instant kill.
Butts, you wimp, the only scary thing about mummies are those review scores wakka wakka
Like the Mecha Heads, these Mummies can also be instantly killed, but with Firaga Sword instead of Thundaga.
Falling down just puts us on the previous floor, though, and lets us grab some other chests.
Oh hey, the tablet! Now we can finally leave this trashfire!
And suddenly, we’re at the top!
How can you see that? It’s on the other side of the planet.
Well, uh… We don’t have a Summoner, so we’re never, ever gonna do that! Bye!
On the way back, the wind drake drops off Lenna, who’s… alive, I guess? Huh?
But then Exdeath shows up (he’s a tree, remember this, it’ll be on the exam), and there’s a demon in Lenna’s body, and it’s a whole thing.
And then the wind drake swoops down and attacks, expelling the demon, but dying in the process. RIP.

The Pyramid doesn’t actually have a boss fight, so this is kind of it. Melusine’s gimmick is changing her weakness with Barrier Change… and that’s it. It’s more annoying than it sounds. I had to record the entire Pyramid and this fight three times due to recording errors, and on the second time I got through it without any Barrier Changes by using Mix to boost Faris’ level so Firaga Sword, which Melusine starts out weak to, does crazy amounts of damage. This time I wasn’t so lucky, but I still got through it pretty easily.
Also zombie Lenna’s in the party now.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, I guess you prolly wouldn’t be seein’ anything like this shit if we weren’t in a Palace.

text.Ann Takamaki: Seriously. This almost feels like a trip abroad or something.

text.Morgana: Hey, now’s not the time to be letting your guard down. I can sense lots of Shadows up ahead!

text.Joker: Let’s push it.

text.ACTION: Further ahead, this sarcophagus is rather suspicious.

text.Ann Takamaki: That is odd ...  Why don’t we check it out?

text.ACTION: If you want… It’s up to you.
Meanwhile, in another room, a different sarcophagus opens.
If we head over to that one, we can press that button as well.

text.Morgana: Ah! It moved!

text.ACTION: Inside, another Anubis, with another gem.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: C’mon, let’s just take it with us. We can figure out how to use it later.

text.ACTION: We near-immediately find a place to put it.

text.Ann Takamaki: Wait, don’t we have a gem now? We should try putting it in here!

text.Joker: Insert the gem

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: This pathway of light is quite impressive. It seems we will be able to pass over it!

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s not gonna disappear while we’re crossing it, right? This is a little scary...

text.ACTION: While we’re here, Morgana learns Wind Break (bleh) to replace Patra, whatever.
Again, some armor and sellables aren’t terrible.
And our next safe room is right up ahead.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’d suck if we had to go through hell again ‘cause we walked up to her without thinkin’ first. So ...  what’s your call? You wanna keep goin’?

text.Ann Takamaki: OK, but we should be careful.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We almost did thanks to you! I mean, do you really wanna help us!? Make up your goddamn mind!

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: ...I’m not sure. There’s not much left at this point though.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This is my fault!?

text.Mot: THIS IS THE PHARAOH’S TOMB. NONE MAY DISTURB HER SLUMBER.

text.Makoto Niijima: Ngh, we can’t retreat now. We’ll just have to do this!

text.ACTION: This is the exact same fight, but the Coffin-borne God just starts with some helpers this time. It’s mindlessly simple, especially because it’s still weak to Wind.
From that fight Makoto learns Dekunda (eliminates all stat debuffs on the party), a fantastic skill that will be replacing Frei.
Music- The Days When My Mother Was There

text.Makoto Niijima: Can you just try to calm down? Nothing good will come of letting your temper flare up like that.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: She did say "there’s not much left" though. The end of this Palace may be drawing close.

text.ACTION: Before we leave this area, climbing into an alcove over on the left side reveals another Anubis statue, hidden rather deviously.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I bet we’re gonna have to use it somewhere. Let’s take it, Joker!

text.Joker: Take the gem

text.Ann Takamaki: OK, we’ve got it now. Let’s go.

text.ACTION: The way forward is where the light is shining, but there’s no way inside just yet.

text.Makoto Niijima: We already have another one of those gems, do we not? We should try placing it in here.

text.Joker: Let’s give it a try.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm, this sight brings a tear to my eye yet again!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You’re so freakin’ weird, dude...

text.ACTION: Now we can follow the path of the light.
Next up, jumping across the statues we saw from earlier.

text.Makoto Niijima: I’d expect so. Joker, if you please.
It may be a rather difficult puzzle for us to solve ...

text.Ann Takamaki: More voices ...

text.Futaba Sakura: I’m ...  I’m tired of eating dinner alone all the time. It’s always just convenience store bentos ...

text.ACTION: For those of you who don’t know, a bento is a common, extremely Japanese form of cuisine. It’s basically an entire meal packed into a box, whether takeout or home-packed. Rice is a traditional ingredient, as well as meat and vegetables. I think the closest thing we have to that is like a TV dinner but this doesn’t seem nearly as outrageously bad for you, as well as possibly being homemade. Anyway, back to the sadness!

text.Futaba Sakura: I wanna go somewhere. Take me on a trip!

text.Ann Takamaki: The one clinging to her mother would be Futaba-chan, right?

text.Futaba's Mother: You know I’m working hard to support you, right!? Ugh!

text.Makoto Niijima: Is that the maternity neurosis the voice from earlier mentioned?

text.Ann Takamaki: I thought it was prettty normal for a child to want to spend time with their parents though ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah. Looks like Futaba was a pretty lonely kid growin’ up ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So these incidents compounded, forcing her mother to suicide ... ?

text.ACTION: The only impression I’m getting here is that Futaba’s mom seemed like an awful person.

text.Ann Takamaki: Huh?

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: I killed her ...  That’s why I’m here in this tomb ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Don’t say that!

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: I will die...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Why’d she get so quiet all of a sudden? What happened to that snarky personality!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Could her heart perhaps be growing weaker?

text.Ann Takamaki: We have to hurry and save her!

text.ACTION: When last we left off, Steely Dan was seemingly defeated when Jotaro plucked his Stand, The Lovers, out of the air!
Jotaro’s all “I’ll punch you to death if I ever see you again” and Steely Dan’s like, OK.
My Stand, The Lovers, just went into her ear!
If you don’t want her to get hurt, stand still and let me stab you in the back! I’ll make sure you never move again!
Steely Dan, you fool, Jotaro’s music is still playing!
Did you not hear me? I told you not to--
Weren’t you gonna stab me? Like this?
Unbeknownst to Steely Dan, one of Hierophant Green’s strings was attached to The Lovers the whole time, wrapping it up!
And The Lovers gets pulled right out of the girl’s ear!
Ask for forgiveness from Enya, the woman you killed. Forgiving you never even crossed my mind.
DIO paid me in advance ...  You can have it all ...
Good grief ...  You really are scum.
What you owe can never be paid back with money!
Oh shit, Quick Time Event, gotta mash Square for the ORAs!
He signed his name and it’s badass. All right, what’s next?

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm? This door...

text.Morgana: It looks familiar...

text.Makoto Niijima: Oh! Futaba’s room!

text.Morgana: That’s it!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Why ain’t it openin’?

text.Morgana: It must be her cognition that no one can enter it.

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: Beyond lies the Pharaoh’s Chamber.
Indeed. However, you need my permission to open this door.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then open it for us.

text.Shadow Futaba Sakura: I cannot. You must have her invite you in.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What the eff. Ain’t this your Palace?

text.ACTION: Ryuji, having briefly flirted with the word “fuck,” decides he doesn’t actually like it after all.

text.Ann Takamaki: What’s she mean, Mona?

text.Morgana: The Shadow is Futaba, but not Futaba herself. In other words, we need the real Futaba’s permission.

text.Ann Takamaki: So, we need to have Futaba-chan open her room and let us in?

text.Makoto Niijima: But I remember Boss saying that she won’t let anyone in.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Right. She’s a serious shut-in.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: How will we convince her to allow us entry?

text.Makoto Niijima: Standing around here won’t help. We’ll just have to give it a try ...  That’s what she wants, after all.

text.Ann Takamaki: I think that we should do it too, even if it means we have to force ourselves in.

text.ACTION: Uhh, didn’t you hear the Shadow? Forcing our way in won’t work. This works on vampire rules.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Someone sure is stoked about this...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We have no choice but to sneak in again.

text.Ann Takamaki: Joker, it’s your call when we do this. Make sure you think of some excuses just in case Boss catches us.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We’re countin’ on you, leader.

text.Morgana: On that note, is everyone clear on what needs doing?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh, that reminds me. Gimme the calling card. The one Alibaba sent us.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What are you going to do with it?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We’re the Phantom Thieves, you know? We gotta announce this. If the Treasure’s there when we get the room open, givin’ this to her will let us take it right away.

text.ACTION: Translation- We can prepare the calling card and take the Treasure on the same day.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Queen, help me think of what to write.

text.Makoto Niijima: I suppose...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We got this covered! You decide on a good time we barge into her room! That’s all you!

text.ACTION: We didn’t quite get Anzu to level 28, but we can Gallows away our Leanan Sidhe to make up for the experience deficit and get Dekaja.
We even get Anzu Eiga for our trouble.
And we fuse our Neko Shogun with Dekaja.

text.Caroline: Oh? Good, you’re here...

text.Justine: I can sense it within you ...  A Neko Shogun with Dekaja...

text.Caroline: What’s wrong, Justine?

text.Justine: It is nothing vital ...  However ...  presiding over the growth of another feels almost ...  nostalgic, in a way ...  Do you feel the same, Caroline?

text.Caroline: Whaddya mean ... ? We’ve never taken care of someone like this before.

text.Justine: You are not wrong about that ...  And yet, our duty to aid his rehabilitation aside, observing his growth feels oddly familiar...

text.Caroline: That can’t be right! The inmate’s growth and this rehabilitation are the exact same thing!

text.ACTION: I kinda lost the plot of this conversation.

text.Caroline: Hey, Inmate. The growth you’re getting from these tasks is helping with your rehabilitation, right?
See, Justine? They’re the same.

text.Justine: Is that not something we should judge for ourselves though ... ?

text.Caroline: Anyway Justine, don’t forget about our job. The duty we’ve been handed is all that matters. Don’t think about anything else.

text.Justine: I suppose ...  you are correct...

text.Caroline: (sigh) I guess you’re gonna keep worrying about this till the inmate finishes his rehabilitation, huh, Justine? Look what you’ve done, Inmate. Getting us all wrapped up in your fate ...  Ugh.

text.Justine: Could it be ... ?

text.Caroline: What’s up?

text.Justine: ...Nothing. But ...  I believe I am beginning to look forward to seeing whether the inmate can complete his tasks.

text.Caroline: You heard her. Don’t disappoint us, Inmate!

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Caroline and Justine is growing deeper...

text.Caroline: OK! On to the next task! ...Justine?

text.Justine: We would like you to harbor a Lachesis with the skill Tetraja within you. You only need speak with us once you obtain it. We will be able to tell.

text.Caroline: Bring us a Lachesis, you hear!? One that knows Tetraja!

text.ACTION: We’re actually a high enough level to try and fuse Lachesis now, but this update’s monstrously long already so let’s save it for further down the road. For now, we should just head home.

text.Morgana: We finally secured our route to the Treasure! All we need to do now is send the calling card.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Mkay, I’ve been waitin’ for this! Anyways, when’re we gonna send it? I guess that part’s up to you, dude. Let us know when you need us!

text.Murmur: I’m sure the Phantom Thieves will do something about it ...
We don’t even know who Medjed is ...  What can they do about it?

text.Whisper: August 21st is the deadline, right? I can’t wait!

text.Murmur: Aw man, we have to wait a whole month?

text.Ann Takamaki: That was fast!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I mean, I already wrote three of ‘em before this, remember?

text.Makoto Niijima: But I came up with almost all of the sentences...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You don’t gotta mention that!

text.Makoto Niijima: Smooth, Ryuji...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The real question here is when we should go to Futaba’s room...

text.Makoto Niijima: Well, um ...  I think our leader should decide.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Look who’s the smooth one now...

text.Makoto Niijima: It really should be up to him though ...  don’t you think?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Absolutely. We have no choice but to carry this out.

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s all on you, Maaku!

text.Morgana: ...There you have it. Sounds like a pretty important task got pushed on you. No point in thinking about it now though. We have to do it. Once you’ve made up your mind, just give the order as usual at the hideout.

text.Young Female Customer: Ah, what about the beach? I could buy a new swimsuit!

text.Young Male Customer: There’s nothing to do at the beach, and it’s going to be hot. We should just go to the movies.

text.ACTION: Boyfriend of the year over here.

text.Newscaster: After issuing their second statement, people are concerned about an impending cyber attack. The Phantom Thieves, however, continue to remain silent.

text.Morgana: This is really getting to be a big deal. I want to just go and take Medjed out, but ...

text.ACTION:
Part 80: 7/27: Psience Is A Dumb Word
	Part 78: 7/27: Psience Is A Dumb Word
I’m actually kind of impressed with Ari’s antics in the last few updates. That looked like a lot of work. Still gonna bury his action figures in the lawn, but interesting stuff.

text.Morgana: Huh ... ? Who could that be at this hour ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The cafe is cool and quiet, and it’s relaxing with the "Sayuri" there. It’s a peaceful place. I’m thinking of relaxing and reading a book. Moreover, we can easily meet up should something occur. We can kill two birds with one stone. If you’d like, we could spend some time together.

text.Morgana: Yusuke’s coming tomorrow, huh? Might be nice to hang out with him. (yawn) I’m going to bed...

text.ACTION: Why does everyone always send their invitations right when they’re going to bed?
Relax, Morgana, we got plenty of time! ...But, you’re right, let’s do it now.

text.Morgana: Sounds like Yusuke’s here. Come on, let’s go downstairs.
There’s not going to be any time to prepare in between, so make sure you’re ready to go beforehand.

text.ACTION: As I mentioned last update, there’s no waiting period on this one, which means no time to make infiltration tools the night before. We’ll manage without it.

text.Office Worker in Cafe Leblanc: Why us? They can’t expect to gain any notoriety by targeting a small business like ours.

text.Bespectacled Office Worker: Is that their way of calling our the Phantom Thieves? Everyone seems to be talking about it.

text.ACTION: A new foible has been added to our plan, however: there’s an enemy gauntlet between here and the exit.

We learn a few skills from these enemies, even if it is annoying to fight before our boss encounter. Ann learns Ambient Aid, which greatly increases the odds of status effects sticking during Rain, Flu, or Pollen weather days. It’s not great, but it’s something to replace the garbage Fire Break, and it’s good for Mementos money farming.
Next, Yusuke learns Tempest Slash, which deals Miniscule Physical damage 3 to 5 times. It replaces Vicious Strike.

Finally, Ryuji learns Shock Boost, which increases the odds of inflicting Shock with Electricity. It’s okay, but Adverse Resolve is so incredibly situational (especially because it’s a situation you should almost never be in) that it’s worth replacing anyway. I still might have replaced Headbutt instead of Adverse Resolve, though.
There’s even a treasure chest in here! Too bad it only contains a Balm of Life, which we can just buy equivalent items of.

To get through this place while minimizing SP use, we keep our SP Adhesives on, leave Ann in the reserves, and have her Diarama everyone after every fight. It’s pretty costly, but we’re not using her here anyway.

text.ACTION: So, this is the real boss this time around. Not Futaba’s Shadow, because as “tsundere” as she was, to borrow the phrase from Yusuke, she still wants our help. No, this is a radical part of her cognition that’s going to fight us every step of the way.

True to Morgana’s word, using any type of Physical attack, including skills, is fruitless, as the beast is out of range. We can use guns, but that’s rather pointless as well. We haven’t exactly been upgrading them, and they don’t do much in the first place. Hilariously though, Ryuji’s fucking shotgun can hit while his Physical attacks can’t.
Here’s our first sign that something is wrong: we’re doing decent numbers, but the beast’s health is barely going down.
For its turn, the beast gets two moves, so it can Slam twice.

It can also use Wing Blast to deal Wind damage and inflict Dizzy. Ryuji’s Wind weakness means we might have been better off bringing Ann (or even Yusuke) for this stage of the fight if we hadn’t already used all her SP healing through the enemy gauntlet, but we want his Tarukaja, and for better or worse this part of the fight doesn’t last long.
Morgana’s Me Patra will clear up that Dizzy easily enough, however.

Futaba’s Persona is the fucking Necronomicon, a fictional grimoire from the stories of HP Lovecraft, as represented by... a UFO. Sure, why not? Written in the 8th century by the "mad Arab" Abdul Alhazred (because Lovecraft was extremely racist, natch), the tome details the truth behind ancient cosmic beings that had come to inhabit Earth, influencing humans for their own ends. Those who read it risk going mad from the forbidden knowledge.

Futaba is also our new navigator, seeing as how we need to get an upgrade midway through every one of these newer Persona games. She can do a whole bunch of shit, but if you’re familiar with Rise’s gimmicks from Persona 4 Golden, it’s a lot of stuff like that. We won’t be covering what she can do until much later, but it’s pretty cool.

So, Cognitive Wakaba Isshiki, or the Sphinx. The Sphinx here represents Wrath, I guess, the true sin of Futaba’s palace, but turned inward instead of outward due to guilt, self-loathing and all that jazz. The real demon of wrath was Satan, but that doesn’t matter because the sinner here isn’t a Shadow.

text.ACTION: We’re going to send Ryuji, because he doesn’t have much utility at this stage of the fight due to his low Magic, lack of support skills, and Wind weakness. Don’t worry, we brought him for a reason beyond Tarukaja.
Don’t let the ballista-summoning fool you into thinking things will be different; Futaba is still Captain Obvious, just like previous navigators.
Sphinx Swipe is a new move that attacks every party member on the field. It’s bad for us!

And here’s the reason we bring Ryuji instead of Ann: 651 fucking points of damage. The real reason Wakaba has been playing keep-away is because she’s incredibly vulnerable to Physical strikes. We could probably do more damage with Yusuke’s Tempest Slash, but he doesn’t have Tarukaja. With Rakunda and Tarukaja both up on Wakaba/Ryuji, we see returns of around 1200 damage.
Wakaba won’t get up until her third turn, which gives us plenty of time to attack.
This is how much damage Freila does with Rakunda, for the record. It’s not great. But we brought Makoto for more than just her damage, as you’ll see shortly.
Don’t complain, Ryuji! Do you want to get knocked on your ass over and over?

This is Dreadful Scream, which is an odd attack that seems to target anywhere from one to three party members. It’s pretty bad for us because it inflicts Despair. It’s big part of the reason to bring Makoto and a few Relax Gels, because we’re sunk otherwise. Notice how it misses Makoto in the above picture: if it hadn’t, we’d be screwed, because I wouldn’t be able to act and everyone would be dead in three turns.
Now, I believe it takes a few turns longer for the ballista to target Wakaba the second time, which means we’re going to have to last with three party members for that much longer.
Anyway, after another round of attacks...

text.Wakaba Isshiki: This isn’t where you’re supposed to be, is it?

text.Futaba Sakura: But I finally got to see you again...
Um, I ...  I love you, Mom...

text.Wakaba Isshiki: I love you too, Futaba. Now, you should get going.

text.Futaba Sakura: Home. I know how to use the Nav now.

text.Ann Takamaki: She left...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That girl marches to the beat of her own drum, doesn’t she?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Like you’re one to talk.

text.Makoto Niijima: But if we have her on our side ...  Wait, what about her Treasure!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh yeah! We almost forgot.

text.Makoto Niijima: Eek!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’s goin’ on!? Wasn’t it supposed to be here!?

text.Morgana: Futaba herself was the Treasure! And she’s gone, so of course it’s empty!
Shoot ...  This is bad!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What’s the matter?

text.Morgana: Not only did the real person come into her own Palace, she awakened to a Persona while she was here! This place could collapse any second now!

text.Makoto Niijima: We’ve accomplished our mission if her Palace is crumbling. We should hurry back to reality.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That would be wise.

text.ACTION: Everyone lands… safely… in the car.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey ...  You guys still alive?

text.Ann Takamaki: I thought I was gonna die in—HEY! Will you let go already!?
Ah, sorry!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: N-Not again...

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...Hm? What’re you guys doing out here?

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, ummm...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That reminds me, where’s Futaba?

text.Sojiro Sakura: What about Futaba?

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, ummm...

text.Makoto Niijima: Ah, yes! We came all this way, so how about we enjoy some coffee?

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh! That’s a great idea!

text.Sojiro Sakura: That’s fine, but...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’m not thirsty though.

text.ACTION: Makoto punches Yusuke in the ribs. Poor guy’s getting it from all sides today.

text.Makoto Niijima: Oh, I almost forgot! I have some business to take care of, so you guys go on ahead.

text.Ann Takamaki: O-OK, gotcha!

text.Makoto Niijima: Futaba? Can you hear me? Please, say something! Please ...  Could this be our fault? Is it because we defeated her monstrous mother ... ?

text.Morgana: No, that was nothing more than a cognitive being created in her mind. Destroying it wouldn’t cause memory loss or put a physical burden on her...

text.Makoto Niijima: What should we do ... ?

text.Morgana: Hey, don’t you know a doctor?

text.Makoto Niijima: You do? Can you contact them?

text.ACTION: I could, but things are a little awkward between us right now. See, I don’t have enough Charm, but you’d know all about that Makoto...
Oh hey Takemi, how’s it going? Your life’s work still meaningless because your patient’s dead? Rough.

text.Makoto Niijima: How much will it be ... ?

text.Tae Takemi: ...That was a joke.

text.Makoto Niijima: So, um ...  how is her condition?

text.Tae Takemi: Her pulse, breathing, temperature, and blood pressure are all normal. No ocular abnormalities either. I’m not sure why, but it seems this girl is in some kind of light stupor. Furthermore, she lacks muscle for her age. I doubt she has much stamina either.

text.Makoto Niijima: I see. The rebound from her awakening was too strong.

text.ACTION: Not in front of the doctor, Makoto.

text.Morgana: There may have been too many abnormal circumstances ...

text.Makoto Niijima: We simply cannot keep quiet about this. We should let Boss know.

text.Morgana: Wouldn’t he figure out our identities!?

text.Makoto Niijima: Still ...  we should tell him, shouldn’t we?

text.ACTION: Stop talking to the cat in front of the doctor, Makoto.

text.Makoto Niijima: Mm, I think that would be best. Letting him know is really the only option we have.

text.Morgana: I guess it can’t be helped now ...  Just keep the circumstances that led up to this a secret, OK?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Oh dear...

text.Makoto Niijima: Um ...  About Futaba ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Futaba-chan’s condition...

text.Sojiro Sakura: What, this? It happens every so often.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh?

text.Sojiro Sakura: She must’ve used up all her energy. It’s like she ran out of batteries. I think it happens ‘cause she doesn’t get enough exercise.
She stays like this for a few days whenever this happens. I’ll make sure she gets plenty of rest. Here, keep an eye on her. I’m gonna go close the store.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, I’m feelin’ pretty frustrated...

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m glad she’s OK ...  but what are we gonna do about Medjed?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: She’s up!

text.Futaba Sakura: Medjed ...   ...  ... . Tired. Gonna sleep for a bit.

text.Ann Takamaki: Futaba-chan! For a bit ... ? How much is she planning on sleeping ... ? We probably shouldn’t wake her up either ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What to do ...

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s too late for us to find another hacker ...

text.Morgana: All we can do is wait for her to wake up...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It is hard for me to even fathom what it could be.

text.Ann Takamaki: People have really been up in arms about the whole cleanse thing...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uhhh, sorry! My bad, dude!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: No matter how you look at it, we need a countermeasure.

text.Ann Takamaki: Our best bet would be Alibaba ...

text.Makoto Niijima: But she may not be capable of it in her current state.

text.Ann Takamaki: I guess we should think of some other ways too then.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes, it would be best to have as many solutions as possible.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well we still got time, so let’s come up with something good, k?

text.ACTION: After all that, we’re just going to find a different solution? Yeah, I don’t think so.

text.Morgana: The chief is with her. I’m sure everything will be OK. Now we just gotta wait for Futaba to wake up...

text.DTD Reporter: Right now, we’re here at the planetarium in Ikebukuro! Looking up and seeing a sky full of stars is so romantic. And the atmosphere here is so soothing!

text.DTD Co-host: Such a magical place. If you want to get close to someone, this is the date spot to visit.

text.DTD Reporter: We’ve got one more place to introduce in our summer special feature! You’ve been living under a rock if you’ve never heard of this one. It’s Destinyland in Maihama! As usual, it’s packed with people. It’s a captivating world of dreams and hope!

text.ACTION:
Part 83: 7/28-7/29: And Then She Slept For Three Weeks
	Part 81: 7/28-7/29: And Then She Slept For Three Weeks

So, we’re waiting for Futaba to wake up. Anyone who’s played Persona 4 is more than familiar with this scenario, waiting until the deadline for the person you saved to magically get better, but this one is over a much longer period of nearly a month.
If you’re wondering why I decided to do the Palace straight away, it’s because I find Futaba’s Crazy Coma kind of hilarious.

text.Chatter: I don’t get it ...  Are they just going to ignore them?

text.Murmur: I’m sure they’re working on it!

text.Whisper: We’re gonna be in trouble if they don’t do anything ...

text.Murmur: I wish they’d take care of it already ... .

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: My desperation has given birth to a new idea ...  These possibilities make my heart dance! I would like you to come with me again if you are able!

text.Joker: I’m eating now. Maybe I should respond later...

text.Sojiro Sakura: But I’m gonna open up shop soon. You either need to go upstairs or get out of here.

text.Morgana: Hm, you have the day off today. Why don’t we go somewhere?

text.Taxi Driver 1: Oh, Medjed? They’re a group of hackers known around the world. They’ve caused trouble before. They target security holes in servers and extract information by accessing sites illegally...

text.Taxi Driver: I don’t really get it, but they’re basically outlaws, right? "Judgment of Justice," my ass.

text.Sharp Lawyer: Yeah, I need to prepare for these cases related to information leaks and unauthorized access. These corporate higher-ups are panicking. They’ve never even heard of Medjed till just now.

text.Serious-looking Lawyer: I suppose they have some pretty big secrets that they’d like to keep, hahaha!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Meanwhile, I am here to observe the public in an attempt to refresh my mind. Do you need something?
(chuckle) You must have a wealth of free time if that is your decision. To be honest, I think I have found the way to pull myself out of my slump. Would you mind joining me again?
I believe I will find what I’m looking for at the church. Let us head over there.
After our enlightening session, I once again attempted to paint. However, nothing I put on the canvas was to my satisfaction ...  Before the gods of art, I am naught but a lost sheep ...

Our theme today shall be anguish! I shall paint the anguish Christ felt as he bore the sins of mankind! Hm, I have seen various sculptures and paintings on the matter ...  but merely replicating them will not do. Would any believers be willing to model and help me capture the true essence of anguish ... ? It seems not ...  Very well. Maaku, you will have to be my model today.

Only a subject naked as the day they were born can convey the true anguish of birth! Now then ...  strip! Take it all-- Actually, perhaps not. Being found stark-naked in a church would be even bigger news than the Phantom Thieves.

Hm, I see ...  So this would be ...  No, perhaps ...  It seems this is not working. I would like to capture anguish, yet you remain calm and composed. Even the slightest wrinkle can change one’s impression of things ... . I shall not compromise, even for this sketch!
Now, raise your hands higher! More ...  Give me more anguish ... ! Bring it to its upper limits! Like this!

Hrm, this position ...  So this is the Passion of the Christ ... ! Forsaken by his disciples, abhorred as a criminal by the public, pierced with nails and hung on the cross ...  I understand now ...  This is true anguish of the Passion ... ! It feels as though something is boiling up within me ... !
This is an art study...
I am attempting to paint anguish, so I decided to use the crucifixion of Christ as a point of reference...

text.Priest: So you’re interested in the anguish of the crucifixion? Hmmm. While it is true that Jesus’ crucifixion on the cross is a symbol of deep suffering ...  It also bears a much more positive message ...  One of resurrection, of forgiveness.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Resurrection ... ? Forgiveness ... ? I’m not sure I understand ...  Those ideas are contradictory to my conception of anguish ...

text.Priest: It may be difficult to grasp what I’m saying right now ...  But try to consider that the anguish one may feel today will someday bring forth new hope. Ah, and by the way ...  I suggest you contain your excitement while here. You may trouble the congregration.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm, hope from anguish ...  ...I’m not sure I understand. I must learn more about the hearts of men ...  Maaku ...  Do you think I will be able to capture the truth someday?
Was that provocation intentional? This is exceedingly strange though. Spending time with you has helped me discover new aspects of myself ...  You are perhaps ...  a mirror of sorts.

text.ACTION: Devoid of any personality of my own, reflecting back what the viewer needs to see? Why, thank you.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: If there is anything I can do in return, please let me know ...  I wish to repay your kindness.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Yusuke is growing deeper...

text.ACTION: I’m not exactly sure what constitutes a “mid-rank” Skill Card, but hey, more shit to never use!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Let us return home for today. I bid you farewell.
Farewell.

text.ACTION: ...This is the best Confidant event in the game.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Goodbye, Maaku.
Yes. Let us drink some tea and calm our minds. Oh, some rice crackers with the tea would be lovely as well.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I am most certainly in the mood

text.Makoto Niijima: Anyway, we should wait a little longer for Futaba to wake up.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: for something salty today.

text.ACTION: This segmented response from Yusuke is so weird and realistic, I love it.

text.Morgana: I understand why you guys feel nervous, but we’ll just have to wait for now.

text.Young Office Worker: "Destructive damage to the Japanese economy" ...  But wasn’t it dead to begin with?

text.Diligent Office Worker: Haha, I’m sure the big companies are in a panic. I don’t think that’s an empty threat, either.

text.Young Office Worker: What are the Phantom Thieves going to do? Well, it’d be funny if they ended up running away from this. Thank you. The curry was delicious.

text.Newscaster: According to experts, there are many corporations that could be potential targets. Companies managing public transport and other utilities are pressured to take countermeasures.

text.Morgana: Medjed is so creepy. They’re really making a big mess out of all this.

Oh, them? They’re faaamoush! Urp ...  OK. H-Here I go ...  Hey ... ! I am a phantom thief!I’m going to steal your hea-- W-Wait ...  Who was I supposhed to impershonate again?
Oh, those h-hackersh are no good! They pop out and shurprise you ...  outta nowhereeee. Pineapple! Shee! Surprises’re bad. Hackersh hide like yucky candy, mished in wi’ the good stuff.
