text.Innocent Grade Schooler: I think the Phantom Thieves are way cooler than him. They’re gonna fight hackers next, right?

text.Rebellious Grade Schooler: Being a hacker would be cool, too. We could steal the answers for all our tests. Anyway, I wonder who’s gonna win. This is gonna be even cooler than Featherman!

text.College Student 2: We’re not kids anymore, y’know ...  Shouldn’t you be prepping for college interviews or something? Also, how’d you do on the finals? Did you even study?

text.Partying College Student: Haha ...  Exams, jobs—it’s all just information warfare, maaan! My skills’ll put Medjed to shame!

text.ACTION: This guy sounds like a stoner Metal Gear boss. “The war of information will be won by those backed by systems of societal control, Scoob!”

text.Elderly Office Worker: They have likely given up. No one has been able to discover their true identities. Which means we must rely on the Phantom Thieves. Though, I doubt they’ll be amenable.

text.Earnest Office Worker: Regardless, they’re garnering a lot of attention ...  So, shall we put an ad on the news station?

text.Tired Office Worker: From what I remember, Medjed attacked whatever it didn’t like. That group caused a lot of damage.

text.Sullen Office Worker: But isn’t this the first time they targeted Japan for a full-scale attack?

text.Tired Office Worker: That’s all because the Phantom Thieves appeared. I can’t stand getting dragged into this.

text.Foreign Barker: Hell no! No one knows who Medjed is ...  Oh ...  Is blaming foreigners for things common in Japan?

text.Drunk Regular: Are you mocking my country? You better shut your mouth before you piss me off!

text.Homeless Man: Eh, it’s got nothin’ to do with you. ...If I play my cards right, I can get the Phantom Thieves blamed for my work ...  Aw, what the hell!? Get outta here, go somewhere else!

text.Adorable Woman: Geography doesn’t matter on the internet. Besides, the Phantom Thieves will take care of them.

text.Rural Young Man: The Phantom Thieves are just a myth! That’s why they haven’t responded! Wake up. This city is built on lies!

text.ACTION: “This city is built on lies!” is my new go-to pickup line.

text.Shiro Asakura: I know you’re a little nervous, but this is just something you gotta do to win people’s hearts. You know, I wanted to be a singer, too. In a way, you realizing your dream is like we both are.

text.Dream-Chasing Woman: You did, Mr. Asakura? Just like me? Well, I guess I can trust you!

text.Chihaya Mifune: Please take a seat.

text.Joker: I don’t think my bond with Chihaya will deepen yet...
Hang out with her

text.Chihaya Mifune: OK, heeere we gooo...

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Chihaya will grow stronger soon...

text.Chihaya Mifune: Well then, see you.

text.ACTION: Why does Maaku keep his phone in his pocket when he goes to bed

text.Yuuki Mishima: Since we’re finally on summer vacation, you should come and help me investigate. We have to punish that deviant and save the children of summer vacation! Let’s go together tomorrow!

text.Morgana: Well, what’s your plan? Do you want to go to the planetarium with Mishima?

text.ACTION: The planetarium escapade is mildly interesting but gets us more points with Mishima and Yusuke, which are both useless. We decide to "respond later" (because I chose the wrong option, oops), but will immediately decline upon waking up. I might show it in a bonus part or something though.

text.Morgana: Don’t forget to respond later, OK?

text.Yuuki Mishima: I already bought two tickets ...  I’ll go twice by myself.

text.ACTION: This is hilariously sad and I love it.

text.Morgana: Really? Did you have other plans?

text.ACTION: ...Yes. I was going to… hang out at the diner all day. Let’s go do that.

text.Elderly Female Customer: Ah, OK, so they’re terrorists. What are these hackers trying to do to us?

text.Elderly Male Customer: They’re ...  Ah, you know. They’re planning on doing some pretty bad stuff. Hey, thanks. I’ll just leave what I owe you here.

text.ACTION: First step in today’s itinerary is to take advantage of Chihaya’s Luck Reading.

text.Chihaya Mifune: OK. Please take a seat.
Reading your luck improvement fortune will cost you 5000 yen. All right, please think of some area in which you’d like to increase your luck.
It seems you will greatly benefit from taking actions that will increase your Knowledge.
That’s all for today’s improvement reading. I hope you’re happy with your fortune. I look forward to your next visit.

text.ACTION: And now to the diner. Maaku gains a boosted Knowledge +2 (4 points instead of 3) and Guts +1.

text.Goro Akechi: Most likely, the Phantom Thieves simply don’t have the means of confronting them. After all, Medjed is quite different from anyone they’ve gone up against thus far. It seems their best option is to reveal their identities before more people are needlessly harmed.

text.Morgana: He really hit us where it hurts ...  We’re going to beat them, though!

text.ACTION: Can we? I’m starting to doubt it.
A while? What the hell does that mean?

And back to the diner. The rainy day bonus is applied weirdly in that it’s another +1 in addition to the +2 after the fact, so boosted it turns into two +2s. This doesn’t actually change anything, because the +2 goes from 3 to 4 and the +1 goes from 2 to 3, meaning boosting it increases the total from 5 to 7 no matter how it’s applied, but it’s interesting nonetheless.
Anyway, Maaku gains Charm +1 and a boosted Knowledge +3.

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s called "Like a Dragon." You know, the one by that famous director. It’s a summer special feature, and I’ve been curious about it for a while. Want to take this chance and go see it?
Let’s meet in front of the movie theater in Shinjuku.

text.Morgana: I wonder what kind of movie it is. (yawn) We should get to sleep.

text.ACTION:
Part 84: 7/30-8/1: I’m Not One Of Those Devilishly Charming Phantom Thieves, No Sir
	Part 82: 7/30-8/1: I’m Not One Of Those Devilishly Charming Phantom Thieves, No Sir

text.Makoto Niijima: Th-That is, a famous director was responsible for this movie. Who wouldn’t want to see it ... ? Why are you looking at me like that? Let’s go inside already!

text.ACTION: Music- A three second loop of “Sauna” from Persona 4
Look how into this Makoto is. It’s adorable.

text.Gangster voice: (laughing) You try to cut ties with me, then you come back for more? I’ll kill you! (two gunshots)

text.Film Protagonist Voice: Boss! Boss! No ...  That bastard shot him! Boooooooss!

text.ACTION: In case it wasn’t already clear, “Like A Dragon” is the English translation of Ryu ga Gotoku, the Japanese name for the Yakuza series, also owned by Sega. The “famous director” Makoto mentioned is a reference to Takashi Miike, who directed the live-action movie based on the first game in the series.

text.Morgana: Makoto’s fists have been clenched this entire time ...  Whatever she said before about the director was probably just an excuse. She loves this stuff ...

text.Joker: I feel like I learned more about the determination that the yakuza have...

text.Makoto Niijima: ...  ...  Um ...  Do you think it’s weird if a girl likes movies like this?

Thanks ...  I think this is the first time I’ve been told that. Sorry that I called you over so suddenly. It felt weird watching a yakuza film all by myself ...  I had fun, though, thanks to you. OK, let’s start heading home.

text.Narrator: Can Yellow Owl overcome the curry, or will he explode first? Revive and fight, Phoenix Rangers! Next episode ...  When It Comes to Curry, Always Bet on Yellow."

text.ACTION: Phoenix Rangers sounds badass. I wish Power Rangers was more like this.

text.Hifumi Togo: ...Huh? Um, please wash it.

text.Persistent Male Fan: I can’t believe that you’re really here ...  in a church ...  I read on the internet that you pray to God for victory. Is that true?

text.Hifumi Togo: No ...

text.Persistent Male Fan: Can I take a selfie with you and post it online?

text.Hifumi Togo: Sorry, I’ve been turning down all such requests ...

text.Persistent Male Fan: By the way, is it true that you’re trying to become a professional shogi player?

text.Hifumi Togo: Well, nothing’s been ...

text.Persistent Male Fan: I’ll be cheering for you to qualify! You’d be the first woman to surpass the third-dan league! I really believe in you!

text.Hifumi Togo: ...Thank you very much.

Men like that approach me all the time. At first, I thought you were one of them ...  ...I really must apologize for being rude to you ...  It bothers me when people make such a big fuss over me ...  Considering that the priest is doing me a great favor by letting me play here ...  You see, he’s my shogi friend. And he’s very kind. He once told me that he wanted to be a professional player. ...And he doesn’t laugh at my embarrassing habit when we play together.

text.ACTION: Hey! I only laugh at you internally!

text.Hifumi Togo: I’m embarrassed just thinking about it ...  Did you see it ... ? It was called "The Venus of Shogi"...

Please stop ...  Ever since I won the female shogi league, I’ve been getting a lot of attention. I just figured I could contribute to the shogi world ...  Besides, my mother seems to be very happy ...  Whenever I win, she rejoices as if it were her own victory ...  So I want to live up to the expectations she has for me ...  ...However, she’s been a bit overzealous lately. She set up the interview and photoshoot. It’s as if she wants to be the manager of a celebrity.
...But it’s fine, because it’s for my mother.

Today, I’ll be showing you something very practical ...  It’s a tactic for using the reserved pawns you’ve taken from your opponent in a more effective way. Nevertheless ...  I apologize. You’re such a good listener, I feel at ease speaking with you ...  Aside from the priest, you’re actually the first person I’ve spoken to about my mother ...

text.Joker: I feel Hifumi’s trust in me growing...

text.ACTION: More opportunities for follow-up attacks, always nice. Basically, this skill allows the occasional chance for a backup party member to pop up and shoot the enemy with you to knock them down.

text.Hifumi Togo: Are you ready ... ?

text.Joker: I feel like playing shogi with Hifumi has helped sharpen my Knowledge...

text.Hifumi Togo: Well then, I look forward to our next match.

text.Haughty Regular: It seems that the world will be affected by all this ...  Don’t you think so too?

Heh ...  A refreshingly honest answer. That kind of innocence is a privilege of the young. At any rate they’ve a strong impression on the hearts of the people. If this were a film, the Phantom Thieves got the opening sequence right. Let’s see what’s next. Well, I’ll be going home then.

text.ACTION: Time for aojiru! Maaku gains Charm +1.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Please, Maaku. I will need your help again. Could you join me.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Yusuke will grow stronger soon, but...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I am in your debt. It seems the answer may have been right under my nose the whole time. You will see soon enough. Follow me.

The truth is, despite my best efforts to convey the meaning of the heart, I am no closer to understanding it. Such a troublesome roadblock never presented itself to me while I was living here ...  As you know, I spent most of my young life in this very house. That is why we have come now. I wish to reevaluate myself within its decrepit walls. By coming to this place, I may be able to rekindle the passion for art I once held. The passion of an inquiring mind on the hunt for pure beauty ...  before I learned of Madarame’s foul nature.

No ...  I surely left it unlocked. What ... ? The door has jammed!? Hm ...  I suppose it was quite an old door to begin with. It had begun to rust even while I was a pupil here. It seems now it has finally broken.

That is a nice idea, but I am unfortunately not the owner of the house. I cannot call a locksmith. I wish I could fix it myself ...  But I struggle with mechanisms as complex as this. I do not have the steady hand required to mend them.

text.Joker: I need to fix the door ...  But I don’t think I’ll be able to with my current Proficiency ...  I might be able to fix it if my Proficiency were Masterful ...

text.ACTION: Masterful is Rank 4, for the record.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm ...  This is a difficult problem. It seems we have no choice but to retreat for today.

text.ACTION: And so the great and powerful Phantom Thieves are obstructed by a broken door. This event is unique, however, in that it lets us go right back to roaming instead of consuming time.
So instead, we head over to Big Bang Burger to partake in the feast of our people.
The lady informs us that the special promotion (where the trial only costs 500 yen) does not apply because it’s not night, but we don’t care.

text.Female Employee: As you are a Second Mate, the difficulty of the mission will be increased. The challenge will cost 1500 yen.
As you have moved up to the rank of Second Mate ...  this is your next foe!

text.Morgana: Holy crap! It’s humongous...

text.Female Employee: This is the Gravity Burger ...  A burger so large that it almost has its own gravitational field. Once again, this will be no easy feat to overcome. But should you conquer this challenge, you will be rewarded with an extravagant prize.

text.Morgana: So this one comes with a prize too ...  Do your best, Maaku!

text.Female Employee: Well then, it’s time to get the thirty-minute Big Bang Challenge started! Ready ...  Go!

text.Joker: All this meat makes sense for a challenge of such cosmic proportions ... !

text.Morgana: It looks good, but it’s so big...
Y-You ...  You’ve done it again!

text.Female Employee: Since you managed to crush the Gravity Burger ...  I present to you the 1st Mate Badge!

text.ACTION: It gives you +30 HP. It’s also garbage.

text.Female Employee: Enjoy your new rank as First Mate. However, one mission still remains ...  I look forward to your next attempt at our challenge!

text.Morgana: You defeated the Gravity Burger this time ...  You’re incredible. You were so admirable, taking on such a daunting task with that intense level of courage!

text.ACTION: All right, we can finally turn in that fucking paper bag to Iwai… when I feel like it.

text.Morgana: Your pace, your strategy of using well-timed drinks, and just the spectacular way you devoured it ...  Everything was perfect!

text.ACTION: Maaku gains Knowledge +2, Charm +2, and Proficiency +2.
And now we can also finally hang out with Takemi again.

text.Toranosuke Yoshida: What kind of friends do you spend your time with? You can withstand difficult times if you have friends who support you through them. I’ll be giving a speech again today. I’d also like you to come with me somewhere after the speech. What’s your availability like today?

text.Matsushita: ...I heard you met with Kuramoto’s grandson.

text.Matsushita: And you can assert your independence there, on a grand stage. To be frank, I’ll be happy as long as the Kuramoto group’s influence diminishes. Hamiru-kun ...  Don’t speak a word of this to anyone, for both our sakes. Very well, then.

text.Toranosuke Yoshida: My friend is trying to take advantage of me, while my former mentor is trying to win me over. To achieve my dream, I have to set aside my beliefs. What should I do?
However, betraying oneself to reach a goal would be a hollow victory indeed.
It’s as if my heart is being manipulated. Perhaps ...  If the Phantom Thieves truly do exist ...  then I’m sure they’re very much like you.

For some reason you stood by me, No-Good Tora, who didn’t have any supporters. I’ve been thinking about this for a while, actually. You must’ve experienced cruelty and injustice in this life. I can tell by the look in your eyes. That’s why I sense your desire to help the weak.
And the strength to stand up to the hecklers, to Matsushita, and to Kuramoto’s grandson. You’re no ordinary high school student. Even I know that much.

Anyway, I just overheard some college-aged people in our store talking ...  They said there was a college student living nearby who abuses animals to relieve his stress ...  And then I remembered that injured cat I saw. I’m thinking maybe he was the one who hurt that cat ...

text.ACTION: So, our new option here is to “Itemize” Personas, similar to a system from Persona 3 FES.

The only really appealing option is turning Principality into Tetraja, because we need that skill card for our next Strength request. However, I prefer to do these the old-fashioned way, so we won’t be doing that. If we did, it would consume both Principality and the Blank Card.

Same for this weapon for Morgana. We can’t actually make it though, because we don’t have a base gun to fuse the Persona into. For a while now we’ve been picking up “Black Kotaganas,” daggers for Joker that are far inferior to any other weapon. Those are the base weapons for fusion. We won’t be mucking around with this too much, but it’s my understanding that, like in Persona 3, you can make some gnarly shit here. We’ll eventually get around to showing this off, don’t worry. I just don’t have anything for which the reward offsets the minor annoyance of the cost.

text.Munehisa Iwai: If it’s too cold for you, put on a jacket, kid. So, whaddya want today?

text.Joker: Hang out with him

text.Masa: Anyways, what’d you wanna talk about?

text.Munehisa Iwai: Oh, right. How’s Tsuda-san doin’?

Why’re you askin’ about him now?

text.Masa: Ohhh, I getcha. You’re still tryin’ to uphold the ol’ code of honor, huh? OK, I’ll tell him you wanna meet up!

text.Munehisa Iwai: Masa’s still on the phone, right? Just stay quiet so I can hear what he’s sayin’.

text.Munehisa Iwai: ...Sounds like there’s some weird stuff goin’ down.
Y’know I was actin’, right? ...At any rate, I honestly wasn’t expectin’ too much outta you. But it looks like you’re gonna actually be some use to me. I’ll be countin’ on you, kid.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Iwai is growing deeper ...

I want to learn more about cognitive psience while we wait for Futaba to regain her strength. If only we could understand it more in depth. Maybe we could solve the mystery of the Metaverse. It would make traversing it easier for us, too.

text.Hifumi Togo: Um, hello. Um ...  Goodbye.

This is really annoying ...  Where is that idiot?

text.ACTION: YEAH, I’M NOT OKAY WITH THIS

text.Chief: ...For someone who specializes in fabricating articles, I’d expect you to be a better liar.

text.Chief: Ohya ...  Are you blackmailing him?

text.ACTION: Her? No. At least, not yet.

text.ACTION: Whoa, way outta line there, buddy!

text.Chief: ...Whatever. Just make sure you don’t miss any deadlines, OK?

text.Ichiko Ohya: Of course. So ...  can we go now?

Well, Ohya ... ?
...Is that so?

You lost all credibility when you started sneaking around like this ...  but fine. I’ll back off. But don’t go pulling any funny stuff, OK? The board wants me to keep a close eye on you. ...You’ve been warned.

text.Ichiko Ohya: Thanks. That guy is one of the execs over at my job. Arrogant bastard, ain’t he? He’s the kind of guy all the girls at a bar would instantly turn down. Anyway ...  that was a real surprise.
Not only are you a good source of info, you’re not half bad as an actor either. You’re honestly the type of guy I’d wanna grab drinks with after work ...  Too bad you’re underage.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Ohya is growing deeper...

Listen, man. You’ve gotta stop being so passive-aggressive about this heat. I know I’m the one with all the money in this house, but we’re not buying a fan. Someone upthread posted about that fan death thing in Korea and it got me spooked, I tells ya!

text.Newscaster: Airports and bus stations are teeming with people carrying souvenirs ...

text.Morgana: Wow, look at how packed it is. Everyone’s so busy.

text.Hifumi Togo: ...I’m sorry. I’m not in the mood to teach shogi today ...  Um, could you join me for a walk?
Thank you. I was thinking of going to the area around Sky Tower today ...  Let’s head on over.
... The digital version of the weekly magazine.
My father’s deteriorating health, and that he’s bedridden ...  The fact that my mother primarily supports us ...  They even reported that my mother works at a night club ...

Which is ...  not untrue ...  But was it really necessary for them to write about all this? Capitalizing on a family’s private matters is just cruel ...  My family’s troubles have nothing to do with my skills as a shogi player ...  My mother was furious when she read the article ...  She said it’ll hurt her career, and that she’ll never forgive whoever wrote it. My father didn’t say anything ...  He just sat there listening to her ...  But he looked troubled ...  My mother told me that ...  We’d be able to easily quell these rumors if I were to become more famous. So now she’s even more insistent on having me do more TV and magazine interviews than before ...

Although I can’t express that to my mother ...  She’s so happy for me. I always believed that if I worked hard as a shogi player, I’d be able to support us ...  But I never expected such a destructive article would be written about me and my family ...  Honestly, nothing good will come from being treated like an idol. People say I’m all looks and no skills. They’re annoyed that I’m in the press all the time. Terrible things have been said about me, suggesting I would do anything to become popular ...  I’m even starting to be shunned in the shogi world. That’s why my senior acted that way toward me. The real reason I practice in the church is that no one wants to play with me. My father used to practice with me from his sickbed, but his illness has made that impossible. Maybe I should stop playing shogi and just get a job ...  That way, my family won’t get hurt again ...
I love shogi ...  I don’t want to quit.

At the end of the day, I love shogi. I’d never be able to give it up. I was just confused because of that article and how my senior treated me ...  However, I think I can see my next move ...  thanks to you. ...You’re helping me realize a lot about myself, outside of shogi.

text.Joker: I can sense a deep bond of trust from Hifumi ...

text.Arrogant Housewife: Exactly. Higher-ups like my hubby are who need to step in if things go south.

text.Modest Housewife: Sometimes, I’m relieved my husband hasn’t climbed so high in the ranks.

text.Homeless Man: No, I’m OK. I still seem to be ...  myself. The Phantom Thieves steal hearts, huh? To be honest, I wish they’d take the heart of ...  you know. I guess I’ll try to persuade him by writing another letter. It’s better than doing nothing ...

text.Dream-Chasing Woman: Aw, that’s so nice! Actually, I’ve always wanted to be an actress ...

text.Fishy Hawker: Yeah! I can tell acting is in your soul. I know you’ll become famous if you take our acting courses!

text.Dream-Chasing Woman: Hm, it seems a little expensive. I don’t have much money, so I’ll have to ask my parents ...

text.Fishy Hawker: No problem at all! I can get you a job where you can make lots of money in just a little time!

text.Woman Pushing Promotion: Have you reevaluated your home security lately? If not, now is the perfect time! We’re having a special promo sale of our total security systems. Join now for bonus benefits! Don’t let this opportunity pass you by! When danger strikes, will you have the protection you need?

text.Sharp Lawyer: Yeah, it’s all over if they can destroy the infrastructure. Those hackers in Medjed know this.

text.Serious-looking Lawyer: If the economy takes a hit too, the current government won’t last either.

text.Sharp Lawyer: The Phantom Thieves might be our last hope. Maybe we really did take peace for granted, you know?

text.ACTION: Now, we reload and craft… more Lockpicks! Woo! The double craft procs without my having to savescum this time, leaving us with 6 more, for a total of twenty. We will not be using all of these by the end of the game.
Maaku gains Proficiency +3, including a bonus +1 from the double craft.
And we rank up in Proficiency! Hooray, now we can open that goddamn door for Yusuke!

text.Ann Takamaki: People are getting even more restless online too.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Are we done for if we lose here ... ?

text.ACTION: Remember how we were going to try to formulate a backup plan? That sure went nowhere, ha.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Maaku’s right. Sorry for messaging you all about such weird stuff.

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s OK. We all feel the same way.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I’ll try and make sure I don’t blow my cover.

text.Makoto Niijima: As should we all.

text.Morgana: It sounds like everyone’s starting to get anxious. But considering how fast the days are closing in, the best thing we can do for now is stay calm.

text.Newscaster: It’s only days until August 21st, the day Medjed will attack, and corporations are scrambling. With no sign of a response from the Phantom Thieves, some suspect they’ve surrendered or ran away.

text.Morgana: Huh? We did not run away! And we’ll never surrender! Just watch and see what happens!

text.Joker: I don’t think my bond with Hifumi will deepen just yet...

text.Hifumi Togo: Now, time for the lesson.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Hifumi will grow stronger soon ...

text.Hifumi Togo: Thank you for today.

text.ACTION: And we head to the diner for what may be near the last time, because by my completely unscientific estimation we’re getting close to capping our Knowledge. So long, Weird Bike.
And another rank up! Hot dog!

text.Young Office Worker: Oh ...  You’re talking about ...  What were they called? Medjed.

text.Diligent Office Worker: You should be ready for any new crisis. That’s why I installed all this new security software.

text.Young Office Worker: Well, I don’t have any info that’d be valuable to them. They’ll only go after the big companies.

text.Newscaster: With Medjed’s day of attack almost here, the anticipation over their showdown is at a fever pitch. People overseas are also showing great interest. Some are even betting on who will win. One bookie says that the odds are on Medjed’s side.

text.Morgana: People are really betting on this? And they think we’re gonna lose?

text.Ichiko Ohya: Speaking of which, the public’s starting to warm up to the Phantom Thieves. Your favorites! (sigh) I can’t gather any news because of the chief. He doubts that I’m dating a younger guy ...  Hey, should we try going on an actual date? Any beaches around here or something?
...Just kidding. You have some Phantom Thieves info for me again today, right?

text.Joker: I don’t think my bond with Ohya will deepen just yet ...

text.Ichiko Ohya: Oh, I look forward to it!

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Ohya will grow stronger soon ...

text.Ichiko Ohya: OK, bye.

text.Play-by-play Announcer: Here’s the pitch ...  Strike three! That’s his tenth strikeout today! It’s a heated pitcher’s battle with neither team scoring runs in the tournament’s final round ...

text.Elderly Female Customer: Ah, that date on that calling card? What kind of crazy thing do you think will happen?

text.Elderly Male Customer: Just ...  All I know is that it’ll be crazy! They’re up against a world-famous group, you know.

text.Sojiro Sakura: "Alibaba won’t lose" or something. What kind of dream was that ... ?

text.ACTION: First thing we do is head on down to ol’ Book Town and buy the first book.

text.Taxi Driver 1: Companies seem to be on high alert. A lot of my customers have complained about how much more work they have.

text.Taxi Driver: Listening to people’s complaints is part of the job. And lemme tell you, everyone’s real stressed out. Still, I dunno if anyone should blindly trust a group that calls themselves the "Phantom Thieves."

text.Joker: I should be able to open the door with my current Proficiency.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You are a tremendous help. Let us return to Madarame’s house.
However, the door appears to be jammed. What shall we do, Maaku?

text.Joker: I think I’ll be able to open the door with my current Proficiency ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Maaku, you are capable of fixing it? ...You never cease to amaze me.

You know, I lived here not long ago, yet it feels almost like the distant past at this point ...  Being here has brought back memories though. Whenever I acted out of line, I was made to sit calmly in this corner. Ah, and over here was a bookshelf, filled to the brim with various tomes. It contained art compilation books for the most part, but there were a few manga tucked away as well ...  At times I would take a break from my art to hide and read them ...  This is also where we would gather to eat when the atelier still had a large pupil count. Sensei is particularly fond of salty food, so ...
Why do I still treat him as my mentor? How long will I allow him to control my life ... ?

Y-Yes ...  My apologies. The truth of the matter is, I used to paint in this room ...  and I did it simply for the joy of painting. No matter what I took as my subject, my hands would move of their own accord to capture its essence ...  But back then, I only saw the superficial beauty of the world. I could not see the grime beneath. After learning the truth behind Madarame’s actions though, everything changed. I strove to fight back against the newfound ugliness I saw ...  To display my talent to those who mocked me ...  I needed to do whatever it took to validate my artistic ability ...  In that search for meaning, darkness took hold of me. ...Ultimately, I began to emulate that which I had so deeply despised in Madarame. You know, Boss told me something very interesting when I was staying with you that one night at Leblanc ...  He said ...  he didn’t believe Madarame took me in for my skill alone. I suppose now that I think about it, there would be no way to know whether or not I would have been talented. ...Maaku, why do you think Madarame decided to take me in?

text.ACTION: Maybe he was impressed by your inability to stop talking, wow.
This is about the moment I realize that for the first time in the entire game I’ve forgotten to bring a matching Persona. Oh well! It’s not worth reloading, there’s ways around it.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It truly is a mysterious beast ...   ...  ...  Even after learning the ugliness of his true nature, a part of me still believes in my former mentor. I simiply cannot come to terms with the stark dualities presented to me ...  The humble house and that loathsome Palace ...  The kind teachers and the fiendishly deceptive artist ...  It seems even the workings of my own heart are inexplicable ...  What, then of my search for pure beauty ... ?

text.Art Patron: Is someone there? I’m coming in.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm? Could that be the police!?

text.ACTION: Ah shit man, I can’t get caught with the goods on me
Oh, that dude? Why is he trespassing on our trespassing?

text.Art Patron: Indeed. Thank you for our conversation back there. More importantly though, why are you here? I couldn’t help but notice the door was open on my way home from work.
Are you perhaps still caught in your slump ... ?

I know a great deal about you, Yusuke-kun. You’ve made a name for yourself by patterning your work after the beautifully detailed "Sayuri" ...  But that painting at the exhibition was ...  quite different from that. Have you begun trying out new styles?
If you’d like, I can advise you. Materials, themes, et cetera. You seem as though you could use a helping hand right now.
Most of your painting was done while living in this residence, correct? Your current lack of patron must be what is holding you back.
I’ve made a living investing in promising young artists like yourself, Yusuke-kun.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: But ...  why have you chosen me? You criticized me so harshly back at the exhibition.

text.Art Patron: Because I feel you have talent. Now, my foundations can provide you an environment that will allow you to focus on developing your skills. If such a lifestyle interests you, we can talk further at a later date. As for today, I have business I must attend to ...  but I hope to hear from you soon.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: My opportunity may have finally arrived ...  And it was all because you opened that door for me ...  Hm, it seems good luck is simply a characteristic of yours. You have my thanks, leader.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Yusuke is growing deeper ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...I must be going now. I’d like to think on this some more. Farewell.

text.Goro Akechi: Medjed is extremely dangerous. Judging from their past actions, they’ll make good on their threat. Of course, Medjed has only resurfaced because the Phantom Thieves recklessly provoked them. If the Phantom Thieves have any shred of decency, they should step forward and take responsibility.

text.Morgana: He says it’s our fault? Can you believe how we got dragged into this?

text.ACTION: I discover Shinjuku has a fucking acupuncture clinic, what?

text.Morgana: This is an acupuncture clinic? Hm, so people get treatments with needles here for their health ...  I bet the drained and exhausted people in Shinjuku come here, seeking immediate relief ...

text.Lala Escargot: I don’t really mind it, but keep yourself in check, OK?

text.ACTION: Let’s look into working here to fulfill that request.

text.Lala Escargot: Or is it that you’re interested in working here at night? A lot of different people visit this bar, so maybe working here could broaden your perspective.
You may not realize it, but you’ve got potential, young man. I can teach you the basics of how things are run here. Don’t worry, you won’t do anything illegal.

text.ACTION: Working at the bar is a returning feature from Persona 4 Golden, and functions almost identically.

text.Lala Escargot: So, did you want to do some work for me today?
All right, go on and change.

text.Ichiko Ohya: Well, aren’t you a hard worker? Well, I guess it’s about time for me to be heading out.

text.Lala Escargot: It’s your first time, so things might be a little scary, but just try to relax. It’s easy work. I’ll need you to help with some chores around the bar. Washing dishes, cleaning tables, the like. I have to entertain the customers, so I can’t do those things myself. That’s why you’re here now! And there you have it. Explanation finito. Do you have any questions?
You’re underage, right? So please don’t touch any of the alcohol. No drinking it, of course, but that also means no serving it either. I’ll do that, don’t worry.

Let’s see ...  There’s just one of me, so sometimes I can’t pay attention to all my customers. Would you be on the lookout for those times? I’m sure they’ll want to talk to you, too. They’re all great people, so don’t worry. I’m sure it’ll be a good experience for you.

Ah ...  Are you interested? I can be your producer if that’s the case. ...Haha, just kidding. I don’t want to break any adult entertainment laws, you know? What you’re wearing now is fine. Well, I guess I’ll have you start immediately, then. It’s almost time for the customers to arrive, so good luck.

text.Morgana: I would have loved to see you all dolled up. Hey, there’s a customer who’s all alone. You should go check up on them.

text.Joker: Which customer should I talk to ... ?

text.ACTION: Based on what customers are present, we can gain a corresponding social stat by spending the evening talking to them.

text.Red-Faced Man (Nagai): This might bore you, but I wanted to ask. What do you think of our nation’s economy? They used tax money as an emergency measure to restore the economy ...  But it only increased our nation’s debt, which in turn burdens us, the citizens ...  Is this really a good strategy for revitalizing the economy ... ?

text.Morgana: Ugh, this is going to take some time ...
I’m surprised anyone could be so long-winded. But you did talk about a pretty difficult topic. I’m sure you gained some Knowledge out of it.

text.Lala Escargot: Oh, right, you were speaking with Nagai-san, right? He’s an elite banker. He talks a lot, but he’s got a wealth of knowledge. I bet you learned a lot by talking to him. Well, here’s your pay. Keep up the good work!

text.ACTION: Pay’s good, but we can get guaranteed social stats from other repeatable opportunities, and in higher quantities.

text.Lala Escargot: All right, you should be going home. You’re still underage, and Shinjuku is dangerous at night.

text.ACTION:
Part 91: 8/20-8/22: Welp, We Tried
	Part 89: 8/20-8/22: Welp, We Tried
Well… fuck. We’re pretty much screwed here. Futaba still hasn’t woken up, Medjed’s on the loose, and the deadline is tomorrow.

text.Newscaster: August 21st—the day Medjed says it will attack—is hours away, and Medjed has been unnervingly quiet. If an attack does occur, we cannot rule out the possibility of it triggering a global recession.

text.Morgana: The deadline’s tomorrow, huh? It’s not a surprise that everyone’s panicking.

text.Female Employee: This is the final task before you can ascend to the rank of Captain. Our store’s behemoth burger stands in your way! A meal of leviathan proportions ...

text.ACTION: Holy moly, is this burger a space elevator!? This doesn’t seem legal!

text.Female Employee: The Cosmic Tower Burger!

This burger is the ultimate embodiment of the limitless nature of space! The volume ...  the flavor ...  the calories ...  Every aspect of this burger is astronomical! If you can succeed at eating the entire thing, you’ll be presented with an extraordinary gift.

text.Morgana: I wonder if anyone’s ever actually finished it ...

text.Female Employee: Well then, it’s time to get the thirty-minute Big Bang Challenge started! Ready ...  Go!

text.Joker: This is a tough battle ... !

text.Morgana: I don’t think you have the luxury of enjoying the taste. Don’t chew, just swallow!
Y-You ...  You’ve done it again!

text.Female Employee: Since you managed to topple the Cosmic Tower Burger ...  I present to you ...  The higest-ranked certification available here: the Captain Badge!
You are hereby promoted to the rank of Captain. No more challenges await you ...  But please do the challenge again and show us how gallant you are! We’ll be wholeheartedly awaiting your return!

text.Morgana: You were so admirable, taking on such a daunting task with that intense level of courage!
Your pace, your strategy of using well-timed drinks, and just the spectacular way you devoured it ...  Everything was perfect!

text.ACTION: Maaku gains Knowledge +3, Charm +3, and Proficiency +3.

text.COMMENT: Protag: Bloated, mouth dripping with grease, speech slurred IatethebigburgerMakotoandnowI’mcharmingenoughtohangoutwithyouPLEASELOVEME

text.Morgana: Come on, we should head home. I’m full just from watching you ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, this ain’t just some normal oversleeping stuff! Our deadline’s tomorrow! If Futaba’s not up by then ...

text.Ann Takamaki: But can she really do anything even if she does wake up ... ?
Yeah ...  If she’s been asleep all this time, do you think she’s having some kind of long dream?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm, dreams are said to be the sorting of memories, after all. She surely needs ample time to face her troubled past.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Her past? You think she’s really facing all that shit right now ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: If that is the case ...  she would probably need a great amount more time to do so.
Yes.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Indeed.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well, just give us a ring if anything changes!

text.Ann Takamaki: We’re counting on you!

text.Morgana: I have to agree with Makoto. Who knows how this might turn out ...

text.Hifumi Togo: It’s even hotter this summer. Um, do you have some time today? I’d like to request a match with you.
Thank you. I look forward to it.
The battlefield is mine ...  The Ultimate Togo Kingdom is complete.

text.Joker: All of my pieces have been taken ...  Hifumi has left me utterly defeated.

text.Hifumi Togo: But to think you could stay standing after being struck by my Silver Infinity Sword ...  You’ve improved, considering that you endured the climbing silver so early in the match. The determination I’m sensing from you is a real inspiration. I must think of a new move ...  I’m afraid you’ll surpass me one day, if I don’t stay sharp.

He’s a very famous shogi player ...  I’m aiming to be the first woman to reach the pro ranking league. I’m sure it will draw a lot of attention, especially after that article ...  However, I don’t intend to lose. This is my chance to display my true skills. ...I confess I am a bit scared, though.
However, that also means I have a chance of winning, even though my opponent is ranked higher. To be honest, I’m not sure how well my skills will hold up against a true professional ...
So, um ...  there’s a move I want to try out. Would you like to play another match ... ?

text.Joker: (nods)

text.Hifumi Togo: Thank you very much. Strategically place your pieces in the enemy’s zone to increase your chances of getting gold. Be sure to use that tactic in your next match. For today, try and steal the pieces you want from me.

text.Joker: I feel Hifumi’s trust in me growing...

text.ACTION: I’m not sure that this is what Hifumi meant by “getting gold,” but whatever. This is a very interesting and very useful skill. There are a lot of skills in this game that involve ambushes, or money, or defeating enemies quickly, so Narikin has some really fascinating synergies. The obvious one, and the only one we really have available at the moment, is combining it with Chihaya’s Money Reading to even further increase the amount of money we obtain.

text.Hifumi Togo: Well then, let’s begin the match ...

text.Joker: I feel like playing shogi with Hifumi has helped sharpen my Knowledge ...

text.Hifumi Togo: Thank you for the match. I look forward to our next one ...

text.Whisper: Are the Phantom Thieves even doing anything?
Hey! What are we gonna do!?
I should never have trusted the Phantom Thieves ...

text.Murmur: What’s going to happen tomorrow ... ?

text.Chatter: I guess there’s nothing the Phantom Thieves could do ...

text.Murmur: Medjed must have been too much for them.

text.Whisper: Stock prices are plummeting again ...

text.Murmur: Maybe Medjed’s true goal was ...

text.Morgana: Futaba’s still asleep too ...  This won’t be good ...

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...Hey.
Today’s the day Wakaba passed. I do this every year ...  Here, I’ve got a cup for you too.

Futaba reminds me so much of her mother. She’s a smart girl. Doesn’t just go with the flow, either. Wakaba ...  Your work and your kid were so fulfilling for you ...  Why’d you have to die so suddenly ... ? ...That reminds me, you saw me talking to that prosecutor-- I mean, that woman in a suit, right? I remembered you were real bothered by it. She might come back, so I guess I should tell you about it. That woman was trying to get information on Wakaba’s research out of me.

text.Morgana: That’s what we heard in the Palace.

text.Sojiro Sakura: You don’t need to know what the research was about. Just know there was some trouble around it. Obviously, Wakaba got dragged into that as well. Now, they ruled her death a suicide ...  but I’ve got my doubts.

text.Morgana: Doubts? Could she have been killed?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Supposedly, there were people who wanted to take her research and use it for their own benefit ...  Don’t get me wrong though. I don’t have a lick of evidence. That’s why I haven’t told Futaba any of this. I don’t want to cause her any more trouble.

text.Morgana: It sounded like she had suspicions of her own based on what she said in the Palace.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Still, there’s one thing I regret. It was right before Wakaba died ...  She told me, "I think I might die." I brushed it off thinking it was just a joke, but if I had just taken her seriously ...  (sigh) That’s another reason I took Futaba in ...  Redemption. She went through such horrible things. Those heartless adults just yelled at the poor girl ...  Hey ...  how do you heal emotional scars?

text.ACTION: Kind of a big question, man.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Of course ...  Sorry.
N-Never mind that ...  How did you get here ... ?

text.Futaba Sakura: Uh ...  I walked.

text.Sojiro Sakura: ...You’re OK!?

text.Futaba Sakura: Was that bad?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Th-That’s not it! I’m just shocked to see you out of the house ...

text.Futaba Sakura: Uh ...  I’m sorry I worried you.

text.Sojiro Sakura: (on the verge of tears)

text.Futaba Sakura: By the way, what’s the date today?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Eh? It’s uh ...  it’s the 21st.

text.ACTION: Sojiro then walks offscreen, because I guess there was something more interesting going on over there.

text.Futaba Sakura: Oh, I remember now. Medjed.

text.Chatter: I heard someone’s tampering with the system.

text.Whisper: Is it Medjed? No, it couldn’t be ...

text.Chatter: What are the police doing? They’re so incompetent ...

text.Murmur: Even the Phantom Thieves couldn’t stop them ...

text.Futaba Sakura: Hmph, "Medjed." Now, how do we cook them?
Roger that.

text.Morgana: Hey, Futaba? We don’t have much time left. Are you sure you could do this!?

text.Futaba Sakura: Is this a dream ... ? I’m going back to sleep ...

text.Morgana: It is NOT a dream! Get up! Say something, Maaku!

text.Futaba Sakura: R-Right.

text.Morgana: Now hurry it up!

text.Futaba Sakura: ...Eh, I guess it doesn’t matter. Let’s get cracking!

text.Morgana: Hey, Futaba!
I don’t think she can hear me ...  Talk about intense concentration. This place is so messy ...  I’m surprised she can focus at all. Futaba? You should really clean your room a bit.
Oh well. Just waiting around is boring. Let’s clean the place up.

text.ACTION: I don’t think a light dusting is gonna do much, Maaku.

text.Morgana: Well, Futaba? We’re done on our end. Are you finished yet?
...  ...  Guess we’ll just have to keep waiting ...
Wh-What’s up? Something happened?

text.Futaba Sakura: It’s finished.

text.Morgana: Finished? What is?
We cleaned it.
Anyway, is it true? Did you really take care of Medjed?

text.Futaba Sakura: I handled them, and someone else handled my room ... ! I don’t understand, but this is good!

text.Morgana: Hey, Futaba! What’s wrong!?
She’s sleeping ...
Well, it looks like it’s been taken care of. I guess we should get home and sleep too ...

text.Murmur: That has to be fake, right? There’s no way!
I’m scared ...  What’s going to happen?

text.Chatter: Are the police taking action ... ? They’re ignoring it? Seriously!?

text.Murmur: Still, I’m sure the Phantom Thieves will do ...  something ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Seriously?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: She must have been quite exhausted. I can’t say I blame her at all.

text.Makoto Niijima: If Medjed’s been affected, it will surely make the news. That should be enough to confirm whether or not the deed’s been done.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: The why don’t we all watch the news together?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes. We should meet up at Leblanc as usual.

text.Ann Takamaki: See you tomorrow, guys!

text.Morgana: We should be in the clear now, right ... ?

text.Newscaster: Some citizens are trying to avoid going outdoors, and people have been in a constant state of worry.

text.ACTION: What are they worried about going outdoors for? Do they think it’s going to turn into the New York scene from Fate of the Furious?

text.Newscaster: Many corporations have been working around the clock without sleep to prepare for the attack.

text.Morgana: Nothing’s changed yet. All we can do is pray ...

text.ACTION: It occurs to me that I haven’t been showing off a particularly infamous part of this game, which is Morgana telling us to go to sleep on any day where we do anything of note. Most times you start in the attic instead of on the ground floor of Leblanc, you can’t go out at night. There’s some parts coming up that are well-known for not letting us go out for a rather long time, but I just thought I’d start including these, so you can better understand the experience and why so many people hate Morgana.

text.Murmur: Seriously!?

text.Chatter: No way ...  I can’t believe it ...

text.Whisper: This isn’t a joke, is it!?
They lost!? How could this happen ... ?

text.ACTION:
Part 92: 8/22: This Update Has Been Hacked
	Part 90: 8/22: This Update Has Been Hacked

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Boss! Hello!
Yo, you look tired.

text.Ann Takamaki: We’ve made ourselves at home.

text.TV Reporter: The site’s main page now displays what is thought to be the mark belonging to the Phantom Thieves ...  Moreso, the personal information of a Japanese man, a possible Medjed member, was illegally publicized.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Aren’t these the guys people have been up in arms about?

text.TV Reporter: Medjed has yet to issue an official reply. Furthermore, their previously announced cleanse of Japan has remained unimplemented for now. Some speculate that they have taken this series of events seriously and ultimately canceled their plan.

text.ACTION: Futaba didn’t really… do much, did she? Doxxed one person and hacked a website.
The group starts giggling and cheering quietly.

text.Sojiro Sakura: What’re you all smirking about ... ?
Well stop it. You’re gonna drive away all my customers.

text.Tabloid Show Host: After the commercial break, we will be asking guests from various fields about this turn of events.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But there ain’t any customers ... ?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Can it ...  My customers are on summer vacation too.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh crap, I just realized our break’s almost over!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: There are still ten days left.

text.Ann Takamaki: I wanna go somewhere, but we can’t just leave Futaba-chan alone.

text.Makoto Niijima: Some things still concern me too, like that "research" ...

text.Sojiro Sakura: Oh! Did you just get up?

text.Futaba Sakura: (nods)

text.Makoto Niijima: Good morning.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It seems she’s cautious of us ...

text.Makoto Niijima: Hey, why don’t we go upstairs? If any customers come, she’ll be even more afraid.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Why don’t you go with them, Futaba? Have fun. It’s about time my regulars show up anyway, so I don’t want you guys loitering around my store.

text.Masayoshi Shido: The issue I want to make clear is the attitude of the police, and more importantly, the government.
Are they doing their best to find an effective countermeasure against these Phantom Thieves? Is it not the government’s duty to create a society where its citizens can live without worry?

text.ACTION: Hey! Under the Phantom Thieves, you only have to worry if you’re an undesirable!

text.Masayoshi Shido: Unfortunately, the current cabinet is powerless. As such, they should be disbanded. I believe now is the time for me to risk my political career in hope of making a new reality. A new political system that goes beyond parties or factions ...  An ideal country of peace and order ...

text.Elderly Female Customer: I have to agree. I hope he can work to ease the anxieties of the elderly.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Hm? Oh sorry, I wasn’t listening.

text.Sae Niijima: And Medjed was in turn defeated by her real-world hacking abilities? This does correlate to the facts as we know them ...  If he’s telling the truth, then Wakaba Isshiki didn’t commit suicide ...  Did a third party target her life with the goal of destroying her research ... ? Wakaba’s death was two years ago ...  That also coincides with when the incidents started occurring ...  Does this other Metaverse user that Madarame and Kaneshiro mentioned ...  really exist ... ? Earlier, I briefly mentioned about those psychotic breakdown incidents that have alarmed the public. All of a sudden, people will lose consciousness or become violent ...  A situation as incomprehensible as that can’t be explained away as "troubled social conditions." ...I suspect that these cases are all connected to a larger, man-made plot. The method involved always muddled the explication, but your story has virtually confirmed its viability.

text.ACTION: Oh man, this is some fresh word salad. Who the fuck uses the word “explication”?

text.Sae Niijima: Although, I wouldn’t have expected a new criminal to come to light from your testimony ...  What did your group think of this other Metaverse user?

How self-centered of you. The Phantom Thieves tamper with people’s hearts without consent. How is that different? Well ...  no matter how you thought of them, there can be no doubting your resolve. Are those incidents because of you or someone else ... ? Either way, I will get to the bottom of this.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Sae is growing deeper...

text.Sae Niijima: Kunikazu Okumura ...  You should know who he is. ...Considering what happened. Your testimony regarding this incident will be serious. I’m sure you understand why. Answer my next question carefully. What did you do to this Okumura?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: To think the cognitive version of a person would transform into a such a horrible monster and attack us ...  That means our enemies aren’t limited to Shadows.

text.Ann Takamaki: I thought the other people were just victims, like the slaves at the castle or the walking ATMs.

text.Makoto Niijima: Even though they seem to be alive, they’re only part of the backdrop ...  the environment. In other words, the Palace ruler determines the form and strength of their cognitions. I would have loved to ask Futaba’s mother how far along she was with her research ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Research, huh ...  She was lookin’ into that cognitive psience stuff, yeah?

text.Makoto Niijima: If we put together all the information we’ve gathered up to this point ...  Abuse of cognitive psience can lead to death, and it may even relate to the psychotic breakdown incidents. Considering the "cognitive" aspect, I sense a strong connection between it and the Metaverse.

text.Morgana: On top of that, the research might have been stolen and used by someone else.

text.Ann Takamaki: You mean those guys that showed Futaba-chan the fake suicide note.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: If that is the case, those people are unforgivable.

text.Makoto Niijima: Hey, Futaba. Is there anything else you can remember?

text.ACTION: Futaba comes back, with more food.

text.Ann Takamaki: C’mon, no fair ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, can I snag a bite?
...Meanie.

text.Makoto Niijima: Why don’t we take a short break?
Even if Futaba is a genius, could she really crush an international hacker organization that easily?

text.ACTION: What are you talking about, Makoto? This is anime. Of course she could.

text.Futaba Sakura: The one who taunted the Phantom Thieves was a guy in Japan. I knew the Medjed members in Japan weren’t anything special, so I wasn’t worried.

text.Ann Takamaki: How do you know that?

text.Futaba Sakura: ‘Cause I’m the founder.

text.Makoto Niijima: Um ...  what do you mean? Should we take that literally?

text.Futaba Sakura: Yep. It was only me at first, back when I was referred to as the hacker of justice. But since I stayed anonymous, a buncha guys from all over the world started using the name.

text.Ann Takamaki: And those were the ones committing cybercrimes.

text.Futaba Sakura: It was a hassle to expose all of them, so I just left them be.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uhhh ...  so Futaba was the true Medjed, and we were freakin’ out over some weak-ass dipshits?

text.ACTION: Yep. Seems like the threat has been completely undermined!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You should’ve told us from the start, Futaba.

text.Futaba Sakura: I discarded the Medjed name a while ago. I’m Alibaba now.

text.Makoto Niijima: Futaba, what do you want to do now? Since you know our secret, we’d like you to join our team.

text.Ann Takamaki: Just like that ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: This may even ensure our investigation of Mementos goes along smoothly.

text.Morgana: Well ...  I guess.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well, Futaba’s real amazin’! She’s gonna be a big help for us, huh?

text.Makoto Niijima: Say, Futaba. How did you find out about us?

text.Futaba Sakura: Secret.

text.Makoto Niijima: Where did you learn to hack?

text.Futaba Sakura: Private.

text.Makoto Niijima: When did you obtain the Nav?

text.Futaba Sakura: I refuse to answer.

text.Ann Takamaki: Futaba-chan sure is unique ...  Still, it’ll be a problem if she doesn’t open up to us some more.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: At the very least, we need to be able to communicate normally with her.

text.Makoto Niijima: What should we do?

text.Ann Takamaki: How?

text.Makoto Niijima: First, we’ll need to help her open up to us. If we each spend an entire day with her, maybe she’ll get more used to being around us.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I see. We do have the time, thanks to summer vacation.

text.Makoto Niijima: We can begin tomorrow.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Let’s go to the beach! There’ll be tonsa people there, plus we got totally dried out in that desert.

text.Ann Takamaki: That’s a great idea! I forgot I hadn’t gone to the beach yet!

text.Futaba Sakura: Uh, excuse me ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: I’ll come by tomorrow. See you then.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Let me help as well. I don’t have anything planned.

text.Makoto Niijima: Thanks. We can set a schedule with everyone else depending on when they’re free.

text.Ann Takamaki: OK!

text.ACTION: Futaba grabs Morgana’s face and begins pulling on it.
What a weirdly patronizing and sexist thing to say, Akechi! Wow!

text.Sae Niijima: How can I stay calm about this!?

text.Goro Akechi: I understand how you feel.

text.Sae Niijima: Thanks to the incident with those hackers, people are calling us incompetent. And on top of all that, the Phantom Thieves are claiming justice is on their side. Don’t make me laugh.

text.Goro Akechi: Medjed was dealt with by either the Phantom Thieves themselves, or some avid supporter. There are no tracks whatsoever, so they must be quite skilled ...  Either way, the general public recognizes the Phantom Thieves as the subjugating party.

text.Sae Niijima: They’re gaining support and influence much faster than we could have anticipated ...

text.Goro Akechi: It is indeed an abnormal situation. I’m beginning to suspect mass manipulation of some kind ...  It’s even possible that a powerful person is behind them, plotting the psychotic breakdowns ...

text.Sae Niijima: It’s rare to hear you speak in that tone.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: They were saying how awesome they think the Phantom Thieves are!

text.Ann Takamaki: I’ve heard things too. It’s becoming a huge topic of conversation.

text.Makoto Niijima: Yeah, it’s really all thanks to Alibaba. You were a great help.

text.Futaba Sakura: It was nothing.

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, that reminds me ...  Remember that stuff about ATMs and banks just stopping? That wasn’t Medjed, was it?

text.Futaba Sakura: Nope, that was totally separate.

text.Makoto Niijima: So people were overreacting to mere coincidence?

text.Futaba Sakura: Either that or those rumors were never true to begin with.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm, you seem to be quite talkative in these conversations.

text.Futaba Sakura: Is that so? I’ll shut up then.
:C

text.Ann Takamaki: I don’t think I get it, but I’m pretty sure she’s angry ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You gotta apologize, Yusuke.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Me? Why?

text.Futaba Sakura: :U

text.Morgana: Hey, is this really going to be OK? I’m worried about how things will be from now on ...

text.Yuuki Mishima: There’s no doubt about it! I mean, they took Medjed down. Even the guys who had been criticizing the Phantom Thieves basically have to accept them now! The news has been spreading like wildfire too. I’ll give it an extra boost on my site as well. I bet the approval rating will be through the roof tomorrow. Look forward to it!

text.Morgana: ...Why is he of all people getting excited about this? Well, the news really did draw a lot of attention. I can’t wait to see what happens.

text.ACTION: So, our current sub-objective next to “Prove your justice to society” is “Rid Futaba of her unease.” Simple.

Anyway, this is one of the rare instances where we have our day consumed but not our night. For the next several days we’ll start in the attic, yes, but we’ll actually have the freedom to leave, holy shit! However, we’ll be spending our days helping Futaba because the game doesn’t want us going to Mementos right now until Futaba gets her codename she needs our guidance.

text.Morgana: Even so, we should keep at it.

text.Newscaster: Temperatures are rising across the country, marking the hottest days we’ve had this summer. Today’s temperature is at a record high, and many are escaping the heat by playing in the water. Throngs of people could be seen at the beach near the city, enjoying the summer weather.

text.Morgana: You have to go to the beach in the summer! We should go!

text.Young Male Customer: It’s not worth going to any beaches in Japan. They’re cramped and dirty; there’s jellyfish ...

text.Young Female Customer: What about a beach outside of Japan? Let’s go on a vacation on a tropical island!

text.Young Male Customer: We don’t have to go now, right? It’s absurd to go somewhere hot in the middle of summer.

text.ACTION: I don’t even like the beach or being outside in general, but holy shit, SEVER.

text.Innocent Grade Schooler: Mine say the same thing! My mom said not to get all proud and arrogant and stuff ...

text.Rebellious Grade Schooler: Yeah, right. Don’t listen to her. Grown-ups lie all the time.

text.Innocent Grade Schooler: I know! My parents were supposed to take me to the zoo the other day, but they broke their promise!

text.College Student 2: I wonder how they pulled it off ...  They really are amazing, huh.

text.Partying College Student: Hey-ey, whatever happened to that Akechi dude? The Phantom Thieves buried that guy—total annihilation!

text.Elderly Office Worker: We should be relieved that nothing happened. What’s more ominous is the Phantom Thieves.

text.Earnest Office Worker: How so? I thought they did well this time ...

text.Elderly Office Worker: Gaining power moves one closer to becoming an authoritarian. That’s just the way of the world.

text.Sullen Office Worker: Yes, I think so. Nothing bad actually happened, so it looks like we’ll all be safe.

text.Tired Office Worker: They admitted their wrongdoing on their own. If our superiors could do that too, it’d be real nice.

text.Sullen Office Worker: Hahaha, that’d be great. It’d be even better if that happened in every company.

text.Foreign Barker: The Phantom Thieves are awesome! They’re like a manga come to life! But, I mean—we can’t rely on them for everything, right?

text.Drunk Regular: Huh? Why not? Stop lecturing us!

text.Homeless Man: You were listening, huh? Scram if you don’t wanna get hurt. The more you struggle and resist in vain, the worse your pain and suffering, you know? Though, it’s always more fun for me when the other guy struggles ...  (chuckle)

text.Rural Young Man: They’re really somethin’ else. I wanna apprentice with ‘em.

text.Adorable Woman: I’m glad you’re finally getting it.

text.Rural Young Man: Yup. Lemme get ya somethin’ nice from the gift store back home—to show I’m sorry.

text.Adorable Woman: I take it back. You clearly don’t get it yet!

text.Fishy Hawker: This is your chance to meet those mysterious superheroes, the "Phantom Thieves!" You interested?

Relax, this’ll only take a second. Just a few seconds, OK? We’re celebrating Medjed’s fall with a party event: An Evening Chat with the Phantom Thieves. Of course, the Phantom Thieves will show up as well! It’ll be a fancy dinner at not a bad price!
What? You scared of the Phantom Thieves showing up? What are you, chicken? Well, in that case, go home already, kid! Geez, I’m wastin’ my breath here!

text.Beefy Trendsetter: He must be hurting so much inside. I wish I could cheer up my dearest Akechi-kun ...

text.Scruffy Romantic: "My Akechi-kun," my ass. Your sparkly eyes are hilarious next to your five o’clock shadow.

text.Beefy Trendsetter: You’ve got nose hair sticking out too, you bushy-haired beast!

text.Shiro Asakura: It’s a heavy burden, making my dream—OUR dream—come true. I was unable to shoulder that.

text.Dream-Chasing Woman: Yeah ...  I gotta work hard to make our dreams come true. You’re right, Mr. Asakura. But I know I can do it!

text.ACTION: Let’s talk to the same guy as last time.

text.Red-Faced Man (Nagai): I’d like to ask for a young person’s opinion on the recent fluctuation in stock prices ...

text.Morgana: ...Well, you might as well humor him.

text.Joker: I talked to a drunk guy and learned so much that I am literally incapable of getting any smarter.

text.Lala Escargot: Oh, my ...  You look quite exhausted. Here, have a seat.

text.Miserable Office Worker: As soon as I talk back, he makes sure I know I’m lower than him. He insinuates he’ll demote me ...  After that, I’ll overhear him talking about me, calling me useless while I’m at work ...  And everything I’ve done, all the results I’m getting ...  Somehow, he’s taking all the credit.

text.Lala Escargot: That is the worst kind of workplace abuse. I cannot believe that man ...

text.Miserable Office Worker: So many people have quit because of stress. And yet, the higher-ups all ignore it. Of all the terrible bosses I could get in the world, why did mine have to be Shinsuke Kishi? (sigh) Hey, Lala. I wish the Phantom Thieves could do something and help me with this ...

text.Lala Escargot: Like how? Are you going to ask them to steal all your stress away?

text.Miserable Office Worker: Hahaha ...  No. I guess it’s impossible. But it’s nice to think about ...

text.Igor: It seems you freed the heart of a frenzied girl and saved her from her haunted past. (chuckle) Another step has been taken to rehabilitation ...  You are progressing quite nicely.

text.Caroline: Our master bestows words of praise upon you! You’d better feel honored!

text.Igor: By the by, more curious information has found its way to your ears.

text.ACTION: At times it can feel like the translators really wanted to use a weird word or choice of phrase that ends up sticking out badly. “By the by” is not a thing an actual human would ever say, and don’t be a smartass and reply to that with “Igor isn’t human.” It’s creepy and weird in a completely separate manner from his own creepy, weird self.

text.Igor: A scientist’s research ...  It seems that world may secretly be known after all. Furthermore, that very research has been stolen and is now used by those with malicious intent ...  I wonder how this will change the approach you take toward your rehabilitation ...
I believe I told you we would spare no expense in cooperating with you. Allow me to grant you a new power worthy of your current self.

text.ACTION: Note- the game developers may have forgotten to add new power.

text.Igor: Though you have my aid, be sure not to let your guard down. Otherwise you may get swept off your feet ...

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Igor is growing deeper ...

text.Igor: ...We shall meet again in the near future.

text.ACTION:
Part 93: 8/23-8/24: Yakuza Seven
	Part 91: 8/23-8/24: Yakuza Seven
Everyone who commented saying “by the by” isn’t actually a weird thing to say: trap sprung, motherfuckers. I know you’re all actually 80.
And our percentage has increased once more.

text.Whisper: Can you believe they actually took down hackers!?

text.Chatter: It’s cool how they don’t reveal what they’re doing.

text.Anon: won’t help me, so fuck em

text.Futaba Sakura: YYYou never mentioned this.

text.ACTION: Yusuke turns, interested in something on the nearby shelf.

Yes. You must be well-versed in speaking when you are student council president. Don’t think too hard about our conversation. We’re just going to talk about ordinary topics today.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: And what do you mean by ordinary topics?

text.Makoto Niijima: You know, things like food or the weather. Well then, let’s begin with food. What do you like to eat, Futaba?

text.Futaba Sakura: Organic ones.

text.Makoto Niijima: Um, that wasn’t exactly what I meant ...
L-Let’s try a different topic! How about the weather? I heard that this heat wave is showing no sign of stopping ...

text.Futaba Sakura: Dunno. I haven’t been out.

text.Makoto Niijima: O-Oh, right ...

text.Morgana: Makoto’s getting overwhelmed ...

text.Makoto Niijima: Th-This is odd ...  It wasn’t supposed to go like this ...

text.Futaba Sakura: W-Waaaaaaaah!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: They appear to be quite shoddily-made.

text.Futaba Sakura: They’re from "Phoenix Rangers Neo Featherman"! No ...  Yellow and Pink’s heads ...  And Red’s been hacked to bits ...  This is all Inari’s fault ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Inari?

text.Futaba Sakura: Your thief clothes were like a fox. According to Japanese folklore, foxes like inarizushi, thus Inari.

text.ACTION: Oh boy, more impenetrable cultural references!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Inari ...

text.Futaba Sakura: Rghhh, they were in the perfect poses too ... ! It was so much work getting them set up just right! You wouldn’t know aesthetics if it hit you in the face, Inari!

text.Makoto Niijima: Yeah ...

text.Futaba Sakura: Mm-hm. Victory is great for action, and Neo’s got the best transforming suit. So cool.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Fascinating. Art depicts a flash of inspiration, but models offer a much different means of enjoyment.

text.Morgana: Huh? Take a look at that—Futaba’s having a regular conversation.

text.Makoto Niijima: It seems she doesn’t have a problem talking to others as long as the subject interests her. I suppose the topics I brought up were not the right ones.

text.Futaba Sakura: So this is all I gotta do? What a breeze!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: In that case, we should advance to the next step. How about we have her spend time in someone else’s room?

text.Makoto Niijima: Yes. She hasn’t had many chances to leave the house yet, so that would be the perfect opportunity.

text.Futaba Sakura: Don’t set the bar so high!

text.Futaba Sakura: Can I wear my mask?

text.Makoto Niijima: I-I think it would be best if you didn’t ...

She’s still got a long way to go, though. I wonder how long before she’s ready for the beach ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes, they have only spoken of the Phantom Thieves for the entirety of today.

text.Makoto Niijima: We’ve been getting attention all over the city.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So ...  how’s the one who helped us take Medjed down doing?

text.Ann Takamaki: Futaba-chan!

text.Futaba Sakura: Shut it, Inari.

text.Ann Takamaki: We have so much to talk about! Oooh, I can’t wait!

text.Morgana: Whoa, this is huge! We won!

All right, I’ll tell you about the shop. It’s a piece of cake for a gun enthusiast like you, right?
If you’re considered an employee, you won’t seem suspicious coming in and out of the shop, right? If you get what I’m sayin’, bring the goods to the back.

Hmph, a kid like you ... ?  ...  ...  ...You goin’ through somethin’ similar? I guess you wouldn’t be doin’ any of this if you weren’t, huh ...  Don’t gimme any details though. I don’t wanna know. text.ACTION: I want more than anything for Iwai to rip off his jacket and have like a full-back lizard tattoo or some shit. I know he’s got the neck tat, but it’s not the same.

Let’s just insult this dangerous former gang member to his face, then.

text.Hifumi Togo: What ... ? You’ll help me think ... ? Thank you so much ... !
My mother told me that I should lose my upcoming exhibition match against the pro ...

It’s a "strategy" she devised ...  She says that if I lose to a man, I’ll get sympathy from women, and as a result get more female fans. Then when I make my comeback, I’ll become a symbol for strong women everywhere. That way, I can use the weekly magazine’s popularity against them and instantly become famous.

I feel my mother may be right. People do love a good comeback story. Coming from the TV industry, my mother does have great insight for entertainment. This time around ...  I couldn’t help but argue. It’s the wrong thing to do ...  I actually got into a fight with my mother. It wasn’t the first time, but ...  What made me sad was ...  I realized my mother doesn’t see me as a shogi player ...  She said that there’s no need for me to be putting so much time and effort into shogi ...  ...And that once I become famous I can quit shogi and make money from my looks.

The only reason she continues to support my shogi career is so she can profit off of me as an idol. She doesn’t mind if I lose a match, as long as I build my reputation and make money. To my mother, shogi is just a vehicle to make me famous ...
Even if it helped me to become famous and eased my parents’ burden ...  I don’t want to turn my back on shogi ...  a game that both my father and I love ...

...If only that were possible. She’s the kind of woman who never changes her mind ...  She wants to achieve her unfulfilled dream of becoming a celebrity ...  through me. I highly doubt she would ever reconsider ...

We blew the lids off countless scandals together. ...That is, until that day came.

We were on the trail of a certain bureaucrat, who was involved in a slush fund to support refugees. He kept himself pretty well guarded, so it was almost impossible to get any solid leads on the guy ...  Then one night, I got a voicemail from Kayo saying she had gotten hold of something big. text.Goro Akechi: This place is more than I imagined it to be. The atmosphere is wonderful. No wonder Sae-san recommended it so strongly to me.

text.Sojiro Sakura: I already told her everything I know. There’s nothing more I got for you people.

text.Goro Akechi: Oh no, that’s not my intention. I just came to enjoy some coffee.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Oh ...

text.Goro Akechi: Oh, you must be Wakaba Isshiki’s ...
I’ll have whatever you recommend.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Coming right up.

text.ACTION: Dude, Sae told you what she did last time she was here. Why the hell would you think Sojiro would be hospitable?

text.Goro Akechi: ...Did I bother you? My apologies. Apparently, my mother was in a relationship with some low-life of a man ...
She was swiftly discarded when he learned she was pregnant ...  That despair would lead to her death.
Thanks to him, I was passed from foster home to foster home. But, I do quite well by myself these days.

text.ACTION: Good for you, buddy. I’d ask how you managed to gain enough of a good education and whatever else you needed to become a fucking police detective at the age of seventeen from those circumstances, but that never made sense in the first place and also I really don’t care.

text.Goro Akechi: Ah, yes. Medjed. ...To thinks they’d be taken down by another hacker.

text.ACTION: What is up with all the non-sequiturs, man? Is your brain a fucking View-Master, just randomly switching from subject to subject as if by the whims of a small, impatient, easily bored child?

text.Goro Akechi: I’m not sure whether Medjed was defeated by the Phantom Thieves themselves or an avid supporter ...
Many kids your age seem to be fans of the Phantom Thieves ...  Do you like them too?
What’s the matter?
(chuckle) Thank you. Although I’d rather not be compared to people like the Phantom Thieves, if at all possible.
Mm, this is delicious. You get to drink this coffee every day? I’m incredibly jealous. I would never have thought you’d be boarding at this cafe ...  We seem to share some kind of bond.
(chuckle) Thank you. I believe that fate brings people together. It’s strange, but talking to you is thought-provoking. Well ...  I think I found my go-to cafe.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Akechi is growing deeper...

text.Chatter: I always change the channel when I see him.
All he ever does is nitpick.
There’s no way the Phantom Thieves are the bad guys!
He’s so desperate. It’s kinda lame.

text.Futaba Sakura: I’m outside Leblanc.
Can we? I bought some.
Mm-hm. I ran into Mona on the way back though.

text.Morgana: If she can do that, she should be good to go. Plus she did a great job dodging that ace detective.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Hold on, Futaba. I haven’t even put out my cigarette yet ...

text.Morgana: C’mon, don’t get the smoke on me!

text.Sojiro Sakura: Hey ...  the cat doesn’t like the smoke! Keep the flames away from him.

text.Futaba Sakura: Daaaaaang! I made a huge one! Sojiro, look! Look!

text.Sojiro Sakura: R-Right. Just be careful, OK? Memories of summer, huh...

text.Morgana: N-Nooo! (cough) (wheeze)

text.ACTION: Aww. That’s legitimately one of the sweetest scenes in the game.

text.Futaba Sakura: I’ll be good on my own, y’know.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I only ask that you try not to get separated from each other in the crowd, OK?

text.Futaba Sakura: No worries. I’ve already made preparations for when that happens.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That don’t make me feel better ...

text.Morgana: Make sure you keep an eye on her. It’s tough enough going solo, let alone watching over someone else. Still, going to enjoy the beach ...  We can finally have a good time!
Futaba ... !

text.Newscaster: Air pressure continues to be high, and it’s expected that today’s sunniness will continue tomorrow.

text.Morgana: Looks like we don’t have to worry about the weather! I can’t wait for tomorrow!
She must have wanted you to see that. I guess good things can happen when you least expect them.

text.ACTION: At least we’re almost done with aojiru buying. Maaku gains Kindness +1.

text.Rocker: Meanwhile, I haven’t made any progress ...  I can’t have that, yo! Listen up, yo! Check out my "Phantom Anthem"! Say Phantom, say Anthem/Say Phantom, say Anthem/Phantom Thieves are on the rise/But m’popularity’s takin’ a dive/They reached top, I’m at a stop/Got m’moms back in the countryside/Big city’s a hard place to reside/Passion in m’head, mess up I’m dead/Say Phantom, say Anthem/Say Phantom, say Anthem/ How was it, m’main man? Wasn’t my performance filled with passion?
Livin’ in the city costs a lot of dough, yo. That’s why I gotta become a big star!

Your fate is very ...  interesting, so I’d like to try a different fortune-telling technique ...  I’ve gone through all my books ...  Maybe I need some that are out of print. Where I can [sic] find some ... ? Oh, never mind. Let’s begin the verification test.

Maybe I should invite her to Book Town...

Hmm, there’s a lot here ...  Which ones would be good as reference?
But since I’ve never had, well, a "normal" job, I didn’t know what to say sometimes. Those would definitely be worth reading!
With those, you feel like just reading them is enough. You end up not actually helping yourself. So I want to learn the ideas in these, and be able to express them to help my customers.
That used bookstore’s sign says "Study of Destiny"! Wh ...  a fortune-telling specific shop!? Hamiru-san, let’s go check it out!

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Chihaya will grow stronger soon...

WHAT HAPPENED TO THE LOBSTERS, I DEMAND TO KNOW

text.Futaba Sakura: It’s because everyone said that I killed her. Everyone looked at me thinking I was a murderer. I ended up hating this world. That’s why I shut myself in and covered my ears. I wished ...  I wished my mom would come back to life. Sometimes, I’d wake up and think it was all a dream. But nothing had changed in the world. That’s why I’d sleep again. It’d be a repeat of that ...

text.Makoto Niijima: Ah ...

text.Futaba Sakura: How she’d work late into the night. How she’d wake up early and make me a boxed lunch every day. How she’d do her best to further her research. How she’d scold me for peeking at her notes.
