text.Makoto Niijima: He seems a little irritated.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I heard he was abusin’ animals just to take his anger out on them.

text.Ann Takamaki: I can’t let him get away with something like that!

text.Morgana: You guys, don’t go easy on him!

text.Shadow Tsuboi: Maybe they die when I use ‘em to blow off steam, but the shelter was gonna kill ‘em, anyway. In fact, I bet those cats are happy to be so useful to humans!

text.Morgana: What a poor excuse for a human being! I could never forgive someone like you!

text.Shadow Tsuboi: Why don’t you complain to the irresponsible people taking their pets to the pound, huh? Well, who cares. You guys are superheroes, right? Then hurry up and destroy this rotten society!

text.Morgana: We’ll take your twisted desires, but first I’ll show you the pain you caused those poor animals!

text.Shadow Tsuboi: Huh? Wait, are you some kind of cat monster?

text.Morgana: Let’s do it, Joker! I’ll show you the wrath of cats!

text.Shadow Tsuboi: Humans and cats are a prime example. Now, who is stronger: me or the Phantom Thieves!?

text.ACTION: Okay, so the first thing Tsuboi will do is increase everyone’s ailment susceptibility using Stagnant Air.
Then he’ll use Flash Bomb to make people dizzy. He might also try to instant-kill someone with Mudo.
This guy’s pretty simple to deal wit--oh goddammit
ANYWAY (thank god the game lets you restart from the beginning of the last boss or miniboss)

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That’s a good idea. Perhaps then, he’ll understand what those animals had to endure.

text.Shadow Tsuboi: I-I’m sorry! Wh-What should I do?

text.Makoto Niijima: Remember the awful things you did to those cats. Doesn’t it make you feel horrible?

text.Shadow Tsuboi: (sob) I’ve done something terrible. I’m even less than an animal. I’m worthless trash...

text.Morgana: I won’t tell you to give up your life. But you will spend the rest of your life in guilt.

text.ACTION: And our reward is yet another Despair weapon, though this one actually does some damage in expense for not having quite as high an application rate.
We have so many goddamn lockpicks
Mementos Scan doesn’t activate as often as you’d like (which is pretty much always), but it’s still good to be able to skip a floor.
Next target, Naguri, the punk assaulting people.

text.Makoto Niijima: He’s got a crazy look in his eyes.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: He’s been known to attack indiscriminately. I suppose he really has lost his sanity...

text.Ann Takamaki: If we don’t make him have a change of heart, I won’t feel safe walking around in public.

text.Morgana: We have to do this.

text.Ann Takamaki: Oh, geez, he’s the annoying type...

text.Shadow Naguri: So, uh, can I help you? You didn’t come to pick a fight with me, did you? That can’t be.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Stop playin’ dumb, you crazy criminal.

text.Shadow Naguri: I’m doing the world a service. We’ve got an overpopulation problem with too many old people. Just think of this as my own personal brand of justice. Anyways, it doesn’t involve you punks!

text.Morgana: Urgh, let’s take him down, Joker!

text.Kin ki: You’ll regret picking a fight with me. I’m going to beat you to a pulp!

text.ACTION: Naguri has a huge health pool, but also takes an absurd amount of damage more than normal enemies. My first attack, a medium Psy spell, did 455 damage to him. Rakunda + Bufula broke 1k. He’ll use Tarukaja, but even with that, his only move worth worrying about is Swift Strike. It’s a really easy fight.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: "Sorry" won’t cut it. You attacked and hurt a lot of people, you know?

text.Makoto Niijima: Tell the police everything.

text.Shadow Naguri: Turn myself in ...  I guess there’s no other way. I’ve been doing something truly horrible. I need to be punished for it ...

text.ACTION: Oh shit, a Charge skill card. Charge (and its equivalent for magic skills, Concentrate) boosts the power of the next Physical skill you use by 2.5 times. Rakunda plus Tarukaja plus Charge equals some Fist of the North Star, exploding a dude with your pinky shit.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We were fortunate to have caught him before anyone died. We should be quite grateful for that fact.

text.ACTION: All right, next is Kishi, the credit-stealing boss.

text.Ann Takamaki: God, he looks pigheaded ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This guy abused his position at work, right? Harassin’ the people under him and all that.

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s people like him who create awful workplace environments ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Let’s talk to him.
Stealing credit from your subordinates is one of the worst things you can do as a superior.

text.Shadow Kishi: That’s my way of management. It’s efficient—I give the orders, and my underlings do all the work. It’s a pretty easy job. As long as the numbers go up, that idiot president won’t say anything. If my underlings have a problem, they should just get promoted. But since I evaluate them...

text.Ann Takamaki: How did someone like you ever get promoted? If I were the president, you’d be fired!

text.Shadow Kishi: Shut up, kids! Your reasoning doesn’t apply in the real world! If you don’t get it, I’ll teach you a lesson as your high and mighty ruler!

text.Morgana: Let’s go!

text.Shadow Kishi: Your coming here happened by circumstance, but the results that follow—they’ll favor me!

text.ACTION: Kishi will use Brain Shake to inflict Brainwash, but has a rather small HP pool and doesn’t seem to have many more tricks than that… until he casts Diarahan to fully heal himself. He’s weak to Bless skills, though, so we can take advantage of that to take him down before he drags this out too long.
From that fight Ann learns Maragion, a multi-target medium Fire spell, which we slot in to replace the strictly inferior Maragi.

text.Shadow Kishi: You’re right. That vicious cycle should have stopped with me. What have I done to my precious subordinates? I made them take responsibility for my mistakes, sent them far away, messed up their lives ...  It’s all my fault ...  All mine ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: How do you intend to take responsibility for all this?

text.Shadow Kishi: I’ll read some business books. I’ll try to do what I can to become an ideal boss ...

text.Makoto Niijima: I want you to think carefully about what kind of boss you’d like to work for. Figure it out.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: An amusement park guidebook!? Even if you abused your subordinates, I guess your kids were real important to you ...

text.ACTION: It’s nice to occasionally see a motive for distortion that isn’t “AAARGH I’M EVIL!”
Hang on, everybody… we’re halfway done… hooray.

text.Morgana: Maybe this means we’re close to our goal?

text.ACTION: On the very next floor, we come to the end of this block, as well as Jochi, the man trying to evict the theater owners in Yongen.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Judging from the smirk on his face, it looks like he’s scheming something awful.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I heard he was threatenin’ this old couple, tryin’ to kick them out of their own movie theater.

text.Makoto Niijima: If we leave him alone, he may resort to violence.

text.Ann Takamaki: We can’t let that happen! Let’s go!

text.Makoto Niijima: It seems like you’re trying to use force to get people to leave their property?

text.Shadow Jochi: Land development is important. Getting rid of stubborn people in my way is part of the job. I’m not just playing around, like you kids are doing!

text.Makoto Niijima: We’re quite serious. We can’t let those who cause problems for others to go unpunished. That includes people like you, who use bullying tactics to get what they want.

text.Shadow Jochi: You’re just pissy-smelling kids acting big. You should’ve stopped playing hero back in preschool!

text.ACTION: Weak to Electricity, likes to use annoying Physical moves. Doesn’t really have a lot else in its kit. The thing about Mementos bosses is that the ones that don’t kick the shit out of you don’t really have that much going for them.

text.Shadow Jochi: Please, isn’t there some way I can have the movie theater?

text.Morgana: Yeah, know when to give up.

text.Shadow Jochi: Oh, er, I’m sorry. I’ll give up. So please, forgive me...

text.Makoto Niijima: I hope you’ll consider the feelings of those who get things take from them from now on.

text.Shadow Jochi: I-I got it ...  I’ll be honest with my superiors. I’ll tell them that no one has any interest in leaving Yongen ...

text.Makoto Niijima: Not just Yongen! You better make up for the awful things you’ve done elsewhere, too!

text.ACTION: Uh, wait a second. He said he was gonna get fired if he didn’t get his bosses this property, right? Doesn’t that just mean they’ll send someone else? Even worse, doesn’t that mean they’re going to keep doing this elsewhere? Hello? Nobody cares? All right.
This is some form of book, likely one that unlocks a new hangout.

Part 103: 9/6: MEMENTOS SUUUUUUUCKS
	Part 99.5: 9/6: MEMENTOS SUUUUUUUCKS
The door behind Jochi opens upon inspection.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Sweet, now we can keep movin’.

text.Morgana: Just be careful, OK? The deeper we go, the stronger the enemies get.

text.ACTION: The word Akzeriuth, even with all these extra “Y”s, is giving me traumatic flashbacks to Tales of the Abyss. The root word of both is the Hebrew word Achzariyut, or cruelty.

text.Morgana: That’s a sign of how much more twisted this place is. I’m sure the Shadows here are stronger, too.

text.Futaba Sakura: Yeah, and looks like there are more enemies here than there were up above. Be careful, OK?

text.ACTION: Eventually, we come to another rest area and I realize I’ve been neglecting to cover an easy-to-ignore source of conversation: Rest area Mementos discussions. In actual Palaces, the option to discuss progress is pretty pointless outside of the game giving you a vague hint of how much further you have to go, but in Mementos the characters actually stop and think about how goddamn weird this place is, holy shit.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Mementos is the Palace of the general public, correct?

text.Morgana: Yeah, what’s your point?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Well, Madarame’s was a museum, Kaneshiro’s was a bank, and the teacher Kamoshida’s was a castle ...  Essentially, it seems that the appearance of a Palace is rooted in the distorted desires of its ruler. But in that case ...  why is this place a subway? Is that what the general public desires?

text.Makoto Niijima: He makes a good point. I wondered the same thing when I first came here ...

text.Morgana: Even I don’t know the answer. The existence of Mementos is a pretty special thing to begin with.

text.Ann Takamaki: Didn’t you say it’s the source of all other Palaces?

text.Morgana: Yeah ...  It’s fundamentally different from just one person’s distortions. The layout changes every time too. Even its current appearance as a subway might be temporary. If that’s true, then ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, I don’t wanna rain on your parade or nothing, but aren’t we here to check that out ourselves? Wouldn’t it be faster to just get to the bottom and be done with it?

text.Makoto Niijima: Perhaps, but ...

text.Morgana: No, Skull is unfortunately right. This isn’t something we’ll be able to find the answer to right now. I’m sure the mystery will be solved if we can reach the depths of this place though.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Did you really hafta say that me bein’ right was "unfortunate"?

text.ACTION: Later, we come across Pisaca, the one new enemy we encounter this entire Mementos visit. It likes to inflict Sleep and use Physical skills, and is weak to Fire.

Next, we encounter the cheater, Nejima. Still can’t believe we’re actually doing this. Besides, he’s just cheating at a video game, I really fucking doubt his distortion is so great that his Shadow will be able to put up any form of resistance against us.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: He looks so ...  pathetic.

text.Ann Takamaki: He’s cheating in a video game, right?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, he’s a cheater. It’s not something an adult should be doin’.

text.Ann Takamaki: Let’s go.

text.Shadow Nejima: In the Gun About world, no one can defeat me! Cheating? I don’t know what you’re talking about ...  The winners are the ones who decide what is right! It’s the winners who decide what justice is! And what greater winner is there than me? I’m the god of the Gun About world! I am the god of the Gun About world! I am invincible! No one can ever hope to defeat me!

text.ACTION: You, uh… You said the same thing twice, dude.

text.Shadow Nejima: No matter how many come against me, no one can ever wound me!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Psh! Idiot! Let’s get him!

text.ACTION: Shadow Nejima (You should actually probably watch this one)

text.Shadow Nejima: Ain’t no matter what you throw my way, you won’t put a scratch on me!

text.ACTION: So, the first thing we’ll notice, and this should set off some alarms immediately, is that this is the only voiced Mementos target in the entire game. I wasn’t kidding when I said "watch this," by the way. You need to hear this dude’s accent.
And he can enrage us, great.
A few turns of pointless, missed attacks later...

text.Futaba Sakura: Look at him, acting all smug because of his cheats ...  We can’t do anything to him at this rate though. Let’s retreat for now and rethink our approach.

text.ACTION: And then we just leave! The great and mighty Phantom Thieves, forced into retreat by a fucking PUBG hacker! What the hell is this game?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Yes ...  Unfortunately, it appears we do not have even a chance of victory.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yo, Morgana. Ain’t there anything we can do?

text.Morgana: I’m not sure. As I’ve already mentioned, the Metaverse is a place where people’s cognitions materialize. Even I can’t predict what will happen here ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit! If only we could figure out what his ability is ...

text.ACTION: We know what his ability is, you dumbass. I just don’t get how “uses cheats in a video game” translates to “his repressed emotions have become an unkillable superbeing.”

text.Futaba Sakura: That’s exactly right!

text.Makoto Niijima: So we’ll need to figure out a way to break through his cheat ...

text.Morgana: That’s fine, but let’s do it somewhere else. It’s not exactly what I’d call safe here. We should talk more where there aren’t Shadows.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We can make it our homework then. Let us think more on this topic after we return to reality.

text.Makoto Niijima: I hope it doesn’t add too much more work to your plate.

text.ACTION: It’s fine, Makoto. I already have to do everything around here.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Homework ...  Eh, I guess that works. Anyways, let’s get goin’.

text.Futaba Sakura: This is the sixth area on this floor, but counting the entire Palace ...  it’s the thirty-third one.

text.Ann Takamaki: Thirty-three areas? I’m starting to feel kind of overwhelmed ...  Just how big is this place?

text.Futaba Sakura: Who knows? This whole place, its overall structure ...  It’s all a mystery. Oh well. Just, uh, hang in there ... !

text.ACTION: We have to head back down, though, because we still have two other targets to take care of. This Mementos trip is a nightmare that will never cease. The game is at least kind enough to inform us when we return to the cheater’s floor, however, so we don’t accidentally go right back into his den.
Another good pull from a random locked chest, all right.
This interaction isn’t important, I just thought it was kinda charming.
We finally make it as deep as we’re going to go today for Mitsuyo Togo, Hifumi’s mother.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: She’s using her just like a pawn, from what I hear.

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s her own daughter ...  What is wrong with her?

text.Ann Takamaki: I don’t know much about shogi, but I do know she’s a bad person!

text.Morgana: It’s as you say, Lady Ann! Let’s get her!

text.Hifumi Togo: I gave birth to her. I raised her! My child should be devoted to serving me! I can finally be happy once Hifumi becomes a famous shogi player!
Hmph. ...She thinks she rose in rank on her own skill, but most of those matches were fixed.

I’m the one who’s been building Hifumi’s commercial value! If I didn’t get rid of all her rivals, she wouldn’t be where she is now! I enlisted private investigators and even criminals to find their weaknesses and destroy them! I paid off anyone who might have complained or spoken out.

text.ACTION: ...Don’t you work in a nightclub? How are you affording all this hush money?

text.Hifumi Togo: Oh, and I even sold stories to those weekly magazines. Heroines and tragedies go hand in hand!

text.ACTION: Don’t quote this line pretending it answers the previous question I just asked, because it doesn’t. They’re not paying you that much money for some dumb tabloid story about an amateur shogi player.

text.Hifumi Togo: One more step, and my vision for Hifumi will be realized. I’m so close to victory! I won’t let anyone get in the way!

text.ACTION: So, I’d actually recommend watching the video for this one, because hoo boy, this fight. At the end there I almost die several times, especially after an incredibly unlucky Mamudoon instant kills the entire party except for Maaku (twice). She can cast heavy Fire, Ice, Electricity, and Curse for over 200 damage per, use medium multitarget spells, and generally kick your shit in. More than once I either survive an attack with HP you can count on one hand or dodge an attack that absolutely would have killed me. It’s easily the hardest (real) fight we’ve been in all day.

And she has a lot of fucking health. But hey, at least she’s weak to Bless. Attacks do so little damage across the board, however, that it’s really better to Baton Pass over to Ryuji and have him use Assault Dive rather than go for the All-out Attack.
Morgana learns Magarula, which replaces Magaru.

Yusuke learns Counterstrike as well, though he’s a total scrub who gets all his kills by camping. It replaces his normal Counter skill, as the former has a 15% chance of reflecting Physical damage as opposed to 10%, and the effect does not stack.

text.Hifumi Togo: I could never win on my own. I had to use Hifumi, I had to...

I never meant to make Hifumi unhappy. Never. But when she won that grade school competition ...  She started being called a "genius girl," and I could never get that out of my head ...  I turned out to be such a horrible mother. I’m sorry, Hifumi, I’m sorry...

text.ACTION: A Bead Chain is an item that lets you fully restore the party’s HP. It’s pretty good.

text.Joker: Mitsuyo seems to have had a change of heart. I should go check with Hifumi...

text.ACTION: Finally, we’re on the last target, who we accidentally skipped because the system for telling you where each target is in each block is just Morgana saying “the closest one’s below/above us, I guess” which is about as intuitive as it sounds. Anyway, we’re going after Oyamada, who’s forcing Takemi to close her clinic. We could have conceivably done this target much earlier in the game, so it’ll be a few blocks behind us and pretty weak.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That bastard looks like he’s been eatin’ well lately.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm. He made a mistake in rushing a drug’s development, and now intends for his subordinate to take the fall.

text.Ann Takamaki: People might die if we don’t change his heart! And a good doctor will have to quit ...

text.ACTION: Takemi’s no Freddie Highmore, that’s for sure. I hope you enjoyed this awful Photoshop goof because it took way longer than it should have.
Also, I kinda take issue with calling Takemi a “good doctor.” She tests her experimental drugs on high school students until they pass out. Plus, she sells a ton of weird pharmaceuticals on the side.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah. We gotta do something!

text.Shadow Oyamada: As head of the medical office, I’m superior to everyone! I deserve all your respect! You should be begging me to examine you! Be grateful I have the compassion to fix you trash!

Ah, you’re that kid who was at Takemi’s. So how’s she doing? She was sooo depressed when she heard her patient died. Oh, I’m so worried about her. Poor girl ...  Hehe ...  Hehehe ...  Hahahahaha! It’s been so long since I’ve felt so exhilarated! Did she quit being a doctor yet? If she hasn’t, then tell her she better hurry it up!

Wha--!? You dare talk to me, your superior, like that!? Grr ...  Your diagnosis is "arrogance with no chance of recovery." I better "treat" you right away! And I’ll blame your death on Takemi messing up again!

text.ACTION: Wait, what does happen if we die in the Metaverse? Is it a P4 situation, where we get ejected into the subway system or something?

Oyamada uses weak Almighty attacks. He probably does some other shit, too, but uh… Morgana got a critical hit with Lucky Punch and the resulting All-out Attack killed him. He was only alive long enough for two party members to take a turn. Laaaaaame.

text.Shadow Oyamada: I want to save people’s lives. And I want to do something great, and help make medical history. But I’m just a mediocre doctor. I’ve only gotten promoted because of my university connections.

text.ACTION: Medical Chief of Staff is a little high in the ranks to rise to out of pure nepotism, isn’t it?

text.Shadow Oyamada: Takemi, though, was so creative. She had all these ideas, and her techniques were extraordinary ... ! Everything I ever wanted—fame, prestige—she earned in just a few short years ...  I was jealous of her. That’s why I tried to take all the credit for her new drug...

text.ACTION: I like getting to just go “man, fuck you.”

text.Shadow Oyamada: Ha ...  Haha ...  If only there were a medication that works on jealousy ...   ...  ...  Takemi’s patient isn’t dead.

I thought she wouldn’t recover, so I moved her to the hospice wing for terminally ill patients. But that patient didn’t believe my diagnosis. She ended up transferring to another hospital. Of course, transferring to another hospital makes our own hospital and university look really bad. That’s why I made everyone tell the same lie: the patient chose to leave the hospice, and then died.

text.ACTION: That’s really dumb and makes no sense!

text.Shadow Oyamada: She doesn’t have much time left, but maybe Takemi could do something about it.

text.Joker: It sounds like the patient is still alive. I should go tell Takemi about this right away ...

text.ACTION: I’ve already recorded a bunch in advance so I bring you this spoiler alert from the future: We’re going to fuck around for over two weeks and not do that.
Well, that’s all of them. Holy shit. We’re done. I… can’t really believe it. It kind of just feels like a part of me died in the process.

The amount of time we spent in Mementos today spanned just under two and a half hours. For context, trying to fit more than an hour of recording into an update usually results in it being obscenely long. A full Palace usually takes around four hours, also, but keep in mind that there’s actual shit to do and forward progression in a Palace, and also I don’t ever fucking try to fit an entire Palace into a single update. This was a nightmare, pure and simple, so mind-numbingly tedious that even as I was playing it I had to split it up over two play sessions, and spending the last nine hours or so trying to wash my hands of it have been excruciating. I’m not trying to whine to you guys about how bad Mementos is, both because that’s pathetic and also because you’ll never truly understand it the way I do when I say FUCK MEMENTOS.
...But on the bright side, we now have about 470,000 yen. So there's that.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: He is invincible at his game, so he is invincible in Mementos as well ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Then how about we just beat him at that game of his? Oh, but he’ll just cheat...

text.Futaba Sakura: How ‘bout we ask for help from a skilled player? Supposedly there’s an insanely good gamer they call the "King" somewhere in this city. I’ve seen all over the forums how he managed to beat this cheater himself with orthodox methods.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real!? Where can we find him?

text.Futaba Sakura: I checked his account from the official server ...  But I couldn’t pinpoint what arcade he goes to. Sorry ...

text.Ann Takamaki: But if he’s really that famous, won’t it be easy to find him?

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s true. OK, we should gather intel on the King at the arcades around the city.

text.Morgana: I didn’t know someone could get famous just by being good at a video game ...  In any case, we might be able to get through this if we can find this King. With his help ...  we’ll crush that cheating jerk for sure!

text.Sojiro Sakura: There’s a bunch of dishes that need cleaning. Sorry, but I’m gonna need you to help with ‘em.

text.ACTION: Eh, fine with me, I spent the day in the Metaverse so it’s not like I’ve got an evening period to waste.

text.Sojiro Sakura: That’s enough help for today. Go on and head up to bed.

text.Futaba Sakura: Have fun. I’ll make sure I keep working on you-know-what after I’m done taking a breather. By the way, Sojiro ...  are people on probation even allowed out of the country?

text.ACTION: According to that one TV quiz we saw months ago, yes!

text.Sojiro Sakura: There’s no law saying they’re not. As long as it’s fine by me, it’s fine in the eyes of the law. I mean, not letting a kid take part in school events probably wouldn’t be good for his rehab.

text.Futaba Sakura: Huh ...  But if anything bad happens on the trip, it’ll be the school’s responsibility.

text.Sojiro Sakura: That’s right.

text.Futaba Sakura: Aren’t you gonna ask for any souvenirs from Hawaii? No hula doll or anything?

text.Morgana: No.

text.Futaba Sakura: Heyyy, Mona’s acting weird!

text.Morgana: Not necessarily ...

text.Sojiro Sakura: Hey, don’t let the cat up on the counter, OK?

text.Futaba Sakura: ...Weird Mona.

text.Makoto Niijima: Thank you. Take care of yourself, Yusuke. And Futaba, we’ll be relying on you for the analysis.

text.Futaba Sakura: Leave it to me.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Just let us know if anything comes up, k?

text.Futaba Sakura: A-OK!

text.Ann Takamaki: Then off we go! Look after Morgana for us.

text.Futaba Sakura: Have a nice trip!

text.ACTION: Part of the reason it was a good idea to go to Mementos today is that we had nothing to lose because our evening would be consumed anyway. I’m going to pretend I totally knew that before I decided to go and it wasn’t just a lucky coincidence.

text.Morgana: Everything’s fine. You don’t need to worry about me ...  You should just focus on your trip. It’s tomorrow, right ... ?

text.Newscaster: They’re called the Phantom Thieves, and they’re at the peak of their popularity. We’re going to try to find out who they are. This spring was when they made their first appearance.

text.Morgana: The peak of our popularity, huh? I guess we should be careful not to get too carried away.
Uh ...  Never mind. Have fun on your trip...

text.ACTION:
Part 104: 9/7-9/9: Aloha, Phantom Thieves
	Part 100: 9/7-9/9: Aloha, Phantom Thieves
100 updates everyone!  Time to celebrate with a Hawaiian vacation! I’m sure this will be vital to the plot and not a huge waste of everyone’s time, especially mine!

text.Joker: (nods)

text.Sojiro Sakura: I’ll look after Futaba and the cat while you’re gone. You owe me one.

text.ACTION: Oh, thank you so much for taking care of your own daughter in my absence, Sojiro. What would we ever do without you?

text.Morgana: Well someone’s excited for their vacation ...

text.Makoto Niijima: It’ll take over six hours to get there, so why not sleep on the plane?

text.Ann Takamaki: I’ll do that...

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s almost time to check in.

text.Ann Takamaki: Phew, looks like it’s gonna take off on time. I feel like a lot of flights headed to America tend to run late or get canceled ...  Is it just me or is Ryuji not here yet?
Coming late even on a day like this?

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s all you’re bringing?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s only four nights, right? Ain’t it enough?
See?

text.Makoto Niijima: I think that was sarcasm...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ooh, sounds good!

text.Ann Takamaki: Lemme join in too! You too, Makoto.

text.Makoto Niijima: All right.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: (rubbing eyes) Holy shit, she’s right...

text.Ann Takamaki: How could you tell, Futaba?

text.Futaba Sakura: You surprised? I snuck an app on Maaku’s phone. I can see all I want through his camera! You’re looking now, right Maaku? Mwehehe. You can’t underestimate the original Medjed.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Talk about a nasty trick ...

text.Makoto Niijima: I am so glad she’s not an enemy of ours.

text.ACTION: In that critical scene, we find out that Futaba is watching us during our every waking moment! Hi-larious!

text.Flight Attendant: Ladies and gentlemen, we have begun our initial descent into Hawaii. We ask that you return to your seats and ensure that your seatbelts are safely fastened.

text.Customs: How long will you be staying?

text.ACTION: So, in the original Japanese, Ryuji was speaking terrible, random English to this dude. I believe he says, “OKAY OKAY! I AM JAPANESE!” As can be seen here, the localization team didn’t even try to translate that joke.

Also worth noting- in the Japanese version, the Customs officer somehow has an even worse, less intelligible accent than Ryuji, because finding a native English speaker for his two lines would probably be a waste of time and money.

text.Ann Takamaki: Mmm, I love it! The tropical air ...

text.Guide: You can find your buses that way.

text.Ann Takamaki: (sigh)

text.ACTION: Ryuji is freaking the fuck out.
Wait a minute, in the lecture a few days ago the teacher said we’d land the morning of the 7th due to the time difference. What the fuck happened to that day? Did King Crimson attack?

(My guess is the game engine doesn’t let the devs go “backwards,” and since we already had a scene that took place on the evening of the 7th, we can’t have a scene following that taking place in the morning. That, or they just fucking forgot. One of those two)

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yes! We’re here! Hawaiiiiiiii!
Is this the smell of Hawaii? Actually, I’ve been wonderin’ since the airport, but what is this smell?

text.Yuuki Mishima: Supposedly the lingering scent of carpet cleaner. It’s coconut-scented. Plus, I’d say the scent of plumeria for the leis are amplifying the tropical atmosphere here.

text.ACTION: Why is Mishima even hanging out with us

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What are you, the king of random facts!?

text.Yuuki Mishima: I’m the type that likes to look up stuff beforehand.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then tell me a cheap but good place to eat.

text.Ann Takamaki: Do that after we’ve figured out room assignments. We can’t go out until we get our keys!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I wanna room with this guy.

text.ACTION: Mishima? Why? Oh, you mean me.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I can’t?

text.Makoto Niijima: It complicates roll call.

text.Ann Takamaki: Everyone butts you out, after all. I bet there aren’t many people who’d be OK rooming with you.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Shuddup, we both stick out like a sore thumb, you know.

text.ACTION: Oh hey, the second person out of two in the entire game who pronounces Ann’s last name the way a normal human being might.

text.Ann Takamaki: No, not yet.

text.Tall Student: In that case, how about rooming with me?

text.Hawaii Student 2: And if it’s OK with you, do you want to walk around together once we’re free to go about? We’ve never gone overseas before, so we thought it’d be reassuring if we had someone who knows English.

text.ACTION: They’re taking advantage of you, you idiot!

text.Ann Takamaki: Well, see you guys later.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Then, is it OK if I room with you?

text.ACTION: Too many people here to be mean… fuck.

text.Yuuki Mishima: It’s decided then.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Anyway, don’t do anything stupid, OK? This isn’t Japan, you know.

text.ACTION: Oh, I guess Ann just ditched those two girls she said she’d help, because we’re never going to hear from them again.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: There sure are a ton of people here. And ...  a lot of tall buildings, like hotels.

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s a little too clean here. It feels like an artificial resort.

text.Makoto Niijima: Still, look how clear the ocean is. The palm trees definitely give off a tropical vibe too.

text.ACTION: Makoto is the worst chaperone ever. She’s spending the entire trip hanging out with her friends.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I thought Ann was pretty impressive, but compared to the foreign ladies ...  eh.

text.Ann Takamaki: Then stop looking!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You think so too, don’t you? Like, these ladies are massive, unlike the girls in Japan!

text.ACTION: I’m struggling to find a way to interpret this other than “Ryuji likes them hefty,” unless he’s talking about cup sizes or something. Either way, TMI.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You like ‘em slim, huh?

text.Makoto Niijima: Moving on, take a look over there. Isn’t that Diamond Head?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But why’s it called that? Are diamonds a local product?

text.Ann Takamaki: Wouldn’t it say online?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, people long ago mistook volcanic rock for it? The eff?

text.Ann Takamaki: Might as well look up recommended places in Waikiki too. Oh right, I wanted to eat pancakes.

text.Makoto Niijima: I wonder if there are any online recommendations of scenic spots.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We should check for cheap and popular restaurants then.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Hey, we’re on our phones and chatting. This is no different from when we’re in Japan.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Even if we’re overseas, we can see all the news in Japan if we got our phones ...  It’s like ...  this ain’t what I was expectin’...

text.Ann Takamaki: We should do something that’s more Hawaii-like.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’s ...  Hawaii-like?

text.Ann Takamaki: Hula dancing ... ?

text.Yuuki Mishima: Oh, by the way, you know how the polls for the Phan-Site ranking’s started, right?

It’s been really lively, huh. I’m the one who made the website, but even I’m surprised. I can’t believe I’m part of such a huge thing! I’m so glad I’ve been rooting for the Phantom Thieves! On the contrary, did you hear about Akechi, that detective against the Thieves? The good-looking one. His popularity plummeted after Medjed was dealt with. Supposedly his official blog’s up in flames. He posed as some hero of justice, but that’s what he gets for not seeing eye to eye with them.
To be blunt, I can’t focus on this trip. I keep thinking about the Phantom Thieves. Don’t you think about them too?

text.ACTION: I don’t wanna talk about work shit here, Mishima.

text.Yuuki Mishima: ...You sure are calm. Something this amazing rarely happens, you know? But, then again, I think I’m feeling a bit tired too ...  Let’s go to bed. Good night.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I thought we were gonna be gettin’ alohas comin’ from all directions and stuff!

text.Ann Takamaki: It costs money to enjoy that atmosphere, you know. There’s not much we can do as students.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What’s with the low energy, Makoto?

text.Makoto Niijima: I just had to listen to the taxi driver complain for thirty minutes straight. I’m used to dealing with students’ troubles, but I never expected to have to do it overseas as well ...

text.Ann Takamaki: That must have sucked...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We should be doin’ some more excitin’ stuff! I mean, we’re in freakin’ Hawaii for god’s sake! Isn’t the school supposed to plan stuff? I wanna go divin’!

text.Makoto Niijima: It seems there wasn’t enough time to come up with any kind of coordinated travel plan.

text.ACTION: Okay, then what the fuck is the point of this trip, both in-universe and in terms of the game’s story? Hello? Why are we fucking around here?

text.Makoto Niijima: That lack of coordination is what led them to using students as chaperones as well.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: By the way, Maaku ...  you’re roomin’ with Mishima, right? How is it? Anythin’ interestin’?

text.Makoto Niijima: Really? Mishima-kun is the one who made the Phan-Site, correct?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Phan-Site ...  Y’know, I do hear people talkin’ about the Phantom Thieves every so often ...

text.Makoto Niijima: Are they really mentioning us ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I think so! We’ve already made our international debut! Man, just talkin’ about that makes me wanna go back to Japan so bad!

text.Ann Takamaki: You really have no chill.

text.Makoto Niijima: Come on, let’s try and forget about those things for now.

text.Ann Takamaki: What are you doing here!?

text.Makoto Niijima: Wasn’t your school supposed to be going to Los Angeles?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Apparently they couldn’t land the plane due to a terrible storm brewing on the west coast. There were no signs of it letting up, so our destination was changed on the spot to Hawaii.

text.ACTION: So, let me get this straight: That typhoon we saw on the news a few days ago hit the west coast of the US. That much I understand. But from there, Yusuke’s school trip, which was coincidentally on the exact same days and for the exact same duration as ours, instead of heading for a different airport on the west coast (or the plane just not leaving at all), decided to go to Hawaii? And they landed at the same airport on the same island, where they headed for the same hotel, where they inexplicably managed to find enough open rooms for another high school class in addition to the one that was already being served there. Is that about right?

I did some research just now and while it makes sense that pretty much any flight from Japan would land at Honolulu International Airport in Oahu (now Daniel K. Inouye International Airport, having changed its name in 2017, after this game likely takes place), which is fairly close to Waikiki, where we seem to be staying, that doesn’t explain the hotel issue at all. A cursory Google Maps search for hotels in the Waikiki neighborhood gives us this image:

Which, as you can see, means that there are several dozen options besides just wherever Shujin picked. I find it kind of unbelievable that Kosei could find enough rooms at any of these hotels for all of its second-years with no prior notice, even still. It is still summer, after all, even if only the tail end, and even if school is starting back up for most tourists. Hell, I have no idea how they even managed to afford all these rooms.
But Yusuke showing up out of nowhere’s pretty funny, I guess.

text.Makoto Niijima: Could it be that what happened at the fireworks festival was his fault as well ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: Don’t go bringing any storms here, you got that?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I’ll do my best.

text.Makoto Niijima: By the way, there’s nothing planned after this. What are you all going to do?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uh ...  Oh yeah, I still gotta buy souvenirs. My mom asked me to grab some stuff for her.

text.Ann Takamaki: I totally forgot about that! We need to pick things up for Futaba and Morgana too.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I was hoping to do some shopping myself.

text.Makoto Niijima: Then it’s settled. I wonder what Morgana would want ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Man, our group’s totally the same even outta Japan ...

text.ACTION: You’d think Yusuke’s school would be pretty cagey about him mingling with the students from another school considering there’s no travel itinerary for them at all.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yeah, it’s been gettin’ real popular in Japan lately. I guess they wanted to branch out.

text.Makoto Niijima: Now that you mention it, I read a news article recently about the success of Okumura Foods.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Ah yes, the company that owns Big Bang Burger.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Okumura ... ? Ain’t that the guy who’s at the top of the Phan-Site rankings?

text.Makoto Niijima: Is that true?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I guarantee it. I don’t make mistakes about that kinda stuff.
Do I hear sarcasm?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: (to Makoto)

text.Makoto Niijima: Oh, it’s probably nothing. Just a rumor I heard about Okumura Foods ...  Supposedly ...  all of their overseas competition has mysteriously pulled out. Never mind. I’m surely just overthinking things. Sis’ habits seem to be rubbing off on me.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, why don’t we take a pic together!? Y’know so we can remember the trip and all!

text.Ann Takamaki: Ooh, good idea!

text.Makoto Niijima: Are you sure you don’t want to be in it? Thanks.

text.Ann Takamaki: Can you not worry about that stuff for one second?
We still have some time to spare, right? Where to next?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: There’s a convenience store down by the beach. How ‘bout there?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That sounds lovely. I would quite like a short rest.

text.Makoto Niijima: All right, let’s head over there.

text.Ann Takamaki: You might be right ...  Oh, shoot! I forgot my sunscreen ...  I’m going to go buy another bottle at the convenience store.

text.Makoto Niijima: I’ll go with you.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I’m so bored ...  By the way, you think we’re the "thieves" everyone here’s been goin’ on about? It’d be pretty freakin’ crazy if that was true, huh?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm ...  I had not heard of such rumors. It sounds wonderful. We are already here, so why don’t we confirm if that is the case?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh! Good idea! Let’s try askin’ around while we wait for Ann and Makoto!

text.Cheerful Woman: You kids are from Japan, right? Are these Phantom Thieves special people like samurai or geisha?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm, I suppose that understanding isn’t necessarily incorrect for someone from a foreign country ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oooooh!

text.Easygoing Man: I read about them in a news article recently. What of it?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That’s actually all I wanted to know. Thanks.

text.Foreign Barker: It’s so awesome how they kick the bad guys’ asses! I wonder how they steal hearts ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...He actually seems to be quite knowledgeable.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Damn, it’s crazy how many people know about us! This is freakin’ awesome!
Hey, ain’t she kinda cute? Maybe we should ask her some questions too.

text.ACTION: Fun detail- the loading screen images for this part of the game have leis on.
Oh, hey. It’s Girl with Watering Can. Didn’t expect to see you again.

text.Girl With Watering Can: Free time is almost up. Shouldn’t you be heading back soon?
Oh, yes ...  By the way, your blond friend seemed very excited on the airplane coming here.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, you’re that girl we saw watering the plants!

text.Girl With Watering Can: Sorry to surprise you. I’m another third-year who was asked to come chaperone this trip. I accepted the task to take my mind off of things, but I wasn’t sure how to spend my free time ...

text.ACTION: Welp, guess we’ll never see her or her unique character model ever again.

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm, that girl you were talking to just now ...  Do you know her?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: No, that was my first interaction with her. She said she was a third-year. Same as you, Makoto.

text.ACTION: Uh, I don’t think you were the one she was asking, Yusuke.

text.Makoto Niijima: Mm-hm. I’ve never really spoken to her though. Ah, it looks like our free time is over. Let’s head back to the hotel.

text.Futaba Sakura: Found it! One after another too ...

text.Morgana: What did you find?

text.Futaba Sakura: Still working. Can’t tell you.

text.Morgana: She can handle this without me ...

text.Futaba Sakura: (to self)

text.Morgana: All I’m good for is driving them around in Mementos ...  I’m basically useless...

text.Futaba Sakura: Kitty! Your mumbling’s distracting me! If you got something to say, just spit it out.

text.Morgana: It’s nothing.
Lemme go!

text.Futaba Sakura: You feel so nice.

text.Morgana: I do not!

text.Futaba Sakura: So smooth and silky. It’s kinda hard to believe fur this soft belongs to a human.

text.Morgana: Don’t make me say it again! I’m a human ...

text.Futaba Sakura: Couldn’t you just be assuming that? I had the wrong assumptions about my mom for the longest time.

text.Morgana: That’s not the same! I understand myself better than anyone!

text.Futaba Sakura: That’s true.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Oh, wow! The president of a company called Okumura Foods is rising very quickly up the rankings!
Come on, you can’t let this chance pass you by! It’s rumored that Okumura Foods exploits their employees. Stuff like underpaying staff to reduce labor costs. That’s how they have so many stores...
Why are you here?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Just hear me out! The guy I’m roomin’ with went and brought his girlfriend back to the room! I felt totally awkward stayin’ in there with them. I’m just gonna sleep here tonight.

text.ACTION: It’s not going to be less awkward with Mishima around, dude.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Even though there are only two beds?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I know that feelin’!

text.ACTION: Oh, jeez. This place is filling up. I’m half-expecting Yusuke to arrive because he got expelled or something.
Also appreciate the implication that Ann’s roommate is the girlfriend of Ryuji’s roommate. I ship it.

text.Ann Takamaki: And she took the key! I stepped outside for just a second and the autolock kicked in! I can’t get back in my room!

text.ACTION: How did you think hotel rooms worked, Ann?

text.Yuuki Mishima: Ever since the Medjed case, many people from overseas have been accessing the website ...  Isn’t it crazy? The Phantom Thieves are finally making their worldwide debut ... ! What should I do about overseas requests?

text.Ann Takamaki: I don’t think we’re the ones you should ask about that ...

text.Yuuki Mishima: They took down Medjed. I wonder who they’ll bring justice to next. It’s not just Japan anymore. The whole world’s waiting to see the Phantom Thieves’ next move.

text.Ann Takamaki: That reminds me, what time is it?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: (yawn) So sleepy ...  I’m feelin’ pretty pooped. You think this could be that jet lag thing?

text.Ann Takamaki: It’ll be too much hassle for me to go anywhere else. I’ll just sleep in here tonight.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, what? I dunno if that’s a good idea.

text.Ann Takamaki: Don’t worry, I trust you guys.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I saw that one comin’...

text.Yuuki Mishima: There are only two beds ...  Even if someone sleeps on the sofa ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: One of us is gonna have to sleep on the floor ...

text.ACTION: Uh, you can’t see it from this angle but Mishima was just sitting in an armchair a few minutes ago. It’s just below the camera’s perspective. I’ve never been able to sleep sitting up but that doesn’t mean it isn’t more comfortable than the fucking floor.
But are we really so insecure we can’t even share the beds? It’s a California king full bed, I promise we won’t touch Ryujiiiiiii.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So who’s that gonna be?
Oh hey, playin’ cards. Why don’t we use these to decide?

text.ACTION: Goddammit, Mishim—wait, why the fuck didn’t Ann have to play!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, where’d Mishima go?

text.Ann Takamaki: He’s in the bathroom.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ain’t he been in there a while?

text.ACTION: If he’s not back in five minutes I’m stealing the other bed.

text.Ann Takamaki: The school trip ...  Shiho was really looking forward to this ...

text.ACTION: I believe this is the last time Shiho is ever mentioned outside of Ann’s Confidant and the only time it’s happened since Makoto joined. What a critical character that the game totally doesn’t just completely discard once she’s served her purpose.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ann ...

text.Ann Takamaki: ...Sorry. I didn’t mean to bring the mood down. But it’s already been almost six months since then, hasn’t it? This all feels so strange.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Right? Hard to believe the rowdy kids at school are now famous all over the world.

text.Ann Takamaki: Don’t you think we still have a lot to learn about each other though? Y’know, things like what kind of people we like ...  So, time to come clean, Ryuji.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Uhhh, well ...  She’s gotta have a good personality. I’m OK with anyone who’s modest and nice ...

text.Ann Takamaki: What about if two girls with equally good personalities confessed to you at the same time?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: If they’re equally nice? Then it’d hafta be the one with the hotter bod.

text.Ann Takamaki: So looks are what’s most important to you.
Your first answer was just superficial. The second answer was your true beliefs. Huh, so you really are that kind of guy ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That ain’t fair!

text.ACTION: It’s kind of a bullshit gotcha question, but to be fair, you walked straight into it, dude.

text.Ann Takamaki: What about you, Maaku? C’mon, spill the beans. What kind of girl is your type?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, are you talkin’ about her ... ?

text.ACTION: So, I picked the “mystery” option, thinking it was a joke, but no, Ryuji actually thinks I’m talking about a specific person here. I’m pretty sure I know who he’s referring to, but it’s weird that they’re even an option at this point. Picking one of the top two options results in the same answer, likely in reference to girls you can probably guess based on the answers themselves. If you pick the bottom answer Ryuji just gets mad at you for dodging the question. While I didn’t mean to voice preference for the character I picked here, I kept it in because it’s a really silly answer even if the game doesn’t seem to agree.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well, we answered honestly. It’s your turn next. So, what kinda guy do you--

text.ACTION: Uh-oh. Looks like Mishima’s having trouble in the bathroom.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So, what kinda guy do you--

text.Yuuki Mishima: M-My stomach ...  Hrgh ... !

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Y’know, wasn’t he drinkin’ the tap water earlier ... ? That’s like, the one thing you’re not supposed to do when you’re outta the country.

text.ACTION: First, I’m goddamn shocked that Ryuji knows anything about what you are and are not supposed to do when traveling. Second, I never realized it before but I guess this makes Mishima our very own Johnny Sasaki. Huh. It’s really rather fitting.

text.SIU Director: Though it was some third-rate tabloid’s article, unnecessary information was leaked, after all. Besides, his investigation of the Phantom Thieves showed no progress since then ...   ...  ... . Yes, there’s a possibility that he’ll betray us out of spite since he was let go. Well then, we’ll make it so that it was a "heart attack." As usual, he’ll be left to deal with the--  ...  ... . Oh? I wouldn’t have thought of that. Well played, sir. It no longer matters if we deal with one or two of those connected to us.

text.ACTION:
Part 105: 9/10-9/11: Exploiting The Morphogenetic Field To Pick Up Chicks
	Part 101: 9/10-9/11: Exploiting The Morphogenetic Field To Pick Up Chicks
So, it’s time for the second half of the Phantom Thieves’ Hawaiian adventure! I’m sure this part of the trip will absolutely justify the whole thing!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit, this isn’t how stuff was supposed to go!

text.Yuuki Mishima: What do you mean ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We ended up walkin’ around same as we always do in Japan ...  I mean we even ate at a freakin’ Big Bang Burger! It’s like we never left!

text.Yuuki Mishima: Whine all you’d like, but that’s what the trip was supposed to be.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But weren’t some other guys gettin’ all cozy with their girlfriends or some shit?

text.Yuuki Mishima: I think...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Then that’s it! That’s what this trip is missin’! C’mon, we totally gotta get movin’ during our free time in the afternoon.

text.Yuuki Mishima: What are we going to do?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Make a once-in-a-lifetime summer memory! Hawaii’s famous for its beaches, and y’know ...  what happens in Hawaii stays in Hawaii! We can get some girls’ numbers durin’ the day, then sneak away to ‘em at night! You in or what?

text.ACTION: I can see no flaws whatsoever with this plan.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Me too ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’ll be great! Neither of us have girlfriends who’d get mad at us about it either!

text.Yuuki Mishima: I guess that’s true, but ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oooh, you get a message? Who could that—Uhhh actually, you don’t gotta answer that. It might be something about you-know-what ...  C’mon Mishima, let’s go!

text.Yuuki Mishima: Wait, what just happened!? It’s only going to be the two of us, Sakamoto!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Don’t gimme that look! We’re goin’ to Waikiki! Try n’ get a little more excited!

text.Joker: I should check when there’s nobody else around ...

text.Makoto Niijima: I can finally take a break from my job too ...  If you don’t have any plans, would you like to take a walk with me?

text.Joker: Looks like I’ve received some messages.

text.ACTION: Oh yeah, I guess if Yusuke’s here that means Hifumi would be, too.

text.Hifumi Togo: My school is giving us some free time to do as we please. Care to walk along the beach? It might help with new moves.

text.Joker: Looks like I’ve received some messages.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait, don’t tell me ...  Was it a girl!? C’mon, you gotta make memories with us instead! We bombed it on that beach in Japan, after all!

text.Joker: This is my last moment of free time. Who should I spend it with ... ?

text.ACTION: So, we have three options here. We can go spend some time with Hifumi or Makoto, or we can go be losers with Ryuji and Mishima. Despite the fact that we have three choices in front of us, it’s possible to have up to five different options here. However, getting any messages beyond the ones we have now requires being in a relationship with the other two characters involved. We, obviously, are not dating anyone right now, so that’s unavailable. I won’t tell you who the other characters are, but if you think about what characters are present on this trip and who we haven’t gotten messages from, you can probably guess.
Anyway, we choose Hifumi. Why not, right? She’s cute.

text.Hifumi Togo: OK, I’ll be waiting ...  in my swimsuit.

text.Joker: We’re meeting at the beach. I should hurry and change into my swimsuit...
It seems like Hifumi has been waiting for me here...

text.Hifumi Togo: Um ...  Do I look strange in this? Perhaps I should go change ...
...Oh, thank you very much. Um ...  ...Shall we take a walk?
Looks like they sell shrimp ...  Shrimp are symbolic of living a long life. Shall we have some?
...Yes.

text.Shrimp Stand Owner: How ‘bout them Phantom Thieves, huh? The guys that steal hearts!
Heard about it on the news! They’re all the rage in Japan, yeah? Say, if y’run into ‘em, tell ‘em I say hello. And ask ‘em to change people’s hearts so everyone loves shrimp!

text.Hifumi Togo: S-Sure ...
Oh, they’re quite ...  pungent.

text.Joker: We gazed out over the ocean while we enjoyed the delicate flavors of a foreign country ...

text.Hifumi Togo: This is a refreshing break from staring at a shogi board all day long. ...I feel as if I’ll be able to come up with some great new moves once I return home.
We would’ve had a more enjoyable time if I had made better conversation ...
Um ...  this is for you ...  I would be delighted if you remembered this day ...

text.Joker: It looks like a turtle ...  Something about the transparent stone reminds me of Hifumi ...

text.ACTION: The Honu Charm is an accessory only equippable by Maaku that gives +5 Endurance and +5 Luck.

text.Hifumi Togo: If only we went to the same school ...
I’d like that. ...Sun is about to set. We should start heading back ...

text.ACTION: The scene where the group talks about Big Bang Burger’s… err… explosion into the restaurant world and their parent company Okumura Foods is the sole sequence in the entirety of the Hawaii trip with any direct narrative purpose, and it’s just to set up this conversation. Don’t get me wrong, I’m not opposed to the idea of some totally inessential downtime for the group. It’s not that the game couldn’t use some fluff where the group just hangs out and relaxes; god knows there was plenty of that in Persona 4. But the Hawaii trip comes at a particularly inopportune time in regards to the story’s flow and pacing, feels pretty redundant after the earlier beach visit, and tragically just isn’t that fucking interesting at all. Persona 5 is a game that simultaneously feels loose as hell pacing-wise and way too rigid and tight for its own good, because while it has a lot of extraneous scenes, most of them are still plot-related and only exist because the game needed a better editor, meaning the game feels really overstuffed and none of the characters have a chance to fucking breathe. Most of the “gang hanging out” scenes have been unfortunately relegated to the text conversations because there’s legitimately just no space left on the game’s calendar for most of it. Hell, that more than a few plot-critical conversations happen via text message says a lot about how this game is structured.
But that’s enough of that rant.

text.ACTION: It’s really weird to me that for this dialogue option there’s no "serious" option. Both of them make you seem like a huge dumbass for not realizing what’s happening immediately. The reason it comes off so strangely is that Japan has a very real phenomenon of "occupational sudden mortality" or "overwork death," also known as karōshi. Now, most of the time this is due to heart attack, but a lot of cases are just straight-up suicides, which is unfortunately not terribly surprising considering Japan’s high suicide rate. It’s also a widespread problem in South Korea and China, which probably won’t surprise you. From the Wikipedia page on the subject, one of the four "typical" cases of karōshi according to the International Labour Organization includes a nurse who died at the age of twenty-two after being forced to work thirty-four continuous hours ...  five times a month. It’s fucked up.

It’s also worth noting that due to government "encouragement" (read: they’re barely doing shit) for companies to limit the amount of hours an employee is "allowed" to work per week in response to some of these deaths, a lot of these hours are classified as unpaid (and often unrecorded) overtime, which companies have gone even further to limit by placing a monthly cap on overtime hours. However, due to incredibly stringent quotas and overbearing workloads, even employees who work at some of these companies can’t afford to take advantage of this and end up working at home or secretly staying at the office with the lights turned off, known as "cloaked overtime." In 2007, Mitsubishi (a banking corporation, not the car manufacturer) instituted a policy allowing employees to go home up to three hours early to care for their families, and two years later only thirty-four out of seven thousand workers had taken advantage of this. And all this isn’t even getting into the societal expectation that salarymen go out drinking with their coworkers constantly. Yeah, that’s a real thing, anime didn’t make that up.

Also I thought it was a little weird that these overwork claims were being pointed at a food service company, as the immediate thought when they’re brought up is not "salarymen," but sure enough, according to this Daily Beast article, one of the worst companies in the country, as selected by a group of journalist and labor activists for their prestigious "Most Evil Corporation of The Year Award" is Mister Donut (they didn’t actually win that award to my knowledge, but the article mentions them as a serious contender).

So, when I say, “maybe there should be a serious option here,” it’s in full acknowledgment of just how pervasive and toxic overwork is in Japanese society. But, uh, maybe the video game industry isn’t really in a position to be throwing stones there, so I guess I understand. All this makes for a rather morbid and serious last four paragraphs, though, so here’s an adorable dog dressed as a police officer!

text.Makoto Niijima: The only daughter of Kunikazu Okumura, CEO of Okumura Foods. Care to explain why you were inside your father’s Palace?

text.ACTION: Wow, you’re remarkably chill about this.

text.Haru Okumura: You looked really good in that biker gang outfit!

text.ACTION: Makoto looks around for eavesdroppers before continuing.

text.Makoto Niijima: So why did you become a phantom thief?

text.Haru Okumura: Things have grown quite serious lately ...  That’s why I want to make amends, even though it may only be for my own satisfaction. But I wonder if this is just running from the problem...

text.Makoto Niijima: Where did you meet Morgana?

text.Haru Okumura: It was pure coincidence. I found a lonely-looking cat in front of our office building.

text.Makoto Niijima: And that was Morgana?

text.Haru Okumura: Mm-hm. And when I followed him, I ended up in the Metaverse ...

text.ACTION: So let me get this straight: After leaving the group in a huff, Morgana walked all the way to the Okumura Foods corporate headquarters in Roppongi. Not only did he somehow know exactly where this building was, he managed to get on and off the subway multiple times to get there. Then, by sheer magical fucking coincidence, he happens to run into Haru, Okumura’s daughter and the only person who can get past the door in his Palace, who decides to follow him for pretty much no reason. Then, he enters the Palace, pulling Haru in with him, despite the fact that however the hell he manages to switch between the real world and the Metaverse without using the app, it has never been established that he can bring other people with him.

text.Haru Okumura: There’s no way for me to change my father’s company ...  But if I became a phantom thief, I thought I’d at least be able to change him...

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Isn’t there any way we can work together?

text.Haru Okumura: What you’re doing is unnecessarily causing a stir among the public. Besides, the Phantom Thieves, who should be helping the weak, are not helping their own teammate.

text.ACTION: In our defense, he’s kind of an asshole.

Maaku and Makoto share a glance. Also, where the hell are Ann and Ryuji? If they already left then they probably would have also seen Haru before I did, and if they’re still inside they’re taking forever.

text.Haru Okumura: And help Mona-chan, who gave me a chance to do just that.

text.Makoto Niijima: But aren’t our objectives the same? It’d be better if we work--

text.ACTION: Maaku and Makoto look at each other… again. This game has a lot of really weirdly directed scenes.

text.Makoto Niijima: It seems getting her cooperation won’t be possible. Let’s consult with the others on our next move. We shouldn’t ignore Morgana either.

text.ACTION: Gah! Sweet merciful Shylock! That fucking nose, dude! Should I… should I be showing this? Is this a hate crime? Man, this is unfortunate!

Okay, yeah, I know this isn’t actually a Jewish thing, there’s no possible way it was intentional. But come on Soejima, this is just over-the-top. He looks like Robert De Niro in Raging Bull dressed up as Vincent Vega. He looks like Bucky Barnes, the suspicious new guardian of the Baudelaire orphans. Fuck it, he looks like Steve Carell in Foxcatcher trying to impersonate me, awful hair included.
Also I looked up this dude’s VA because I didn’t recognize it and he’s done some notable stuff, like Kittan from Gurren Lagann, but most importantly, he’s motherfucking Spandam from One Piece.

You know, that dude whose entire character design was Mankind but a total wimp and with the serial numbers filed off? This isn’t important or relevant in any way, it’s just all I can fucking hear now! This has been this update's installment of useless voice actor trivia only I care about!

text.Haru Okumura: No, not at all ...  Um, what’s this about Phantom Thieves?

text.Kunikazu Okumura: It’s jealousy of the successful. Nothing but the barks of the masses who lack the resolve to sacrifice what’s needed for their well-being. Both the young and the old are overjoyed with some foolish idols. This country has no future.

text.ACTION: Okay, wow, this is certainly some dialogue.
Hashino-san, please let me go home, I need to see my family.
Not until you finish writing the rest of Okumura’s lines.

Oh god, this character is such a flat boring caricature, what the hell am I gonna do? Well, maybe if I half-ass it he’ll just fire me. (bangs out the rest in two minutes) I’m done, sir. It’s not terribly subtle, but--

text.Kunikazu Okumura: Are you still having doubts about me?

text.Haru Okumura: No ...

text.Kunikazu Okumura: More importantly, I hope things are going well with that young man.
He may not seem like it, but he’s still the son of an influential politician. Be cordial with him. He’ll eventually become a necessary connection for this company—or rather, for me.

text.Haru Okumura: I understand ...  I will do the best I can.

text.Kunikazu Okumura: Good. That’s how a daughter of Okumura should be.

text.ACTION: Remember how one scene ago I said this game’s cutscenes were weirdly directed? Well, in this scene Okumura sits down, crosses and uncrosses his legs multiple times, and then stands back up. It doesn’t really convey anything at all and kind of just seems like they thought the scene was too “static” so they had him move around pointlessly.

Alternatively, it’s actually a really accurate and understated portrayal of ADHD, and I’m going to say it was absolutely intentional. Thank you, Katsura Hashino, for being such an understanding and empathetic artist.
You’re welcome. Also, the gays are hilarious.

text.Whisper: Why are the Phantom Thieves letting him go free?

text.Chatter: What’s the point of that poll!? Hurry up and take him out already!

text.Whisper: I’m disappointed. What kind of heroes are they?

text.Murmur: Just hurry up and send a calling card already.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s prolly just a prank.

text.Futaba Sakura: Agreed. He’s probably taking the Beauty Thief with him too.

text.ACTION: Wait, how is that possible? We confronted her today, and then we went home. How could she avoid you at school if she only met you at the end of the current school day? What the hell?

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m not sure how I feel about you saying that. I mean, we’re the Phantom Thieves ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The method is indeed a classic one, but it is a safe bet.

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah, I think it’s better than just looking for them randomly.

text.Futaba Sakura: I’m gonna have all sorts of snacks! No teachers to stop me on this field trip!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Welp, why don’t we get this over with?

text.Makoto Niijima: Let’s do it tomorrow.

text.Newscaster: Former Okumura Foods employees have begun raising their voices in protest. Their complaints include unpaid overtime and health problems caused by overwork. Some protestors started to get violent outside their headquarters in a fierce dispute with police. It’s highly suspected that this protest is related to the window vandalism incident a few days ago.

text.Joker: It sounds like a lot of people are protesting Okumura Foods.

text.ACTION: Wait, so did Morgana not vandalize the windows? But the vandalism was the entire reason we went to Okumura’s Palace! He was just there by coincidence? That’s bad writing!
Wait, shit, I think there’s a plot hole here ...  Hmm ...  Fuck it, I’ll just do some more coke.

Part 108: 9/17-9/18: Animal Cruelty
	Part 104: 9/17-9/18: Animal Cruelty

When we left off, we had discovered that someone was cavorting around Mementos filling requests all willy-nilly. It’s probably Morgana and Haru, who we need because Haru is the only person who can get us further in Okumura’s Palace Morgana is our friend, I guess.

text.Boy 10: I mean, there are tons of other companies that do the same thing.

text.Dissatisfied First-Year: Maybe they’re singling him out for all of the praise he gets? Besides, there are a bunch of strange rumors starting to surface about his company ...

text.Boy 10: Oh, you mean like all that stuff happening to his competitors? Don’t tell me you buy that occult BS. I’m sure it’s a coincidence.

text.ACTION: believes in phantom thieves but not mental breakdowns. For more information, watch his YouTube channel where he roleplays a statue of some really old Greek dude to find out why the Phantom Thieves are the best and why eating tuna will turn you into a gay feminist dolphin or some shit!

text.Chouno: Come on, you’re young! Hawaii doesn’t even count as going to a foreign country. It’s full of Japanese tourists. I bet you were able to speak Japanese wherever you went, weren’t you? The shopkeepers will use Japanese to pressure you into buying things as if their life depended on it. I’m used to it though, so I actually haggle with them in English. Mr. Hamiru! Show me how much your English has improved. We have a saying in Japanese: a skilled hawk hides its talons. What hides its claws in English?

text.ACTION: Oh. That’s just way too easy. Worth noting- 99% of people got this one right, but like one dude actually picked “pig,” it seems.

text.Chouno: Very good! "Cats hide their claws" is the saying. Are you hiding some claws of your own? There are actually a lot of other expressions involving cats.

text.Joker: I feel like I got a little smarter from being able to answer that question ...

text.Chouno: "A cat has nine lives" for instance.

text.ACTION: Oh, Morgana better have nine lives after all this bullshit.

text.Chouno: It means that cats are so resilient that they wouldn’t die even if you killed them.

text.ACTION: That’s absurd. I dunno about cats, but people die when they’re killed.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I mean, duh. He was doing tons of shady shit.
Hell yeah!

text.Makoto Niijima: That aside, does everyone remember the plan for today?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: I’m sure they’ll come.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I hope you’re right ...
I know already! And why’re you just sayin’ that to me!?

text.Makoto Niijima: We need to be wary of the Beauty Thief too.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So we’re doing a stakeout here.

text.Futaba Sakura: We better be ready for the long haul!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hold that thought.

It’d be best if you don’t accept them so recklessly.

text.ACTION: Uh, we never really acted with all that much care ourselves in regards to what requests we took on. We’re still going after a fucking arcade cheater, guys.
Also Yusuke’s second sentence here is just remarkably callous. Chill out, dude.

text.Haru Okumura: That’s not what I intended ... ! But ...  that would be my fault ...

text.Morgana: Why’re you apologizing!?

text.Ann Takamaki: Ryuji!
We’re sorry too, Morgana. We weren’t taking your feelings into consideration at all.

text.Morgana: Lady Ann...

text.Ann Takamaki: Ryuji didn’t really mean what he said, you know? He wants to apologize...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Well, it’s like ...  It was my bad too ...

text.ACTION: What the hell is wrong with you dude
Sometimes this game just says exactly what I’m thinking, and it rules.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Ann’s setup was completely ruined.

text.Morgana: Oh, is that right!? So I AM just some useless cat to you guys!

text.ACTION: Now, hold on, just because Ryuji is a total idiot doesn’t mean that’s what we think! It’s what I think, but I’m not an actual character in this narrative, so that’s irrelevant!

text.Morgana: You’re so full of yourselves, but do you have the skills to back that up!?
Try and catch me then! Get in, Beauty Thief!
If you can’t do this, don’t count on me ever coming back!

text.Futaba Sakura: There they go ...

text.Makoto Niijima: Geez! This isn’t what we came here to do!
We need to go after him and talk things through.

Morgana takes off down the right tunnel.

When we inevitably reconcile, I’m not letting this fucking cat spend all day in my bag and make it smell like turds.

text.Makoto Niijima: Stop complaining and let’s get after him again!

text.Ann Takamaki: Mona! Will you listen!?

...Or it’s funny, I guess? That our “friend” just got into a “car” accident?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dammit! Freakin’ Morgana!

text.Haru Okumura: Are you sure that was what you wanted ... ?

text.Morgana: ...Of course it was!

text.Haru Okumura: I would never do such a thing ... !

text.Morgana: Haru!
(nyeeh)
Dammit ...  I really am ...  useless at this rate ...  Someone ...  Anyone ...  Is anybody out there ... !?

text.Sugimura: Will you shut up, you stupid cat!?

Seems like he’s already getting it wakka wakka

Oh god, it’s Mitsuru all over again. I assume Haru at least knows how to eat a fucking hamburger though, so that’s one point for her.

Mona-chan ... ?

You love being here, don’t you?
I was lying to myself too, but when I formed a contract with my Persona ...  I understood it all.

text.ACTION: Maybe don’t step all over Haru’s moment, Ann. Geez.

text.Haru Okumura: I thought that since an adult with responsibilities made the decision, it couldn’t be wrong. I was such a fool, tied down by vague notions and stayed quiet as my marriage partner was chosen ...

text.ACTION: Oh man, that’s certainly some grammar there.

text.Haru Okumura: But I won’t tolerate this anymore.
Phew ...  That’s how I truly feel.

text.Morgana: Wh-Why’re you looking at me all of a sudden?

text.Ann Takamaki: Morgana ...

text.Morgana: ...I wanted a reason of my own—a reason to stay with the Phantom Thieves. I don’t have anyone I want to save or get revenge on. Someone like me has no reason to stay here ...  That’s why ...  to me ...  this team is ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Come on, say it! You can do it!

text.ACTION: Ann’s just killing every moment she can tonight, huh?

They're bringing it back! Anyway, that's all. Thank you for understanding.

I’ll make sure to work hard to pay my dues. It’s too late to cancel our deal, got it?
We’re re-forming our give-and-take deal.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Morgana is growing deeper...

text.ACTION: Endure will let each party member with the appropriate Confidant Rank withstand one otherwise-fatal attack per battle. It’s pretty fucking vital for the endgame, and we’ll want it on all our characters we plan on using heavily. We’re not quite into “mandatory” territory yet, though, which is good because most of our party’s currently hovering between Rank 5 and Rank 7.

text.ACTION: No idea what the fuck this means, but okay.

text.Futaba Sakura: Hm?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oh crap! The last train’s comin’ up!

text.Makoto Niijima: Let’s continue this another time.

text.Futaba Sakura: Stay at our place. I’ll arrange it.

text.Morgana: Man. This place is as drab as always ...

text.ACTION: Glad to see you’re happy. We spent five days worried about you, and then you just turn up, almost kill us via hit-and-run, and then come crawling back after being emasculated, even though it turns out the entire reason you left was to prove your worth to us, which ended up being wholly at odds with nearly every single one of your words and actions in the interim? Like, we thought you were just mad for poorly-defined reasons in relation to us not going after Okumura immediately, but then it seemed like you were just mad because Ryuji was mean to you (which was pretty damn hypocritical, I might add), and then it turns out you were just harboring a massive inferiority complex and wanted to be accepted even though we spent several days explicitly chasing after you? I don’t really understand the logic here. Furthermore, you only came back once it was proved thoroughly that you couldn’t hack it by yourself, which is weird because none of the underlying issues behind your initial leaving of the team have been addressed. Or wait, maybe they have been, because there actually weren’t any. It’s confusing. Also, again, you tried to kill us, dude. Not cool.

text.Morgana: It might not be easy for her to relax right now, but I hope this’ll at least help her cheer up a bit.

text.Morgana: All those employees have definitely been suffering. They must be at the end of their wits.

text.ACTION: Not how anyone has ever phrased that, Morgana.

text.Joker: My body feels like a boulder slowly sinking into quicksand...

text.ACTION: Aww, I guess I did kinda miss this dumb cat.

(to Haru)
