text.Haru Okumura: Of course. I should be the one cordially asking to be allowed on the team.

text.Morgana: From here on, we may be going up against the culprit behind those mental shutdown occurrences. This’ll be different from our training in Mementos. You better brace yourselves.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You’re suddenly lecturin’ us?

text.Morgana: You’re too naive! Haru’s barely a hair better than an amateur.

text.ACTION: Oh, I see. So she got one of the shitty formless Patronuses, like all the lame D-tier members of the DA no one ever cared about. That’s rough, girl.

text.Futaba Sakura: Weak? Really?

text.Morgana: She can transform at the very least, but to be frank, she may slow us down. A lot.

text.Haru Okumura: I’m sorry for causing such trouble ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Nah, don’t worry about it. It’s actually convenient for us to target that CEO.

text.Makoto Niijima: There’s a lot of negative comments in regard to the Phantom Thieves. "The names of obvious criminals have come up, so why haven’t the Phantom Thieves acted yet!?"

text.Futaba Sakura: The way they’re getting heated is on a different level.

text.Morgana: Don’t forget about the intel on the mental shutdown cases, all right?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Of course! We’ll get ‘em both!

text.Morgana: October ...  uhh, 10th, was it? We’re gonna change Okumura’s heart by then!
As Phantom Thieves, it’s our duty to punish him!

text.Newscaster: The company has remained silent in response to questions from the media. Intense questioning from the media will likely continue until they get a satisfactory explanation.

text.Morgana: We need to do something before Haru gets wrapped up in all this.
Oh, and you didn’t get all rusty while I was gone, did you?

text.ACTION:
Part 109: 9/19: Get Smoked
	Part 105: 9/19: Get Smoked

text.Morgana: If Haru’s sold off, our failure will sully the Phantom Thieves name.

text.ACTION: “Sold off”? That’s a really weird way of phrasing that, man.

All right! New mission! Time to fuck around, ignore every single one of our friends and responsibilities, talk to every NPC in the game again, and blitz through the Palace in a single day, putting tremendous strain on myself as well as you, the viewing audience!

text.Elderly Male Customer: It’s the government’s fault. Why do they pick on people on the National Pension like us? Young people are pathetic, too. They’re so quick to complain and claim they’re getting exploited.

text.ACTION: Surely this can’t be because they’re actually getting exploited, you fucking raisin? No, it must be those whiny children who are wrong.

text.Kind Old Woman: You think so? I think they work just as hard as we did, don’t they?

text.Sad Old Man: No! They’re weak, I’m telling you!

text.ACTION: Not quite sure what that was about...

text.Boom Box: We’ve been gathering stories about the corrupt bosses that people have worked for. We’ve gotten tons of responses so far. People have been sending stories of such terrible things ...

text.Old Man 3: They’re blowing things out of proportion. Young people today are just too soft.

text.ACTION: Kill all the old people, it’s the only way to be sure.

One thing we’re going to try to do at least a few times for the rest of the game is buy more materials and transmutable weapons wherever and whenever we can. I have no idea if I’ll end up using any of this, but it’s worth a shot.
Oh no! The dog is sick!
Also, I guess we really are using the “sold off” terminology. That’s pretty uncomfortable, not gonna lie.

text.Dog loving Girl: Huh? Kotaro seems kinda tired though ...

text.Mother: This summer was really hot, so he’s a little worn out ...  Let’s leave the bad guys to the Phantom Thieves and let him rest.

text.Aggressive Reporter: Stirring up the popularity of the Phantom Thieves was a success. Now we’ll focus on Okumura Foods!

text.Young Cameraman: We shouldn’t go too far ...  Okumura’s a major sponsor of ours, you know.

text.Aggressive Reporter: I told you, don’t get cold feet! Our viewers can’t get enough of the Phantom Thieves’ craze! We’ll get to bash both the police and the politicians. It’ll be double the fun. (snicker)

text.Protesting Man: That is the fate of an economic supremacist, contaminated by the surge of darkness!

text.Clear-Eyed Man: Stand up, Phantom Thieves! Apostles of the Sun! Go and fulfill the will of the Sun God!

text.Protesting Man: Please remember this: The Phantom Thieves only exist thanks to the Sun God!

text.Young-Looking Woman: Thinking about what happened with Okumura Foods made me realize that ...

text.Middle-Aged Woman: I’m not sure that’s a good comparison ...  Anyway, how old did you tell your boyfriend you were?

text.Young-Looking Woman: ...I told him I was 15 years younger than I really am.

text.ACTION: Okay, I don’t mean to alarm anyone, but between her description as “Young-looking Woman,” her previous obsession with Akechi, and her rather extreme predilection for dating men massively younger than her, I think this woman might be an actual pedophile.
Kishi? That dude we did a change of heart for like two weeks ago?

text.Shinsuke Kishi: Knock it out of the park and the drinks are on me! Just be ready for an all-night rager!

text.Miserable Office Worker: No, no, nooo—I can’t. My wife would kill me.

text.Morgana: Looks like the change of heart worked.

text.Arrogant Housewife: It’s all lies! Everyone’s out to get Okumura Foods because they’re jealous of its success!

text.Modest Housewife: Are you sure? My husband, he never receives any overtime pay, so ...  I wonder if they’ll pin this on the CEO. He should probably just admit the truth. Ohoho ...

text.Novice Pick-Up Artist: The girls love lines like that. It’s all thanks to the Phantom Thieves!

text.Veteran Pick-Up Artist: Hoho, you’re starting to get the hang of it. Hit a homerun with that Love Thief line, did you?

text.Novice Pick-Up Artist: Actually, the "Love Thief" line didn’t work out so well. I always hear it’s lame and hard to get...

text.Fishy Hawker: Oh, got you interested, huh? Well, if that’s the case, you ought to see our new product!
Don’t be so full of yourself, kid. I’m no Phantom Thief, but I can make you beg for forgiveness, too.

text.Serious-looking Lawyer: Who knows? It’s not as flashy a target as Medjed though. Companies all over the country exploit their workers. Will taking down one of them change anything?

text.Sharp Lawyer: I’m sure it will affect public opinion. I guess we’ll sit back and watch what they do.

text.Beautiful Maid: Ugh, don’t tell me what to do, you annoying jerk.

text.Fast-Talking Man: Whoa, it’s true! She’s a real-life tsundere maid! Yeah, harsh on the outside, and shy on the inside.

text.ACTION: In case you’ve never watched a bad anime and thus don’t know what “tsundere” means, it’s basically what this dude just described, summed up in the oft-used phrase, “it’s not like I like you or anything.”

text.Beautiful Maid: Gross ...  Gross, gross gross! Don’t come near me!

text.Skinny Man: Must be a leak from the opposition party. I read about that on a news blog.
See for yourself. Just search for "Okumura Foods" in the archives and you’ll find a lot of articles.

text.Busy Young Man: Don’t worry! I cut my losses! If I want to rule the market, I should know when to back out! I’m gonna live as a trader. No, I was born to be a trader!

text.Fiancee of Busy Young Man: Huh? Wait, what about your job?

text.Busy Young Man: Didn’t I tell you? I quit! We’ll rrrevolutionize ourselves and live like celebrities!

text.ACTION: This game has so many pure, wonderful idiots.
But now, the real reason we came to the arcade.

text.Arcade Spectator: Oh, I’ve heard about him. He’s just a little guy, huh? Must still be in grade school ...  He’s dual-wielding ... ?

text.ACTION: *ahem* Sorry, I’m terminally incapable of hearing the words “dual-wielding” and not freaking out after the copious amounts of SAO I’ve consumed.

text.Loud Spectator: Yeah, he’s playing two opponents all by himself. And it’s still too easy for him.

text.Joker: The King may have some tips on how to defeat the cheater. I should negotiate with him...

text.Shinya Oda: Don’t take it personal; I turn everyone down. ...Later.
Annoying, huh ... ? Oh, you mean that guy who cheats. It really makes me mad when he does that ...  But I can still beat him, so I don’t really care. Just forget about him.
So, you’re saying you wanna beat the cheater? You seem like a nice guy ...  but just let it go. The Phantom Thieves are really cool, aren’t they!? Are you a fan, too? Have you ever met them?

text.ACTION: Oh god, I just noticed that his jacket says “NOOB” in addition to the “GET SMOKED” cap, this is amazing.

text.Shinya Oda: But, um ...  Teaching you how to play Gun About won’t be easy ...  And I won’t get anything out of it ...
Geez, you’re really persistent. I’m just a grade schooler, y’know. How about this ...  I wanna get to know the Phantom Thieves.
...It’s probably impossible, but if you can help me do that, then I’ll teach you how to play. Well, whaddaya say? Is it a deal?

text.ACTION: It’s a big ask, kid, but I like your moxie. Let’s do this!

text.Shinya Oda: ...Wait, what? You’re not gonna say no!? Well, if you really want to THAT much, then ...  I thought for sure you were gonna give up ...  Wow, I didn’t see this coming. But the Phantom Thieves hide their true identities, right? Are you sure I can get to know them?

Huh? You’re gonna tell them my name?  ...  ...  My name’s Shinya Oda. Tell the Phantom Thieves my name, and have them post it somewhere only they’d be able to access. That’ll be good enough as an autograph, and proof that they know my name.

text.Morgana: We need something credible for this kid to believe us. Didn’t Futaba say she hacked into Gun About’s server or something? Let’s bring this up with her. Might lead us to some good ideas.

text.ACTION: Futaba isn’t actually available to hang out today, but “activating” this stage of the Shinya sidequest “summoned” her. However, we still can’t hang out with her, because the game will make us go back to Shinya instead once we’re done here.

text.Futaba Sakura: So, did he tell you how to take down that cheater?

text.Morgana: He’s going to, on one condition: he wants us to introduce him to the Phantom Thieves. We can’t just give ourselves away though. That’s where you come in. Maybe you could hack into the Gun About server and do something?

text.Futaba Sakura: But we won’t be able to get in touch with him that way ...

text.Morgana: A calling card ... ? What are we going to steal?

text.Futaba Sakura: Oh, how about the home page? I already hacked into it, so it’s as good as stolen!

text.ACTION: After you already used the home page once to send a message to that cheater, you’d think they’d have closed that glaring vulnerability.

text.Morgana: Hm, OK. I’ll write a calling card saying that we’re going to steal the Gun About home page. After that, you’ll need to leave evidence that the Phantom Thieves hacked into it. The King will have no choice but to believe it was really us.

text.Futaba Sakura: Oooh, this sounds like fun. I’ll put our logo smack dab at the top of the front page.

text.Morgana: Perfect. We’ll go see the King. Oh, and we’ll let you know before we talk to him, so wait for our word to start the hacking.

text.Futaba Sakura: All right, you can count on me.

text.Morgana: Should we ask Futaba about the hacking?

text.Futaba Sakura: It’ll be fine! Leave it to me! OK, I’m hacking in now.

text.ACTION: So, uh… Shinya. Oh sweet, innocent Shinya.

So, Shinya is voiced by Barbara Goodson, probably best known as Laharl from Disgaea (and fucking Rita Repulsa, how could I possibly forget) ...  and it’s really just a hell of a performance. Here’s the entire event, just so you can hear it, but ...  click wisely.

text.Shinya Oda: Huh? HUH? There’s something written on it ...  "Thanks for your support. Please help those in need. This is a promise to you from the Phantom Thieves: We’re going to post a secret message, just for you, on the game’s official website."  ...  ...  Is ...  Is this for real? I mean, you can probably just buy one of these cards at the store ...

text.ACTION: “You were gone for like an hour, dude. I may be twelve but I’m not fuckin’ stupid.”

text.Shinya Oda: Just like they did on Medjed’s site! Which means ...  you were able to contact the real Phantom Thieves! No way! How’d you do it?

That’s so cool ...  So they want to remain anonymous ...  Wow, I can’t believe they sent me a message ...  I wasn’t expecting much from you, Hamiru-san, but you’re actually pretty cool. I wish I was able to talk with them—or something—though ...  But you fulfilled your part of the deal, so I’ll teach you how to shoot.
You should be able to inflict a lot of damage to the cheater this way. ...Let’s get started.
...C’mon, you gotta aim.
...No, no, no. You’re just stopping their movement by doing that.
Are you taking this seriously!? You gotta focus on your second shot!

text.Joker: He’s almost like a different person when he gets mad. His instructions are precise, but also spartan-like...

text.Loud Spectator: That’s what happens when he teams up with another player. And why everyone also watches him from a distance ...

text.ACTION: The second line there is delivered really strangely. The actor was clearly going for “sardonic” but it comes out as “rushed to meet non-existent lip flaps.”

text.Shinya Oda: I think you’ll be able to beat that cheater now.
Sorry ...

text.ACTION: Do you? Because it didn’t happen today!

text.Shinya Oda: But I think you have a lot of potential. More than most people! If you want ...  I can teach you a few other moves too! I have the ultimate trump card. So tell me more about the Phantom Thieves!

text.ACTION: What’s this kid gonna want in return though? Are we gonna have to show up in-costume to Shinya’s birthday party?

text.Joker: I’ve made a deal with Shinya...

text.Sae Niijima: Either you taught yourself ...  or you had a capable coach by your side ...  Where did you learn how to handle a gun!?

text.ACTION: “I learned it from a child who’s really good at a video game. What’s that look for? I’m telling the truth, cop.”
Yeeeeep, forming a Confidant with this young child, what of it

So, Tower is an interesting arcana, symbolizing destruction, revelation, and sudden change. When reversed, it represents avoidance of disaster and fear of change. It’s probably the most universally “negative” card in the deck.

Down Shot lets us spend all the ammunition in our clip to down a single enemy. This is pretty much only worth it on Treasure Demons and enemies without weaknesses due to the exorbitant ammunition cost, but it’s still handy occasionally. It should also go without saying that it’s fucking worthless on bosses, just like every other interesting part of combat in this game.

text.Shinya Oda: I gotta go. See ya later!

text.Joker: Interacting with Shinya has made my heart grow ...  I feel like my Kindness has increased...

text.Haru Okumura: I truly apologize for what has happened in this case.

text.Futaba Sakura: So formal!

text.Haru Okumura: But I’m the newest member. I need to act respectfully.

text.Makoto Niijima: We don’t really pay mind to those kinds of things. Furthermore, you’re already one of us.

text.Haru Okumura: Thank you, Mako-chan.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Do you mean me?

text.Haru Okumura: Sorry, I think my fingers typed that subconsciously ...  I’m just so glad to have found a friend my age.

text.Makoto Niijima: Not a problem. That personal touch is actually refreshing.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Great. I hope we get to be the bestest of friends, Mako-chan.
Uh, sorry ‘bout that. I sorta got carried away ...

text.ACTION: We have a new message from Mishima, while we’re here.

text.Yuuki Mishima: And if the land speculators aren’t coming by, they can actually start showing movies there again!

text.Morgana: That might be a good place to go see a movie! You should invite someone to go with you sometime!

text.Newscaster: It has become clear that harsh work conditions are the norm at Okumura Foods. Escalating criticism of President Okumura has considerably worsened the company’s public image.

text.Morgana: Our target’s Okumura! People will definitely stop bugging us once we actually take him down!

text.President Tanaka: This site uses text-to-speech for an easy-to-understand shopping experience!

text.ACTION: We can only have one package incoming at a time, and the more we spend the more will be available. Simple.

text.President Tanaka: Forget any silly doubts or skepticism you might have, and just sign up now!

text.Morgana: This site is incredibly shady ...  So, are you gonna sign up?
...Is it really OK to use your real name on a site like this?

text.President Tanaka: Hello, and welcome to Tanaka’s Shady Commodities! Mr. Hamiru, you’ve opened the door to possibilities that normal people can only dream of! Now, you can find all the rate items you could possibly want!

text.ACTION: We’re just going to buy literally everything we can: the Nirvana Ring, the Black Rock, the Five-inch Nail, and three Condenser Lenses. The Nirvana Ring gives high resistance to Bless damage. The Black Rock lets us transmute a Persona into an accessory. The Five-inch Nail deals 50 Curse damage to a foe, which is useful if you don’t have that on a Persona yet but not that useful because you can’t buy them in bulk. The Condenser Lenses are just crafting materials.

text.President Tanaka: Good news, Mr. Hamiru! Wh-Why, you’ve already spent over 10,000 yen! Your member rank is now Black! Now you can purchase all of our Black-tier products! Your order will arrive soon. We understand your excitement, but we ask for your patience! We hope to see you again soon!

text.ACTION: Fun fact- Tanaka’s is the only portrait in the entire game with no animations. Well, I assume. I didn’t actually check.

text.Souse: Ha ...  Heh ...  Hahahahaha!
Me OK? Yer the one talkin’ to a rock ...  jus’ sittin’ ...  on the shide of the road ...  But even a rock like me c’n help people! Throw me! Jus’ throw me at th’ evil corporationsh!

text.ACTION: All three responses are about the same, which is a bit disappointing coming from our old friend Drunken Souse.

text.Rebellious Grade Schooler: That’s dumb! A phone is way better. If you had one, you could look at the Phantom Thieves fan site!

text.Innocent Grade Schooler: Oh, that’d be so cool! They have rankings and stuff, right?

text.Rebellious Grade Schooler: Yeah, it’s really popular right now! I’m gonna ask my parents to get me a phone too.

text.College Student 2: I didn’t go to college to wind up at a company like that.

text.Partying College Student: Anyways, buuuddy, while the Phantom Thieves take care of those assholes ...  We party, party, party!

text.Earnest Office Worker: Yes, even though many were skeptical of them until recently.

text.Elderly Office Worker: We hate to think, therefore we are easily controlled. Japan is becoming a country of imbeciles.

text.Earnest Office Worker: I guess that means there’s going to be people making a fortune off of them again.

text.Adorable Woman: The Phantom Thieves’ll take care of him. Don’t you worry. I hope they do it soon, too.

text.Rural Young Man: The fire department back home would’ve come to the rescue right quick.

text.Adorable Woman: Aaaaand this conversation’s over.

text.Foreign Barker: That’s so messed up! They treat their employees like livestock!
I’m glad my manager doesn’t treat me like that ...

text.Sullen Office Worker: Young people seem excited about them too. They’re saying it’s a sign that times are changing. I hope their next target is that hotshot president. That guy’s an enemy to office workers everywhere.

text.Tired Office Worker: They’ll target the president if they call themselves heroes. They already got my hopes up.

text.Beefy Trendsetter: Shut up, you ...  chunky, hunky ...  cake of beef!

text.ACTION: Sometimes I wonder why I even bother transcribing these fuckers’ dialogue.

text.Beefy Trendsetter: Just you watch! I’ll reveal the Phantom Thieves as the monsters they really are!

text.Scruffy Romantic: What are you talking about? When you get angry, you’re more of a monster than they are!

text.Shiro Asakura: This is important, you idiot. How do you think we get by? They’re a real important sponsor, one we can’t afford to lose, so we gotta take good care of them!

text.Sojiro Sakura: Sorry, and thanks. Oh ...  The regulars’ll be here any minute.

text.ACTION: What are you doing, people!? Grab your muskets!
I question whether anyone will understand that joke, but the idea of making a goof no one will get kinda cracks me up anyway, so it’s worth it.

text.Sojiro Sakura: All I want in a relationship is spicy stimulation followed by some smooth, relaxing comfort. And I can get both of those things from my curry and my coffee. That’s enough for me.

text.Gaudy Customer: He always dodges my questions like that. He’s so clever. By the way, what are your thoughts on So-chan’s life of solitude?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Anyway, the only thing I care about in life is making sure my customers are satisfied.

text.ACTION: Also, your teenage daughter. I assume, anyway.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Nothing makes me happier than seeing people relax in here. Come back anytime, OK?
But I guess food service relies on keeping the right distance from people ...  Not too far, not too close.

text.ACTION: Shit, haven’t seen this guy in a while.

text.Futaba's Uncle: Well ...  I just learned something VERY interesting! Futaba’s been shut off from both school and society this whole time, huh? That’s not good parenting.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Yeah? And what have YOU done to care for her?

text.Futaba's Uncle: You know quite well what I’ve done ...  and it’s about time you pay up.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Don’t be ridiculous. Futaba had a terrible life living with you ...  Plus, I already gave you most of the inheritance for custody! Is that still not enough for you!?

text.Futaba's Uncle: We could always find out in court. I wonder who’d win between a blood relative and a mere legal guardian ...

text.Sojiro Sakura: You ...

text.Futaba's Uncle: Oh, and not to mention that kid you have here! I’ve heard all about him and his criminal record. That leaves us with a "parent" who won’t let her go to school and a delinquent housemate on probation ...  Doesn’t quite seem to be the best environment for Futaba, now does it?
Y-You have a problem, punk!? I’ll sue you for intimidation!
Futaba-chan! Long time no see!
See what I’m saying? She’s a total wreck. This is clearly not a healthy situation.

text.Sojiro Sakura: She’s only like this because she saw you here!

text.Futaba's Uncle: Hmph, don’t make me repeat myself ...  You can’t beat me in court, so you may as well just give me the money.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Grrr ...

text.Futaba's Uncle: Well, I hope you reach the right decision! Bye now!

text.ACTION: “Bye now!”? That’s what he says after threatening to strip Sojiro of custody? Are he and Sae friends or something?

text.Futaba Sakura: Sojiro...

text.Sojiro Sakura: That man ...  is Futaba’s uncle.

text.ACTION: It’s actually not that surprising. He alluded multiple times to being related to Futaba.

text.Sojiro Sakura: After Wakaba died, Futaba was passed around all her relatives ...  His place was the last. He treated her like garbage. He never fed her, and forced her to sleep on the floor like an animal. He didn’t even let her bathe ...  Once I learned that, I knew I had to step in.

text.ACTION: My god, this dude is a fucking cartoon supervillain. This is the plot of the unproduced third Rescuers film, isn’t it?

text.Sojiro Sakura: I couldn’t stand for that kind of horrible treatment, so I decided to take Futaba under my care. Even back then, he was whining about all the damn expenses. I threw some cash his way, thinking that would put the issue to bed ...  but now he’s back for more. I don’t even know how he managed to find me here ...  Maybe paying him was a mistake.

Either way though, it’s my fault Futaba didn’t leave her room. I just didn’t know how to help her through it ...  I’d make curry, leave it by her door, and go. If not for you, I’d probably still be waiting for her to come out.
They say blood’s thicker than water, right? I wonder what’d be the best for Futaba ...

text.ACTION: Not that fucking dude! Holy shit, are you really considering this!?

text.Sojiro Sakura: Haha ...  Look at me, spilling my heart out to a punk like you. Though ...  it’s kinda weird. For some reason, I just feel like telling you this stuff. It’s like you’re peering into my heart ...  Heh, I guess there really is something special about you.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Sojiro is growing deeper...

text.ACTION: There’s really no reason to be making coffee at this point in the game, especially once you unlock Affinity Reading, so I’ve never made use of Coffee Mastery. From what I hear, though, it upgrades coffee’s SP restoration from 30 to 100. Not bad.

text.Sojiro Sakura: I should be heading home. I’m still worried about Futaba. Don’t stay up too late, you hear? Oh, and ...  thanks.

text.Joker: I can see the compassion hidden beneath Sojiro’s actions ...  I feel my Kindness growing ...

text.ACTION:
Part 110: 9/20-9/21: Fucking Mishima
	Part 106: 9/20-9/21: Fucking Mishima

text.Boy 10: I do have some Big Bang Burger coupons, but we ...  probably shouldn’t go there anymore, huh?

text.Energetic-Looking Guy: Uh, no. I hear you’ll have a psychotic breakdown if you eat there. I mean, haven’t all of Okumura’s enemies died in strange ways? Maybe he feeds them poisoned burgers ...  What a monster.

text.ACTION: Why would he poison his own customers, idiot?

text.Boy 10: You know, I voted Okumura on the Phan-Site ...  The Phantom Thieves have a duty to punish bad people. I hope they take care of him soon.

text.Calm Student: All the craziness that’s happening is freaking me out. You think the Phantom Thieves’ll save us again?

text.Energetic Student: Hmm, they’re probably too busy for us right now. First, they have to focus on Okumura!

text.Morgana: That’s the spirit!

text.Chatter: Hamiru-kun drew this? It’s like, totally perfect.
So Hamiru’s part of the Phandom too? This is awesome!
It kinda feels like the Phantom Thieves are gods or something. They’re fighting for all of us!
I wish they’d pick up the pace though. I can’t wait much longer!
They should just get moving on that shithead executive! Enough loafing around!
Phantom Thieves! Phantom Thieves!

text.ACTION: How is this news just now getting out?

text.Newspaper Club Member: The newspaper club must stand strong despite it all. Go ahead and tell me what you want to know.

text.ACTION: But aren’t you the entire newspaper club…? Eh, whatever.

text.Newspaper Club Member: Some say the Phantom Thieves are responsible, but it’s apparently confirmed to be suicide.
I wonder if there was anything we could have done to prevent this from happening ...

Big Bang is attracting a lot of interest. It’s already pretty well known among high school students. Employee exploitation by companies is a social issue, so it might be interesting to do a feature on it.
I’m surprised you know about her! Most people don’t know that Okumura-senpai is the daughter of the Okumura who runs that company.
People find out this company is exploiting its employees, and some look to the Phantom Thieves. The extremists are asking them to strike already. Maybe the Phantom Thieves are tired of it by now.

text.Energetic First-Year: Yeah, I’ve seen her around. She takes care of the flowers in front of the school.

text.Motivated First-Year: I heard she’s engaged. Can you believe that? She’s still in high school!

text.Energetic First-Year: She lives in a different world. This school is just too weird ...

text.Ikesugi: Oh, that was you. I knew I felt someone looking at me. Well.. We could start off as friends.

text.Creepy Female Student: Yes ... ! This is my chance! Er, I mean, uh ...  Thank you ...  very much!

text.ACTION: Mogami needed two full months to say that?

text.Friend of Tired Student: Who cares? Actually, shouldn’t you worry about how this might affect recommendations? I’m seriously going to be angry if I can’t get a recommendation because of all this!

text.ACTION: Shujin is a wonderful school full of compassionate students and caring faculty.

text.Boy 12: It’s crazy how it all gets back to Shujin Academy again. So President Okumura is their next target?

text.Suave Male Student: I’m sure he is since he’s hit the top rank so fast. I can’t wait to see him break down and grovel.

text.Boy 13: I guess that’s what happens when you cut down labor costs too much. Business management is tough work.

text.ACTION: “Treat your workers like human beings” is real tough, yeah.

text.COMMENT: Protag: I’m right here, dude.

text.Calm Basketball Player: --a suicide attempt, sex crimes by a teacher, our principal died ...

text.Fiery Soccer Player: You’re right. That is a lot to happen in just one year. Maybe this school really is cursed.

text.Calm Basketball Player: That makes sense. A curse would explain why we can’t get any decent members or win any games.

text.Student Athlete in a Jersey: The food there is cheap, but it’s filling. It might suck if Big Bang weren’t around anymore.

text.Student Athlete 2: Nah, bad guys should be punished. And those press conferences where they apologize are fun to watch.

text.Gaudy Female Student: You don’t like places like that either, do you, Sensei?

text.Teacher 1: Of course not. But it isn’t always clear whether or not something can be considered exploitation.

text.ACTION: Whaaat? Really? Then maybe we should just get rid of all companies!

text.Starry-Eyed Student: If I had only paid more attention. I failed to save him as a Phantom Thief of Hearts.
It’s kind of you to say that. Don’t worry. I won’t make that kind of mistake ever again. Yes, this is a test from fate. I’ll do all I can to live up to everyone’s faith in me!

text.ACTION: We haven’t hung out with Ryuji in… *checks* ...literally four months. Let’s rectify that!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh ... ? You sure we’re gonna be OK not headin’ in?

...Eh, I guess it ain’t gonna hurt gettin’ a change of pace. So, uh ...  I’ve been thinkin’ about what to do with the track team ...  But I realized I’m not the kinda guy to come up with epic plans that can save the day. So, I think I’m gonna do this the one way I know how. Can you come with?

I’ve gotta tell Nakaoka and Takeishi what’s goin’ on with that asshole of a teacher ...  I mean, there’s no way the track team’s gonna make a comeback without them. Come with me to the courtyard, man.
You prolly didn’t realize, but I recorded Yamauchi’s whole convo back at the monja shop! I’m a genius, I know.

text.ACTION: That’s your whole plan? You intimated you had something… I don’t know… dumber up your sleeve a minute ago. Also, I’m shocked you managed to figure out how to record a phone call.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Anyways, uh ...  I might need some backup here. Can you stick around?

text.Takeishi: Nakaoka!? Wh-What the hell!? Are you guys gonna gang up on me!?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Dude, chill. I just wanna talk. Listen. This here is what’s really goin’ on with the track team.

text.Yamauchi: ...  ...  And the best part is, not only are Takeishi’s parents loaded, but his mother’s the president of the PTA.  ...  ...  But until then, he can show the others the value of obedience.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It’s Yamauchi’s voice, ain’t it? And on top of that, shit’s gone down just like he said.

text.Takeishi: ...  ...  Yamauchi’s right. I don’t have talent ...  I’m not like you guys. I ran so damn hard, but you two were always so far ahead ...  How’s a guy like me supposed to succeed? How am I supposed to be proud of myself!?
My dad always talks about how proud he is of his son ...  He told everyone I’d get a track scholarship like he did ...  That I’d follow in his footsteps as a second-generation Taisei grad ...

text.ACTION: From a cursory Google, Taisei (full name Taisei Gakuin University) appears to be a private university in Osaka, though it only gained its current name in 2003, so I’m not sure it’s the one this guy is referring to because his dad would probably use the old name. Also, the one I found isn’t actually ranked that high in terms of Japan’s universities, so actually it’s pretty unlikely that this kid is dying to get in anyway. I’m just going to assume they made a school up.

text.Takeishi: That’s why I listened to Yamauchi. He said if I was the captain, he’d write me a great letter of rec ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...So you trusted what he was sayin’ about Nakaoka ‘cause of stupid crap like that?
master of tact.

text.Takeishi: You couldn’t know how I feel ...  Nobody does!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Like hell I don’t know!
Maybe you should stop tryin’ to live for them, and just try livin’ for yourself. You think you gotta betray people to be proud?
If that’s seriously what you think, you’re wrong!
I mean, the bastard’s never been interested in track before ...  But you kept quiet. You knew he was walkin’ all over you, and you just let him do it.

text.Nakaoka: ...Yeah. I was afraid ...  Without Yamauchi, we still wouldn’t have a team ...  or a place to belong.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...You missed runnin’ that bad? Y’know ...  it ain’t so scary not havin’ a place you belong. You can kinda be free that way. If anything, I’m more scared of bein’ a crappy person. I mean, I used to be like you guys ...  afraid, lyin’ to myself ...

text.ACTION: "Man, I’m glad I’m not awful anymore, like you guys are."

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That is, before I met this dude.
So ...  if you wanna hit me or something, go ahead. I’m ready.

text.ACTION: Woohoo! Violence toward a domestic abuse victim as comedy!

text.Nakaoka: Hahaha, I’m actually starting to feel a little better already.

text.Takeishi: Me too. I think I can finally put all of this behind me. Nakoaka ...  I’m sorry.

text.Nakaoka: I’m sorry too. So ...  you wanna bring back the track team?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...Thanks.
For real though ...  you were a big help. You were pushin’ me to be cool that whole time. It’s kinda like I was doin’ a sprint ...  and you were runnin’ next to me.

text.ACTION: And now Ryuji gets Endure. Given that he’s pretty much a mainstay in our party at this point, this will be very helpful.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I think my mouth’s bleedin’, so we’ll hafta eat some other time. Later!

text.Haughty Regular: Are you among those who are waiting to see the president of that company meet his judgment?

Haha, I appreciate your honesty. I also can’t deny the excitement I feel in my heart. It’s clear that they have power. They have an ethical obligation to use it wisely. The pressure and expectations that burden exceptional people ...  I know it well, hahaha.

text.Newscaster: He has testified that he claimed to be a phantom thief in his post because he wanted the attention.

text.ACTION: Wait, if he was just arrested, how could he have also testified? The more formal definition of that word specifically relates to statements made in court.

text.Newscaster: Police have warned people to be cautious of crimes that exploit the Phantom Thieves bandwagon.

text.Morgana: I wish people would stop pulling stunts like this. But maybe this happens once you become famous.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Ugh, my head hurts ...

text.Joker: Sojiro seems concerned about Futaba’s uncle ...  Is it OK for me to stick my nose into Sojiro’s and Futaba’s problem ... ?

text.ACTION: YOU’RE A FUCKING PHANTOM THIEF, MY DUDE, THAT’S ALL YOU DO
And so we need Rank 5 Kindness to progress Sojiro’s Confidant further.

text.Munehisa Iwai: I got work for you to do around the shop today. ...You got some time later?
All right, come to the back when you’ve finished.
...It’s about that secret Tsuda mentioned. There’s more to it than my havin’ been in the yakuza. I just wanna make sure you don’t go sayin’ somethin’ stupid if you run into Kaoru ‘round here ...
She had this baby with her, and the whole time she was there she kept goin’ on about how she wanted to sell it.
Figured she was just some cracked-up junkie lookin’ for drug money. But then when I told her no, she sat the baby down and ran off. ...That baby was Kaoru.
Thinkin’ back on it, I’m still not really sure why I took him in ...

text.ACTION: The Song of Life coming to PS4 April 17th! Preorder your special edition copy today and receive a hardcover art book, as well as ...
...two drink glasses, two coasters, and some fucking ice stones for some goddamn reason (????)! Sure, why not?
What were we talking about? Oh right, bad parenting.

text.Munehisa Iwai: Not only did I have to leave the clan, but now I’m stuck runnin’ this shop I don’t even like. (chuckle) Every day’s an uphill battle. I still haven’t managed to tell Kaoru I was in the yakuza though ...
...Lemme ask you somethin’. How would you feel if you found out your parents were wrapped up in some dirty shit?

text.ACTION: Well, it’s implied our parents kinda suck already, so I doubt we’d care that much.

text.Munehisa Iwai: That’s how my mom was. She’d spend every night out drinkin’, runnin’ around town with all sortsa guys.

text.ACTION: "And then when she got home she was mercilessly slutshamed by me! It was disgraceful all around!"

text.Munehisa Iwai: I couldn’t stand to see her destroy herself like that. Often I wished I could’ve had someone else as my mom.

text.ACTION: I mean, yeah, she sounds pretty irresponsible, but the part about the guys just seems kinda unnecessary, Iwai. I thought you were cool.

text.Munehisa Iwai: So ...  I didn’t wanna make Kaoru go through the same thing. I wanted to make sure he had a good childhood. That’s why I left the clan. I did everythin’ according to the code, but now Tsuda’s draggin’ me back ...  Once he remembered I run this fake gun shop, he came by askin’ me to make custom models for him.

text.ACTION: We should get Iwai and Ryuji together to plot their ongoing war against the letter “G.”

text.Munehisa Iwai: Truth is, Tsuda’s got all sortsa dirt. Not just on what happened when Kaoru was a baby, but on me and the rest of my family too. Who knows what’d happen if Kaoru learned the truth ...  When it’s all said and done, he’s gonna try and take everythin’ I have. If word gets out about my past, people’re gonna treat Kaoru like he’s no different than me. After all, everyone knows shitty parents end up makin’ shitty kids ...  And once he’s got that stigma, he’ll be stuck with it. When shit goes wrong, he’ll always be the one who gets blamed. That’s how it was with me.

text.ACTION: So, you’re trying to prevent Kaoru or anyone else from finding out that you used to be in the yakuza. But you still work at a shady-ass fake gun shop. How is that better? Also, I feel like it’d be really easy to find out you used to be in the yakuza! You even have a neck tattoo, dude!

text.Munehisa Iwai: ...That’s why I turned to the yakuza. Nobody else would accept me. That’s also why I can’t turn Tsuda down. He’s just got too much power.

I bet Kaoru’s sick of havin’ a weak-ass dad like me. Anyways, I was tryin’ to stall Tsuda with bullshit prototypes while I figured out a way to stop him ...  But that bastard’s real good as keepin’ his cards close to his chest. Plus, he caught wind of what I was tryin’ to do and started keepin’ tabs on me 24/7.

text.ACTION: Well, that can’t be economical for him.

text.Munehisa Iwai: Thankfully, that’s just about when you showed up, kid. (sigh) Sorry for bringin’ all that shit up out of the blue. ...You prolly don’t want anythin’ to do with me after that, huh?

text.ACTION: Iwai likes it when we neg him, apparently.

text.Munehisa Iwai: Oh, right. Just remembered I never gave you a reward for that info. Hm ...  How about I give you a discount on the special menu? That should keep you quiet for a while. Pretty good deal, huh?

text.Joker: It feels like my bond with Iwai is growing even deeper...

text.ACTION: Oh hey, a discount for the service we’ve never once used and may never end up using because as it turns out it’s not very good. How swell.

text.Munehisa Iwai: Kaoru’s been eatin’ a ton lately after cram school. He’s prolly gonna have another growth spurt soon. Anyways, I’m closin’ up for today. You should head home too.

text.Joker: I feel like helping Iwai with his work has honed my Proficiency...

text.Munehisa Iwai: Take it easy, kid.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: –is an important work in the history of literature for being the first to use the word "robot."

text.Black-Haired Student: Duh. Make him have a change of heart. These corrupt companies should just go bankrupt!

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Hey! You’re in class right now! Quit talking about Okumura and the Phantom Thieves! Geez ...  Hamiru-kun! You were listening at least, right? The word "robot" didn’t come from English. So, what country did it come from?

text.Collaborator 1: Well, the word "robot" actually comes from an old Czech word--

text.Sadayo Kawakami: That’s right. It originated from Czechoslovakia, a European country. I suppose the question was a little obscure.

text.ACTION: It’s literally my favorite fucking movie, woman.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: The word "robot" comes from the Czech word "robota."
"Robota" actually means "slave labor."
Existing only for slave labor ...  Even from the origin of their name, robots are pitiful.

text.ACTION: Well, you could argue we’re not too different ourselves, having to keep working in order to live ...

text.Morgana: She seems tired ...

text.ACTION: That’s sexist, David Tennant. For shame.

text.Morgana: But anyhow, if Okumura doesn’t see others as people, we need to change his heart!

text.ACTION: We need more points with Iwai to reach the next rank.
For whatever reason, instead of playing in Shibuya, the “operation active” theme for this segment of the game plays in Yongen. Weird.
Today’s a Futaba kind of day.

text.Futaba Sakura: Whaddya wanna do today?
You know we’re in the middle of an operation, right? Are you sure you don’t wanna infiltrate ... ?
R-Really? Eh, I guess I can’t complain too much since you’re hanging out with me. If you’re free, it’s promise list time! What should we do next?

text.ACTION: This is obviously spelled incorrectly in multiple different ways, but given Futaba, I’m not sure it’s actually unintentional.

text.Futaba Sakura: Get in there! Go, go!
"Learn about my generation."
Wait, I think I can do the next one too! "Have a normal conversation with a stranger my age"! Hmmm, where can I find lots of young people ... ? By jove, I think I’ve got it! Let us be off, Maaku!

text.Sojiro Sakura: Wow, you guys have actually started getting pretty close. Not like that’s a bad thing though. Anyway, be careful out there.

text.Futaba Sakura: I’ve heard all about the unlimited fountain drinks at these places ...  Well ... ? Where are they? I don’t see ‘em anywhere!

text.Yuuki Mishima: Oh crap, and you’re with a girl ... ?

text.Futaba Sakura: Is this a friend of yours?

text.ACTION: THIS IS THE BEST DIALOGUE OPTION IN THE ENTIRE GAME

text.Futaba Sakura: Hmmm. How ‘bout I ask him to help with my promise?

text.Yuuki Mishima: What promise ... ?

text.Futaba Sakura: W-Wellll ...

text.Yuuki Mishima: So, wait. You’re saying that you, a girl ...  want to talk to ...  me? I see. In that case, I guess I don’t have a choice. Nope, none whatsoever. I’ll just have to help you out.

text.ACTION: Oh fuck, the nerd’s getting his hopes up!

text.Futaba Sakura: Oooh, you’re so nice!

text.ACTION: Yeah, nice. That’s certainly a word you might use, especially capitalized and in conjunction with the word “Guy.”

text.Futaba Sakura: My name’s Futaba Sakura, and don’t you forget it!

text.Yuuki Mishima: U-Uh, OK ...  I’m Yuuki Mishima, but everyone just calls me Mishima ...

text.Futaba Sakura: Hrmhrmhrm. It seems like help always comes my way when I need it most. Maybe my luck stat’s really high.
Youth ...  The unknown frontier ...

text.Yuuki Mishima: Hm, maybe I should try talking about my hobbies ...
Do you like computers?

text.Futaba Sakura: Mm, I’m always online.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Me too! What sites do you use? I usually keep to forums myself ...  Or are you more into streaming? I’d gladly subscribe to your channel.

text.ACTION: you can’t see it, obviously, but i’m fucking apoplectic right now
i have literally never been this angry, and i doubt i can even get angrier
OH HEY MOTHERFUCKER, TURNS OUT I COULD
...Wait. What the fuck did you just say?

Holy shit dude, what the hell is wrong with you? Using internet-speak or memes in real life is something I thought we just fucking understood was verboten as members of a civilized society. The only person you should be discussing that shit with is your goddamn psychiatrist. I let Futaba off the hook for it because she’s socially stunted, what’s your excuse?
...I’m shaking right now. Fu--Mothe--Shi--Godda--Hm. None of these are working. Excuse me for a moment.

Okay, so listen here… *consults notes* ...fucktrumpet. I treat you with respect—not a lot, but certainly more than you deserve—and you bring this curse upon my family!? What the hell is wrong with you!? This is the end, asshat. You ever set foot near either one of us again I may actually murder you, Mishima. No court will possibly convict me. Say one more word and I’ll leap across this fucking table, so help me...

text.Yuuki Mishima: H-Huh? That’s all you took from that conversation ... ?

text.ACTION: *low pitched whirring sound* Oh, hey. Thanks to a flaw in my programming, it seems my “Rage” value overflowed and reset back to zero! How quaint!

text.Futaba Sakura: Ah, I’ve got it! The overwhelmingly forgettable appearance, generic speech style, and total lack of sex appeal ...  Nishima ...  Are you an NPC!?

text.ACTION: So, the “correct” answer, “He’s the protagonist,” gives us three notes. “Savage” gives us none. Picking the third option here will give us enough points to proceed to the next rank, while the second will not. However, not only is the second option much funnier than the third, I’m not going to fucking compliment Mishima, are you insane!?
So, yes, I am actually, legitimately derailing this playthrough for the sake of giving Mishima a single minor burn. It’s worth it.

text.Futaba Sakura: But it’d be even more savage to lie about what he is! And besides, NPCs are an important piece in the jigsaw puzzle of gaming!

text.Yuuki Mishima: You’re not making this any better ... ! And more importantly, my name isn’t Nishima ... !

text.ACTION: He doesn’t even correct her if you don’t pick this option. Laaaame.

text.Futaba Sakura: Anyway, I’m glad you spawned here! I killed two promises with one Nishima today! "Learn about my generation" and "have a normal conversation with a stranger my age"! Aw yeah! I think I gained a ton of EXP on this adventure. And it’s all ‘cause you brought me here, Maaku. Thanks!

text.Joker: I can sense Futaba’s innocent joy...

text.Yuuki Mishima: Anyway, uh ...  what are you doing after this?

text.Futaba Sakura: Going home.

text.Yuuki Mishima: O-Oh ...  Right ...

text.ACTION: Well, at least we got to watch Mishima get shot down.

text.Futaba Sakura: C’mon, Maaku! We’re off!

text.Newscaster: Okumura Foods has gotten a lot of flak for how its work conditions have worsened in recent years. It’s believed that significantly more workers are suffering than the general public is aware of. Some say it’s natural to rely on the Phantom Thieves when the government has been ineffective.

text.Morgana: He really is a bad guy ...  And we’re the only ones who can take him down.

text.ACTION: You know what we’ve never done? Visited Akihabara at night. Let’s go see what’s up!

And as you can see, there’s… fucking nothing here, because all the people left and all the shops are closed! Whoops! Hey, who’s… Oh. Hey Mishima, when did you relocate here? (He relocated here pretty much as soon as this place unlocked)

text.Yuuki Mishima: The Phan-Site’s blowing up! So, you did the request I asked you to do. Thanks! Hey, um ...  There’s something I wanted to talk to you about. It’s super important. Do you think you can make some time right now?

text.ACTION: Hey, Mishima, I just wanted to say I’m sorry for getting so upset at your casual use of internet language that has become inextricably associated with both rampant right-wing authoritarianism and white nationalism as well as just being a terminally lame asshole. I know it’s not your fault, you can’t help being so offputting. Let’s hang out tonight, just you and me. I know we haven’t done that in a while.

text.Yuuki Mishima: You’re the only one I can talk to about this. We should go somewhere quiet if possible ...  How about Inokashira Park?

text.ACTION: Mishima looks around for eavesdroppers, then continues.

text.Yuuki Mishima: This one’s massive!

He’s great at acting, has solid conversational skills ...  He’s even been in all sorts of commercials. If you manage to change his heart, everyone will HAVE to start paying attention to the Phantom Thieves. ...He’s gotta be doing some shady stuff, I just know it.

text.ACTION: You guys might not believe this, but I’m starting to regret deciding to hang out with Mishima tonight!

text.Yuuki Mishima: And no, I’m not saying that out of jealousy. I heard a rumor that a famous idol fell into his clutches ...  You need to act, on behalf of her fans!
Anyway, isn’t it your job to listen to the public’s wishes? You have to change his heart!
Well? Pretty good tactic, huh? Aren’t I an amazing producer? Just you wait ...  I’m gonna put the Phantom Thieves on the map! You’ll practically be swimming in requests!

text.Joker: Mishima’s motivation seems to be growing stronger ...

text.Yuuki Mishima: I’m not boring ...  I’m not a zero ...   ...  ... .
Hey, take out your phone.
Don’t worry ...  This request will boost your popularity, guaranteed. After all, I’m the only reason you guys have gotten this far, right?
The Phantom Thieves’ success is thanks to me ...  and the Phantom Thieves are changing the world ...  That means I’m the one who’s responsible for those changes ...
...Bye.

text.ACTION: Well, this has been a one-two punch of some of Mishima’s Most Embarrassing Hits, but at least we can go to bed, end the update, and not have to see any more of him for the time bei--

text.Morgana: Huh ... ? Who could that be at this hour ... ?

text.Yuuki Mishima: Are you into that stuff, Hamiru? Oh, right. You probably need all sorts of tools like that for your Phantom Thieves work. Well, how about it? It’ll be the perfect way to spend the day off!

text.Morgana: Akihabara, huh ...  Well do you want to go with Mishima to the electronics shop?

text.ACTION: The electronics shop visit gives us points with Mishima (literally useless) and Chihaya, who we don’t need points with. As such, this decision makes itself.
Oh sweet heavens, hitting “Decline” has never felt so good.

text.Morgana: You’re not interested in electronics? Or did you have something else to do?

text.ACTION:
Part 111: 9/22-9/23: Avoiding Awkward Conversations
	Part 107: 9/22-9/23: Avoiding Awkward Conversations

text.Shinya Oda: I’ll be at the arcade today, so stop by if you feel like playing. I’ll teach you a bunch of tricks.

text.ACTION: How’d you get my phone number, kid?

text.Joker: I’m eating now. Maybe I should respond later...

text.Sojiro Sakura: Oh, and make sure you eat your curry before it gets cold.

text.Morgana: We got an invitation to go out. Let’s reply once we finish eating.

text.ACTION: So, we have another day off. I don’t know what for. Probably Arbor Day or something, there are a lot of random Japanese holidays (I just checked, it’s “Autumnal Equinox Day,” and Monday’s day off was for “Respect for the Aged Day,” both of which are somehow even dumber than the joke example I just gave).
We head over to Chihaya to boost our affinity with Futaba. It’s not enough, unfortunately.
I guess we should hang out with the child, failing other options (okay, fine, Makoto was actually available today, I just wanted to get the next skill before the Palace for some ill-defined reason).

text.Shinya Oda: You can get all kinds of Phantom Thieves stuff. I got a Phantom Thieves badge. I wonder what I’ll get next ...  You’re here to train, right? Well, are you ready?

text.Morgana: What are you gonna do? Are you gonna have Shinya teach you how to shoot?

text.Shinya Oda: Let’s keep playing.

text.ACTION: Okay, so, how to explain this? In non-voiced scenes, Confidant characters will occasionally have little voiced “barks,” or short phrases that don’t match the text of the scene, but fit with the spirit. Why do I bring this up? Well, for this line, Shinya’s bark is “You bastard!”
... That’s right. He swears in the non-canon voice lines, but not in the text itself. This is fucking baffling to me.

text.Shinya Oda: Don’t you get it!? You can’t just shoot all over the place!

text.Loud Spectator: ...Yeah, but he’s got such a bad attitude.

text.ACTION: I really wanna know if he calls him “bipolar” or something else in the Japanese text.

text.Loud Spectator: I wonder how long that high schooler’s gonna be able to keep up ...

text.Shinya Oda: Gahhh! You haven’t gotten better at all! When are you gonna learn!?
Thanks to you taking so long to figure it out ...
I’ve always been good at shooting games ...  But I absolutely NEVER wanna lose at Gun About. So I guess I tend to get all heated up about it ...

text.Calm Employee: Do I need to call your mom?

text.Shinya Oda: ...Fine. I’ll leave, all right?
I ...  really wanted to keep playing.

text.ACTION: You must have deep pockets, kid. Where are you getting all this money for arcade games?

text.Shinya Oda: ...My house is so boring. No one’s ever there and there’s never anything to do. Adults and high schoolers are so lucky. They get to play all night long. Having that much time helps you get stronger ...  ...I wish I could play all day instead of going to school. I’d never lose another game ...  ...I need to get really strong, like the Phantom Thieves.

Seriously though, I can’t stop thinking about that employee. He was super annoying, huh? If he says something again, I might just have to use that move on him. The one I taught you, remember? You should use it sometime.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Shinya is growing deeper...

text.ACTION: Bullet Hail lets us sometimes follow up an ambush with a smaller All-out Attack using our guns. It’s pretty neat, and we’ll see it next time we go into the Palace.

text.Shinya Oda: Well, it’s just a move in the game, so it wont’ work against actual people ...  ...I wish it did. Then I’d be strong in real life. I need to be able to win in real life ...   ... ...
...I’m gonna head home.

text.Joker: Interacting with Shinya has made my heart grow ...  I feel like my Kindness has increased...

text.Shinya Oda: Later. Say hi to the Phantom Thieves for me1

text.ACTION: We got 3 Condenser Lenses, a Five-inch Nail, a Black Rock, and a Nirvana Ring.

text.Morgana: Oh, yeah-- You bought stuff from Shady Commodities.

text.Game Show Host: Now, which of these is the punishment for forced labor, the most grievous offense? A: Ten years in prison./B: A twenty million yen fine.
The correct answer is ...  A! An inhumane executive gets ten years in jail!

text.Lawyer on Game Show: Okumura Foods is likely only guilty of long hours and unpaid overtime—not forced labor. Many say the punishment for that’s too lenient: six months in jail or a three hundred thousand yen fine.

text.Morgana: The punishment is too soft in both those answers! That’s why people are looking to us ...

text.Joker: It feels like I’ve improved my Knowledge.

text.Diligent Office Worker: I wonder ...  I bet it’s better than Okumura Foods though. But geez, are you OK? Don’t overwork yourself.

text.ACTION: So here’s Haru’s starting skillset, with the exception of one of her support skills, Fast Heal. Fast Heal lets her recover from ailments in half the time, which is theoretically kind of useful but in practice you’re still hopefully wiping that shit off ASAP. In dire situations, though, it lets her recover faster so she can use Amrita Drop, which cures every ailment for a single party member. Psy Break is a Break skill, and is thus garbage. Psio and Mapsio are Medium Psy, of course, but Triple Down is the interesting thing here, dealing Light Gun three times to all foes.

You may be wondering why we haven’t seen much in the way of Gun skills. At this point, we’ve even seen more of Bless and Curse attacks than Gun. Well, for some weird reason there are only four Gun skills in the entire game, and two of them are reserved for the absolute endgame. What that means is that not only does Haru fill a valuable niche with her Gun affinity, she’s probably going to be keeping Triple Down for the entire rest of the game. Because damn, is it a good skill.

Not that you’d know it from this fight, though. The smaller robots are weak to Wind, but resist damn near everything else, including Gun. They’ve also got an annoying habit we’ll go into later. Anyway, Haru’s affinities are Psy and Gun (though she doesn’t resist Gun like she does Psy), as well as weakness to Nuke, you know, the predictable shit. The rather paltry number of Gun skills in the game may lead some to the conclusion that it’s a waste of skill slots, and that they should focus on her Psy output. This is a fucking trap. Her Strength and Magic aren’t terribly far apart, but the skills she does get push the balance waaaaaaaay over towards Gun, to the point where I’ll probably end up disposing of most of her Psy skills.
Anyway, in terms of melee weaponry, Haru uses axes, and her gun is...
...a grenade launcher!? Where did she get a fucking grenade launcher!?

I haven’t really been going into the differences between the various characters’ gun selections, so I’ll start now. I can’t find any good documentation on any of this, so a lot of it’s just guesses! Uh-oh!

Maaku’s pistol is all-around fine, decent ammo capacity and damage. 2 clips of 8 shots.
Ryuji’s shotgun is high damage, but low-ammo. I assume the accuracy suffers as well. 2 clips of 4 shots.
Ann’s SMG is low damage, high-ammo, with the caveat that she cannot choose her target, which is picked at random from the available enemies every time she fires. 3 clips of 12 shots.
Morgana’s slingshot is a fucking slingshot. Medium damage, low ammo. 3 clips of 5 shots.
Yusuke’s goddamn AR-15 is moderate damage, high-ammo. 2 clips of 12 shots (!!!).
Makoto’s revolver is high-damage, low-ammo. 2 clips of 6 shots, duh.
Haru’s motherfucking grenade launcher is actually just okay in the damage department, but hits every enemy on the field. 6 clips of 1 shot.

Characters cannot use more bullets than are in their clip in a single action, and they reload every action.
One thing these robots can use is Recarmdra, a nasty little skill.
Using it will fully restore the HP of the other enemies...
...while setting the user’s HP to 1. This is an enemy-only skill, naturally. The robots can also use Haru’s own Triple Down, which can turn into a massive problem. We want to take them out quick.
Thankfully, the party member the game automatically subbed out for Haru was Ryuji and not Morgana, so they go down quick due to their Wind weakness.
Haru’s cut-in is uncharacteristically cold, yikes.
Haru’s Psy skills, in addition to being trippy as fuck, hit FianceBot’s weakness rather well.

Milady is based on Milady de Winter, from the novel The Three Musketeers by Alexandre Dumas. The character is a spy for Cardinal Richelieu and one of the primary antagonists of the story, serving mainly to oppose d’Artagnan. I had kind of assumed she was more of a heroic character based on the nothing I knew about her role in the story, but no. She’s a murderer who commits countless grievous crimes and then gets executed. Ouch.

So, the airlocks on the far side have a capital Omega symbol (Ω), while the near side have a lowercase Alpha (α). This will end up being hella confusing but ultimately has no importance whatsoever because it never matters which door in a pair is which, so ignore the symbols on the actual doors. Later airlocks will have a smaller α or Ω underneath the door (not on these for reference, unfortunately), which is actually important, infuriatingly, and we will actually have to pay attention to. I did not realize this or even notice those symbols on those airlocks until I was taking screenshots for this update. I can only imagine how annoying it must be to not be able to figure out anything because you never saw them and the game signposts the wrong information here. I say "I can only assume" because while I’ve heard many a horror story about this part of the Palace ...  I’ve never run into any trouble here whatsoever. By either sheer blind luck or incredible intellectual aptitude (and it’s not the second one), I have stumbled through this part of the Palace perfectly on the first attempt both times I played it, with a full year between attempts. Here’s a crude map of the area. We pulled the blue switch, changing it from alpha to omega. Then we head east through the orange omega path. If you want to get this done faster, you can skip this part and head south through the blue omega path, but I wanted to fight more enemies. However you make it to the southmost building, pull the eastern switch to change blue to alpha, head up into the middle building, and pull the switch inside to change orange to omega. Then, go back to the eastern blue switch, change it back to omega, and head back to the northwestern airlock. You’ll be back in the building you found the first switch in, and after pulling that switch to change blue back to alpha, you can head west and finally north to the exit.

The first thing we need to do is proceed normally through buildings 1 and 2 until we reach building 3. Once, there we need to make absolutely sure not to activate the lever right there. It’s a trap, the first of two to my limited understanding.

text.ACTION: These are the switchers. Every time we go through a green airlock, all other green airlocks will cycle to the opposite state, “on,” or “off.” It’s pretty simple, though I can imagine it causing a real headache in conjunction with some of these other mechanics.
Here’s the steps to complete this area:

Head north from building 1 to building 2.
Head east from building 2 to building 3.
Head to the southeast exit of building 3 without pulling the northern lever. This is crucial. There’s probably still a solution if you do that, but I don’t know what it is. Exit to building 4.
Head north to building 5. 
Head east to building 6.
Go to the easternmost airlock and go to building 9.
Go west to building 8.
Go west again to building 7.
Pull the lever in building 7.
South to building 6 again.
Middle airlock to building 8.
East to building 9.
North to building 10.
Pull the lever in building 10.
North to building 11.
Pull the lever in building 11.
South to building 12.
Using the blue airlock on the eastern wall, head back to building 10. Using the green airlock is another trap.
Pull the lever in building 10.
Use the green airlock on the southwestern wall to go back to building 12.
Head south to building 13.
Head west to building 14.
South to building 2.
West to building 15.

That’s it. Awful complex, don’t it sound? Well, it’s not, really. I did it by accident twice, and it only took me twenty minutes this time (which includes a death). Most of the time you really only have one option for advancement. Still, I’ve heard some bad things about this part of the palace. Be wary.

So, as you can see (or actually, can’t see in this picture, thanks Futaba), we have thirty minutes to defeat Okumura. That’s about twice as much time as we’ll realistically need even if we’re taking our time, so don’t worry about it. Its real purpose here is just to make it super obvious when I use footage from a different take.

I should also mention that these enemies are the same ones we encountered as minibosses throughout the Palace, weaknesses and all. In fact, these are the only times during a “boss” that we can hit a weakness or get a critical hit, and likewise the only opportunity in a “boss fight” we’ll have to Baton Pass. Why not bring Yusuke instead of Ryuji, then? Well, even with Yusuke’s slightly higher Physical stat, Ryuji just has better skills for this situation. Swift Strike hits everything 3-4 times, and if he gets a critical hit, then every hit on that enemy also crits. Also, Yusuke’s Baton Pass skills only hit one enemy at a time, and we’re going to spend this phase of the fight dealing with groups that we want to take out as swiftly as possible, meaning party attacks are vital. We could switch out Haru, especially because of her lack of Baton Pass, but she’s also got some good skills for this, like Mapsio and Triple Down, and I’d feel bad missing her dialogue with her father.
Despite the ability to knock enemies here down, we cannot get All-out Attacks, either.
This first round of enemies goes down without getting an action. They also say really fucked-up shit like “I CAN FINALLY REST...” when they die, holy crap!
This is Mammon’s cue to summon more with Work Order. For most of this phase, leaving an open enemy slot at the end of your party’s round will cause him to summon more to replace them.

I’m not even going to bother going into the weaknesses of these enemies because while some of them are weak to Psy or Fire or Wind or Nuke, we already know most of this from the dungeon, and we’re going to be spending most of our turns spamming Physical and occasionally their weaknesses if they’re weak to Psy for Haru. Other than that, it’s Swift Strike, Swift Strike, Mafreila, Triple Down, with the occasional Mediarama from Makoto. I’m also not really going to go into what they actually do, because unless you’re really doing poorly it should take a few rounds before anyone gets an action. Most of the time an enemy did end up getting a turn here, it was “dazed” and unable to act.

One group proves too much for us to completely take down in a single turn. It also uses a move that inflicts Hunger on Haru. Hunger is pretty common in this fight. It’s an enemy-exclusive status effect, as I have explained earlier, that reduces the afflicted party member’s outgoing damage (but not healing, crucially) to about 30% or so, based on my observation. We could have brought in Morgana instead of Makoto to heal it with Me Patra, but I have my reasons for not wanting to do that.
If an enemy has been alive for longer than a turn, Mammon may use Sacrifice Order (and later, double Sacrifice Orders to affect two different enemies).
The enemy with the red plume of smoke above its head will, you guessed it, explode on its next turn.

It does a lot of damage, but not so much as to be totally devastating. I eat a few of these over the course of this fight because he picks enemies with full health when I needed to heal, and it’s fine.

text.Tired Office Worker: She’s more worried about the company than you? Well, it’s kind of the same with my wife ...

text.ACTION: That’s kind of an interesting conversation to me. We haven’t really thought about the potential damage just receiving a calling card would do to a public company at this point, and it’s nice to see that reflected in some of these conversations.

text.Beefy Trendsetter: I hope they fail! An enemy of Akechi-kun’s is an enemy of mine!

text.Scruffy Romantic: Goodness ...  If Akechi-kun found out about you, you’d be his enemy too. I know you use his voice as your alarm clock!

text.Shiro Asakura: You wanna make your big debut, right?

text.Dream-Chasing Woman: Of course! I’ll work as hard as it takes!

text.Shiro Asakura: Good, good ...  Never lose that drive.

text.ACTION: Let’s resolve this hanging matter with Hifumi’s mother.

text.Hifumi Togo: ... The thing is, something unexpected happened ...  Can we talk?

text.Joker: Hang out with her

text.Hifumi Togo: Please sit down so we can talk.
She told me that ...  most of my matches thus far had been fixed in my favor. She also admitted that she was the one who sold that story to the weekly magazine ...

I ...  I had no idea. I feel so ashamed ...  However, thinking back, I do recall some of my opponents making poor moves at odd times ...   ...  ...  I’ve always wanted people to recognize my shogi skills ...  but I suppose I never had any. I became so conceited as a result of all those fake victories ...  Why did my mother confess all of a sudden ... ? It’s as if she had a change of heart ...
...That can’t be. Perhaps they eavesdropped on our conversation?

text.Joker: (vigorous sweating)

text.COMMENT: Protag: Yeah, I-I’m glad it happened, but it totally wasn’t because of any of those Phantom Thieves, who are probably really awesome and can do a pull-up and don’t smell like cat.

text.ACTION: Well, at least she was cool with it! That retroactively makes it okay!

text.Hifumi Togo: It was painful to hear the truth, but I’m glad that my mother had a change of heart. I’ve decided ...  ...I’m not going to lose.
Oh, sorry! I was referring to the exhibition match ...  I’m going through with it, as planned. ...However, before that, I’m going to confess everything.

I know I’ll receive a lot of criticism ...  but I must ensure the truth is known. This next match will showcase my true talents. I don’t know how it’s going to go ...  but I hope you’ll watch. As your teacher, I promise to put up a good fight so I don’t embarrass myself.

text.Joker: I feel Hifumi’s trust in me...

text.Hifumi Togo: ... I would be lying if I told you that I’m not scared. My kingdom is a house of cards ...  I’m not sure if it can withstand a true battle. However, I intend to fight with dignity to the very end, as a queen should. There’s a new move I’d like to test out for the exhibition ...  Will you stay for another game? Please come at me with all you have ...

text.Joker: I feel like playing shogi with Hifumi has helped sharpen my Knowledge...

text.Hifumi Togo: ...I see, so there’s still room for improvement. I’d like to do this again some time.

text.ACTION:
Part 124: 9/27-9/28: Yuuki Mishima, The Hero
	Part 116: 9/27-9/28: Yuuki Mishima, The Hero

text.Mature-Looking Girl: Yeah, it’s a new fall fragrance. It’s supposed to be mysterious, like the Phantom Thieves. I thought I’d wear it to show my support while they’re out there taking down an evil corporation.

text.ACTION: Girl #2 here is explicitly described here as “Phangirl,” for the record.

text.Gentle Girl: A show of support, huh? I could post a photo online of all the Phan merch I’ve amassed. Maybe they’ll be motivated by how passionate their fans are.

text.Rocker: Don’t know what you’re talking about, old man. I’m all about rock n’ roll—nothing else!

text.Old Man talking to Rocker: I saw some pretty hilarious videos of you online, but maybe I got the wrong guy?

text.Rocker: I express myself best through music. My next song is a ballad praising the Phantom Thieves ...  I give you ...  "Phantom Thieves Jongara Bushi"! Haaa, appeeearing iiin Tooohhh-kyooohhh ...

text.ACTION: It’s occuring to me that this dude’s musical genre gimmick doesn’t really work in pure text form even in the original game, and double doesn’t work in LP form.

text.Middle-Aged Woman: Well, you also lied to him about your age. Are you sure you have the right to complain?

text.Young-Looking Woman: That’s different. Anyway, I asked the Phantom Thieves to give him a change of heart.

text.Middle-Aged Woman: Geez ...  I think maybe it’s you who might need a change of heart.

text.ACTION: These CHATTER messages are getting intense.
All right, I guess we should finally get to telling Takemi about her patient.

text.Tae Takemi: There’s nothing to talk about ...

text.Morgana: Why don’t you tell Takemi about Oyamada?

text.Tae Takemi: Oh fine ...  I’ll go to you, so wait there.
Yes?

text.Girl s Father: I wanted to speak with you right away! The hospital that was on the news is the same one you used to work at, right!?

text.Tae Takemi: The hospital on the news?

text.Kind Old Woman: But I knew you weren’t capable of doing those terrible things.

text.Tae Takemi: ...Wh-What’s going on?

text.Kind Old Woman: Oh, my. You really don’t know, do you?

text.Girl s Father: Chief of Staff Oyamada turned himself in. He was manipulating things behind the scenes. Turns out he was the one who made that terrible medical error, and laid the blame on his subordinate!

text.Tae Takemi: Is that ...  true?

text.Girl s Father: It’s been on news channels all over the country!

text.Tae Takemi: I haven’t ...  seen it ...

text.Girl s Father: I just knew something didn’t quite add up about that story.

text.Kind Old Woman: I never believed someone like you could have ever done something like that.

text.Sick Girl: Hooray! Doctor! But ...  What’s a medical error?

text.Tae Takemi: What? Um ...  It’s something that shouldn’t be allowed to happen ...  I guess.

text.ACTION: Girl’s Father and Old Lady begin chatting idly.

text.Tae Takemi: Oyamada surrendering himself ...  at such a convenient time ...  Why ... ? ...It doesn’t matter. It’s too late. It doesn’t change the fact that I couldn’t save her ...
There’s ...  no way ...

text.Girl s Father: Oh, it must’ve been difficult for her too. I heard she’s been moved to another hospital ...

text.Tae Takemi: I’ll compensate you well. Whatever you want, however much, just let me know.

text.Joker: (nods)

text.Tae Takemi: We’re going to have to move quickly today, so you may experience some pain during the examination. ...Sorry. Just hang in there, OK?

text.ACTION: Sad to break the “It’s for my exams” chain, but it’s worth it not to ruin this moment.

text.Tae Takemi: Once the medicine is perfected, I’ll introduce you to Miwa-chan and tell her how much you helped. All right, into the examination room you go.

text.Joker: I feel like cooperating in that shady clinical trial has increased my Guts ...

text.Tae Takemi: That’s all for today. Take care.

text.Haru Okumura: His reaction was quite vague when I spoke to jim too ...  Is this what normally happens?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Madarame was in a similar state after we changed his heart.

text.Makoto Niijima: It’ll be OK, don’t worry. All we have to do is wait.

text.Haru Okumura: ...You’re right. I’ll just believe it’s going to work. Thank you, and sorry for asking so many times. I’ll message you again if there is more progress.

text.ACTION: Just relax, Haru. I’m 1000% positive this’ll go off without a hitch. Why, I’d stake the Phantom Thieves’ reputation on it!

text.Morgana: I get why Haru is worried ...  but let’s just wait for the change of heart to go through. Don’t worry, it’ll be just like it always is.

text.ACTION: DO YOU GET IT??? DO YOU GET IT, YOU GUYS??? SOMETHING BAD’S GONNA HAPPEN!!!!

text.Haughty Regular: Are you among those who are waiting to see the president of that company meet his judgment?

Haha, there’s no need to hide it. There’s no shame in projecting your suppressed hopes onto them. It’s clear that they have power. They have an ethical obligation to use it wisely. The pressure and expectations that burden exceptional people ...  I know it well, hahaha.

text.COMMENT: Protag: jerk-off motions

text.Newscaster: Former Okumura Foods employees who feel they are victims have formed an association and held a meeting. The association exchanged ideas among one another and vowed not to give up until justice is done.

text.Morgana: Oh, they’re all working together. It’s tough to do something big all by yourself.

text.ACTION: Not enough to get Hifumi to the next rank, unfortunately.
We’re already flush with cash, but we decide to go to Untouchable to sell our Palace goodies.
Whereupon we’re treated with this message. I’ll probably actually try to take advantage of this at some point, but not just yet.
And it’s 50% off because we’re at Rank 5 with Iwai.

text.Taxi Driver: The worst. Even if I drive all day, I still barely meet quota.

text.ACTION: Well, let me tell you about this great little startup called Uber—now, you have to supply your own car, and pay for gas, and you won’t make anything near a living wage, but hey, at least the company’s so awful in so many different ways they’re losing money too!

text.Passerby Office Worker: Yeah, well—don’t get me started on my bosses. These days they’re little more than slave-drivers ...

text.Taxi Driver: Maybe we need to ask the Phantom Thieves for help.

text.Passerby Office Worker: I hope they take down my boss when they’re done with Okumura.

text.Yuuki Mishima: The Phan-Site’s blowing up!

text.ACTION: Oh, hey Mishima. Guess we should hang, or whatever.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Oh, so I’ve been researching that actor, and I came across some substantial new info.
Are you free to hear what I found?

text.ACTION: Oh, awesome, what fresh hell will prevent us from reaching the next rank here? Getting sick of your shit, Mishima.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Thanks. Let’s head to the diner then.

He probably just couldn’t live with himself after what he did to her ...  His reputation did a total 180 after he announced the marriage though. People used to hate him, but now all everyone wants to talk about is how sweet and manly he is. At any rate, we can’t oppose the will of the public. Good thing we decided not to change his heart.

text.ACTION: Yeah, it is good we all decided that.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Support for the Phantom Thieves would’ve really dropped if we had. ...I need to make sure our next target is one we can win against.

Oh, by the way ...  I came up with a new plan of attack. If we really wanna make you guys famous, we need to do more than just answer promising requests. Right now there are tons of idiots out there doubting you, and trying to influence others to do the same. So ...  we’re gonna purge them.
There’s not really any better way to phrase it though.

text.ACTION: How about not phrasing it at all because we’re not doing that, you imbecile?

text.Yuuki Mishima: The truth is, I looked up some of these idiots who were criticizing you and sent them warning messages. You know, something like, "If you don’t change your wicked ways, you’ll be our next target."
I’ll have you know, it’s been working wonders. They totally stopped dissing the P-Thieves!

text.ACTION: Hold on, gonna send the brainwashing crew after my forums nemesis. What!?

text.Yuuki Mishima: There are still some people who say they don’t believe, but deep down they’re just afraid of you guys.

text.ACTION: The audio clip for this line is a creepy-ass laugh and I hate it.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Plus now that all those haters are gone, people are putting a bunch more info on the forum. Post after post after post, it’s all "please" and "help me" ...  ...This is so much fun.
All I did was find my own way to change people’s hearts. I’m above the simple stuff like producing and advertising now. I can change the world. I have the strength to do that now ...
Akiyama-kun ...

text.Akiyama: Yo, Mishima ...  I haven’t seen you since graduation.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Hahaha ...  We actually saw each other here not that long ago ...

text.Akiyama: ...Oh yeah, I guess you’re right.  ...  ...

text.Yuuki Mishima: ...Akiyama-kun?

text.Akiyama: What?

text.Yuuki Mishima: Are you OK?

text.Akiyama: ...Whaddya mean? Does it look like I ain’t OK?

text.Yuuki Mishima: I dunno, you just seem ...  quiet.

text.Akiyama: ...Shut your mouth, zero. I don’t got time to be listening to you.
