text.Yuuki Mishima: He acts like I’m a total nothing, but he still takes time to try and mess with me ...   ...  ...   ... I’ve changed though. I’m way better than a loser like him.
I even heard he’s been hanging out with some shady people ...  They’re all scum. I wish we could change their hearts, for the good of our society...
All right, it’s decided! Your next target is gonna be Akiyama-kun!
Let’s see, where’s his info ...
...  ...  Are you guys gonna come after me someday too ... ?

text.ACTION: I should find this hilarious, but today I take no joy in this. Mishima, you gotta calm the fuck down.

text.Yuuki Mishima: ...  ...  H-Hahaha ...  Good joke, Hamiru.  ...  ...  Anyway, I’m heading home. I’ll send you Akiyama-kun’s info later ...

text.Joker: I should discuss this with the others...

text.Ann Takamaki: Didn’t he give us some other weird request too? Something about that handsome actor? Is Mishima-kun trying to take advantage of us ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Apparently he has also threatened anyone who dares speak ill of the Phantom Thieves on his forum. Perhaps we should enact a change of heart on Mishima, not this Akiyama fellow.

text.ACTION: We’re really considering this? Holy shit, wow.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Whoa, wait up. He ain’t that bad.

text.Morgana: Hm ...  I guess we could find out what’s happening if we managed to find his Shadow. I mean, he’s already worried that we’re gonna change his heart, right? We’ll probably be able to track down his Shadow in Mementos. All things considered, I think our best course of action would be to defeat it and change his heart.

text.Haru Okumura: Mishima-kun ... ? It feels almost wrong to consider such an option ...

text.ACTION: Haru, have you even met Mishima? You’ve been a Phantom Thief for less than two weeks. I’m not saying you’re wrong to be skeptical here, but don’t act like you have some great personal objection.

text.Futaba Sakura: We can’t have him keep causing problems for us though.

text.Makoto Niijima: Either way, we can decide whether or not we change his heart later. For now, we must meet his Shadow.

text.Morgana: Yeah. Let’s head into Mementos and track down Mishima’s Shadow!

text.ACTION: Okay, we’ll do it first thing after school tomo--
Okay, now this is just getting ridiculous.

text.Shadow Yuuki Mishima: Could you be ...  the Phantom Thieves!? (looks around) Hahahaha! So you wanna change my heart, even after everything I’ve done for you guys!?

If you just shut up and listened to what I told you, the Phantom Thieves would get even more famous ...  And if you did that, I’d get some of the spotlight too. I wouldn’t be just some stupid zero anymore ...  There’s finally some hope back in my life ...  So why? Why are you so insistent on stopping me ... ?
I wanna talk to your leader ...  alone.

text.Joker: (nods)

text.ACTION: The others leave. This seems like a great idea!

text.Shadow Yuuki Mishima: Before you came along, I knew my role in life. I was supposed to be the guy everyone messed with ...  I had accepted that I was a zero, embraced it even ...  But once I figured out you were one of the Phantom Thieves, everything changed ...  You just HAD to get close to me ... !
I want to change society too ...  I want the world to notice me! If I can just make the Phantom Thieves famous, maybe I’ll end up famous too ... !

I’m not sure ...  but I don’t have any other choice! I don’t have any special powers like you guys ...  Heck, nobody even pays attention to me ... ! In the end, that’s why I need you guys ...  You’re the only way I’ll be able to make a name for myself!

text.ACTION: I can’t even make fun of this, it’s just sad, really.

text.Shadow Yuuki Mishima: But if I can’t push my way into the spotlight now, when will I ... !? Anyway, just bring it on already! You’re here to fight, aren’t you!?

text.ACTION: “Do it yourself” is one of my favorite choices in the game.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I’m sure he learned something if he’s been spendin’ all this time with us amazin’ heroes, yeah?

text.Shadow Yuuki Mishima: I need to be famous ... ! I need to ...  I ...

text.ACTION: Well, that was, to my knowledge, by far the longest Confidant event in the entire game. We didn’t even get a rank up out of it. Goddammit, Mishima.

text.Anon: They better not screw it up

text.Morgana: I love the sound of the word "chief." I’d like to be called that too, someday.

text.ACTION: I just imagined Sojiro with Morgana’s head. Yeersh.

text.Hungry Student: Have you seen the Totem Pole at the diner in Shibuya yet?

text.Discerning Student: Haha, yeah—it really is a Totem Pole.

text.ACTION: I’m impressed by these students’ knowledge of the customs of the indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast. As for me, whenever I think of a totem pole, I think of that one episode of Hannibal. You know the one.

text.Discerning Student: It’s so colorful. I just love watching people try to eat it!

text.Hungry Student: I’m amazed whenever someone can eat it really neatly.

text.Morgana: Eating a Totem Pole? Neatly? I wonder why they call it the Totem Pole?
I can’t imagine what kind of food looks like a totem pole ...  And eating it impresses people? The mystery deepens ...

text.ACTION: It’s probably just a tall, thin thing. Not some elaborate mystery, cat.

text.Morgana: The Totem Pole at the diner, huh ...  OK ...  I’m interested.

text.ACTION: Looks like the diner got a new item on the menu. We might have to stop in eventually, even if we don’t need the Knowledge.

text.Chouno: It seems so many of us have experienced this that a term has been created for it. The English name for that particular phenomenon can be abbreviated to "PVS" ...  Would anyone like to tell me what that stands for? Mr. Hamiru! Let’s hear it. What is this phenomenon commonly called in English?

text.Morgana: OK, let’s try to puzzle out this acronym! So "PVS," referring to when you mistakenly think your phone is going off ...  What’s the P?
Right. It’s gotta start with "phantom," since you’re only imagining it. So next is the V part. That means it’d be "phantom..." what?
That’s it! When your phone buzzes, you say it’s "vibrating." Last is the S. So if we have "phantom vibration" so far ...

text.ACTION: Chouno's all, "You’re taking a really long time, dude. Stop muttering to your meowing desk and answer the question."

text.Chouno: Good! The correct English term is "phantom vibration syndrome." If you’re anxiously waiting for someone to contact you, your brain will apparently trick you. This is an affliction that can only affect a modern society, where being connected 24/7 is commonplace.
When I was a student, I’d get all worked up waiting for my S.O. to call me at night. Nowadays people complain if you don’t reply to a text you just saw. Kind of obnoxious, if you ask me.

text.Morgana: Think it’ll ever get to a point where we’ll be able to read each other’s minds? ...I’ll pass on that, thanks.

text.Futaba Sakura: Hey, are you free today?
Only one thing left on the promise list ...  "Being OK without you around." But before that, there’s something I wanna show you, Maaku. Come to my room.
See, everything on here is marked off as being done.

But that’s kinda ...  wrong. There was one promise I lied about doing ...  One promise I never actually finished. It was "get along with Kana-chan." This all started back when I was in elementary school.

text.ACTION: Oh boy, bracing for a long story…

text.Futaba Sakura: I used to get bullied pretty hard for how weird I was ...  The other kids always accused me of cheating because I’d get perfect scores on my tests. Then one time I turned in a test with nothing written down instead ...  but the school ended up yelling at my mom. My life at school was horrible. Sometimes during recess, I’d lock myself in the bathroom and cry ...  I didn’t have a single friend ...  I was always alone. But then a girl named Kana transferred to my school ...  She was absent a lot at first, then when she was there, the other kids bullied her ...  like they did to me. But one day, she said something to me: "Good morning." She started saying it every day from then on.

To be honest ...  I completely ignored her the first few times. I thought the bullies had put her up to it. But without fail, she’d come over to me to say good morning ...  Then eventually, I decided to say it back. It felt like my heart was gonna shatter into a million pieces ...  But apparently, she’d been saying it to me that whole time because she thought we could be friends. She was the first person who didn’t mind how weird I was ...  I was so happy about making a friend that I told my mom. That’s when she added something to my promise list. "Get along with Kana-chan." B-But ...  I couldn’t do it. One particularly windy morning, Kana-chan dropped her diary and the pages flew everywhere. I didn’t really mean to look ...  but I ended up seeing everything she had written down. And ...  once I see something, I can’t forget it ...  It was all so horrible ...  She wrote about how her parents hit her, how they made her take pictures in weird clothes ...  Kana-chan’s diary was full of stories like that ...  Then when I asked her about it ...  she got really defensive. I felt terrible, but she just kept yelling at me for reading it ...

text.ACTION: “Sounds like it was her fault.” Jesus christ!

text.Futaba Sakura: I just ...  froze up ...  And then ...  I ran. I ran ...  and ran ...  I wanted her to stop yelling. I wanted to go back to how things were before ...  ...Kana-chan ended up moving away pretty soon after that. I haven’t talked to her since. So ...  I lied to my mom. Even after Kana-chan left, I would tell her we were best friends. Every month, she’d write that promise on my list ...  and every month, I’d lie about it.

Sorry for not helping her, though she was going through even worse stuff than I was ...  Sorry for reading her diary ...  Sorry ...  for running away ...  I hate being such a coward ...  But I think I might be able to face my fears now that I’m a promise-settling Phantom Thief! "Get along with Kana-chan" ...  I’m gonna do it for real this time!

text.Joker: (nods)

text.Futaba Sakura: Y-You have to help me now, got it!?
This is another part of our deal!

text.Joker: It feels like Futaba is starting to depend on me...

text.ACTION: Active Support adds a few new moves to Moral Support, all of which are utterly fantastic. “Charge” here means “Charge/Concentrate,” as it adds both effects, meaning your next Physical/Gun or magical attack will deal 2.5x damage. SP recovery is always handy, too.

text.Futaba Sakura: Oh, and.. sorry I wasn’t too hospitable today. That’ll have to wait for next time! Now, make like a cheetah and dash outta my room!
The Phantom Thieves have been trending all over the country.

text.Haru Okumura: Not a day passes that I don’t hear people talking about the Phantom Thieves in the city too ...

text.Ann Takamaki: That just means people are really starting to count on us, right?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: This fervor may be too extreme. It is a dangerous omen. We could face great danger if anyone manages to discover our true identities.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Don’t scare us like that! Ain’t no way somebody’s gonna figure that out!

text.Makoto Niijima: Either way, this excitement has definitely piqued the public’s interest in the Phantom Thieves. We’ll need to be even more careful from now on.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Why do we gotta be the ones who sneak around? It don’t make sense ...

text.DTD Reporter: People come to enjoy the beauty of nature, and a few come to pray for help in finding love. It’s also the most popular shrine on New Year’s and a great place to hang out near Takenoko Street.

text.ACTION: I really thought we’d have max Kindness by now so I didn’t bother restocking on Mega Fertilizers, whoops.
There we go. Maaku gains Kindness +3.

text.Street Accessory Seller: I doubt a kid like you could possibly understand, but ...  Hm? You look like you know what’s up, unlike all those phonies. I think you deserve to buy my wares. My art. Look at that Charm ...  You can buy whatever you want.

text.ACTION: Street Accessory Seller will sell us a bunch of (overpriced) accessories. Some of them unlock after getting to Rank 2 or 3 Charm, however. He also only appears on certain nights. I’ve just been ignoring him up until now.

The Vitality Sash gives 30 HP, the Stamina Sash gives 20 HP, the Chakra Choker gives 10 SP, the Soul Choker gives 30 SP. The three belts give Auto-Tarukaja, Auto-Rakukaja, and Auto-Sukukaja, respectively, which gives you the requisite buff at the start of battle. None of this is worth shit, except the belts, and even those are worse than SP Adhesive 3. We buy another Black Rock and probably never talk to this dude again.

Now, one may consider that the corporate culture of Okumura Foods hasn’t changed one fucking bit due to Okumura’s failure to confess his misdeeds as of yet, so the company is just gonna keep doing evil shit and buying from them is supporting a bad business. To that I say:

We first partake in one of the “autumn-only” promotions going on and buy a Moon Burger, which restores 120 HP to the entire party. Then, we go for the challenge, which is discounted to 500 yen because it’s night. There’s no further ranks, as the employee reminds us, but we’ll do it anyway.

text.Female Employee: As I’ve already explained, there are no more rewards...

text.ACTION: That’s all right ...  I’m in it for the sport.

text.Female Employee: However, to commemorate your further challenge success, we will grant you some free burgers.

text.ACTION:
Part 125: 9/29-9/30: A Second Chance You Probably Don’t Deserve
	Part 117: 9/29-9/30: A Second Chance You Probably Don’t Deserve
It’s getting intense, is what it is.

text.Murmur: The sooner they get it done, the better it is for society.

text.Chatter: We’re counting on you, Phantom Thieves ...  Don’t let us down.

text.Whisper: Those politicians and Okumura both deserve divine punishment!
Aw, this place is sold out of Phantom Thieves merch too?

text.Ushimaru: It’d spell the end of this country if kids started wanting to become more like the Phantom Thieves. You’re already in your second year of high school. You should have a clear vision of your future. If you’re looking for safety and stability, a civil servant is a good option. Hey, Hamiru. Not all civil servants work in government offices. Which of these occupations is a civil one.
Oho ...  I’m impressed you knew that. Only the cormorant fishermen of Nagaragawa are officially used by the imperial household.

text.ACTION: “Cormorant” fishing? According to my incredible internet proficiency, I have discovered that a cormorant is a type of bird, trained by Asian fishermen to catch fish for them. That’s rather quaint.

text.Ushimaru: Those fishermen are granted spots on the Imperial Household Agency’s Board of Ceremonies. That said, you can’t break into that industry even if you wanted to since it’s a hereditary occupation. If you want a government job, try for a spot in the Diet—though some may say that’s hereditary too.
I’m honestly fed up with politicians these days. Isn’t there anyone who seriously wants to improve this country?

text.Morgana: Oh yeah, they said on the news that the cabinet’s approval rating went down again. They’re the complete opposite of us. Our popularity and approval have been going through the roof.

text.ACTION: And there’s no way it could ever stop...
And Hifumi’s ready for the next rank.

text.Sad Old Man: They should leave reforming society or whatever to the people we elect and put in charge.

text.Kind Old Woman: Maybe ...  Hey, shouldn’t we be doing something too?

text.Sad Old Man: What are you talking about? We’ve worked so hard up until now, so I say our work is done.

text.Shinya Oda: By the way, have you eaten yet, Hamiru-san? I’m starving ...  But the hunger doesn’t really bother me when I’m playing.
What!? Are you sure? OK, today’s training will be a "lecture." If you pay for my meal, I’ll let you have the course for free.
I get my meal, and you get your training, so we’re both happy. Now, stop wasting time and take me some place to eat!
I gotta eat good because I’m fighting a war.

...Didn’t I tell you? I’ve been having serious battles with kids at school. They attack me in large numbers, so I can’t let my guard down. All they did today was throw eraser crumbs in my lunch, though, so I won that round.

...It’s a war. I’m on the defensive right now, but I’m looking for a chance to counterattack. I could finish them in a second if I put my mind to it. It’s just that ...  now’s not the right time. It gets kind of annoying having to watch my back all the time, though ...  Maybe I can ask the Phantom Thieves to take care of them ...

text.Kind Mother: Well, today you lost ...  So that means you’ll just have to try harder next time. Now, eat up and feel better.
Of course not. You did your best, and that’s all that counts. Now, no more crying.

text.Shinya Oda: What a joke ...  Once you lose, it’s over.

text.ACTION: “Goddamn kids today and their participation trophies!”

text.Shinya Oda: That’s what my mom told me. My mom’s fighting with the school ...  About how classes are taught, the way teachers treat students, the size of the classes ...  Since the divorce, my mom’s been taking care of me all by herself. She says it’s exhausting.

text.ACTION: That’s a weird thing to say! I mean, it’s true, child care is exhausting and expensive, but it’s weird to put that on the kid.

text.Shinya Oda: She leaves really early to go to work. Then she comes home really late to take care of me. It’s no wonder she demands so much from the school, you know? But all my classmates make fun of her and call her a complainer ...  When I tell them to stop, they call me a momma’s boy ...  That’s how the war started. My mom gets made fun of because I’m weak! That’s why I gotta get stronger!

text.ACTION: Shinya seems happy with her though.

text.Shinya Oda: But I’ve got a long way to go ...  Oh, before I forget, I need to show you something ...  Don’t tell anyone else about this, OK? But I’m going to show you a guaranteed way to win!

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Shinya is growing deeper ...

text.ACTION: Warning Shot lets us potentially skip the negotiation process by firing a… warning shot. It apparently works a very, very high percentage of the time. I never got Shinya past Rank 2 in my original file, so everything from here on is uncharted territory, and let me just say that this Confidant gets us some amazing shit.

text.Shinya Oda: ..I wish I could be a member of the Phantom Thieves and help them defeat the bad guys in the world.
Oh, it’s kinda late. I guess I should go home ...

text.Joker: Interacting with Shinya has made my heart grow ...  I feel like my Kindness has increased...

text.Shinya Oda: Thanks for the food. Later!

text.ACTION: Oh no! I accidentally did an INFORMATION CRIME!
No, but seriously, I’m cracking up at how stiff that reads.

text.Game Show Host: Consider the following ...  A: Divulging someone’s crimes/B: Insult in an internet post/ Which of these counts as slander? You be the judge!
The correct answer is...A! Spreading around someone’s criminal history ...  is a crime!

text.Lawyer on Game Show: If you publicly say something that hurts someone’s reputation, even if it’s true, it’s slander! Insults are usually not considered defamation, and even if it was, it’d be libel on the internet.

text.Morgana: Oh, you got it right. So everyone who spreads rumors about you is guilty of slander, eh?

text.Joker: It feels like I’ve improved my Knowledge.

text.ACTION: Maaku gains Knowledge +1, despite the fact that this seems wrong! Or maybe that's just one more way Japan's a little more fucked up than I realized!

text.Ichiko Ohya: You have any good stories? I’m takin’ a little break, so I’m all ears.
Lala-chan, two drinks please ...

text.ACTION: Both of them are for her, I presume.

text.Ichiko Ohya: Here, take a seat.

text.ACTION: Wait, Lala actually gave it to Maaku!?

text.Ichiko Ohya: Thanks to my quota ...  and that shithead chief. But I made some progress on my personal investigation. I did some research on the Phantom Thieves. I’m starting to get the impression they might actually be the real deal. No signs of an internal power struggle, no dirty money changing hands ...

text.ACTION: Well, we just had an internal power struggle like two weeks back, and a lot of our revenue is technically from counterfeiting, so...

text.Ichiko Ohya: I can kinda understand now how someone like you became a fan. The more I get to know about the Phantom Thieves, the better I understand them ...

I can relate to their sincerity. They remind me of how I used to be. I already know firsthand that fighting the evils of society is a never-ending, thankless job ...  But I still do it nonetheless. I bet the Phantom Thieves share that same type of passion.

text.Lala Escargot: (giggle) I never thought I’d hear you talking about passion, Ichiko-chan. Maybe all this talk about the Phantom Thieves has influenced you. Or maybe it’s just the kid.

text.Ichiko Ohya: Maybe ...  I mean, he is a pretty big fan of theirs, so ...
...What? You found Kayo ... !?
Where is she ... ? What do you mean, you can’t tell me!? Why the hell not!? Hey! What’s going on!? Wait!

That was one of my journalist friends. He thinks he found Kayo. He followed up on a pretty far-fetched string of rumors for me, but now he’s saying he doesn’t want to get involved. ...Dammit! Why the hell won’t he tell me what’s going on!? I can’t just give up now!

text.Lala Escargot: A-At least that’s progress! I mean, we didn’t even know Kayo-chan was still alive before now, so--

text.Chief: Well, not anymore. I’ve cut off all your resources. I suggest that you drop this investigation if you don’t want to face the consequences!

text.Ichiko Ohya: Wait ...  You’re the one who pressured my contact to keep quiet?

text.Chief: I told you ...  This is where your wild goose chase ends. Oh, and I’ll be doubling your quota again. No more of this personal investigation. Got it?

text.Ichiko Ohya: What!? Are you trying to kill me?

text.Lala Escargot: Hey now, Mr. Chief ...  Can you really do that?

text.Chief: I don’t think anyone asked for your opinion, bitch.

text.ACTION: I’m about to leap out of this fucking chair, man. You take that back.

text.Chief: Listen to me, Ohya. Give it up, unless you wanna end up just like that stupid friend of yours!

text.Ichiko Ohya: Don’t talk about Kayo like that ...
If you even think about talking shit on Kayo again, I won’t hesitate to beat the living crap out of you!

text.Chief: Whoa, hold on ...

text.Lala Escargot: Take back everything you just said ...  or I’m gonna do even worse.

text.Chief: It’s too late now! The higher-ups have decided to put that incident to rest, and that’s what we’re doing! You understand!?

text.Ichiko Ohya: What should I do? Should I go knock him out!?
Hmph. I know I’d be playing right into his hands if I let him get to me, but ...  God dammit!

Just stay calm and think ...  Arghhh! This sucks! An even greater quota is gonna be a problem ...  but I can’t give up now! I promise, I won’t stop fighting! I’ll prove it to you with another great article! "Exclusive: The Phantom Thieves, Stealing Hearts and Changing Lives!" (sigh) Sorry, I really will try and calm down now ...

text.Joker: I can sense Ohya’s passionate devotion...

text.ACTION: Just further security level reductions. It’s a weird mechanic and this Confidant is weird for having its sole purpose be to avoid dealing with it.

text.Ichiko Ohya: ...I’m still frustrated though. All that bullshit he said is really getting to me. I wish I was better at controlling my emotions. Like you are.

text.ACTION: I actually didn’t mean it like that, but whatever.

text.Lala Escargot: More importantly, Ichiko-chan ...  how are you gonna manage having your quota doubled?

text.Ichiko Ohya: I’ll just work twice as hard! I should be fine as long as I keep getting good info from my favorite source here.

text.ACTION: Wouldn’t getting your quota doubled twice result in the amount of work rising like, exponentially, though?

text.Ichiko Ohya: Oh, that reminds me! Lemme hear all about today’s scoop.

text.Joker: I spoke about the Phantom Thieves in a way that somehow piqued Ohya’s interest ...  I feel like my Charm has increased...

text.Ichiko Ohya: I should be going ...  See you next time you have info for me.

text.Anon: no more big bang burg, lmao

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, are you keepin’ up with comments online? There’s a lot of hate for Okumura, and a lot of expectations for us. I hope Haru’s dad has a change of heart soon.
I know! Ain’t it awesome!? This’ll be a huge uproar again. As usual, it’ll be a while before we see some results, but maaan, I am SO lookin’ forward to this.

text.ACTION: Yes, I’m sure everything will be fine...

text.School Intercom: Um ...  Mr. Inui, please come to the faculty office at once.

text.Inui: Oh ... ? ...I’m going to the faculty office, so make sure you take this time to study.

text.Morgana: Ah! The teacher’s back ... !

text.ACTION: And we can rank up Shinya next time.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Meanwhile, I am here to observe the public in an attempt to refresh my mind. Do you need something?

(chuckle) You must have a wealth of free time if that is your decision. Do you remember Director Kawanabe of the Japanese Art Support Foundation? ...The man who offered his support to me at Madarame’s house.

text.ACTION: Oh, yes! The time we broke into a place and then he broke in after us!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I would like your assistance with him. Do you have time to spare?
You are truly kind. I find it quite suspicious that he would offer money to a mere high school student like myself ...  I am grateful for his offer ...  but I am unsure of what to do.
...Indeed. I must cling onto any semblance of hope I can find in this world ...
Very well. I will call him.

... I would appreciate it if you could join me, Maaku. Your presence could help ease my societal discomfort, as well as diffuse the temptation of money. Furthermore, your composure will allow you to tell if he is truly attempting to scam me. Kawanabe-san is waiting for us at the sushi bar. I already told him that you will be coming, so let us go.

text.ACTION: We’d better eat up before the sushi gets cold.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Before that ...  there is something I would like to ask. ...Just who are you?

text.Art Patron: Hm ...  An interesting question. My work involves gallery management, but my hobbies are diverse. The foundation is but one of those hobbies. Broadly speaking, we’re responsible for scouting and nurturing talented youth involved in the art world. We offer free scholarships, mediate study abroad programs ...  and we also connect young artists to customers. ...At a time, even Madarame participated in our organization.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Sensei ...  I-I mean, Madarame?

text.Art Patron: Indeed. A good many benefited from his time working with us. We were aware of the dark rumors about him ...  but we could never have seen his confession coming. I suppose it’s likely he was deceiving us that whole time ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...This is all because of him. It is his fault I can no longer view paintings with a pure heart ...

In the past, simply the desire to paint led me to seek beauty. But now, I find myself constantly weighed down by the search for awards or the praise of others ...  An ugly attachment has fastened itself upon my work ...  I can no longer paint how I used to. My art ...  is tainted.

text.Art Patron: ...I see. However, it would be wasteful to let your talent dry up. Our foundation would gladly support you. Not only a former student of the infamous Madarame, but someone with those looks ...  There is definitely a market for you. We’ll sell you as the "tragic, handsome artist."

Exactly as it sounds. Having your ideas stolen by Madarame, losing a place to live, hungry for food ...  That unstable air about you makes for the perfect tragedy. A story like yours will sell even to those who don’t understand art.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: A story ... ?

text.Art Patron: If you don’t have one in the modern climate, nobody will even mention your name. ...Don’t worry, we’ll handle the details. But in return, you must sell your work through my gallery. We will take a mediation fee, but you’ll be granted steady revenue and a nice customer base as well.

text.ACTION: This seems sketchy, but I wonder how much of that’s just the track literally named “Suspicion” playing in the background. When you think about it, most of it’s really rather benign. Oh no! They’re going to promote him and his work in exchange for… a fee!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: In the end, this is only about money! That which taints pure beauty ...

text.Art Patron: How immature ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Excuse me!?

text.Art Patron: It seems you haven’t learned anything after all. You’re not looking at reality objectively. Is wealth really that horrible?
And beyond that, how long will you continue to chase those illusions of yours? Purity ...  Art ...

text.ACTION: Oh, I see the issue here. This dude doesn’t believe in ~the power of art~. It’s just a means to an end for him. For shame.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Sh-Shut your mouth! I reject your offer!

text.Art Patron: Hmph ...  I thought you of all people would have the resolve to use art to make a living.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I have that resolve! However, I also believe such a life should only come via proper assessment!

text.ACTION: This is a really fancy way of saying “he thinks that you should have to think really hard about shit before you have money” or something, I dunno, I thought I understood.
It probably actually just means that he should understand art or money or both before he tries to use art to make money, it’s just not phrased well.

text.Art Patron: Hm? In that case, I have an opportunity for you. My foundation will soon be holding a competition for young artists from around the nation. The prize shall be our support. We’ll bring customers from around Japan to see the next great talent. ...There will be a great deal of pressure on you, should you enter. Or perhaps ...  are you too afraid?

text.ACTION: “I’m a 65-year-old man calling you a chicken! What are you gonna do about it, art-boy?”

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What did you say ... !?

text.Art Patron: I wonder if you have what it takes to withstand a skill-based assessment of that magnitude. ...I look forward to finding out. Now then, it seems there’s no use in any further discussion. You can have them send the bill to my office.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Why is it that all artists talk about is money, money, money!? Has the true meaning of art been lost!?

text.ACTION: Look man, I got 500k on me right now. Maybe I ain’t the best person to talk to about this. I’m just telling you what you want to hear at this point, money’s fuckin’ great!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You are correct ...  My passion can change the world. However ...  I would starve to death without money. Passion alone may fill my heart, but it cannot fill my stomach ...  What a troubling predicament ...  Anyhow, I am quite glad that you chose to accompany me here. I may have bit my tongue off in anger had it been only me. In other words ...  you are a soothing force in my life.

text.ACTION: Yeah, all that sentiment is so embarrassing, Maaku. Aren’t you so above it all?

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Yusuke is growing deeper...

text.ACTION: And now there are no skill cards we cannot duplicate. Rad.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I ...  I will partake in Kawanabe’s exhibition. I am going to display my ability and prove him wrong. ...Come, let us go home.  ...  ...  Actually, we should eat first. The sushi has done nothing wrong, after all.
Now then, let us head off.

text.ACTION: “Just a heads up- nothing’s changed. Just gonna keep stressing you guys out by worrying about this constantly. Okay, laters!”

text.Makoto Niijima: I appreciate the consideration.

text.Haru Okumura: I’ve yet to truly speak with him though.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: As I’ve said before, this is just what happened to Madarame. There’s no need to worry.

text.ACTION: If you’re having trouble reading it, the bottom option says “No need to get hasty.” I misread it as “nasty” several times.

text.Ann Takamaki: He’s right. We don’t need to be worried.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: In that case, ain’t it time to be talking about our next celebration party?

text.ACTION: You know, those things that always go well!

text.Futaba Sakura: Too soon. Too stupid.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What was that!?

text.Makoto Niijima: We can talk about that some other time. For now, let’s wait patiently.

text.Haru Okumura: Yes. I’ll contact everyone if anything comes up.

text.Newscaster: Our reporters succeeded in getting an interview with a man who used to work for the company. What he described was a harsh work environment where employees are not allowed any freedom.

text.Morgana: Whoa. Having a job sounds like a lot of hard work. What are you gonna do when you’re an adult?

text.ACTION: I’m an anime, Morgana. I’m never going to be an adult.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Oh, right. Do you think we can talk about last time again?

text.ACTION: Fine. I can’t believe I’m not done with you after your most recent escapade, but I’m so close to dropping you completely, just give me a damned excuse.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Thanks. I want to go somewhere I can talk to you alone ...  How does the park sound?

text.ACTION: Here we go, he’s probably going to send us after this dude again...

text.Yuuki Mishima: Huh!? W-Well, actually ...  I was just gonna say the same thing.
I mean, going after him wouldn’t even help you guys get famous. It’d practically be pointless.

text.ACTION: For real dude, it’s bad for you.

text.Yuuki Mishima: ...Wait, how’d you know about that!?

text.ACTION: I crawled inside your soul, dipshit. Not that I needed to do that to see how much you wanted to be famous.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Of course a thief who steals hearts would see what’s going on in the depths of my psyche ...

text.ACTION: We almost went through with it, too! Was really close, but you were just too pathetic. It wouldn’t have been sporting, really.

text.Yuuki Mishima: You know, I first started the Phan-Site so I could spread your message of justice to the world ...  But before I knew it, the only reason I wanted to help you guys was so I could get famous myself. Though maybe that’s always been the real reason ...  I don’t know ...  I thought I was doing it out of respect for you guys ...  Yet deep down, I think I really just wanted to show the world I’m more than some stupid zero. Look where that got me though ...  I’m just a selfish loser clinging desperately to your popularity ...  I don’t deserve to work alongside the valiant Phantom Thieves.

text.ACTION: Well, at least he’s realizing it and doing some serious introspection. This is good for you, man.
Wait, dude, you don’t need to--
goddammit man, you gotta ruin every moment, don’t you?
For some reason Alleycat restarts here despite the fact that it was already playing.
Welp. That’s Mishima for you. Even when he’s doing something right it’s somehow pathetic. *sigh* That’s just him, though.

text.Yuuki Mishima: I’m such an idiot ...  Hahaha ...  I can’t even run away right ...  (sigh) Working alongside the Phantom Thieves has made me feel like I myself can change the world ...  But it’s only ever been you guys ...  I’m still just as powerless as always. That’s the truth ...  Hahaha ...  I wonder if there’s really any way a pathetic guy like me can help you...

text.ACTION: …Dammit, Mishima. I’m… I’m giving you another shot. You haven’t really earned it, but… it’s worth a go, at least. Just… try. Try and be better. Hopefully I won’t regret this.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Thank you ...  I’ll just have to think of what that might be ...  Wait, that’s it ... ! The Phan-Site! How could I have forgotten something as important as that!? I don’t want it to be about public relations anymore though. First and foremost, that site needs to be a safe haven for people in serious trouble. After all that happened to me with Kamoshida, I know how hard it can be to speak out against injustice ...  So ...  as long as there are voices crying out to the Phantom Thieves, I’m gonna help them be heard.

text.ACTION: This seems like a good first step. Good thinking, man.

text.Joker: Mishima seems to be showing renewed motivation...

text.ACTION: Even more experience, great! Even if Mishima isn’t always on the ball as much as we’d like, his Confidant abilities are at least top-notch.

text.Yuuki Mishima: I’m still worried about some of the rumors I’ve heard about him, but I’ll do some more research. By the way, he’s not as bad a guy as he pretends to be. Apparently he’s super sweet to his girlfriend. Can you imagine that? They’ve been talking about getting married even since back in middle school. ...I’m honestly kinda jealous.

text.ACTION: Good on you Mishima, acknowledging that even your tormentors contain multitudes.

text.Yuuki Mishima: Anyway, I’ll see you later.

text.ACTION:
Part 126: 10/1-10/2: Turtlenecks Are Back In Style
	Part 118: 10/1-10/2: Turtlenecks Are Back In Style
What? We’re back to winter uniforms already? Gonna need to get reacquainted with the old turtleneck.

text.Glasses-wearing worker: Well, even if the CEO has a change of heart, the company’s image is still in ruins ...  I imagine their stocks plummeted.

text.Tired Office Worker: Do you think Okumura really exploited his employees? Every little rumor goes viral these days. What if it was all just a lie? If so, the real victims here are the employees themselves.

text.Glasses-wearing worker: Nah, the rumors about Okumura Foods were all well-known in the industry. You’re overthinking it.

text.Makoto Niijima: Thanks. Well then, let’s step inside the student council room.
His days and his nights are reversed due to his work, so he often sends me a "good morning" late at night...
I’m not sure. I’d definitely tell Eiko if he asked me on a date ...  But for now things are generally pretty normal. Mostly messages like "how’s your bf" and "hope u had a gr8 day 2day."

text.ACTION: Imagining Makoto trying to pronounce these messages is giving me life.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Do you think their relationship could actually be serious? Was I just biased to think that all he wants from Eiko is her money?

text.ACTION: He’s at best like, what? Early-to-mid twenties? Dating a girl who probably isn’t even eighteen yet? It’s fucked, girl!

text.Makoto Niijima: I mean, it does sound like a TV show. A lying host that tricks women into debt, then forces them to sell their bodies..

text.ACTION: I’ve probably gotten wrapped up in this exact C-tier Substory five or six times at this point with all the Yakuza I’ve played. When’s Kiryu show up to trash this clown?

text.Makoto Niijima: But ...  those kinds of things exist in reality as well. Immoral hosts, human trafficking rings ...  My father even mentioned to me about gangs of men that look specifically for depressed women in Shinjuku ...  They take advantage of the loneliness those girls feel to force them into horribly abusive situations ... . Then after ensuring the girls are buried in crippling debt, they make them sell their bodies to pay it off. There are other ways they force girls into it as well. Blackmail, illegal immigration ...

text.ACTION: This is getting awful specific, ah geez.

text.Makoto Niijima: There are countless victims of schemes like that ...  Countless gangs as well. My father was going after a particularly notorious one when ...

text.ACTION: A truck!? Sorry, that’s just not where I thought that story was going.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...The impact killed him instantly.

At first it was thought to be an accident ...  But at the funeral, I overheard my father’s supervisor speaking with my sister. He was saying my father had likely been assassinated. They suspected that the gang he was investigating hired the driver ...

text.ACTION: This seems like an awful complicated method of murder versus using like… a knife or something.

text.Makoto Niijima: I don’t know. The driver died on impact as well ...  but apparently they found drugs in his bloodstream.

text.ACTION: So, the plan here was get this random driver hopped up on the good shit, somehow convince him to get in his truck and ram a pedestrian at enough speed to absolutely kill him, and hope both of them die? Any number of things could have gone wrong here! What if the driver didn’t recognize Mr. Niijima, a man he’s likely never seen before, or killed the wrong dude due to all them drugs? What if he missed? It’s already kind of implausible that he managed to pick a single guy off the street while doing forty or whatever and ram into him. Hell, what if the driver had survived? Then they have a witness, you idiots!
It seems to me like they wanted something that could be framed as an accident, but the circumstances are ridiculously absurd, sorry.

text.Makoto Niijima: Either way, that gang has been pushed back into the shadows thanks to the Shinjuku clean-up operation ...  I’m not sure any of that would have happened if not for the incident with my father...

text.ACTION: I kind of want to say "That’s a horrible story," because jesus christ, but I settle on trying to console her with "He was a noble man," which is almost a worse option in retrospect because I don’t know her father and he was a cop. I justify it to myself by remembering all those times I heard about incidents of Japanese men threatening people with knives or being violently drunk or whatever and the cops showing up and rolling them into a big futon. Man, Japanese cops are way better than American cops (do not @ me about this, I know all cops are bad, and I’m sure there’s some Japanese version of me who thinks Japanese cops suck and American cops rule because of all the murder they get to do).

text.Makoto Niijima: I wish I could be a little more like him myself ...  Instead, I’ve just been hesitant. That’s actually why my sister became a prosecutor to begin with. She couldn’t stand by and watch as evil prevailed over justice ...  That passion undoubtedly came from our father. Our mother passed away many years back, so when father was killed, we had to survive on our own. The responsibility ...  The pressure of that all fell on my sister. Because of that, she can’t help but talk down on our father at times ...  She says death is no different than surrender ...

text.ACTION: "Getting murdered is for the weak, Makoto."

text.Makoto Niijima: But ...  I still look up to him. I was often lonely because of how much time he spent at work ...  But seeing him tirelessly pursue one case after the next was nothing short of incredible. That was how my father chose to live his life ...  Trying to bring justice and order to the world around him.
Come to think of it, there was something he used to say to me all the time ...  "The most important part of your life is how you choose to live it."
Hm ...   ...  ... . How have I chosen to live ... ? And more importantly, how do I want to live ... ?

To be honest, I’ve been determined to follow the path my sister laid for me ...  After my father’s death, I wanted to lighten the burden on her as much as I possibly could ...  O-Oh, we were supposed to be talking about Eiko here.

text.ACTION: Yeah, and you made it all about yourself. Tsk tsk.

text.Makoto Niijima: Sorry for going so off topic ...  You know, I’ve never actually talked to anyone about my father. It’s such a painful memory to look back on ...  But I feel comfortable discussing it with you. And beyond that, I think I understand my life a bit better now ...  So ...  thank you.

text.Joker: I can sense a deep bond of trust from Makoto...

text.ACTION: Shadow Factorization is kind of a weird throwaway skill that doesn’t seem that handy, but it actually really is. Not having to constantly check enemies’ Analysis pages and knowing exactly which enemies currently have Tetrakarn/Makarakarn up can be incredibly useful.

text.Makoto Niijima: "Mayb I’ll like, skip college n just get married 2 Tsukasa instead." I guess she’s choosing how she wants to live too. As long as she’s sure she’ll be happy ...
Oh, another message. Huh ... ? "U serious abt Hamiru-kun?" "Wanna hav a double wedding?"

text.ACTION: My heart is set on another, regretfully.

text.Makoto Niijima: I mean, I couldn’t even begin to think about marriage at this point in my life.
That’s the best method I have of keeping tabs on Eiko and Tsukasa. At any rate thanks for listening to me today. I’ll let you know if anything urgent comes up. See you later.

text.Goro Akechi: My apologies for spending so much time here. It’s just such a calming place for me.

Haha, sorry. I will be on my way. One more thing though ...  I heard a calling card has finally been sent. If the rumors of internal affairs at Okumura Foods are true, their president should surely be judged. However, it should be up to the government or police to do so ...  This is an unfortunate situation.
It seems they have yet to find anything though ...  I suppose we will have to see what happens. I must be going now. The coffee was delicious.

text.DTD Reporter: On these irregularly broadcast specials, we share limited-edition items that are all the rage! Today we’re going to be talking about the relaxing and therapeutic scent of Refresh Aroma! With its special mix of autumn ingredients, this item has been flying off the shelves.

text.DTD Co-host: This is from Body Chop, right? I hope the one in the underground mall in Shibuya still has some.

text.Foreign Barker: Big Bang Burger’s in a tough spot, right? Let’s show ‘em some Japanese spirit and lend ‘em a hand!

text.Shop Manager: Look, the Japanese only like to show solidarity when obligated to do so. No one wants to be seen working with a company known to exploit their employees!

text.ACTION: Oh, Foreign Barker, your heart’s in the right place, but...

text.Sadayo Kawakami: I’m still in shock. I don’t know where to start explaining ...  There’s other stuff I want to ask you about, too. You’ll request me today, right?
OK, thanks. I’ll head over right away, so just wait for me.

Takase-kun’s guardians came to my house today and apologized to me! They told me I won’t have to send them any more money! And that they’ll return everything I paid them. It’s like they’re completely different people ...  like what happened with Mr. Kamoshida. ...Hey. You wouldn’t be, um ...

Anyway, it’s such a relief. They apologized about Takase-kun ...  and admitted that what they did was terrible. They even told me that I am a good teacher. And so, I decided to really quit my part-time maid job today. I’ve been talking to my boss about it ever since I was hospitalized. It took a while to work out who would cover my shifts. I didn’t want to inconvenience anyone. Now I can finally make a fresh start as a teacher. I can take care of my students and earn their trust. That’s the ideal teacher I aspire to become. I bet I’ll be an old woman by the time I achieve my dreams.
...I was always able to rely on you, Master.

text.ACTION: After everything, we’re still doing the “Master” shtick, huh? I thought now that we’re at the end of this we might drop it. Just creeps me out, is all.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: You helped me come to a lot of realizations, because you were such a good listener.

text.ACTION: This really just means she needed someone to talk at until she came to those realizations herself. I didn’t do shit. Well, besides free her from indentured servitude.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Thanks again. ...Oh crap!

text.ACTION: One last time, eh? Still gets me. It’s not just the hollow, soulless eyes, though. I think a lot of it is the lips, which suddenly become way too prominent. Yeergh.

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Today marks the day I graduate from being your maid. ♥

text.Joker: I feel a deepened connection with Kawakami...

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Can you handle the cleaning on your own? I’m pretty worried about the state this place is in. I feel like you don’t put much thought into your diet either ...  Besides, won’t you be lonely? Hm?
But I guess I’m not surprised. It must be so bizarre, having your homeroom teacher in your bedroom.
But you won’t mind me visiting the cafe area downstairs, right? We can chat over curry.

text.Joker: (nods)

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Despite how I am, you never gave up on me. So, as your homeroom teacher, I’ll always protect you. Oh, and of course I’ll keep my initial promise too. The one about slacking off in class. I’ll see you at school!

text.Morgana: Huh ... ? Who could that be at this hour ... ?

text.Futaba Sakura: You have tomorrow off, right? Have any plans? Let’s go see "Back to the Ninja"!

text.ACTION: We don’t need any points with Futaba, and the movie gives points in Knowledge, which we’re maxed on. We must therefore regretfully decline.

text.Morgana: You’re turning her down? Well, it IS your choice. (yawn) We should go to bed.

text.Anon: They better not screw it up

text.Chatter: They should just execute everyone who causes trouble for society.
Ooh, maybe they could take down my boss!

text.Whisper: Politicians who knock the Phantom Thieves are just sore losers.

text.Murmur: What about Akechi-kun? Is he too afraid of backlash to comment?

text.Haughty Regular: I’d like to ask them to target some people I know, too. I deal with far too many ignorant fools.

Ah, it’s those ignoramuses who can only insult me after they fail to comprehend my film critiques. Like the Phantom Thieves, I have a policy as well. The masses will never dictate my convictions. Of course, I know I am alone, thinking this way. But such is my destiny, and I humbly accept it.

text.ACTION: This guy absolutely posts in Cinema Discusso.

text.Male Host: Here’s what we’ve got for you today! Donut-Worry! Eating these mysterious doughy rings soothes the heart! Order now and get 20!

text.Female Host: It’s true! Sweets are like a mental tranquilizer!

text.Male Host: And it can be yours ...  for the low price of 1980 yen!

text.ACTION: I don’t need this, but also let’s go for it.

First order of business on this gloomy Sunday is to head over to the church. Why, you ask? Well, there’s something special that happens at the church on Sundays that the game is loath to tell you about.

text.Priest: All of them regain something important by reflecting on their past. By the way ...  You’ve come at a good time today. We are currently accepting small donations from people who wish to support our church and its work. If you donate, you will receive an item suitable for the amount of your donation.

text.ACTION: So, this is the church “shop.” We can get two of the first two items and one each of the latter two.

The Baptismal Water, as you can see, lifts all stat buffs for all foes. The Exorcism Water lifts all debuffs on all allies. The Sacramental Wine fully restores everyone’s HP. The Repentance Ashes heals all ailments on all allies. All of these are quite useful, as most items that have similar effects have either nasty drawbacks or are only single-target. We decide to clean house and buy this place out.
Next, we head over to buy some aojiru we don’t want for a stat we no longer need. We’re also behind a week in the rotation because we fought Okumura last Sunday. Maaku gains Charm +1.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That reminds me, I would like to speak with you and the others. Do you have some free time today?
I would like other opinions as well. I shall send out an invite and see who has time to meet. I wish to do so at Leblanc, if that is all right with you.

text.ACTION: Oh hey, what a coincidence, only the pre-Yusuke party members were able to show up! Also, Ryuji brought his manga for some reason.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Boss was even kind enough to serve us coffee before he went shopping ...  Now then ...  I have a vital request.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hit me with your best shot! All the tough problems’re gonna have to go to Maaku though.

text.Ann Takamaki: Hmm, I can help with any subject that’s not math.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm ... ? Do you two honestly believe I would ask you here for help in my studies ... ?
The truth is, I am planning to display my work in a competition. The one organized by Kawanabe of the Japanese Art Support Foundation. You remember, yes Maaku?

text.ACTION: That dude we met two days ago? It’s a little hazy, better refresh my memory.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I must win and prove not only my ability, but my intense passion for art as well. However ...  I am having quite a bit of trouble determining what my next subject should be. I have given this painting a fair amount of thought, but nothing has come to me yet. Hence ...  I was hoping to hear your opinions on an ideal subject.

text.ACTION: Yeah game, how long are you gonna keep bringing that up?

text.Ann Takamaki: Anyway, maybe you should paint something people find pretty.

text.ACTION: Thanks, Ann. You’re a great help.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm ...  So in the end, we return to the concept of beauty. Maaku, what subject do you think would most capture beauty?

text.ACTION: I don’t know if the Ann option here is a joke, or if it has nothing to do with the ongoing “stripping” joke, but I’m not picking it. Enough of that gag. Now, the issue is that it’s actually the “correct” option, and picking the one I chose will require us to go to Chihaya a bunch to get more points with Yusuke. Derailing the LP over a minor dialogue choice once again!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm? You think Morgana is beautiful ... ? ...Well, I suppose beauty is in the eye of the beholder. But honestly ...  him?
Where have all of my studies gone ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: You know, I’m not really sure what you mean by pure beauty. I mean yeah, it’s a pretty painting. But ...  I’m not sure I really consider it a pure beauty or whatever.

text.ACTION: Christ, Ann! That’s his mom! Show some respect!

text.Ann Takamaki: I dunno, I guess it just feels more gentle to me. ...Honestly, I almost cried the first time I saw the "Sayuri." It felt kinda like I was a baby again in my mother’s arms. She was watching over me, telling me everything was gonna be OK ...  That was the gentleness that painting made me feel.

text.ACTION: I assume she’s talking about the first time she saw the “true” Sayuri and not Madarame’s awful-looking paintover because otherwise this makes no sense in reference to motherhood.

text.Ann Takamaki: ...This is coming from someone with absolutely no art knowledge though!

text.ACTION: Really? Because it felt like you kinda “got” it.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Gentleness ... ? That is yet another aspect the "Sayuri" captured that I cannot ...  ...Is my heart too cloudy?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It ain’t cloudy, dude.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Are you sure about that? Painting used to be all my heart desired ...  I needed nothing else in life. But now ... ? What now!? I have become overwhelmed with a need to prove myself to Kawanabe ...  to prove myself to the world. I looked down on Madarame for focusing so sharply on fame and money, yet I too yearn for the praise of others! In truth, often times I regret declining Kawanabe’s offer ...

text.ACTION: Again, it was like two days ago. That’s not much time to really regret it.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Maaku’s right, dude. Ain’t nothing wrong about doin’ your best to make a livin’.

text.Ann Takamaki: And you just want someone to acknowledge your work, right? That’s some serious passion.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: But ...  how can passion be born from these repulsive thoughts ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Listen here, dude. I was totally like you back on the track team.

But, y’know, even through all that ...  I was tryin’ to help my team out. Sure it’s a solo sport, but nobody’s gonna run ‘til they puke if they don’t got teammates they wanna inspire. I guess what I really wanna say is, you gotta do stuff for people beyond just yourself if you wanna succeed.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm ...  Is that how it is ... ?  ...  ... . So the sincere gentleness held within the "Sayuri" ...  The warmth of its heart ...  It was all for the sake of those who gaze upon it ... ? How interesting ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Whaddya see!?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It is something that wells up within the heart until it breaks free ... ! It is a gift, given by a subject unto its viewer ... ! Yes, I finally see the truth ... ! The three of you have my sincerest gratitude! You have been a truly tremendous aid!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: U-Uh ...  ...How exactly?

text.Joker: We somehow managed to help Yusuke out ...

text.ACTION: I dunno, I feel like I generally understand the arc of the conversation and how we managed to help Yusuke, even if Yusuke’s dialogue itself can be pretty fucking inscrutable at times.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Yusuke is growing deeper...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: If you’ll excuse me!

text.Ann Takamaki: He looked pretty inspired though, so he’ll be fine ...  right? Anyway, are you guys hungry? I might ask Boss to make me something once he gets back. Hm, maybe curry this time.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: God, you eat so freakin’ much ...  Oh yeah, and what was that crap about bein’ good at everything ‘cept math? It ain’t nice to lie, y’know.

text.Ann Takamaki: I wasn’t lying! It’s just really hard to get good grades at Shujin!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: If you’re not gettin’ good grades, you shoulda known Yusuke wasn’t gonna ask you to study with him!

text.ACTION: To be fair, you also thought that, Ryuji.

text.Joker: Ann, Ryuji, and I enjoyed the rest of our time together ...   ...  ...  It’s getting late ...  I should probably take them to the train station ...

text.Futaba Sakura: This is utter chaos.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The public dislike of Okumura has grown exponentially as well. How are you holding up, Haru?

text.Haru Okumura: We’ve been receiving anonymous threats almost every day now ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That’s scary...

text.Haru Okumura: But our security is tight, so it’s been OK so far.

text.Makoto Niijima: I believe things will calm down once we finish this, Haru.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: And what about us? Are we gonna get all popular and shit again?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Let us not concern ourselves with that for now. I only pray that things calm down.

text.ACTION: No rank up for Yusuke in the cards today.

text.Munehisa Iwai: ...I got a security escort task for you. This is somethin’ I can only entrust to you.

text.ACTION: Oh shit! Finally, some real action!

text.Munehisa Iwai: Will you do it?
The person you’ll be escorting ...  is Kaoru. Get dinner with him at that diner in Shibuya.
Now, go. I gotta take car of some business with Tsuda. I’ll be there after I handle that. See ya soon.

text.Kaoru: You know, it’s pretty rare for him to invite people out like this. He must see something in you, Hamiru-san. I doubt he’d ever actually admit it though ...   ...  ...  By the way, um ...  has he said anything to you? About me ...  weighing him down?

...To be honest, he’s been acting super weird recently. More than anything, he seems stressed out. I’ve even heard him mentioning my name on the phone a few times ...  But then every time I’ve gone to ask him about it, he’s told me there’s nothing to worry about. I dunno, it just makes me anxious somehow ...  I mean, we’re supposed to be a family.  ...  ...  I’m not sure if you know this, but ...  he’s not my real father. He just took me in after my parents died in a car crash. Apparently he was a good friend of theirs.

text.ACTION: Well, it’s at least an interesting lie.

text.Kaoru: Honestly, I can’t remember a single thing about them ...   ...  ...  I wonder if my dad even considers me to be a part of his family ...
You think so ... ?  ...  ... . Now that I think about it, um ...  have you ever seen his tattoo?
The gecko on his neck.

text.ACTION: Oh, you mean his sick gang tat—SHIT

text.Kaoru: The truth is, I have a really bad scar in the same spot from my parents’ car crash.

text.ACTION: Hmm ...  I don’t see shit. Either someone was lazy, or forgot, or the model team was fighting with the writers because of all the incidental character models in this fucking game and this was their one act of rebellion! ...It’s probably just the first one.

text.Kaoru: Back when I was a kid, everyone picked on me for it. My dad would always come home to find me in tears.

text.ACTION: My god, children are cruel. Kill all children, that’s what I always say. …Shinya can live. Maybe.

text.Kaoru: That’s why he got that tattoo. He said it could be the new Iwai family crest. Oh, and I did some research on geckos. It turns out they symbolize protecting one’s home and family. I had almost forgotten about that, to be honest. Maybe he cares about me more than I realize ...

text.ACTION: We don’t often get to see Iwai from the left, so holy shit that giant peace sign on his jacket caught me by surprise.

text.Munehisa Iwai: You two look like you’re havin’ fun. What’ve you been talkin’ about?
Guess there’re worse things you could be talkin’ about though. Wait ...  did you get a girlfriend, Kaoru?

text.Kaoru: Th-That’s not what we were talking about!

text.Munehisa Iwai: Anyways, I can’t stay long. I’ve got errands I need to take care of. Figured it’d be nicer to at least drop by instead of tell you over the phone.

text.Kaoru: What errands? ...Or can you not tell me?

text.Munehisa Iwai: What’s that s’posed to mean? It’s just work stuff.
Order anythin’ you want. It’s on me!

text.Kaoru: O-OK...

text.ACTION: Ix-nay in front of Aoru-kay, genius.

text.Munehisa Iwai: I’m goin’ now to meet with the guy who set it all up. I’ll have to fill you in on the details some other time. Anyways, this is all thanks to you, kid. It’s real nice havin’ a reliable part-timer to help ‘round the shop.

text.Joker: It feels like my bond with Iwai is growing even deeper...

text.Munehisa Iwai: Dangerous? ‘Course not. Well, I’m outta here. You can hang onto my wallet, Kaoru. Eat as much as you want.

text.Kaoru: See you at home ...

text.Joker: Kaoru and I ate dinner together...

text.ACTION:
Part 127: 10/3-10/5: The Dumbest Girl In The Universe
	Part 119: 10/3-10/5: The Dumbest Girl In The Universe

text.Sadayo Kawakami: I saw a lot of errors on the previous test, so please be more careful in the future.
Today’s examples will be on your entrance exam, so make sure you know them.

text.Boy 13: I talked to her this morning about my future ...  and she was super polite. Friendly, even.

text.Boy 11: Yeah, I know what you mean. She even gave me advice about my girlfriend.

text.Joker: Now that she’s back on her feet, Kawakami seems to be working hard as a teacher...

text.ACTION: Kawakami’s rested and reinvigorated. Good for her.

text.Hiruta: Stealing hearts? Social reform? Don’t give me this Phantom Thieves nonsense. It’s all so unscientific. I mean, how could they target Big Bang Burger and Okumura Foods? They’re criminals! That artificially consummate flavor ...  Enough volume to fill a small universe.

text.ACTION: I see Mr. Hiruta went to the Code Talker school of burger appreciation.

text.Hiruta: Are the Phantom Thieves trying to steal the galaxy called junk food from me!? That said ...  Hamiru-kun. The night sky may be filled with countless galaxies ...  but in the entire universe, which of these is closest to its density of stars.

text.ACTION: Imagining three watermelons in the sun is giving me a right chuckle, I tell you what.

text.Hiruta: Hehe. I expected as much out of you. Yes. The correct answer is three watermelons in the sun. Three bees in the whole of Europe works too. In other words, the universe is essentially empty. There are countless stars in the sky, but the universe is even more vast than that. Even within our galaxy, the stars are separated by a great distance even though you can see so many.
Close, but yet far ...  Hehe, you could say the same of our hearts.

text.Morgana: Ugh, if he only knew the places we’ve been ...

text.ACTION: I’m getting worried about the public’s reaction to all this.

text.Shinya Oda: You’re going to train today too, right?
Okaaay ...  Let’s just play a game then.
Sounds like they had another success, huh? That’s cool.
It’s probably because they think I’m weak. If only I was as strong as the Phantom Thieves ...

text.Takekuma: Hah, my bad. I didn’t mean it like that. I just thought we should be friends, since we’re both gamers. The name’s Takekuma. I make a living from gaming, more or less. Ever heard of me?

text.Shinya Oda: ...Yeah, you’re the guy from all those videos online!

text.Takekuma: And you’re the one they call the King, right? I’ve always wanted to play you ...  But I don’t know if it’s a good idea ...  I mean, if I beat you, your rank will definitely drop. And I don’t need people bashing me for beating a kid.

text.Shinya Oda: That’s it! We’re playing! I won’t lose!

text.Takekuma: As I expected of the King ...  OK, let’s get this started.

text.ACTION: Christ, look at Takekuma. What is that hand supposed to be, a scouter? What a fuckin’ dork.
Also, shout out to this lady, reading her phone over someone else’s shoulder:
And this dude, trying to cop a feel:

text.Shinya Oda: How ... ?

text.Loud Spectator: That’s Takekuma, isn’t it? He’s awesome!

text.Shinya Oda: I missed!?
...Th-That doesn’t count! Let’s play again!

text.Loud Spectator: The King got slaughtered! Ha! That’s hilarious!

text.Shinya Oda: One more ...  One more game!

text.Takekuma: No matter how many times we play, the end result will be the same. We should probably stop, for your sake.

text.Shinya Oda: Shut up! You cheated, didn’t you!?

text.ACTION: Cheer on the child throwing a tantrum! This is a good idea!

text.Takekuma: Man ...  I guess the King is just a little kid after all ...  Looks like I overestimated your ability. I’d feel bad beating you again, so I’m going to go. Make sure you practice for the next time we play.

text.Shinya Oda: You’ve gotta be kidding me ...

text.ACTION: Maybe encouraging him in this situation isn’t the greatest plan, but I feel kinda bad. He’s just a kid.

text.Shinya Oda: I’m the one who’s gonna win in the end! If I lose, it’s all over for me!
I’m gonna beat him next time for sure. This isn’t over. The strongest always win in the end. Just like the Phantom Thieves ...  Watch, I’ll win for sure next time! I’m not a loser, you’ll see!

text.Joker: Shinya is more motivated than ever before...

text.ACTION: That’s not necessarily a good thing. I may be grooming a young Eric Cartman in the making.

text.Shinya Oda: ...Crap, it’s late. I gotta go ...  Man, that Takekuma though! Telling me to practice for next time ...  A grown-up shouldn’t spend so much time playing video games!

text.Joker: Interacting with Shinya has made my heart grow ...  I feel like my Kindness has increased ...

text.ACTION: Oh hey, we maxed out Kindness while we’re at it. Nice.

text.Shinya Oda: ...Today tired me out. I’ll see ya later ...

text.COMMENT: Protag: Hey Sojiro, I hung out with a kid today and he was such a shit that I basically turned into the fucking Buddha incarnate! I can help you with your problem now!

text.ACTION: We get the 20 Donut-Worrys. They cure Fear.

text.Sharp Detective: ...Criminal Affairs, OCD, 5th Organized Crime Countermeasures Section, Special Task Force.

text.Chatter: ...Oh, so you’re a cop, huh?

text.Morgana: The heck? That’s like a tongue twister. Does he have to say all that in every episode?

text.Ichiko Ohya: OK ...  Sit down.
All my connections who knew where Kayo was are gone, thanks to the chief and my publisher ...  ...Well, say something.
Well, I guess it is pretty obvious. (sigh) Pulling all these consecutive all-nighters is really wearing me down.

text.Lala Escargot: At this rate, you’re going to work yourself to death. You’ve been meeting your quota, right?

text.Ichiko Ohya: The chief really wants me to mess up, but I’m not going to give him the satisfaction. Haha ...

text.Lala Escargot: He’s like some kinda tyrant.

text.Ichiko Ohya: Tell me about it. It’s a race to see whether I can find Kayo before he crushes me ...

text.Lala Escargot: That’s not good! Shouldn’t you do something about the chief before you keep chasing Kayo-chan’s case?

text.Ichiko Ohya: There’s nothing I can do about a guy like that. He’s rotten to the core. And despite how he acts, the higher-ups like him. I have no one to go to. It’s over.

text.Lala Escargot: Yeah, he didn’t seem like the kind of guy to change his mind ...  But at this rate, you won’t be able to continue your investigation ...  What do you think, kid?

text.Joker: I need to do something about the chief and help her...

text.Ichiko Ohya: Ughhh, I’m gonna die ...
Why? You gonna try to find his weakness? His name is Shinpei Honjo. I heard that he’s a good husband, and he used to cover economic foreign policy ...
Don’t go trying anything heroic.

text.Lala Escargot: She’s saying this for your own good. Got it, kid?

text.Ichiko Ohya: I wonder where Kayo is ...  Sorry, but I don’t feel like getting any info from you today ...

text.ACTION: Uhh, with your quota as it is, can you really afford not to ask me anything?

text.Ichiko Ohya: Thanks for coming all the way out here though. I’ll see you around ...

text.Joker: I need to free Ohya from her chief’s oppressive demands...

text.Dissatisfied First-Year: C’mon, they aren’t gonna murder him. Besides, I’m pretty sure the principal killed himself.

text.ACTION: Student #2 here is named “Slightly-appalled Guy” and I love it.

text.Energetic-Looking Guy: No way, that was the Phantom Thieves sending a message! "Wake up, people. It’s time to atone!" Or something like that. I’d kill for that kind of power ...

text.ACTION: Light Yagami here just openly admitting he wants the power to murder people.

Today, we decide that if Ann’s not going to have an SP Adhesive 3, she can at least have better Fire on the off-chance we use her, so we visit the accessory shop 37 Degrees Celsius in the underground mall.

text.Makoto Niijima: Do you think you could maybe come with me to see her?
Thank you. It is reassuring to know you’ll be there with me. She’s waiting over at Big Bang Burger. Let’s go.

text.Eiko Takao: Well, um ...  I was wondering if you could maybe lend me some cash.
It’s nothing real major, but I need it like, right now ...  I’ll pay you back though, honest! Pleeease!

text.ACTION: Makoto and Maaku turn to each other, then look back at Eiko.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Does this have to do with Tsukasa?

text.Eiko Takao: Mm-hm ...  He dropped a super expensive bottle of sake at work, so the club’s making him pay for it ...  but he needs help.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...He’s lying to you, Eiko. Don’t give him any money.

text.Eiko Takao: He’s not lying! I know you’re all weird about the fact that he’s a host, but my Tsukasa’s not like that! He’s really gentle, and honest too ...  He even calls me "princess"! I’m the only one he says that to, y’know. He says it’s ‘cause I’m special.

text.Makoto Niijima: So he calls you his special princess ...  What do you think, Maaku-kun?
Every girl who gives him money is his "princess." That way he can never get their names mixed up.

text.Eiko Takao: Don’t accuse him of that stuff! You don’t have any proof!

text.Makoto Niijima: ...You’re not wrong about that. But did you ask anyone at his club about the broken bottle?

text.Eiko Takao: W-Well, um ...  no ...  He told me not to talk to them about it though! He’s too proud to have me go crying to his boss.

...Please, Makoto. You’re the only person I can trust. All my other friends would rather focus on cram school and entrance exams than take time to help me ...  And who knows what my parents’d say if I tried to ask them ...  Please. Even a little ...

text.Makoto Niijima: ...I think you should end your relationship with him. If you don’t put a stop to this, he might try to drag you into some suspicious line of work.

text.Eiko Takao: Oh, he already got me a job. It’s nothing weird though. I’m just serving drinks at a bar to help him pay off that broken bottle. He said I’ll be number one in no time. Maybe I’ll just keep doing it after I graduate high school though. I mean, it’s not like I’m gonna go to college.

text.Makoto Niijima: You can’t just do what he says! He’s trying to deceive you ... !

text.Eiko Takao: ...A smart person like you totally wouldn’t understand what it’s like. You’re just gonna go to a good college, work at a fancy company, and then what? At the end of the day, your life’s gonna be totally boring. I mean, is that seriously how you wanna live?

text.Makoto Niijima: I ...  I’m not sure yet. But be that as it may, you should still stay as far away from him as you can.

text.Eiko Takao: ...So you’re not gonna help me? Ugh, just forget it. I can make it up if I just let some customers take me out on dates after work.

text.Makoto Niijima: Eiko, wait! I didn’t want to have to tell you this, but Tsukasa has been texting me almost constantly. Recently, he’s been asking if my sister and I live alone, and that he’d be glad to help us out. Even today he asked me if I’m still happy with my boyfriend ...  Listen to me, Eiko: He’s not serious about you.

text.Eiko Takao: Don’t gimme that crap! Tsukasa’s just so nice that he’d worry about my friends for me ...  Wait, you were texting him behind my back? What the hell, Makoto!?

text.Makoto Niijima: It was mostly him texting me ...

text.Eiko Takao: Ugh! You have the grades, the looks, a cool boyfriend ...  and you seriously still want more!?

text.ACTION: Thank you for the compliment! I think you’re swell too!

text.Eiko Takao: Tsukasa is all I have ... ! You can’t take him from me!
Yeah right. Just keep your hands off! I’d never forgive him if you stole him away, Makoto ... !

text.Makoto Niijima: You know, I think she’s exactly the kind of girl those gangs in Shinjuku are on the lookout for. Lonely, depressed girls who have nowhere to vent their frustrations ...

text.ACTION: What is it with this city and its sea of predators lying in wait to victimize women, monetarily or otherwise?

text.Makoto Niijima: Eiko’s family is quite well off. Her multi-talented younger brother seems to be the sole focus of her parents’ attention though. I’m sure that’s why she fell for Tsukasa in the first place. He treats her like she’s special. But ...  asking a high schooler for money isn’t normal boyfriend behavior. She needs to realize that. You’re going to help, right?

text.Joker: (nods)

text.Makoto Niijima: Eiko’s blessed to have both money and a family ...  yet she’s still trying to break free from them. She’s almost the exact opposite of me. ...But I guess in a sense, watching her now is almost like looking back at my past self. I was so blinded by my own convictions that I never stopped to consider other alternative viewpoints on the world. But ...  that’s not the right way to live. I want to show her that, just like you did for me.

text.Joker: I can sense a deep bond of trust from Makoto...

text.Makoto Niijima: I know she wants me to stay out of her business, but I’d never forgive myself if I let this come to pass.  ...  ...  What is the right way to live ... ? ...At any rate, we’re going to catch that horrible host. I’ll let you know once I’ve thought of how to do it. Thank you again for today. I’ll see you later.

text.Newscaster: Their influence has expanded beyond Japan—even foreign nations know about the Phantom Thieves. Some countries are even taking bets about what the Phantom Thieves will do next.

text.Morgana: They even knew about us in Hawaii, right? We’ve really gotten famous.

text.ACTION: Finally, Yusuke’s ready. And it only took an extra 15k after we intentionally picked the wrong option!

text.Chihaya Mifune: There’s something I’d like to talk about. The ADP case is more complicated than I thought ...  (sigh) What am I going to do ... ?
I’ve been trying to use this as an opportunity to investigate into the ADP’s seminars so I can expose him ...  But the deeper I dig, the scarier everything becomes.
The ADP apparently doesn’t profit at all from sales of the Holy Stones. It’s nothing more than a front.

text.ACTION: Wait, so not only is this organization somehow not managing to profit off of selling hunks of rock salt for 100k a piece, it’s only a side business? Why in the hell are they so insistent about her selling more of these giant pieces of nothing if they don’t tangibly benefit from it in any way?

text.Chihaya Mifune: Most of their revenue actually comes from the seminars.

text.ACTION: Self-help’s a lucrative business, man. Why work to improve yourself when you can have someone talk at you until you feel like you’re doing something to improve yourself?

text.Chihaya Mifune: There, they give their patrons some sort of mind-altering drug ...

text.ACTION: That took a turn! Holy shit!

text.Chihaya Mifune: After which, they’re encouraged to donate their life’s savings to the "benefit of the ADP." People have gone missing after seminars ...  Families have been torn apart by this madness ...

text.ACTION: This is like an unholy amalgamation of five or six different conspiracy theories about cults, many of which have little factual basis but are just kind of fun to think about in a scary way, so they endure. I actually took a class recently on the subject of cults and new religions in general, and while I think the teacher may have been a bit too even-handed on the subject when most of us really just wanted to hear about the gnarly shit like the sick fucks we are, I learned a lot. Brainwashing’s not really a thing, for one, and brainwashing facilitated by mind-altering chemicals is just hilarious nonsense.
I’m pretty sure Scientology is still a scam, though, I don’t care what she said. Speaking of scams, back to Chihaya’s Kooky Kult! (Khihaya? No, that doesn’t work)

text.Chihaya Mifune: And I ...  I was a part of it all. By selling these fraudulent stones, I was in direct support of their horrible actions.

text.ACTION: In what way? It’s still unclear.

text.Chihaya Mifune: I know this doesn’t make up for what I’ve done ...  but I want to help the others come to their senses. Barely anyone within the ADP will talk to me though, and those who do won’t actually hear me out. What should I do, Hamiru-san ... ? These people are all heading down a path toward great ruin ...
Right. I’ll just have to admit to everything that’s been going on, even if I get dragged down too ...  That’s ...  the only way ...

text.Joker: It looks like Chihaya’s not sure how to approach this issue ...  She might do something rash at this rate ...  I should take care of the chairman before that happens ...

text.Chihaya Mifune: I’m the only one who can stop him ...  right?
Oh, the chairman ... ? It’s Yuichi Fukurai. Why do you ask ... ?

text.ACTION: I love just picking the most suspicious responses possible. "I can’t tell you because then you’ll be an accessory."

text.Chihaya Mifune: O-Oh ...
My future is in line with that of the Trickster ...  What does that mean ... ? Even so, my fate remains unchanged. I am destined to stay a monster ...  Hm ...

text.Joker: I need to take care of the chairman for Chihaya ...

text.Chihaya Mifune: I’ll have to think on this for a while. Let’s finish for today ...  Well then, goodbye ...
