text.Makoto Niijima: You who holds my mask shall soon understand the true might of the fairy queen...

text.ACTION: Queen Mab, also known as Medb or Meive, is the fairy queen in Celtic myth. She was immortalized in Mercutio’s monologue in Romeo and Juliet.
Now, time to enter the Palace.

text.Goro Akechi: And for that, we will need to have a member’s card.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Where’re we gonna get one though? There’s not too many places we can go right now.

text.Goro Akechi: Hm ...  I doubt we will find one simply lying on the ground in the main hall. I suggest we head for the backroom.

text.Morgana: Huh ... ? But why?

text.Goro Akechi: I will explain later. In any case, let’s try to find an entrance.

text.ACTION: These Unicorns use Physical Strikes and are weak to Curse.
Oses also use Physical along with charging up and inflicting Rage. They’re weak to Bless.

Yusuke learns Deadly Fury, an upgrade to Rising Slash that keeps the Baton Pass strength boost and ups its attack power from Heavy to Severe. I apologize for saying Ryuji is straight-up better than Yusuke, which isn’t exactly true even yet; Yusuke does have higher base Strength, and learns his Physical skills a bit sooner. His support skills are just marginally less useful.

text.Goro Akechi: Then let us check around. We may find something useful.

text.Ann Takamaki: Like ...  what?

text.Futaba Sakura: Mwehehe ...  I get it ...  You mean some kinda customer data terminal.

text.Goro Akechi: Haha, I am glad you’re so quick to understand. Though even if I were to find such a terminal, there is nothing my meager skills could do about it ...

text.Futaba Sakura: That’s where I come in. Leave it all to me!

text.ACTION: These are Powers. They’re weak to Curse and use Physical and Bless skills.
Makoto learns Marakukaja to replace Rakukaja.
These Kikuri-Himes have no attack skills whatsoever, preferring to use Makarakarn to repel our magic at us, as well as heal themselves. They’re weak to Fire.
This is a Valkyrie. It’s not weak to anything. It has Physical attacks and Dodge Phys as well as Counterstrike, so Physical attacks aren’t recommended.
We eventually come to a safe room.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That thing really don’t want anyone gettin’ past there, huh ...  You wanna try attackin’ it?

text.Makoto Niijima: Or we could always find another route. We may be able to sneak around it and avoid fighting. What do you want to do, Joker? We’ll follow whatever you decide.

text.ACTION: That you suggest there’s an alternate path means there absolutely is one, so I’ll go with that.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Understood. In that case, let us find another way in.

text.ACTION: Back near the safe room, we can climb up some boxes to find an alternate route through—what else?—a vent.
Now, we’re on the other side of the door the Shadow was standing in front of, and we could just leave ...  but nah. Let’s fight it anyway.

text.Futaba Sakura: You can do it. I’ll do my best to support you guys too!

text.ACTION: And we get a free ambush out of it.
These girls are weak to Wind and can use strong Electricity and Fire spells, along with Concentrate to up their power. Not that they get a chance to do much of that.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hey, it dropped something ...  Is this some kinda keycard?

text.Morgana: It might help us open stuff up further in. We should probably hold onto it for now.

text.Goro Akechi: Then let us be grateful for its existence and proceed onward.

text.ACTION: A bit further in, we come across more guards in front of a different room.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Talk about bein’ heavily guarded. They’re practically screamin’ at us ‘bout how there’s something important in there.

text.Goro Akechi: It would be foolish to overlook this, though perhaps even more foolish to meet them head on ...  What is your call, Joker?

text.ACTION: Right next to that corner is a barred door.

text.Makoto Niijima: There’s an authentication device next t oit though. Let’s try using the keycard from earlier.
Great. Now we’ll be able to get through here, Joker.

text.ACTION: The room contains nothing but another vent.

But the vent leads into the guarded room, meaning we intentionally went back and did a skippable fight in order to skip a different, harder fight. Though it turns out that if we decided to just do this fight anyway, the door was locked, so we couldn't do that either.

text.Ann Takamaki: OK then, let’s hurry up and take that guard down!

text.Goro Akechi: Very well then. We shall defeat it at once!

text.ACTION: And the great thing about getting an ambush is...

Motherfucking BULLET HAIL can trigger! The rest of this fight is pretty simple, though he resists Physical and Dodges Electric attacks so Ryuji’s not that useful. He mainly just tries to crit us with Miracle Punch.

text.Goro Akechi: Ah, aren’t those what we are looking for? Oh ...  There are no names on them. They’ll be unusable if they remain unregistered.

text.Futaba Sakura: Mweheheh! I can handle that!
I wasn’t sure what name to give it, so I just thought of a random one: Taro Tanaka.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That’s way too simple! Aren’t they gonna figure that out?

text.ACTION: "Taro Tanaka," for the most of you who aren’t going to get that, is the Japanese equivalent of "John Doe." I only understood it because I vaguely remember the name used as an alias from Durarara!.

text.Futaba Sakura: Um, they already know what we look like, and that we’ve intruded into the Palace ...   ... Then again, it’s prolly better to be safe than sorry.
Joker, you can hold on to this card and the map. Don’t lose ‘em, ‘kay? As for the Taro Tanaka card ...  Hmmm ...  Crow, get rid of it next time you see a garbage can.

text.Goro Akechi: Hm ... ? Why me?

text.Futaba Sakura: These kinds of chores always fall to the newbie.

text.Ann Takamaki: We can also use that elevator now, right?

text.Makoto Niijima: According to the map, it would be quicker to use this path than to go back the way we came. Come, let’s hurry on.

text.ACTION: Stop fooling around and throw out the damn card, Akechi!
Valkyrie is strong against Gun, so firing at her gives us a chance to see Oda Special in action. Yep, that sure is 8 damage.
Anyway, we eventually wrap around to the earlier area with the chandeliers we hop across, but before we go to the elevator, we’re going to go back to the Velvet Room.

text.Ananta: The power of creation that has awakened inside of you shall henceforth be within your mask.

text.ACTION: Ananta, or “Shesha,” is the king of all nagas in Hindu mythology and one of the primal beings of creation, depicted with as many as one thousand heads. Vishnu rested upon Shesha, and upon waking up created the universe. At the end of each Kalpa (time period allotted to the earth) the serpent destroys all of creation.
Next up, Daisoujou from Mithras and Queen Mab.

text.Daisoujou: You with the body immune to rot... Let us welcome the impending day of salvation together as one...

text.ACTION: Daisoujou is… fuckin’ weird and creepy, and I’m just going to post the wiki’s description along with the game’s here, holy shit:
“A monk who died while fasting, his spiritual power allows his body to continue to exist without rotting. It is said that he will appear before people on the day of salvation.”
That’s not so bad, right? I mean, except for being wrong, because that’s clearly not a preserved corpse but a fucking skullman, but whatever. Well…

“Based on the Buddhist mummies, Sokushinbutsu. These monks performed self-mummification by starving themselves for about three years. At the end of these three years, they were entombed alive with just enough room to sit cross-legged. A tube was placed in the ground, leading to the tomb for air. The monk had a bell with him and every day, someone would listen for the bell to make sure the monk was still alive. When the bell no longer rang, the air tube was removed and the tomb was completely sealed. A thousand days later, the body would be exhumed. If it was preserved, it was revered as a god.”
You may also have noticed the skill Samsara. That’s a unique skill to Daisoujou that cannot be passed on from fusion. It has a high chance to instant-kill every enemy on the field. It’s pretty great.

Finally, we’re going to fulfill the request for a Bugs with Samarecarm. Bugs is an Advanced Fusion from Pixie, Pisaca, and Hariti. Hariti naturally learns Samarecarm, so we just need to make sure Bugs gets it.

text.Bugs: You the badass with the mask? C’mon dude, let’s play!

text.ACTION: Bugs, or the Bugbear, is the literal Boogeyman. It’s used by mothers to frighten their children into behaving.

text.Justine: I see you have brought us a Bugs with the skill Samarecarm ...

text.Caroline: Hmph. You make it seem easy. Well, the assignment is done...
So, uh ...  me and Justine had a little talk. I dunno how to put this ...  but we don’t know each other too well, even though we’re so close.

text.Justine: We have also come to realize that each of us complements the faults of the other quite nicely ...

text.Caroline: I don’t think I’ve ever had a deep convo like that with anyone before. Oh, and it made me remember something super important. I bet you wanna hear what that was. Isn’t that right, Inmate!?
The thing that I remembered ...  is something someone once told me. You explain it, Justine.

text.Justine: Essentially, the twenty-two arcana represent a journey ...  The Fool embarks on a pilgrimage through the numbers, overcoming Death and eventually obtaining the World. In short, this journey is the tale of one’s path through life.

text.Caroline: So we realized something. If this wild card thing—the potential of the Fool—proves that you’re a traveler ...

text.Justine: Then your becoming stronger will lead us all in the right direction. That may be the true meaning of rehabilitation. Or perhaps it is something beyond even that ...  Regardless, one thing we can be sure of is that this list was written with the intent of being completed.

text.Caroline: Understanding and having faith in that intent is the change this list has brought about in us.

Not that somebody like you would be able to comprehend that. But for us ...  it was something really important to learn. Oh, and ...  I think we might know who that voice in my head was too. I can’t tell you right now though.
First of all, we don’t have any way to actually prove it.

text.Justine: Secondly ...  if it is indeed true, everything we have come to know would be thrown into question. Regardless, we have grown able to reflect on ourselves thanks to you. This may not be something I should be saying to you ...  but I have quite enjoyed out time spent together.

text.Caroline: You hear that, Inmate!? You’d better overcome this ruin stuff! Keep surviving, all the way until we learn the truth ...  together!

text.Justine: We vow to do everything in our power to assist you ...  For the sake of your future, and our own.

text.Joker: I feel like my bond with Caroline and Justine is growing deeper...

text.Caroline: Don’t expect us to play nice just ‘cause we believe in you though! We’re gonna be as strict as ever!

text.Justine: Now then, it is time I assign you the final task before you receive your immensely powerful reward.
Please bring us a Seth with High Counter. Speak to us again once you have obtained it.

text.Mechanical Voice: Authentication complete. You can now access the following floors: The Standard Floor/The Members Floor.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It didn’t say nothing about the one for the manager ...

text.Goro Akechi: Well, the floors we have access to are limited by player ranking. That must mean the members floor is the highest we can go for now.

text.Futaba Sakura: It’s impossible to mess with the data on the card too. It’s nothing like the ones I’ve seen before.

text.Haru Okumura: So we can’t go directly to the manager’s floor ...  In that case, what exactly should we do?

text.Goro Akechi: Our first move should be to head upward. Either way, we have no more business on this floor.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You wanna just get this over with right now, huh? That makes this easy. Bring it on.

text.Shadow Sae Niijima: Do not speak to me as though you are my equal. I am the manager of this casino, as well as its number-one player. At the moment, you lack the qualifications to fight me.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It would seem she looks down on us.

text.ACTION: Got any more stunning insight to share with us, Councilor Troi?

text.Goro Akechi: And what if we would like to battle you, no matter what?

text.ACTION: Uh, we’re not actually here to fight her, guys. We’re supposed to at least pretend the boss fight isn’t mandatory.

text.Shadow Sae Niijima: I had to win time and time again in order to reach my number-one rank. If you want to face me, you must continue to win as well.

text.Haru Okumura: Continue to win ... ?

text.Goro Akechi: It must have to do with the fact that this place is a casino.

text.Shadow Sae Niijima: Correct. Do you have the confidence to win ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: We might just pull the rug out from underneath you if you aren’t careful.

text.Shadow Sae Niijima: I don’t expect much from you ...  but I’ll be waiting.

text.Futaba Sakura: It’s going up ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I wasn’t expecting to come all the way to a Palace only to end up gambling ...

text.Ann Takamaki: What about you guys?

text.ACTION: The group looks around at each other.

text.Morgana: Looks like this is going to take longer than expected.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We don’t got time to waste!

text.Goro Akechi: No need to worry. Leave this to me.

text.Makoto Niijima: You know how to do this?

text.Goro Akechi: I’m well-informed on what it takes to win. In any case, we need to hurry and change her heart. If she acts recklessly, both her chances of promotion and reputation as a prosecutor will drop greatly. Sae-san didn’t use to be like this, did she?

text.Makoto Niijima: My sister must have lost her sense of justice because her desires became distorted ...

text.Goro Akechi: Do you think there was a particular event that triggered her Palace’s creation?

text.Makoto Niijima: ...I believe it’s related to my father’s death. My sister took on all the responsibilities of dealing with it herself. Trying to earn a living wage, gain a promotion in a male society, and uphold justice at the same time ...  Those things may have weighed her down and led to the distortion within her heart.

text.Goro Akechi: ...My apologies, but we don’t have time to be sentimental. The longer we wait, the more people will learn about us. The investigation will advance as well. Hence, we must infiltrate this Palace as quickly as possible.

text.Morgana: She did challenge us to reach her, after all. Niijima’s Treasure must be at her managerial base of operations. Either way, we have to get there!

text.ACTION: Well, we’ll see what else this Palace has in store next time. But that doesn’t mean we’re done here for today! Now that Akechi’s joined our party, we can do something I’ve been anticipating for a while!
See, for 60 real US dollars, you can buy a pack of all the DLC costumes off the PlayStation Network! And I’m an idiot, so of course I decided to buy it for the sake of showing it off in this LP!

By going to the “Outfits” section of the Equipment menu, we can put on outfits that change our appearance. This does nothing to affect our stats, but that doesn’t mean nothing changes. We’ll go into what that means in a later episode!
Now, without further ado, it’s time for the…

Yes, I’m putting on something of a fashion show here! We’ll be covering the basic set of costumes in today’s appearance. Hope you like awkward camera angles and shit-ass JPG compression, because those are the real stars tonight!

Why, it’s the incredibly stylish Phantom Thieves! Well… mostly stylish. Poor Akechi here probably thinks he looks cool as hell, while I’m just thinking “I hope he doesn’t rip his band uniform.” He also breaks the male trend of cool, impractically large collars. Gotta say I don’t understand Makoto’s antipathy for her outfit, it’s dope and the cape (not visible here, sadly) rules. Haru’s might be my favorite, though, especially with the ammo belt. Why does Ann’s costume have a boob window? Yusuke’s weird tail always makes me laugh, by the way. I’m also less sure how much I like the pirate look for Ryuji the more I see it.
This is also Morgana’s only costume for today’s show, but look forward to his appearance changing in future installments.

Maaku goes for the standard look, but pulls it off. There have been many jokes made in the past about how Ryuji’s shirt here says “HOMO RULES” instead of “NO MO,” and I can only say I approve. Gotta wonder how Haru manages to have a totally unique uniform for both seasons without the faculty complaining, but she pulls it off. Makoto also manages to make a fairly standard uniform her own. Akechi loses points for his tie clipping into his shirt, sadly. All I can say about Yusuke is that Kosei’s purple shirt for the summer uniform is cool as hell.

Maaku is the only person in the game who looks good in the Shujin turtleneck, which unfortunately kind of includes Makoto. She makes up for it though with her… vest? Whatever the hell that is, it’s nice. I like how Ryuji just lets the suspenders hang out of his pants. Ann’s hoodie is dope and if I was a girl I would buy one. Maybe I will anyway. Haru’s sweater is goddamn adorable and I will not hear otherwise. Are the gloves a standard part of the uniform of whatever school Akechi goes to? The fleur-de-lis on Yusuke’s shirt is pretty cool I guess.

Maaku, rocking that watch, nice. Ryuji’s shirt seems to say “ON U R MARK” instead of “UR,” but okay. I like the sunglasses clipped onto Ann’s shirt there, and the shirt wrapped around her shorts. Haru’s unfortunately looking rather plain. Futaba’s got a cool shirt, but the person playing Tetris on it really needs to step up their game. Really like Makoto’s blouse here. That shirt is not doing you any favors, Yusuke buddy.

Like the v-neck, Maaku. Not liking Ryuji’s hoodie so much, it’s a little gaudy, though that’s just him I guess. Ann’s wearing like a letterman jacket or something, which is an odd fit for her. Please cover up, Futaba, and I don’t just mean that because you’re probably really cold not wearing your jacket on your actual shoulders. Haru and Makoto both look nice in their coats. Akechi’s sweater-vest just cements his dork status, though. Nice jacket, Yusuke.

Now we get to the awkward part of this where I review a bunch of teenagers’ swimsuits… yeah, pass. I only included this in the first place because we haven’t seen Haru’s yet. Though Yusuke’s hoodie is real silly and I appreciate it.
Really like both of these outfits, but what in the goddamn hell is “JL MK !”?

Part 152: 11/13: 6500 Miles To Graceland
	Part 143: 11/13: 6500 Miles To Graceland
I’m glad this song is good, because outside of the occasional switch to Last Surprise for a battle, it’s all I hear for most of this Palace!

text.Goro Akechi: It should be quite clear. We must play in the casino and win. Customers are divided into the different floors based on the rank of their play. If we wish to enter a higher floor, we will need to increase our rank.

text.Futaba Sakura: So that means we gotta win and gain the right to head up. And as I mentioned earlier, a different kinda member’s card is used depending on your rank. We’ll have to obtain a card for the high limit floor somewhere around here.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: For real!? Ugh, what a pain!

text.Goro Akechi: Why don’t we begin by walking around this floor? That should be a good method of gaining intel.

text.ACTION: This room is fairly empty outside of some treasure spots, the cashier’s desk up ahead...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So all of this is going according to her plan ...  I cannot help but feel we’re being manipulated here.

text.Casino Shadow: First, we will be providing you with a welcome gift. Please accept these coins.

text.ACTION: We receive 1000 coins and a handy/gaudy counter to keep track of them that will stay onscreen all the time outside of cutscenes and battles so we don’t ever forget whose rules we’re playing by!

text.Ann Takamaki: He’s just giving them to us!?

text.Goro Akechi: Perhaps this is a show of confidence. It seems she truly has no intention of losing.

text.Casino Shadow: Now then, to the left of the counter is the dice game area, while to the right are the slots. Please head to whichever strikes your fancy.
Furthermore ...  this is a map of the members floor. Please accept it.

text.Haru Okumura: That means we should probably start with the dice game ...  right?

text.Casino Shadow: Ah, one more thing. Casino coins can be exchanged for prizes at this very counter. Please feel free to ask us about this service.

text.Morgana: Prizes? What do you think we can get from there ... ?

text.Casino Shadow: Our most desired prize is a member’s card for entry into the high limit floor. However, the price of exchange for this item is 50,000 coins.

text.Goro Akechi: I see ...  I believe I have figured out Sae-san’s intent behind this.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That’s absurd! 50,000 coins!?

text.Casino Shadow: (chuckle) We also allow players to borrow coins if need be, up to the current total on their card.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I don’t wanna do that! Owin’ cash to a weird-ass casino inside someone’s head is way too scary!

text.Morgana: Oh well ...  Standing around here won’t get us anywhere. So, should we head to this dice game?

text.Goro Akechi: Actually, do you mind if I speak to you all beforehand? There is something on my mind.
It would not surprise me in the least if they were rigged somehow.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You think she’s cheatin’!?

text.Goro Akechi: Remember, this is a courthouse in the real world. Sae-san is quite particular about "winning" here. To compound that, defendants in Japan are prosecuted at a rate of 99.9%. Victory is nigh unattainable.

text.Ann Takamaki: What!? How can a percentage like that really be possible? Are all those verdicts the correct ones?

text.Goro Akechi: Not exactly ...  The investigators are human too, after all.

text.Ann Takamaki: Then ...

text.Goro Akechi: You are not the first to poijnt out the rigged nature of this system. The prosecution is near unbeatable. That’s why cases of false accusation cause such a stir: They are exceedingly rare.

text.ACTION: I think this is supposed to say "cases of exoneration" or something similar. "Cases of false accusation" implies that people being falsely accused is rare, rather than people being found innocent. Also, that still sounds awkward, but hell, it ain’t my job to fix this.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: But it’s total bullshit gettin’ arrested even when you’re not guilty!

text.Goro Akechi: Indeed, and if we do not hurry, the Phantom Thieves will fall victim to a similar fate.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...We’re going to win this, no matter what.

text.ACTION: Now that we’ve regained control, let’s head for the dice area. First though, we see this present. The presents are a little different from ordinary treasure spots.
Grabbing one will give us 100, 150, or 200 coins on the spot. It’s nifty but ultimately totally unnecessary unless you completely fuck up somehow.

text.Ann Takamaki: Y-Yeah, I guess ...  That’s not really how a normal high schooler would describe it though ...

text.ACTION: Yusuke’s a good boy, Ann. Don’t try to change him.

text.Makoto Niijima: In any case, we should proceed further in.

text.ACTION: First, let’s head into one of the dice rooms.

text.Casino Shadow: Please enjoy this simple game in which you guess the total number that will appear on three cast dice. A correct prediction will double your bet, while three matching dice will triple it. Most importantly, matching sixes is a supreme victory! Regardless of what your initial bet was, the payout will be quintuple that! Buy-in for this game is only 25 casino coins. Would you like to play?
Would you like to continue playing?

text.Joker: Continue

text.ACTION: What is it, Akechi? I feel a hot streak coming up!

text.Ann Takamaki: Wait, you mean cheating ... ?

text.Goro Akechi: Even if we continue playing here, there is no chance of victory. We should retreat for the time being.

text.Haru Okumura: But we won’t be able to earn coins if we don’t play.

text.Goro Akechi: Yes, that is exactly why we will stop them from rigging the game. Considering the scale of this operation, I doubt they are cheating via analog methods. I expect there is a control room of sorts that determines the win percentages for the entire area.

text.Morgana: So that’s where we’ll strike. All right, let’s go look for anywhere that seems suspicious!

text.ACTION: After reloading to keep my coin count pristine because I’m incredibly dumb like that, we find this vent on the north wall.

text.Futaba Sakura: Super convenient, don’tcha think? Anyway, based on what Crow was saying, the games in here are all totally rigged.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Oooh, so we’re gonna catch ‘em in the act! I guess that’s easy ...  C’mon, let’s get to it!

text.ACTION: This Ganesha has the same attacks its boss form did last update, but it’s weak to Psy this time around.
Queen Mab here is also near-identical to its boss form from the last update, including its Wind weakness.

Climate Decorum is a skill for Haru that doubles her evasion against all skills during Pollen, Rain, or Flu. It’s decent enough but we’re probably not going to get a chance to use it with Akechi subbed in for her. We slot it in for Fast Heal anyway.
(We’re not a fifth. The game doesn’t recognize that we’ve progressed since reaching the beginning of this floor, and even still that’s a really low estimate that makes me suspect they cut something)
Further in, Ryuji learns Elec Boost to replace Deathbound. His Electric attacks are now 25% stronger.

Subrecover SP restores 1% of the backup party’s SP after battle. This is clearly not enough to really rely on even just as an incentive to switch between party members, but it does mean we can now Auto-Recover with impunity because Morgana and Ann will recover most of what they lose if we don’t take a lot of hits.
Akechi also learns Attack Master to replace Kouga. Attack Master gives him Tarukaja at the start of battle, and it’s pretty useful. Weird that he gets it instead of Ryuji, though.
We also run into this Treasure Demon, Orlov. At this point I’m saving most of my bullets for Oda’s Down Shot to use on Treasure Demons or pesky enemies without weaknesses.
And we make it to the control room.

text.Makoto Niijima: So this is the cheating control room ...  What should we do, Joker?

text.Goro Akechi: Very well. Let us dispatch it swiftly.

text.ACTION: Bullet Hail on a miniboss always feels nice.
This dude is weak to Bless and goes down right quick.
Morgana learns Diarahan, which fully heals one ally, to replace Diarama.
Ann learns Burn Boost to replace Dormina. We haven’t used Dormina since Kamoshida’s Palace, and while it was handy there we don’t really need it now.
Yusuke learns Masukukaja to replace Sukukaja. Sukukaja is kind of lame. Masukukaja is fucking awesome and well worth a skill slot.
Makoto finally learns Freidyne to replace Freila.

text.Futaba Sakura: C’mon, we should stop the rigging.

text.Goro Akechi: Hold on a moment, I have an idea I’d like to discuss.

text.ACTION: Oh god, where did the rest of you come from!?

text.Goro Akechi: I’ve devised an easier way of doing this ...  A way to get all the coins we need.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: All of them in here?

text.Ann Takamaki: Is that even possible ... ?

text.Goro Akechi: It is now. I’ve deduced how to win the games.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You can do that!?

text.Futaba Sakura: Wait, this is a job for me! It’ll be a breeze!

text.Haru Okumura: Cheating seems somehow wrong though ...

text.Goro Akechi: The odds here are stacked against us. We would never win if we stuck to normal methods. We do not have any time to waste either. It would be best for us to focus on our objective.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...You’re right. Changing my sister[‘s heart is the ultimate goal here.

text.Goro Akechi: I feel bad asking this, but may we borrow your expertise yet another time, Oracle?

text.Futaba Sakura: I’m game! But man, you sure give a lot of orders for a noob!
The other rooms should at least be back to normal honest gambling now too. Anyway, I marked our special room on the map. Make sure you use that one!

text.Goro Akechi: Perfect. Now, let us head into the fray.

text.ACTION: Let’s head over to the marked room, then.

text.Casino Shadow: Both buy-in and payout are five times the normal amount! A single customer is limited to four plays!
The buy-in is 125 coins! Would you like to play the game?
Would you like to continue playing?

text.Goro Akechi: Of course.

text.Casino Shadow: Excellent, sir. Please predict the next sum.
Would you like to continue playing?

text.Ann Takamaki: You bet we do!

text.Casino Shadow: In that case, please predict the next sum!

text.Futaba Sakura: We can play one more time, right? We’re gonna keep it rolling!

text.Casino Shadow: U-Understood, ma’am ...  P-Please predict the next sum ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hot damn! We got a shitton of coins in like, no time!

text.Goro Akechi: We’ve retrieved the device. Our next move is up to you, Joker.

text.ACTION: Wait, what device? What the hell are you talking about?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I thought we were done winnin’ here. Wanna go somewhere else?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Have we reached our goal?

text.Goro Akechi: It still may not be enough.

text.Morgana: Are you seriously planning on taking every last coin in here?

text.Goro Akechi: Ahaha, it was a joke. However, it would be nice to have a little more coinage on hand, would it not? Everyone wait here. Skull, I would like you to come with me.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Why me?

text.Goro Akechi: Because I am the "brains" here, am I not?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Oh, sure.

text.Morgana: ...Time to see what he’s made of.

text.Haru Okumura: That was amazing! It was like magic!

text.Ann Takamaki: I could totally get addicted to this!

text.Morgana: Where are Crow and Skull?

text.Makoto Niijima: Whoa ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So ...  heavy ...

text.ACTION: They just give you another 3000 coins because we need a certain amount for the next section. I guess Akechi rigged a different table? With the “device?”

text.Goro Akechi: We still have a long way before we reach our goal though. Now then, on to the slot machines.

text.Casino Shadow 2: Here you will be playing a game that requires you to match the patterns on the rotating wheels.

text.Makoto Niijima: We’re here to win coins, not to play your game.

text.Casino Shadow 2: I am well aware of that. Though to be perfectly honest ...  I’ve been granted permission to kill every last one of you here.

text.ACTION: These guys are weak to Nuke, and their only skill is Wage War, which inflicts Rage on the entire party. They’re chumps, though Akechi isn’t that useful since they Null Bless and Reflect Curse. I do learn in the process though that if an enemy reflects your own weakness back at you, you don’t get knocked down.

text.Ann Takamaki: Wait, why didn’t the guests around us react to that battle?

text.Goro Akechi: It is probably due to Sae-san’s perception of the other people in the courtroom. Perhaps as she sees it, they only care for their own victory, while ignoring the needs of others.

text.Makoto Niijima: That reaction is certainly different from what we saw on the lower floor. I wonder if that trend grows stronger the higher up you go in the court system.

text.Goro Akechi: It is possible. In any case, we can now freely access the Slot Room. We should go look around. ...Although I doubt we will find a fair fight waiting for us in this scamming casino.
I would expect they’re all rigged to prevent us from ever winning.

text.Morgana: Then should we deal with that first?

text.Goro Akechi: No, I believe it would be prudent to examine this slot area further. Casinos hold their higher-limit slots somewhere in the back. If we were going to circumvent their trick, would it not be more efficient to do so on those?

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s assuming we’ll even be able to solve the problem.

text.Goro Akechi: I trust in your ability to handle such a matter.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: A-Aight, let’s go look for that sweet, sweet slot machine!

text.ACTION: Near the entrance, we come across this terminal.

text.Ann Takamaki: Can you mess with it and figure out how they’re cheating, Oracle?

text.Futaba Sakura: Wellll ...  this one’s on standby. Uh, basically I’m gonna have to activate it remotely from a main terminal somewhere else.

text.Goro Akechi: So this one is useless unless we can access the main hub. Oh well. We should at least commit this place to memory for now.

text.ACTION: Off in the distance there we can see a tasteful bunny girl. Like in Madarame’s Palace, the female-variant Shadows don’t give chase, but instead summon additional Shadows upon spotting you.
The lady in the middle should be familiar—she’s a Kushinada, and we’ve already summoned one of her. She uses Matarukaja to boost her party’s attack and Mabufula to deal Ice damage.

These guys are Kumbhandas, and while they’re still only able to cast Wage War, their resistances are a little different—instead of Null Bless, Repel Curse, and a Nuke weakness, they’re weak to Ice and merely resist Curse (though they also Null Fire).

text.Casino Security Guard: Let him feel like he’s on a winning streak, then make him lose big on the final round.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Tch, they’re tellin’ the dealers how to rig the games ...

text.Goro Akechi: We anticipated as much.

text.ACTION: Earlier I said I’d show off the animation for Eigaon, and while I might gif it later, here’s the meat of it. It’s dope.

text.Goro Akechi: This must be the main hall of the slot room.

text.ACTION: Eventually, we make it into the main hall.

text.Ann Takamaki: Wait, all cherries wins you 5,000 coins, BAR gets you 10,000, while a 777 gives you 50,000!? Whoa! That’ll get us all the coins we need in one fell swoop!

text.Morgana: Assuming we can win, that is. If the reward’s high, the risk will surely be high as well.

text.Goro Akechi: Either way, our goal here is to gain a member’s card for the high limit floor. It would make the most sense for us to utilize this slot machine in some way, shape, or form. However ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Lemme guess, "We will need to stop their cheating first"? There’s no doubt this one’s rigged too.

text.Goro Akechi: Haha, I’m glad you understand. Now then, let us search the area. Hopefully we will find something that can give us a little more information about this slot.

text.Futaba Sakura: There’s prolly a terminal for info back behind the thing. Try looking there, Joker.
Mweheheh ...  Let’s see ...  ...Wow, they’re going really hard on this whole cheating angle. We wouldn’t have won a penny here.

text.Makoto Niijima: Do you think you’ll be able to disable their rigging of it?

text.Futaba Sakura: Not from this terminal. It looks like there are multiple different-colored control panels throughout this area. Out of those, I’ll need the red and green ones. I should be able to control things from there.

text.Makoto Niijima: Do you know where we can find them though?

text.Futaba Sakura: Uh, you know this is me we’re talking about, right? I can predict where they might be. One’s most likely near the entrance to this area. The comm link ran all the way out there. The other should be back in the staff passageway ...  somewhere. That’s all I can figure out.

text.Goro Akechi: Hm, so the entrance to the slot room ...  and some location tucked away in the staff passageway ...

text.Morgana: I guess we’ll just have to go looking for them! Let’s hurry up and get this done fast!

text.ACTION: So, the wording here is a little confusing. When Futaba said “the entrance to this area,” I on my first run thought that meant “this room,” and didn’t know why the panel wasn’t here. It’s simple enough to check, though. That first panel we found is one of the ones we’re looking for here, so let’s go.

text.Ann Takamaki: That means we just need to find the green panel now. Let’s go!

text.ACTION: As for the green panel ...  my first run, I got stuck on this for maybe half an hour. See, I just couldn’t find it, backtracking everywhere. I even went back to the backroom of the dice area, thinking that maybe they were trying to trick me. Well, they were. Just not like that.
Hidden behind these crates to the left...

Why, it’s a treasure chest and the panel! The issue wasn’t that I didn’t know about this area, by the way. It’s marked on the map, after all. The issue is that the panel is infuriatingly hidden on a wall you have no reason to look at unless you’re coming from an absurd angle.

text.Futaba Sakura: Gotcha! We’ll be done after this.

text.Goro Akechi: ...Hold on.
Oracle, would it be possible to also tamper with the average win percentages for the slot machines?

text.Makoto Niijima: So you want to take advantage of the system, just like we did for the dice game.

text.Goro Akechi: Essentially. My aim here is the giant slot machine.

text.Ann Takamaki: You mean the one that’s 5,000 coins a play!? I don’t know if that’s really possible ... !

text.Futaba Sakura: Oooh, sounds like fun to me. Just gimme a sec.
The giant one’s still only on an 8:2 ratio though. There’s honestly no guarantee it’ll work properly.

text.ACTION: Yep, that’s just about on the same level of fucked as everything else in our lives.

text.Haru Okumura: Does that mean it will miss two times out of ten? That’s somewhat concerning ...

text.Goro Akechi: It should be fine. Nothing the Phantom Thieves do can ever be truly considered risk-free, after all. If we want to succeed, we simply have no other choice but this.

text.Makoto Niijima: That seems like a sound argument to me. Very well, let’s leave this to Joker then.

text.Ann Takamaki: I-I wonder if we’ll actually manage to score that 50,000 ...

text.Morgana: She’s right. There’s a 20% chance the rig won’t work, and even if we win, it might not be enough.

text.Goro Akechi: This is a big gamble, Joker. Are you sure about this?
50,000 coins, hm? ...You truly are special, Joker.

text.ACTION: You ever watch this video where two Australian dudes win the double jackpot at this Japanese arcade not-pachinko game and it’s just nonstop coins raining down for like, multiple minutes? That’s what this reminds me of.

text.Chatter: Hey, doesn’t that sound like a jackpot to you?
What!? Who got it?

text.Goro Akechi: It is no surprise the customers are reacting to this commotion. We should leave for now.

text.Ann Takamaki: But what about the coins!?

text.Makoto Niijima: Those are just for show. The actual coin total has already been added to our card.

text.ACTION: Then why was Ryuji pushing around that fucking cart full of coins earlier!?
Akechi’s got the gambling madness in his eyes.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: You wish to win more coins? I’m pretty sure we have enough.

text.Goro Akechi: More is always better than less. Then again, I suppose we are already good to go.

text.Morgana: That’s right ...  We have 50,000 coins now! Let’s go exchange them for a member’s card to the high limit floor!

text.ACTION: We head back to the counter.
While we’re here, we have enough to buy yet another Soma (full HP and SP restore to all allies) as well as a Bead Chain (full HP restore to all allies). They’re both well worth it.
We also pick up the High Limit Card. Eh.

text.Goro Akechi: I hope I was able to contribute in some meaningful way. Come, let us head over to the elevator.

text.Morgana: They’re greeting us in front of the elevator? This doesn’t give off a welcoming vibe though ...

text.Goro Akechi: This must be due to the instigation of Sae-san. We should be prepared to fight.
We merely followed your rules.

text.Shadow Sae Niijima: Hmph! I am the manager of this casino, and the rules deem that I am the victor!

text.Goro Akechi: It appears both the Sae-san of the real world and that of this world are at their wit’s end ...

text.Shadow Sae Niijima: ...I think our guests will be leaving now.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: You’re the only one who’s gonna be leaving, black suit!

text.Morgana: Things would’ve been so much simpler if we could do this from the start!

text.ACTION: This enemy Drains Wind, uses Ziodyne and Garudyne, and can use Diarahan to heal itself to full. If only it had enough health to survive a full round, especially after Akechi gets a lucky crit on it...

text.Shadow Sae Niijima: Criminal trials are but a gamble to be won, and us prosecutors arrange the gambling table. Hence, losses are unacceptable! We must win, even if it has to be on false charges!

text.Makoto Niijima: Are you serious, Sis!?

text.Haru Okumura: Mako-chan ...

text.Shadow Sae Niijima: Don’t think such a petty trick could defeat me. I may have to acknowledge your skills—if you can make it up to the manager’s floor, that is.

text.Goro Akechi: I wish I didn’t have to hear that from Sae-san herself ...

text.Makoto Niijima: Sis is completely distorted! We have to stop her, quickly!

text.Haru Okumura: We all feel the same way.

text.Morgana: There’s no time to waste. She mentioned something about a manager’s floor, right? Let’s try heading up there. We’ll change Niijima-san’s heart for sure.

text.Mechanical Voice: You can now access the following floors: The Standard Floor./The Members Floor./The High Limit Floor.

text.Futaba Sakura: But she’s so close I can almost smell her now. The next floor’s prolly gonna be the last one.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Welp, let’s get on up to the high limit floor!

text.ACTION: All right, during tonight’s Phashion Phrenzy, we’re taking a look back through Persona history! We’ll be looking through costumes from every main game in the series, as well as some related titles. It’s also worth pointing out that whenever Maaku wears an outfit from a different game, the battle music changes from Last Surprise to a track from the respective game! I’ll be including those songs as well here. The victory themes change too, but those are more incidental (read: I’m too lazy).
This track is the main battle theme from the PSP remake of the first Persona game. Don’t play that game, it’s not very good.
God we look like such fucking nerds noooooooo! What’s with the outrageously huge tie for the girls!? Morgana is dressed up as Trish, a fairy from Persona 1 who charged you to heal.
This track is the main battle theme from the Persona 2: Innocent Sin remake for PSP. That game is better than Persona 1 but still utterly impenetrable and totally irrelevant to modern Persona.
Much better already. Kinda flat, but still stylish. Morgana is dressed up as Trish once again, while Akechi is dressed up as a student from Kasugayama High School, probably Jun.
This track is the main battle theme for the vanilla, FES, and male route of P3P versions of Persona 3. This is a great song but I would have killed for them to have included Wiping All Out.
I like this outfit on these characters more than I liked it in actual Persona 3. The Evokers are also a nice touch. Morgana is dressed up as Aigis, the real main character of that game.
This track is the normal battle theme of Persona 4 Golden. I’m glad it’s this one because I’m so fucking sick of Reach Out To The Truth, you have no idea.
Nice glasses, everyone. Morgana is dressed up as Teddie, naturally. Also the way Akechi wears his uniform is a clear callback to Naoto, hah.
This track was remixed for SMT III: Nocturne and most people probably know it from there.

I like the uniform, but I know absolutely nothing about Shin Megami Tensei if..., and it wasn’t localized. Great pull, Atlus. Morgana appears to be ...  Raidou Kuzunoha? This game was an inspiration for the high school setting of the Persona series, and other elements like the Arm PCs seem to have inspired other games like SMTIV.
This track plays in the third stage of Babel, Obelisk. I never got past the first stage, rip.

Part 153: 11/13-11/14: The Pointless Interlude
	Part 144: 11/13-11/14: The Pointless Interlude
Ah, we’ve made it to the high limit floor. Now it’s just a straight shot to--

text.Casino Shadow: Beyond this point is the high limit floor. Do you have a reservation?

text.Casino Shadow: Do you have a reservation?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Even though we got the coins?

text.Ann Takamaki: I can’t imagine how though ...

text.Goro Akechi: Her cognition ... ? Essentially, Sae-san needs to think of us as being allowed to enter, correct? Hm. This casino is the courthouse in reality ...  So that floor must be a place only authorized personnel are given access to ...  ...I would say it has to be the courtroom.

text.Ann Takamaki: You really are an ace detective.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: He’s come to understand the workings of the cognitive world so quickly.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I was just like that too, right?

text.Morgana: It took you ages to get it, Ryuji.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I just ...  got a different sense of time, that’s all!

text.Futaba Sakura: Ryuji! Go piss off the police!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hell no!

text.Makoto Niijima: We just need to attend a trial. Still, how are we supposed to know which trials my sister will be attending ... ?

text.Goro Akechi: Leave that to me. I have some connections that come to mind. I will contact you once I manage to arrange a time. We should return to the real world for today though. Well, see you all at the courtroom.

text.ACTION: Ah, so we come to another cognition block. Not counting Futaba’s because that didn’t actually impede our day-to-day progress, this is the second one… of two. Yep. What a great, involved gameplay mechanic.

text.Nav: Now returning to the real world from Niijima’s Palace. Thank you for your hard work.

text.Morgana: It feels like we’re fairly close to the Treasure now. There’s no doubt we’re nearing the end.

text.Makoto Niijima: I wonder how much we still have left ...  There’s a chance we’ll run into powerful enemies ahead ...  Or maybe I’m worrying too much ...  Well, I’ll be waiting to hear from you about our next venture.

text.Haru Okumura: I’m surprised she’s taking part in court at a time like this ...  She must be busy with the Phantom Thieves investigation as well ...

text.Goro Akechi: She is originally a public prosecutor, after all.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That’s gotta be tough...

text.Goro Akechi: She may be our enemy, but I do sympathize with her in this regard.

text.Makoto Niijima: Our enemy ...

text.Goro Akechi: Oh, my apologies. That’s not quite what I meant.

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s OK. You were just telling the truth. Anyway, we’ll need to act tomorrow, right? Thanks for letting us know.

text.Goro Akechi: You’re most welcome. At any rate, let us meet on-site after school tomorrow.

text.ACTION: Yep! We’re heading straight into the Palace tomorrow! We don’t even get a choice! Why did they even make us leave?

text.Sadayo Kawakami: Fineee ...  I’ll have you know I trained while working in Victoria. My skills are amazing. OK, I’ll head over right now, so just wait for me.

text.Souse: Th-The Phantom Thievesh! They’re ...  They’re hereeeee! Pl-Pleash don’t kill me! I wanna live! I wanna live! Urp ...

text.Burly Officer: (sigh) Everyone’s so scared ...  I guess people would be worried since we haven’t caught them yet.

text.Souse: Do not worry! I, Shido, will lead you! I’mma take care of ev’rything!

text.Beefy Trendsetter: Do you know how much harm they’ve caused to people? They’re terrorists, I tell you! And you can’t count on the police. It’s time for the great detective Akechi to shine!

text.Scruffy Romantic: Where has he been, anyway? I haven’t seen him on TV at all lately ...

text.Elderly Office Worker: ...You think so? I believe the final outcome is a foregone conclusion. The new political party will definitely win. Their leader is a master of media.

text.Earnest Office Worker: I see ...  Although it IS a national election, which is basically a popular vote ...

text.Munehisa Iwai: There’s somethin’ I gotta ask you to do. You’re free now, yeah?
...Kaoru wants to talk to you. Hold on; I’ll call him over.

text.Kaoru: I learned a lot about myself, so ...  I just wanted to show my appreciation.

text.Munehisa Iwai: Hmph ...  Intruding in on another private family moment.

text.Kaoru: You’re still droning on about that? I mean, it was quite a shock ...  but that’s what made you take me in, right? So who cares?

text.Munehisa Iwai: Whoa there, kiddo ...

text.Kaoru: If you had just told me all of this sooner, you wouldn’t have been threatened.

text.Munehisa Iwai: Who your parents are and where you come from stays with you for your entire life. Thanks to my loser parents, I got bullied by complete strangers, and--

text.Kaoru: My father isn’t a loser though! He’s a brilliant business owner.

text.ACTION: “Brilliant” is a word, sure. I’d probably use “mad sketchy,” myself.

text.Munehisa Iwai: Stop tryin’ to ruin the moment. (sigh) So in the end, I was just fightin’ my own demons ...  Stuck in my crappy childhood and all the problems I had growin’ up ...  My view of Kaoru was all distorted ...  ‘cause of my rotten childhood memories.

text.Kaoru: I forgive you.
Why did you help my father out?
You willingly got involved in a yakuza dispute ...  Would someone normally take that big of a risk?
Hmmm ...  I’d understand if you were a member of the Phantom Thieves.

text.ACTION: Goddammit, I am so bad at hiding this!

text.Kaoru: Fighting for the underdogs ...  like a gentleman thief, you know? People have their own opinions, but ...  I think the Phantom Thieves are super cool! I mean, the sexual harassment incident involving that teacher?

text.ACTION: “And all that murder they did? So cool!”

text.Munehisa Iwai: We gotta go, Kaoru. The supermarket’s about to close. Aren’t you in charge of dinner tonight?

text.Kaoru: Oh crap! Please excuse me!

text.Munehisa Iwai: Kids grow up quick. They can be a pain in the ass, but they’re worth it. ...All right, let’s close up shop. Go pull down the shutter.
Seems like he had a change of heart, just like them people they’ve been talkin’ about on TV.
I can’t be the only one who was saved by his change of heart. Wonder who else knows ...

Heh, if you say so. Well, don’t worry. It ain’t really none of my concern. Man, you really had me fooled. That whole thing about being an enthusiast was all just BS. I hired you as a mere pawn ...  and now you’re Kaoru’s bro ...

text.ACTION: Oh, just dropping any pretense. Okay.

text.Munehisa Iwai: (chuckle) Interesting ...  All right, I’m gonna put all my effort into that special menu we talked about.

text.Joker: (nod)

text.Munehisa Iwai: I don’t like to owe nobody nothin’, so I’ll do my best for ya. ...Because that’s the kinda support I can provide.

text.Joker: I feel a strong bond with Iwai...

text.ACTION: Iwai is cool. It’s just kind of a shame his Confidant is shockingly boring even with all its yakuza intrigue and the fact that his Confidant bonuses are, as you might have guessed from my repeated unfulfilled promises to utilize them, kind of useless. He’s voiced by Kaiji Tang, a guy I’m liking more and more. He mainly plays really gruff characters with similar intonations, but he’s actually got way more range than that.

text.Munehisa Iwai: And the knives are just replicas. They’re even less useful than a butter knife, y’know?
...We were in the middle of closing shop, weren’t we? Well, let’s get to it.

text.Joker: I feel like helping Iwai with his work has honed my Proficiency...

text.Munehisa Iwai: Later.

text.Morgana: Old movie posters are kind of scary. Maybe it’s the color ...
It talked about movie techniques in such great detail. It really makes you appreciate film more ...  You know, we should go to the movie theater sometime!

Apparently Cinema Treasures also stacks with Luck Reading so a first viewing can get boosted to 7 points, which can then be boosted to 10. We didn’t watch many movies though, so this wasn’t really worth reading earlier. The documentation on this one is kind of iffy but I’m pretty sure that’s how it works.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Just being here causes my body to tense up.

text.Haru Okumura: I’m shocked that Niijima-san can think of somewhere this solemn as a casino ...

text.Futaba Sakura: So Makoto’s sis is that lady who’s overflowing with the aura of a capable woman.

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Mm-hm.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: By the way, what’s this trial about?

text.Futaba Sakura: I read about that in a magazine! He went on a vacation with his mistress to some fancy hot springs!
