text.Sae Niijima: I gathered the best of the best and fought for a case ...  but as Makoto must’ve told you, it was denied. At this rate, it won’t end with just Shido’s innocence. This trend will continue spiraling down. There’s even the possibility that crimes using the Metaverse will advance onto a national scale.
...But, that’s not what I’m here to tell you. We’re in danger because we know the truth. It’s only a matter of time before we’re apprehended. It wouldn’t be odd if they were to charge in now.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This makes no effin’ sense ...

text.Makoto Niijima: Sis ...

text.Sae Niijima: There’s nothing more I can do with my resources ...  That’s why ...  I want to ask for your help. I wondered if there was any way you could do something one last time. I know that I’m in no position to ask this of you.

text.Ann Takamaki: That doesn’t matter to us! So what are we gonna do? Should we change the hearts of all Shido’s followers?

text.Makoto Niijima: Even if Futaba were to research all of them, it’d take time.

text.Futaba Sakura: There’s too little information ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We can only target individuals ...  Are we no match against the national power?

text.Morgana: ... If we use Mementos, we might be able to do something.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: There’s something we can do there?

text.Morgana: Like I told you before, Mementos is the Palace of the general public. It’s the source of all distortions, and is maintained by the people’s "collective unconsciousness."

text.Makoto Niijima: Wait ...  Do you mean that there’s a Treasure even in Mementos!? And if we go after that--

text.Morgana: The collapse of Mementos should affect the public as a whole. The state of society would change too. If everyone’s hearts grow to hold Shido responsible for his actions, things might start going our way.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...That’s a bold plan, but an interesting one.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Sounds good to me!

text.ACTION: I wish the game played this up instead of having Sojiro and Sae just standing here stonefaced with nothing to say while we have a long conversation with this cat they can’t understand.

text.Morgana: ...But if we’re gonna do this, there’s one thing you all need to realize.
To begin with, why does something like the human cognition exist as another, substantial world? The reason for that is most likely sleeping within Mementos. ...We’ll be destroying that, you know.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: ...I don’t see where you’re goin’ with this.

text.Morgana: So if other criminals appear, you won’t be able to steal their Treasure and change their hearts.

text.ACTION: The Phantom Thieves look at each other.

text.Haru Okumura: We’ll have to discard this way of life ...

text.Ann Takamaki: I think we need to do this. I mean, we’re the group who’s reforming society, right?

text.Morgana: Maaku ...  What do you think as our leader? You’ll lose your powers if Mementos is erased. Will you still do it?

text.Ann Takamaki: Yeah, that’s right!

text.Morgana: You guys have all grown, huh? ...All right.

text.Sae Niijima: Did you come up with a plan?

text.Makoto Niijima: Whether is succeeds or not is another story though.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Miss Prosecutor ...  looks like this is gonna be our last job.

text.Sae Niijima: Last job ... ?

text.Haru Okumura: Once we accomplish our duty, we entrust the world to respectful adults.

text.ACTION: That seems like a bad idea!

text.Haru Okumura: That is our condition for accepting this job.

text.Sae Niijima: This is a "deal" then ...  That’s certainly a heavy condition. But very well, I accept. I swear to make Masayoshi Shido stand and be tried in the court of law. Besides ...  my pride won’t allow me to be continually saved by you all without doing anything in return.

text.Makoto Niijima: We’ll be counting on you.

text.Sojiro Sakura: Looks like it’s decided then?

text.Ann Takamaki: You’re the leader, Maaku, and this is officially our last mission. C’mon, say something!

text.Futaba Sakura: We already said that before though!

text.Haru Okumura: That’s fine. We’re doing it for real this time, after all.

text.Morgana: We don’t have much time, right? We should carry this out tomorrow.
...I’m counting on you guys. No matter what happens, you better see it through!
We’ve spent so much time together, but it all went by in a flash ...

text.ACTION: Just once more, for old time’s sake.

text.Newscaster: The streets are full of people and illuminated by colored lighting ...  Couples out with their children can be seen shopping for presents.

text.Morgana: Tomorrow’s Christmas Eve, huh ...  The only present I want is for my plan to succeed. I’ll be looking forward to it.
...This really is a nice and comfy little room.

text.ACTION: Nothing left to do. Let’s just sleep.

text.Morgana: OK ...  Good night.
...Actually, never mind. You must be tired.

Honestly ...  you’re amazing. There’s definitely something special about you. You dodge everything the enemies throw at you like it’s your destiny. At first I just thought you were going to be a useful tool for me ...  but now this is where I belong.
Aren’t you only going to be here for a year?
Still ...  it makes me happy to hear that. ...It’s not like me to say all that embarrassing stuff. But still ...  I think it’s fine. For tonight, at least.

text.ACTION: Mercurius, or Mercury, is the Roman equivalent of the Greek god Hermes, as you might have been able to guess from the winged sandals. He is the god of (deep breath) financial gain, commerce, messages, communication/divination, travelers, boundaries, luck, trickery, and thieves. He also guides souls to the underworld. He holds a caduceus in his left hand in most depictions, though they reversed it in this game for some reason. Here’s a fun fact about Mercurius: he’s notably less cool than Zorro!
Mercurius now nullifies Wind and resists Bless. We opt not to give him Evade Elec because we’re not really using Morgana much.

text.Joker: I can’t keep them open any longer...

text.Morgana: If gods really do exist ...  They’re being too hard on him ...

text.Igor: The source of what was hindering your rehabilitation ...  To think it would be the ignorant masses to which you tried to prove your integrity. Did they themselves not show elation for those who are unseen? Despite all that, they now say you do not exist. They toyed with you, yet none take responsibility. The distortion of man’s world is endlessly deep ...  Fixing it may now be impossible even with the appearance of a Trickster ...
The time of ruin is nigh ...  One due to the distortion of man’s own heart, from which none can escape ...

text.ACTION: Looks like Igor’s lost hope in humanity. This can’t be good…

Part 191: 12/22: Side Note- This City Is Built On Lies
	Part 180.5: 12/22: Side Note- This City Is Built On Lies
Well, let’s see what the citizens of Tokyo have to say now that they can’t spoil the game for us.

text.Chatter: He’s seriously still going on about the Phantom Thieves? What a hopeless idiot ...  He’s stuck in some kinda dream world.

text.Morgana: They’re not responding well to this at all ...  something’s wrong ...

text.Calm Student: I don’t even know anymore ...  Apparently, the Phantom Thieves were also just an internet rumor.

text.Energetic Student: Oh, well. All of that stuff pretty much has nothing to do with us.

text.Morgana: Something’s definitely off here ...

text.ACTION: Ah, Newspaper Club Member. I’ve missed our chats.

text.Newspaper Club Member: You went back to your parents’ place, right? Well, let’s make this next year a good one. I feel this weird vibe in the air. I wonder if it’s because of all the election chaos. The information the mass media is showing is pretty complicated, and it’s getting me frustrated.

I’m sorry to hear that. Hopefully something good will happen this year. I feel this weird vibe in the air. I wonder if it’s because of all the election chaos. The information the mass media is showing is pretty complicated, and it’s getting me frustrated.

Ahaha, acting cool, are you? Let’s make this next year a good one. I feel this weird vibe in the air. I wonder if it’s because of all the election chaos. The information the mass media is showing is pretty complicated, and it’s getting me frustrated.

text.Energetic First-Year: Oh, you mean the new prime minister? Hey, do you remember all the fuss about the Phantom Thieves?

text.Motivated First-Year: It’s like none of it ever happened. Pretty insane, if you ask me.

text.Energetic First-Year: No one could really steal someone’s heart like that. We’re so dumb for believing any of it.

text.Boy 5: I pretty much failed all my finals. I’m so screwed ...

text.Boy 13: You just need to adopt a new mindset. Get a fresh start in the spirit of the new year. Still, the year could have ended better. I mean, we still haven’t decided on a prime minister.

text.Fiery Soccer Player: Well, there’s been a big change in government. We can make that same kind of change next year!

text.Calm Basketball Player: I dunno if this big change in government is a good thing. Shido collapsed, and he looks worn out. Mannn, it’s almost Christmas! Can’t something good happen already?

text.Teacher 1: No, I voted for someone named Yoshida. He’s not the kind of politician who stands out though.

text.Gaudy Female Student: So he’s plan and simple like you? That’s hilarious!

text.Teacher 1: Well, I trust serious, low-key people more for that kind of job. Oh, how’d you do on your finals?

text.Gaudy Female Student: Gah ...  Sensei, you’re plain and simple, all right. Plain and simply cruel ...

text.ACTION: Kind Faculty Member is a good guy.

text.Starry-Eyed Student: Was it all just some illusion? Am I really just going crazy?
Right!? The Phantom Thieves really do exist! It’s weird that I feel insecure about this though. I mean, I used to idolize them so much ...
Hey, come on! Don’t tell me you didn’t know about their glorious comeback!? It’s weird that I feel insecure about this though. I mean, I used to idolize them so much ...

text.Young Cameraman: We should just stop pursuing this story, like the director instructed us to ...

text.Aggressive Reporter: He was serious when he said that the station won’t broadcast reports about the Phantom Thieves. The look on his face made me think that there’s no guarantee we’d live if we disobeyed him.

text.Protesting Man: I can only request this of you, my right-hand man, for you are the one who saved me!

text.Clear-Eyed Man: G-Great Sun God ... ! I will follow you!

text.Protesting Man: Then raise your hands with me! Wake the apostles of light, sleeping in Shibuya!

text.Rocker: Remember I still have this guitar/Don’t forget, I still have this song/ Hm, something’s not right ...  The whole city seems like it’s in a daze ...  The big bad got his just desserts, and that totally rocks, but ...  Where’s all the excitement?

text.Middle-Aged Woman: What!? Are you sick!?

text.Young-Looking Woman: It’s almost Christmas, and I don’t have a boyfriend ...

text.Middle-Aged Woman: Oh, you ...

text.Novice Pick-Up Artist: Wh-What’s wrong, Senpai?

text.Veteran Pick-Up Artist: ...It’s my loss, Kouhai.

text.Novice Pick-Up Artist: So it’s just like Shido said ...  Political power backed by just vanity and lies isn’t needed.

text.ACTION: I have no idea what these pick-up artists are talking about, but that’s nothing new.

text.Modest Housewife: Yes, we need him to bring real change to Japan. My son is nearing his entrance exams. I want a better Japan waiting for him on the other side.

text.Stylish Male Student: From what I saw on the internet ...  it looks that way. There’s no actual proof. Anyone who really believed in that was an idiot. How could a heart be stolen, anyway?

text.Easygoing Shujin Girl: I might be an idiot ...  but it would be nice if they were real ...

text.Sad Old Man: The politician who’s supposed to lead our country has fallen ill ...

text.Old Man 4: It’s the same sort of tragedy that happens in every era. Heroes fall before reaching their goals.

text.Sad Old Man: If we could just give him a little of whatever life we have left to live...

text.Boom Box: Now on to the next track on our countdown of this year’s hits ...  This one’s from the popular idol Rise Kujikawa-san, who has garnered support across the board.

text.Old Man 3: Hmph, who do they think they are, acting so happy? Nothing in the world’s been solved at all.

text.ACTION: Don’t talk that way about Rise, old man!

text.Mother: Hey ...  You can cry if you want. You don’t have to hold it in.

text.Dog loving Girl: (sniff) I want to see you again ...  Kotaro ...  (sob)

text.Mother: You’re a good girl for doing your best not to worry Kotaro. And now, he’ll be watching us from the sky.

text.ACTION: I’m not crying. You’re crying. Shut up.

text.Woman Pushing Promotion: If you’ve been safe this year, why not invest more in your safety for next year? Wanna-B-Alert is operating even over the new year! We work our hardest to give you peace of mind! Sign up for our end-of-the-year, last minute contract promotion for a free Wanna-Wanna-kun kagamimochi!

text.Sharp Lawyer: ...Only Shido knows. We’ll have to wait for him to get better.

text.Serious-looking Lawyer: Some people are trying to build a case against him, but it’ll be impossible to find him guilty.

text.Sharp Lawyer: Yeah, he’s the leader of the ruling party. The current prosecution can’t touch him.

text.Fast-Talking Man: I voted for Shido! United Future won with a landslide victory! But then I heard Mr. Shido got sick after campaigning too hard ...

text.Beautiful Maid: Oh, what perfect timing. Sheesh, you can never count on politicians.

text.Plump Man: That guy is finished. Why isn’t the garbage media covering the Phantom Thieves?

text.Skinny Man: For a netizen, you’re pretty uninformed. Didn’t you hear? The Phantom Thieves never existed. All along, the stories about them were just information terrorism, planned out by foreign countries.

text.Busy Young Man: Yes, a celebrolution! I’ve become a billionaire from stock trading! Listen. It’s about Prime Minister Shido. The companies ...  all linked to him ...

text.Frowning Officer: Yeah, OK, good for you. Man ...  The weird ones always come out near the end of the year.

text.Diligent Office Worker: Who knows? Maybe it was a broadcasting accident. I heard it might have been a prank, too.

text.Young Office Worker: It’s also strange how no one’s seen Shido. Especially since he was so confident at the beginning. I’m starting to not care about the elections. It’s not like they’re going to change anything, anyway.

text.Innocent Grade Schooler: They don’t talk about the Phantom Thieves on TV anymore, either. Is everyone going crazy?

text.Rebellious Grade Schooler: Yeah, my parents are suddenly saying the Phantom Thieves were never real at all ...

text.Innocent Grade Schooler: Mine too! It’s so weird ...  I can’t stop thinking about it whenever I try to do my homework.

text.Foreign Barker: But the Phantom Thieves never even existed? So, what we saw was ...  what? An illusion?
None of the regulars seem to care anymore. I’m so confused ...

text.Rural Young Man: This place ...  It suits ya. And with them Phantom Thieves gone, I know ya’ll be safe.

text.Adorable Woman: Yeah ...  People are saying that maybe they were made up after all.

text.Rural Young Man: I wonder what they really were ...  It’s kinda sad, knowin’ they’re gone.

text.ACTION: Let’s finish this off by hearing from our irreplaceable stereotypes over in Shinjuku.

text.Beefy Trendsetter: Fishy? No, you smell more like a beast. You really need to shower, even in the wintertime.

text.Scruffy Romantic: That’s not what I mean! Isn’t it weird that they’re saying the Phantom Thieves were just an illusion?

text.Beefy Trendsetter: Yeah ...  They were Akechi-kun’s rivals, too. I wonder if they’re trying to cover something up ...

text.Morgana: ...  ...  You and everyone else ...  You’ve all grown so much ...  No, this is no time to get sentimental. We’re going to end this on a bang! All right, let’s go!

text.ACTION: For sure. We’ll take care of this first thing.
...Right after we go to school! Why do we have class on Christmas Eve!?

text.Makoto Niijima: ...  ...  It’s finally time. You think it’ll go well?
Right. It’s something only we can do. See you at the usual place after school. I’ll tell everyone to come.

text.Female Student: Hey, look at that! Look who got the top score!

text.Joker: I wonder what score I got...

text.ACTION: Hahaha, eat shit peons! I am your superior!

text.Morgana: That’s amazing! Everyone’s gonna have their eyes on you now!

text.ACTION: Maaku gains Charm +3. That’s it. There is no other reward, and it is entirely pointless to do well on this exam because we already have maxed Charm.
Now, let’s head out for real!

text.Ann Takamaki: "The door to the depths of Mementos has been opened ... " Wait, does that mean--

text.Morgana: ...We’re really gonna do this, right?

text.Ann Takamaki: Of course!

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Why’re you askin’ now?

text.Morgana: I-I just thought, what am I gonna do if you guys freak out and bail on me!

text.Haru Okumura: Isn’t Mona-chan behaving ...  a little odd?

text.Ann Takamaki: You know, you’re right ...

text.Haru Okumura: Yeah ...

text.ACTION: For some weird fucking reason, they decide to start you on the first floor of Mementos, despite us needing to go to the very fucking bottom. I guess it’s because they can’t guarantee you’ve ever actually progressed beyond the first floor, because they were assholes and pretended this shit was optional when it actually wasn’t, but can you imagine if you’d never set foot back in Mementos, coming in here and having to go through like sixty-something floors of this bullshit? Thankfully, we got all the way to the last gate on our previous visit, so we’re fine.
Anyway, let’s head back up to the entrance.
Fuck everything, let’s just go home.

text.Makoto Niijima: We don’t know when the police might come after us, so we should avoid heading outside for now.

text.Futaba Sakura: But doesn’t not being able to replenish our supplies put our entire plan at risk?

text.Haru Okumura: In that case, how about we just go to the shops we need ... ? No wandering outside though.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: ...That seems to be a valid point of compromise. What are your thoughts, Joker?

text.Ann Takamaki: Just remember you can never be too cautious, OK? If we get caught this time, we’re done for.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Guess that means no more goin’ for beef bowls ‘til we figure out what to do with Mementos ...

text.Morgana: All right then, where are we going?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Mkay, the search continues!

text.ACTION: In Persona 4, the final dungeon was a surprise, so the game let you temporarily leave the TV world on the last day of the game to go shopping for weapons and supplies. This is just following from that example.
Anyway, let’s warp down to that final floor we reached.

text.Makoto Niijima: It should be. Why, what’s wrong?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: I dunno, it looks just like all the other ones ...  I was thinkin’ it’s a little disappointin’ ...  Maybe we worked too hard to get down here or something.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The lack of unforeseen circumstances is nothing to complain about. Let us continue.

text.Futaba Sakura: It’s some big, fossil-looking thing ...  Is that the Treasure ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So this is where that crowd of people was trying to reach ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: People are walking in and out of there, so the other side of the wall must be ...  Wait! It’s not a wall, but a giant door ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Guess that means the Treasure’s not here. C’mon, let’s stay focused.

text.Morgana: I bet that means the inner depths the Meta-Nav was talking about before are right ahead.

text.Futaba Sakura: Hold on. The door only opens from this side ...

text.Ann Takamaki: ...What do you mean?

text.Futaba Sakura: Well, I took a quick peek at the mechanism inside the door ...  And it looks like you can only open it from here. We can get in, but nothing can get out.

text.ACTION: Then how are we going to get out?

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s as though whatever lies within has been locked away ...

text.Haru Okumura: Wait, so you’re saying that the people going in there are choosing a life of imprisonment ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I have never felt such eerieness before ...  What is this place ... ?

text.Morgana: We’ll find out once we reach the depths. Come on, let’s go.

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s so creepy ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So those strange pipes tunneling through Mementos were originating down here after all ...  You know, I have been considering this for some time ...  but they remind me somewhat of veins ...

text.Ann Takamaki: I mean, what does everyone think this world is ... !?

text.Morgana: Calm down, Lady Ann. The Treasure is definitely here, and that’s what’s important now. And I can sense something else ...  A tremendous presence that’s coming from much deeper within ...

text.Makoto Niijima: I don’t know that I want to find out what that may be ...  but we must harden our resolves. It’s time to head for the depths!

text.ACTION: Well, we’re in the belly of the beast now. Let’s proceed onw-wait, what?
Hey, Caroline. What are you doing outside of the Velvet Room?

text.Caroline: You ...  Hmph. ...Guiding inmates along in their rehabilitation is our duty ...  OK. I’ll help you a bit.

text.Joker: It feels like my stamina and health has recovered somewhat...

text.Caroline: (blushing)

text.ACTION: Now, this is the game throwing you a bone. It knows that you’re pretty fucked if you run out of SP here and don’t have any restoratives, so it allows you to replenish your HP and SP with Caroline. Unfortunately, this does not replace any bullets you use, so watch out.
Up ahead, we find a crowd waiting before a door.

text.Morgana: It looks like they’re all trying to get past that door ...

text.Ann Takamaki: But why’s it so crowded!?

text.Futaba Sakura: It looks like the door’s keeping them all out. We’ll have to try and look for another way in.

text.ACTION: Conveniently, there are platforms we can jump to nearby.

text.Futaba Sakura: Huh, it looks like we can go in through here too. Be careful, OK?

text.Ann Takamaki: The Shadows out front were trying to get in here, right? What could it be ... ?

text.ACTION: Up ahead, we immediately come across a peculiar room.

text.Futaba Sakura: Are those ...  chains on them? ...Is this a prison!?

text.Makoto Niijima: Technically speaking, I would say it’s someone’s Shadow ...

text.Female Shadow Prisoner: Don’t open the cells, OK? I have no intention of leaving this place ... !

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: What’re you saying? You’re being kept in a prison.

text.Morgana: This reminds me of Kamoshida’s castle ...  They’re like the "slaves" we saw there.

text.Old Shadow Prisoner: In the depths within is a system that grants desires ...

text.Ann Takamaki: A system that grants ...  desires?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Something like that exists ... ? Here!?

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s no use. You can’t reason with these people.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: They’re truly "distorted," just like the scenery here ...

text.Man 5: You end up searching for stuff or being troubled because you’re outside the prison. There are things you don’t need to know to live on.

text.Old Shadow Prisoner: He’s right. Things like the details on the system, the locked "Quarantine Cell" ...

text.Makoto Niijima: Quarantine? Who’s locked in there?

text.Old Shadow Prisoner: Supposedly a great and truly dangerous criminal, but who would want to check a place like that? Come now, we don’t have to chat like this. Why not come inside?

text.Mementos Shadow: Removing your restraints is not allowed. Outsiders ...  must be eliminated!

text.ACTION: These guys are weak to Wind and use Physical and Hamaon. Simple.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Wait a sec ...  This is everyone’s Palace, right? Not like Kamoshida’s castle ...  Who’s keepin’ these people here ... ?

text.Haru Okumura: Mona-chan ... ?

text.Morgana: I’ve ...  seen this place before.

text.Ann Takamaki: Hold on though. It wasn’t open until we came here today.

text.Morgana: Sorry ...  It’s just a sense I’m getting. Still ...  it feels like I’m really close to remembering something important ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Y’know, comin’ in here was what you wanted from the beginning. We just gotta keep movin’ on!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: On top of that, I’m curious to know who the ruler of this place is.

text.Morgana: Yeah ...  You’re right.

text.Haru Okumura: Wait, what about these people ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: Leave them be. They’ll be taken care of if we erase Mementos.

text.Futaba Sakura: Hey, it’s dangerous to keep standing around here! Let’s get going!

text.ACTION: Before we continue, I’ve got some exciting news! See, if I’m going to spend the rest of my fucking life doing this, I figure I might as well make fat stacks in the process! So, I’ve decided to sell the fuck out and accept one of the many corporate sponsorship deals that have been cluttering my inbox! Now, I’m a discerning, careful person, so I wouldn’t pick just anyone. No, I could only the best, most responsible, ethical, and kind partnership, which is why I chose…
Amazon dot com, baby!!!!! Surely there is no company with a better reputation at the current moment!
...I’m being informed that my time is better spent elsewhere. Which is why I went with the runner-up, Facebook!
Anyway, we now encounter our first enemies.
And I start to notice, to my chagrin, that this update might as well be called “Maaku Hamiru And The Dungeon Full Of Enemies We Already Fucking Have!”
This is Moloch. It’s weak to Ice, uses Fire and Psy, and inflicts Fear.
This writhing mass is our target for the afternoon.

text.Drained Businessman: The world is already complete ...  There’s nothing left to do ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: The hell ... ? Is this some kinda prison cell too ... ?

text.Ann Takamaki: Plus there are those blood vessel things coming down into it ...

text.ACTION: I fucked up an ambush on these Melchizedeks. Again, weak to Wind, use Hamaon and Physical.

text.Futaba Sakura: Calm down. It doesn’t seem like it’s a trap or anything. Try touching it again, Joker.
Hmmm. There seems to be more to this prison, but right now this is a dead end for some reason.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Then this must be a security system. Will we be able to proceed if we disable it?

text.Futaba Sakura: ...Prolly. I’ll need you to look into it a little more though. Do it again, Joker. It looks like touching it turns it back off, so it can’t be that dangerous, right?

text.ACTION: Maaku turns the device back on.

text.Futaba Sakura: So the color of a spot changes when you walk on top of it ...  Joker, try making the entire floor blue for now.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: D-Dude, you have any idea what that’s gonna do? Are you sure it’ll be safe?

text.Futaba Sakura: Eh, all great things start with a leap of faith! The decision is yours, Joker!

text.ACTION: Well, that’s certainly one way to approach this. Our objective now is to make all the tiles blue.
We start on A1 (which does not start as a blue tile), then move south through B1 and C1, east to C2, north to B2, east to B3, north again to A3, then west twice through A2 and finally back to A1.
The last tile that turns blue needs to be the one we started on, because this will happen.

text.Futaba Sakura: Aha ...  It’s probably connected to the color of the floor somehow. So since we changed all the spots on the floor to blue, the device’s color changed too. Joker, try touching it now.

text.ACTION: Joker touches the device. If this was not the final space we stepped on, the device will turn yellow again the moment we turn one of the other tiles back, so watch out.
The path forward lowers and the weird Legend of Zelda chime sounds.

text.Futaba Sakura: So that device is not only a switch, but also the wall that’s blocking our path.

text.Haru Okumura: That’s a pretty elaborate device ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It is only natural that security is tight in a prison. Then again, no inmates actually wish to leave ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Ugh, can’t you just try takin’ it easy on us this time!?

text.ACTION: This is kind of bullshit, because you don’t automatically enter the fight. Instead, the instant the cutscene ends, you’re detected by the enemies and they start chasing you.
Suffice it to say, I fuck up the preemptive strike again. These Nebiros(es) use Physical and Curse, including instant-kills. They’re weak to Bless.
This is Gozer Lillith. It uses Ice, Fire, and Wind, can remove buffs and debuffs, and can drain your SP. It’s weak to Fire.

text.Dull-Eyed Student: Nobody listens if we try to oppose them ...  All that happens is our spirits are crushed ...  It might be smarter to just accept life for what it is and surrender to their will ...

text.Haru Okumura: This is just like how I used to be ...  If I had stayed like that, I would sound just like her now ... !

text.ACTION: This is Dionysus. It has no weaknesses and uses Debilitate (a fucked-up move that lowers all three of an ally’s parameters), Electricity, and Physical. It also can use Thermopylae to raise all three of its own parameters if you ambush it.

text.Befuddled Man: All of this is going to end soon anyway ...  You might as well patiently await your demise ...

text.Ann Takamaki: It’s all ...  going to end? What is he saying ... ?

text.ACTION: Eh, I’m sure that ominous warning is nothing to worry about.

text.Stern Businessman: Following those things is the only correct way of living. What is there to be confused about? Anyone who can’t do that is just an outcast. All you really have to do is obey the rules ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: How pathetic ...  He should be more aware of his situation ...

text.ACTION: Up ahead, we run into another puzzle device.

text.Futaba Sakura: It should be, for the most part. Give it a try, Joker.
The mechanism should still be the same though. We just need to make all of them blue in the end.

text.ACTION: Stepping on the blue tile returns it to yellow, of course.
Okay, this one is barely any more complicated than the last one. The only complication is that we have to double back a couple of times.

Start on A1, then head south once to B1. Then, head east to B2, and immediately head back to your only option, B1. Then head south twice through C1 and D1. Then go north again to B1. You will notice that A1, B1, and C1 are all still yellow, so head south again to C1, then go north through B1 to A1. All of the circles are now blue.

text.Exhausted Young Man: No matter how much they beat or kick you ...  it is all for your own self-benefit in the end ...  If anything, I should feel thankful ...  This is exactly what I deserve ...

text.Ann Takamaki: ...It hurts hearing this. I had the exact same mindset in the past ...

text.ACTION: Again, a rather basic shape that should not be too difficult to figure out.
Once more, start on A1. South twice through B1 and C1, east to C2, south to D2, north back to C2, west back to C1, north back to B1, east to B2, and finally head west to return to B1 and north to A1.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It truly seems to go on ad infinitum ...  Where does it lead?

text.Morgana: I never expected there would be this much here ...  But the Treasure’s presence is getting stronger. We’re going in the right direction for sure.

text.ACTION: At the bottom, we find another circular room.
Oh, shit! Was not expecting to see ol’ Mophead McSpeedo again!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: No ...  Madarame ...

text.Haru Okumura: Father isn’t around anymore ...

text.Futaba Sakura: ...Sorry.

text.Haru Okumura: No, it’s OK. More importantly, look there.

text.Suguru Kamoshida: I finally get to live without having to think for myself now.

text.Ichiryusai Madarame: I mistakenly thought myself to be talented ...  but now I think I’m a fool for wanting too much.

text.ACTION: Even this Kaneshiro’s facial expressions are great.

text.Junya Kaneshiro: I’m done actin’ like a big shot. Who cares if I’m stupid? It’s not like you get punished for bein’ dumb. Nobody needs to strive to be more than they really are.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: These people seem completely different than they were before ...

text.Makoto Niijima: I don’t think it’s because they had a change of heart though ...

text.Morgana: Wait ...  Have they chosen a life of captivity after they lost their distorted desires ... ?

text.Masayoshi Shido: Unfortunately, Okumura isn’t here with us.

text.Haru Okumura: Now if you don’t mind, what in the world is this place?

text.Masayoshi Shido: It’s supposedly called the "Prison of Regression."

More importantly, does this look like captivity to you? Why, it’s the exact opposite. The utmost freedom is available to anyone who desires it here. This is the freedom to not make decisions ...  The release from having to think for yourself.
It is far more marvelous than the country I wished to create ...

text.Haru Okumura: Release from having to think ... ? But that’s ...

text.Masayoshi Shido: However, there are some fools who cannot stay put in this place. In other words, they are escaped convicts ...  Of course, I’m talking about our past selves. Such people are segregated from this peaceful world and locked away in their own Palace.

text.Makoto Niijima: So those are the Palace rulers ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We ...  sent ‘em back here ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I don’t understand ...  Just what have we been doing by using the cognitive world ... ?

text.ACTION: C’mon, guys. This is definitely weird and certainly changes our understanding of “distortions,” but we’re about to fuck this place up anyway. It doesn’t really matter.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: That’s true, but ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: This ain’t the time to be gettin’ confused! We’re here as the society-fixin’ Phantom Thieves today!

text.Makoto Niijima: Having the freedom to not make your own decisions only means that someone else is controlling you! Tell me. Who is the ruler here? Who made all of this ... ?

text.Masayoshi Shido: What an odd question to ask. It should be obvious: every member of the general public.

text.ACTION: I mean, yeah, duh. We kinda knew that. Or at least, I thought we did.

text.Masayoshi Shido: Haven’t you learned anything in school? The collective ruler of a democratic society is its people.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: D-Don’t lie outta your ass like that! I mean, there was a guard here earlier! That means someone’s gotta be lookin’ out for you guys, right?

text.Masayoshi Shido: You may be right. We are the ones "looking out" upon everyone else.

text.Makoto Niijima: So the ones who least want the prison to be tampered with ...  are the prisoners themselves ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: It don’t matter what this guy’s talkin’ about ...  We’re gonna erase all of Mementos anyways! C’mon, let’s keep goin’! Mona! The Treasure’s in the deepest part, right!?

text.Morgana: I saw the humans in here ...  and realized I looked different than them for some reason ...

text.Makoto Niijima: Is that why you thought you would regain your true form if we destroyed Mementos?

text.Morgana: Sorry ...  I’m still missing a lot of my memories ...  But I know I started randomly checking a bunch of Palaces ...  Then my next memory is about that bastard Kamoshida’s.
Dammit ...  We got careless!

text.Makoto Niijima: Let’s run!

text.ACTION:
Part 193: 12/24: The Sweet Embrace Of Nihilism
	Part 182: 12/24: The Sweet Embrace Of Nihilism

So, we start off this update immediately bumrushed by Shadows and caught in an ambush because you’re not ready for a fight immediately after that cutscene with the camera facing the wrong direction! Also, it’s a double fight, because fuck you.
Ryuji learns Maziodyne to replace Mazionga.
Futaba also learns Subrecover SP EX, which automatically replaces Subrecover SP. Now backup party members will have their SP restored by 3% instead of 1%.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Destruction is ...  pleasing? She cannot be in her right mind. It is as though she wishes for the world to end ...

text.ACTION: This is Chernobog. It is weak to Bless and Fire, uses a bunch of different Physical moves, and can cast Mudoon. It also drains Curse and Ice and blocks Electricity.
This is Baal. It drains and uses Wind, as well as Physical, Matarukaja, and Charge.

text.Wry-smiling Woman: I heard there were some others who escaped this place, but they found their way back recently ...  Wouldn’t it be better if people just lived with the hand they’ve been dealt? How hilarious ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Is she talkin’ about Kamoshida and all the others ... ? I dunno how to put this ...  but I’m thinkin’ these people’re more human than the ones in reality ...

text.Dull-Eyed Young Man: And besides ...  it’s going to be happening soon ...

text.Futaba Sakura: So he just wants to see the world from online, huh ... ? I know how that might feel, but it gets old after a while. I can speak from experience ...  And besides that, what’s "happening soon"?

text.Smirking Woman: So, why don’t you guys come join us? The world’s going to end soon anyway, so you might as well ...

text.Haru Okumura: When did these people begin to think this prison is a comfortable place to live ... ?

text.ACTION: Ann learns Fire Amp to replace Evade Ice.

Haru also learns Cripple (50% damage boost to Gun attacks, stacks with Snipe) to replace Amrita Shower. Amrita Shower is plenty useful, but here in the endgame we’re generally going to want Maaku to be taking care of ailment relief.
We finally come to our first safe room. This dungeon isn’t terribly long in comparison to the others, but the safe rooms are still spread very thin.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Even though this is the cognitive world, I find it hard to believe this is underneath Shibuya ...

text.Haru Okumura: It’s known as a city of freedom, both in fun and in fashion ...

text.ACTION: “Freedom” is certainly a way to describe the fashion of TWEWY, sure.

text.Makoto Niijima: Yes, it’s a brilliant place. The crosswalk in front of the station is internationally-known nowadays. And yet, people seem to somehow consider it a prison for them ...

text.Ann Takamaki: A city of freedom ...  Is that really true?

text.Morgana: What do you mean?

text.Ann Takamaki: Like, all Shibuya really is to me is a congested station where changing stops is frustrating ...  Are the people here really free ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That aside, how far you think we’re at now, Mona?

text.Morgana: O-Oh, let’s see ...  Maybe halfway ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm, we’ve come pretty far.

text.Morgana: But wait ...  The Treasure feels a lot closer than it ever has before ...  What’s going on here ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: We did pass through Mementos to get here. It may make sense if we take that fact into consideration.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Welp, we just got another half to go! Let’s get fired up and do this!

text.ACTION: The saferoom itself is at a minor fork in the road. We head north and immediately come across another device.
Looks simple enough. Start on A2, south to B2, east to B3, south through C3 and D3, west through D2 and D1, north through C1 and B1, east again to B2, and north to A2.
Uhh, hold on a second. South… West… East… Argh, no!
Thankfully, Makoto’s here to inform us we’re boned.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Huh? Whaddya mean?

text.Makoto Niijima: Given the room’s shape and number of spots, there’s no mathematical way we can make it all blue.

text.Haru Okumura: Then, what do we do ... ?

text.Makoto Niijima: I’m not sure ...  but if this is really a security system, there has to be a way past it.

text.ACTION: Makoto doesn’t seem to understand what the purpose of a security system is.

text.Makoto Niijima: We may want to try checking elsewhere for the time being.

text.ACTION: On our way out of this area, we spot this weird indentation. I forget to examine it, but you’ve played enough JRPGs to know that we have to put some manner of doohickey in there.
We head south at the fork this time.

text.Haru Okumura: There’s something shining back there ...  What could it be?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Either way, if it is worth being protected, it should be safe to assume that it’s of value to us. What do you think, Joker? Shall we defeat it and take whatever it is protecting?
Understood!

text.Mementos Warden: Hmph, I won’t deny that you’ll need it to continue onward. But mark my words, you’ll never get your hands on it. After all, you’ll have to go through me to do so!

text.ACTION: This guy’s weak to Psy and Nuke and drains Physical, Gun, and Curse. He uses powerful Physical attacks exclusively.
He doesn’t put up much of a fight, though.

text.Makoto Niijima: Hm ...  What do you think this could be used for ... ?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Who knows? It’ll prolly come in handy though. I mean, that strong-ass Shadow was guardin’ it.

text.Resigned Middle-Aged Man: I’ve heard there’s a place reserved for the most terribly evil people of them all ...

text.Futaba Sakura: ...Do you think that could be the Quarantine Cell we heard about?

text.Hopeless Student: Here, any wish can become reality ...  and isn’t that all anyone wants out of life?

text.Morgana: These people really think their wishes are going to come true ... ?

text.ACTION: South to B2, east to B3, south to C3, west to C2, east to C3, south to D3, west to D2 and D1, north to C1 and B1, east to B2 and B3, south to C3, north to B3, west to B2, and finally north to return to A2.
Another one of these massive spirals downward, eh?

text.Makoto Niijima: We’re so far underground at this point ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: I hope we don’t suddenly find ourselves in a giant pool of lava ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Still, we gotta keep going ... !

text.Haru Okumura: Doesn’t that cell seem ...  different from the others?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Supposedly, the most sinful, most dangerous inmate is held within ...

text.Morgana: This place smells familiar for some reason ...

text.Haru Okumura: Mona-chan ... ?

text.Morgana: This is it.

text.Haru Okumura: Born ... ? Inside the prison?

text.Ann Takamaki: Wait, then are YOU the dangerous inmate!?

text.Morgana: No ...  the inmate wasn’t me ...
Someone created me here ...  To guide all of you ...

text.Haru Okumura: Guide ... ? And who is this someone ... ?

text.Morgana: Ngh ...  I can’t remember ...  Damn it ...  I’m so close ...  but my memory is too foggy ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Y’know, hearin’ all this just makes me wanna know what’s inside.

text.Mementos Shadow: Alert! Alert! Capture them at once!

text.ACTION: And the game throws you into an automatic ambush. Bullshit.
The dragon dude uses Fire and Physical (which he can Charge), and the Nebiroses are near-identical to their regular Shadow forms. The only hurdle here is the fact that they get to act first.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Given how important this cell appears to be, the depths of Mementos must be near. Mona’s memories may return if we continue on ...

text.Morgana: Yeah ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: So, we’re finally gettin’ close to the public’s Treasure, huh?

text.Morgana: Now that I think about it, it makes sense that Mementos would connect to some place like underneath Shibuya. Everyone crams themselves into packed underground boxes day after day without any complaints ...  From my standpoint, those are the true inmates of Mementos. It’s no surprise the places are connected.

text.Makoto Niijima: You know, the voices of the public may have led the Phantom Thieves on more than any criminal ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Seriously! Let’s hurry up and steal that Treasure so we can crush Mementos!

text.Haru Okumura: We truly are reforming society ...  Let’s go!

text.ACTION: I guess we’re just leaving the Quarantine Cell behind, then? No way that could possibly be important.
This is Thor. He’s weak to Psy, drains Electricity, and uses powerful Physical and Electric skills. He can also use Tarukaja and Charge, and he has Shock Boost and Elec Amp.
Yusuke replaces Kamu Susano-o’s Heat Wave with Vorpal Blade, which deals Severe Physical to all enemies.
Morgana learns Wind Amp. I replaced Masukunda with it, but immediately realized that I fucked up and actually wanted to get rid of Samarecarm, oops.
The guy on the right is Belial. It’s pretty much identical to its “boss” form, in that it has no resistances outside of blocking Curse and uses Maragidyne, Myriad Slashes, and Charge exclusively.

text.Cynical Middle-Aged Man: The only reason you can act so grand is that you live in a safe zone, devoid of possible failure. How does it feel to hear the truth? Are you relieved to know you’ve been fooling yourselves? Now what I really can’t understand is what you call "happiness." But whatever, I guess. Everyone has their own way to reach it. Either way, stop trying to tell us what to do. This is how we can attain true happiness. I don’t care what you guys think of it. We have no reason to listen to your complaints!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Hm ...  If you truly believe all of that, then you are free to do as you wish.

text.Unfriendly Woman: It was a fun joke while it lasted, but it’s old news now. Tell me something a little more exciting.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: A joke!? Bullshit! Y’know people have actually died from those mental shutdowns, right!? You ever thought of that!?

text.Vacant Young Man: I’d rather use that time for myself before it’s too late ...

text.Makoto Niijima: There’s no such thing as "time for yourself" in a prison cell. Why are they acting like this ... ?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: How can one who cannot open their eyes be a judge of beauty ... ?

text.ACTION: Another device here. It’s hard to tell in this image, but the platform we’re currently walking on is transparent. This doesn’t actually effect anything in the upcoming puzzle, and it might as well just be a blank tile. I will mark it red in the diagram.
Hm… as we step on more tiles, the lights on them darken.
Still, nothing to worry about. East through A2 and A3, south through B3 and C3, west through C2 and C1, north through B1 and back to A1. Finished.

text.Makoto Niijima: But what could those patterns on the floor have meant ... ?

text.Futaba Sakura: I’m pretty sure I figured it out while I was watching ...  There was a limitation on this area. You could only change the colors up to ten times. Any more than that and we’d have had to start over.

text.Ann Takamaki: You solved a puzzle like that on your first try, Joker ... ? That’s seriously incredible!

text.ACTION: Eh, not really. As long as you don’t double back you can’t fuck this one up.
But Futaba’s correct. Stepping on an eleventh tile will deactivate the whole thing and you’ll have to try again.

text.Resigned Young Man: And my dreams ... ? I just have to deal with never seeing them come true. It’s a cruel fact of life.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: "Reality is ending"? That is similar to what the others in the prison are saying ...  What could that mean?

text.ACTION: Up ahead, we come across another barrier and another device. We obviously can’t solve this one yet due to the presence of the barrier, but here’s what it would have looked like:

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: My apologies, but we did not come here seeking approval.

text.ACTION: West from the start at A2 to A1, south to B1, east from there all the way to B5, north to A5, south to B5, north to A5 again, and west three to return to A2.
And our reward is another thingamajig.

There are a couple of ways to do this one, but I did a figure-eight: east from the start at A2 to A3, south to C3, west to C2, north through B2 to A2, west to A1, south to C1, and east to C2, whereupon we use B2 again to reach A2. Please note that the diagram and these instructions are relative to the default camera position when you start the puzzle, not the map. I actually had to go back and remake some of my diagrams because they were inconsistent about this.
Further in, we come across Yamata-no-Orochi. It is weak to Nuke, blocks Ice, and uses Mabufudyne and Oni-Kagura (Medium Physical to the party with a chance of Rage).
Aaaaaaaaaaaaand this is a visit from your IT department, also known as Mara. It blocks Gun, drains Fire, and reflects Curse. It also uses Fire, Curse, Physical, and Almighty.

text.Tired Middle-Aged Woman: It won’t matter soon enough anyway ...

text.Morgana: I see ...  She doesn’t realize what being governed by someone really means ...

text.Calm Young Man: Just let me see out the end of this world in peace ...

text.Makoto Niijima: I’m curious as to why everyone believes the world is coming to an end ...  What could they mean ... ?

text.ACTION: Let’s try this one. West from the start at A3 to A1, south all the way to D1, east to D2, north to C2. Then, west to C1, north to B1, and north to A1… and we’re out of moves.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Are you certain about that?

text.Makoto Niijima: Absolutely. Taking the shape and number of spots into account, no route could complete that quick. Having said that, there seems to be another device in this room. Why don’t we try that first?

text.ACTION: Yes, there are actually three devices in this room.
We’ll start with the third one, all the way to the east (because that’s the one we need to do first).
Start at A2, west to A1, east to A3, south to B3, north to A3, west to A2, east to A3, west back to A2. Easy peasy, and with two moves left.
The device’s platform lowers, allowing us to complete the next puzzle in the sequence.
The platform that lowered was C2. We start at A3, west to A1, south to C1, east to C3, north to A3. Bing badda boom.
And now the obstruction that prevented us from finishing that first puzzle is gone.
Start at A3, west to A1, south to D1, east to D2, north all the way to A2, south to B2, north to A2, east back to A3. Ten moves.

text.Ann Takamaki: About time ...  Now we can keep moving forward!

text.Haru Okumura: Nicely done, Joker!

text.ACTION: And we finally come across another safe room, which means we’re at the end of Mementos Depths.

text.Haru Okumura: It seems we’ve made it quite far ...  What are your thoughts, Mona-chan?

text.Morgana: We’re almost to the Treasure ...  Its presence is really close now ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: So the time has finally arrived ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Yup, this is seriously it. Let’s take the public’s Treasure, you guys!

text.Ann Takamaki: But ...  what’s going to happen once we actually take it?

text.Makoto Niijima: I doubt that alone will be enough to make everything right. Still, it is worth going through with ...

text.Haru Okumura: Mm-hm. I’m sure that everyone’s hearts will change somehow.

text.Futaba Sakura: It’d be super weird if people all over the city just started crying and apologizing for stuff though!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Well, results are yet unknown, but we have come this far ...  We must continue onward.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Hell yeah!

text.Morgana: The word failure’s not in my dictionary!

text.Ann Takamaki: This is the end!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: The labor we have put in up to this point shall finally come to fruition!

text.Makoto Niijima: That’s right!

text.Futaba Sakura: I’m here too, so you guys don’t gotta worry about anything!

text.Haru Okumura: Let’s bring all of our hard work to a triumphant close!

text.ACTION: Before we continue, let’s do some last-minute fusin’.
First, Cybele from Yamata-no-Orochi and Baal. We have to pay 94900 yen to fuse above our level, though.

text.Cybele: I’ll hunt you down and skin you if you dare cheat on me. I’m your mask now ...  You better be ready.

text.ACTION: Cybele is the Phrygian mother goddess of the earth, who is also associated with wildlife (lions in particular) and vegetation. She was a protector of several city-states, including Athens. According to her in-game description, she took Attis, her priest, as a lover, but he was driven insane when he was forced to marry another.
Also on the docket for today, Siegfried from Thor and Byakko.

text.Siegfried: Your soul shall act as a tool to transform my dauntless might into an unstoppable mask.

text.ACTION: Siegfried is the German name of the hero from the epic poem “Das Nibelungenlied.” His original Norse name was Sigurd. He slayed the dragon Fafnir, and bathed in his blood to make himself invincible. However, a leaf that had stuck to his shoulder gave him a weak spot.
Now, let’s head back down and make our approach towards whatever lies at the heart of Mementos.

text.Tired Businessman: I feel sick just thinking about it. All I can really do now is ignore it, I suppose.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: What a load of shit ...  Hey! The world’s not gonna get better on its own, y’know!

text.Timid Young Man: I might lose the one place I belong if I put myself out there ...  I’m afraid of that happening, so I think I’ll just stay as I am ...

text.Ann Takamaki: Uh, your current situation should be what’s scaring you! How’s he OK with all of this ... ?

text.ACTION: Only one way forward now. What’s that ahead of us…?

text.Makoto Niijima: It’s so big ...  I can’t believe there’s such a giant thing all the way down here ...

text.Haru Okumura: Is everyone’s Treasure inside?

text.Morgana: Yeah ...  That should be the case.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: But this bizarrely ominous air about it ...  It could be likened to a temple of sorts ...

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: Th-There’s no point freakin’ out now! C’mon, let’s go!

text.ACTION:
Part 194: 12/24: The Heart Of The World
	Part 183: 12/24: The Heart Of The World
We’ve entered the shrine. What are those veins ahead of us?

text.Morgana: It has to be ...  Let’s go.

text.ACTION: Let’s jump down these “stairs” and check it out.
This is our last opportunity to go back and do anything in Mementos, Mementos Depths, or the shops. We’re going to plow ahead anyway. Never look back.

text.Futaba Sakura: And ...  what’s that thing in the middle?

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It appears this is our final destination ...  the depths of Mementos.

text.Haru Okumura: In that case, is the Treasure of Mementos somewhere in here?

text.Morgana: I’ve never been here ...  but I can sense it.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: But something that large will be impossible to carry out of here.

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We just gotta make it disappear, right? If we can’t move it, then we’ll just hafta destroy it!

text.Morgana: Yeah ...  That will work.

text.Ann Takamaki: Once we do that, the entire Metaverse is going to disappear, right? This is finally it ...

text.Futaba Sakura: Oh, I guess it’s no surprise we’ve been discovered.

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Even the inmates are starting to liven up. How eerie ...  Are they planning something?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: That must mean this thing’s gotta be the Treasure. They saved us the trouble of checkin’!

text.Makoto Niijima: ...Hold on. Something’s off.

Shido said the masses are allowing themselves to be held captive here ...  Could they truly be operating this gigantic system that eliminates iutruders on its own? The prison guards and soldiers were very organized too ...

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: Are you trying to say that someone else rules this place? Is it not the public?

text.Ryuji Sakamoto: We don’t have time to worry about that! Leave it for later!

text.Morgana: All right, guys! We better not lose now!

text.ACTION: Hello, old friend. It’s a pleasure to hear you again.

text.Futaba Sakura: All right, let’s do it!

text.ACTION: Well, it seems our final boss for this evening is a giant… cup. Okay, then.
Let’s start with some Charge and Matarukaja as a show of our new power.
Hey, we’re already making progress. This thing doesn’t have that much health. We’ll be done here in no time.
Ow. Whatever, though. This thing only gets one turn, who cares?
Pff, is this it, you overgrown bucket? You’re not even putting up a fight! I took out a third of your health in two turns, you call yourself a boss!?
Huh? The prisoners are freaking out!

text.Yusuke Kitagawa: It seems hopeless if there are this many inmates supporting it ... !

text.Ann Takamaki: Who’s that!?

text.ACTION: Okay, this is actually really weird and silly, but I should probably mention it. In Persona 3 and Persona 4, Igor was voiced in Japanese by Isamu Tanonaka. Unfortunately, Tanonaka died in 2010, so his role was scaled back considerably for later games, with all of his following appearances using archive audio. That’s part of the reason the Igor we spend most of this game with was a fake. However, they did not actually recast Real Igor. If you play the Japanese vocal track, it’s again just archive audio, with any lines they don’t have just being muted.

Anyway, in the English versions of Persona 3 and 4, Igor was played by Dan Woren. The “Warden” (Fake Igor) in 5 is voiced by David Lodge, but they didn’t get Woren back for this game either, instead using Kirk Thornton for some fucking reason, because hey, he was already in the booth recording for the SIU Director, I guess!
